TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.phas.text: If the second input $g$ is phase independent, concrete phase advection by any first input $f$ vanishes. The direction may have a nonzero phase speed, but it acts on a constant phase slice. This is the compatibility needed for means appearing as the advected field.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.phas.summary: A phase-independent field cannot be differentiated in phase

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.phas.text: If $\langle\kappa,f\rangle=0$ at every slab point for the first input $f$, phase advection of any second input vanishes. The selected phase direction is then the zero vector. The conclusion depends on transversality of the advecting field, not phase independence.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.phas.summary: A transverse field cannot advect in the phase direction

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.phas.text: For a profile independent of phase on the slab, the derivative within the slab applied to the unit phase direction is zero at every slab point. The proof compares the actual derivative of its constant phase slice with the derivative of a constant function. No time-independence conclusion is drawn.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.phas.summary: An independent profile has no phase derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.phas.text: If the scalar pressure profile is phase independent, its concrete fast gradient vanishes. Its scalar phase derivative is zero, so multiplying by the transported covector still gives zero. This supplies the pressure compatibility required of a mean output, for arbitrary periodic coefficient profiles.

If a periodic profile equals its phase average, its underlying smooth profile is independent of phase on the slab. The average is already known to ignore the output phase coordinate, and the equality transfers that fact. This turns the abstract mean-output condition into actual phase independence.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.phas.summary: A fixed point of averaging is phase independent

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.phas.text: For each time and label, the phase slice of a periodic profile has period one. This also holds for the stored representative outside the slab, where that representative is zero.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.phas.summary: A bundled profile has period one in phase

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.prof.text: The actual phase-averaging operator restricts to periodic vector profiles because its output is phase independent. It is a linear map using the same unit-period integral as the smooth-profile operator. The construction changes neither the time domain nor the coefficient functions outside their existing representation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.prof.summary: Average within the space of periodic profiles

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.prof.text: When the underlying smooth profile is independent of phase on the slab, the periodic phase-averaging operator fixes it. The proof lifts the corresponding smooth-profile identity. This establishes one direction of the correspondence between actual phase independence and being fixed by the concrete averaging operator.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.prof.summary: The mean of an independent profile is itself

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.prof.text: The periodic phase-averaging operator is idempotent: averaging an already averaged profile returns the same result. The first average is phase independent, so the fixed-point lemma applies. This supplies the concrete projection law required by the abstract finite-hierarchy solvers.

Averaging any smooth vector profile produces a profile independent of the output phase coordinate. The proof evaluates the same phase integral at two output phases; their time and label coordinates agree. The input need not already be periodic for this phase-independence statement.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.prof.summary: The phase mean no longer depends on phase

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.prof.text: The underlying smooth profile of the periodic phase mean equals the smooth-profile phase mean of the input. This definitional equality transfers the integral evaluation formula to the periodic space. It confirms that the submodule restriction does not replace averaging with an unrelated linear projection.

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.rest.text: A linear map $L$ between smooth profile spaces restricts to their periodic submodules when its output is proved periodic for every periodic input. The restriction changes the spaces, not the underlying operation. It therefore supplies closure of concrete differentiation and averaging operations without introducing a new formula.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.rest.summary: Restrict a linear operator to periodic profiles

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.rest.text: A bilinear operation on smooth profiles is restricted to periodic inputs and periodic outputs using the supplied proof that periodic inputs give periodic outputs. Linearity in each argument is retained. This expresses concrete advection and operator-field multiplication on the periodic space while keeping their original action on functions.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.rest.summary: Restrict both arguments of a bilinear operator

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.rest.text: After restricting a bilinear operator $L$ to periodic profiles, its underlying output on $f,g$ equals $L(f,g)$ computed on the underlying profiles. The statement exposes the actual operation before restriction. Its proof is immediate because the periodicity certificate changes only the space of the output, rather than changing its values.

The underlying smooth profile of a restricted linear operator is the original map $L$ applied to the input’s underlying profile. This is a definitional equality. The closure proof certifies periodicity while leaving the computed function untouched, enabling transfer of previously proved pointwise formulas.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.rest.summary: Read the original linear operator after restriction

TorusEuler.HierarchyProfilePoint.text:
The profile domain is the product of real time, three-dimensional labels and a real phase. Time restrictions and periodicity are imposed by separate slab and profile definitions.

This is a type abbreviation for the source type displayed here. It does not by itself assert a PDE, nonvanishing, smoothness or an existence theorem.

TorusEuler.HierarchyProfileReflectionPar.text:
The reflected profile has sign -1 for velocity and sign +1 for pressure and even label coefficients.

The sign is any real scalar in the definition. The intended even/odd cases are sign=1 and sign=−1; for other signs the condition may force additional degeneracy.
TorusEuler.HierarchyProfileReflectionPar.summary: Even and odd parity under joint reflection

TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.text:
The profiles, divergence completions and two parts of the pressure at each level of the finite expansion.

The record contains five arbitrary sequences. It does not impose the hierarchy recurrence, support, parity or initial conditions; these enter through separate laws and the constructed expansion.
TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.summary: Oscillations, means and pressures at each level

TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.AgreesBefor.text: Two profile families agree before $p$ when their velocities, completions, means, and oscillatory pressures agree at every index $i<p$. Mean pressures are deliberately absent: the preliminary source never reads them. This is the exact relation needed to replace a truncated recursion prefix by the completed family.

TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.LevelMem.text: At one storage level, requires the oscillation, completion and mean to belong to the velocity submodule, and both scalar pressures to belong to the pressure submodule. The record is abstract and can express more than parity. Remember that the completion stored at index $p$ is the paper correction at level $p+1$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.LevelMem.summary: The velocity and pressure components have their prescribed symmetry

TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.LevelMem.Y_.text: If both level $p$ and level $p-1$ satisfy the membership record, their oscillation and preceding stored completion sum to a velocity-class element. Natural-number subtraction appears because the formalization stores the completion of wave $p-1$ there. At index zero this subtraction stops at zero, so applications use the construction’s zero conventions.
TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.LevelMem.Y_.summary: The oscillation and preceding completion keep velocity symmetry

TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.LevelMem.Z_.text: Uses membership at the current and previous storage levels to place the full block $Z_p$ in the velocity submodule. First the oscillation and preceding completion form $Y_p$; then the mean is added. Closure under addition supplies the result, with no equation or phase-independence conclusion implied.
TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.LevelMem.Z_.summary: Adding the mean preserves the block symmetry

TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.Y.text:
The level-$p$ oscillatory block $Y_p=V_p+C_{p-1}$. This algebraic definition takes a family of hierarchy profiles and a natural-number level $p$. It introduces no equation or estimate. The separate construction sets $C_0=0$, so the first block is $V_1$, and the frequency estimates explain why the preceding divergence correction belongs at the next oscillatory level.

The predecessor $p-1$ is natural-number subtraction, so $p=0$ selects index zero. Uses at positive levels and the zero initial correction establish the paper interpretation; the definition alone is not a recurrence.
TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.Y.summary: Oscillation with the preceding divergence correction

TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.Z.text: The full level-$p$ block is $Z_p=Y_p+B_p$. Here $Y_p$ contains $V_p+C_{p-1}$: the correction stored at index $p-1$ in the formalization corresponds to the paper’s $C_p$. This definition alone imposes neither phase independence on the mean nor transversality on the oscillation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.Z.summary: The oscillatory block with its mean correction

TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.divergence_.text: The finite velocity has zero divergence when every completed oscillation $V_i+C_i$ and every mean $B_i$ has zero image under the supplied linear divergence map. The theorem assumes these properties on retained indices only. It does not establish that the map is a differential divergence.
TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.divergence_.summary: Sum the divergence-free completed waves and means

TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.pressure.text: The finite pressure is the sum of $p_p+q_p$ over $1\le p\le P$. These fields represent the oscillatory pressure and the pressure from the mean equation. Neither zero phase mean nor the normalization $\bar q_1=0$ follows from the sum itself; later construction lemmas supply them.

TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.pressure_me.text: Adds the oscillatory and mean pressure components over the retained finite depth, using submodule closure. Membership is assumed for every storage level. When the submodule is the even-reflection class this gives the pressure parity, but the generic statement itself is not restricted to any particular symmetry or differential equation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.pressure_me.summary: The total pressure inherits the pressure symmetry

TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.velocity.text: For a nonnegative depth $P$, this is the finite sum of the oscillations $V_p$, their generated divergence corrections and the means $B_p$, for $1\le p\le P$. The formal indexing stores the correction generated by $V_p$ at index $p$; the paper denotes it by $C_{p+1}$. Consequently the sum in paper notation is $\sum_{p=1}^P(V_p+C_{p+1}+B_p)$. If $P=0$, it is zero. The definition applies to arbitrary families in an additive space; transversality, phase means, differential equations and estimates are not assumptions of this sum. Evaluation at the transported phase and addition of the parent produce the physical approximate velocity.
TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.velocity.summary: The sum includes the last divergence correction

TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.velocity_eq.text: If $P\ge1$, $C_0=0$, and both $V$ and $B$ vanish at $P+1$, then the finite velocity equals the sum of the blocks $Z_i$ for $1\le i\le P+1$. The added block consists only of the final completion, stored at index $P$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.velocity_eq.summary: Include the last divergence correction as one block

TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.velocity_eq.text: Let $P\ge1$ and suppose the first correction in the paper's indexing is $C_1=0$. For arbitrary families of vectors in an additive group, the formal statement proves $\sum_{p=1}^P(V_p+C_{p+1}+B_p)=\sum_{p=1}^P Z_p+C_{P+1}$, where $Z_p=V_p+C_p+B_p$. The stored correction at index $p$ is generated by $V_p$, which accounts for the shift by one. Thus the completed final oscillation contributes $C_{P+1}$ even though there is no retained $V_{P+1}$. This is an equality of finite sums; no evolution equation, support property or norm estimate is used.
TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.velocity_eq.summary: Reindexing gives the expansion displayed in the introduction

TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.velocity_me.text: If every storage level has the prescribed memberships, the finite sum defining the perturbation at depth $P$ lies in the velocity submodule. Each summand includes the oscillation, its stored completion and the mean. The theorem is finite and algebraic; it makes no assertion about an infinite hierarchy or its convergence.
TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.velocity_me.summary: The finite perturbation inherits the velocity symmetry

TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.velocity_su.text: For a linear averaging map, suppose every oscillation and completion averages to zero and every mean is fixed by averaging. Subtracting the average of the finite velocity then leaves exactly the sum of $V_p+C_p$. This algebraic identity applies to any depth, including the empty sum.
TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.velocity_su.summary: Subtracting the mean leaves the completed oscillations

TorusEuler.HierarchyRelayCoefficientJets.text:
A finite smooth coefficient budget shared by the normalized potential and pressure operators and the inverse-radius coframe rows.

Unlike a raw word bound, this predicate explicitly includes smoothness of the phase-independent coefficient lift. It records derivative estimates as assumptions rather than deriving them.
TorusEuler.HierarchyRelayCoefficientJets.summary: Derivative bounds for potential and pressure coefficients

TorusEuler.HierarchyRelayCoefficientJets.text: If order-$j$ coefficient jets are bounded by $C_jA\mathsf D^{qj}$ and $\ell\mathsf D^q\le1$, their weighted finite-order budget is $(\sum_{j\le n}C_j)A$. The coefficient is globally smooth, and all scalar budgets and scales are nonnegative. Thus the derivative-order growth is absorbed by the label radius, while $A$ retains the order-independent parent loss.
TorusEuler.HierarchyRelayCoefficientJets.summary: Rescaling absorbs the derivative-order growth of parent coefficients

TorusEuler.HierarchyRelayWordBound.text:
A uniform bound for the individual weighted derivatives in the finite sup norm. The order counts labels and phase together.

The predicate bounds totalized directional derivatives and includes the zeroth word. It alone does not assert smoothness; the analytic estimates separately require smooth inputs before interpreting higher words as classical derivatives.
TorusEuler.HierarchyRelayWordBound.summary: A uniform bound for every weighted derivative word

TorusEuler.HierarchyRelayWordBound.clm_a.text: Applying a bounded coefficient to a bounded profile costs the product of their word bounds with the finite Leibniz factor.
TorusEuler.HierarchyRelayWordBound.clm_a.summary: Leibniz bounds for applying a coefficient field

TorusEuler.HierarchyRelayWordBound.finit.text: A uniform bound $B$ for every admissible weighted derivative word gives a finite word norm bounded by the number of words times $B$. The nonnegativity of $B$, which is part of the word-bound hypothesis, also bounds the inserted zero value in each supremum set. This converts individual derivative bounds into the exact finite norm.
TorusEuler.HierarchyRelayWordBound.finit.summary: A bound on each derivative controls their finite sum

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.text:
This is the subtype of functions belonging to the smooth-profile submodule. The stored representative is zero off the time slab and smooth within it; global smoothness across the two time boundaries is not asserted by the type.

The abbreviation inherits the zero-off-slab convention and within-slab smoothness. It does not state smoothness as a function on all real times.

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.advect.text: A linear direction map $D$ turns an advecting profile into a smooth direction field on the time–label–phase slab. The resulting bilinear operator differentiates the second profile along that field using the actual slab derivative. This separates the geometry of the direction from differentiation of the advected profile.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.advect.summary: Use one profile to choose another’s derivative direction

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.advect.text: At a slab point $x$, advection of $f$ by $a$ is the derivative of $f$ within the closed slab at $x$, evaluated on the direction $(Da)(x)$. The positive-time and membership hypotheses justify this pointwise formula. It shows explicitly that the derivative falls on the second argument.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.advect.summary: Read advection as an actual directional derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.applyF.text: This bilinear map evaluates an operator-valued smooth profile on a vector-valued smooth profile pointwise. The first argument provides a bounded linear operator at each point, while the second provides its input. Joint smoothness is preserved, and both additive and scalar linearity are proved in the profile spaces.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.applyF.summary: Multiply a smooth operator field by a profile

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.applyF.text: At an on-slab point $x$, applying an operator-valued profile $A$ to a profile $f$ gives the bounded linear operator $A(x)$ applied to $f(x)$. This equality exposes the concrete pointwise multiplication behind the construction. It supplies the evaluation rule used in coframe directions and material derivatives.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.applyF.summary: Read the operator applied to its local vector

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.consta.text: The constant profile has the specified value $a$ throughout the closed slab and uses the standard zero representative outside it. It supplies coordinate directions and fixed vectors to profile operators. Although the profile is called constant, its representative need not be globally constant when $a$ is nonzero.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.consta.summary: The constant profile with a given value

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.consta.text: For any point of the slab $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, the value of the constant profile with value $a$ is exactly $a$. The theorem distinguishes the mathematical constant on the slab from its zero extension outside. It is used when fixed time, label, or phase directions enter differential operators.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.consta.summary: Evaluate a constant profile within the slab

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.contDi.text: Graph evaluation preserves the full joint smoothness within the slab.
Fixing any time in the closed slab gives a globally smooth function of label and phase. The conclusion includes boundary times because the profile stores smoothness within the slab.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.contDi.summary: A smooth slab profile has smooth spatial slices

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.deriva.text: For $0<T$, this linear map sends a smooth profile to its Fréchet derivative within the slab, represented again by zero extension. Positive slab length gives unique derivatives at the time endpoints. The result is a profile of continuous linear maps on the full time-label-phase space.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.deriva.summary: Differentiate within the closed time slab

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.deriva.text: For positive slab length, a direction profile $D$ defines a linear differentiation operator on smooth profiles. It first takes the derivative within the slab and then evaluates that derivative on the direction at the same point. The direction may vary in time, label, and phase.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.deriva.summary: Differentiate along a smooth field of directions

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.deriva.text: The directional derivative profile evaluates at $x$ to the Fréchet derivative within the slab applied to the direction $D(x)$. The hypotheses require positive slab length and membership of the evaluation point. This is the explicit chain-rule form used to interpret label, phase, and time differentiation.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.deriva.summary: Read the directional derivative at a slab point

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.deriva.text: At an on-slab point, applying the profile derivative gives exactly the Fréchet derivative of its stored function within the closed slab. The hypothesis $0<T$ supplies positive slab length. No global differentiability of the zero extension is asserted or needed to read this equality.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.deriva.summary: Evaluate the actual derivative within the slab

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.diverg.text: A transverse profile plus its curl completion yields a divergence-free Eulerian field after graph evaluation. The covector is nonzero, the inverse-label chart is twice differentiable, and the coframe and covector must agree with its actual derivative at every graph label. This theorem transfers the already-established slow-fast cancellation to ordinary spatial divergence.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.diverg.summary: A completed transverse oscillation is physically divergence free

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.diverg.text: Given the inverse-label derivative and agreement of the coframe and covector at the graph point, ordinary Eulerian divergence equals the graph evaluation of total profile divergence. The profile is smooth on a positive-length slab and the chosen time lies in it. This also works at time endpoints because only spatial differentiation is used.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.diverg.summary: Graph evaluation turns profile divergence into Eulerian divergence

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.diverg.text: A zero profile divergence transports to zero Eulerian divergence.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.diverg.summary: Zero profile divergence gives an incompressible physical field

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.eq_zer.text: The field is smooth on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$; phase periodicity is unnecessary for this continuity argument. A smooth correction that vanishes before activation also vanishes at $t_0$, provided $0<t_0\le T$. This supplies the zero value at the beginning of the active interval in §5.4. When $t_0=0$, the same conclusion comes from the prescribed zero initial velocity, rather than from earlier vanishing.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.eq_zer.summary: Continuity carries inactivity to the activation time

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.eq_zer.text: Every smooth slab profile is stored as a function that vanishes outside the slab $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$. The hypothesis identifies such an outside point, and the theorem projects the stored zero-extension property. It says nothing about a smooth extension across the time endpoints; derivatives used later are derivatives within the slab.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.eq_zer.summary: Profiles are represented by zero outside the slab

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.exists.text: Smooth label fields $B$ and $q$ satisfying the mean momentum equation on the slab are lifted to phase-independent profiles and recorded as a mean output of the hierarchy. The conclusion preserves their actual values and proves the concrete material-plus-label-gradient equation. No endpoint conditions or existence of $B,q$ are proved here; those belong to the endpoint mean solver.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.exists.summary: A supplied smooth mean equation gives the hierarchy mean output

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.exists.text: Smooth phase-independent strain and covector coefficients, nonzero initial covectors, their covector evolution, and a smooth periodic zero-mean source give a concrete transverse output. The velocity starts at zero, and both velocity and pressure are periodic in phase. The theorem invokes the smooth transverse ODE solver, then identifies its momentum equation with the hierarchy operators.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.exists.summary: The smooth zero-initial transverse solve supplies hierarchy data

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.exists.text: Given smooth velocity and pressure on the slab, zero velocity phase mean, pointwise transversality, and the prescribed momentum equation, this theorem records them as a transverse output of the hierarchy. The conclusion preserves both supplied functions on every slab slice. It assumes the analytic solution and does not prove its existence or impose an initial condition.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.exists.summary: A supplied transverse solution realizes the hierarchy equation

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.ext.text: Two smooth slab profiles agreeing on the slab are equal as stored functions, because both use the specified zero extension outside it. No global continuation argument is involved.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.ext.summary: Equality on the slab determines the stored profile

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.fderiv.text: For a positive slab and closed envelope set $S$, a profile vanishing before activation or at labels outside $S$ has zero full within-slab derivative there. Closedness makes the inactive condition relatively open. Local equality to zero and uniqueness of within derivatives justify the result; pointwise vanishing at an isolated point would not suffice.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.fderiv.summary: A derivative vanishes on the relatively open inactive region

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.graphR.text:
Read the actual smooth profile on the transported graph.

The profile is only asserted smooth within its time slab. Its stored zero extension is used outside; graph evaluation alone does not prove global smoothness across the time endpoints.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.graphR.summary: Reading a profile on the transported graph

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.hasDer.text: The phase direction ranges over the entire real line at each fixed time and label.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.hasDer.summary: The phase derivative along a profile slice

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.hasDer.text: Restriction to a time line extracts the actual time derivative, including at the boundary of the closed slab.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.hasDer.summary: The time derivative along a profile slice

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.hierar.text:
The actual profile operators in (5.20) and (5.25) on a closed time slab.

Derivative values must be read with the regularity and slab hypotheses of the source construction; raw totalized derivatives alone do not establish classical differentiability.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.hierar.summary: Concrete differential operators on the time slab

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.hierar.text: Evaluation of the material operator is the within-slab time derivative of the profile plus multiplication by M. The operator has been expressed in parent labels, so no separate label transport term appears here.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.hierar.summary: The material operator is time derivative plus strain

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.labelA.text: If the coframe and both input profiles are phase independent, their label advection is phase independent as well. The derivative acts only on the label slice, whose values do not change with phase. This verifies the mean-product condition used to cancel the source’s inactive-region average.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.labelA.summary: Slow advection of means remains independent of phase

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.labelD.text: The operator profile $G$ acts pointwise on a velocity profile, and its result is inserted into the label component of the joint direction. The resulting map is linear in the velocity. The definition uses the given coframe values but does not assert that they come from an inverse flow.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.labelD.summary: The coframe turns velocity into a label direction

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.labelD.text: At an on-slab point $x$, the direction selected from $G$ and $u$ is exactly $(0,G(x)u(x),0)$. Thus only the label coordinates vary. The theorem exposes the pointwise meaning of the composed profile maps without imposing extra geometry on $G$.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.labelD.summary: Read the coframe direction in coordinates

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.labelG.text:
The three scalar coframe derivatives form the Eulerian label gradient.

Derivative values must be read with the regularity and slab hypotheses of the source construction; raw totalized derivatives alone do not establish classical differentiability. Finite sums and index sets are defined at zero order or empty ranges as well. The paper use supplies the intended order and level restrictions.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.labelG.summary: The three slow derivatives of a scalar profile

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.labelG.text: The bundled slow gradient is the sum of within-slab directional derivatives in the three coframe directions, multiplied by their Eulerian basis vectors. This is an evaluation identity at a point of the slab, rather than an estimate.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.labelG.summary: The slow gradient written in coordinate directions

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.labelG.text: The coframe label gradient of a scalar profile is the coframe transpose applied to its ordinary label gradient.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.labelG.summary: Label pressure gradients use the transposed coframe

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.linear.text: For a smooth periodic parent flow and coefficient profiles equal to its actual inverse coframe, strain and transported covector, the physical graph of the material and pressure operators equals the linearized momentum expression. The time derivative is taken within the closed slab. The proof polarizes the nonlinear graph identity to remove quadratic self-advection of the perturbation.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.linear.summary: The profile mean equation becomes physical linearized momentum

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.map.text: A bounded linear map $\Phi:E\to F$ acts on each value of a smooth slab profile, producing another smooth profile. The result is linear in the input profile. Boundedness gives continuous linear postcomposition and therefore preservation of the supplied smoothness on the slab.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.map.summary: Apply a bounded linear map to profile values

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.map_ap.text: At a point $x$ of the time slab, the profile obtained by applying the bounded linear map $\Phi$ to the values of $f$ has value $\Phi(f(x))$. This is the pointwise interpretation of bounded linear postcomposition. The on-slab hypothesis removes the constructor’s zero-extension branch before applying the map.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.map_ap.summary: Evaluate a mapped profile within the slab

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.moment.text: At a slab point, the residual of the parent plus a graph-read perturbation equals the graph-read concrete profile momentum plus the parent residual. The assumptions identify $G$, $M$, and $\kappa$ with the actual inverse-label derivative, parent gradient, and transported covector. The inverse-label transport equation and differentiability hypotheses are supplied explicitly.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.moment.summary: Profile momentum evaluates to the physical residual identity

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.moment.text:
Let $U$ be smooth and periodic on $[0,T]	imes\mathbb R^3$, with smooth inverse flow $a=X_{t,0}(x)$, and let $W(t,a,s)$ and $q(t,a,s)$ be smooth profiles. Identify their coefficients with $(D_aX)^{-1}$, $M=
abla U\circ X$ and $\kappa=(D_aX)^{-T}k_*$. Then the momentum residual of $U+W^
atural,p+q^
atural$ equals $R_U$ plus the evaluation of $(\partial_t+M)W+(W\cdot\widetilde{\mathbf d})W+\widetilde{\mathbf d}q$, where $f^
atural(t,x)=f(t,a,k_*\cdot a)$. Spatial differentiability of $p$ is required at the evaluation point. The time derivative is taken within $[0,T]$. This is the coordinate identity used in Lemma 5.8, before applying the expansion equations.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.moment.summary: Transport the complete profile momentum into physical coordinates

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.ofSmoo.text: Given a function $f$ that is smooth on the closed slab $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, this returns the same function on the closed slab and zero everywhere else. The construction creates a representative suitable for pointwise linear algebra. It requires smoothness only within the slab and does not make the zero extension globally smooth.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.ofSmoo.summary: Represent a smooth slab function by its zero extension

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.ofSmoo.text: At a point $x$ of the slab $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, the zero-extended representative evaluates to the original value $f(x)$. The membership condition is essential because the constructor replaces values outside the slab with zero. This lemma removes the representation wrapper in pointwise equations.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.ofSmoo.summary: The zero-extended representative agrees with the function on the slab

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.phaseD.text: If the fixed-time, fixed-label phase slice of a smooth profile is constant, its joint within-slab derivative in any pure phase direction $(0,0,c)$ vanishes. The time must belong to the slab. This establishes the vanishing phase-advection and phase-gradient conditions required when a mean field is placed into the hierarchy.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.phaseD.summary: Phase-independent profiles have zero phase derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.phaseD.text: The transported covector profile $\kappa$ is converted to its inner-product functional and applied to an advecting velocity. The scalar result is inserted into the phase coordinate. This gives a linear map from velocity profiles to pure phase directions, including zero when the velocity is transverse.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.phaseD.summary: Contract velocity with the transported covector

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.phaseD.text: At a point of the slab, the phase direction built from $\kappa$ and $u$ is $(0,0,\langle\kappa,u\rangle)$, with both fields evaluated at that point. Only the phase component changes. This identity makes the transversality condition visible as the vanishing of the entire fast direction.

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.phaseG.text:
The fast scalar derivative of the pressure multiplies the transported covector.

Derivative values must be read with the regularity and slab hypotheses of the source construction; raw totalized derivatives alone do not establish classical differentiability.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.phaseG.summary: The fast pressure gradient follows the transported covector

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.phaseG.text: At a slab point, the fast gradient is the directional derivative in the phase variable multiplied by the covector. The derivative is taken with time and label fixed.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.phaseG.summary: The fast gradient is covector times phase derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: Let $T>0$ and let $V$, a matrix field $G$, and a covector field be smooth on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$. The formal definition first uses the covector at phase zero, assumed nonzero, to form $Q[V]=-\partial_s^{-1}(\kappa\times V/|\kappa|^2)$, and then takes the curl of $D_aQ[V]G$ at fixed phase. In the paper $G=(D_aX)^{-1}$ and $\kappa$ is independent of phase, giving $C[V]=\mathbf d\times Q[V]$. The formula alone assumes neither transversality nor periodicity. To conclude that $V+C[V]$ is divergence free, the covector and derivative directions must come from the same flow and $V$ must be transverse.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: Take the curl of the phase potential at fixed phase

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: Fix $T>0$, an activation time $\tau$ and a closed label set $S$. Suppose the smooth profile $V(t,a,s)$ vanishes for every phase whenever $0\le t\le T$ and either $t<\tau$ or $a\notin S$. With smooth derivative matrix $G$ and nonzero covector, the formal statement proves the same vanishing for $C[V]$. Phase integration preserves the label set, and label differentiation is local on its open complement. This gives the support control used by the construction. The paper states the conclusion for the support at each fixed time; the formal hypothesis uses one common closed set throughout the interval.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The correction vanishes wherever the common support condition holds

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: At any slab time, including an endpoint, assume the entire label-phase slice of $V$ vanishes. Its concrete divergence completion vanishes on that slice as well. The proof uses only label and phase operations, so no time neighborhood of zero values is needed. A nonzero covector on the slab is required by the completion construction.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: Completion preserves an identically zero time slice

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: Fix $t\in[0,T]$, $T>0$, and a twice continuously differentiable coordinate map $A$. Suppose the derivative directions at label $A(x)$ equal $D_xA$, the nonzero covector there equals $(D_xA)^Tk_*$, and $\kappa\cdot V=0$ for all labels and phases. The formal statement proves $\partial_s(\kappa\cdot C[V])=-\mathbf d\cdot V$ at every $x,s$, with $\mathbf d=(D_xA)^T\nabla_a$. In the paper $A=X(t,\cdot)^{-1}$. No claim about an arbitrary unrelated matrix field is made. This is the derivative identity preceding (3.6); recovering $\kappa\cdot C[V]$ itself additionally uses its zero phase mean.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The correction cancels the slow divergence after phase differentiation

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: On $[0,T]$, let $V$ be smooth, period one in phase and of zero phase mean, with $V(t,-a,-s)=-V(t,a,s)$. Assume the smooth derivative matrix and covector are even under the same reflection and the covector at phase zero never vanishes. The formal statement proves $C[V](t,-a,-s)=-C[V](t,a,s)$. The normalized phase primitive changes the parity once, and the label curl changes it again. This is the correction part of the oddness argument in §3.1. Oddness of the physical velocity follows after evaluation along an odd inverse flow; that evaluation is not part of this conclusion.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: Simultaneous reflection of label and phase changes the correction sign

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: For a nonzero covector and transverse input, the profile plus its curl completion has zero slow-plus-fast divergence. The hypotheses identify the coframe $G$ with the derivative of a twice differentiable inverse chart $A$ and $\kappa$ with its adjoint applied to the launch covector. This proves the geometric claim at every phase, rather than merely along one evaluated graph.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The completed transverse profile is divergence free in the chart

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: At a time in the closed slab, applying the profile’s within-slab derivative to $(0,d,0)$ equals the ordinary Fréchet derivative of its fixed-time, fixed-phase label slice applied to $d$. The label line remains entirely within the slab. This identifies the coordinate calculus used by the concrete hierarchy with familiar spatial derivatives.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The label component of the joint derivative is spatial differentiation

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: For a positive slab length, this linear operator takes the joint within-slab derivative of a smooth vector profile and restricts it to label directions. Its output is a smooth profile of continuous linear maps. The following evaluation theorem identifies it with the ordinary label derivative on the slab, including endpoint times.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The profile derivative with time and phase fixed

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: At any time in $[0,T]$, evaluating the profile label differential gives the ordinary Fréchet derivative of the label slice with time and phase fixed. Positive slab length ensures the joint derivative operator is valid. The spatial inclusion stays inside the slab, so no time-boundary extension is needed.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The encoded label differential is the ordinary spatial derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text:
The slow divergence contracts the label derivative with the inverse-flow differential in the Eulerian directions.

The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The slow divergence in parent coordinates

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: At fixed time and phase, the slow divergence is the trace of the label derivative composed with the inverse-flow differential. This identifies the coordinate definition with the invariant contraction used in the paper.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: Slow divergence is a coframe trace contraction

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text:
Averaging the actual unit-period phase yields a smooth phase-independent profile.

The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: Averaging a smooth profile over one phase period

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: At a point of the slab, evaluation of the averaged profile is the unit-period phase mean at the same time and label. The result explains the average operator used by the hierarchy.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The bundled phase average equals the unit-period integral

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: Let $T>0$, let $V$, $G$ and $\kappa$ be smooth profiles on the closed time slab, and assume $G$ is independent of phase and $\kappa(t,a,0)\ne0$. The formal statement proves $\int_0^1C[V](t,a,s)\,ds=0$. It uses the normalized potential, whose mean is zero, and commutes phase integration with the label derivative. No transversality or period-one hypothesis on $V$ is needed for this average identity. In the paper $G=(D_aX)^{-1}$, so its phase independence is automatic. This fixes the integration constant when the longitudinal derivative is integrated to obtain (3.6).
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: Averaging commutes with the curl when its coefficients are phase independent

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: If every on-slab phase slice is constant, the phase average equals the original profile. The proof identifies the integrand with a constant and uses the normalized average of a constant. Equality outside the slab follows from the common zero-extension representation.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: Averaging leaves a phase-independent profile unchanged

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: If the coframe is independent of phase and the potential has zero phase average, its slow curl also has zero phase average. The proof commutes the label derivative through the phase integral and then applies the fixed linear curl map. The phase-independence hypothesis on the coframe $G$ is essential to moving that coefficient outside the average.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The slow curl preserves zero phase average

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: For $T>0$, take smooth profiles $V$ and $\kappa$ with $\kappa(t,a,0)\ne0$ on $[0,T]$. The potential is formed at each fixed $(t,a)$ using that covector and the primitive whose average over $0\le s\le1$ is subtracted. The formal statement proves $\int_0^1Q[V](t,a,s)\,ds=0$. It does not require $V$ to be transverse, periodic or of zero phase mean. Those latter phase conditions ensure periodicity of the potential in the paper; subtraction of an additive mean by itself does not turn a primitive with nonzero drift into a periodic function.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: Subtracting the primitive mean fixes its additive constant

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text:
The fast divergence contracts the phase derivative with the transported covector.

Derivative values must be read with the regularity and slab hypotheses of the source construction; raw totalized derivatives alone do not establish classical differentiability.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The phase derivative contribution to divergence

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: At a slab point, the fast divergence is the inner product of the covector with the phase derivative of the vector profile. The label coordinates are fixed in this derivative.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: Fast divergence pairs the covector with the phase derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text:
The slow Eulerian curl of the potential in the label chart.

The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The slow curl in parent label coordinates

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: For smooth $Q(t,a,s)$ and matrix field $G(t,a,s)$ on $[0,T]$, $T>0$, the formal statement identifies the slow curl at any time in the interval with the ordinary curl components of the linear map $D_aQ\,G$. Time and phase are held fixed in this derivative. When $G=(D_aX)^{-1}$, the three columns give the Eulerian coordinate directions expressed in labels, and the expression is $\mathbf d\times Q$. The equality holds without assuming that $G$ arises from a flow. It displays the one label derivative in the correction; it is not a quantitative norm estimate.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The slow curl uses one label derivative of the potential

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: Let $T>0$, fix $t\in[0,T]$, and let $A:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ be $C^2$. Suppose the smooth matrix field $G$ satisfies $G(t,A(x),s)=D_xA$ for every $x,s$. For every smooth potential $Q$, the formal statement proves that the divergence at fixed phase of its slow curl vanishes at labels $A(x)$. Indeed, after composition with $A$ this is the usual divergence of the curl of $Q(t,A(x),s)$. In §3.1, $A$ is the inverse flow. The compatibility with a single coordinate map is essential; the result is not asserted for arbitrary derivative directions.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: A common coordinate map supplies the divergence cancellation

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: If the coframe and potential are each one-periodic in phase at a fixed time, their slow curl is one-periodic as well. Equality of phase-shifted potential slices gives equality of their label derivatives. The theorem does not need phase independence of the coframe, only the stated periodicity.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The slow curl preserves phase periodicity

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: If the coframe and potential are even under joint reflection of labels and phase, taking the slow curl makes the result odd. A label derivative reverses the potential’s reflection sign, while the coframe does not change it. The statement holds for smooth profile representatives on a positive-length slab.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The slow curl of an even potential is odd

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text:
The total divergence operator for a vector profile at arbitrary label and phase.

The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The sum of slow and fast profile divergence

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: On the slab, evaluating the total profile-divergence operator gives the sum of the coframe-weighted label trace and the covector paired with the phase derivative. This theorem unfolds both encoded operators into ordinary derivatives. It holds for any smooth input profile and does not require transversality or zero divergence.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: Total profile divergence is the slow trace plus phase contraction

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: If each inverse chart is surjective and twice differentiable, and the coframe and covector agree with its derivative, the completed transverse profile has total divergence zero as a profile-space equality. Surjectivity matters: it extends the cancellation from labels reached by the chart to every label and every phase on the slab.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: Surjective inverse charts give divergence cancellation at every label

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: For a phase-independent mean profile, zero physical divergence of its graph evaluation implies zero total profile divergence, provided the differentiable inverse charts are surjective and the geometric coefficients match them. Phase independence transfers the physical graph’s conclusion to arbitrary phase values. The solenoidal physical mean is an explicit hypothesis.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: A solenoidal physical mean has zero profile divergence

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text:
The actual phase primitive defining $Q[V]$. The covector is read at phase zero because the geometric covector is phase independent.

The definition builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in its body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The phase primitive defining the vector potential

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: On the slab, the profile potential evaluates to the normalized phase primitive of the cross product with the covector at phase zero. The construction requires a nonzero covector; reading it at phase zero matches its later phase-independent use.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The bundled potential has the pointwise integral formula

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: At a fixed time and label, a one-periodic velocity profile with zero phase mean gives a one-periodic normalized wave potential. The covector is nonzero throughout the slab so the profile constructor is defined with its regularity proof. The statement does not require transversality because periodicity depends on the primitive’s mean, not on fast-curl inversion.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: A periodic zero-mean input has a periodic potential

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: With an even nonvanishing covector and an odd velocity under joint label-and-phase reflection, the normalized potential is even. The velocity must also have periodic zero-mean phase slices. Reversing phase changes the sign of integration, cancelling the input’s odd sign; the zero-mean normalization prevents an extra constant.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: An odd velocity has an even normalized potential

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.slabTi.text: This linear operator takes the derivative of a smooth slab profile $f(t,a,s)$ in the direction $(1,0,0)$. Time changes while label and phase remain fixed. Its input $T>0$ makes the closed slab a domain with unique derivatives. After graph evaluation the same operation corresponds to a material derivative, so it must not be read as a fixed-position Eulerian derivative.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.slabTi.summary: Differentiate a profile at fixed label and phase

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.slabTi.text: At a point $z$ belonging to the profile slab, the fixed-label time derivative evaluates to the Fréchet derivative of the profile within the slab, applied to $(1,0,0)$. The membership hypothesis is essential because profile representatives are set to zero outside the slab. This gives the concrete meaning of the linear operator before its chain rule along the inverse flow.

Let $T>0$, let $U$ be a smooth periodic velocity on $[0,T]	imes\mathbb R^3$, and let $X$ be its two-time flow. Write $A(t,x)=X(t,0,x)$ for the inverse label map. For a smooth profile $f(t,a,s)$ and a fixed covector $k$, evaluate $f$ at $(t,A(t,x),k\cdot A(t,x))$ to obtain $f^
atural$. The formal statement proves $(\partial_t+U\cdot
abla)f^
atural=(\partial_t f)^
atural$ at every point of the closed slab. On the right, both label and phase are held fixed; endpoint time derivatives are taken from within $[0,T]$. This is the first-order identity behind the auxiliary note's formula for every order. Higher orders require repeated application; they are not the conclusion of this single declaration.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.slabTi.summary: Transporting a profile converts its time derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.smooth.text: A smooth profile carries smoothness within the closed time–label–phase slab. This projection of its membership condition is the regularity input for the concrete differential operators.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.smooth.summary: A bundled profile is smooth within its slab

TorusEuler.HierarchySourceTermBounds.text: This proposition bundles the exact mean decomposition, the zero-mean relay, three mean-product estimates, the parent residual estimate, and the relay, slow and fast transverse estimates. Derivative hypotheses are requested only when $n+1\le H$, and level hypotheses only from two through $P$. It is an input contract for assembly, not an existence theorem for those estimates.
TorusEuler.HierarchySourceTermBounds.summary: The individual source estimates needed by the recurrence

TorusEuler.HierarchySupportLaws.text:
Local operations preserve vanishing on the inactive region. Slow advection of two means is again fixed by the phase average.

These are preservation properties supplied for an operator family. The record does not prove locality or support preservation for arbitrary linear maps.
TorusEuler.HierarchySupportLaws.summary: Support properties of the hierarchy operations

TorusEuler.HierarchySupportLaws.construc.text: For depth at least one, propagates inactive-region membership through every oscillation, completion and oscillatory pressure, and through all retained transverse sources. It assumes support preservation of the selected transverse solver and completion. Means need only be fixed by averaging; neither their velocity nor their pressure is asserted to vanish on this region.
TorusEuler.HierarchySupportLaws.construc.summary: The selected recursion keeps oscillations in the inactive submodule

TorusEuler.HierarchySupportLaws.remainde.text: Subtracts the retained tail sum of mean-mean label advections from the finite remainder and proves that the difference lies in the inactive submodule. All oscillations, completions and oscillatory pressures must be inactive. This identifies what remains; it does not assert that the full remainder vanishes outside the envelope.
TorusEuler.HierarchySupportLaws.remainde.summary: Only slow products of means survive outside the oscillations

TorusEuler.HierarchySupportLaws.transver.text: At level at least two, assumes older oscillations, completions and pressures vanish on the inactive region, while every mean is fixed by averaging. The preliminary source differs there from a sum of mean-mean products; subtracting its average removes that sum. The supplementary source also vanishes because its differentiated oscillatory factor is inactive.
TorusEuler.HierarchySupportLaws.transver.summary: Centering removes the surviving mean products outside the envelope

TorusEuler.HierarchyTransverseOutput.text:
Package an oscillatory velocity and pressure with zero phase mean and vanishing fast advection in every test direction. These are the algebraic constraints expected of a transverse hierarchy solve; the evolution equation is supplied by the solver separately.

The structure records velocity, pressure, zero phase mean, and zero fast self-advection constraints. It does not assert an ODE solve or nonzero amplitude, so the all-zero output is allowed.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTransverseOutput.summary: A transverse oscillation with its pressure

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.text:
This subtype imposes both period-one phase dependence and simultaneous label–phase lattice invariance on a smooth slab profile. These are exact function identities, not properties of a chosen Fourier approximation.

The underlying representative is zero outside the slab, with smoothness and twisted periodicity on its stored domain. The abbreviation adds no existence assertion for nonzero waves.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.summary: The space of twisted periodic slab profiles

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Label.text: This predicate asks that the phase-zero label slice be spatially periodic at every time of the slab. It does not by itself assert phase independence or periodicity at other phase values. Those additional facts are supplied when phase-independent coefficients or phase averages are sent to the torus mean solver.

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.text: Stores the deformation, inverse, material strain and time derivative on the label torus, with their evolution equations and exact profile values. Both inverse identities, finite coefficient bounds and the one-sided endpoint Hessian inequality are required. These are hypotheses for a real endpoint problem, not merely names for arbitrary bounded matrices.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.summary: The deformation data required by the endpoint mean solver

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.text: Requires the deformation, inverse and strain lifts to be even at every time in the closed slab. This property is used only when selecting the odd mean and even pressure from an endpoint solution. It does not assert oddness of the forcing or automatically establish parity of the solved fields.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.summary: The mean coefficients are even in their spatial labels

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.text: Uses the record’s identity for the values of the inverse coframe to show that the coframe profile has the same value at every phase. It is a lift of a torus coefficient depending only on time and label. This independence is needed for averaging and for slow advection of mean fields to remain a mean.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.summary: The inverse coframe profile is independent of phase

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.text: When the transverse covector agrees with the adjoint inverse deformation applied to the carrier, the mean geometry supplies smooth lift and pullback maps. They satisfy the time-evolution law, a left-inverse identity, and the transverse-projection identity. The theorem also proves the covector is nonzero on the active interval, using the geometric data rather than assuming an arbitrary projection.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.summary: The mean geometry supplies transverse coordinates and projection

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.text: Assume the central wave, coframe and strain bounds, compatibility of the covector, and the displayed small label-variation condition. Every fixed-plane homogeneous solution at a label within $2\ell$ of a lattice point has weighted growth at most $e\mathsf D^3$. The theorem also supplies the positive central norm and its continuous within-interval derivative. The interval length is bounded by $T\le1$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.summary: The central wave controls forward growth on the envelope

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.text: At any time in the closed slab, the generator formed from the transverse strain, lift and pullback is spatially periodic in the label. This lets the forward stability estimate near the origin be transferred to every periodic copy of the envelope. The theorem states an exact periodicity property, not a bound on the generator.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.summary: The fixed-plane generator is periodic in the label

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.text:
The parent deformation lifts the fixed launch plane into the moving transverse plane.

The map is defined on the orthogonal complement of the launch covector. For k=0 that domain is the whole space; the actual launch assumptions exclude zero before treating it as a two-dimensional plane.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.summary: Lifting the launch plane into the transported plane

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.text:
The inverse parent deformation reads the coordinates of the transverse projection in the fixed launch plane.

The projected pullback is defined for arbitrary coefficient values. Its inverse relationship with the lift requires the coframe identities and a nonzero transported covector.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.summary: Reading fixed coordinates after transverse projection

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanR.text: Collects a mean output together with divergence-free label velocity, displacement vanishing at both endpoints, and the physical-component relation $B=Fv$. It keeps the raw endpoint solution and states whether the output is unchanged or its odd part. Recovery and nonincreasing label-norm fields preserve quantitative information through that optional symmetry selection.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanR.summary: One endpoint mean with its normalization and recovery data

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paper.text: Packages the qualitative approximation properties, oscillation and mean Hölder bounds, residual estimate, signed pressure-Hessian cap, central-gradient error and perturbed-flow deformation for one fixed physical approximation. Every field concerns that same hierarchy and parent graph. The cutoff, the switch size and cost parameters are supplied freely; their identification with the paper quantities belongs to constructors. This proposition requires the listed facts rather than establishing them by its definition.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paper.summary: The physical estimates for one common approximation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.text:
Exact coefficients with their physical values on the parent label slab.

The coefficient profiles are tied by value equalities to the specified U, X and k. The record also contains analytic mean and transverse data. These obligations must be constructed; they are not inferred from arbitrary profile fields.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.summary: The physical coefficients carried by the parent geometry

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.text: Builds the physical leading input from the explicit stationary-shear velocity and pressure profiles. The hypotheses require a nonzero carrier, a positive envelope fitting inside the centered cell, and phase width in $(0,1]$, as well as the exact parent and flow identifications. Both switch sources are zero because this first wave is already present at activation. Momentum, parity and transverse equations are included as proof fields.

For any set $S$ containing the support of the periodized radial envelope, the constructed leading input vanishes at every slab point whose label lies outside $S$ (the inactivity condition with activation time $0$). The proof uses vanishing of that envelope for both velocity and phase pressure; the two switch sources are identically zero. The conclusion is restricted to the hierarchy slab through the definition of inactivity, rather than an assertion about every real time.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.summary: The first profiles vanish outside the envelope

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.text: Assume the parent velocity is the stationary shear at every time and the two-time flow is its flow, $X(r,t)$ equal to the shear flow over time $t-r$. The theorem identifies the general twisted hierarchy operators with the explicit first-wave operators by comparing the inverse deformation, material gradient and transported covector. It licenses reuse of the explicit wave equations for the actual parent geometry; it does not select that geometry.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.summary: The stationary shear gives the same operators

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.text: Proves surjectivity of the inverse parent chart and evaluates the coframe and covector on that chart. They become its Jacobian and the adjoint Jacobian applied to the carrier. The identities use the actual flow inverse relation, providing the chain-rule data needed when profiles are read as physical fields.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.summary: The profile coframe becomes the actual inverse-chart derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.text: Converts the parent-geometry reflection theorem into the evenness condition on mean coefficients for the exact selected coefficient record. The value identities tie the profile inverse and strain to their torus lifts. This lets the mean solver’s conditional symmetry clause apply to an odd forcing without selecting a new coefficient system.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.summary: The selected mean coefficients have the required even symmetry

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.text: For a divergence-free smooth periodic parent and a certified mean result, proves zero total profile divergence of the physical-component mean. Phase independence removes the fast derivative. The slow part follows from the volume-preserving parent deformation and divergence-free label velocity through the Piola identity, rather than from phase averaging alone.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.summary: The physical mean is divergence free in profile coordinates

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.text: Assume $0\le t_0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge1$, smooth periodic $U$, both deformations bounded by $\mathsf D$ and velocity derivatives bounded by $R_n\mathsf D^j$. Put $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$, $a\ge16$, and $\lambda=|\kappa(t_0,0)|>0$. For a positive continuous weight $\gamma$, zero-mean transverse profiles satisfy $\|C[V]\|_{[n],\gamma}\le K_n\lambda^{-1}\|V\|_{[n+1],\gamma}$, where $K_n=C_n\mathsf D^{2(15+a)}$. If $V_t+MV+\kappa\mathsf p_s=f$ with centered pressure, the same coefficient bounds $(\partial_t+M)C[V]+\mathbf d\mathsf p$ by the sum of the next-order norms of $V,f$. Centering of $V,f$ holds throughout $[0,T]$; transversality and the equation are needed only on $[t_0,T]$. These norms differentiate label and phase, not time, before dividing by $\gamma$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.summary: Bound the correction and its material derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.text: Let $0\le t_0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge1$ and $\lambda=|\kappa(t_0,0)|>0$. Assume a smooth periodic parent with both deformation bounds $\mathsf D$ and velocity derivative bounds $R_n\mathsf D^j$, and a localized seed whose leading velocity and pressure admit smooth compatible phase profiles. With $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$, $a\ge16$, and positive continuous $\gamma$, the formal statement supplies full-interval profiles agreeing with the unswitched $A_1,\mathsf p[A_1]$ on $[t_0,T]$. There they solve the homogeneous transverse equation. Both $C[A_1]$ and $(\partial_t+M)C[A_1]+\mathbf d\mathsf p[A_1]$ are bounded at order $n$ by $C_n\mathsf D^{2(15+a)}\lambda^{-1}\|A_1\|_{[n+1],\gamma}$. Nothing asserts vanishing of the unswitched wave before activation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.summary: Estimate the leading wave throughout the active interval

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.text: Specializes the mean-result divergence theorem to the exact output chosen by the physical solvers. It requires the actual parent flow, smooth periodic divergence-free velocity, and $T\le1$ for the endpoint solver. This supplies a concrete zero-divergence certificate for the physical graph construction without changing the selected mean.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.summary: The selected mean solve satisfies the graph divergence requirement

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.text: For an actual odd smooth periodic parent flow, proves evenness of the inverse coframe, material strain, transported covector and deformation at labels. Oddness of the flow and evenness of the derivative of an odd map supply the sign relations. Profile parity outside the slab uses their zero representative convention.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.summary: An odd parent gives even deformation, strain and covector

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.text: The transverse covector of the parent geometry equals the adjoint of the mean inverse coframe applied to the fixed carrier $k$ at every slab point. This is the compatibility relation needed by the fixed transverse coordinate system. It identifies two representations of the same wave vector without introducing a new quantitative bound.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.summary: The carrier is pulled back by the inverse coframe

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.text: At a slab time and label, the parent geometry identifies its mean inverse with the derivative of the inverse flow evaluated along the forward flow, its strain with the physical velocity gradient there, and its covector with the transported wave vector $(D_aX)^{-T}k$. These are exact value identities connecting the stored coefficient profiles to the parent field.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.summary: Read the transverse coefficients from the parent flow

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Phase.text: Records that the integral over one phase period vanishes for every time on $[0,T]$ and every label. The field is already a smooth twisted profile; this predicate adds its normalization. It is used when taking periodic phase primitives and when multiplying by coefficients independent of phase. It contains no estimate on the profile's size.

Let $f$ have zero phase mean at every slab time and label, and let $c$ be a profile of continuous linear maps that is independent of phase on the slab. Then the pointwise application $c\,f$ also has zero phase mean, since at each time and label the fixed linear map passes through the phase integral.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Phase.summary: A phase independent coefficient preserves the zero mean

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Phase.text: If a smooth twisted profile $f$ satisfies $\int_0^1f(t,a,s)\,ds=0$ for every slab time $t\in[0,T]$ and label $a$, and $T>0$, then every time derivative $\partial_t^if$, taken within $[0,T]$, has the same zero phase mean at every slab time and label.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Phase.summary: Time differentiation preserves the zero phase mean

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Combines $T\le1$, a physical leading input, and a phase-independent odd profile whose value on the slab at $(t,a,s)$ equals the parent momentum residual evaluated at $X(0,t,a)$, the time-$t$ position of the label $a$. The pressure $p$ and parent geometry are fixed parameters. The depth $P$ indexes later constructions but is not constrained by the structure; existence does not establish the quantitative approximation estimates.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Parent residual and data for the finite expansion

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: This predicate requires a graph-evaluated profile time derivative of order $j$ to have spatial derivative bound $CB^m$ whenever $j\le q$ and $j+m\le N$. Time derivatives are taken on the profile before graph evaluation, so they are material derivatives after a flow readout. The total-order restriction is part of the predicate; it does not assert all pairs with $j\le q,m\le N$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Geometric spatial bounds for material profile time derivatives

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: This proposition records zero phase mean for the leading pressure and for the activation force of the leading wave, transversality of that force to the wave covector $\kappa$, and equality of the completion switch (the term removed at level two) with the divergence correction of the activation force. It does not store a new solution or numerical estimate. Together with the leading momentum equation already in the physical data, these fields justify the level-two relay cancellation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The leading wave normalization needed by the first correction

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: From the leading normalization data, the stored completion switch has zero phase average. The proof rewrites it as the divergence correction of the activation force and uses the finite solver’s centering property together with the zero phase mean of that force. This makes the switch suitable for both the averaged-source cancellation and the recurrence assembly.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The leading normalization centers the completion switch

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Defines the profile multiplying the activation derivative as the centered wrapped unswitched leading velocity plus its wrapped slow curl completion. It is a raw function of time, label, and phase. The definition itself does not claim time smoothness across activation; subsequent residual formulas only require its regularity on slices where the switch derivative is nonzero.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Unswitched leading velocity together with its completion

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: At a time on the parent slab, assumes two jets of the wrapped unswitched leading velocity, three jets of its actual wave potential, and two radius-weighted inverse-coframe jets. It bounds the activation primary by $\mathrm{BV} + \lVert \mathrm{curlOfDerivativeCLM}\rVert \cdot \ell^{-1}\cdot 4\cdot \mathrm{BP}\cdot \mathrm{BG}$. The identity uses the actual inverse deformation from parent geometry; the jet estimates are hypotheses, not consequences of the seed interface alone.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Two primary jets follow from the exact wrapped potential

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For a hierarchy-regular active seed, assumes three scaled jets of the raw unswitched leading velocity, three scaled potential-coefficient jets, and two radius-weighted inverse-coframe jets. Centered wrapping and the normalized potential estimate then give two jets of the actual activation primary. The explicit budget is $\mathrm{BV} + \lVert \mathrm{curlOfDerivativeCLM}\rVert \cdot \ell^{-1}\cdot 4\cdot (16\cdot \mathrm{BK}\cdot \mathrm{BV})\cdot \mathrm{BG}$, exposing every finite derivative cost.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Three leading jets control two completed activation jets

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: At a slab time where the switch derivative is nonzero, the unswitched primary profile is smooth in label and phase. Its product with the switch derivative is already a smooth profile; division by this nonzero time-only scalar recovers the primary. The theorem intentionally makes no such inference on slices where that derivative vanishes.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Recover primary smoothness on an active switch slice

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: When the leading input is exactly the later-wave input built from the stated seed and parent, the sum of its two switch profiles at every slab slice equals the derivative of the time switch times the primary activation profile. The identity uses the same coframe and transported covector as the hierarchy and applies to all labels and phases.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Both activation sources share one time factor

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: At depth $P\ge2$, the last retained velocity is a selected transverse correction with no activation switch. Its material completion plus label pressure gradient is bounded by the normalized relay estimate applied to its actual source. The right side uses measured oscillation and source sizes at order $n+1$, multiplied by one inverse frequency.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The last retained wave controls the linear tail

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Assuming $2\le P$, a smooth periodic odd divergence-free parent, smooth periodic even pressure, and the parent label flow, derives the qualitative equations and symmetries of the approximate fields. It discharges the previous theorem’s mean-divergence premise using the physical solver’s Piola identity. The conclusion remains qualitative: numerical size and pressure estimates are proved separately.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The selected hierarchy satisfies the qualitative approximation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text:
For $P\ge2$, take the finite expansion built from the same smooth periodic parent $U,p$, its flow $X$, a leading profile with the prescribed reflection symmetry, and the actual residual $R_U=U_t+U\cdot
abla U+
abla p$. Assume $U$ is odd and divergence free. Then $V=U+W^
atural$ and $\Pi=p+\mathsf P^
atural$ are smooth and periodic on $[0,T]$, $V$ is odd and divergence free, and their momentum residual is the evaluated expansion remainder plus the two activation terms. Here $f^
atural(t,x)=f(t,X_{t,0}x,k_*\cdot X_{t,0}x)$. This proves the qualitative part of Lemma 5.8 for the selected construction; quantitative norm estimates are separate.
