TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The constructed expansion supplies the qualitative physical assertions

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: At an index in levels two through $P$, the actual mean forcing is fixed by the hierarchy average. The averaged source is already phase independent, and the parent residual has the same property. This supplies the correct input condition for the selected mean solve and later label-only norm comparisons.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Every retained mean source is phase independent

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For a level between two and $P$, the relay’s phase average vanishes if the leading pressure and completion switch are centered. The proof identifies the previous completion with the selected curl construction, obtains its zero mean, and combines this with the retained pressure normalization. This isolates the linear contribution from the mean source.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The selected linear relay has zero phase mean

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For a retained level, the phase average of the actual source before the mean solve is a sum of oscillation advection, divergence–oscillation products, and mean–mean advection. The theorem uses the genuine inverse label flow, zero pressure mean, and centered switch. Its proof imports the geometric cancellation that replaces the fast averaged product by a slow derivative.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The selected mean source contains exactly three slow products

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For every correction field $v$, the velocity used by the child flow equals the already defined physical approximate velocity plus $v$. The identity is definitional and ensures that the flow estimate and cutoff estimate refer to the same field. Smoothness, smallness, and divergence conditions on $v$ are imposed only when applying those estimates.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The child flow uses the same approximate velocity

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: This definition is six times the product of the numbers of admissible mixed words through orders $n$ and $n+1$, multiplied by $2^n2^{n+1}$. It collects the combinatorial factors in the completion estimate. Parent geometry, frequency, and input norms are deliberately kept outside this order-only quantity.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The explicit derivative-count factor in the curl estimate

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Fix bounds $\|D^jU\|\le W_n\mathsf D^j$ for $1\le j\le n$, a smooth periodic parent flow with both deformation norms at most $\mathsf D\ge2$, and a central seed satisfying the transverse stability and positive coupling conditions (5.5). If $0<T\le1$, $\lambda\ge1$, $|\kappa(t_0,0)|=\lambda$, and the envelope is sufficiently small, then the completed unswitched wave $A_1+C[A_1]$, in coordinates $(a/\ell_*,s/h)$ with $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, has derivatives of orders zero through two bounded by $\gamma(t)C\mathsf D^{a+27}\lambda^{-5/4}$ on $[t_0,T]$. Here $\ell_*^{-1}\le\mathsf D^a$ and $\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|$. The constants are selected before the parent. This supplies a pointwise derivative bound, not the whole residual estimate (5.48). The transverse stability assumption is $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for every transverse homogeneous solution $\mathbf b$ and $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Bound the completed leading wave before activation is applied

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Let $T>0$, $0\le t_0\le T$, $\gamma$ continuous and positive on $[t_0,T]$, $S\subset[t_0,T]$ closed, and let a vector profile $f$ vanish at all $t\in[0,T]\setminus S$, with $\gamma\le C_\gamma$ on $S$ and $C_\gamma\ge0$. Let $\ell>0$, $h>0$, $\mathsf D\ge1$, $\Lambda\ge1$, $L\ge1$, $M\ge0$, $\ell^{-1}\le\mathsf D^a$, $h=\Lambda^{-1/2}$, $|k|\le\mathsf D\Lambda$. Let $A(t,\cdot)$ be smooth with $B(t,A(t,x))=D_xA(t,x)$, $B(t,\cdot)$ smooth and $\ell^m\|D^mB(t,x)\|\le L\mathsf D$ for $m\le N$, $t\in[0,T]$. Suppose the amplitude-weighted norm of order $m$ of $\partial_t^if$ is at most $M\Lambda^\alpha$ for $i\le q$, $m\le N$, and $\mathsf D^{\max(a,1)+1}\Lambda^{3/2}\le\Lambda^2$. Then for all $j\le q$ and $j+m\le N$, $t\in[0,T]$ and $x$, $\|D_x^m[\partial_t^jf(t,A(t,x),k\cdot A(t,x))]\|\le(6\cdot2^NL)^N4^N\,M\,C_\gamma\Lambda^\alpha\,(\Lambda^2)^m$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: A profile supported in a closed time set keeps its small amplitude on the graph

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For a physical approximation of depth at least one over a smooth periodic parent velocity $U$ with label flow $X$ on $[0,T]$, let $0\le t_0\le T$, $\gamma$ continuous with $0<\gamma\le1$ on $[t_0,T]$, the leading wave inactive before $t_0$ on a closed set, and the switch profile vanishing off a closed set $S\subset[t_0,T]$ on which $\gamma\le\Gamma$, $\Gamma\ge0$. Let $\ell,h>0$, $\mathsf D,\Lambda,L\ge1$, $M,O,R,W\ge0$, $\ell^{-1}\le\mathsf D^a$, $h=\Lambda^{-1/2}$, $|k|\le\mathsf D\Lambda$, $\ell^m\|D^m_y[DX_{t\to0}(X_{0\to t}(y))]\|\le L\mathsf D$ for $m\le N$, and $\mathsf D^{\max(a,1)+1}\Lambda^{3/2}\le\Lambda^2$. Suppose the factorial time norms of order $q$ (spatial order $N$) satisfy: mean, unweighted, $\le M\Lambda^{-5/2}$; oscillation, amplitude-weighted, $\le O\Lambda^{-5/4}$; remainder, unweighted, $\le R\Lambda^\alpha$; switch, amplitude-weighted, $\le W\Lambda^{-5/4}$. With $e=q!T^{-q}$ and $c_L=(3\cdot2^NL)^N4^N$, $c_{2L}=(6\cdot2^NL)^N4^N$, the profiles evaluated along the inverse flow $x\mapsto X_{t\to0}(x)$ satisfy, for $j\le q$, $j+m\le N$, spatial bounds $\|D^m_x\partial_t^j(\cdot)\|\le C\,B^m$ with $(C,B)$ equal to $(c_LeM\Lambda^{-5/2},\mathsf D^{a+1})$ for the mean, $(c_{2L}eO\Lambda^{-5/4},\Lambda^2)$ for the oscillation, $(c_{2L}eR\Lambda^\alpha,\Lambda^2)$ for the remainder and $(c_{2L}eW\Gamma\Lambda^{-5/4},\Lambda^2)$ for the switch.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The finite hierarchy gives four graph bounds

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For a smooth periodic parent with its label flow, the inverse label map and the coframe $B(a)=D(X(t,0))(X(0,t,a))$ are smooth at every slab time. Evaluating $B$ at the inverse label of an Eulerian point returns the inverse flow derivative at that point. The proof uses the actual flow inverse identity.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The graph coframe is the inverse flow derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: This real expression collects the graph differentiation cost, retained higher-level count, coefficient jet bounds and level-loss factors in the higher-pressure estimate. It contains no carrier-frequency decay itself; the theorem multiplies it by $\mathrm{freq}^{-5/12}$. Its purpose is to expose how constants depend on depth and parent coefficients.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The explicit coefficient in the higher-pressure Hessian estimate

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: This scalar field is the physical graph of the sum of selected transverse pressures at levels two through $P$. The leading pressure is excluded. This separation is needed because the higher terms are bounded in operator norm using the transverse equation, while the leading term is controlled by a one-sided Hessian estimate.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Read the higher selected oscillatory pressures together

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Let $0<T\le1$ and let the constructed finite approximation have depth $P\ge1$. Assume its leading velocity, pressure and both activation terms vanish for $t<\tau$ or outside one closed label set $S$. If $0\le t\le T$ and either $t<\tau$ or $X(t,\cdot)^{-1}(x)\notin S$, the formal statement gives zero for the whole oscillatory velocity. The residual there is precisely the retained remainder of interactions between the mean corrections, evaluated along the inverse flow. This proves the localized part of the assertion in §1.3. It does not give the same support to the means or assert that the entire approximate Euler residual vanishes outside the wave.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Outside the transported support only interactions between means remain

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: The leading-pressure field is the inverse-label graph of the pressure component of the selected leading output. It refers to the same leading input used to construct the hierarchy. To apply the signed seed estimate, a later theorem explicitly identifies this output pressure with the regular seed’s twisted pressure.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Read the leading selected pressure in physical coordinates

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Assume the leading output pressure is exactly the twisted pressure of the supplied regular seed, and that seed has a primary budget at every slab time. For a smooth periodic parent flow, the actual leading pressure then satisfies the explicit signed Hessian upper bound. The equality hypothesis between the two pressures prevents applying a seed estimate to an unrelated selected pressure.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Transfer the signed seed estimate to the selected leading pressure

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Reads the velocity of the leading transverse output on the same inverse-flow phase graph used for the complete approximation. It isolates the leading wave from the rest of the retained oscillation. This definition does not require $P\ge1$; identifying it as the first term of the retained sum is a separate theorem with that depth hypothesis.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Eulerian readout of the prescribed leading wave

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: If the approximation's leading input is the explicit first-wave input, evaluating its velocity on the physical phase graph recovers the localized transported profile. The equality holds for $t$ in the closed slab. The inverse flow is the stationary shear at negative time, so the phase and label substitutions are the ones used in the explicit first-wave construction.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Reading the first profile gives its physical wave

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Reads the phase average of the retained profile velocity along the inverse parent flow. This produces the Eulerian mean correction, whose profile is independent of phase. It is separated from the oscillatory correction because its estimates and support differ: the mean may extend throughout the torus and before the wave activates.

For at least one retained level and a smooth periodic divergence-free parent flow, the actual physical mean correction has zero spatial divergence at all slab times. The proof uses the selected mean divergence equations and the physical graph identity. This supplies a necessary hypothesis when taking divergence of the summed physical momentum equation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The physical mean correction is divergence free

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For $P\ge1$, the physical mean correction equals the graph of the sum of selected mean profiles from level two through $P$. The first mean profile is zero by construction. This identity links the velocity field already used by the approximation to exactly the mean sum appearing in the pressure calculation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The mean velocity begins at the second level

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text:
For the finite hierarchy built from a parent flow and its leading wave, the phase average of the retained velocity profile, evaluated at $a=X_{t,0}(x)$ and $s=k_*\cdot a$, equals $(\sum_{p=1}^{P}B_p)^
atural$. The first mean is zero, so this is $ ar W^
atural=(\sum_{p=2}^{P}B_p)^
atural$ in §5.6. The equality uses the zero phase averages of each oscillatory profile and its curl correction. It is an exact identity for the selected expansion, not an estimate and not an assertion about arbitrary independently chosen mean fields.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Phase averaging recovers the selected mean corrections exactly

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Fix a finite order $q$ and a depth $P\ge1$. Suppose the selected expansion satisfies its level estimates through order $q+1$, with frequency $\lambda\ge1$, positive continuous weight on $[t_0,T]$, and inverse-flow coefficients obeying $\ell_*^j\|D^jB\|\le L\mathsf D$ for $j\le q+1$, where $B(X_{t,0}x)=D(X_{t,0})(x)$. Assume $\ell_*^{-1}\le\mathsf D^a$ and the hierarchy loss is at most $K\mathsf D^c$. If $b\ge a+1,6c$ and the chosen constant absorbs the displayed finite sum, then $\|\bar W^\natural(t)\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\le C_{\rm mean}\mathsf D^{b(m+2)}\lambda^{-5/2}$ for every $m\le q$ and $t\in[0,T]$. Phase independence removes the fast phase derivative cost. The theorem assumes these quantitative inputs; it does not establish all of Lemma 5.8 from the parent alone.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The mean retains its frequency decay at every fixed order

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text:
Let $U$ be smooth and periodic on $[0,T]	imes\mathbb R^3$, let $X$ be its flow, and take a selected finite hierarchy of depth $P\ge1$. Write $ ar W^
atural$ for the evaluated phase mean, $ ar q^
atural$ for the sum of mean pressures, and $ ar f^
atural$ for their summed sources. Then $(\partial_t+U\cdot
abla) ar W^
atural+( ar W^
atural\cdot
abla)U+
abla ar q^
atural= ar f^
atural$ throughout $[0,T]$. Endpoint time derivatives are taken from within that interval. This is the linearized equation used in Lemma 5.9. The mean fields are those supplied by the hierarchy; the assertion is not an existence theorem for an arbitrary source.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Summing mean equations gives the linearized Euler equation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: The physical mean forcing is the inverse-label graph of the sum of the level-$i$ mean forcings over levels two through $P$. This sums the actual forcing records, including the single parent-residual contribution at level two. It is a concrete velocity-valued function whose momentum identity and estimates are established subsequently.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Sum the selected mean sources on the physical graph

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: This definition takes the negative phase average of the hierarchy source at index $i$ and subtracts the parent residual exactly when $i=2$. It is the actual mean forcing used by the selected construction. The function is defined at every natural index, but its equation and estimates are invoked on retained levels two through $P$.

The mean-pressure field is the graph of the finite sum of selected scalar pressures $q_i$ at levels two through $P$. This retains the actual pressure supplied by each mean solve. It does not replace those pressures with an independently chosen Poisson solution; the Poisson equation is derived from their summed linearized momentum equation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Sum the selected mean pressures on the physical graph

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text:
For a smooth periodic divergence-free parent $U$ and its flow on $[0,T]$, take the selected hierarchy of depth $P\ge1$. Its summed mean velocity $ ar W^
atural$ and source $ ar f^
atural$ satisfy $\Delta ar q^
atural=\operatorname{div} ar f^
atural-2\operatorname{tr}(
abla U\,
abla ar W^
atural)$ at every time and point, where $ ar q^
atural$ is the summed mean pressure. This is the Poisson equation in the proof of Lemma 5.9. The trace is the trace of the product of the two derivative matrices, not their scalar product. The equation follows from the linearized momentum equation and the zero divergence of both velocity fields.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Divergence determines the Hessian source for the mean pressure

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Assume the measured levels of the chosen physical approximation satisfy the order-two bounds. Then the unweighted seminorms of its summed means and actual mean sources are bounded by the same level-count factor times $C\,\mathrm{loss}^6\mathrm{freq}^{-5/2}$. This specializes the abstract finite-sum estimate to the exact sources stored in the physical construction.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The actual mean velocity and force share one finite bound

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: At an active time $t\in[t_0,T]$, suppose $0<\gamma\le1$, $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, $|k_*|\le\mathsf D\lambda$, $\ell_*^{-1}\le\mathsf D^a$, and the inverse-flow coefficient satisfies $\ell_*^j\|D^jB\|\le L\mathsf D$ for $j\le1$. If $\|W_{\rm osc}-V_1\|_{[1],\gamma}\le C_1\mathsf D^{e_1}\lambda^{-23/12}$ and $\|\bar W\|_{[1]}\le C_2\mathsf D^{e_2}\lambda^{-5/2}$, then the sum of their physical derivative norms at the origin is at most $(48LC_1\mathsf D^{\max(a,1)+1+e_1}+24LC_2\mathsf D^{a+1+e_2})\lambda^{-5/12}$. Here evaluation uses $a=X_{t,0}(x)$ and phase $k_*\cdot a$. The formal statement stops at this intermediate bound; obtaining $|E_c|\le\lambda^{-1/3}$ also requires the step smallness condition.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: One physical derivative preserves decay of the nonleading terms

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Assume inactive leading data on a closed support, positive envelope length, prescribed phase width, a positive weight bounded by one, controlled coefficient jets and actual level bounds at orders one and two. Then the higher oscillatory pressure Hessian is bounded on the entire slab by its explicit prefactor times $\mathrm{freq}^{-5/12}$. Support propagation supplies zero pressure before activation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The actual higher pressures obey the full-slab Hessian bound

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For the actual physical approximation, parent flow and incompressibility hypotheses establish the summed linearized equation and divergence constraint. Together with second-order bounds on the selected mean and forcing sums, controlled inverse coframe jets, and a parent-gradient Hölder bound, this gives the displayed Hessian norm estimate with frequency decay $\mathrm{freq}^{-5/2}$. The bound is for the actual selected mean pressure.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The selected mean pressure has the expected small Hessian

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Denotes the hierarchy operators on twisted profiles built from the inverse deformation, strain, and transported covector of the parent geometry. The approximation data appear only as an argument making the operators accessible from them; their contents do not change the operator choice. These are the same parent operators used for the transverse, mean, and curl completion equations.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Operators determined by the parent geometry

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Subtracts the phase average from the full retained velocity and reads the result on the graph determined by the inverse parent flow $X(t,0,\cdot)$. The result is the Eulerian oscillatory correction. Removing the average here is algebraic; the later graph-sum identity identifies it with the completed transverse levels.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Eulerian readout of the zero mean oscillation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For the selected depth-$P$ expansion, this is the physical evaluation of all curl corrections and the transverse velocities from level two onward. In the paper’s indexing it is $(\sum_{p=2}^{P}V_p+\sum_{p=2}^{P+1}C_p)^\natural$. Evaluation means $a=X_{t,0}(x)$ and $s=k_*\cdot a$. The stored curl correction at index $p$ corresponds to the paper’s $C_{p+1}$, which explains the different indices in the formula. For $P\ge1$ the hierarchy identities identify this field with $(W_{\rm osc}-V_1)^\natural$. Its definition supplies neither a smallness estimate nor the central-gradient bound.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Retain every curl correction after removing the leading oscillation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For the physical approximation data of a parent and $P\ge1$, the physical oscillation remainder equals the inverse-label graph of the total profile minus its phase average and first transverse profile. This is equality of velocity fields, with no estimate. The depth hypothesis identifies the selected first profile with the leading input. Later bounds differentiate this exact remainder at the origin.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Remove the leading wave from the centered expansion

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Assuming at least one retained level, the physical oscillation remainder is the graph of the full retained profile minus its phase average and its first transverse velocity. The construction identifies that first velocity with the given leading output. This equality connects the named physical remainder to the measured profile sum used in the central estimate.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The physical remainder is the leading-subtracted oscillation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: From order-one actual level bounds, a controlled inverse-flow coframe, admissible label and phase scales, and a loss bound $\mathrm{loss} \le  K \cdot  D^c$, bounds the physical remainder’s derivative on the active slab. Its frequency decay is $-5/12$, obtained from $-23/12$ after one carrier derivative costs $3/2$. The displayed constant retains depth cardinality, coframe, and loss dependence.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: One physical derivative leaves a decaying oscillatory remainder

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Assuming that $X$ is a two-time label flow of the parent, $X(s,s,a)=a$ and $\partial_tX(s,t,a)=U(t,X(s,t,a))$ on the slab, together with smoothness of the parent on the closed slab and spatial periodicity, the Eulerian higher oscillation remainder is jointly smooth on that slab. The argument combines smooth retained profiles with smooth inverse labels. This is qualitative regularity; it does not establish the small derivative bound used for the central error.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Smoothness of the higher oscillation on the graph

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Identifies the zero-mean part of the constructed velocity with the graph of the sum of $V_i+C_i$ over $1\le i\le P$. The completion stored at index $i$ belongs to velocity $V_i$; the paper denotes that completion by $C_{i+1}$. The equality comes from the solver construction and includes the empty-depth case.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The oscillation is the sum of completed levels

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Assuming $1\le P$, splits the oscillation into the prescribed leading velocity and the oscillation remainder. The proof separates the first summand and uses that the constructed $V_1$ is the given leading output. The remainder includes the leading curl completion as well as all transverse and completion terms from levels two onward.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Separate the leading wave from the oscillation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Assuming the leading transverse profile is zero on the initial slice, the physical oscillatory velocity is identically zero at time zero. The proof includes all retained transverse profiles and their completions, using completion’s preservation of a zero slice. No lower bound on retained depth is needed for this statement; an empty sum also vanishes.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The physical oscillation vanishes initially

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: With $P \ge  1$, a closed support set, $0 < \tau$, and inactive leading data, the Eulerian oscillation vanishes whenever $t \le  \tau$ or the inverse label lies outside that set. The non-strict time inequality includes the activation slice. The theorem concerns the oscillation only; mean corrections need not vanish there.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The oscillation vanishes through a positive activation time

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For positive retained depth, closed label support and nonnegative activation time, inactive leading data imply that the physical oscillation vanishes through activation and outside the transported support. When activation equals zero, a separate hypothesis explicitly supplies the leading zero initial slice. This extra endpoint premise avoids inferring a boundary value from an empty interval of earlier slab times.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Include the activation endpoint in the vanishing statement

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Let $P\ge1$ and $\lambda\ge1$. Suppose the selected hierarchy has order-zero level bounds with constant $C\ge0$ and loss $L\ge1$, its oscillation vanishes before $t_0$, and its continuous weight satisfies $0<\gamma(t)\le1$ on $[t_0,T]$. If $C_{\rm step}\ge2PCL^2$, then $|W_{\rm osc}^\natural(t,x)|\le C_{\rm step}\lambda^{-5/4}$ for every $t\in[0,T]$ and $x\in\mathbb R^3$. Here the physical field is evaluated through the inverse parent labels and phase $k_*\cdot a$. This is the summation step behind (5.47). The level estimates and preactivation vanishing are assumptions of this helper result.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Sum weighted level bounds without paying a derivative cost

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Let $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D,\lambda\ge1$, and let a smooth periodic divergence-free parent have deformation norms at most $\mathsf D$. Assume its inverse-flow coefficient has derivatives $\|D^jB\|\le C_j\mathsf D^{7j+1}$. Require $0<\ell_*\le1$, $\ell_*\mathsf D^7\le1$, $\ell_*^{-1}\le\mathsf D^a$, $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$ and $|k_*|\le\mathsf D\lambda$. A selected depth-$P\ge2$ expansion must satisfy its qualitative physical properties, preactivation vanishing and level bounds through order two with loss $\mathsf D^r$ and continuous weight $0<\gamma\le1$. If $b\ge2\max(a,1)+6r+9$ and $C_{\rm step}=\Gamma_P\mathsf D^b$ dominates the explicit coefficient costs, then $C_{\rm step}\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$ implies that every smooth periodic divergence-free $v$ with each derivative through order two bounded by $\lambda^{-5/2}$ admits a flow $Y$ of $V+v$ satisfying $\|D Y_{0,t}\|,\|D Y_{t,0}\|\le C_{\rm step}\lambda^{1/4}$ on $[0,T]$. The weight here is arbitrary; quantitative hierarchy and coefficient estimates are premises.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Small scaled gradients control both directions of the perturbed flow

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text:
Fix the selected finite hierarchy over $U,p$ on $[0,T]$, and assume its assembled physical fields have already been proved smooth, with odd divergence-free velocity and the exact residual identity. The formal statement records those properties for $V=U+W^
atural$ and $\Pi=p+\mathsf P^
atural$, and rewrites their residual as $R_P^
atural+R_{\widetilde\chi}^
atural$. The latter is the sum of the leading activation term and its curl completion. Here $f^
atural(t,x)=f(t,X_{t,0}x,k_*\cdot X_{t,0}x)$. This declaration collects established properties; it does not independently derive them from the standing parent assumptions. That distinction matters when comparing this link with Lemma 5.8.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Collect the established physical properties and split the residual

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Fix $m\ge0$ and $P\ge1$. Suppose the selected hierarchy has level bounds through order $m+1$ with loss $\mathsf D^r$, vanishes before activation, and has $0<\gamma\le1$ afterward. Assume $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, $|k_*|\le\mathsf D\lambda$, $\ell_*^{-1}\le\mathsf D^a$, and scaled derivatives of the inverse-flow coefficient through order $m+1$ are at most $L\mathsf D$. For $b\ge\max(a,1)+1,2r$, the evaluated oscillation belongs to $C^{m,1/2}$ and obeys $\|W_{\rm osc}^\natural(t)\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\le C_{m,P}\mathsf D^{b(m+2)}\lambda^{3(m+1)/2-5/4}$ on $[0,T]$. This is only the first estimate in (5.48). The extra derivative supplies Hölder control; the level and coefficient estimates are premises here.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: One extra profile derivative gives the half Hölder bound

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For a fixed approximation of positive depth, assumes its qualitative properties, all-order actual level estimates, a positive amplitude weight bounded by one, inactivity before launch and coframe jet bounds. It derives the oscillatory and mean Hölder estimates with the explicit prefactors above. Scale assumptions and the two exponent inequalities for the graph cost and the loss remain inputs; the theorem does not establish the level recurrence itself.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Physical Hölder estimates from the measured levels

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Let $U$ be smooth, periodic and solenoidal on $[0,T]$, with flow $X$, and take a selected expansion of depth $P\ge1$. Its leading velocity, pressure and activation correction vanish before $t_0$ and outside a closed label set. Assume $\mathsf D,\lambda\ge1$, $\ell_*>0$, $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, $\ell_*^{-1}\le A$, $|k_*|\le K\lambda$, and continuous $0<\gamma\le1$ on $[t_0,T]$. Scaled derivatives of $G=DX^{-1}$ through order two, and of $G^T,M,P_\kappa$ through order one, are bounded by $J\ge0$; $\ell_*^{-1}J\le\mathsf D^a$. Also $\|DU\|_{C^{0,1/2}}\le C_U\mathsf D^2$. Suppose the actual hierarchy level bounds hold through order two with loss $\mathsf D^r$ and common constant $C$. Then $\|D^2\sum_{p=2}^P\mathsf p_p^\natural\|_\infty\le6(A+K)J(P-1)C[8J+(32J^2+32JA)\mathsf D^r]\lambda^{-5/12}$, and $\|D^2\sum_{p=2}^P\bar q_p^\natural\|_\infty\le48\|D^2\Delta^{-1}\|\,13824(P-1)C(1+C_U)\mathsf D^{6r+2a+2}\lambda^{-5/2}$. The operator is the periodic multiplier with zero constant mode. These are absolute bounds for the two nonleading pressure components throughout $[0,T]$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The two nonleading pressures have different frequency decay

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Identifies the approximation’s leading velocity and pressure with a supplied regular seed, then combines the seed's primary pressure budget with a smooth periodic odd parent flow. It proves a signed upper Hessian bound on the entire slab and the exact rank-one central gradient with the selected smooth switch $t\mapsto\theta(r(t-t_0))$. The full approximation’s higher corrections and central error are outside this declaration.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Reading the seed pressure and central gradient

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text:
Let $V=U+W^
atural$, $\Pi=p+\mathsf P^
atural$ be an assembled approximation on $[0,T]$. Assume the leading pressure has upper Hessian bound $L\lambda^{-1/4}I$, the higher and mean pressures have Hessian norms at most $H\lambda^{-5/12}$ and $M\lambda^{-5/2}$, and $L+H+M\le C_{m step}$. Assume also the exact central identity $D V_1^
atural=\widetilde\chi\mathbf a\otimes\kappa$, first-order hierarchy and inverse-flow bounds, $0<\gamma\le1$, and that their central remainder cost is at most $C_{m step}$. If $\lambda\ge1$ and $C_{m step}\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, then $D^2(\Pi-p)\le C_{m step}\lambda^{-1/4}I$ on $[0,T]$, and $D V(t,0)=D U(t,0)+\widetilde\chi\mathbf a\otimes\kappa+E_c$ with $\|E_c\|\le\lambda^{-1/3}$ on $[t_0,T]$. This combines supplied estimates; it does not prove them separately.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Combine the signed pressure bound with the central remainder estimate

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For a fixed constructed family on $[0,T]$, $H_p$ is its preliminary source and $R_U\circ X$ its phase-independent residual. The source for the level-$p$ mean equation is $-\langle H_p\rangle_s$, with the additional term $-R_U\circ X$ only at $p=2$. This is exactly the distinction in (5.27). The source belongs to the same selected expansion as its mean correction and is the quantity estimated in the unweighted norms of Theorem 5.6.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Cancel the phase average and the parent residual

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Assume $P\ge2$, a smooth periodic divergence-free parent and its flow, and a constructed family whose leading velocity, pressure and activation contribution vanish before $t_0$ and outside a closed label set $S$. For $W=\sum_{p=1}^P(V_p+C_{p+1}+B_p)$ and $\mathsf P=\sum_{p=1}^P(\mathsf p_p+\bar q_p)$, the formal theorem gives $\widetilde{\mathbf d}\cdot W=0$ and momentum residual $R_P+R_{\widetilde\chi}$. It also gives all phase-average, support and terminal conventions, and identifies $R_P$ with the final linear terms and quadratic interactions above depth $P$. Outside $S$, the remainder is phase independent. Every profile is smooth on $[0,T]$ and satisfies the phase period and coupled label translations. The construction is an input here, not an existence conclusion.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Identify the sums, residual, support, and smoothness

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Let $P\ge1$, $\lambda,L\ge1$, and $\gamma$ be continuous with $\gamma>0$ on $[t_0,T]$. For the selected finite expansion suppose every retained level at order $n$ satisfies the numerical bounds with a common constant $C\ge0$: velocity plus frequency-weighted pressure $\le CL\lambda^{e_p}$, mean source $\le CL^5\lambda^{m_p}$, mean $\le CL^6\lambda^{m_p}$, transverse source $\le C\lambda^{e_p}$, mean also $\le C\lambda^{e_p-1/2}$, measured $Y_p,Z_p\le CL^2\lambda^{e_p}$, and correction $C_{p+1}$ at most $CL^2\lambda^{e_p-1}$, where $e_p=-5/4-2(p-1)/3$ and $m_p=-5/2-2(p-2)/3$. Then $\|W_{\rm osc}\|_{[n],\gamma}\le2PC L^6\lambda^{-5/4}$ and $\|\sum_{p=2}^PB_p\|_{[n]}+\|\sum_{p=2}^P\bar f_p\|_{[n]}\le2PC L^6\lambda^{-5/2}$. Norms sum scaled label and phase derivative suprema; the weighted norm uses $[t_0,T]$, the other $[0,T]$. This is summation of supplied bounds, not their proof; the mean source still includes the parent residual at level two.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Sum the actual level estimates through the chosen depth

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: The strain profile stored in the physical approximation data is phase independent. This is read from its physical value as a pulled-back parent gradient and is used in averaging and cancellation identities.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The parent strain has no phase dependence

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Let $U$ be smooth and periodic on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3$ with label flow $X$, and let $1\le B_{\rm m}\le B_{\rm w}$, $C_U\ge0$ and $C_{\rm mean},C_{\rm osc},C_{\rm tail},C_{\rm sw}\ge0$, with $\|D^m_x\partial_t^iU(t,x)\|\le C_UB_{\rm m}^m$ for $i\le q$, $m\le N$, $t\in[0,T]$. Suppose that along the inverse flow, for $j\le q$ and $j+m\le N$, the $m$th spatial derivatives of the $j$th time derivatives of the mean, oscillation, remainder and switch profiles are bounded by $C_{\rm mean}B_{\rm m}^m$, $C_{\rm osc}B_{\rm w}^m$, $C_{\rm tail}B_{\rm w}^m$ and $C_{\rm sw}B_{\rm w}^m$. Let $i\le q$, $t\in[0,T]$ and $K=(1+2^{N+q}C_U)^i$. If $i+m+1\le N$, then $\partial_t^i$ of the mean correction at time $t$ lies in $C^{m,1/2}$ with norm at most $3(m+1)KC_{\rm mean}B_{\rm m}^{m+1+i}$, and $\partial_t^i$ of the approximate velocity lies in $C^{m,1/2}$ with norm at most $3(m+1)K(C_U+C_{\rm osc}+C_{\rm mean})B_{\rm w}^{m+1+i}$. If $i+2\le N$, then $\partial_t^i$ of the residual lies in $C^{1,1/2}$ with norm at most $6K(C_{\rm tail}+C_{\rm sw})B_{\rm w}^{2+i}$. Time derivatives are taken within $[0,T]$ at fixed $x$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Four graph bounds give Hölder bounds for the time derivatives of the approximation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Turns the approximate pressure at time $t$ into a smooth periodic potential on the torus, using smoothness and periodicity from the qualitative properties of the approximate fields. On the slab its lift is the actual approximate pressure. Off the slab the definition deliberately chooses the zero potential, making a family defined at every time available to the Fourier-cutoff interface.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: A periodic pressure potential on each slab slice

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: At a time $t\in[0,T]$, the lift of the slice potential at $t$ is exactly the approximate pressure at $t$. The proof selects the in-slab branch of the definition. This identity is used to rewrite the cutoff interface’s pressure gradient back to the pressure in the physical momentum equation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The slice potential equals the approximate pressure

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: The component signed and norm bounds, a sum of constants at most $C_{\rm step}$, and the actual qualitative properties of the physical approximation give the parent Hessian plus $C_{\rm step}\lambda^{-1/4}$ as an upper quadratic bound for the pressure potential. This is the form needed for the next endpoint coercivity argument. It remains a one-sided inequality.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The pressure potential retains the parent plus step upper bound

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Assume the physical approximation properties, twice differentiable parent pressure and a signed Hessian bound for the pressure increment. The lifted torus pressure potential then has Hessian bounded above by the parent Hessian plus that increment bound. The argument uses equality of the selected lift with the physical pressure on the slab, so no extra pressure term is introduced.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Pass the correction bound to the torus pressure representative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Given a parent pressure $p$, parent transition family $X$, and the selected depth-$P$ hierarchy, define $\Pi(t,x)=p(t,x)+\mathsf P(t,a,k_*\cdot a)$ with $a=X_{t,0}(x)$. The profile $\mathsf P$ is the sum of the hierarchy’s oscillatory and mean pressures. This is the pressure in the approximate momentum equation of §5.6. The definition alone neither imposes zero spatial mean on $\Pi$ nor asserts the Poisson equation of an exact Euler solution. In particular, the later pressure paired with $S_\Lambda V$ is defined separately by its zero-mean Poisson problem and compared with this $\Pi$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Evaluate the same finite pressure expansion as the velocity

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Given a signed leading Hessian upper bound and norm bounds for the higher and mean Hessians, the total pressure increment has a signed upper bound with the sum of the three constants at scale $\mathrm{freq}^{-1/4}$. Frequency at least one permits the faster-decaying terms to be enlarged. The component estimates are hypotheses here, not derived in this assembly theorem.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Add the three exact pressure contributions at the step scale

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For a retained hierarchy containing its first level, the pressure minus parent pressure equals the three named physical fields: leading pressure, higher oscillatory pressure and mean pressure. This is equality of scalar functions at every time. It is the decomposition used to combine the component Hessian bounds without introducing an untracked remainder.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The pressure increment is exactly leading plus higher plus mean

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For at least one retained level, the pressure increment is exactly the leading selected pressure graph plus the higher transverse-pressure graphs and the mean-pressure graphs at levels two through $P$. This equality is valid as a function at every time. It uses the construction’s zero first mean pressure and selected first transverse pressure.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Separate the selected pressure into three profile sums

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Evaluates the retained profile velocity at an independent time, label, and phase. The expression reads the ordinary function underlying the twisted, periodic, smooth retained velocity at depth $P$. This field still lives in label and phase coordinates; composing with the inverse flow and setting the phase to the carrier dot product happens in the Eulerian definitions.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Retained velocity before reading the phase graph

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: The retained velocity is one-periodic in its phase variable for every time and label. This is a defining property of the intermediate space of phase-periodic profiles. No restriction $t\in[0,T]$ is needed, since the profile remains periodic and is zero away from its time slab.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: One phase period leaves the retained velocity unchanged

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For any integer lattice vector $n$, translating the label by $n$ and translating the phase by $k\cdot n$ leaves the retained profile unchanged. This is skew periodicity, not separate periodicity of the label variable at fixed phase. It permits arbitrary real carrier vectors while producing periodic Eulerian fields on the transported phase graph.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Lattice shifts carry the matching phase shift

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For $t\in[0,T]$, the map $(a,s)\mapsto u(t,a,s)$ given by the retained profile velocity $u$ is smooth on the full label and phase space. This follows from membership in the smooth-profile space rather than an estimate on its derivatives. The statement fixes time; it does not assert that the zero extension is smooth across the endpoints of the slab.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Smoothness in label and phase at fixed time

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For a fixed depth, smooth profiles are periodic in phase and satisfy $F(t,a+n,s+k_*\cdot n)=F(t,a,s)$ for $n\in\mathbb Z^3$. The finite hierarchy is obtained by successively applying the endpoint mean solve, transverse solve, and curl correction, starting from the chosen leading wave. The parent residual and activation terms are fixed inputs. These are the actual profiles used in Proposition 5.4; their estimates are subsequent conclusions of Theorem 5.6.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Build the finite hierarchy from the physical inputs

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Given parent coefficient caps, nonnegative costs, depth at least two, $1\le\lambda\le\lambda_{\rm next}$, leading inactivity, and $0<\gamma\le1$ on the active slab, measured-level bounds through order two and the certified cutoff’s tail estimate give its corrected pullback-jet bounds. The oscillatory jets have order two and frequency decay $-5/4$; the mean jets have order one and decay $-5/2$. The parent exponent is $6r+8$, with $r$ the loss power. Inactivity and the weight bound permit unweighting; frequency ordering absorbs the next-frequency tail, which contributes only to the mean.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Measured levels and the actual tail supply corrected pullback jets

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Reads the hierarchy remainder at depth $P$ together with the leading and completion switches on the Eulerian graph. This is the candidate physical residual produced by the finite expansion. Its equality to the momentum residual of the defined velocity and pressure is a theorem under parent smoothness, incompressibility, flow, and depth assumptions.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Retained tail plus both activation contributions

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For the exact later-wave leading input and every slab time, the residual is the retained tail read on the inverse-flow graph plus the switch derivative times the transported primary activation profile. The hypothesis identifying the leading input ties this formula to the selected seed, so the activation field is not an unrelated auxiliary source.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The later residual is the tail plus the switched primary

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text:
Let $U$ be a smooth odd periodic parent with flow $X$, and let the leading profile of a selected finite expansion come from an even localized seed and a smooth cutoff $\widetilde\chi$ vanishing before $t_0$. Then its defined physical residual equals $R_P^
atural+\widetilde\chi\,{}^{\prime}(A_1+C[A_1])^
atural$ throughout $[0,T]$. Evaluation is through $a=X_{t,0}(x)$ and $s=k_*\cdot a$. The cutoff and seed must be the ones used to form that expansion. This identifies the two activation contributions with the completed unswitched leading wave. The equality is a decomposition of the constructed residual; identifying it with $V_t+V\cdot
abla V+
abla\Pi$ uses the separate physical momentum identity.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Separate expansion depth from the derivative of the time cutoff

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For every time, the defined physical residual splits into the graph of the retained hierarchy remainder and the graph of the sum of the two switch profiles. This is a definitional additive identity and does not require a depth bound. Equality with the actual Euler momentum equation is supplied separately by approximation properties.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Separate the retained residual from the activation source

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: If both stored switch profiles are zero, the defined residual is exactly the graph of the hierarchy remainder at every time. This is the no-switch situation used for the first wave. The theorem only simplifies the decomposition; it does not assert that the retained tail or the momentum residual itself is zero.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: With no activation source only the retained tail remains

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Specializes the general tail-plus-primary readout estimate to the actual seed, switch derivative, and hierarchy leading input. The supplied measured tail, primary jet bounds, coframe estimates, and coefficient caps give first-order half-Hölder residual control. The theorem derives the residual identity and needed primary slice smoothness from the exact compatibility hypothesis identifying the leading input with the later-wave input.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Bound the residual of the selected later-wave graph

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: From an unweighted order-two bound on the actual retained tail, a weighted order-two primary bound, graph coframe estimates, and $|\sigma|\\gamma \le  S$, obtains first-order half-Hölder residual control by $\mathrm{Cstep} \cdot  \mathrm{freq}^2 \cdot  (\mathrm{freq}^{-2\cdot \mathrm{depth}/3} + S)$. The residual decomposition and scalar caps are explicit hypotheses. Primary smoothness is needed only where $\sigma \ne  0$; inactive or zero-switch slices are treated separately.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Read the tail and activation bounds into physical space

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Take a selected expansion over a smooth odd periodic parent with flow $X$, using an even seed and the same smooth cutoff $0\le\widetilde\chi\le1$, zero before $t_0$. Let $\mathsf D,\lambda,L\ge1$, $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, $|k_*|\le\mathsf D\lambda$ and $\ell_*^{-1}\le\mathsf D^a$. Assume $\ell_*^j\|D^j[DX_{t,0}\circ X_{0,t}]\|_\infty\le L\mathsf D$ for $j\le2$, $\|R_P\|_{[2]}\le C_R\lambda^{-5/4-2P/3}$, and every derivative through order two of $(A_1+C[A_1])(t,\ell_*a,hs)$ is bounded by $\gamma(t)C_A\mathsf D^p\lambda^{-5/4}$. Here $C_R,C_A\ge0$ and $\gamma$ is continuous and nonnegative on $[t_0,T]$. Require $C_{\rm step}\ge6(24L)^2\max\{16C_R\mathsf D^{2(\max(a,1)+1)},C_A\mathsf D^{2(\max(a,1)+1)+p}\}$. Then $R_V(t)\in C^{1,1/2}$ and $\|R_V(t)\|_{C^{1,1/2}}\le C_{\rm step}\lambda^2(\lambda^{-2P/3}+\sup_{[t_0,T]}|\widetilde\chi'|\gamma)$ for every $t\in[0,T]$. The remainder norm is the finite sum of scaled label and phase derivative suprema on the full slab.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Keep the actual weighted activation derivative in the residual estimate

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Combines the actual later-graph estimate with the scheduled depth and switch-smallness hypotheses. At every slab time it concludes both first-order half-Hölder regularity and a norm at most the next frequency’s power $-7/2$. The weighted primary and unweighted retained-tail bounds remain explicit inputs, as do the scalar caps and $\mathrm{Cstep} \cdot  \mu$ budget.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The selected later-wave residual meets the scheduled decay

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For frequency $\lambda\ge2$ and depth six times the next frequency exponent, converts the supplied residual-rate estimate into the next frequency’s power $-7/2$. The hypotheses include $\mu\ge1$, nonnegative $C_{\rm step}$, and $C_{\rm step}\mu\le\lambda^{1/16}$. The proof identifies both depth and switch errors with the next-frequency scale $-4$ before absorbing prefactors.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The chosen depth makes the residual small for the next wave

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For approximation data with both switch profiles zero, derives first-order half-Hölder residual regularity and the next-frequency power $-7/2$ bound from the measured retained tail. The proof applies the general readout theorem with zero primary and zero switch. It still requires graph coefficient control, the scheduled depth, and the scalar absorption budget.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The first-wave residual meets the same scheduled decay

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Given the leading normalization data and one active-interval coefficient budget, this theorem returns two inequalities: completion of any centered input $v$ satisfies $\|C[v]\|_{[n],\gamma}\le L\,\mathrm{freq}^{-1}\|v\|_{[n+1],\gamma}$, and each selected relay at a level $2\le i\le P$ is bounded by $L\,\mathrm{freq}^{-1}$ times the preceding measured oscillation plus source at order $n+1$. The supplied cap inequalities place both explicit order constants under $L$; the theorem does not choose those caps.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The selected completion and relay obey a common bound

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For a selected physical approximation with its leading compatibility data, actual parent flow, and smooth periodic parent velocity, one relay coefficient budget gives both completion and relay estimates. The assumptions include a positive frequency and amplitude weight and a cap on the explicit coefficient cost. Relays are covered through level $P+1$; the measured mean force uses time order $q-1$ while oscillatory profiles use $q$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: One coefficient budget controls completion and every selected relay

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: The theorem derives the recurrence for the actual finite hierarchy from support, cancellation, and linear estimates, after receiving coefficient caps and primitive bounds at the required finite orders. Residual, leading-wave, mean-solver, and transverse-solver bounds remain explicit final premises. The conclusion is the full norm recurrence of the hierarchy (seed, forcing, solve, completion and reconstruction rows); obtaining the depth-decay theorem requires the separate numerical induction.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The selected physical profiles satisfy the norm recurrence

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: On the actual selected profiles, assume the parent flow and regularity laws, vanishing before activation, positive scales and amplitude weight, the six primitive linear bounds, and source coefficient caps. With depth $P\ge2$, $n+3P\le H$, $K,L\ge1$, and the frequency smallness condition, obtain the mixed norm recurrence, all retained level bounds, oscillation and mean sums, and the final remainder estimate. Mean forcing uses time order $q-1$, computed in the natural numbers, so it is $0$ when $q=0$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Run the finite hierarchy recurrence in mixed time norms

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: The source for correction level $i$ is $-(H-\overline H)$, the negative phase-mean-free part of the source before the mean, minus the specified mean-phase advection term. It is computed from the actual finite hierarchy, its depth, and its activation completion. The definition neither solves the transverse equation nor asserts mean zero; these properties are supplied by the selected solver theorem at valid correction levels.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The exact source of a selected transverse correction

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: At a retained correction level $2\le i\le P$, the selected velocity and carrier-normalized pressure satisfy a factorial time-norm bound in terms of the exact selected force. Besides positive frequency and amplitude weight, the theorem assumes an undifferentiated inverse estimate (the weighted norm of $V_i$ at most $C_0$ times that of the selected force) and four coefficient time budgets. It uses equalities with the actual transverse solver output, so the estimate remains attached to the retained profiles.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Time bounds for the exact retained transverse solution

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: This variant of the selected transverse time estimate accepts the ordinary measured oscillatory row, which includes velocity plus normalized pressure, as its zeroth-order input. At a level in $2,\dots,P$, discarding the nonnegative pressure term supplies the velocity bound required by the previous theorem. The same positive-frequency, weight, and four coefficient-budget assumptions are retained.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Use the measured spatial row to start transverse time estimates

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: If the prescribed level-one pressure has zero phase mean, then every retained pressure does. The proof separates level one from higher levels, where the pressure is produced by the selected transverse solver and inherits its normalization. No statement is made about unretained indices, and no mean-pressure normalization is inferred from this oscillatory result.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Every retained oscillatory pressure is centered

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Returns the canonical finite-hierarchy solvers of the physical construction, using the parent geometry together with the assumption $T\le1$ in the approximation data. These solvers provide the endpoint mean inverse, transverse equation, and curl completion used in all retained levels. The definition supplies selected solution operators; the estimates for their outputs are proved separately.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Selected mean transverse and completion solutions

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: If the parent frequency $\mu$ is at least one, the schedule exponent parameter is positive, and $C_{\rm step}$ is at most the new frequency’s power $1/32$, then $C_{\rm step}\mu$ is at most its power $1/16$. The large scheduled exponent bounds the parent frequency by another $1/32$ power; no nonnegative assumption on $C_{\rm step}$ is needed.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Absorb the parent frequency into the step budget

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: The material operator applied to the sum of selected means, plus label and phase gradients of the summed mean pressures, equals the sum of the actual mean sources. This is an exact identity of profiles. It follows by adding each selected mean equation and includes an empty retained range without requiring a lower bound on $P$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The selected mean equations add without an extra error

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Defines the scalar $q!T^{-q}$ used to extract any derivative through order $q$ from the factorially weighted time seminorm. It bounds the individual extraction costs when $0<T\le1$. The definition itself permits arbitrary $T$; the following extraction theorem supplies the positivity and upper bound that give this expression its intended meaning.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The common factorial time extraction cost

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For a physical approximation of depth at least one, let $S\subset\mathbb R^3$ be closed and suppose the leading input (velocity, pressure and completion switch) vanishes at every point of $[0,T]$ whose time is before $t_0$ or whose label lies outside $S$. Then for every $t\in[0,T]$ with $t<t_0$, the oscillatory profile, that is the depth-$P$ velocity profile minus its phase average, vanishes at $(t,a,s)$ for every label $a$ and phase $s$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The oscillatory profile vanishes before activation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Under the smooth periodic parent and flow hypotheses, each time derivative of the actual approximation residual equals the sum of derivatives of the graph-read hierarchy remainder and the combined switch profile. Both the leading and completion switch forces remain in that combined term. This exact identity is used before applying separate amplitude and support bounds.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Residual time derivatives split into tail and activation terms

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For a smooth periodic parent with its label flow, each Eulerian time derivative of the selected approximation splits into the parent derivative, oscillatory correction derivative, and mean correction derivative. The theorem uses the exact velocity decomposition and smoothness of the inverse-flow graph evaluations. It is a function equality at a time in the positive-length slab, without estimating any term.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Velocity time derivatives split into parent and two corrections

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: If a profile is zero at every label and phase outside a closed time set, each of its time derivatives is also zero there at slab times. Closedness makes the complement a neighborhood on which the time curve is zero. The proof uses local congruence of within-time derivatives, so it covers slab endpoints without imposing new boundary conditions.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: All profile time derivatives vanish outside closed support

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For a depth-$P\ge1$ selected expansion, assume level estimates through order two with loss $\mathsf D^r$, bounds on all scaled inverse-deformation coefficients, preactivation vanishing, and $0<\gamma\le1$ on $[t_0,T]$. Set the added perturbation $v$ to zero and pull the correction into parent labels: $c=(D_aX)^{-1}W$. In coordinates $(a/\ell_*,s/h)$, its oscillation has derivatives through order two bounded by $A_{\rm osc}\mathsf D^{2r+1}\lambda^{-5/4}$; its phase mean has derivatives through order one bounded by $A_{\rm mean}\mathsf D^{6r+1}\lambda^{-5/2}$. Both hold on $[0,T]$. This does not state the second-order mean estimate displayed in the paper’s proof of Lemma 5.10, or handle a nonzero perturbation. The weaker intermediate estimate suffices for the subsequent flow proof.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Only one mean derivative is required for the flow argument

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For $P\ge2$, the actual selected remainder is bounded on the full slab by an explicit finite-pair constant times $\mathrm{freq}^{-5/4-2P/3}$. Premises include level bounds through order $n+1$, inactivity, coefficient and relay caps, and $L^6\mathrm{freq}^{-1/12}\le1$. The activation switch is excluded from this remainder and must be estimated separately.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The actual residual tail has the claimed frequency decay

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For a parent velocity $U$, its transition family $X$, and the selected depth-$P$ hierarchy, define $V(t,x)=U(t,x)+W(t,a,k_*\cdot a)$, where $a=X_{t,0}(x)$ and $W$ is the retained velocity profile. This is $V=U+W^\natural$ at the start of §5.6. The profile contains transverse oscillations, their curl corrections and the mean terms from the same finite recursion. The definition alone does not say that $V$ is incompressible or solves Euler; the construction separately proves zero divergence and identifies its nonzero momentum residual. Its smoothness assertions concern the closed interval $[0,T]$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Add the evaluated finite correction to the parent velocity

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For $P \ge  1$, sums the actual level estimates to bound the oscillatory profile, its leading-subtracted remainder, and its phase average. Their frequency rates are respectively $-5/4$, $-23/12$, and $-5/2$, with explicit depth-cardinality and loss factors. The oscillatory bounds use the positive amplitude weight; the mean uses an unweighted seminorm. No Eulerian graph derivative is taken yet.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Sum the measured oscillation remainder and mean bounds

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For a hierarchy of depth at least one and the explicit first leading input, the physical velocity equals stationary shear plus the leading wave, higher oscillatory remainder and mean correction. The time belongs to the closed parent slab. This identity keeps the selected correction fields themselves, so subsequent estimates apply to the actual approximation rather than to unrelated witnesses.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The first velocity separates its four terms

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For the finite approximation on $[0,T]$ at depth $P\ge1$, the formal statement is the exact equality $V=U+V_1^\natural+W_{\mathrm{osc}}+B$, where $U$ is the parent, $V_1$ the activated leading profile, $W_{\mathrm{osc}}$ contains the remaining oscillations and divergence corrections, and $B$ is the sum of the phase-independent means. Evaluation uses the inverse parent flow and the phase $k_*\cdot a$. The components are those of the already constructed finite family. This equality explains the decomposition in §1.3; it does not itself bound the residual or establish the smallness of any summand.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The approximate velocity separates parent, leading wave, oscillations and mean

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: The approximate velocity equals the parent plus the zero-mean oscillation plus the mean correction. This is an identity for any physical approximation data, obtained by inserting and subtracting the profile average at each graph point. It needs no lower bound on depth and does not provide estimates for any of the three summands.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Split the velocity into parent oscillation and mean

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Combines measured levels through order $P+1$, graph coframe control, a positive weight at most one, inactivity before activation, and parent jet bounds to bound the order-$P$ physical velocity norm. The result is $1+\|V\|\le3\lambda^{2(P+1)}$ for the scheduled new frequency $\lambda$. Explicit graph-cost inequalities and prefactor caps absorb all dependence on order and depth.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The retained physical velocity satisfies the full-depth budget

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Collects joint slab smoothness, spatial periodicity, velocity-type oddness, even pressure, Eulerian divergence freedom, the full profile divergence identity, and exact equality between the momentum residual and the candidate residual of the expansion. The fields are already fixed by the approximation data; the structure records propositions about them. It deliberately contains no residual smallness, pressure Hessian, or growth estimate.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Qualitative equations and symmetries of the approximate fields

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For a supplied cutoff stage with cutoff bounds and the full-depth velocity estimate, proves that the difference between cutoff and untruncated velocities is smooth, periodic and divergence free. On the slab its order-two half-Hölder norm is at most the child frequency to power $-5/2$. This is the small correction required by the next deformation estimate.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The cutoff tail is small enough for the child flow

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Given the step numerical budget and a full-depth Hölder bound for the actual approximation, bounds the weighted truncation error by the fifth inverse power of the following frequency. The cutoff is taken at the fifth power of the child frequency. This theorem performs the numerical absorption; the approximation-size estimate $1+\|V(t)\|_{C^{P,1/2}}\le3\lambda^{2(P+1)}$ remains an explicit hypothesis.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The scheduled Fourier tail decays at the next frequency

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For each time in the slab, rewrites the exact residual equation using the lift of the smooth periodic slice potential. The time derivative is the derivative within $[0,T]$, so the statement includes both time endpoints. It identifies the equation used by the cutoff stage without asserting that this residual vanishes.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Write the momentum equation with the slice potential

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Given approximation data for the finite hierarchy whose qualitative properties hold (smoothness on the slab, periodicity, the parities, divergence freedom and the exact momentum equation with its residual), an even multiplier $\psi$ and any radius $\Lambda$, there exists a truncated-child stage on $[0,T]$ with radius $\Lambda$ and multiplier $\psi$ whose input velocity and residual are exactly the hierarchy's velocity and residual. Such a stage contains the Fourier-cut velocity, smooth, odd, divergence free and with frequencies in $|k|\le2\Lambda$, together with its zero-mean Poisson pressure. The pressure used in the construction is the potential already built from the data. No numerical cutoff bounds are asserted.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The finite hierarchy's velocity and residual admit a truncated-child stage

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Collects a transverse output, two switch profiles, the leading momentum identity, and the odd velocity and even pressure parities. The parent geometry fixes the actual hierarchy operators. The identity includes the leading switch, while the completion switch is retained separately for the finite expansion. This structure does not itself require nonzero amplitude, normalization, or quantitative bounds.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Leading profiles and the two activation sources

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Requires the leading velocity, phase pressure, leading switch, and completion switch to vanish on the inactive region determined by $T$, $\tau$ and $S$. That region lies on the time slab and consists of times before $\tau$ or labels outside $S$. The four conditions concern the supplied leading input only; later support propagation is a separate theorem.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: A common region where leading inputs vanish

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Constructs the physical leading input for the parent data, using a seed over the same parent’s material gradient and transported covector. It requires seed regularity, the smooth periodic odd parent flow, and even seed amplitude. The output, momentum identity, and two activation sources are those already proved for the wrapped seed; parent reflection supplies the needed coframe and coefficient parities.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Build the physical leading input from the selected seed

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For a closed set $S$ containing the support of the periodized radial envelope, the later-wave physical input is inactive before $t_0$ and outside $S$. It packages the four established vanishing statements for velocity, pressure, and the two switch sources. The construction hypotheses match those of the preceding construction from the selected seed, so support belongs to that exact selected input.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The physical leading input inherits its envelope support

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Builds the physical leading input of the hierarchy for a smooth periodic odd parent flow and a regular seed with even label amplitude. It constructs the leading transverse pair, the leading activation source, its curl completion, the momentum identity and their required parity. The cutoff is supplied rather than chosen, and no quantitative seed or pressure estimates are part of this constructor.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Constructing the physical leading input from the paper cutoff

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Let $0\le t_0<T$, and take the constructed smooth seed, its radial envelope inside the label cell, $0<h\le1$, and the transported nonzero covector. Assume a smooth periodic odd parent and an even seed on $[t_0,T]$. For any smooth $0\le\widetilde\chi\le1$ on $[0,T]$ vanishing before $t_0$, the formal statement gives $C[\widetilde\chi A_1]=\widetilde\chi C[A_1]$ and identifies the corresponding activation term as $\widetilde\chi'C[A_1]$. Both equalities hold for every label and phase after the prescribed extension from the centered cell. The statement verifies (3.7) for this selected wave family; the paper formulates the identity for arbitrary suitable leading data. The seed regularity hypothesis requires $0\le t_0<T$, $0<h\le1$, envelope radius $0<\ell_*<1/4$, and $M$, $\kappa$ and $\mathbf a$ jointly smooth on $[t_0,T]\times\mathbb R^3$ with $\kappa\ne0$ there.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The cutoff multiplies the correction and its activation term

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For a seed launched at time zero with the constant first cutoff, the constructed physical leading input has both its leading activation source and its completion activation source equal to zero. Smoothness, periodicity, parent oddness and amplitude evenness are retained hypotheses. The velocity itself is not zero: only the sources generated by differentiating its constant time cutoff vanish.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The first wave has no completion activation source

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For the leading input built from the paper cutoff, all four relevant profiles vanish before activation and outside a closed label set $S$ containing the envelope support. The conclusion is the bundled inactivity property. The support inclusion and closedness of $S$ are explicit, because curl completion must also vanish in the same region.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The leading input vanishes in its inactive region

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: If an approximation’s leading data equal the leading input constructed from the paper cutoff for the given parent and seed, the approximation carries the leading relay data. The theorem derives this interface from the explicit leading equation and completion, rather than assuming it as an unrelated field. It does not provide the quantitative relay-coefficient estimates needed later in the recurrence.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The constructed leading input supplies the relay identity

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Take the selected smooth localized seed with $0<h\le1$, a radial envelope contained in the label cell, and a smooth periodic odd parent whose transported covector is nonzero. Assume the seed is even on its active interval $[t_0,T]$. For any smooth cutoff $\widetilde\chi$ on $[0,T]$ valued in $[0,1]$ and zero before $t_0$, the sum of the leading and correction activation terms equals $\widetilde\chi'(A_1+C[A_1])$ at every label and phase. This is (3.8) for the selected periodically extended wave. It is an exact identity; a small residual also requires a bound on $\widetilde\chi'$ and the wave during activation. The seed regularity hypothesis requires $0\le t_0<T$, $0<h\le1$, envelope radius $0<\ell_*<1/4$, and $M$, $\kappa$ and $\mathbf a$ jointly smooth on $[t_0,T]\times\mathbb R^3$ with $\kappa\ne0$ there.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Differentiating the cutoff multiplies the entire completed leading wave

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.text:
Smooth phase-independent coefficients of the actual affine-wave equation on the label torus.

The initial covector is required nonzero, and its evolution equation and joint smoothness are fields of the record. Later-time nonvanishing is proved from these conditions, rather than assumed from a totalized norm expression.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.summary: The coefficients of the transverse affine-wave equation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.text: Shows that changing only phase leaves the covector profile unchanged on the time slab. Both profile values equal the same actual covector at that time and label. This is needed when averaging fast advection and constructing the divergence completion; it follows from the record’s value identity, not just its periodicity.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.summary: The covector profile does not depend on phase

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.text: Propagates the initial nonzero covector along its linear transport equation at a fixed label. Continuity of the strain gives uniqueness, so a nonzero initial solution cannot become zero. The conclusion concerns the represented covector at phase zero on the closed slab; phase independence transfers it to other phases.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.summary: The transported covector stays nonzero on the slab

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.text: Derives spatial periodicity of the represented covector on each certified time slice. Phase independence turns the lattice-phase twist into ordinary label periodicity. The proof concerns the coefficient’s representation and does not itself establish the covector transport equation or its nonvanishing, which are separate fields of the coefficient record.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.summary: The transported covector is periodic in its labels

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.text: Derives label periodicity of the actual strain field on the closed time slab. Its values equal those of a twisted profile independently of phase, so the twist’s compensating phase shift has no effect. This extracts a property of the physical coefficients from their equality with the stored profile representation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.summary: The represented strain is periodic in its labels

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.text: Given a nonzero scalar frequency $\lambda$ and smooth transverse coefficient data (strain $M$ and evolving covector $\kappa$), this constructs all four transverse time coefficients from their actual formulas. The scalar frequency and the covector are distinct: covector nonvanishing is inherited from the coefficient data. Joint smoothness and periodicity allow the coefficients to be bundled as phase-independent profiles. The returned equalities identify the coefficients of this same transverse equation; no inverse estimate is part of the construction.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.summary: Construct the coefficients for the selected transverse solve

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.text: The fields are smooth on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, one-periodic in phase, and invariant under $(a,s)\mapsto(a+n,s+k_*\cdot n)$. The transverse solution consists of a velocity $V$ and pressure $\mathsf p$ satisfying (5.15), with $V(0)=0$ and zero phase mean for the pressure. Its pressure is the normalized primitive specified by (5.16). The formulation also records the support and reflection properties used in §5.5: vanishing of the source before activation or outside a label set passes to both fields. The equation is $V_t+MV+\kappa\mathsf p_s=f$, with $\kappa\cdot V=0$, $\langle V\rangle_s=\langle\mathsf p\rangle_s=0$, and $V(0)=0$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.summary: The forced equation includes its normalized pressure

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.text:
Let a transverse profile $V$ and its normalized pressure $q$ solve the transverse equation with source $F$ on $[0,T]$. For a differentiable inverse-label map $A$, assume its derivative is the inverse coefficient $G$ and $\kappa=G^Tk_*$. Then $
abla q^
atural=(\mathbf d q+P_\kappa(F-2MV))^
atural$, where $q^
atural(t,x)=q(t,A(t,x),k_*\cdot A(t,x))$ and $P_\kappa=\kappa\otimes\kappa/|\kappa|^2$. In Lemma 5.9 the source is $f_p+f_p^S$. This equation replaces one fast phase derivative by forcing and velocity terms. It is an identity, not yet the Hessian bound; one further derivative and quantitative profile bounds are still required.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.summary: Use the equation before taking another physical derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.text: For an actual solution of the transverse equation, assume zero-mean forcing, inactivity outside a closed label support and before $t_0$, a positive differentiable weight, compatible lift and pullback, homogeneous weighted forward stability, and the displayed coefficient bounds. Then the weighted norm of the velocity plus $\mathrm{freq}$ times the weighted norm of the pressure is bounded by the explicit transverse solve constant times the weighted norm of the source. The active interval must satisfy $t_0<T$.
