TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.summary: The transverse solution obeys a weighted finite-order estimate

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.text: For $\lambda>0$, the phase derivative of the normalized pressure profile $\lambda p$ equals the pressure-velocity coefficient acting on the selected velocity plus the pressure-source coefficient acting on $F$. This promotes the ordinary phase-slope equation to profile equality. It is an identity for the chosen pressure, whose zero phase mean is used separately to recover its norm.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.summary: The normalized pressure equation holds as a profile identity

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.text: For positive carrier frequency $\lambda$, the phase derivative of $\lambda p$, with $p$ the selected pressure, is the sum of the normalized pressure-velocity coefficient acting on the selected velocity $V$ and the pressure-source coefficient acting on $F$. This is an ordinary phase derivative, not a time derivative. It preserves the pressure of the same selected transverse result and supplies its inverse-carrier scaling.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.summary: The normalized pressure has the selected phase slope

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.text: The pointwise projected velocity equation for a transverse result is promoted to an equality of twisted profiles: $\partial_tV$ is the sum of coefficient application to velocity and to source. Positive slab duration supplies unique within-derivatives. The same output velocity profile $V$ occurs on both sides, which is needed when its successive time norms are estimated.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.summary: The selected velocity equation holds as a profile identity

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.text: For the selected result, use a positive slab, $0\le t_0\le T$, and a continuous positive amplitude $\gamma$ on $[t_0,T]$. Assume $\lambda>0$, nonnegative $C_0,C$, the undifferentiated weighted estimate $W(V)\le C_0W(F)$, and bounds by $C$ on the time seminorms of the four coefficients. The weighted time norm $\mathcal J_q$ of velocity plus $\lambda$ times that of pressure is at most $K\,\mathcal J_q(F)$, the source norm through the same order, where $K=(1+2c_1C)(1+Tc_2C)^q(C_0+1)+2c_1C$ and $c_1,c_2$ are the costs of applying a row and a matrix coefficient. Zero phase mean recovers pressure from its slope and preserves the inverse-frequency gain.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.summary: Bound time jets of the same transverse velocity and pressure

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.text: For an existing transverse result with velocity $V$, its time derivative equals the stored velocity coefficient $-M+2P_\kappa M$ applied to $V$ plus the source coefficient applied to $F$. The result is an assertion of an actual derivative within $[0,T]$ at each slab time and label-phase point. It eliminates pressure using the result's own phase-slope equation, retaining the same solution and force rather than invoking a fresh inverse.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.summary: Eliminate pressure in the selected transverse velocity equation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.text: This structure stores the velocity generator $-M+2P_\kappa M$, the source projection, and two normalized pressure coefficients $-2|\theta|^{-2}\theta^TM$ and $|\theta|^{-2}\theta^T$ as smooth twisted profiles, together with their exact slab values. Only the pressure coefficients use the normalized covector $\theta=\lambda^{-1}\kappa$. The fields certify identification with the supplied transverse coefficient data; they do not include numerical bounds, solve an equation, or assert positivity of $\lambda$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.summary: The four coefficients of the transverse velocity and pressure

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc.text: On $[0,T]$, with $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$ and $\lambda\ge1$, the parent velocity is smooth and periodic, has a flow $X$, and satisfies $\|D_aX\|,\|(D_aX)^{-1}\|,\|\nabla U\|\le\mathsf D$. Continuous torus representatives of $U$ and its actual momentum residual $R_U$ are supplied, with Fourier supports in radii $2\mathsf D$ and $4\mathsf D$ and $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$. The underlying mean-equation data also carry inverse-deformation and strain bounds at most $\mathsf D$. This collects quantitative hypotheses, not their proof. Oddness and incompressibility are not additional fields of this declaration; they must be supplied when later physical conclusions need them. The parent is permitted to have nonzero residual.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc.summary: Specify the parent data used in the quantitative hierarchy

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc.text: Collects the radius identities, carrier and deformation bounds, inverse-flow smoothness, coframe identities, all-order velocity and coframe jets, low-order pressure coefficients and parent-gradient Hölder estimate. These are propositions about one fixed parent geometry and the chosen tables $R$ and $C$. The structure itself does not assert that the tables exist or are uniform across different parents; the construction theorem supplies that quantifier order.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc.summary: The parent bounds needed for physical readout

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc.text: Chooses one envelope exponent threshold before the truncated parent and launch data. Given an odd parent, a launch time strictly inside the slab, nonnegative switch rate, normalized central covector and a central wave satisfying the localized seed requirements (covector and amplitude equations, transversality, stability and coupling), it constructs a localized seed with the specified widths, hierarchy regularity and even label amplitude. The central wave is assumed, not produced by this theorem.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc.summary: A regular localized seed for every admissible parent

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc.text: From a positive slab of duration at most one, $D\ge2$, frequency at least one and a nonzero carrier, constructs parent geometry and a truncated-parent interface. Inputs include a smooth periodic flow, deformation and strain bounds, the signed Hessian-minus-residual inequality, concrete band-limited velocity and residual representatives, and the residual size. The theorem packages precisely these assumptions; oddness and solenoidality are not extra binders here.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc.summary: Building the parent interface from physical hypotheses

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc.text:
Let $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$, $\lambda\ge1$ and $k_*
e0$. Suppose $U,p$ are smooth, $U$ is periodic with flow $X$, and $\|D_aX\|,\|(D_aX)^{-1}\|,\|
abla U\|\le\mathsf D$. Supply continuous torus representatives of $U$ and $R_U=U_t+U\cdot
abla U+
abla p$, supported in Fourier balls of radii $2\mathsf D$ and $4\mathsf D$, with $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$. If $D^2p-
abla R_U\le I$ as quadratic forms, the formal statement constructs the parent coefficient data for the mean and transverse equations, with the quantitative parent bounds. It assumes the coercivity inequality; it does not prove it from Fourier truncation. No exact Euler equation for $U$ is required.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc.summary: Construct mean and transverse data from the physical hypotheses

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc.text: Let a smooth periodic parent on $[0,T]$ have deformation and gradient bounds $\mathsf D\ge2$, velocity and residual Fourier radii $2\mathsf D,4\mathsf D$, and residual size at most $\lambda^{-5/2}$. Normalize $|\kappa(t_0,0)|=\lambda\ge1$, take $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$ with integer $a\ge7$, and $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$. For a smooth profile with the combined lattice translation law and any positive continuous weight on an interval $[\tau,T]\subset[0,T]$, evaluation through inverse labels gives the derivative and $C^{m,1/2}$ bounds of (5.44)–(5.45), with costs $C_m\mathsf D^{(a+1)m}\lambda^{3m/2}$ and one additional derivative for Hölder control. Phase-independent profiles omit the frequency factor. Constants precede the parent; the derivative sum counts ordered coordinate sequences and the target may be any real normed space.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc.summary: Obtain both weighted estimates uniformly from the truncated parent

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc.text: Let $\lambda\ge1$, $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$, $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, $L=\mathsf D^{2a+b_0}$ and $0<\gamma\le1$. Assume the parent coefficient, residual and coercivity bounds, the central transverse stability and positive coupling, and $L^6\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$. A physical expansion with the required leading-wave and correction estimates satisfies the level, finite-sum, and remainder bounds of Theorem 5.6. This statement takes that expansion and its leading estimates as inputs. The construction from a parent and central wave is supplied by further existence results, so this conditional estimate alone is not the whole construction.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc.summary: The supplied leading estimates control every retained level

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc.text: Assume a smooth odd periodic solenoidal parent with both deformation bounds, band limits, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$, together with a nonzero stable central seed of positive coupling and $0<\gamma\le1$. Require $\mathsf D^{6(2a+b_0)}\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$. A truncated parent and prescribed central wave determine a localized seed and a finite expansion satisfying the estimates of Theorem 5.6 at every derivative order. The constants are fixed before the parent data. This result uses the later-wave time cutoff; the more general construction subsequently allows any admissible cutoff after the seed has been chosen.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc.summary: Choose one localized seed and expansion for all orders

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc.text: Take $0\le t_0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$, $\lambda\ge1$, smooth periodic $U,p_U$, and the flow $X$. Both $U$ and $R_U=U_t+U\cdot\nabla U+\nabla p_U$ are odd, with Fourier radii $2\mathsf D,4\mathsf D$ and $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$. The velocity gradient, both deformations, and the two endpoint-operator bounds are at most $\mathsf D$. Additional supplied geometry specifies the mean and transverse equations; its full definition is not included. At the origin require a nonzero transverse central solution, normalized coupling at least $\mathsf D^{-1}$, $|\kappa(t_0,0)|=\lambda$, $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$, and weighted propagation factor $\mathsf D$ for every homogeneous transverse solution. For sufficiently large $a,b_0$, set $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$, $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$ and $L=\mathsf D^{2a+b_0}$, with $L^6\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$. One seed is chosen before every smooth cutoff $0\le\widetilde\chi\le1$ vanishing for $t<t_0$ and every $P\ge2$. Each then admits an expansion satisfying all level and sum bounds, with $\|R_P\|_{[n]}\le C_{n,P}\lambda^{-5/4-2P/3}$ simultaneously for every $n$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc.summary: One selected seed serves every cutoff and every finite depth

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc.text: Assume a smooth odd periodic solenoidal parent with both deformation bounds, band limits, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$, together with a stable central seed of positive coupling and $0<\gamma\le1$. Require $\mathsf D^{6(2a+b_0)}\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$. Given a localized seed satisfying the regularity and central-wave assumptions, the later-wave activation produces one expansion obeying the level, sum, and remainder bounds of Theorem 5.6. The construction derives the leading estimates from this seed. The same profiles satisfy every derivative order, rather than being chosen anew when the requested order changes.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc.summary: A fixed localized seed yields all derivative estimates

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc.text: Assume a smooth odd divergence-free periodic parent on $0<T\le1$ has deformation and gradient bounds $\mathsf D$, Fourier radii $2\mathsf D,4\mathsf D$ for velocity and residual, and residual size at most $\lambda^{-5/2}$. Its smooth periodic pressure and mean-equation data are fixed. Let $0\le t_0<T$, $|\kappa(t_0,0)|=\lambda\ge1$, and let the nonzero transverse central seed obey (5.5) with $0<\gamma\le1$. Absolute exponents and depth-dependent constants can be chosen before these data so that, for $P\ge2$ and $\Gamma_P\mathsf D^b\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, one localized seed works for every admissible time cutoff. For each cutoff an expansion exists satisfying the velocity, residual, pressure, central-gradient and flow estimates of Lemmas 5.8–5.10. This is an existence statement for selected expansions, rather than a universal statement about every family satisfying the recursion.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc.summary: Choose one seed before choosing its time cutoff

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc.text: Consider a smooth periodic parent on $[0,T]$, $0<T\le1$, with $\|D_aX\|,\|(D_aX)^{-1}\|,\|\nabla U\|\le\mathsf D\ge2$, velocity and residual Fourier radii $2\mathsf D,4\mathsf D$, and residual size at most $\lambda^{-5/2}$. If $|\kappa(t_0,0)|=\lambda\ge1$, then every integer envelope exponent $a\ge7$ admits the coefficient estimates used for physical evaluation, with $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$. The order constants and one common exponent are chosen before the parent. The conclusion includes inverse-flow derivative bounds and scaled bounds for the coefficients entering the pressure and flow estimates. These estimates are derived from the specified parent data, not added as independent hypotheses on that parent.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc.summary: Derive the inverse coefficient estimates before choosing the parent

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc.text: Chooses universal exponent thresholds, then a cost table $K(H)$ for a supplied seed-cost table, before the parent and depth. For a fixed approximation of depth at least two, it assumes relay identities, launch normalization, central-wave and inactive-region data, weighted leading bounds through order $H$, and frequency absorption. It derives the actual measured recurrence through $H$; its tail bound additionally requires $n+1+3P\le H$ for the depth $P$. It does not select the approximation or prove the input seed estimates.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc.summary: Uniform recurrence and tail bounds at a chosen order

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc.text: Chooses a nonnegative order table $V$ before any particular parent, scale or frequency. For every truncated hierarchy parent, derivatives of positive order $j\le n$ of its velocity are bounded by $V(n)D^j$ on the slab. The proof applies the real Bernstein estimates to the band-limited parent gradient. Order zero is not included.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trunc.summary: One derivative table works for every truncated parent

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text:
The parent coefficient budgets for the normalized potential, pressure, and the three coframe contractions in the linear relay.

This proposition requires genuine smooth coefficient fields and finite mixed-word bounds. It is a supplied budget, not a theorem that arbitrary parent data have those bounds.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: Parent coefficient bounds used by the linear relay

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: If $\mathsf D\ge1$, $L\ge0$, and $|\ell^{-1}|\le\mathsf D^q$, the budget $L(1+|\ell^{-1}|)\mathsf D^{15}$ is bounded by $2L\mathsf D^{15+q}$. The theorem enlarges a supplied budget accordingly. It does not choose the width; the crucial bound $|\ell^{-1}|\le\mathsf D^q$ must come from that earlier parameter choice.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: The chosen width becomes a fixed parent power

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: Every field of a relay coefficient budget with value $A$ remains true under a larger value $B\ge A$. The theorem applies the assembly rule with both parts enlarged by the inequality $A\le B$. The derivative orders and coefficient functions stay fixed, so this step changes only the numerical allowance, not the underlying relay.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: A relay coefficient budget can be enlarged

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: Given four potential or pressure coefficient bounds at order $n+1$ and three families of geometric row bounds at order $n$, this theorem builds one common budget for all coefficients of the linear relay. The common value $K$ must dominate both the potential allowance $K_p$ and the geometric allowance $K_g$. All analytic estimates are inputs here; the proof only enlarges and packages them.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: Combining potential and geometric coefficient allowances

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: This proposition records all-order label-derivative bounds for the inverse coframe, strain, normalized covector, and inverse squared covector norm. Their slopes are seven, six, seven, and sixteen, with fixed residual powers. It also records slice smoothness and nonvanishing of the covector. The index set $X$ ranges over times or any chosen subset without requiring time derivatives.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: The parent derivatives needed for the linear relay

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: Given coefficient data for completion and relay, this condition says that one number $K$ bounds the unweighted full-slab factorial time norms, of time order $q$ and with no Hölder quotients, of all of them. The four inner coefficients (potential, differentiated potential, pressure amplitude and pressure source) are bounded at spatial order $n+1$; each of the three curl rows, material rows and pressure-gradient rows is bounded at spatial order $n$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: One bound for all normalized relay coefficients

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: For profiles $G,M,\kappa$ and reals $\ell$ and $\lambda$, this bundles seven coefficient profiles with their exact values at every slab time, label and phase, all read from $G,M$ and $\hat\kappa=\lambda^{-1}\kappa$ at phase zero: the potential $v\mapsto-|\hat\kappa|^{-2}\hat\kappa\times v$; the differentiated potential $v\mapsto|\hat\kappa|^{-2}(M^*\hat\kappa\times v+\hat\kappa\times Mv)-2|\hat\kappa|^{-4}(\hat\kappa\cdot M\hat\kappa)\,\hat\kappa\times v$; the pressure amplitude $v\mapsto-2|\hat\kappa|^{-2}\hat\kappa\cdot Mv$; the pressure source $f\mapsto|\hat\kappa|^{-2}\hat\kappa\cdot f$; and for $i=1,2,3$ the curl row $w\mapsto\ell^{-1}(G^*e_i)\times w$, the material row (curl row composed with $M$, minus the curl row built from $GM$) and the gradient row $p\mapsto\ell^{-1}p\,G^*e_i$. No bounds or nonvanishing are asserted.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: The normalized coefficients of completion and relay

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: Write $\hat\kappa(t,a)=\Lambda^{-1}\kappa(t,a,0)$ and evaluate $G,M$ at phase zero. Say $g$ has a mixed bound with amplitude $A$ and costs $C_n$ if $\|D^n_a\partial_t^ig(t,a)\|\le C_nA\,\mathsf D^{pn}$ for all $i\le q$, all $n$, $t\in[0,T]$ and all $a$, time derivatives within $[0,T]$. This structure records: mixed bounds with amplitude $A_{\rm in}$ and costs $C_{\rm in}$ for the four inner coefficients $v\mapsto-|\hat\kappa|^{-2}\hat\kappa\times v$, the time-derivative coefficient built from $M$ and $\hat\kappa$, the pressure row $v\mapsto-2|\hat\kappa|^{-2}\langle\hat\kappa,Mv\rangle$ and the source row $v\mapsto|\hat\kappa|^{-2}\langle\hat\kappa,v\rangle$; and, for each coordinate $i$, mixed bounds with amplitude $A_{\rm out}$ and costs $C_{\rm out}$ for the curl, material and pressure-gradient rows built from $G$, $M$ and $\ell^{-1}$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: Mixed bounds for the relay coefficients, separated inside and outside the phase primitive

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: This collects joint time-label smoothness on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3$ for seven label families built from $G$, $M$, $\kappa$, $\ell$ and $\Lambda$, with $\hat\kappa=\Lambda^{-1}\kappa(t,a,0)$ and $G,M$ read at phase zero: the four inner potential or pressure coefficients (the potential $v\mapsto-|\hat\kappa|^{-2}\hat\kappa\times v$, its time coefficient, the pressure amplitude row and the pressure source row $v\mapsto|\hat\kappa|^{-2}\langle\hat\kappa,v\rangle$), and the three coordinate-indexed outer geometric coefficients (curl, material and gradient rows) for each $i$. No mixed-jet size is asserted.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: Joint smoothness of the seven relay coefficient families

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: Let relay coefficient profiles be given whose values on $[0,T]$ are the seven coefficient formulas, with $0<T\le1$, $\ell\ge0$, $\mathsf D\ge0$, $A_{\rm in},A_{\rm out}\ge0$, $\ell\mathsf D^p\le1$, costs $C_{\rm in},C_{\rm out}\ge0$, and the mixed bounds of the preceding structure. Put $c(C,q,n)=(q+1)\,N_4(n)\sum_{j\le n}C_j$, where $N_4(n)$ is the number of multi-indices in four variables of order at most $n$. Then for every $n$ and every phase scale $h$, with $K=c(C_{\rm in},q,n+1)A_{\rm in}+c(C_{\rm out},q,n)A_{\rm out}$, the factorial time norm $\sum_{i\le q}\frac{T^i}{i!}\|\partial_t^i\cdot\|_{[\cdot]}$ (unweighted, scales $\ell,h$) of each of the four inner coefficients at spatial order $n+1$, and of each curl, material and gradient row at order $n$, is at most $K$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: Mixed label bounds give the relay coefficient budget

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: For $T>0$, a phase width $h$ and a vector profile $v$ with zero phase mean, the completion profile is $\lambda^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^3c_i\big(\ell\,\partial_{a_i}\partial_s^{-1}[P\,v]\big)$, where $P$ is the potential coefficient, $\partial_s^{-1}$ the normalized phase primitive and $c_i$ the $i$th curl row of the coefficient bundle. Its agreement with the actual curl completion is a separate theorem.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: Completion as three normalized coordinate terms

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: Assume $T>0$, the phase average of $v$ vanishes, $G$ and $\kappa$ are independent of phase, $\kappa(t,a,0)\ne0$ for every slab time and label, $\ell\ne0$ and $\lambda>0$. Then the coordinate completion profile of $v$ equals the selected periodic curl completion of $v$: the curl, pulled back through $G$, of the normalized phase potential $\partial_s^{-1}\big(-|\kappa|^{-2}\kappa\times v\big)$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: The normalized coordinate completion is the actual curl completion

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: For positive carrier $\lambda$, a nonnegative cap $K$, and the common coefficient budget, bounds the weighted time norm of the coordinate completion at order $n$ by the common order constant times $K^2\lambda^{-1}$ and the input norm of $v$ at $n+1$. The input $v$ is centered, and the weight $\tau$ is bounded on a subset of the slab. This theorem estimates the coordinate completion; identifying it with the selected physical curl completion is a separate theorem.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: Completion keeps one inverse carrier factor after time differentiation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: For a matrix profile $G$, a real $\ell$ and a coordinate index $i$, this is the field $(t,a)\mapsto\big(v\mapsto\ell^{-1}\,(G(t,a,0)^{\mathsf T}e_i)\times v\big)$, with $G$ evaluated at phase zero and $e_i$ the $i$th coordinate vector.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: The label row for the pulled-back curl

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: For every cost sequence $C_n\ge0$ and every $q$ there are sequences $K_{\rm in}(n),K_{\rm out}(n)\ge0$ such that the following holds. Let $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge1$, $A\ge1$, $\ell\ge0$ with $\ell\mathsf D^{16}\le1$, let $G,M$ (matrix) and $\kappa$ (vector) be phase-independent twisted profiles with $\hat\kappa=\Lambda^{-1}\kappa(t,a,0)\ne0$ on $[0,T]$, and suppose $G(t,a,0)$, $M(t,a,0)$, $\hat\kappa$ and $|\hat\kappa|^{-2}$ satisfy $\|D_a^n\partial_t^ig\|\le C_nA\mathsf D^{16n}$ for $i\le q$, all $n$, $t\in[0,T]$. Then there are relay coefficient profiles equal on $[0,T]$ to the seven coefficient formulas whose budget, for every $n$ and phase scale $h$, is $K_{\rm in}(n)A^6+K_{\rm out}(n)|\ell^{-1}|A^2$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: Relay coefficient costs chosen before the parent data

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: For a matrix profile $G$, a real $\ell$ and a coordinate index $i$, this is the field $(t,a)\mapsto\big(r\mapsto\ell^{-1}r\,G(t,a,0)^{\mathsf T}e_i\big)$, a linear map from scalars to vectors, with $G$ evaluated at phase zero.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: The label row for the pulled-back pressure gradient

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: For a twisted profile $f(t,a,s)$, this is the function of time and label $(t,a)\mapsto f(t,a,0)$. It asserts nothing about other phases or about periodicity in the label.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: A profile read at phase zero

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: For the inverse coframe $G$ and strain $M$ (matrix profiles read at phase zero), a label width $\ell$ and a coordinate index $i$, this row is $(t,a)\mapsto M\circ c_i(G)-c_i(GM)$, where $c_i(H)$ is the curl row $v\mapsto\ell^{-1}(H^{\mathsf T}e_i)\times v$ with the same inverse label-width factor. It is the geometric contribution to the material derivative of a completion; the formula is algebraic.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: The label row for the material derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: Given phase-independent twisted profiles $G,M,\kappa$ on $[0,T]$ and the joint smoothness of the seven relay coefficient formulas, this constructs relay coefficient profiles: twisted profiles, independent of phase, whose values at every $(t,a,s)$ with $t\in[0,T]$ equal the corresponding coefficient formula evaluated at $(t,a)$ from $G(t,a,0)$, $M(t,a,0)$, $\Lambda^{-1}\kappa(t,a,0)$ and $\ell$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: Relay coefficient profiles built from smooth label formulas

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: For a vector profile $\kappa$ and a frequency $\Lambda$, this is the field $(t,a)\mapsto\big(v\mapsto-|\hat\kappa|^{-2}\,\hat\kappa\times v\big)$ with $\hat\kappa=\Lambda^{-1}\kappa(t,a,0)$. Division by zero is assigned zero, so where $\hat\kappa=0$ the coefficient is zero.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: The normalized potential coefficient on label space

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: This label field evaluates the strain $M$ and the normalized covector $\hat\kappa=\Lambda^{-1}\kappa(t,a,0)$ at phase zero, then applies the algebraic coefficient appearing in the time derivative of the wave potential: $v\mapsto|\hat\kappa|^{-2}\big((M^{\mathsf T}\hat\kappa)\times v+\hat\kappa\times Mv\big)-2\langle\hat\kappa,M\hat\kappa\rangle|\hat\kappa|^{-4}\,\hat\kappa\times v$. It is linear in the profile amplitude $v$ and nonlinear in the normalized covector.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: The time coefficient of the normalized potential

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: On the slab, the differentiated potential coefficient of the bundle takes the same value at every phase for given time and label. This follows from its stored formula, which uses only $M$ and $\lambda^{-1}\kappa$ at phase zero; no time derivative is computed.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: The differentiated potential coefficient is independent of phase

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: The potential coefficient in the supplied bundle is phase-independent on the time slab. Its defining equality evaluates a canonical function of the normalized covector at phase zero, so changing the output phase does not change the value. This property is needed to preserve the zero phase mean before taking the potential primitive.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: The potential coefficient is independent of phase

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: For profiles $M$ (matrix) and $\kappa$ (vector) and a frequency $\Lambda$, with $\hat\kappa=\Lambda^{-1}\kappa(t,a,0)$, this is the scalar row $(t,a)\mapsto\big(v\mapsto-2|\hat\kappa|^{-2}\langle\hat\kappa,M(t,a,0)v\rangle\big)$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: The normalized pressure coefficient multiplying the velocity

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: Shows that the pressure amplitude row $v\mapsto-2|\hat\kappa|^{-2}\hat\kappa\cdot Mv$, multiplying the velocity in the normalized oscillatory pressure, is phase-independent on the slab. The bundle fixes it as a canonical function of $M$ and the normalized covector $\hat\kappa=\lambda^{-1}\kappa$ at phase zero. This allows that row to pass through phase averaging.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: The pressure amplitude coefficient is independent of phase

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: This scalar row maps a source vector to $\langle k,f\rangle/\|k\|^2$, using the phase-zero normalized covector. Together with the strain-dependent pressure-amplitude row it expresses the normalized pressure in the relay. The abbreviation merely identifies the coefficient function, leaving smoothness, valid normalization, and mixed bounds to later statements.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: The normalized pressure coefficient multiplying the source

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: Shows that the row multiplying the forcing profile in the normalized pressure depends only on time and label. Its stored value formula reads the normalized covector at phase zero, so every independent phase gives the same row. Consequently it can preserve a forcing profile's zero phase mean before the pressure primitive is taken.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: The pressure source coefficient is independent of phase

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: For $T>0$, a width $h$ and vector profiles $v,f$ with zero phase mean, the relay profile is $\lambda^{-1}$ times the sum over $i=1,2,3$ of five terms, each a row applied to $\ell\,\partial_{a_i}\partial_s^{-1}[\,\cdot\,]$: the curl row on the primitive of the differentiated potential coefficient applied to $v$; the curl row on the primitive of the potential coefficient applied to $f$; the material row on the primitive of the potential coefficient applied to $v$; and the gradient row on the primitives of the pressure amplitude applied to $v$ and of the pressure source applied to $f$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: Relay as five normalized terms in each coordinate

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: For $T>0$, vector profiles $v,f$ with zero phase mean, $\ell\ne0$, $\lambda>0$, a slab time $t\in[0,T]$ and a label-phase point $x$, the coordinate relay profile at $(t,x)$ equals the physical relay built from $G,M,\kappa$ at phase zero, the potential of $v$, its time source from $v,f$, and the oscillatory pressure. This is an identity of explicit expressions; no evolution equation for $v$ is assumed.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: The measured relay equals the canonical physical expression

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: Let $\lambda>0$, $K\ge0$, let the coefficient bundle satisfy the common bound $K$ at time order $q$ and spatial order $n$, and let $v,f$ have zero phase mean. For any time set $A\subseteq[0,T]$ and weight with $|\tau|\le C$ on $A$, the $\tau$-weighted factorial time norm at order $n$ of the relay is at most $c_nK^2\lambda^{-1}$ times the sum of the same norms of $v$ and $f$ at order $n+1$, with $c_n$ nine times the sum of the vector and pressure primitive costs.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: Relay keeps one derivative loss and one inverse carrier factor

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: For each spatial order $n$, this constant is nine times the sum of the vector primitive cost and the pressure primitive cost at order $n$. It depends only on $n$; time order and coefficient sizes enter through the separate coefficient bound $K$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: One order constant covers completion and relay

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: Proves nonnegativity of the common completion and relay constant at every spatial order. Unfolding leaves operator norms, finite cardinalities, natural powers, and positive numerical factors. The result is used when multiplying coefficient and source inequalities in the mixed-time completion and relay bounds.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: The common relay order constant is nonnegative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.text: This measures a profile family and its exact algebraic source expressions using full-slab supremum seminorms for means and active amplitude-weighted supremum seminorms for oscillations and pressure. Half-Hölder difference quotients are excluded from these measurements. It supplies actual nonnegative measurements, while the analytic recurrence inequalities and hierarchy equations are still separate requirements.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.summary: Insert genuine spatial measurements into the hierarchy recurrence

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.text: The omitted completion–oscillation and mean–oscillation phase interactions $(C_i\cdot\kappa)\partial_sY_j$ and $(B_i\cdot\kappa)\partial_sY_j$ are bounded by the supplied fast coefficient cap $K L\,\mathrm{freq}^{3/2}$. Inactivity before $t_0$ transfers $C_i$ and $Y_j$ to active amplitude norms $\|\cdot\|_{[n],\gamma}$, while the mean stays unweighted on the full slab. The resulting products use the completion or mean at order $n$ and the oscillation $Y_j$ at order $n+1$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.summary: The two omitted fast interactions have measured bounds

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.text: The theorem bounds three terms separately: the averaged oscillation advection $\langle(Y_i\cdot\mathbf d)Y_j\rangle_s$, the averaged divergence product $\langle(\mathbf d\cdot V_i)Y_j\rangle_s$, and advection $(B_i\cdot\mathbf d)B_j$ between means. Their bounds use the measured hierarchy sizes at order $n+1$. Inactivity converts full-slab oscillation norms to active weighted norms, while the nonnegativity of the frequency parameter permits discarding the pressure part of the measured oscillation size.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.summary: The three slow contributions to a mean source

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.text: Replacing the positive amplitude weight by a positive constant multiple divides both the measured oscillatory level and its measured source by that constant. This uses the exact seminorm scaling for velocity, pressure and source. The result is restricted to these two quantities; it does not state a similar change for the unweighted mean levels.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.summary: Velocity and source sizes change by the same factor

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.text: The actual measurements satisfy the reconstruction inequality for $Y_p=V_p+C_{p-1}$ and the identity that the measured $Z$ level is the measured $Y$ level plus the measured mean level. The pressure contribution is nonnegative and can enlarge the oscillation bound. Here the measured $Z$ level is a sum of two measurements, rather than the norm of the combined profile $Z_p=Y_p+B_p$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.summary: Reconstruct the oscillatory and mean budgets from the profiles

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.text: Assume a common cap on the order-$n$ norms of the three scaled rows of the coframe matrix, with $3Q_n^2$ times that cap at most $KL$, and assume every $Y_p$ vanishes before $t_0$. Then the full-slab norm of a tail label product $(Z_i\cdot\mathbf d)Z_j$ is at most $KL$ times the two measured sizes $\|Y_i\|_{[n+1],\gamma}+\|B_i\|_{[n+1]}$ and $\|Y_j\|_{[n+1],\gamma}+\|B_j\|_{[n+1]}$. The first factor is enlarged to that order by monotonicity. The theorem requires $\ell\ne0$ and the supplied numerical coframe inequality.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.summary: A slow tail product costs one more mixed derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.text: Given coframe and fast-covector caps, phase independence of the coframe $G$, and inactivity of all oscillations and corrections, this theorem supplies the bundle of individual source estimates for the measured profiles. It still takes the exact averaged-source identity, centered-relay identity, residual bound, and relay bound as inputs. Thus it assembles the quadratic estimates; it does not independently derive those four premises.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.summary: Putting the actual sources into the norm recurrence

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.text: If $V_{P+1}$ and $B_{P+1}$ vanish, the measured sizes of $Y_{P+1}$ and $Z_{P+1}$ both equal the measured size of the completion $C_{P+1}$ produced by $V_P$, and the mean size at that index is zero. The formalization indexes a completion by the velocity that produced it. This is the paper’s convention $Y_{P+1}=Z_{P+1}=C_{P+1}$ expressed in that indexing.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.summary: At the last index only the completion remains

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.text: When the oscillatory part $Y_i$ vanishes before activation and $\gamma\le1$, the full-slab unweighted norm $\|Z_i\|_{[m]}$ is bounded by the measured amplitude norm $\|Y_i\|_{[m],\gamma}$ of its oscillation plus the unweighted mean $\|B_i\|_{[m]}$. The proof applies the triangle inequality to $Z_i=Y_i+B_i$ and changes norms only on the inactive oscillation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.summary: The full velocity is bounded by its measured pieces

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.text: Builds the source-term bounds for the actual twisted operators, measuring mean forcing with $q-1$ time jets and oscillatory forcing with $q$. It requires nonzero scales $\ell,h$, a phase-independent $G$, a positive active weight $\gamma\le1$, inactivity of oscillations and completions before $t_0$, coefficient caps $2(3Q_n^2r_n)\le KL$ and $2Q_n^2U_n(h^{-1}\kappa)\le KL\lambda^{3/2}$, and phase-independent means. Exact mean-source identities, centered relay identities, the lower-order residual bound $KL\lambda^{-5/2}$, and the relay estimate are supplied hypotheses. Natural subtraction gives $q-1=0$ when $q=0$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.summary: The actual sources use one fewer time derivative for means

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.text: Bounds the three kinds of omitted products: slow label products of $Z_i=Y_i+B_i$, fast completion products $(\kappa\cdot C_{i-1})\partial_sY_j$, and fast mean products $(\kappa\cdot B_i)\partial_sY_j$, with factors $KL$, $KL\lambda^{3/2}$ and $KL\lambda^{3/2}$. All conclusions use the full time order $q$. The theorem assumes nonzero scales, coefficient caps $2(3Q_n^2r)\le KL$ and $2Q_n^2U_n(h^{-1}\kappa)\le KL\lambda^{3/2}$, a positive active weight at most one, and inactivity of oscillations and completions. The resulting estimates are supplied to the finite-depth residual theorem.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.summary: The omitted nonlinear terms obey the full time order bounds

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.text: This constructs the finite mixed-word seminorm of a twisted profile after restricting time to a set $A$ and multiplying by a time-only weight $\tau$. The explicit boundedness proof covers every profile and admissible word. A true-or-false switch controls whether half-Hölder difference quotients are included with the pointwise measurements.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.summary: Measure actual scaled derivatives on a chosen time set

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.text: The actual seminorm evaluates to the finite-word norm of the time slices $t\mapsto\tau(t)f(t,\cdot,\cdot)$ for $t\in A$. The equality is definitional and exposes that weighting occurs at fixed time before label and phase differentiation. The separate boundedness proof certifies the suprema while leaving their exact measurement formula unchanged.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.summary: Read the finite norm of the weighted time slices

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.text:
The Appendix D seminorm with the reciprocal seed amplitude on the closed interval $[t_0,T]$, where the seed is strictly positive.

The definition requires $0\le t_0\le T$, $T>0$, continuity of $\gamma$ and strict positivity at every active time. The compact-interval reciprocal bound is proved before selecting a numerical bound. Division by a vanishing amplitude is therefore excluded at the intended times.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.summary: The finite norm divided by the seed amplitude

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.text: The amplitude seminorm is exactly the finite-word norm of the profile divided by $\gamma$ on $[t_0,T]$. Continuity and strict positivity of $\gamma$ on that compact interval justify bounded inverse weight, including both endpoints. Only label and phase derivatives are measured; the weight is constant on each spatial slice.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.summary: The amplitude-weighted norm uses the closed active interval

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.text: For a continuous strictly positive amplitude $\gamma$ on $[t_0,T]$, averaging a profile over the phase does not increase its amplitude-weighted order-$n$ norm. Compactness gives a bound for $\gamma^{-1}$, allowing the bounded-weight theorem to apply. No assumption that $\gamma\le1$ or that the profile vanishes before activation is needed for this contraction.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.summary: Phase averaging preserves the amplitude bound

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.text: If the mean–mean label product is fixed by phase averaging, subtracting the average leaves only terms with an oscillatory factor. Assuming $Y_j$ vanishes before activation and $\gamma\le1$, the centered norm is bounded by twice the slow cost times the weighted-plus-mean factor norms. The second factor consumes order $n+1$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.summary: Centering removes the product of two means

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.text: This enlarges the first factor’s order in the centered slow-product estimate from $n$ to $n+1$, leaving the second already at $n+1$. Monotonicity of weighted and unweighted seminorms proves the bound. The same mean-invariance, inactivity, and $\gamma\le1$ hypotheses are retained for use in the recurrence.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.summary: Both centered-product factors may use the next order

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.text: For $0<\gamma\le1$, a completion profile $C$ that vanishes before activation has its full-slab norm controlled by its amplitude norm. The fast advection $(C\cdot\kappa)\partial_sY$, minus its phase average, is then bounded by twice the product estimate. The covector remains unweighted, and the derivative falls on $Y$ at order $n+1$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.summary: Centering a fast product costs a factor two

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.text: On the active interval $[t_0,T]$ with continuous positive $\gamma$, label advection $(z\cdot\mathbf d)g$ is controlled by the amplitude norm of $z$ and the full-slab unweighted norm of $g$, with one extra derivative on $g$. The inverse amplitude is a bounded time multiplier. No derivative of $\gamma$ enters this estimate.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.summary: The advector can carry the amplitude weight

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.text: With the same positive continuous amplitude, the weight may instead be placed on the differentiated profile $g$. The advector $z$ is measured without weight on the full slab, while $g$ uses order $n+1$ on the active interval. The coframe cost and nonzero label width remain hypotheses.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.summary: The differentiated profile can carry the amplitude weight

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.text: If every time slice has scaled jets bounded by $\gamma(t)B$, its amplitude-weighted seminorm is bounded by the number of admissible words times $B$. The theorem assumes nonzero scales, $B\ge0$, a nonempty slab, and continuous strictly positive $\gamma$. Positivity justifies cancelling the inverse weight after spatial and phase differentiation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.summary: Scaled jets control the amplitude-weighted finite norm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.text: Bound the exact sum of derivative seminorms by a common word bound.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.summary: Word bounds control the exact weighted norm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.text: Let $T>0$, $0\le t_0\le T$, and let $\gamma$ be continuous and positive on $[t_0,T]$. Let $f(t,a,s)$ be a twisted profile with $\int_0^1f(t,a,s)\,ds=0$ for all $t\in[0,T]$ and all $a$. Then for all scales $\ell,h$ and every order $n$, the amplitude-weighted finite profile norm (the finite norm of $f/\gamma$ on $[t_0,T]$, without Hölder part) satisfies $\|f\|_{[n],\gamma}\le2\|\partial_sf\|_{[n],\gamma}$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.summary: The phase derivative controls a profile with zero phase mean

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.text: Increasing the derivative order from $n$ to $m$ with $n\le m$ cannot decrease the amplitude seminorm. The active interval, scales, and positive amplitude function are unchanged. The proof adds nonnegative word measurements, so it does not require a comparison between distinct seed amplitudes.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.summary: Higher spatial orders enlarge the same amplitude-weighted norm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.text: For a continuous positive weight $\gamma$ on the active closed interval and a positive constant $c$, replacing the weight by $c\gamma$ divides the amplitude seminorm by $c$. The statement holds whether or not Hölder quotients are included. Positivity prevents the inverse factor from degenerating and preserves the seminorm interpretation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.summary: Multiplying the weight divides the amplitude seminorm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.text: For smooth profiles on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, one-periodic in phase and satisfying $f(t,a+n,s+k_*\cdot n)=f(t,a,s)$, take $h\ne0$ and a continuous positive weight $\gamma$ on $[t_0,T]$, $0\le t_0\le T$. Let $\|\cdot\|_{[n]}$ sum the suprema of derivatives in the directions $\ell_*\partial_{a_i},h\partial_s$ through order $n$, each multi-index once; the weighted norm divides these suprema by $\gamma$. Set $Q_n=2^{n+1}\binom{n+4}{4}$. Then $\|(Z\cdot\kappa)\partial_sY\|_{[n],\gamma}\le Q_n^2\|h^{-1}\kappa\|_{[n]}\|Z\|_{[n]}\|Y\|_{[n+1],\gamma}$. The coefficient and $Z$ use the whole time interval. Substituting $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$ and the parent covector bound gives the $\lambda^{3/2}$ cost in (5.39); that parent estimate is not a conclusion here.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.summary: A fast derivative costs the scaled wave vector

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.text: For the product $(\mathbf d\cdot V)Y$, this version assigns the reciprocal amplitude to $V$, which is measured at order $n+1$. The second factor uses the full-slab unweighted order-$n$ norm. The theorem allows either choice of whether the half-Hölder part is included in the norms, and obtains the same $3Q_n^2L$ coframe cost.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.summary: Weighting the factor inside the divergence

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.text: Here the amplitude weight is assigned to $Y$, while the differentiated factor $V$ is measured in the unweighted order-$(n+1)$ norm. The estimate applies on the active interval with positive continuous $\gamma$, nonzero label width, and the supplied scaled-row bound. This placement is needed for mixed mean–oscillation interactions.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.summary: Weighting the factor outside the divergence

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.apply.text: An operator-valued twisted profile acts pointwise on a vector-valued profile with the same carrier. Each factor repeats under the same joint shift, so the result does too. This bilinear operation retains smoothness and phase periodicity and supports the concrete hierarchy’s coefficient multiplications.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.apply.summary: Apply compatible operator and vector profiles pointwise

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.apply.text: At a point $x$ of the profile slab, the pointwise application of an operator profile $A$ to a vector profile $f$ evaluates to the continuous linear map $A(x)$ applied to $f(x)$. This exposes the ordinary pointwise meaning of the bundled bilinear operation. The lemma is used to turn equalities of profile values into the Leibniz identities needed for the time norm.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.apply.summary: Evaluate an operator profile on a vector profile

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.apply.text: The underlying periodic output of pointwise application in the twisted space is the corresponding periodic application of the two underlying inputs. This definitional equality exposes the original operation. It lets the proof of a concrete equation ignore the additional lattice-symmetry wrapper without losing that certified property.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.apply.summary: The twisted product retains ordinary operator application

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: The coefficient-independent twisted phase average is the actual unit-period integral.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: The twisted average is the unit-period integral

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: The lattice-compatible correction has zero phase average. This supplies the completion law of the finite solver.

For the constructed hierarchy, the phase average of the source equals the three slow-product sums. The hypotheses identify the selected completion with the concrete curl completion, impose phase-independent geometric coefficients and zero-mean selected pressures, and require a surjective label map with the correct coframe. The result establishes the cancellations that the abstract assembly lemma previously assumed.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: The selected twisted hierarchy has the exact averaged source

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: If $C$ has zero phase average and $D$ agrees on the slab with a scalar time multiple of $C$, then $D$ also has zero average. The theorem uses this pointwise equality on the slab and does not demand differentiability of the scalar function. This handles the activation multiplier in the leading completion relay.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: A time multiplier preserves zero phase average

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: The abstract averaging operator evaluates to the ordinary one-period phase mean of the profile at fixed time and label. It identifies the algebraic hierarchy source split with the paper's averaging convention.
The concrete phase-average operator is idempotent. Taking a second full-period average therefore leaves the first average unchanged.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: Averaging a mean profile leaves it unchanged

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: A hierarchy average is a phase-independent, label-periodic mean profile.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: Averaging produces a periodic mean profile

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: All fields are smooth on $[0,T]$, periodic in phase and compatible with label translations; $\mathbf d=(D_aX)^{-T}\nabla_a$. If $Y$ has zero phase average and $B$ is independent of phase, then $\langle(Y\cdot\mathbf d)B\rangle_s=0$. The parent deformation coefficients are also phase independent. This removes one kind of mixed product when averaging $H_p$ in the proof of Theorem 5.6, leaving only interactions between two oscillations or two means.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: The mixed label interaction has zero phase average

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: Here the deformation coefficients in $\mathbf d=(D_aX)^{-T}\nabla_a$ are phase independent and all profiles are smooth and phase periodic on $[0,T]$. For a phase-independent $B$ and a zero-mean oscillation $Y$, the average of $(B\cdot\mathbf d)Y$ vanishes. Smoothness allows label differentiation to commute with phase averaging. Together with the reversed interaction, this supplies the mixed-product cancellation used after (5.42) to express the mean source using only the three displayed sums.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: The other mixed label interaction also averages to zero

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: The product of two phase-independent means under slow advection is phase independent.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: Slow advection of means is phase independent

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: Assume $G$ is independent of phase and the scalar pressure profile has zero phase mean at every time and label. Then its label-gradient profile $\mathbf d\mathsf p$ has zero phase average under the twisted operators. The derivative-of-average identity and coefficient independence are both needed; zero mean of pressure alone would not remove a phase-dependent coefficient.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: A phase-independent coframe preserves the pressure cancellation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: The phase average of a twisted vector profile is genuinely periodic in the labels at phase zero. A label translation changes the phase by the carrier pairing, but averaging over a full period removes that shift. This supplies an ordinary torus field for the mean solver, rather than merely a twisted field.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: Averaging removes the phase twist from the labels

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: The label-coordinate material relay preserves the unit-period phase mean zero.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: Material evolution preserves zero phase mean

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: The profiles are smooth on $[0,T]$, with phase period one; $\langle\cdot\rangle_s$ denotes integration over one phase period. The phase average of $(B\cdot\kappa)\partial_sY$ is zero whenever $B$ and $\kappa$ are phase independent and $Y$ is periodic. No zero-mean condition on $Y$ is needed for this identity. Applying it to each term of (5.28) proves that the supplementary source is admissible for the transverse equation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: The supplementary forcing has zero phase average

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: Let $V,Y$ be smooth profiles on $[0,T]$, one-periodic in phase with the coupled label translation law. Suppose $G,\kappa$ are independent of phase, $\kappa\ne0$, and a surjective $C^2$ map $A(t,\cdot)$ satisfies $G(t,A(t,x))=D_xA(t,x)$ and $\kappa(t,A(t,x))=D_xA(t,x)^Tk_*$. Set $\mathbf d=G^T\nabla_a$ and $C[V]=\mathbf d\times[-\partial_s^{-1}(\kappa\times V/|\kappa|^2)]$, where the primitive has zero phase mean. If $\langle V\rangle_s=0$ and $\kappa\cdot V=0$, then $\langle(C[V]\cdot\kappa)\partial_sY\rangle_s=\langle(\mathbf d\cdot V)Y\rangle_s$. This is (5.42) with $V=V_{i-1}$. The formal statement allows any such $Y$, independently of the expansion; no zero-mean condition on $Y$ is needed.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: Phase integration turns the correction into a label divergence

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: The full-period phase average preserves reflection parity.

Let the deformation and strain coefficients be phase independent, and let the preceding correction, pressure and subtracted activation term each have zero phase average. The preceding curl correction and oscillatory pressure have zero phase average, so their linear contribution to $H_p$ averages to zero. The activation term removed at level two also has zero average. This leaves the quadratic terms, together with the separately added parent residual at level two, as the forcing of the mean equation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: Linear corrections do not contribute to the mean source

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: Take smooth phase-periodic profiles on $[0,T]$, with phase-independent $G,M,\kappa\ne0$ induced by a surjective $C^2$ map $A$: $G\circ A=DA$, $\kappa\circ A=DA^Tk_*$. Write $\mathbf d=G^T\nabla_a$, $Y_i=V_i+C_i$, $Z_i=Y_i+B_i$. Assume every $V_i$ is transverse and has zero phase mean, every $B_i$ is phase independent, and $C_{i+1}=\mathbf d\times[-\partial_s^{-1}(\kappa\times V_i/|\kappa|^2)]$; a pair $V_i=C_{i+1}=0$ is also allowed. The pressure $\mathsf p_{p-1}$ and subtracted activation correction have zero phase mean. For $p\le P$, $H_p=(\partial_t+M)C_p+\mathbf d\mathsf p_{p-1}+\sum_{i+j=p}(Z_i\cdot\mathbf d)Z_j+\sum_{i+j=p+1,i\ge2}(C_i\cdot\kappa)\partial_sY_j$, minus the activation correction when $p=2$, satisfies $\langle H_p\rangle_s=\sum_{i+j=p}[\langle(Y_i\cdot\mathbf d)Y_j\rangle_s+\langle(\mathbf d\cdot V_i)Y_j\rangle_s+(B_i\cdot\mathbf d)B_j]$. Indices are positive. Thus $-\bar f_p$ equals this sum only for $p\ge3$; level two adds $R_U\circ X$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: Only slow quadratic interactions survive phase averaging

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text:
On a twisted profile every mixed jet is bounded on the slab, so any bounded time multiplier gives a genuine real-valued finite seminorm.

The interval is nondegenerate by the assumption $T>0$ and the chosen time set lies within it. The assumed bound on the weight $\tau$ bounds the weight, while profile smoothness and periodicity bound the sampled jets. An empty time set is allowed and gives a harmless zero seminorm.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: The finite seminorm with a bounded time weight

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text: The bundled seminorm evaluates to the exact finite mixed-word norm of the weighted slices. Its construction includes a bound on the time weight and requires the indexing times to lie inside the closed slab.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: The weighted seminorm equals the finite derivative norm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text: Phase averaging is contractive for the supremum-based finite mixed seminorm with any bounded weight depending only on time, on a time set $A$. Each constant derivative word commutes with averaging, and the norm of its phase integral is bounded by the corresponding supremum. The formal statement uses the supremum version of the norm, without the half-Hölder part; no Hölder contraction is claimed here.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: Phase averaging decreases each weighted finite norm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text: A pointwise bilinear product is bounded by the product of the factor seminorms when the product's weight equals $\tau_f\tau_g$ on the time set and all three multipliers are bounded. The explicit constant is the admissible-word count times $2^n$ times twice the bilinear-map norm. The result covers both supremum and optional half-Hölder measurements.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: Place a product’s time weight on its two factors

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text: For a centered profile, phase-independent coframe and covector, and nonzero covector, the weighted completion norm costs one extra mixed derivative and one inverse positive frequency. The theorem assumes the geometric curl-row and normalized-potential coefficient budgets. Its explicit constant contains admissible-word counts, powers of two, and $K^2$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: The completion gains one inverse frequency

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text: Let smooth profiles on $[0,T]$ be one-periodic in phase and compatible with $f(a+n,s+k_*\cdot n)=f(a,s)$. Fix $\ell_*\ne0$, a time subset $S\subset[0,T]$, and bounded scalar weights $r,q$ on $S$. Write $\|f\|_{[n],r}$ for the finite sum of suprema of scaled label and phase derivatives multiplied by $|r(t)|$; the weights are not differentiated. Set $\mathbf d=G^T\nabla_a$. Suppose each of the three coefficient rows of $\ell_*^{-1}G$ has unweighted order-$n$ norm at most $L$ on $[0,T]$. With $Q_n=2^{n+1}\binom{n+4}{4}$, the formal estimate is $\|(Z\cdot\mathbf d)Y\|_{[n],rq}\le3Q_n^2L\|Z\|_{[n],r}\|Y\|_{[n+1],q}$. The parent derivative bounds needed to turn $L$ into a power of $\mathsf D$ are separate.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: Control a product with one extra label derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text: The actual fixed-weight seminorm is monotone in derivative order.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: Weighted seminorms increase with derivative order

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text: If $A\subseteq B\subseteq[0,T]$, the seminorm on $A$ is at most the seminorm on $B$ with the same multiplier and derivative order. Boundedness of the multiplier is assumed on the larger set. The comparison restricts available samples and does not compare different weights.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: A smaller time set has no larger weighted norm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text: Assuming $h\ne0$, the order-$n$ norm of the fast advection $(Z\cdot\kappa)\partial_sY$ is bounded by two product constants, the unweighted norm of the scaled covector $h^{-1}\kappa$, the order-$n$ norm of the advector $Z$, and the weighted order-$(n+1)$ norm of $Y$. The bounded time weight $\tau$ lives on the time set $A$; only the differentiated profile carries it.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: Fast advection costs one mixed derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text: Let $f$ be a smooth twisted profile with zero phase mean at every slab time and label, $T>0$, $A\subseteq[0,T]$, and $|\tau|\le B$ on $A$. Then the weighted spatial seminorm $\sum_{|\beta|+j\le n}\sup_{t\in A,a,s}|\tau(t)\,\ell^{|\beta|}h^j\partial_a^\beta\partial_s^jF|$, without Hölder quotients, of the normalized phase primitive $F=\partial_s^{-1}f$ is at most twice the same seminorm of $f$. The weight is a time multiplier and is not differentiated.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: The normalized primitive costs at most a factor of two

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text: The order-$n$ seminorm of one scaled label derivative is bounded by the order-$(n+1)$ seminorm of the original profile, with the same bounded time weight. The statement allows the norm both with and without its half-Hölder part. Constant directions commute, so the extra derivative belongs to the enlarged finite family without differentiating the time weight.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: A scaled label derivative consumes one order

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text: The weighted seminorm through order $n$ of one scaled profile derivative ($\ell\partial_{a_1}$, $\ell\partial_{a_2}$, $\ell\partial_{a_3}$ or $h\partial_s$) of a profile $f$ is bounded by the original profile's weighted seminorm through order $n+1$. Here the seminorm is the finite profile norm with scales $\ell,h$ after multiplying by a time weight $\tau$ bounded on a subset $A$ of the time slab, with either choice of including Hölder quotients. The derivative acts only on label and phase variables, leaving the weight untouched.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: A scaled derivative spends one spatial order

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text: Let smooth profiles on $[0,T]$ be one-periodic in phase and compatible with $f(a+n,s+k_*\cdot n)=f(a,s)$. Fix $\ell_*\ne0$, a time subset $S\subset[0,T]$, and bounded scalar weights $r,q$ on $S$. Write $\|f\|_{[n],r}$ for the finite sum of suprema of scaled label and phase derivatives multiplied by $|r(t)|$; the weights are not differentiated. Set $\mathbf d=G^T\nabla_a$. Suppose each of the three coefficient rows of $\ell_*^{-1}G$ has unweighted order-$n$ norm at most $L$ on $[0,T]$. With $Q_n=2^{n+1}\binom{n+4}{4}$, the formal estimate is $\|(\mathbf d\cdot Z)Y\|_{[n],rq}\le3Q_n^2L\|Z\|_{[n+1],r}\|Y\|_{[n],q}$. The parent derivative bounds needed to turn $L$ into a power of $\mathsf D$ are separate. The statement also permits the corresponding norms with half-Hölder seminorms added.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: Control the other slow quadratic interaction

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text: If every full-slab scaled coframe-row norm is at most $L$ and $\ell\ne0$, the weighted order-$n$ divergence norm is bounded by $3Q_nL$ times the weighted order-$(n+1)$ norm of $V$. Here $Q_n$ is the finite product constant. The factor three counts spatial coordinates; the weight stays entirely on $V$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: The three coframe rows bound slow divergence

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text: If a profile $R$ evaluates to the raw relay of centered profiles $V$ and $F$, a common normalized coefficient budget bounds its weighted order-$n$ norm by the explicit order constant times $K^2\lambda^{-1}$ and their order-$(n+1)$ norms. The weight is only bounded in time; the frequency $\lambda>0$ and $\ell\ne0$ are explicit hypotheses.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: The linear relay gains one inverse frequency

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.compl.text:
The same periodic curl completion, restricted to the lattice-compatible profiles of the finite hierarchy.

The constructor requires T>0, phase independence of the covector and its nonvanishing on the slab. The returned twisted profile is built from a proved completion, not a default branch on failed hypotheses.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.compl.summary: The curl correction within the twisted profile space

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.compl.text: For a zero-phase-mean velocity $V$ and phase-independent coframe $G$ and covector $\kappa$, the bundled completion evaluates to the pulled-back curl of its relay potential. Covector nonvanishing is required to form the smooth potential. The result identifies the actual completion profile with the concrete curl expression used in finite-order estimates.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.compl.summary: The centered completion is the pulled-back curl

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.compl.text: For a twisted zero-mean odd input and even coframe and covector, the twisted completion remains odd under joint label-and-phase reflection. The covector is phase independent and nonzero on the slab. The result is inherited from the periodic completion; lattice compatibility and parity are separate properties retained by the wrapper.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.compl.summary: The lattice-compatible correction retains joint oddness

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.compl.text: For a positive slab, phase-independent nonzero covector profile and zero-mean velocity profile, computes curl completion at a closed-cell point from the supplied raw field. The result factors out the time scalar. Smoothness of the multiplied raw field and its equality to the profile on the cell are explicit hypotheses; unique differentiation justifies the spatial derivative at cell faces.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.compl.summary: The completion of a scalar multiple on the closed cell

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.compl.text: The wrapped curl completion preserves a time-only scalar factor on the whole label space. It uses only the profile identity at the given time.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.compl.summary: A time factor passes through the wrapped correction

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.compl.text: The periodic profile underlying the twisted completion is exactly the periodic completion of the underlying input. This is a definitional equality: the twisted constructor only adds the proof of lattice compatibility. Its assumptions include positive slab length, phase independence of the covector, and nonvanishing covector values on the slab.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.compl.summary: Forgetting the twist reveals the same periodic completion

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.compl.text: For a profile of zero phase mean, the twisted completion has the same underlying smooth profile as the original slow-curl completion. The comparison assumes a phase-independent, nonzero covector.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.compl.summary: The twisted correction agrees with the smooth correction

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.compl.text: With phase-independent inverse coframe and covector and a nonvanishing covector on the slab, completing the zero profile gives zero. The proof exposes the relay potential, whose zero input has zero potential and label derivative. This identifies the inactive or absent forcing case without choosing a nonzero correction.

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.concr.text: For a positive time slab and even coframe, material matrix and covector profiles, proves that the concrete hierarchy operators preserve odd velocity and even pressure submodules. The sign changes of label and phase derivatives are accounted for explicitly. This supplies only operator closure; parity of the selected analytic solves remains a separate requirement.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.concr.summary: Even coefficients preserve odd velocities and even pressures

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.const.text: For a selected finite construction with $P\ge1$, the velocity $V_{P+1}$ and mean $B_{P+1}$ beyond the retained depth vanish by the construction’s index rule. Consequently the measured last-index sizes of $Y_{P+1}$ and $Z_{P+1}$ equal the size of the final completion $C_{P+1}$, and the mean size is zero. The parent residual must be phase independent, as required by the finite hierarchy constructor.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.const.summary: The selected expansion has the required last-index values

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.const.text: For $2\le p\le P$, the selected relay has an inverse-frequency bound in terms of the measured oscillation and source at level $p-1$. At $p=2$, the transverse activation force is canceled exactly by the selected completion of the activation switch; later levels use the selected transverse source. The coefficient budget, normalized pressures, coefficient evolution, and switch identity are all explicit premises.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.const.summary: Each selected relay is controlled by the preceding level

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.const.text: Take a fixed depth $P\ge1$ and smooth profiles compatible with phase and label translations. The leading pressure must be even and the activation contribution odd. If the parent coefficients are even and the leading velocity and residual are odd, parity-preserving mean, transverse, and curl operations propagate the reflection law under $(a,s)\mapsto(-a,-s)$. Every velocity correction is odd and each pressure is even. The statement also gives parity of the total correction and remainder used in §5.5.1.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.const.summary: Odd velocities and even pressures persist in the recursion

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.const.text: For relay levels $2,\dots,P+1$, the exact constructed relay equals the analytic wave-relay formula using the preceding velocity and adjusted force. The theorem also proves that both relevant phase averages vanish. Its assumptions include phase-independent nonzero carrier geometry, the coframe and covector evolution laws, exact completion, activation compatibility, and zero pressure means. The final level is included although it lies beyond the solved transverse corrections.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.const.summary: Identify every selected relay including the final remainder term

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.const.text: Adds the hypothesis $0<\tau$ on the activation time to the strict-inactivity construction theorem and extends all its vanishing and remainder identities through the activation slice. The conclusion still leaves the slow mean-product tail, rather than forcing the entire residual to zero. All support and completion hypotheses remain tied to the selected finite recursion.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.const.summary: The support conclusion extends through positive activation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.const.text: For any activation parameter, propagates vanishing of oscillations, completions, oscillatory pressures and transverse sources on the strict inactive region. The tail equals the slow mean-product sum there. Closed envelope, positive slab, depth at least one, and preservation by the actual chosen transverse solve and completion are explicit hypotheses.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.const.summary: The twisted expansion has its exact inactive-region remainder

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.contD.text: For the supplied strain and evolving nonzero covector, a nonzero scalar frequency $\lambda$ gives joint smoothness of all four transverse coefficient formulas. The proof propagates covector nonvanishing from the underlying coefficient data and excludes zero squared norms before differentiating reciprocals. The result concerns coefficient regularity on the slab and does not supply any uniform derivative bound.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.contD.summary: The actual transverse coefficients are jointly smooth

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.contD.text: A twisted profile, evaluated at any time in the closed slab, is smooth in label and phase. The lattice condition is additional structure; it does not change this slice regularity statement.

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.deriv.text: For positive slab length, the actual periodic slab derivative restricts to twisted profiles. The translation law for the derivative proves its output lies in the same carrier space. The result is a profile of continuous linear maps on joint coordinates, preserving access to all time, label, and phase directions.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.deriv.summary: Differentiate while retaining the carrier twist

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.deriv.text: Taking the underlying periodic profile after differentiating in the twisted space yields the periodic derivative of the underlying input. This definitional identity shows that the carrier constraint adds proof structure only. It allows concrete formulas for the derivative within the slab to be reused directly.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.deriv.summary: The twisted derivative is the same periodic derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.direc.text: For $T>0$ and a fixed vector $v=(\tau,\alpha,\sigma)$ in the time, label and phase variables, this is the linear map on twisted profiles $f(t,a,s)$ on $[0,T]$ sending $f$ to $Df\cdot v$, the derivative of $f$ within $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ applied to $v$. The result is again a twisted profile.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.direc.summary: Differentiation of a profile along a fixed direction

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.direc.text: Let $T>0$, let $v$ be a fixed vector in the time, label and phase variables, and let $x$ be a point of the profile slab $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$. The bundled directional derivative of a twisted profile $f$ along $v$ evaluates at $x$ to the within-slab Fréchet derivative of the underlying function at $x$, applied to $v$. This is an evaluation identity on the slab only.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.direc.summary: Evaluating a directional derivative on the slab

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.direc.text: The derivative of the pointwise application $Af$ in a fixed direction is the derivative of $A$ applied to $f$ plus $A$ applied to the derivative of $f$. The slab duration is positive and the bundled profiles are smooth. The proof works with Fréchet derivatives within the slab, so the identity remains valid at the time endpoints.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.direc.summary: Directional derivatives obey the operator application rule

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.direc.text: Let $T>0$ and let $v,w$ be fixed vectors in the time, label and phase variables. For every twisted profile $f$ on $[0,T]$, differentiating along $w$ and then along $v$ gives the same profile as differentiating along $v$ and then along $w$, including at the times $0$ and $T$.

For a positive slab duration, any constant direction $v$, and a fixed continuous linear map $L$, differentiating the profile $Lf$ in direction $v$ equals applying $L$ to the differentiated profile. Smoothness is part of the profile space. The proof uses the chain rule for Fréchet derivatives within the slab and uniqueness of derivatives on the closed slab; it is not a statement about a time-dependent map $L$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.direc.summary: Directional differentiation commutes with a fixed linear map

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.diver.text: The graph evaluation of the finite hierarchy’s velocity is divergence free when every completed transverse solver output and every mean output has zero profile divergence. The theorem assumes those solver properties, the graph derivative, and the coframe and covector identities. It transports the abstract finite construction’s divergence result and does not itself establish the solver hypotheses.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.diver.summary: The finite constructed perturbation is divergence free on its graph

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.euler.text: For a jointly smooth periodic parent $U$ with label flow on a positive closed slab, take $B\ge1$, $C,D\ge0$, and the stated bounds on parent time derivatives and on material graph derivatives. When $i\le q$ and $i+m+1\le N$, the $i$th fixed-position time derivative of the graph of the profile belongs to spatial $C^{m,1/2}$ at every slab time. Its norm is bounded by $3(m+1)(1+2^{N+q}D)^iCB^{m+1+i}$. The additional spatial order supplies the half-Hölder seminorm, including at the time endpoints.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.euler.summary: One extra spatial order gives the Hölder graph bound

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.euler.text: For a smooth periodic parent $U$ with label flow $X$, this recurrence expresses the next fixed-position time derivative of the graph $F(t,x)=f(t,a,k\cdot a)$, $a=X(t,\cdot)^{-1}(x)$. It is the previous derivative of the graph of $\partial_tf$ minus $\sum_{l\le i}\binom il D_x\partial_t^{i-l}F\,[\partial_t^lU]$, a binomial sum of spatial derivatives of lower graph time derivatives applied to parent velocity time derivatives. The assumptions $T>0$ and $t\in[0,T]$ include the closed-slab endpoints.
