TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.euler.summary: Convert one further profile time derivative to Eulerian form

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.eval_.text: At any slab point, the joint derivative within the slab applied to $(0,0,1)$ equals the ordinary one-variable derivative of the phase slice. The entire phase line remains in the slab at its fixed time. Unlike the time-direction lemma, this statement does not need positive slab length.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.eval_.summary: The joint phase direction equals the ordinary phase derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.eval_.text: For positive slab length and a point in the slab, applying the joint derivative to $(1,0,0)$ equals the one-variable derivative within $[0,T]$ with label and phase fixed. The conclusion includes endpoint times. It is a within-interval derivative, not a global derivative across the zero extension.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.eval_.summary: The joint time direction equals the slab time derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.text: Given smooth label fields $B$ and $q$, spatial periodicity of both, and the mean momentum equation, the theorem packages them as a twisted mean output. Their exact values are preserved on the slab. Phase independence supplies the required twist automatically. The theorem assumes the analytic mean solution and does not enforce endpoint conditions itself.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.summary: A periodic physical mean enters the twisted hierarchy

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.text: On $0<T\le1$, constructs a mean result for a source fixed by the concrete average. The endpoint inverse supplies the raw fields. If coefficients are even and the forcing odd, reflection averaging selects compatible parity without increasing the label norm; otherwise the raw solution is retained and the conditional parity clause remains valid.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.summary: Solve and optionally symmetrize the actual mean equation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.text: Assume $0\le t_0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$, $\lambda=|\kappa(t_0,0)|\ge1$, smooth periodic $U$, both deformation and gradient bounds $\mathsf D$, velocity derivative bounds $R_n\mathsf D^j$, and a nonzero central seed with relative transverse growth at most $\mathsf D$ and normalized coupling at least $\mathsf D^{-1}$. For a small enough radius, $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$ and $\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|$, supported solutions satisfy $\|V\|_{[n],\gamma}\le C_n\mathsf D^{20}(\gamma(t_0)^{-1}\|V(t_0)\|_{[n]}+\|f\|_{[n],\gamma})$. If the centered forcing vanishes before activation, its zero-initial solution also satisfies $\|V\|_{[n],\gamma}+\lambda\|\mathsf p\|_{[n],\gamma}\le C_n\mathsf D^{20}\|f\|_{[n],\gamma}$. Profiles are smooth on $[0,T]$ and satisfy phase and coupled lattice periodicity; support lies within $2\ell_*$ of lattice points. The transverse stability assumption is $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for every transverse homogeneous solution $\mathbf b$ and $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.summary: One parent power controls all transverse derivative orders

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.text: Drops the two equalities identifying numerical bounds from the version of this existence theorem with explicit bounds and returns a parent-geometry record. All smoothness, periodicity, carrier nonvanishing, pressure differentiability and coercivity assumptions remain. This is an existence statement for the same construction, not a weaker analytic input requirement.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.summary: The parent geometry exists under the stated flow bounds

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.text: From a smooth periodic parent and its flow, constructs coframe, strain and transported-covector profiles with exact physical values. A nonzero carrier, inverse-flow bound, strain bound and pressure-Hessian-minus-residual-gradient inequality are explicit inputs. The resulting mean coefficient bounds equal the supplied $\mathsf D$ and $L$, preserving their quantitative provenance.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.summary: The actual parent flow supplies both solver coefficient systems

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.text: This consequence of the unit-duration construction retains the bounds needed on the actual active interval. The constants $K^{\rm rec}_n$ are selected before the parent data and do not depend on carrier frequency or retained hierarchy depth. The parent, flow, radius and derivative hypotheses remain required; the theorem supplies coefficient budgets rather than selecting a wave.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.summary: Choose the coefficient bounds for the actual transverse solve

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.text: From the given nonnegative parent derivative table, choose one nonnegative constant at every order. For every compatible parent with sufficiently small positive envelope and normalized launch carrier, explicit lift, pullback, pressure and generator bounds exist. Both the actual-duration and unit-duration solve coefficients are bounded by the same $K_nD^{20}$. This extra unit-duration estimate supports later uniform choices.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.summary: Choose coefficient budgets valid up to unit duration

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.text: Given a nonnegative table of parent derivative constants, the theorem chooses one exponent $A\ge30$. For every parent satisfying the displayed smoothness, flow, derivative and central-wave hypotheses with $\ell\le\mathsf D^{-A}$, the weighted forward estimate holds near each lattice copy of the envelope. The exponent is chosen before the parent, so it is uniform over this specified class.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.summary: Choose an envelope exponent for uniform forward stability

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.text: Given a positive slab with $T\le1$, a label flow, smooth periodic parent velocity and pressure, and oddness of both velocity and its momentum residual, constructs physical approximation data with the prescribed leading input $L$. The residual profile is the pullback of the actual parent residual. The theorem allows every natural depth $P$ and adds no independently selected forcing.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.summary: Use the actual parent residual in the hierarchy

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.text: Given a nonnegative parent derivative table, choose natural exponents $p$, $s_0$ and order constants before the parent data. For every permitted envelope exponent $s\ge s_0$, the actual selected mean satisfies a bound with loss $\mathsf D^{p+2+2s}$ and one additional source derivative. The phase scale is arbitrary because the source and mean are phase independent. The parent and mean coefficient compatibility hypotheses remain essential.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.summary: The selected mean loses one source derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.text: The theorem chooses an envelope exponent and order constants so every compatible physical hierarchy satisfies the transverse-solve recurrence with loss $\mathsf D^{20}$. The leading input must be inactive off the periodic envelope and before activation. The bound $T\le1$ is carried inside the physical approximation data, although it is not a separate visible parameter in the theorem.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.summary: The actual parent yields a uniform transverse level bound

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.text: The actual residual pulled back along the forward parent flow is an admissible mean source, with its value independent of phase.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.summary: The pulled-back parent residual is an admissible mean

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.text: Chooses fixed exponents and order-dependent constants before the parent and source. For a genuine periodic flow with the stated velocity jets, deformation bounds and coefficient identities, bounds the selected mean’s order-$n$ label norm by an order-$(n+1)$ source norm times a power of $\mathsf D$. The optional odd selection costs no additional constant.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.summary: The selected mean satisfies the finite label estimate

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.text: This combines the transported raw-derivative theorem with coefficient assembly. The output sequence $L$ depends on the parent derivative sequence $R$, while the parent flow, normalized frequency, time subset, and order are quantified afterward. Under the stated smoothness, deformation, normalization, and width assumptions it bounds every concrete relay coefficient by $L_n(1+|\ell^{-1}|)\mathsf D^{15}$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.summary: A genuine parent flow supplies the normalized relay budget

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.text: For a fixed nonnegative parent derivative sequence $R$, the theorem chooses $C$ before the parent, frequency, and time subset. Smooth periodic velocity, a genuine label flow, forward and inverse deformation bounds, and central frequency normalization then give the bundle of raw relay derivative bounds. Nonvanishing of the normalized covector is derived from the transported geometric bounds.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.summary: Transported parent fields supply the raw relay derivatives

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.text: Given a fixed nonnegative parent derivative sequence, this theorem chooses an order-constant sequence controlling the scaled transported covector. A smooth periodic parent flow with bounded deformation and central frequency normalization supplies the label jets. The resulting bound is $K_nD^2\mathrm{freq}^{3/2}$ under the prescribed phase width and label-width condition.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.summary: The transported covector has the required fast coefficient bound

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.text: The strain and nonzero covector are smooth and phase independent, with $\kappa_t=-M^T\kappa$; source profiles satisfy the phase period and the coupled label-translation law. For a smooth source with zero phase mean, this result constructs a transverse solution of (5.15) with zero initial velocity and normalized pressure. It also supplies the support and reflection properties required by the finite expansion. The statement proves existence with these properties; uniqueness among all solutions is established separately. The equation is $V_t+MV+\kappa\mathsf p_s=f$, with $\kappa\cdot V=0$, $\langle V\rangle_s=\langle\mathsf p\rangle_s=0$, and $V(0)=0$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.summary: A zero-mean source determines velocity and pressure

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.text: Given time order $q$ and nonnegative input cost sequences, this chooses an output sequence $C_n$ before the slab, scalar frequency $\lambda$, and fields. Assuming $\lambda\ne0$, $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge1$, nonnegative label width $\ell$, and $\ell\mathsf D^p\le1$, the three mixed bounds $|D^n\partial_t^i\cdot|\le C_nA\mathsf D^{pn}$ for the strain $M$, the normalized covector $\theta=\kappa/\lambda$, and $|\theta|^{-2}$ yield common amplitude $\mathsf D^{e_M+2e_\kappa+e_Q}$, with natural exponents. It bounds all four selected coefficient time seminorms and two explicit coefficient mixed bounds, for $-M+2P_\kappa M$ and $-2|\theta|^{-2}\theta^{T}M$. Covector nonvanishing comes separately from the supplied coefficient data.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.summary: Choose one old-parent bound for all transverse coefficients

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.text: Given a seed and its hierarchy regularity certificate, constructs velocity and pressure representatives on the whole parent slab with zero phase means. Their values equal the actual unswitched leading wave and pressure throughout the active interval only. The proof smoothly extends the amplitude and scalar pressure coefficient before multiplying by their fixed periodic phase profiles, preserving the zero means without asserting the wave equation outside the active interval.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.summary: Unswitched waves have smooth representatives with exact active values

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.text: From a nonnegative all-order sequence $C$, the theorem selects a sequence $L$ so that any bundle of raw parent derivative bounds satisfying $\mathsf D\ge1$ and $\ell\mathsf D^{16}\le1$ gives a common relay budget. The allowance is $L_n(1+|\ell^{-1}|)\mathsf D^{15}$. The chosen sequence precedes the coefficient functions and the time index.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.exist.summary: All relay coefficients share one finite allowance

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ext.text: Twisted profiles are equal once their values agree on the slab. The proof reduces to extensionality of their underlying smooth representatives.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ext.summary: Equality on the slab determines a twisted profile

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.fderi.text: For any lattice vector, the derivative within the slab of a twisted profile satisfies the same joint translation identity. Both its representative and the slab domain are invariant under that translation. The theorem concerns the actual within-domain derivative, including at boundary times, without assuming global smoothness of the zero extension.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.fderi.summary: The slab derivative keeps the carrier-dependent lattice period

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.freq_.text: Multiplying the output by the carrier before measuring its words bounds the carrier-weighted seminorm of the original output.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.freq_.summary: Frequency-weighted output bounds the pressure seminorm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.graph.text: For a profile $f(t,a,s)$ and an arbitrary label map $A(t,x)$, define $f^\natural(t,x)=f(t,A(t,x),k_*\cdot A(t,x))$. In §5.6 the map is $A=X_{t,0}$, the inverse parent flow. The supplied profiles are smooth on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, periodic in phase, and satisfy $f(t,a+n,s+k_*\cdot n)=f(t,a,s)$. They are assigned zero outside the time interval; this assignment does not assert smooth continuation through its endpoints. The definition alone does not make $f^\natural$ periodic: that also uses $A(t,x+n)=A(t,x)+n$. No phase average is taken in this evaluation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.graph.summary: Turn a label and phase profile into a physical field

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.graph.text: Reading a finite sum of twisted profiles on the physical graph equals the pointwise sum of their individual graph readings. The statement works for any normed target and any chosen inverse-label map. It is the linearity identity needed to split the constructed total pressure into separately estimated components.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.graph.summary: Physical graph evaluation commutes with finite sums

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.graph.text: For a phase-independent twisted profile, a bound on the actual unweighted seminorm gives graph jets retaining the input frequency exponent $\alpha$. The theorem requires the inverse-label scale and coframe estimates, positive frequency, and smooth chart, but no phase-width or carrier bound. The graph field is identified with the phase-zero mean composed with the inverse labels.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.graph.summary: The measured mean avoids the phase-frequency derivative cost

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.graph.text: A whole-slab unweighted seminorm bound gives graph jets with frequency exponent $3n/2+α$, under the same positive-scale, carrier, chart, and coframe assumptions as the weighted estimate. The proof uses unit amplitude weight on $[0,T]$. Thus no inverse amplitude weight is introduced for the depth remainder.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.graph.summary: The unweighted remainder has the full physical derivative cost

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.graph.text: A bound on the actual amplitude seminorm gives physical graph jets with restored factor $\gamma(t)$ and frequency exponent $3n/2+\alpha$. The theorem assumes positive coordinate scales, $\mathsf D,\lambda,L\ge1$, continuous positive weight, and the precise chart and coframe estimates. It assembles the seminorm-to-jet conversion with the physical chain rule, retaining explicit order and parent constants.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.graph.summary: A measured weighted profile gives explicit physical jet bounds

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.graph.text: A twisted profile with reflection multiplier $\pm1$ retains that same multiplier after evaluation on an odd inverse-label map. The assertion is pointwise in time and space. The profile’s joint reflection reverses both label and phase, matching the two changes caused by a spatial reflection of the inverse labels.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.graph.summary: The profile reflection sign survives graph evaluation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.hasDe.text: Let $T>0$, $t\in[0,T]$, $a\in\mathbb R^3$ and $s\in\mathbb R$. For a twisted profile $f$, the function $r\mapsto f(t,a,r)$ is differentiable at $s$, and its derivative there is the value at $(t,a,s)$ of the phase-derivative profile $\partial_sf$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.hasDe.summary: The phase operator is a genuine derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.hasDe.text: Under the same inactive-prefix hypothesis and positive activation time, every mixed spatial jet has time derivative zero within the full slab at activation. Smoothness provides a derivative, and uniqueness on the nondegenerate closed inactive prefix identifies its value with zero. This conclusion concerns one time derivative, not all time orders.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.hasDe.summary: The time derivative of each spatial jet also vanishes there

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.hasDe.text: For a twisted profile with complete target, the normalized phase mean has a within-time derivative equal to the phase mean of the profile’s time derivative. The assertion holds at every time of a positive-length closed slab. Joint continuity and genuine derivatives on the compact unit phase interval justify differentiation under the integral, including at temporal endpoints.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.hasDe.summary: Averaging in phase commutes with one time derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.hiera.text:
The Appendix D norm of the launch slice, with no amplitude weight.

The singleton launch time lies in the positive closed slab by its explicit membership argument. Smooth periodic profile slices ensure the actual finite derivative values are bounded.
A label coefficient controlled in the scaled coordinates controls all of its mixed words at the physical labels.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.hiera.summary: Scaled label derivatives control mixed coefficient words

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.inact.text: The differential operators for the actual twisted hierarchy satisfy the inactive-region laws used by the ordered recursion.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.inact.summary: Concrete operators preserve the inactive region

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.inact.text:
Twisted profiles vanishing at each inactive point form a submodule.

This is a subspace of profiles whose values vanish on the specified inactive region. It asserts value support, not by itself support of arbitrary derivatives across a nonsmooth boundary.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.inact.summary: Twisted profiles supported in the active region

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.inver.text: Assume $\mathsf D\ge1$, $\ell\ge0$, $\ell\mathsf D^7\le1$, smooth inverse-flow derivatives, and raw order-$j$ bounds $C(j)\mathsf D^{7j+1}$ with nonnegative costs. The actual inverse coframe then has unweighted order-$m$ norm at most the finite coefficient-order constant times $\mathsf D$. The phase width is arbitrary because this coefficient is independent of phase.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.inver.summary: A small label radius absorbs inverse-coframe derivative growth

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.inver.text:
Let $U$ be a smooth odd periodic velocity on $[0,T]$, $T>0$, with flow $X$. Suppose a smooth profile satisfies $f(t,-a,-s)=\sigma f(t,a,s)$. Then its physical evaluation satisfies $f^
atural(t,-x)=\sigma f^
atural(t,x)$ for every $t\in[0,T]$, where $f^
atural(t,x)=f(t,X_{t,0}x,k_*\cdot X_{t,0}x)$. The reason is that the inverse flow is odd. The formal assertion allows any real factor $\sigma$; the applications use $-1$ for velocity and $1$ for pressure. It transfers a supplied profile symmetry and does not establish the hierarchy’s symmetry by itself.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.inver.summary: The inverse parent flow preserves the profile reflection law

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.inver.text: The reciprocal of a positive continuous amplitude is bounded on every nonempty compact subset of the active interval.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.inver.summary: The reciprocal amplitude stays bounded on compact intervals

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.itera.text: At $t\in[0,T]$, iterating the time derivative within $[0,T]$ of a fixed mixed spatial word agrees with applying that word to the profile time derivative $\partial_t^jf$. The label and phase point $x$ stays fixed. The assumption $T>0$ and the smooth profile structure justify the derivative interpretation, including one-sided values at the endpoints; the theorem asserts equality, not a seminorm bound.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.itera.summary: Time jets are the fixed-coordinate derivatives

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.itera.text: For a smooth twisted profile $f$ with values in a complete normed space, $T>0$, a slab time $t\in[0,T]$, a label $a$, phase endpoints $c,d$ and any order $i$, the $i$th time derivative within $[0,T]$ of $r\mapsto\int_c^df(r,a,s)\,ds$ at $t$ equals $\int_c^d\partial_t^if(t,a,s)\,ds$. The integral is oriented, so $c>d$ is allowed, and $t$ may be an endpoint of the slab.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.itera.summary: Time derivatives pass through a fixed phase integral

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.itera.text: For a smooth twisted profile $f$ with values in a complete normed space, $T>0$, a slab time $t\in[0,T]$, a label $a$, a phase $s$ and any order $i$, the $i$th time derivative within $[0,T]$ of $r\mapsto\partial_s^{-1}f(r,a,\cdot)(s)$ equals $\partial_s^{-1}(\partial_t^if)(t,a,\cdot)(s)$. Here $\partial_s^{-1}g(s)=\int_0^sg-\int_0^1\int_0^qg\,dq$. No zero phase mean is assumed.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.itera.summary: Time derivatives pass through the normalized phase primitive

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.label.text: The slow advection uses the actual label derivative and the coframe.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.label.summary: Slow advection uses the coframe label derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.label.text: Let $\ell\ne0$. The slow label advection of $g$ by $z$, namely $(t,a,s)\mapsto D_ag(t,a,s)\,[G(t,a,s)z(t,a,s)]$, equals $\sum_{i=1}^3\big(\ell^{-1}[Gz]_i\big)\,(\ell\,\partial_{a_i}g)$, where $[\,\cdot\,]_i$ is the $i$th coordinate. Each scalar factor is the $i$th row of the inverse deformation $G$ scaled by $\ell^{-1}$ and applied to $z$; each vector factor is a scaled label derivative of $g$. The identity holds as an equality of profiles; $h$ is arbitrary.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.label.summary: Slow advection is the sum of three scaled products

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.label.text: Label advection has sign minus the product of the two profile signs.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.label.summary: Slow advection multiplies signs and reverses parity

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.label.text: The label pressure gradient reverses the reflection sign with an even coframe.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.label.summary: The slow pressure gradient reverses parity

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.map.text: A bounded linear map on the value space acts pointwise on twisted profiles and preserves their lattice translation identities. It also preserves the existing unit phase period and smoothness. The resulting linear operator changes values only by the specified bounded linear map, without altering the carrier or domain.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.map.summary: Linear images preserve the carrier-compatible translation law

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.map_e.text: At a point of the profile slab $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, applying a continuous linear map to a profile and then evaluating equals applying the map to the original profile value. The evaluation passes through the twisted, periodic, and smooth profile spaces in turn. Membership in the slab is retained explicitly because the underlying representatives are extended by zero outside it.

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.map_v.text: The underlying periodic profile of a linear image in the twisted space is the periodic linear image of the underlying profile. The equality is definitional. It confirms that preserving the carrier-dependent lattice condition introduces no additional transformation beyond the supplied bounded linear map.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.map_v.summary: The carrier-compatible linear image retains its formula

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.mater.text: For a real number $L$ and a nonnegative integer $N$, this defines the number $(3\cdot2^NL)^N\cdot4^N$. It is the prefactor used when spatial derivatives through order $N$ of a profile evaluated on a label graph are estimated; the definition itself places no condition on $L$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.mater.summary: A fixed-order factor for graph differentiation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.mater.text: Taking the active interval to be $[0,T]$ gives the equality between material completion plus pressure gradient and the four raw relay terms. The theorem retains the actual coefficient evolution and normalized-pressure premises. It proves equality for the supplied profiles; it does not select a solution of the transverse equation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.mater.summary: The material completion identity on the full slab

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.mater.text: This version derives both the velocity time equation and the normalized phase-pressure formula from the bundled momentum equation, transversality, and zero means. Together with coframe and covector evolution, they identify material completion plus pressure gradient with the explicit four-term slow relay on the full slab. The theorem therefore removes the separate pressure-formula premise of the earlier representation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.mater.summary: The momentum equation supplies the full relay representation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.mater.text: The actual relay evaluation is determined by the selected momentum equation and its normalized phase pressure.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.mater.summary: The momentum equation determines the relay identity

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.mater.text: With phase-independent coframe, strain, and covector, the material derivative of the centered completion plus the label pressure gradient equals the raw relay on $[t_0,T]$. Hypotheses supply coefficient evolution, zero velocity mean, nonvanishing covector, the velocity equation, and the chosen pressure formula. The strict inequality $t_0<T$ provides unique differentiation on the active interval.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.mater.summary: The active material derivative equals the four relay terms

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.mater.text: Assume both the velocity and the switch force are transverse and centered, and their momentum equation holds on the slab. Then subtracting the completion of the force from material completion plus pressure gradient leaves the homogeneous relay of $V$. The proof first derives the forced relay identity and then cancels the force’s own potential contribution.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.mater.summary: Subtracting the switch completion removes the activation force

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.mater.text: Evaluate the abstract hierarchy material operator as the within-time derivative of the profile plus the parent gradient applied to it. The identity holds on the time slab with positive duration.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.mater.summary: The material operator on a twisted profile

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.mater.text: The material derivative preserves the reflection sign with an even material matrix.

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.meanG.text: Defines $[3\,2^mL]^m4^m$, the explicit graph-derivative factor for a phase-independent profile. There is no oscillatory phase contribution, so this coefficient omits the extra factor two from the oscillatory version. It helps express the paper’s distinction between a frequency-dependent graph loss and the parent-only loss for means.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.meanG.summary: The derivative cost of a phase independent graph

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.meanO.text: If a nonnegative loss factor $L$ is at most $K\mathsf D^r$, the sixth power of that loss in the finite mean budget can be replaced by $K^6\mathsf D^{6r}$. The frequency is nonnegative and the profile constant is nonnegative. This numerical comparison exposes the fixed parent exponent while leaving depth in the finite level count.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.meanO.summary: Replace the mean loss by a fixed parent power

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.meanP.text: If every actual retained level from two through $P$ satisfies the order-two hierarchy bound, the sums of mean velocities and mean sources are each bounded by the number of levels times $CL^6\lambda^{-5/2}$, with $L$ the loss factor. The source includes the parent residual only at level two. Frequency and loss are at least one.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.meanP.summary: Sum the order-two mean and source estimates

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.meanS.text: If the concrete phase-average operator fixes $F$, evaluating at phase zero gives a smooth label field periodic on the lattice. Every other phase has the same value. This turns the algebraic mean-source hypothesis into an actual phase-independent forcing for the endpoint solver; it uses the concrete average, not an arbitrary projection.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.meanS.summary: An averaged source is a smooth periodic label field

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.meanS.text: Let $0<T\le1$ and let $S(t,a,s)$ be a twisted profile on $[0,T]$ equal to its own phase average. For every order $n$ and every $i\le q$, the unweighted label norm $\sum_{|\beta|\le n}\ell^{|\beta|}\sup_{t\in[0,T],a}|\partial_a^\beta\partial_t^iS(t,a,0)|$ is at most $q!\,T^{-q}\sum_{j=0}^q\frac{T^j}{j!}\|\partial_t^jS\|_{[n]}$, where $\|\cdot\|_{[n]}$ is the unweighted finite profile norm with scales $\ell,h$ and no Hölder part.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.meanS.summary: Each source time derivative is bounded by the factorial time norm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.mem_i.text: Unfolds the submodule membership condition into equality with zero on the strict inactive region. It applies to the underlying representative of a twisted profile. The equality is definitional and gives no derivative or support propagation by itself; those results use the closed envelope and profile smoothness separately.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.mem_i.summary: Inactive membership means vanishing at every inactive point

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.mem_r.text: Unfolds membership in the reflection submodule into the profile’s sign equation under simultaneous reflection. The equivalence is definitional and holds for every real sign. It provides the notation bridge between abstract submodule propagation and concrete parity statements for the nested twisted-profile representative.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.mem_r.summary: Submodule membership is exactly the reflection equation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.mixed.text: If a smooth profile vanishes throughout the earlier part of the slab and $0<t_0\le T$, every mixed spatial derivative word vanishes at activation. Earlier slices and all their spatial derivatives are zero, and continuity of the derivative profile gives the endpoint value. The strict positivity of $t_0$ is essential to the left-limit argument.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.mixed.summary: Every spatial derivative vanishes at a positive activation time

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.momen.text:
Let $U$ be smooth and periodic on $[0,T]$ with smooth inverse flow. Identify the hierarchy coefficients with $(D_aX)^{-1}$, $M=
abla U\circ X$ and $\kappa=(D_aX)^{-T}k_*$. Construct a depth-$P\ge2$ hierarchy whose phase-independent residual input is exactly $R_U\circ X$, where $R_U=U_t+U\cdot
abla U+
abla p$. Assume the leading momentum equation has the prescribed activation source. Then the momentum residual of $U+W^
atural,p+\mathsf P^
atural$ is precisely the evaluated hierarchy remainder plus the leading activation source and its curl completion. Spatial differentiability of $p$ is required at the evaluation point. This proves the cancellation in (5.46); no approximate change-of-coordinates error or uncancelled copy of $R_U$ remains.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.momen.summary: The finite hierarchy removes the actual parent momentum error

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.norm_.text: Assume phase-independent mean velocity and forcing have second-order profile bounds of size $C_{\rm mean}D^b\mathrm{freq}^{-5/2}$, with controlled inverse-label coefficients and parent gradient Hölder norm. If their physical graphs satisfy divergence-free linearized momentum, the graph pressure Hessian has the displayed norm bound with the same frequency decay. The equation and divergence condition are premises, not consequences of the norms.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.norm_.summary: Mean profile estimates imply a physical Hessian estimate

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.norm_.text: Assume each retained higher pressure vanishes on the hierarchy inactive region and the summed Hessian is bounded at every active time. A nonnegative bound then holds on the whole closed slab. Before activation the pressure sum is identically zero as a spatial function, so its Hessian vanishes without requiring a weighted estimate there.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.norm_.summary: Extend the higher-pressure bound to inactive times

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.norm_.text: Assume the solver selects genuine transverse results, the physical coefficient identities and first-order coefficient bounds hold, and the actual levels satisfy the order-one and order-two bounds. Then the Hessian norm of the sum of pressures at levels two through $P$ is bounded by the explicit prefactor times $\lambda^{-5/12}$. The active time also needs $\gamma(t)\le1$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.norm_.summary: The higher oscillatory Hessian gains five twelfths

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.norm_.text: For $T>0$, a jointly smooth periodic parent $U$ with label flow $X$, and $B\ge1$, $C,D\ge0$, assume $|D_x^m\partial_t^lU|\le DB^m$ for parent time orders $l<q$ and spatial orders $m\le N$. Assume $|D_x^m|\le CB^m$ for graph evaluations of the profile time derivatives of order $j\le q$ with $j+m\le N$. The $i$th fixed-position time derivatives of the graph have bound $(1+2^{N+q}D)^iCB^{m+i}$ when $i\le q$ and $i+m\le N$, throughout the closed slab. Each converted time derivative consumes at most one spatial order.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.norm_.summary: Eulerian time derivatives spend additional spatial orders

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.norm_.text: Let $T>0$ and let $f(t,a,s)$ be a twisted periodic profile on $[0,T]$ that does not depend on the phase $s$. Let $t\in[0,T]$, $\ell>0$, $\mathsf D\ge1$, a frequency $\Lambda>0$, $L\ge1$, $C\ge0$ and $\ell^{-1}\le\mathsf D^a$. Let $A(t,\cdot)$ be smooth with $B(A(t,x))=D_xA(t,x)$ for a smooth matrix field $B$ satisfying $\ell^m\|D^mB(x)\|\le L\mathsf D$ for all $m\le N$ and all $x$. Suppose that for every $i\le q$ and $m\le N$ the unweighted finite label norm of order $m$ (scale $\ell$, phase scale $h$, without Hölder part) of $\partial_t^if$ is at most $C\mathsf D^p\Lambda^\alpha$. Then for $j\le q$, $m\le N$ and every $x$, the function $x\mapsto\partial_t^jf(t,A(t,x),k\cdot A(t,x))$ satisfies $\|D_x^m(\cdot)(x)\|\le(3\cdot2^NL)^N4^N\,C\mathsf D^p\Lambda^\alpha\,(\mathsf D^{a+1})^m$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.norm_.summary: Time derivatives of a mean profile on the graph cost only the label scale

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.norm_.text: For a positive continuous weight $\gamma$, a profile bound in weighted time-derivative seminorms gives graph derivatives with amplitude $\gamma(t)\,\mathrm{freq}^{\alpha}$. Assuming phase width $h=\mathrm{freq}^{-1/2}$, carrier bound $\|k\|\le D\,\mathrm{freq}$, and the supplied readout-coefficient bounds, each spatial derivative costs $D^{\max(a,1)+1}\mathrm{freq}^{3/2}$. Orders satisfy $j\le q$ and $m\le N$; the estimate holds on the active interval.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.norm_.summary: Oscillatory graph derivatives retain the amplitude weight

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.norm_.text: At an active time $t$ and for an admissible derivative word, the norm of the unweighted mixed derivative is at most $\gamma(t)$ times the amplitude seminorm. Strict positivity of $\gamma$ allows its inverse to be canceled. This restores the actual size of a field from its normalized spatial measurements.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.norm_.summary: Recover a pointwise derivative with its amplitude factor

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.norm_.text: Fix $T>0$, a smooth profile $f(t,a,s)$, a spatial seminorm $N$, and integers $0\le i\le q$. Define $\mathcal J_q(f)=\sum_{r=0}^q(T^r/r!)N(\partial_t^r f)$, differentiating with label and phase fixed. The formal statement proves $N(\partial_t^i f)\le i!T^{-i}\mathcal J_q(f)$. It applies to any real seminorm, including the weighted and unweighted measurements used for oscillations and means. Positivity of $T$ is essential when dividing by its weight. The estimate itself imposes no frequency schedule and does not bound $T^{-i}$ by a parent-frequency power; that is a separate numerical step in the auxiliary argument.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.norm_.summary: A weighted sum controls each individual derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ofLab.text:
Embed a smooth periodic label field as a phase-independent profile.

The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ofLab.summary: Embedding a label field as a mean profile

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ofLab.text: On the slab, the phase-independent embedding evaluates to the supplied label field. Joint smoothness and spatial periodicity justify the embedding; phase is absent from the value formula.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ofLab.summary: The embedded label field has its original values

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ofLab.text: For a jointly smooth spatially periodic label field $f(t,a)$ on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3$, embedded as a profile that does not depend on phase (for any carrier $k$), assume $0<T\le1$, nonnegative scales $\ell,\mathsf D,A$ with $\ell\mathsf D^p\le1$, nonnegative constants $C(n)$, and a raw mixed bound for $f$ on $[0,T]$ through time order $q$ with slope $p$, amplitude $A$ and constants $C(n)$. Then its coefficient time norm $\sum_{i\le q}\frac{T^i}{i!}\|\partial_t^if\|_{[n]}$, with the unweighted finite profile norm, is at most $(q+1)W_n\big(\sum_{j\le n}C(j)\big)A$, where $W_n$ counts the multi-indices $(\alpha,j)$ with $|\alpha|+j\le n$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ofLab.summary: Periodic label coefficients satisfy the profile time estimate

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ofPha.text: A smooth coefficient that is phase independent and label periodic belongs to the twisted space for every carrier $k_*$. The phase shift becomes irrelevant by independence, and the label shift is removed by the label-periodicity hypothesis. Both hypotheses are needed: phase independence alone does not provide label periodicity.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ofPha.summary: Embed an ordinary periodic coefficient into the twisted space

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ofPha.text: The underlying periodic profile of the twisted embedding is the periodic embedding of the same phase-independent smooth profile. This equality is definitional. The label-periodicity proof certifies the extra twisted condition while all function values and existing phase-periodic structure remain unchanged.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ofPha.summary: Embedding a coefficient only adds its lattice certificate

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ofSmo.text:
A smooth function that is both phase-periodic and twisted-periodic defines a twisted profile when restricted to the time slab.

The constructor requires the smoothness and two periodicity proofs as arguments. It stores the zero extension outside the slab; agreement with the given function is asserted on the slab.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ofSmo.summary: Making a twisted profile from a smooth function

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ofSmo.text: A field smooth on the time-label slab and periodic in its label is made into a twisted profile that ignores the independent phase. The twist law follows from the given spatial periodicity. The constructor preserves the input on the slab and uses the smooth-profile zero-extension convention outside it; it does not provide a new ambient smooth extension.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ofSmo.summary: Bundle a phase-independent periodic coefficient profile

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ofSmo.text: At every $t\in[0,T]$, the profile built from smooth periodic label slices evaluates to the original coefficient $f(t,a)$, independently of the phase argument. The statement explicitly retains slab membership. Outside the slab the chosen representative is zero, so the construction's evaluation is not asserted equal to an unrestricted input there.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ofSmo.summary: Read the bundled coefficient on its time-label slab

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ofSmo.text: The constructor restricts a smooth phase-periodic and lattice-compatible function to the slab representation. Evaluating the resulting profile at a slab point gives the original value.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ofSmo.summary: The constructed twisted profile retains its slab values

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ofTwi.text: A phase-periodic profile whose on-slab slices satisfy the joint label-phase translation law $f(t,a+n,s+k_*\cdot n)=f(t,a,s)$ is placed in the twisted submodule. The underlying profile remains unchanged. The supplied hypothesis covers all lattice vectors, labels, phases, and slab times, so no additional periodic wrapping is performed.

The underlying periodic profile of the twisted profile built from $f$ and its translation law is exactly $f$. This definitional equality makes the geometric certification invisible to subsequent value calculations. It records that adding carrier-compatible lattice symmetry does not average, truncate, or otherwise alter the solver’s profile.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ofTwi.summary: The twisted wrapper keeps the periodic profile

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ofWra.text: A smooth profile with unit-periodic phase is multiplied by a radial envelope and extended through the centered lattice cell with the carrier-dependent phase shift. The inequalities $0<r$ and $2r<1/2$ keep support away from cell boundaries. The result is a smooth twisted profile on the slab.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ofWra.summary: Wrap a localized profile with the exact carrier phase

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ofWra.text: At an on-slab point $(t,a,s)$, the wrapped radial profile is exactly the envelope times the original profile evaluated at $(t,\bar a,s-k\cdot a+k\cdot\bar a)$, where $\bar a$ is the centered representative of $a$ and $k$ the carrier. The equality exposes both localization and the associated phase shift. It does not identify the result with the unwrapped profile at arbitrary labels; centering may change the label and phase.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ofWra.summary: Read the localized profile after carrier-compatible wrapping

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ofWra.text: If the unwrapped profile has a given reflection multiplier under simultaneous label and phase reversal, radial localization and carrier-twisted wrapping preserve that law. The positive-radius and cell-gap hypotheses control the boundaries of the centered extension. The theorem handles arbitrary real multipliers through a bounded linear scalar map.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ofWra.summary: Radial localization and wrapping preserve the joint symmetry

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.oscil.text: Defines the explicit order factor $[3\,2^m(2L)]^m4^m$ used when reading an oscillatory profile on the Eulerian graph. The extra factor two records both label and phase contributions. It is a numerical coefficient only; the graph estimates separately assume the profile and coframe derivative bounds to which it is applied.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.oscil.summary: The derivative cost of an oscillatory graph

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.paper.text: Let $T>0$ and let $f$ be a smooth profile with values in a real normed space, one-periodic in phase and obeying $f(t,a+n,s+k_*\cdot n)=f(t,a,s)$. At $t\in[0,T]$ let $A(t,\cdot)$ and $B$ be smooth with $B(A(t,x))=D_xA(t,x)$. Require $\ell_*>0$, $\mathsf D,L\ge1$, $\ell_*^{-1}\le\mathsf D^a$, and $\ell_*^j\|D^jB\|_\infty\le L\mathsf D$ for $j\le m+1$. Assume $f$ is phase independent. Put $f^\natural(t,x)=f(t,A(t,x),k_*\cdot A(t,x))$, $N_j=\|f\|_{[j]}$ and $K_j=[3\,2^jL]^j4^j\mathsf D^{(a+1)j}$. The formal statement bounds the sum over all ordered coordinate derivatives of length $m$ by $3^mK_m1N_m$, and gives $f^\natural(t)\in C^{m,1/2}$ with norm at most $3(m+1)K_{m+1}1N_{m+1}$. Here $N_j$ sums scaled label and phase derivative suprema through order $j$, each multi-index once. The explicit constants depend on $L$; they are not order-only constants.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.paper.summary: Phase independence removes the fast derivative factor on the full interval

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.paper.text: Let $T>0$ and let $f$ be a smooth profile with values in a real normed space, one-periodic in phase and obeying $f(t,a+n,s+k_*\cdot n)=f(t,a,s)$. At $t\in[t_0,T]$ let $A(t,\cdot)$ and $B$ be smooth with $B(A(t,x))=D_xA(t,x)$. Require $\ell_*>0$, $\mathsf D,L\ge1$, $\ell_*^{-1}\le\mathsf D^a$, and $\ell_*^j\|D^jB\|_\infty\le L\mathsf D$ for $j\le m+1$. Assume $f$ is phase independent. The weight $\gamma$ is continuous and positive on $[t_0,T]\subset[0,T]$. Put $f^\natural(t,x)=f(t,A(t,x),k_*\cdot A(t,x))$, $N_j=\|f\|_{[j],\gamma}$ and $K_j=[3\,2^jL]^j4^j\mathsf D^{(a+1)j}$. The formal statement bounds the sum over all ordered coordinate derivatives of length $m$ by $3^mK_m\gamma(t)N_m$, and gives $f^\natural(t)\in C^{m,1/2}$ with norm at most $3(m+1)K_{m+1}\gamma(t)N_{m+1}$. Here $N_j$ sums scaled label and phase derivative suprema through order $j$, each multi-index once. The explicit constants depend on $L$; they are not order-only constants.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.paper.summary: Retain the amplitude weight while using only label derivatives

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.paper.text: Let $T>0$ and let $f$ be a smooth profile with values in a real normed space, one-periodic in phase and obeying $f(t,a+n,s+k_*\cdot n)=f(t,a,s)$. At $t\in[0,T]$ let $A(t,\cdot)$ and $B$ be smooth with $B(A(t,x))=D_xA(t,x)$. Require $\ell_*>0$, $\mathsf D,L\ge1$, $\ell_*^{-1}\le\mathsf D^a$, and $\ell_*^j\|D^jB\|_\infty\le L\mathsf D$ for $j\le m+1$. Assume $\lambda\ge1$, $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$ and $|k_*|\le\mathsf D\lambda$. Put $f^\natural(t,x)=f(t,A(t,x),k_*\cdot A(t,x))$, $N_j=\|f\|_{[j]}$ and $K_j=[3\,2^j(2L)]^j4^j\mathsf D^{(\max(a,1)+1)j}\lambda^{3j/2}$. The formal statement bounds the sum over all ordered coordinate derivatives of length $m$ by $3^mK_m1N_m$, and gives $f^\natural(t)\in C^{m,1/2}$ with norm at most $3(m+1)K_{m+1}1N_{m+1}$. Here $N_j$ sums scaled label and phase derivative suprema through order $j$, each multi-index once. The explicit constants depend on $L$; they are not order-only constants.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.paper.summary: Each physical derivative carries the fast phase cost

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.paper.text: Let $T>0$ and let $f$ be a smooth profile with values in a real normed space, one-periodic in phase and obeying $f(t,a+n,s+k_*\cdot n)=f(t,a,s)$. At $t\in[t_0,T]$ let $A(t,\cdot)$ and $B$ be smooth with $B(A(t,x))=D_xA(t,x)$. Require $\ell_*>0$, $\mathsf D,L\ge1$, $\ell_*^{-1}\le\mathsf D^a$, and $\ell_*^j\|D^jB\|_\infty\le L\mathsf D$ for $j\le m+1$. Assume $\lambda\ge1$, $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$ and $|k_*|\le\mathsf D\lambda$. The weight $\gamma$ is continuous and positive on $[t_0,T]\subset[0,T]$. Put $f^\natural(t,x)=f(t,A(t,x),k_*\cdot A(t,x))$, $N_j=\|f\|_{[j],\gamma}$ and $K_j=[3\,2^j(2L)]^j4^j\mathsf D^{(\max(a,1)+1)j}\lambda^{3j/2}$. The formal statement bounds the sum over all ordered coordinate derivatives of length $m$ by $3^mK_m\gamma(t)N_m$, and gives $f^\natural(t)\in C^{m,1/2}$ with norm at most $3(m+1)K_{m+1}\gamma(t)N_{m+1}$. Here $N_j$ sums scaled label and phase derivative suprema through order $j$, each multi-index once. The explicit constants depend on $L$; they are not order-only constants.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.paper.summary: The weight survives composition with inverse labels

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.paper.text: Sums the order constants $C_j$ for all $j<m+2$, so the last included order is $m+1$. This is the table needed to turn a mean-profile derivative bound into an order-$m$ physical Hölder estimate, which spends one additional spatial derivative. The definition imposes no sign restrictions on the table.

Combines the phase-independent graph cost through order $m+1$, the retained-level count and the cumulative order table into the mean correction’s Hölder prefactor. Unlike the oscillatory case, the graph readout contributes no phase-frequency loss. The parent and frequency powers are specified by the applying estimate, not by this coefficient alone.

Combines the order-$(m+1)$ oscillatory graph cost, the number of retained levels and their common coefficient into the prefactor for the order-$m$ Hölder estimate. The factor $3(m+1)$ accounts for passing from derivative bounds to the chosen spatial norm. This definition contains no frequency or parent-scale powers; those appear separately in the theorem.

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: Fast advection is the phase derivative times the covector pairing.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: Fast advection is the covector pairing times phase derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: Assuming $T>0$, at a time in the closed slab the fast advection equals $\langle\kappa,Z\rangle$ times the derivative of the fixed-time slice of $Y$ in the phase direction $(0,1)$. The proof restricts the slab derivative to label and phase variables; it differentiates neither time nor the advecting factor.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: Fast advection differentiates the phase slice

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: Let $h\ne0$. The fast phase advection of $g$ by $z$, namely $(\kappa\cdot z)\,\partial_sg$, equals the product of the scalar profile $h^{-1}\,\kappa\cdot z$ with the scaled phase derivative $h\,\partial_sg$, as an equality of profiles. The label scale $\ell$ is arbitrary. The reciprocal phase width thus sits in the coefficient $h^{-1}\kappa$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: Fast advection retains the covector and phase derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: If the advected profile is phase independent, its phase derivative vanishes and so does fast advection by any vector profile. This does not require the advecting profile to be transverse.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: A phase-independent input has no fast advection

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: If the advecting profile is perpendicular to the covector at every slab point, its pairing in the fast-advection operator is zero. The advected profile may depend on phase.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: A transverse advecting field has no fast advection

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: Fast phase advection has sign minus the product of the profile signs.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: Fast advection multiplies signs and reverses parity

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: For $T>0$, this defines the linear phase-derivative operator on bundled twisted profiles $f(t,a,s)$: it differentiates along the fixed direction $(0,0,1)$, with time $t$ and label $a$ held fixed, giving $\partial_sf$. The phase coordinate ranges over all real numbers.
Let $T>0$, $t\in[0,T]$, $a\in\mathbb R^3$ and $s\in\mathbb R$. For a twisted profile $f$, the value of $\partial_sf$ at $(t,a,s)$ equals the ordinary derivative at $s$ of $r\mapsto f(t,a,r)$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: The phase operator is the ordinary phase derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: For a twisted pressure profile $q$ independent of phase on the slab, the fast gradient $\kappa\,\partial_sq$ of the concrete twisted hierarchy operators is zero. The proof lifts the periodic-space result through the twisted wrapper. It requires actual phase independence of the pressure and does not infer that property merely from lattice compatibility.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: A twisted mean pressure has no fast gradient

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: Evaluate the abstract fast pressure-gradient operator as the phase derivative of the scalar profile times the wave vector. This is the concrete phase part of the hierarchy gradient.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: The phase pressure gradient on a twisted profile

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: The fast pressure gradient reverses the reflection sign with an even transported wave vector.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: The fast pressure gradient reverses parity

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: A smooth comparison profile $f$ agreeing with a twisted profile on the entire centered cell transfers its scaled jet bound to that profile everywhere. The time lies in $[0,T]$, and both label and phase scales are nonzero. Twisted lattice translations transport derivatives to the cell; unique differentiability handles points on its boundary.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: Cellwise agreement transfers the scaled derivative estimate

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: If the phase average of the profile $v$ is the zero profile, then the scalar phase mean $\int_0^1v(t,a,s)\,ds$ of every slice at a slab time $t$ and label $a$ vanishes. The proof evaluates the bundled equality at phase zero and unfolds the averaging operator. Although the accompanying description says the two hold exactly together, the formal statement proves only this implication; its use here needs no converse.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: A zero profile average gives zero instantaneous phase means

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: Let $T>0$ and let the twisted profile $f$ have zero phase average $\int_0^1f(t,a,s)\,ds=0$ at every time $t\in[0,T]$ and label $a$. Then every bundled time derivative has the same zero phase average: $\int_0^1\partial_t^if(t,a,s)\,ds=0$ for all $i$, all $t\in[0,T]$ and all $a$, including both ends of the interval.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: Time derivatives preserve zero phase mean

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: For a transverse velocity satisfying the bundled momentum equation on all of $[0,T]$, the pressure equals the zero-mean phase primitive of the slope $(\kappa\cdot f-2\kappa\cdot MV)/|\kappa|^2$ whenever its phase mean is zero. The proof specializes the active-interval result to $t_0=0$. The evolution and nonvanishing of the covector are necessary premises, not consequences of the momentum identity alone.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: The full-slab pressure is the normalized primitive

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: On a nondegenerate active interval, covector evolution and $\kappa\cdot V=0$ imply the pressure-slope formula from the momentum equation. The zero phase mean then identifies the pressure $\mathsf p$ with its normalized phase primitive. Nonvanishing $\kappa$ justifies division by its squared norm; the hypothesis $t_0<T$ permits unique within-interval differentiation at the endpoints.

For $T>0$ and a smooth twisted profile $f$ with zero phase mean at every slab time and label, this is the smooth twisted profile whose value at $(t,a,s)$ is the normalized phase primitive $\int_0^sf(t,a,r)\,dr-\int_0^1\int_0^qf(t,a,r)\,dr\,dq$. Zero mean makes it one-periodic in phase, and it keeps the lattice twist $F(t,a+n,s+k\cdot n)=F(t,a,s)$ with the same carrier $k$ and slab.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: The centered profile has a normalized periodic primitive

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: Evaluating the bundled phase primitive profile at a slab time $t\in[0,T]$, label $a$ and phase $s$ gives the scalar-phase normalized primitive $\int_0^sf(t,a,r)\,dr-\int_0^1\int_0^qf(t,a,r)\,dr\,dq$ of the corresponding slice of $f$. The hypotheses $T>0$ and zero phase mean are retained from the constructor. This exact value formula is restricted to $t\in[0,T]$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: Read the periodic primitive at a point on the slab

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.physi.text: For a retained level $p$ with $2\le p\le P$, the concrete hierarchy with leading data vanishing on the inactive region satisfies the measured transverse-solve inequality. The hypotheses supply weighted forward stability, bounds on the coefficient derivative words, and a numerical majorant of the explicit combined velocity and pressure solve constant by $K_{\rm rec}L$. Support propagation supplies the corresponding inactivity of the actual source. Thus the estimate applies to the selected construction rather than an unrelated solution.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.physi.summary: The selected hierarchy inherits the transverse solve bound

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.physi.text: Instantiates the abstract support theorem with the physical mean, transverse and curl solvers. The coefficient records supply the necessary phase independence, nonvanishing and support-preservation properties. Positive activation extends vanishing to the launch slice; depth at least one and $0<T\le1$ remain required. The tail consists of slow mean products on that region.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.physi.summary: The physical solvers preserve support through positive activation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.physi.text: Assume $0<T\le1$, depth $P\ge1$, a closed support set, valid mean and transverse solution operators, and leading velocity, pressure and activation error vanishing on the indicated region. Before activation or outside the envelope, all transverse velocities, curl corrections, oscillatory pressures, and transverse sources vanish. There the remainder equals a sum of products $(B_i\cdot\mathbf d)B_j$. This proves the final support assertion of Proposition 5.4. The means may persist on that region because the endpoint problem selects their initial values globally in time.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.physi.summary: Only interactions between means remain outside the wave

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.physi.text: Combines the selected endpoint mean, the selected zero-start transverse solve and the concrete curl completion into the finite hierarchy solver record. The coefficients provide phase independence and nonvanishing needed for averaging and completion identities. This creates the operators used by the ordered recursion; it does not itself choose a depth or build a finished perturbation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.physi.summary: The finite expansion uses actual mean and transverse solves

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.physi.text: For a zero-mean forcing and a positive slab of duration at most one, the output of the physical transverse solver is the output of a selected transverse result, a solution record carrying its pressure-slope identity. The proof names the concrete selected result. This compatibility witness is needed because higher-pressure estimates use the pressure-slope identity carried by that result, not only an abstract output record.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.physi.summary: The physical solver returns its actual transverse solution

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.point.text: This bundles pointwise application of a continuous bilinear map $B$ as a bilinear map between twisted profile spaces, $(f,g)\mapsto B(f,g)$. It first maps the first profile into a profile of linear maps, then applies that operator profile pointwise to the second profile. Smoothness and the twist law follow from the existing profile operations; no estimate or inverse equation is supplied.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.point.summary: Apply a fixed bilinear map to two profiles

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.point.text: At any point $x$ in the profile slab, the pointwise bilinear product of $f$ and $g$ under $B$ has value $B(f(x),g(x))$. The statement only unwraps the profile construction. This evaluation identity is used to match a general continuous bilinear map to the concrete products and spatial norm estimates appearing in the hierarchy.

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.profi.text:
The concrete phase average closes the twisted space.

The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.profi.summary: Phase averaging within the twisted profile space

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.profi.text: The underlying periodic profile of the phase average in the twisted space equals the periodic phase average of the underlying input. This definitional equality keeps the actual integral formula available. The extra lattice compatibility is proved using translation invariance of a full-period phase integral.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.profi.summary: Read the same phase mean after adding the twist

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.profi.text: The concrete twisted completion gives the solenoidal input required by the theorem that the constructed velocity has zero divergence. The transverse-output equation alone supplies pointwise transversality via the skew-periodic probe.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.profi.summary: The completed transverse output has zero profile divergence

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.profi.text: This is the full-slab version of the potential-time identity, taking activation time zero. The hypotheses require the nonvanishing covector, its adjoint evolution, and the velocity’s momentum equation at every time in $[0,T]$. The result is a within-slab derivative at any chosen time, including either endpoint.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.profi.summary: The potential-time formula on the whole slab

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.profi.text: On $[t_0,T]$, a velocity satisfying the supplied transverse momentum equation has potential-time derivative given by the zero-mean phase primitive of the explicit potential time source built from $M$, $\kappa$, $V$ and the forcing. The covector must be nonzero and solve its adjoint evolution on the full slab. The pressure term disappears because its cross product with the covector vanishes. This theorem states a within-interval derivative, not an extension beyond the endpoints.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.profi.summary: The transverse equation differentiates the potential on the active interval

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ratio.text: A constant rescaling of the amplitude weight preserves forward stability.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ratio.summary: Constant amplitude rescaling preserves forward stability

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.rawMe.text: Let a mean solve on $[0,T]$ be given, with output mean profile $B$ and raw mean velocity $b_{\rm raw}(t,a)$, where $B(t,a,0)$ equals either $b_{\rm raw}(t,a)$ or its odd part $\tfrac12(b_{\rm raw}(t,a)-b_{\rm raw}(t,-a))$ on $[0,T]$. For $\ell\ge0$ and all $n,q$, the unweighted finite profile norm of order $n$ of $\partial_t^qB$ is at most $\sum_{|\beta|\le n}\ell^{|\beta|}\sup_{t\in[0,T],a}|\partial_a^\beta\partial_t^qb_{\rm raw}(t,a)|$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.rawMe.summary: The selected mean inherits each raw time-derivative bound

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.refle.text:
Reflection is an actual linear self-map on the twisted profile space.

The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.

A twisted profile with the required reflection multiplier at every slab point has the same law for its whole representative. Reflection preserves time, so the off-slab values on both sides are zero. The theorem is a representation lemma used before proving first-wave coefficient and velocity symmetries.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.refle.summary: Extend a twisted profile’s reflection law outside the slab

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.refle.text: Defines the real submodule of twisted profiles satisfying a specified sign under simultaneous label and phase reflection. Sign minus one describes odd velocity profiles, while sign one describes even pressures. The definition accepts any real sign, but the concrete Euler parity arguments use only these two values.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.refle.summary: Profiles with a fixed simultaneous reflection sign

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.refle.text: The equation reflection f = sign • f is equivalent to the pointwise reflection-parity predicate. The scalar sign is arbitrary here; odd and even applications use −1 and 1 respectively.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.refle.summary: Operator equality characterizes the reflection sign

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.refle.text: Evaluation of the reflection operator equals evaluation of the original profile at the point with label and phase negated. This is the value identity used in parity calculations.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.refle.summary: Reflected profiles evaluate at the reflected point

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.refle.text: The linear reflection map is an involution on twisted profiles. This is an algebraic property of the simultaneous label and phase reversal.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.refle.summary: Reflecting twice recovers the original profile

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.relay.text: For $T>0$, a profile $f$ with zero phase mean and a phase-independent profile of linear maps $c$, this is the twisted profile $\partial_s^{-1}(c\,f)$, the normalized phase primitive of the pointwise application. The coefficient may depend on time and label; its phase independence keeps the zero mean needed for the primitive.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.relay.summary: Apply a coefficient before taking the normalized phase primitive

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.relay.text: At any slab time $t\in[0,T]$ and label $a$, evaluates the bundled relay primitive as the normalized primitive, at phase $s$, of $\sigma\mapsto c(t,a,0)\,f(t,a,\sigma)$: the coefficient at phase zero applied to the phase slice of $f$. Phase independence of $c$ makes that zero-phase coefficient equal to the coefficient at every phase. This is a value identity.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.relay.summary: Read the relay primitive using the coefficient at phase zero

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.relay.text: For $T>0$, scales $\ell,h$, a coordinate $i\in\{1,2,3\}$, a profile $f$ with zero phase mean, a phase-independent coefficient $c$ and an operator-valued profile $R$, the relay term is $R\big(\ell\,\partial_{a_i}\partial_s^{-1}[c\,f]\big)$: apply $c$, take the normalized phase primitive, take one scaled label derivative, then apply $R$. The row $R$ need not be phase-independent; the result is again a twisted profile on the same slab.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.relay.summary: One coefficient row after a differentiated phase primitive

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.relay.text: Evaluates the relay term as the row applied to a scaled label derivative of the normalized primitive, with the inner coefficient read at phase zero. The identity holds at every time on the slab and every label-phase point. It exposes exactly which derivative acts on the primitive and its inner coefficient, before time or spatial norm estimates are applied.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.relay.summary: Read one relay term as a weighted coordinate derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.remai.text: Assumes the finite remainder and completion-switch term are odd and uses the leading momentum equation to identify the leading switch term. Even material and covector coefficients turn the odd leading velocity and even pressure into another odd term. Adding them preserves reflection parity of the complete profile residual.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.remai.summary: The switch error preserves the odd residual

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.restr.text: A linear operation $L$ on periodic profiles restricts to twisted profiles when it is proved that every twisted input produces all required lattice translation identities. The operation’s underlying values do not change. This separates a concrete operator formula from the extra proof that it respects the carrier geometry.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.restr.summary: Restrict an operator to the carrier-compatible space

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.restr.text: This restricts a bilinear map $L$ on periodic profiles to inputs and outputs with the same carrier-dependent lattice symmetry. The supplied closure proof covers both arguments jointly. Linearity in each argument is retained, allowing concrete advection and pointwise operator multiplication in the twisted hierarchy.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.restr.summary: Preserve the common twist in a bilinear operation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.restr.text: The underlying periodic profile of the restricted bilinear output is $L(f,g)$ applied to the underlying periodic profiles of $f$ and $g$. This is a definitional equality, confirming that both arguments and the result are merely being regarded in a smaller certified space. It transfers concrete bilinear evaluation formulas without additional analytic assumptions.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.restr.summary: Read the bilinear operation before the twisted wrapper

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.restr.text: The underlying periodic output of a restricted linear map is exactly $L$ applied to the underlying periodic input. This definitional identity removes the twisted wrapper in computations. The accompanying closure proof changes the certified function space but does not change any value of the operation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.restr.summary: The carrier restriction leaves the linear operation unchanged

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.text: This definition turns the $i$th row of the inverse coframe $G$ into a scalar-valued linear-map profile and multiplies it by $\ell^{-1}$. Pairing it with an $\ell$-scaled label derivative recovers an unscaled physical derivative. The definition preserves the twisted-profile structure through a fixed continuous linear map.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.summary: An inverse-coframe row divided by the label width

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.text: At a point of the closed time slab, the bundled coefficient applied to a vector $v$ is $\ell^{-1}(Gv)_i$. Unfolding the fixed linear map proves the identity. Neither invertibility of $G$ nor nonzero $\ell$ is needed for this evaluation formula; those conditions belong to later estimates.

An exact phase-independent profile representation of a smooth coframe field transfers its mixed bound to each scaled coframe row. The output factorial time norm at spatial order $n$ is at most the label-time conversion cost times $\ell^{-1}A$. The hypotheses include $0<T\le1$, nonnegative scales and costs, and $\ell\mathsf D^p\le1$; no derivative order is spent on a time derivative.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.summary: A scaled coframe row costs one inverse label width

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.text: The fixed-time derivative of $V$ is evaluated in the $i$th label direction scaled by $\ell$, giving another twisted profile. The phase-width parameter $h$ is present in the common mixed-direction notation, but this coordinate uses the label branch. The hypothesis $T>0$ supports the slab derivative construction.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.summary: One label derivative with its width included

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.text: For $t\in[0,T]$, the value of the scaled derivative profile is the directional derivative of $V(t,\cdot)$ in the corresponding mixed label direction. The theorem unfolds the profile derivative and fixed evaluation map. It justifies applying ordinary fixed-time product estimates to the bundled hierarchy operation.

This profile sends a vector to its inner product with $\kappa/h$. The map is applied to the bundled smooth twisted profile, so its periodicity and slab interpretation are retained. It isolates the coefficient measured separately from the advector and differentiated profile in the fast-advection estimate.

At a time $t\in[0,T]$, evaluation of the bundled scaled coefficient is exactly $h^{-1}\langle\kappa(t,a,s),\cdot\rangle$. The equality unfolds the successive smooth and periodic profile wrappers. It imposes no nonzero-width assumption, so it remains an evaluation identity when $h=0$.

Let $0<T\le1$, $\ell,\mathsf D,A\ge0$ with $\ell\mathsf D^p\le1$, $\lambda>0$, $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, $C(n)\ge0$. Let $\kappa$ be a profile with $\kappa(t,a,s)=f(t,a)$ on $[0,T]$, and assume $\lambda^{-1}f$ satisfies the mixed bounds on $[0,T]$ through time order $q$ with slope $p$, amplitude $A$ and constants $C(n)$. Then the profile $(t,a,s)\mapsto h^{-1}\langle\kappa(t,a,s),\cdot\rangle$ satisfies $\sum_{i=0}^q\frac{T^i}{i!}\|\partial_t^i(\cdot)\|_{[n]}\le(q+1)W_n\Big(\sum_{j=0}^nC(j)\Big)A\,\lambda^{3/2}$, with the unweighted finite profile norm on $[0,T]$ and $W_n$ the number of multi-indices $(\alpha,j)$ in the three label directions and the phase with $|\alpha|+j\le n$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.summary: The fast coefficient retains its explicit frequency loss

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.text: For a phase-independent twisted profile, the unweighted seminorm at any phase scale controls the scaled jets of its phase-zero label field with phase scale one. The equality follows because changing the phase has no effect on values. The time must lie in a positive-length slab; no extra carrier-frequency factor is introduced.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.summary: A mean profile uses unit phase scale without changing its budget

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.text: At any time in a positive-length slab, the actual unweighted mixed-word seminorm bounds scaled slice jets with factor $4^n$. No separate bounded-supremum hypothesis is needed: smoothness, twisted periodicity, and the compact time slab provide it. The seminorm is taken without Hölder quotients, so it is the finite supremum norm.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.summary: The actual unweighted seminorm controls every scaled slice jet

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.text: On an active interval $[t_0,T]$ inside the slab, a continuous strictly positive amplitude weight gives slice jets bounded by $\gamma(t)4^n$ times the amplitude seminorm. Compactness bounds the reciprocal weight, ensuring the real suprema are meaningful. Only label and phase derivatives are taken, so no time derivatives of the weight enter.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.summary: The actual amplitude seminorm recovers the weight on each slice

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.text: For $T>0$, scales $\ell,h$ and an index among four, this is the linear operator on smooth twisted profiles $f(t,a,s)$ taking the derivative in one constant direction of the profile variables: $\ell\partial_{a_1}$, $\ell\partial_{a_2}$, $\ell\partial_{a_3}$, or the phase derivative $h\partial_s$. The time component of the direction is zero; it is neither a time derivative nor a derivative along the flow.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.summary: One scaled label or phase derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.text: Let $T>0$, $t\in[0,T]$ and $f$ a smooth twisted profile. At $(t,a,s)$ the scaled derivative of $f$ in one of the directions $\ell e_1,\ell e_2,\ell e_3$ (label) or $he_s$ (phase) equals the ordinary directional derivative in that direction of the fixed-time slice $(a,s)\mapsto f(t,a,s)$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.summary: Reading a scaled derivative on a fixed time slice

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.text: At an active time with positive continuous weight and $\gamma(t)\le1$, the scaled fixed-time profile has an order-$n$ jet bound given by $4^n$ times its amplitude seminorm. This converts the hierarchy derivative-word norm into ordinary Fréchet derivative bounds. The weight cap is required to pass from the weighted estimate to the unweighted slice.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.summary: Convert the weighted profile norm into a slice jet bound

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.selec.text: For $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge1$ and $\ell_*>0$, consider the selected mean $B=D_aXv$ with a phase-independent source. Assume its endpoint inverse estimates, spatial coefficient bounds through order $n$, and half-Hölder bounds for time derivatives of $K,\Omega,D_aX$ through order $q$. The source and $(D_aX)^T$ are needed only through order $\max(q-1,0)$. The formal statement bounds the unweighted $\mathcal J_q(B)$ by an explicit nonnegative expression in those bounds, $\mathsf D$, the inverse exponent, $n$ and $q$, linear in the source bound. Thus, for $q\ge1$, the source is differentiated once less than the mean. At $q=0$ the source order is zero, not minus one.
