The endpoint-inverse data are inverses, of norm at most $\mathsf D^p$, of the fixed-time and mixed projected coefficient maps, with coercivity $\mathsf D^{-2}$ for $K$ and $1/(2\mathsf D^2(1+L)^2)$ for the mixed coefficient, where $L$ bounds $|M|$; the spatial seminorm is $\|f\|_{[n]}=\sum_{|\alpha|+j\le n}\ell_*^{|\alpha|}h^j\sup_{[0,T],a,s}|\partial_a^\alpha\partial_s^jf|$, with each multi-index counted once.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.selec.summary: The selected mean gains one source derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.selec.text: For a mean solve on $[0,T]$ with $T\le1$, a nonnegative label scale $\ell$ and a nonnegative bound $C$, suppose every raw mean time derivative through order $q$ has label norm $\sum_{|\beta|\le n}\ell^{|\beta|}\sup_{t,a}|\partial_a^\beta\partial_t^ib_{\rm raw}(t,a)|\le C$ for all $i\le q$. Then the factorially weighted time norm $\sum_{i=0}^q\frac{T^i}{i!}\|\partial_t^iB\|_{[n]}$ of the hierarchy's selected mean $B$, with the unweighted profile norm of order $n$, is at most $(q+1)C$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.selec.summary: Raw mean bounds control the factorial time norm of the selected mean

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.slice.text: This function reads the actual values of a twisted hierarchy profile at time $t$, retaining label and phase as free arguments. It only fixes time. Smoothness of the resulting slice is proved when $t$ belongs to the slab; outside it the underlying profile convention gives zero values.

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.slowL.text: This definition forms the slow divergence $\mathbf d\cdot V$ of $V$ using the coframe $G$, then equips it with phase periodicity and lattice-twisted periodicity. The derivative acts in label variables only. The construction preserves the actual divergence values on the slab and is used inside the averaged completion source.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.slowL.summary: The label divergence as a twisted scalar profile

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.slowL.text:
The slow divergence times a second vector profile in the averaged completion source.

The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.slowL.summary: Slow divergence multiplied by a second vector profile

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.slowL.text: The bundled product evaluates to the slow label divergence of V multiplied by Y. It is the term obtained when phase integration by parts removes a fast derivative from the averaged source.

Let $\ell\ne0$. The product of the slow divergence $\operatorname{tr}(D_aV\circ G)$ with the vector profile $Y$ equals $\big(\sum_{i=1}^3\ell^{-1}[G(\ell\,\partial_{a_i}V)]_i\big)\,Y$, where $[\,\cdot\,]_i$ is the $i$th coordinate. Thus each term is a scaled row of $G$ applied to a scaled label derivative of $V$; the extra label derivative falls on $V$ and not on $Y$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.slowL.summary: Slow divergence differentiates the first factor

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.slowL.text: At a slab point, slow label divergence is the sum of the three coordinate components of the derivative of $V$, evaluated along $G$ applied to each standard basis vector. This is the coordinate contraction representing the divergence in label coordinates. The theorem identifies values; no bound on the coframe is assumed.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.slowL.summary: Evaluate divergence in the three coframe directions

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.slowL.text: The equivalent trace contraction by rows puts the label derivative in a fixed coordinate direction before applying the coframe.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.slowL.summary: Slow divergence written as coordinate row contractions

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.slowL.text: When $\ell\ne0$, slow label divergence equals the sum of the three scaled coframe rows applied to the corresponding scaled label derivatives. Each factor of $\ell$ cancels its inverse. The proof rewrites the trace coordinate by coordinate and uses the derivative of the fixed-time label–phase slice.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.slowL.summary: Slow divergence is a sum of three contractions

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.slowL.text: The underlying smooth profile of the twisted slow divergence of $V$ is exactly the concrete slow divergence $\mathbf d\cdot V$ built from $G$. The theorem is a definitional equality after forgetting the two periodicity wrappers. It lets derivative and averaging lemmas use the actual divergence rather than reason through the extra structure.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.slowL.summary: Forgetting periodic structure recovers the slow divergence

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.solve.text: Chooses one mean result, whose existence the preceding theorem proves, for the same coefficients and mean source. The chosen result includes the endpoint, normalization, recovery and conditional symmetry certificates. Subsequent estimates refer to this exact selected result, rather than to another mean solution that happens to satisfy the equation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.solve.summary: Select a certified physical endpoint mean

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.solve.text: Assume smooth phase-independent strain and nonzero covector with $\kappa_t=-M^T\kappa$, and smooth source profiles on $[0,T]$ compatible with phase and label translations. This is the solution of (5.15) used at each level of the expansion: its velocity starts from zero and its pressure has zero phase mean. It is selected from the proved existence result for a smooth source with zero phase mean. Its equations and support properties therefore accompany the selected fields. The equation is $V_t+MV+\kappa\mathsf p_s=f$, with $\kappa\cdot V=0$, $\langle V\rangle_s=\langle\mathsf p\rangle_s=0$, and $V(0)=0$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.solve.summary: Each forcing is assigned its transverse solution

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.spati.text: For a phase-independent profile, smooth inverse-label map and controlled coframe jets through order two, its physical graph has first-order half-Hölder norm at most $13824Q^2$ times the second-order unweighted profile seminorm. The scale condition $\ell^{-1}C\le Q$ accounts for physical derivatives. No carrier-frequency loss appears because the profile has no phase dependence.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.spati.summary: Convert a label mean bound into a physical Hölder bound

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.spati.text: For a jointly smooth periodic parent with label flow, every fixed-position time jet of a twisted profile evaluated on the inverse-flow graph is spatially periodic on the closed slab. The proof first uses the twisted periodicity law to obtain periodicity of the graph and then differentiates equal time slices. It does not require separate periodicity assumptions on each jet.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.spati.summary: Eulerian time derivatives of the graph stay periodic

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.spati.text: If the label map commutes with integer translations by the same translation, evaluating a twisted profile on its phase graph gives a spatially periodic field. The statement uses the twist relation to cancel the phase shift.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.spati.summary: Twisted periodicity gives periodic graph values

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.spati.text: Actual inverse parent labels supply the affine lattice shift.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.spati.summary: Inverse parent labels give the required lattice shift

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.text: The cost multiplies the number of admissible derivative words of length $n$ by $2^n$ and twice the operator norm of continuous linear evaluation $(x,A)\mapsto Ax$. It depends on spatial order $n$ and the source and target spaces. This explicit constant is carried unchanged into the factorial time product estimate; it is not a uniform bound over all spatial orders.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.summary: The spatial cost of coefficient application

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.text: For every natural spatial order $n$ and any normed source and target spaces, the cost of applying a matrix coefficient to a profile is nonnegative. That cost is the number of nondecreasing derivative words of length at most $n$ in four directions, times $2^n$, times twice the operator norm of the evaluation map $(B,v)\mapsto Bv$. The proof uses the sign of this finite count, the power of two and the operator norm. This is the sign needed when replacing coefficient norms by larger bounds in the transverse time recurrence.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.summary: The coefficient application cost is nonnegative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.text: Let $\lambda>0$, let $K$ and $P$ be nonnegative integers with $P=6K$, and put $\lambda_+=\lambda^K$. The formal statement rewrites the expansion's remainder factor as $\lambda^{-5/4}\lambda_+^{-4}$; its exponent before rewriting is $-5/4-2P/3$. This is precisely the arithmetic used in auxiliary equation (2.5) to obtain the next-frequency decay. No bound for a residual or profile is assumed or proved here. Such an analytic bound must already contain the stated remainder factor. All fractional and negative exponents in this identity are real powers of positive numbers.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.summary: The chosen depth yields the next-frequency power

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.text: If the parent derivative cap satisfies $D\le C\mu^A$, with $\mu\ge1$, nonnegative $C,D$, and $i\le q$, the conversion factor $(1+2^{N+q}D)^i$ is at most $(1+2^{N+q}C)^q\mu^{Aq}$. This scalar inequality makes its parent-frequency exponent independent of spatial order $N$, although the finite coefficient still depends on $N$ and $q$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.summary: Eulerian time conversion costs a fixed parent power

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.text: For a continuous bilinear map $B$ and an order $n$, this is the number $W_n\,2^n\,(2\|B\|)$, where $W_n$ is the number of multi-indices $(\alpha,j)$ in the three label directions and the phase with $|\alpha|+j\le n$. No time order appears in the formula.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.summary: The spatial product constant in the time norm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.text: Assume the profile equation $\partial_tV=AV+BF$ and that the factorially weighted time norms of the coefficients $A,B$ through order $q$ are at most a nonnegative $C$. Then the amplitude-weighted time norm of the velocity $V$ through order $q$ is bounded by $(1+T K_n C)^q$ times the sum of its undifferentiated weighted norm and the time norm of the source $F$, where $K_n$ is the spatial application cost at order $n$. The undifferentiated velocity norm remains an input. Thus this theorem extends a base estimate; it does not prove the inverse estimate from the differential equation alone.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.summary: Inductively control time derivatives of the projected velocity

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.text: Any real seminorm of a finite sum is at most the sum of the seminorms of its terms. The private helper works in an arbitrary real module and requires no profile or smoothness structure. It is the algebraic triangle inequality used before estimating each binomial term in the time-differentiated product.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.summary: A seminorm bounds a finite sum term by term

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.text: For positive $T$, the next factorial weight $T^{i+1}/(i+1)!$ is at most $T$ times its predecessor $T^i/i!$. The exact relation includes division by $i+1$, which can only reduce the nonnegative value. This inequality converts the positive-order terms of a time seminorm into a shorter seminorm of the first time derivative.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.summary: The next time weight costs one slab factor

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.text: Let $\lambda>0$, let $a$ be a nonnegative integer, and assume $\mathsf D^{\max(a,1)+1}\le\lambda^{1/2}$. Then the formal statement proves $\mathsf D^{\max(a,1)+1}\lambda^{3/2}\le\lambda^2$. It is a numerical implication, valid without constructing a profile. In the auxiliary argument, $\lambda^{3/2}$ is the cost of a phase derivative after physical evaluation, and the factor involving $\mathsf D$ comes from the label derivatives. The frequency schedule is needed separately to establish the hypothesis at sufficiently late stages. The declaration gives no estimate for a phase-independent mean or for the derivatives of the parent velocity.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.summary: A parent-scale bound absorbs the phase cost

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.text: With $0\le t_0\le T$, positive $T$, and an amplitude $\gamma$ continuous and positive on the active interval $[t_0,T]$, the weighted norm of the pointwise product $Af$ is bounded by the spatial application cost times the unweighted norm of the coefficient $A$ and the weighted norm of the field $f$. The reciprocal amplitude belongs only to the operand side. The proof bounds it on the compact active interval before using the product estimate.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.summary: A coefficient acts on an amplitude-weighted profile

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.text: The factorially weighted time norm of the pointwise product $Af$ satisfies the same application estimate as its spatial norm. Time derivatives of the coefficient are measured in the unweighted norm on the full slab $[0,T]$, and those of the field retain the reciprocal-amplitude norm on the active interval $[t_0,T]$. Positivity and continuity of $\gamma$ are inherited hypotheses. No time derivative falls on that amplitude weight.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.summary: The weighted coefficient product keeps its spatial cost

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeD.text: For $T>0$ and a smooth profile $f(t,a,s)$ on $0\le t\le T$, the formal object is differentiation in the direction $(1,0,0)$ of the variables $(t,a,s)$. Thus it represents $\partial_t f$ with both the Lagrangian label $a$ and the independent phase $s$ fixed. At the two time endpoints the derivative is taken within the closed interval. It preserves the class of smooth profiles used by the construction. After evaluation along the inverse parent flow this derivative becomes the material derivative $\partial_t+U\cdot\nabla_x$. It is therefore not the derivative at a fixed physical point used in auxiliary Lemmas 1.2 and 1.3.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeD.summary: The label and independent phase remain fixed

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeD.text: Let $T>0$, $t\in[0,T]$, and let $f$ be a twisted profile. For every label and phase $(a,s)$, the value of $\partial_tf$ at $(t,a,s)$ equals the derivative within $[0,T]$ at $t$ of $u\mapsto f(u,a,s)$, with $a$ and $s$ held fixed.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeD.summary: Time differentiation fixes label and phase

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeD.text: For smooth slab profiles $A$ and $f$, the time derivative at fixed label and phase obeys the two-term product rule $\partial_t(Af)=(\partial_tA)f+A\,\partial_tf$. Unlike commutation with a fixed linear map, the coefficient profile is differentiated as well. The result is an equality of profiles, derived by specializing directional differentiation to $(1,0,0)$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeD.summary: Differentiate both factors in a time-dependent coefficient product

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: For $T>0$ and a nonnegative integer $i$, this is the $i$-fold composite of the profile time derivative $f\mapsto\partial_tf$ on twisted profiles on $[0,T]$, with label and phase held fixed. The zeroth power is the identity, and the output is again a twisted profile.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Iterated time derivative of a profile

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: Given $T>0$, a nonnegative integer $q$, and any spatial seminorm $N$ on the smooth profiles, the formal object is $\mathcal J_q(f)=\sum_{i=0}^q T^iN(\partial_t^i f)/i!$. The derivatives hold label and independent phase fixed on $[0,T]$. This is a seminorm: it need not distinguish all nonzero profiles. If $N$ includes division by the positive central amplitude $\gamma$, that division occurs after differentiating $f$; no derivative of $\gamma$ is introduced. The definition supplies the time weights in the auxiliary note, but does not itself specify the spatial norm, its derivative weights, or its domain of suprema; those depend on the chosen $N$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Time derivatives are measured before being summed

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: Let $T>0$, $0\le t_0\le T$, and let $\gamma$ be continuous and positive on $[t_0,T]$. Measure $f$ by $W_n(f)=\sum_{i\le q}\frac{T^i}{i!}\|\gamma^{-1}\partial_t^if\|_{[n]}$, with suprema over $[t_0,T]$ and no Hölder quotients. Then $W_n(f-\langle f\rangle)\le2W_n(f)$, where $\langle f\rangle$ is the phase average. The proof uses the triangle inequality and the fact that phase averaging does not increase this norm.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Centering in phase costs at most a factor of two

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: For a completion $C$ that vanishes at slab times before activation $t_0$, and an active weight with $0<\gamma\le1$ on $[t_0,T]$, this bounds the centered fast advection $F-\langle F\rangle$, $F=(\kappa\cdot C)\,\partial_sY$, using amplitude norms on both fields: $W_n(F-\langle F\rangle)\le2Q_n^2\,U_n(h^{-1}\kappa)\,W_n(C)\,W_{n+1}(Y)$. The phase scale must satisfy $h\ne0$. The scaled covector $h^{-1}\kappa$ remains unweighted, and the target $Y$ uses order $n+1$. The factor two comes from centering; inactivity permits replacing the completion's full-slab norm by its amplitude norm.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: The centered fast completion uses two amplitude measurements

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: Let $h\ne0$ and let $\gamma$ be continuous and positive on $[t_0,T]$. For the fast advection $(\kappa\cdot z)\,\partial_sg$, one has $W_n\big((\kappa\cdot z)\partial_sg\big)\le Q_n^2\,U_n(h^{-1}\kappa)\,U_n(z)\,W_{n+1}(g)$, where $W$ is the factorial time norm on $[t_0,T]$ weighted by $\gamma^{-1}$, $U$ the unweighted one on $[0,T]$, both of time order $q$, and $Q_n$ the quadratic product constant. No upper bound on $\gamma$ and no vanishing before $t_0$ are assumed.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: The fast product weights its differentiated oscillation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: This unfolds the time seminorm $\mathcal J_q$ into $\sum_{i=0}^qT^iN(\partial_t^if)/i!$, the sum of $T^i/i!$ times the spatial seminorm $N$ of the $i$th profile time derivative. The proof of positive duration is part of its construction. Spatial amplitude weights, if present in $N$, are applied after differentiation rather than differentiated together with the profile.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Read the time norm as a finite weighted sum

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: Given a spatial estimate, with nonnegative constant $C$, for the pointwise application of operator profiles to vector profiles, the time norm of $Af$ is bounded by $C$ times the time norms of $A$ and $f$. The hypothesis applies to every pair of input profiles. The proof combines the actual binomial application formula with the general factorial convolution inequality.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Apply the time product bound to operator profiles

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: Let $T>0$, a time order $q$, scales $\ell,h$, an order $n$, a time set $A\subseteq[0,T]$ and a weight $\tau$ bounded on $A$. For a profile $B$ of linear maps and a vector profile $f$, write $\mathcal J_q(g)=\sum_{i=0}^q\frac{T^i}{i!}N(\partial_t^ig)$ for the corresponding seminorm $N$. Then $\mathcal J_q(Bf)$ in $\|\cdot\|_{n,A,\tau}$, the finite profile norm of order $n$ with scales $\ell,h$ in which the profile is first multiplied by a weight $\tau(t)$ bounded on a time set $A\subseteq[0,T]$ and suprema are taken over $t\in A$ is at most $W_n\,2^n\,(2\|\mathrm{ev}\|)$ times $\mathcal J_q(B)$ in the unweighted finite profile norm on $[0,T]$ times $\mathcal J_q(f)$ in the weighted norm. Here $W_n$ counts multi-indices $(\alpha,j)$ with $|\alpha|+j\le n$, and $\mathrm{ev}(L,v)=Lv$ is the evaluation bilinear map, of operator norm at most one; time derivatives of the coefficient are included. Hölder quotients are included or omitted alike on both sides.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: A time-dependent coefficient acts with its measured norm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: Let $T>0$, a time order $q$, scales $\ell,h$, an order $n$, a time set $A\subseteq[0,T]$ and a weight $\tau$ bounded on $A$. For any matrix profiles $G,M$, covector profile $\kappa$ and vector profile $f$, the phase average $\int_0^1f(t,a,s)\,ds$, as the averaging operator of the hierarchy built from $G,M,\kappa$, satisfies $\sum_{i=0}^q\frac{T^i}{i!}\|\partial_t^i\bar f\|_{n,A,\tau}\le\sum_{i=0}^q\frac{T^i}{i!}\|\partial_t^if\|_{n,A,\tau}$, where $\|\cdot\|_{n,A,\tau}$, the finite profile norm of order $n$ with scales $\ell,h$ in which the profile is first multiplied by a weight $\tau(t)$ bounded on a time set $A\subseteq[0,T]$ and suprema are taken over $t\in A$ without half-Hölder quotients.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Phase averaging does not increase the time norm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: Assume a binomial identity is supplied for every target time derivative through order $q$, and each product term is estimated with nonnegative cost $C$. Then the target factorial time norm is at most $C$ times the product of the two input time norms. The operation $B$ is an arbitrary function here; its needed properties are carried by those explicit hypotheses.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Combine a Leibniz identity with spatial product estimates

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: Given nonnegative $C$ and a binomial-convolution bound for every target time derivative through order $q$, the target time seminorm is at most $C$ times the product of the two input time seminorms. The factorial weights cancel the binomial coefficients, and positivity bounds the remaining triangular convolution by a product. The lemma assumes the derivative-by-derivative estimate instead of deriving a Leibniz identity.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Lift a jetwise bilinear bound to the time norm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: On a set $S\subseteq[0,T]$, assume the bounded weights satisfy $\tau_{fg}=\tau_f\tau_g$. The time norm of the bilinear product is bounded by the original finite-word spatial product cost times the two weighted time norms. Weights are applied to each differentiated slice; no derivative of $\tau_f$, $\tau_g$, or $\tau_{fg}$ is taken or assumed.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Multiply weighted profiles after taking their time jets

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: Assumes the mean–mean slow advection of $B_j$ by $B_i$ is unchanged by phase averaging. It also requires $\gamma\le1$ on $[t_0,T]$, inactivity of $Y_j$ before launch $t_0$, nonzero radius $\ell$, and the row cap $L$ on each scaled coframe row. For $Z_i=Y_i+B_i$, the centered label product $F-\langle F\rangle$ of $Z_i,Z_j$ is bounded by $2(3Q_n^2L)$ times the product of the two sums $W_{n+1}(Y_i)+U_{n+1}(B_i)$ and $W_{n+1}(Y_j)+U_{n+1}(B_j)$ of amplitude-measured oscillations and unweighted means, each at spatial order $n+1$. The cancellation is an explicit hypothesis here.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: The centered slow source loses its mean–mean term

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: Let $\ell\ne0$ and suppose each of the three scaled rows $\ell^{-1}e_i\cdot G$ has unweighted full-slab factorial time norm at most $L$ at order $n$. Let $A\subseteq[0,T]$ and bounded weights $\tau_Z,\tau_Y,\tau_P$ on $A$ satisfy $\tau_P=\tau_Z\tau_Y$ there. Then the $\tau_P$-weighted time norm at order $n$ of the slow advection $D_ag\,[Gz]$ is at most $3Q_n^2L$ times the $\tau_Z$-weighted norm of $z$ at order $n$ times the $\tau_Y$-weighted norm of $g$ at order $n+1$. All norms have time order $q$ and no Hölder quotients; $Q_n$ is the quadratic product constant.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Slow advection preserves the chosen split of time weights

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: Let $T>0$, $0\le t_0\le T$, and let $\gamma$ be continuous on $[t_0,T]$ with $0<\gamma\le1$ there. Suppose the profile $f$ vanishes at every slab time $t<t_0$, for all labels and phases. Then, for every time order $q$, spatial order $n$ and scales $\ell,h$, the factorial time norm $\sum_{i\le q}\frac{T^i}{i!}\|\partial_t^if\|_{[n]}$ measured on all of $[0,T]$ with weight one is at most the same norm measured on $[t_0,T]$ after multiplying each time derivative by $\gamma(t)^{-1}$. The half-Hölder quotients are either included on both sides or omitted on both; $\gamma$ itself is never differentiated.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: The active amplitude norm controls the full time slab

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: If a smooth raw field agrees with a twisted profile on the centered cell during $[t_0,T]$, bounds for its scaled active time derivatives transfer to the profile’s weighted time norm. The label and phase scales must be nonzero, the active interval must have positive length, and $\gamma$ must be continuous and positive. The final constant is the sum of factorial time weights times the number of admissible words.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Active cell derivatives control the wrapped profile norm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: If the target seminorm of each time derivative of $g$ is bounded by $C$ times the source seminorm of the corresponding time derivative of $f$, the same factor $C$ bounds the complete time norm through order $q$. The hypothesis is made derivative by derivative and must be supplied. No linear operator or commutation property is inferred merely from this summation lemma.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Sum a linear estimate over all time orders

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: If $p\le q$, the time seminorm $\mathcal J_p$ is bounded by $\mathcal J_q$ for the same spatial seminorm and profile. The proof includes a shorter finite sum in a longer one. All new terms are nonnegative because $T>0$ and $N$ is a seminorm; no bound on individual derivatives is assumed.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Increasing time order enlarges the time seminorm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: A pointwise comparison $N\le M$ between spatial seminorms carries to their factorial time seminorms at every fixed time order $q$. The proof applies the comparison to each time derivative and multiplies by its positive weight. The derivative order and underlying profile remain unchanged, so this is an order comparison of norms rather than a regularity result.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: A larger spatial seminorm gives a larger time norm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: With $h\ne0$, bounds fast advection $(\kappa\cdot z)\,\partial_sg$ using the measured scaled covector $h^{-1}\kappa$, an advector $z$ at spatial order $n$, and the differentiated profile $g$ at $n+1$. The output time weight splits exactly as $\tau_P=\tau_Z\tau_Y$ on the measured set $A\subseteq[0,T]$. The multiplicative constant is $Q_n^2$; the carrier and reciprocal phase-width losses remain in the coefficient $h^{-1}\kappa$, rather than being hidden in this numerical constant.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Fast advection keeps the phase width inside its coefficient

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: Let the values lie in a complete normed space, $T>0$, and let $f$ have zero phase mean at every slab time and label. Take any time set $A\subseteq[0,T]$ and weight $\tau$ with $|\tau|\le C$ on $A$. Then the factorial time norm $\sum_{i\le q}\frac{T^i}{i!}\|\tau\,\partial_t^i(\cdot)\|_{[n]}$, with suprema over $A$ and no Hölder quotients, of the normalized phase primitive $\partial_s^{-1}f$ is at most twice the same norm of $f$. The time order $q$, spatial order $n$ and scales $\ell,h$ are the same on both sides.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: The phase inverse has the same cost in time norms

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: If a fixed continuous bilinear map satisfies a spatial seminorm bound with nonnegative constant $C$ for all pairs of profiles, its factorial time seminorm obeys the same product estimate with the same $C$. The theorem proves the required Leibniz identity for this map and sums it. There is no additional factor depending on time order in the spatial product cost.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Spatial bilinear estimates keep their cost in time norms

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: For a continuous bilinear map $B$, profiles $f,g$, a time set $A\subseteq[0,T]$ with $T>0$ and a weight with $|\tau|\le C$ on $A$, the weighted factorial time norm of the pointwise product $B(f,g)$ through time order $q$ and spatial order $n$ is at most $c_n(B)$ times the unweighted full-slab time norm of $f$ times the weighted time norm of $g$. Here $c_n(B)=2^{n+1}\|B\|$ multiplied by the number of mixed multi-indices of order at most $n$. Each time norm is $\sum_{i\le q}\frac{T^i}{i!}\|\partial_t^i(\cdot)\|_{[n]}$, with the same Hölder choice throughout; the weight multiplies after differentiation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: The factorial time product keeps the spatial constant

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: Let $f$ have zero phase mean, let $c$ be phase-independent, and let $|\tau|\le C$ on $A\subseteq[0,T]$. The $\tau$-weighted factorial time norm at spatial order $n$ of $R\big(\ell\partial_{a_i}\partial_s^{-1}[cf]\big)$ is at most $2\,c_n(B_R)\,c_{n+1}(B_c)\,U_n(R)\,U_{n+1}(c)$ times the $\tau$-weighted norm of $f$ at order $n+1$. Here $U$ is the unweighted full-slab time norm, $B_R$ and $B_c$ are the evaluation maps applying $R$ and $c$, and $c_m(B)=2^{m+1}\|B\|$ times the number of mixed multi-indices of order at most $m$. The time order is $q$ throughout.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: The relay term spends one label order and two coefficient norms

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: Let $D_i$ be one of the four scaled directions $\ell\partial_{a_1},\ell\partial_{a_2},\ell\partial_{a_3},h\partial_s$. For $T>0$, a time set $A\subseteq[0,T]$ and a weight with $|\tau|\le C$ on $A$, the factorial time norm $\sum_{i\le q}\frac{T^i}{i!}\|\tau\,\partial_t^i(D_if)\|_{[n]}$ is at most the same norm of $f$ at spatial order $n+1$. The weight, the time set, the time order $q$ and the Hölder choice are the same on both sides.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: The time norm retains the same spatial derivative cost

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: For nonzero radius $\ell$ and a common time-norm cap $L$ on the three scaled coframe rows, estimates the slow divergence product $\operatorname{tr}(D_aV\circ G)\,Y$ with exact splitting $\tau_P=\tau_V\tau_Y$ of the two time weights. The first field $V$ is measured at spatial order $n+1$, while $Y$ is measured at $n$. The factor is $3Q_n^2L$. The extra label order is spent on the first field.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: The divergence product spends its extra order on the first field

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: The time seminorm $\mathcal J_{q+1}(f)$ is bounded by the undifferentiated spatial seminorm $N(f)$ plus $T$ times $\mathcal J_q(\partial_tf)$, the time seminorm through order $q$ of the first profile time derivative. This holds for any spatial seminorm on a positive-length slab. The recurrence loses no spatial order and is the summation step used in the transverse time induction.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: The next time norm uses one differentiated profile

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: Let $\ell\ne0$ and suppose each scaled row $\ell^{-1}e_i\cdot G$ has unweighted factorial time norm $U_n\le L$. With $U_m$ the unweighted factorial time norm of time order $q$ and spatial order $m$ on the whole slab $[0,T]$, the slow advection satisfies $U_n\big(D_ag\,[Gz]\big)\le3Q_n^2L\,U_n(z)\,U_{n+1}(g)$. This is the split-weight estimate with all three weights equal to one.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Slow advection estimate on the full time slab

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: Let $h\ne0$. With $U_m$ the unweighted factorial time norm of time order $q$ and spatial order $m$ on $[0,T]$, the fast advection satisfies $U_n\big((\kappa\cdot z)\partial_sg\big)\le Q_n^2\,U_n(h^{-1}\kappa)\,U_n(z)\,U_{n+1}(g)$. The carrier and the phase width are contained in the coefficient norm $U_n(h^{-1}\kappa)$; no frequency assumption is made.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Fast advection estimate on the full time slab

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: Uses constant time weights equal to one in the slow divergence product bound for $\operatorname{tr}(D_aV\circ G)\,Y$. Given nonzero $\ell$ and the coframe row cap $L$, the first vector field $V$ is measured through spatial order $n+1$ and the second $Y$ through $n$, with time order $q$ for both, on the full slab. The factor is $3Q_n^2L$, from the three coordinate rows and two products.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Slow divergence product estimate on the full time slab

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: Suppose $r$ agrees on the slab with the wave-relay formula built from mean-zero profiles $v$ and $f$. A coefficient budget at order $n$, positive frequency $\lambda$, nonzero label width, and a bounded time weight then yield the factorial time estimate for $r$. The right side costs the explicit relay constant times $K^2/\lambda$ and the order-$(n+1)$ norms of $v$ and $f$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Estimate the actual relay from its exact phase representation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: For a positive-length slab, the time seminorm of order zero satisfies $\mathcal J_0(f)=N(f)$. The finite sum has only the undifferentiated profile, with weight one. This connects the higher-time estimates to the undifferentiated mean and transverse estimates already available in the main construction; no new inverse estimate is proved here.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: The order-zero time norm is the spatial norm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: Let $T>0$ and $t\in[0,T]$. Evaluating the profile time jet $\partial_t^if$ of a twisted profile at $(t,a,s)$ gives the $i$th closed-slab derivative within $[0,T]$ of the scalar-time slice $u\mapsto f(u,a,s)$, with label and phase fixed. Both endpoints of the positive slab are included.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Profile time derivatives are genuine derivatives within the slab

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: For every natural order $n$, the time derivative $\partial_t^n(Af)$ is $\sum_{0\le i\le n}\binom ni(\partial_t^iA)(\partial_t^{n-i}f)$, the $i$th coefficient time derivative acting on the complementary field time derivative. Positive $T$ supports the closed-slab calculus. Induction uses the first-order product rule and Pascal’s identity, without spending label derivatives.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: The binomial rule for time-dependent coefficient profiles

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: Let $T>0$, $i\ge0$ and $v$ a fixed vector in the time, label and phase variables. For every twisted profile $f$ on $[0,T]$, the $i$th time derivative of the derivative of $f$ along $v$ equals the derivative along $v$ of $\partial_t^if$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Time derivatives commute with fixed directional derivatives

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: Let $T>0$ and let a profile take the values $f(t,a)$ at every $(t,a,s)$ with $t\in[0,T]$. Then for every order $i$, $t\in[0,T]$ and $(a,s)$, its $i$-th time derivative at $(t,a,s)$ equals the $i$-th derivative within $[0,T]$ of $r\mapsto f(r,a)$ at $t$. The derivative is at fixed label and phase.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: A label field keeps its time derivative after bundling

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: The order-$i$ profile time derivative of $Lf$ equals $L$ applied to $\partial_t^if$, assuming $T>0$. The proof iterates the directional commutation rule in the time direction. This removes fixed linear contractions from repeated differentiation without changing spatial derivative orders or introducing coefficient derivatives.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: All profile time jets commute with fixed linear maps

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: For a bundled smooth twisted profile on a positive closed slab, the jth time jet commutes with every fixed weighted label-and-phase derivative word. Both ℓ and h remain constant during differentiation. Induction on the word reduces the claim to commutation of time and constant directional derivatives. No estimate or growth bound for either side is included.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Time derivatives commute with fixed spatial words

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: If $f$ is phase independent, each of its profile time derivatives is also phase independent. The assumption $T>0$ provides the legitimate within-time derivative, while phase independence supplies equality of slices at all phases. The proof differentiates these equal functions on the same interval, retaining the special mean-field class during Eulerian conversion.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Time derivatives preserve independence of phase

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: For $T>0$, any order $i$ and a smooth twisted profile $f$ with zero phase mean, the $i$th time derivative within $[0,T]$ of the normalized phase primitive $\partial_s^{-1}f$ equals the normalized phase primitive of $\partial_t^if$, as an equality of twisted profiles. The time derivative $\partial_t^if$ again has zero phase mean, so its primitive is defined; endpoint times are included.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: The bundled primitive commutes with time differentiation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: The $n$th profile time derivative of a fixed bilinear product is the sum of $\binom ni B(\partial_t^if,\partial_t^{n-i}g)$ over $i\le n$. The only time-domain requirement is positive slab length, since the profile spaces supply smoothness. The proof derives this from operator application and commutation with the fixed map $B$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Time jets satisfy the bilinear binomial formula

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: States equality of bundled vector profiles obtained by averaging in phase before or after any time jet: $\partial_t^i\langle f\rangle=\langle\partial_t^if\rangle$, where $\langle f\rangle(t,a)=\int_0^1f(t,a,s)\,ds$. The hypothesis $T>0$ ensures a nondegenerate closed time interval. The proof evaluates profiles, rewrites the phase average as its integral from zero to one, and uses the fixed-interval derivative interchange.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Phase averaging commutes with every time derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: For a smooth lattice-twisted profile $f$ on a slab with $T>0$, every time derivative of order $j$ commutes with each of the four scaled directions $\ell\partial_{a_1},\ell\partial_{a_2},\ell\partial_{a_3},h\partial_s$: $\partial_t^j(D_if)=D_i(\partial_t^jf)$ as profiles. The scales $\ell,h$ are fixed real numbers and the direction is constant in time.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Time and scaled spatial derivatives commute

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: For $T>0$, every $i$ and every twisted profile $f$ on $[0,T]$, the time derivative of order $i+1$ equals $\partial_t$ applied to $\partial_t^if$, as an equality of profiles.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: The last time derivative after the earlier ones

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: For $T>0$, every $i$ and every twisted profile $f$ on $[0,T]$, the jet of order $i+1$ equals the order-$i$ jet $\partial_t^i$ applied to the first time derivative $\partial_tf$. Both sides are powers of the same linear operator, so no extra smoothness is needed.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: The first time derivative before the later ones

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: For $T>0$ and every twisted profile $f$ on $[0,T]$, the time derivative of order zero is $f$ itself. This is the base case of induction on the time order.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: The zeroth time derivative is the profile itself

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: Assumes a smooth profile $f$ is zero at every slab time strictly earlier than $t_0$, for all labels and phases. At any such time $t<t_0$ in $[0,T]$, every bundled time jet $\partial_t^if$ is also zero at every label and phase. The conclusion still requires $t<t_0$; it does not assert the value at the activation time itself. The argument uses local equality to zero within the closed slab.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Every time derivative vanishes before activation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.trans.text: In the actual parent chart the coframe and covector solve the two closed-slab geometric differential equations of the relay.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.trans.summary: Evolution equations for the coframe and transported covector

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.trans.text: This definition adds the differentiated velocity contribution and the carrier-weighted pressure contribution, then counts the admissible derivative words through order $n$. The pressure portion also includes the direct source coefficient. It records a finite explicit constant rather than asserting that a transverse solve has already been constructed or bounded.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.trans.summary: The combined velocity and pressure solve coefficient

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.trans.text: For nonnegative reference coefficient bounds and $\mathsf D\ge1$, the explicit solve coefficient with duration $r\le1$ is bounded by a reference constant times $\mathsf D^{20}$. The reference constant is nonnegative and depends on derivative order, while the parent exponent twenty does not. The statement is a numerical comparison of the defined coefficients.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.trans.summary: The parent cost of the transverse inverse is fixed

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.trans.text: This explicit expression is $(1+2K^{\mathrm s}_nC)\,(1+TK^{\mathrm v}_nC)^q(C_0+1)+2K^{\mathrm s}_nC$, where $K^{\mathrm s}_n$ and $K^{\mathrm v}_n$ are the costs of applying a row and a matrix coefficient at spatial order $n$. It combines the repeated velocity-equation factor, the undifferentiated inverse constant $C_0$, and the normalized pressure application cost. It depends on $T$, spatial order $n$, time order $q$, and coefficient bound $C$. The formula records how the velocity and pressure estimates are added after the zero-mean phase estimate.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.trans.summary: The fixed-order cost for the transverse time estimate

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.trans.text: Assume $0\le T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge1$, and nonnegative inverse and coefficient costs bounded respectively by $A_0\mathsf D^a$ and $A\mathsf D^b$. The transverse time constant is at most its unit-time version with coefficients $A_0,A$, multiplied by $\mathsf D^{a+b(q+1)}$. The spatial order may affect the fixed constant, but it does not enter this exponent.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.trans.summary: The transverse time cost has one fixed parent power

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.trans.text: If the slab length $T$ and both input constants $C_0,C$ are nonnegative, the combined transverse time cost is nonnegative for every spatial order $n$ and time order $q$. The proof uses nonnegativity of the scalar and vector application costs. This lemma concerns the numerical formula only; it does not establish coefficient bounds or the undifferentiated inverse estimate.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.trans.summary: The transverse time cost is nonnegative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.trans.text: This real expression collects the product-rule factor, lift and pullback bounds, homogeneous forward bound, interval duration, and the derivative-word factor for the transverse ODE. It is the coefficient multiplying the source seminorm before summing over words. Its arguments are unrestricted real numbers; positivity is imposed when using it as an estimate.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.trans.summary: The coefficient for a differentiated transverse velocity

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.trans.text: Bounds the explicit transverse-velocity coefficient with duration factor $r\le1$ by the unit-duration coefficient times $B+H$. The listed coefficient caps and $H$ are nonnegative. The quantity $B$ is unrestricted, since its contribution is unchanged on both sides. This algebraic simplification does not supply the inverse or source estimates that use the coefficient.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.trans.summary: Replacing a short duration by a unit duration

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.trans.text: If a twisted vector profile has zero phase advection against every twisted test profile, its pointwise inner product with the covector vanishes throughout the slab. The proof constructs a sine probe whose phase derivative is nonzero at the chosen point. The universal quantifier over test profiles is essential; a single test would not suffice.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.trans.summary: Vanishing phase advection against every test forces transversality

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.twist.text:
The actual material derivative $(\partial_t+M)$, the label and phase pressure gradients $\mathbf d$ and $\kappa\,\partial_s$, the label and phase advections and the phase average act on twisted profiles. The coframe, material matrix and wave vector can enter through the embedding of phase-independent coefficients when they are periodic in the labels.

Default values: this object is built by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions in its definition. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.twist.summary: Concrete material, gradient and advection operators

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.twist.text: The underlying periodic output of this twisted hierarchy component equals the corresponding periodic operation: the actual full-period phase average. This is a definitional equality. The lattice-compatibility proof is retained in the outer wrapper, while the concrete value calculation is exactly the one already established in the periodic space.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.twist.summary: Read averaging before the twisted restriction

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.twist.text: The underlying periodic output of this twisted hierarchy component equals the corresponding periodic operation: the label derivative of the second field selected by the first field and G. This is a definitional equality. The lattice-compatibility proof is retained in the outer wrapper, while the concrete value calculation is exactly the one already established in the periodic space.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.twist.summary: Read label advection before the twisted restriction

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.twist.text: The underlying periodic output of this twisted hierarchy component equals the corresponding periodic operation: the scalar pressure gradient in the coframe G. This is a definitional equality. The lattice-compatibility proof is retained in the outer wrapper, while the concrete value calculation is exactly the one already established in the periodic space.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.twist.summary: Read the label gradient before the twisted restriction

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.twist.text: The underlying periodic output of this twisted hierarchy component equals the corresponding periodic operation: time differentiation plus multiplication by M. This is a definitional equality. The lattice-compatibility proof is retained in the outer wrapper, while the concrete value calculation is exactly the one already established in the periodic space.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.twist.summary: Read the material operator before the twisted restriction

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.twist.text: The underlying periodic output of this twisted hierarchy component equals the corresponding periodic operation: the phase derivative of the second field selected by the first field and κ. This is a definitional equality. The lattice-compatibility proof is retained in the outer wrapper, while the concrete value calculation is exactly the one already established in the periodic space.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.twist.summary: Read phase advection before the twisted restriction

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.twist.text: The underlying periodic output of this twisted hierarchy component equals the corresponding periodic operation: the phase derivative multiplied by κ. This is a definitional equality. The lattice-compatibility proof is retained in the outer wrapper, while the concrete value calculation is exactly the one already established in the periodic space.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.twist.summary: Read the fast gradient before the twisted restriction

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.twist.text: For every integer lattice vector, a twisted profile’s representative is periodic under the corresponding joint label-phase shift. This theorem exposes the proof stored in the twisted submodule. The three value projections pass through the twisted, periodic, and smooth wrappers to the actual function.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.twist.summary: Read the stored carrier-compatible translation identity

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.twist.text: The periodic completion of twisted data is invariant under every prescribed joint lattice-and-phase shift. The covector must be phase independent and nonzero on the slab. Translation covariance of the normalized potential gives equality of label derivatives; outside the slab, both sides vanish by the profile convention.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.twist.summary: Curl completion preserves the joint lattice and phase shift

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.twist.text: A twisted profile is invariant under label translation by an integer vector together with the matching phase shift. This identity is what makes graph evaluation periodic in physical space.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.twist.summary: Values agree after the simultaneous lattice shift

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.text:
The unweighted norm measures the entire time slab.

The positive-time hypothesis and the constant unit weight make the sampled derivatives bounded on the whole closed slab. This is a seminorm on bundled profiles, so it does not infer regularity from a bare numeric bound.

With weight one and all times in $[0,T]$, the phase average has no larger order-$n$ mixed seminorm than the original profile. This is the unweighted specialization of the bounded-weight contraction. It is used before estimating averaged quadratic terms, preserving the derivative order already assigned to their factors.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.summary: Phase averaging decreases the full-slab norm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.text: A whole-slab bilinear product is bounded using the first factor’s full unweighted norm and the second factor’s active amplitude norm. The second factor must vanish before activation, and the positive amplitude must be at most one. The proof combines the product inequality with the inactive-profile comparison, retaining an explicit word-count constant.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.summary: Control a whole-slab product using its inactive oscillatory factor

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.text: If the twisted average fixes a profile, its unweighted mixed seminorm equals the label-word norm of the phase-zero slice. The proof first deduces phase independence from the averaging identity. This version matches the certificate returned by the mean solver and avoids requiring a separate pointwise independence premise.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.summary: A profile fixed by averaging has the label-only norm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.text: For a phase-independent twisted profile on a positive slab, the unweighted mixed seminorm without Hölder quotients equals the label-word norm of the phase-zero slice. The phase scale is arbitrary because words involving phase derivatives vanish. This is an exact equality, with no additional constant or derivative loss.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.summary: The unweighted mean norm is exactly the label norm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.text: On the full slab, label advection $(z\cdot\mathbf d)g$ costs $3Q_n^2L$ times the order-$n$ norm of $z$ and the order-$(n+1)$ norm of $g$. The assumed bound $L$ on the three scaled coframe rows and nonzero label width are explicit. Setting both time weights to one in the general product estimate gives this unweighted form.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.summary: Slow advection costs one label derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.text: If the profile is zero before activation and the active amplitude satisfies $0<\gamma\le1$, its full-slab unweighted seminorm is at most its active amplitude seminorm. Before activation every spatial derivative is zero; afterward dividing by $\gamma$ enlarges every measurement. The conclusion is not valid for a general mean profile lacking the inactivity assumption.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.summary: The active weighted norm controls the whole inactive-prefix profile

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.text: If a twisted profile equals a phase-independent label coefficient on the slab and every admissible derivative word of the coefficient is bounded by $B$, its unweighted finite seminorm is at most the number of admissible words times $B$. The hypothesis that the profile and the coefficient agree on the slab connects the abstract coefficient to the profile being measured. This avoids replacing the actual norm by an unrelated allowance.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.summary: A coefficient word bound controls its exact seminorm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.text: For n ≤ m, the order-n unweighted seminorm is at most the order-m seminorm. The scales, Hölder flag and profile are unchanged.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.summary: Unweighted seminorms increase with derivative order

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.text: This specializes the bounded-weight fast-advection estimate to weight one on all of $[0,T]$. The differentiated profile still costs one extra mixed derivative, while the covector and advector use order $n$. The hypothesis $h\ne0$ is retained; the theorem does not itself estimate the scaled covector by a frequency power.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.summary: Unweighted fast advection costs one mixed derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.text: Assume $G$ is phase independent, its label derivatives satisfy the supplied bounds by constants times powers of $\mathsf D$, and $\ell\mathsf D^q\le1$ with nonnegative scales and constants. The scaled-row norm is bounded by the number of admissible words times the sum of derivative constants times $|\ell^{-1}|L\mathsf D^p$. The residual inverse width stays explicit; the order-dependent factor $\mathsf D^{qj}$ is absorbed.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.summary: Label scaling absorbs derivative-dependent parent powers

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.text: For a phase-independent covector with normalized label-jet bounds, $h=\mathrm{freq}^{-1/2}$ and $\ell D^7\le1$ imply the exact scaled-covector seminorm is bounded by an order constant times $D^2\mathrm{freq}^{3/2}$. Positive frequency justifies the normalization. The proof separates $h^{-1}\mathrm{freq}$ from the width-scaled label derivatives.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.summary: The scaled phase covector costs frequency to the three halves

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.text: The norm of $(\mathbf d\cdot V)Y$ is bounded by $3Q_n^2L$ times the order-$(n+1)$ norm of $V$ and order-$n$ norm of $Y$. The theorem retains the choice of whether the half-Hölder part is included, the common scaled-row bound, and $\ell\ne0$. It follows by taking all time weights equal to one.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.summary: A divergence product differentiates its first factor

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.text: Let $T>0$, $\ell,\mathsf D,A\ge0$ with $\ell\mathsf D^p\le1$, $C(n)\ge0$, and let a profile take the values $f(t,a)$ on $[0,T]$, where $f$ satisfies the mixed bounds on $[0,T]$ through time order $q$ with slope $p$, amplitude $A$ and constants $C(n)$. Then for every $i\le q$ and every $n$, $\|\partial_t^i(\cdot)\|_{[n]}\le W_n\Big(\sum_{j=0}^nC(j)\Big)A$, with the unweighted finite profile norm on $[0,T]$ for any phase scale $h$ and $W_n$ the number of multi-indices $(\alpha,j)$ in the three label directions and the phase with $|\alpha|+j\le n$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.summary: The label length absorbs the spatial derivative rate

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.text: Let $0<T\le1$, $\ell,\mathsf D,A\ge0$ with $\ell\mathsf D^p\le1$, $C(n)\ge0$, and let a profile take the values $f(t,a)$ on $[0,T]$, where $f$ satisfies the mixed bounds on $[0,T]$ through time order $q$ with slope $p$, amplitude $A$ and constants $C(n)$. Then $\sum_{i=0}^q\frac{T^i}{i!}\|\partial_t^i(\cdot)\|_{[n]}\le(q+1)W_n\Big(\sum_{j=0}^nC(j)\Big)A$, using the unweighted finite profile norm on $[0,T]$ and $W_n$ the number of multi-indices $(\alpha,j)$ in the three label directions and the phase with $|\alpha|+j\le n$. The condition $T\le1$ makes each weight $T^i/i!$ at most one.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.summary: Summing time derivatives without changing the amplitude

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.veloc.text: An equality of twisted profiles $(\partial_t+M)V+\kappa\,\partial_s\mathsf p=F$ yields the within-slab scalar-time equation at every label and phase. The proof evaluates the profile equality and applies the pointwise lemma. Phase independence of the strain and covector remains explicit; transverse and mean-zero constraints are separate facts.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.veloc.summary: The bundled momentum equation gives every slice equation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.veloc.text: At one slab point, a twisted momentum equality determines the within-slab time derivative of $V$ as forcing minus strain and phase-pressure terms. Phase independence of $M$ and $\kappa$ allows their values to be read at phase zero. Smoothness is already part of the profile type, so the result includes endpoint derivatives.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.veloc.summary: A pointwise momentum identity gives the time derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.waveR.text:
The fixed-time formula for the four slow relay terms, with the actual transported covector and the genuine phase profiles.

Reading coefficients at phase zero is appropriate once the coefficient profiles are phase independent. The raw expression does not itself impose that property or the momentum equation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.waveR.summary: The slow relay in the actual parent chart

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.waveR.text:
The explicit order constant in the normalized linear relay estimate.

The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.waveR.summary: The explicit derivative-order constant for the relay

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.waveR.text: At relay level $p$, this definition uses the preceding transverse forcing: with $H$ the source before the mean at level $p-1$, it is $-(H-\overline H)$ minus the mean-phase advection term, where $\overline H$ is the phase average. At level two it is set to zero because the activation completion is subtracted separately in the relay. The definition gives a value for every $p$; later identities restrict to levels $2,\dots,P+1$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.waveR.summary: The preceding force after removing the activation completion

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.weigh.text:
Evaluate the profile at times in $A$, with a scalar multiplier depending only on time. Using inverse amplitude here leaves label and phase orders intact.

The time index set $A$ and scalar weight are arbitrary here; $A$ may be empty and the weight may vanish. Smoothness and norm applications separately require slab membership and the appropriate weight bounds.
A scalar time weight may be applied to the velocity slices before taking their normalized potential and slow curl.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.weigh.summary: Time weights pass through the normalized curl correction

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.weigh.text: A pointwise representation of an actual twisted source as the raw relay also represents its weighted slices using the weighted input slices.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.weigh.summary: The relay formula passes to amplitude-weighted slices

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.weigh.text: Restricting the scaled coframe-row profile to a time set $A$ and weighting by one gives exactly the raw coefficient function used in the mixed-word estimate. The hypothesis $A\subseteq[0,T]$ ensures every evaluation lies in the slab. This identifies two encodings of the same row, without adding a coefficient bound.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.weigh.summary: The bundled row equals the coefficient in the norm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.weigh.text: For a time in the slab, multiplying a smooth profile slice by an arbitrary scalar time weight leaves its label and phase dependence smooth. The weight needs no time differentiability for this fixed-time statement.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.weigh.summary: Weighted slices are smooth in label and phase

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.wordB.text: The actual measured source controls every normalized derivative word.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.wordB.summary: The amplitude seminorm controls every normalized word

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerBase.text: Packages a zero-index stage, the first child stage and the wave linking them, all at activation zero. It fixes the first coupling to $2\pi$. The field called stationary is not itself required to be time independent. The explicit stationary-shear realization supplies that additional property when constructing the base.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerBase.summary: The initial stage and its first completed wave

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerBase.ofFirstWav.text: Builds the induction base from the stationary shear parent and the actual first cutoff child. The first wave uses the constant-one cutoff and activation time zero. Required inputs include the prescribed tilt, support, oscillation and correction estimates, a central split, a bound on remainder derivatives, cutoff-tail control, and lifetime conditions; the proof imports the explicit first-wave central calculation.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerBase.ofFirstWav.summary: Assemble the first cutoff wave over the stationary shear

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerBase.tip.text: Turns a certified base pair into the index-zero tip, using the lifetime bound to fit the first endpoint inside the stationary slab. All stored velocities and wave data are reused directly. The construction changes their packaging, rather than choosing replacement stages with only equal numerical bounds.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerBase.tip.summary: The initial pair forms a valid induction tip

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerCentralWaves.text: Adds central wave vectors, amplitudes, cutoffs, gradient errors and physical crossings to an existing stage family. Equalities identify the preceding and current wave pairs with those of each crossing. Bounds on strength, coupling and comparison errors are explicit components. These identities prevent the terminal argument from combining estimates for unrelated wave or velocity sequences.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerCentralWaves.summary: Central waves belonging to the same stages

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerCentralWaves.ac.text: Shows that activation time $t_{j+3}$ is strictly later than $t_{j+2}$. The stored crossing occurs after the switching time, and the positive physical growth rate makes that delay positive. This is compatible with the separately imposed equality of the first two wave activations at zero.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerCentralWaves.ac.summary: Successive later activations are strictly separated

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.text: Stores lifetime bounds, one certified base and a successor function for every compatible finite prefix. Unlike the formulation that only asserts that each certified prefix has some successor, the function returns a particular step. Iterating this one function defines all later fields coherently; it is not a separate independent choice of a finished tower at each length.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.summary: A base pair and a chosen extension operation

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.ac.text: Defines the activation sequence with $t_0=0$ and, at index $n+1$, the activation of the $n$th generated pair of stages. The first two positive indices therefore both evaluate to zero, $t_1=t_2=0$. Subsequent lemmas identify later activations with the crossings selected by actual successor steps.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.ac.summary: The activation times read from the generated tips

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.ac.text: Identifies the activation $t_{n+3}$ with the crossing time of the step selected at the $n$th generated pair. The index shift accounts for the two initial waves already present at activation zero. This equality is what connects strict crossing delays and terminal interval estimates to the activation sequence used by the limit theorem.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.ac.summary: Later activations are the selected physical crossings

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.ac.text: Identifies the activation $t_{n+2}$ with the next activation stored in the $n$th generated pair of stages. This is a consistency lemma, true by definition, between the global sequence and the local wave record. It allows local increment bounds to become bounds on consecutive entries of the single global activation sequence.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.ac.summary: The next activation comes from the current completed wave

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.ac.text: Computes activation at positive index one as zero using the activation stored by the base tip. This is the first completed wave supplied by the base pair. Subsequent physical crossing choices do not change that initial activation, and strict growth is only asserted after the two initial waves.

Computes $t_2=0$ from the zero next activation of the base pair, carried into its first successor pair. The crossing selected by that successor is $t_3$. Keeping these indices separate avoids confusing the second launch with the first strictly later crossing.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.ac.summary: The second activation time is zero

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.ac.text: Computes activation at index zero as zero directly from the first branch of the global activation definition. This extra index belongs to the initial parent bookkeeping. The equality makes no claim about later crossing times or strict growth of the physical wave activation sequence.

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.ce.text:
Given one recursive construction of periodic approximate velocities $U_j$, the formal statement collects its central covectors $\kappa_j$, amplitudes $\mathbf a_j$, cutoffs $\widetilde\chi_j$ and errors $E_{c,j}$. On $[t_j,S_j]$ they satisfy $
abla U_j(t,0)=
abla U_{j-1}(t,0)+\widetilde\chi_j\mathbf a_j\otimes\kappa_j+E_{c,j}$, with $\|E_{c,j}\|\le\lambda_j^{-1/4}$. The cutoff is one after $t_{j+1}$. At that time, $\pi\le
u_j\le4\pi$ and $C^{-1}\lambda_j^{1/4}\le|\kappa_j||\mathbf a_j|\le C\lambda_j^{1/4}(4\log\lambda_{j+2})^2$, where $C\ge2$ is the construction's fixed constant and $
u_j=(\kappa_j/|\kappa_j|)\cdot
abla U_{j-1}(\mathbf a_j/|\mathbf a_j|)$. For every later wave, its preceding pair and older gradient are those of these same stages; its selected first crossing is exactly the next activation time. This organizes data already supplied by a construction. It does not prove that a construction exists or identify the central covectors with a separately localized phase.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.ce.summary: Identifies the central waves belonging to the constructed velocities

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.ol.text: After identifying the activation times attached to the two objects, proves that the older stage in the $n$th generated pair is exactly the retained stage $U_n$. The identification is needed because the type of a stage depends on its activation time. This is an identity of certified stage objects, stronger than a statement that their velocities merely satisfy the same bounds.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.ol.summary: The older tip member is exactly the retained earlier stage

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.se.text: Applies the stored successor function to the exact pair and history generated at length $n$. This names the same step used by the next recursion branch. Later equalities identify its crossing and child with the activation and stage sequences, so compatibility is carried through to the terminal estimates.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.se.summary: The successor chosen at the generated prefix

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.sl.text: Defines the global slab sequence by applying the fixed parameter endpoint formula to each stage index and its generated activation. It introduces no independent sequence of endpoints. Subsequent strict-decrease and lifetime results therefore refer to the same intervals on which the retained stage certificates were constructed.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.sl.summary: The endpoint of each retained physical stage

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.sl.text: Proves strict decrease from each retained endpoint to the next. At the initial step, the one-quarter half-length bound leaves the first endpoint below one; at later steps, the current tip’s nesting theorem applies. This gives genuine time-domain containment for all members of the exported family.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.sl.summary: The retained stage endpoints strictly decrease

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.st.text: Returns the stored base stage $U_0$ at index zero and the parent of the $n$th generated pair at index $n+1$. Its type records the corresponding activation time $t_n$. Thus the exported sequence uses the same stage objects that were passed from one local construction to the next.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.st.summary: The retained physical stage at each activation

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.st.text: Proves nonnegativity of the global activation sequence, including its extra zero index. At positive indices the generated tip carries the necessary certificate. This is used to place active intervals inside the closed time slabs where the corresponding velocities, pressures and flows have their stated regularity.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.st.summary: Every retained stage begins at a nonnegative time

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.st.text: Exports the generated velocities, residuals, activation times, slabs and oscillatory increments into the stage family that the limit argument takes as input. Every estimate is taken from the retained stage or its actual linking wave. The older-velocity equality reconciles local and global formulas, while the identity between the physical and Leray-projected residuals is used in the required orientation.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.st.summary: The compatible construction becomes one limit-input family

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.ti.text: Projects the current pair of stages from the recursively generated pair-and-history at length $n$. The returned pair retains its index $n$, hence the types of its older and parent stages. This abbreviation changes only notation and does not perform an additional selection of stage or wave data.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.ti.summary: The final pair of stages in the generated history

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.tr.text: Builds the pair of current stages and history by recursion on $n$. At zero it uses the fixed base. At a successor it applies the stored successor function to the exact previously generated pair and appends that step. This is the construction that ensures all finite prefixes belong to one common sequence.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.tr.summary: One recursively chosen compatible history at every length

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.tr.text: For $k\le n$, restricting the generated length-$n$ history to index $k$ yields exactly the generated history at length $k$. The proof combines the recursive defining equation with preservation of earlier lookup under appending. This supplies the common-prefix property required for a single infinite sequence of approximate solutions.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.tr.summary: Every generated history restricts to the same earlier history

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.tr.text: Unfolds one recursion step of the history construction, identifying the next pair and history with those obtained by appending the step selected at length $n$. The equality holds by definition. It exposes the exact compatibility needed in later lookup proofs rather than merely matching the lengths of the two histories.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.tr.summary: The next generated history appends the selected step

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.text: The parameters are an integer $b\ge1$, a threshold $\mathcal B$, integer orders $q_j$, real frequencies $\lambda_j$, and two comparison constants. They satisfy $q_1=1$, $\mathcal B(1)\le\lambda_0$, and, for $j\ge1$, $\lambda_j=\lambda_{j-1}^{320b(q_j+1)}$ and $q_{j+1}=\max\{s\in\mathbb N:1\le s\le q_j+1,\ \mathcal B(s)\le\lambda_{j-1}\}$. For every integer $s\ge1$, $\mathcal B(s)>0$ and $\log\mathcal B(s)\ge4[320b(s+2)]^3$. The real strength constant is at least $2$ and the integer comparison constant at least $240$. Monotonicity of $\mathcal B$ and domination of analytic constants are not included. The recurrence uses nonnegative integer powers; the maximum rule starts with $q_2$, so it says nothing about $q_0$. These numerical conditions do not construct velocity fields.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.summary: The frequency recurrence and order selection are imposed

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.Life.text: Collects a one-quarter upper bound for the first half-length, positivity of every half-length, the negative frequency-power upper bound, and contraction by a factor of at least four. These are arithmetic hypotheses on the chosen schedule. Together with activation increments they place each child endpoint strictly inside its parent interval.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.Life.summary: The numerical bounds that nest the time slabs

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.Step.text: The finite index type has one constructor for each analytic family label and three additional constructors for cutoff-tail, step, and mean costs. This lets a single threshold mechanism see all four families. Even if the analytic label type is empty, the three numerical cost rows remain present and must still be dominated.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.Step.summary: One finite index includes every kind of cost

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.Step.text: This structure records analytic costs with two natural indices and a finite family label, a cutoff-tail cost, a step constant, and mean costs. It is data supplied before the common schedule is chosen. No field asserts that these numbers bound an actual profile; the numerical selection theorem later makes the schedule dominate the supplied table.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.Step.summary: The four families of costs required by a step

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.Step.text: An analytic row at indices $m,p$ sums absolute costs from derivative order zero through $m+3p$. The other three rows return the cutoff-tail, step, or mean cost at their indicated indices. This reserve is what later yields analytic control through $4P+1$ when the threshold is sampled at $m=P+1$ and $p=P$.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.Step.summary: Analytic rows reserve three extra depth orders

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.Step.text: The formal object enlarges the list of fixed constants used to choose $\mathcal B$. For each additional family of constants $c(q,n,P)$ and each requested spatial order $m$, it inserts $\sum_{q=0}^m\sum_{n=0}^{m+r(q,P)}|c(q,n,P)|$, where the nonnegative integer $r(q,P)$ reserves extra spatial derivatives. The original analytic constants are retained, and the cutoff, step and mean constants are unchanged. This is a definition of the enlarged list, not an existence theorem for the velocity. It makes the auxiliary note's extra time-order requirements explicit and permits them to be fixed before the initial frequency is chosen.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.Step.summary: The original estimates share an enlarged majorant

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.Step.text: This proposition packages the required parent, child, next-frequency, depth, radius, and phase-width inequalities at one index. It includes domination of analytic costs through $4P+1$, step and recurrence smallness, mean and full-wave rates, cutoff-tail decay, and the final residual exponent. These are numerical hypotheses for later analytic assembly, not statements about any selected velocity or Fourier cutoff.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.Step.summary: All numerical inequalities for one scheduled physical step
