TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.Step.text: The numerical budget of one scheduled step, taken for the cost table enlarged by the auxiliary time estimates, implies the original step budget with exactly the same parameters. The proof takes each original analytic cost from the part of the enlarged table that copies the original table; the cutoff, step and mean entries are retained unchanged. This ensures that adding the terminal requirements does not discard the hypotheses used by the physical construction.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.Step.summary: The enlarged schedule keeps the original step budgets

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.abs_.text: Fix finite families of the original and additional constants, a nonnegative integer exponent parameter $b$, and a reserve $r(q,P)$. Set $K(s)=320b(s+1)$. If the time order and depth satisfy $q,P\le7K(s)$ and the spatial order satisfies $m\le7K(s)+r(q,P)$, the formal statement bounds $|c(q,m,P)|$ by the enlarged threshold at $s$. Each absolute value occurs in one of its finite nonnegative sums. The statement is uniform over the admitted indices and does not depend on a constructed velocity. It proves a bound for the threshold obtained from this particular enlargement, not for an arbitrary function merely denoted by $\mathcal B$.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.abs_.summary: The enlarged majorant bounds every admitted entry

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.even.text: For arbitrary fixed real $C$ and $A$ and positive $\varepsilon$, for all sufficiently large $i$ one has $C\lambda_i^A\le\lambda_{i+1}^{\varepsilon}$. Neither $C$ nor $A$ needs to be positive. The proof first makes the parent frequency dominate $C$, then makes the adjacent exponent $K(q_{i+1})$ at least $(1+A)/\varepsilon$. Positivity of the scheduled frequency justifies the real-power identities.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.even.summary: A fixed parent polynomial fits any positive child power

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.even.text: For a frequency sequence satisfying the construction's schedule, fix real numbers $C,A$ and $\varepsilon>0$. The formal statement gives an index after which $C\lambda_{j-1}^{A}\lambda_j^{-\varepsilon}\le1$. The index may depend on $C,A,\varepsilon$ and the chosen schedule; it is not uniform over increasing derivative orders or exponents. The frequencies are positive and $\lambda_j=\lambda_{j-1}^{K_j}$ with $K_j$ tending to infinity. This is the numerical absorption used with $\varepsilon=1/12$ in the auxiliary recurrence. The conclusion is an eventual inequality, not an estimate on any prescribed initial stage.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.even.summary: Frequency separation makes every fixed loss small

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.even.text: Fix a spatial order $m$ and a time order $q$. For all sufficiently large $i$, with $K=K(q_{i+2})=320b(q_{i+2}+1)$, both orders are at most $7K$, and the step depth plus $q+2$ is at most $7K$. Since the depth is $6K$, the remaining growing margin accommodates the fixed extra time derivatives. The starting index may depend on both fixed orders.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.even.summary: Every fixed derivative order eventually fits the reserve

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.exis.text: Produces one threshold $N$ such that every admissible parameter record with $\lambda_0\ge N$ satisfies the lifetime bounds: $\tau_1\le1/4$ and, for every $j$, $0<\tau_{j+1}\le\lambda_j^{-1/16}$ and $4\tau_{j+2}\le\tau_{j+1}$. The proof combines the schedule estimate with the explicit floor $4^{16}$. The threshold precedes the universally quantified parameter record, so it is not chosen separately at each induction step.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.exis.summary: A single frequency threshold supplies all lifetime bounds

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.exis.text: Given a finite family of signed order-dependent costs, an exponent at least one, comparison constant at least 240, and strength constant at least two, every sufficiently large initial frequency admits one schedule with lifetime bounds. At every stage it dominates the absolute values of all tabulated costs through the stated sevenfold exponent cutoff in both indices. The chosen threshold and all prescribed constants remain exactly fixed.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.exis.summary: One schedule absorbs all prescribed fixed-order costs

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.exis.text: Fixing the cost functions and a sufficient absolute exponent first, the theorem chooses a lower bound so every larger initial frequency admits parameters with the prescribed constants, lifetime bounds, and the numerical step budget at every index. The floor also includes the requested initial constraint, $e^4$, and the cutoff constant. The assumption that step costs are at least one remains explicit.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.exis.summary: A single initial threshold supplies all numerical step budgets

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.exis.text: Fix the main and auxiliary constant families, an extra derivative reserve, and the main numerical parameters. Assume that $b$ meets the main step's stated exponent lower bound, the comparison constant is at least $240$, the strength constant is at least $2$, and each step constant is at least $1$. The formal statement fixes the enlarged threshold and then finds $N_1$ such that every $N\ge N_1$ admits the required frequency schedule with $\lambda_0=N$. It preserves the main lifetime and step estimates. An auxiliary constant of orders $q,m,P$ is at most $\lambda_i$ when $q,P\le7K(q_{i+2})$ and $m\le7K(q_{i+2})+r(q,P)$. This selects numerical parameters; it does not by itself construct the Euler fields.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.exis.summary: The threshold precedes the initial frequency choice

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.firs.text: Sets the stationary shear's tilt to the coupling ratio associated with gain $4\log(\lambda_3)$. The input is a certified parameter record: its threshold floor and frequency recurrence already force positive large frequencies. The first-wave selection later exposes the gain and small-tilt inequalities in the form needed by the stationary geometry constructors.

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.pare.text: If the initial frequency is at least $e$ and the activation time t₀ is nonnegative, the child endpoint time P.slab (n+1) t₀ is at least $\lambda_n^{-1/8}$. The proof bounds the logarithmic factor in the scheduled half-length from below. Here slab is the final time of the interval starting at zero, not the duration measured from activation.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.pare.summary: The endpoint time bounds the parent scale

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.slab.text: Defines the stage endpoint from its index and activation time. Index zero has the fixed endpoint $S_0=1$; at index $n+1$ it is $S_{n+1}=t+2\tau_{n+1}$, the activation plus twice the scheduled half-length. The definition fixes the time bookkeeping before any stage field is selected.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.slab.summary: The final time of each stage

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.slab.text: Under the same initial-frequency and nonnegative-activation hypotheses, the inverse endpoint time to any natural power q is at most $\lambda_n^{q/8}$. Positivity follows from the parent-frequency lower bound before taking reciprocals. The estimate makes extraction of a fixed time derivative polynomial in the parent frequency, including the case $q=0$.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.slab.summary: Inverse time powers cost parent frequency

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.slab.text: Unfolds the positive-index endpoint into the activation time plus twice the preceding-index half-length. This keeps the indexing of stages and physical half-lengths explicit in later inequalities. Strictly later endpoints require positivity of the half-length, supplied by the lifetime certificate rather than this equality.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.slab.summary: Each later endpoint follows its activation

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.slab.text: Computes the zero-stage endpoint as one, regardless of the activation argument. This is the stationary parent convention used to start the recursion. The equality follows directly from pattern matching and does not by itself assert existence of a stationary Euler field on that interval.

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.step.text: For the frequency schedule, let $b\ge1$ be an integer and $K(s)=320b(s+1)$. At the internal step numbered $i\ge0$, which constructs the paper's wave $j=i+1$, the formal definition sets the depth equal to $6K(q_{i+2})=6K_{j+1}$. This is exactly (7.2) after accounting for the index shift. The depth and derivative orders are nonnegative integers. The definition chooses how many profiles enter the finite expansion; it does not itself prove the expansion estimates or smallness of its remainder.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.step.summary: Fixes the depth using the next derivative order

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.step.text: The floor is the maximum of one, the prescribed absolute exponent, the flow loss $\max(a,1)+(\max(a,1)+p)+1$, and six times the recurrence exponent. It is chosen before the frequency schedule. Requiring the schedule exponent to dominate this floor supplies all four exponent comparisons used by the step budget.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.step.summary: One exponent absorbs radius, flow, and recurrence losses

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.step.text: When the parameter threshold function is exactly the table’s fixed-order threshold, the exponent dominates the stated floor, the initial frequency meets the cutoff floor, and every step cost is at least one, all stages satisfy the numerical step budget. The proof uses schedule growth and cost domination, including the analytic derivative reserve. It does not establish that the supplied costs bound the actual hierarchy.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.step.summary: The selected threshold supplies every step inequality

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.sum_.text: For $\mathsf D\ge1$, nonnegative coefficients on a finite set, exponents bounded by $b$, and coefficient sum at most $\Gamma$, the sum of coefficient-weighted powers of $\mathsf D$ is at most $\Gamma\mathsf D^b$. The argument compares every power with $\mathsf D^b$ before summing. An empty index set is allowed and leaves the explicit coefficient-sum hypothesis.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.sum_.summary: A finite sum shares its largest parent exponent

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.term.text: The exponent $K(q_{i+1})=320b(q_{i+1}+1)$ relating $\lambda_i$ to $\lambda_{i+1}$ tends to infinity with $i$. The proof compares it from below with the already diverging order sequence $q_{i+1}$. This is the quantitative separation behind the ability to absorb any fixed parent-frequency polynomial into a positive power of the next frequency.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.term.summary: Adjacent frequency exponents tend to infinity

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.term.text: For any admissible parameter record, the frequency sequence is monotone. The recurrence raises the preceding frequency to the scheduled positive exponent, and the initial frequency is already greater than one. This supplies comparisons between parent, child, and later frequencies without changing the chosen sequence.

The frequencies $\lambda_i$ of an admissible parameter schedule tend to $+\infty$ as the stage index $i$ tends to infinity. This is stronger than a sequence of occasional large values: every fixed real lower bound is exceeded for all sufficiently large $i$. The proof uses the schedule recurrence $\lambda_{i+1}=\lambda_i^{K(q_{i+1})}$ and the initial frequency strictly above one.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.term.summary: The scheduled frequencies tend to infinity

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.term.text: Every admissible parameter schedule has $\lambda_0>1$. The proof uses the positive exponent parameter $b$, the logarithmic lower floor $\log\mathcal B(1)\ge4K(2)^3$ on the threshold at order one, and the initial-frequency condition $\lambda_0\ge\mathcal B(1)$. No auxiliary estimate is assumed. This excludes degenerate bases when real powers and growth comparisons are used later.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.term.summary: The initial scheduled frequency exceeds one

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.term.text: The order sequence $q_i$ tends to infinity. The proof combines frequency growth with the rule choosing the greatest admissible order and the fixed threshold function $\mathcal B$. Thus every fixed derivative order eventually fits the schedule; the theorem does not assert that one stage works simultaneously for all unbounded orders.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.term.summary: The scheduled derivative orders tend to infinity

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.term.text: Let the frequency schedule be fixed, assume $\lambda_0\ge e$, and let the activation time of a child interval be nonnegative. If $T$ is that interval's scheduled right endpoint and $\mu$ is the parent frequency, the formal statement proves $T^{-1}\le\mu^{1/8}$. The schedule gives $T>0$, so this reciprocal is the ordinary reciprocal. Consequently a derivative extraction cost $i!T^{-i}$ is at most $i!\mu^{i/8}$ for fixed $i$. The result establishes the time-scale part of the auxiliary note's polynomial bounds; it says nothing by itself about the reciprocal label radius or other powers of $\mathsf D$.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.term.summary: Time extraction costs a fixed parent power

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.text: Defines finite compatible histories by two constructors: an initial certified base, and appending an actual successor of the current tip. The type is indexed by both length and tip. This records compatibility in the type itself, which later allows a single infinite construction to retain every earlier stage without reselecting it.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.summary: A finite history indexed by its exact last stages

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.activeSl.text: Combines monotonicity of retrieved activation times with reverse monotonicity of their endpoints. The current closed active interval is therefore contained in each earlier retrieved active interval. The result is a domain inclusion for one compatible prefix, not a universal comparison of independently chosen stage intervals.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.activeSl.summary: The current interval lies inside every earlier active interval

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.exists_l.text: For $k+1\le n$, extracts a genuine successor step linking the two consecutive retrieved pairs of stages. The equality also identifies the later history as the earlier one with that step appended. This is the key bridge from compatibility encoded by prefixes to quantitative relations between successive physical crossings.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.exists_l.summary: Consecutive historical tips share an actual recorded successor

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.initial_.text: Retrieves the initial tip of any compatible prefix and proves its exit coupling equals $2\pi$. The base constructor supplies the equality, and appended steps preserve the initial lookup. This fixes the normalization for the finite coupling recurrence without assuming that every later coupling is unchanged.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.initial_.summary: Every compatible history starts with coupling two pi

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.later_wa.text: For an existing prefix and a selected later wave, proves the first coupling lies between $\pi$ and $4\pi$ and the coupling ratio equals the next scheduled value. The gradient is explicitly that of the actual parent. The base-frequency floor $e^4$ and compatible prefix are required before the child stage is constructed.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.later_wa.summary: The selected exit has the correct physical couplings

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.lookup.text: Given $k\le n$, recursively retrieves the pair of stages and compatible history at index $k$ from a prefix of length $n$. Both objects are returned together. At the current endpoint it returns the whole prefix; otherwise it descends into the previously recorded prefix, never choosing a different earlier construction.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.lookup.summary: Retrieving the history at an earlier index

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.lookup_a.text: Proves that the activation stored in any earlier retrieved pair is at most the current pair’s activation. The index restriction $k\le n$ is essential. Induction over actual appended steps uses their nonnegative activation increments, rather than imposing monotonicity as an unrelated property of a separate time sequence.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.lookup_a.summary: Earlier waves activate no later than the current wave

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.lookup_a.text: If $k\le n$, looking up index $k$ after appending a successor gives the same pair and history as looking it up before the append. The two proofs of the index bound may differ, but no earlier data change. This is the finite compatibility invariant used when extracting a common sequence.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.lookup_a.summary: Appending a stage preserves every earlier prefix

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.lookup_l.text: For indices $k\le l\le n$, first retrieving the prefix at $l$ and then retrieving $k$ gives the same pair and history as retrieving $k$ directly. The proof follows the two ways a prefix is built. This guarantees coherence of historical stage data across nested uses of the lookup operation.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.lookup_l.summary: Repeated restriction agrees with direct restriction

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.lookup_s.text: Computes lookup at the prefix’s own index, returning exactly its current tip and history as a dependent pair. The result is stronger than equality of projected velocities. It supports later identity arguments where the stored successor must be attached to precisely the prefix that generated it.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.lookup_s.summary: Looking up the current stage returns the whole prefix

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.next_act.text: Places the next physical comparison interval inside every earlier active interval recorded by the prefix. It first fits inside the current interval using the lifetime bounds on the half-lengths $\tau_j$, then uses the prefix containment theorem. This lets the next construction safely consult old wave equations throughout its own complete comparison window.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.next_act.summary: The next comparison remains inside all recorded wave intervals

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.next_cou.text: Assuming the base frequency is at least $e^4$, bounds the first coupling at a newly selected crossing between $\pi$ and $4\pi$. The candidate crossing must start from the current exit coupling and scheduled ratio, and target the next scheduled ratio. Only the existing prefix and this comparison are required; the new child stage need not already exist.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.next_cou.summary: The next coupling is controlled before building its child

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.schedule.text: For a consecutive pair of historical indices inside the prefix, obtains the scheduled crossing relation between their exit couplings. It extracts the recorded successor linking the two retrieved pairs and applies that step’s crossing theorem. Thus the recurrence uses real recorded crossings throughout the finite history.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.schedule.summary: Every adjacent pair inherits its actual physical crossing

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.slab_le_.text: Shows that the current parent endpoint is no larger than the endpoint of any earlier retrieved parent. The proof composes containment supplied by the actual appended tips. This transports older smoothness and wave estimates to the smaller current interval while preserving which earlier stage they describe.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.slab_le_.summary: The current endpoint fits inside every earlier slab

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.tip_pare.text: For a certified finite prefix, the parent endpoint time at its tip is at most one. The initial case uses the lifetime bound on the first slab, and an appended step uses the strict decrease of the next endpoint. This ensures that all subsequent parent estimates apply on a duration no longer than one.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.tip_pare.summary: Every parent slab stays inside the unit interval

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.text: Stores a continuous torus velocity, a normalized periodic pressure and a two-time flow for one specified stage and activation. Smoothness, oddness, divergence freedom, Fourier support, deformation and the one-sided bound $D^2\pi_n\le(\sum_{i<n}\lambda_i^{-1})I$ are certified. The residual is the physical momentum expression for these same fields, and a stored identity equates it with the Leray-projected momentum on the closed slab $[0,S_n]$.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.summary: One actual truncated parent with its pressure and flow

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.text: This record contains a smaller positive time slab inside the stage domain, its actual hierarchy geometry, matching momentum residuals, and periodic Fourier-band residual data. It also stores a half-unit residual derivative bound and an odd phase-independent residual profile with the correct pulled-back values. These are certificate fields for an already given stage, not conclusions available from arbitrary geometry.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.summary: The inductive parent restricted to the next endpoint interval

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ce.text: Assume the launch relation identifies the fixed carrier with the forward-flow adjoint applied to $\kappa(t_0)$, and assume $\kappa$ solves the central adjoint equation. Then $\kappa$ equals the flow-transported label wave vector on the active interval. The origin-fixing property and uniqueness of the covector equation connect the two constructions.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ce.summary: The chosen central covector is the transported carrier

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ce.text: Given the launch identity and central wave data on the active interval for the central velocity gradient, this theorem rewrites the central wave using the actual flow-transported label wave vector and strain along the parent trajectory. Since the flow fixes the origin, the strain is unchanged. All central-wave inequalities are transported with the same constant $\mathsf D$.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ce.summary: Use the transported carrier in the central wave data

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.de.text: Given the restriction of a stage to a smaller slab $[0,T]$, the stage flow still satisfies the lattice-equivariant deformation bounds on the smaller interval with the parent frequency as its bound. The proof restricts the flow, lattice-equivariance and deformation estimates using the inclusion of the slab. It does not reconstruct the flow or enlarge the original stage interval.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.de.summary: The restricted parent retains its deformation bounds

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ex.text: Chooses absolute exponent floors and then a monotone order budget for any nonnegative seed costs. Under the actual central-wave, inactivity, positive-weight and leading-profile assumptions, plus $L^6\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, it proves the measured recurrence, all retained-level bounds and an order-two remainder estimate. The reserve is $H=\max(m,3)+3P$ and $L=\mathsf D^{2a+b_0}$. These estimates precede selection of the final frequency schedule.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ex.summary: One order budget controls the actual finite hierarchy

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ex.text: The stage transverse bound remains valid when the weight is $\mathrm{freq}^{3/4}\lVert b(t)\rVert$ instead of the central amplitude norm. The positive carrier frequency makes this a positive constant rescaling, and both source and solution sizes change by the same factor. The same envelope exponent and parent loss are retained.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ex.summary: Normalize the weight without changing the solve constant

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ex.text: There are an integer $A\ge30$ and constants $K_m\ge0$ such that the following holds for every stage on a slab. Suppose $\lambda_j\ge2$, $0\le t_0<T$, $0<\ell\le\lambda_j^{-9A}$, $\lambda>0$ with $|\kappa(t_0)|=\lambda$, the carrier is the pulled-back covector at the origin, a center wave runs on $[t_0,T]$ with scale $\mathsf D=\lambda_j^9$, the approximation data have depth $N\ge1$ with leading wave inactive before $t_0$, and $\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|b|$ is continuous and positive on $[t_0,T]$. If, for all $m$, the four transverse time coefficients have unweighted time norms at most $C(m)\mathsf D^e$, then for every $m$ and $2\le i\le N$ the oscillatory velocity-and-pressure measure is at most a transverse time cost depending on $m,q,K_m,C(m)$, times $\mathsf D^{20+e(q+1)}$, times the oscillatory source measure.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ex.summary: The selected transverse solve has a uniform time recurrence bound

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ex.text: One envelope exponent and nonnegative order table work for all restricted inductive parents. With frequency at least two, compatible launch data, a central wave and inactive leading hierarchy input, the actual levels satisfy the transverse-solve bound with loss $(\mathrm{frequency}^9)^{20}$. The weight here is the unnormalized central amplitude norm; normalization is handled in the next module.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ex.summary: The inductive stage supplies the transverse recurrence

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ex.text: There is a nonnegative table $V_N$ such that every restricted stage with frequency $\lambda\ge2$ has order-$j$ velocity derivatives bounded by $V_N(\lambda^9)^j$ whenever $1\le j\le N$. The table is chosen before the stage. Order zero is deliberately absent: only derivatives of the velocity are needed here.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ex.summary: One derivative table controls all inductive parents

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ex.text: Chooses order-dependent nonnegative constants for the unweighted finite derivative seminorm of the actual pulled-back parent residual. It assumes initial frequency at least one, slab duration at most one, nonnegative label scale and $\ell\mathsf D^6\le1$. For every order the bound is $C_m\lambda_{n+1}^{-5/2}$; phase width is unrestricted because this residual is independent of phase.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ex.summary: The actual parent residual has the level-two size

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ex.text: For a nonnegative input cost array and time order $q$, choose coefficient cost arrays before the stage data. A parent admissible on a positive slab of length at most one, with frequency $\lambda_n\ge2$, a launch covector whose transported carrier at the central label has length $\lambda>0$ at some time of the slab, and the supplied velocity mixed bound with amplitude $A\ge1$, yields jets of the forward coframe, inverse coframe, strain, normalized covector, and reciprocal squared length, at scale $\mathsf D=\lambda_n^9$. All share spatial slope sixteen; reciprocal time growth uses its separate explicit amplitude.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ex.summary: Derive all flow coefficient jets on the selected parent slab

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ex.text: For the actual admissible parent, velocity and residual mixed bounds through order $q$ imply a mixed bound for the residual composed with the parent flow. The residual amplitude keeps $\lambda_{n+1}^{-5/2}$ and is multiplied by $(1+\mathsf DA)^q$, with $\mathsf D=\lambda_n^9$ and spatial slope six. Costs are chosen before stage data, and the statement does not request an extra residual time derivative.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ex.summary: Pull back the residual while retaining its small frequency power

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.fl.text: The flow of an inductive parent fixes the origin at every time in the restricted slab. The proof uses the odd stage velocity and uniqueness of trajectories. This permits central strain and covector identities to be evaluated at the spatial origin instead of along a potentially moving central trajectory.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.fl.summary: Oddness keeps the parent flow at the origin

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ph.text: Given a stage restricted to $[0,T]$, a duration $T\le1$, a leading input $L$ and a depth, this definition builds the physical approximation data. Its residual is exactly the pulled-back parent residual profile stored with the restriction, with the stage’s momentum identity proving the required value equation. This ensures that later residual estimates apply to the same field that enters the selected hierarchy.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ph.summary: Building the approximation with the parent’s actual residual

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ph.text: The leading input of the newly assembled physical approximation is, by definition, the supplied input $L$. This equality records that the construction preserves the chosen wave, rather than selecting a second seed. It is valid at every depth and is used when transporting inactivity, pressure normalization, and switch identities into the approximation data.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ph.summary: The assembled approximation keeps the supplied leading wave

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ph.text: The physical approximation’s parent residual is exactly the residual profile already stored in the restricted parent. This definitional equality is important for quantitative estimates: no residual with merely similar bounds has been substituted. The theorem supplies identity of the fields, while the residual’s momentum interpretation is proved in the constructor.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ph.summary: The assembled approximation keeps the supplied parent residual

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ph.text: At depth at least two, a leading input over the parent restricted to $[0,T]$ gives the full set of qualitative properties of the physical approximation: smoothness of its fields, their exact Eulerian equations and the parities of the odd construction. The proof applies the general assembly theorem using the parent’s actual flow, smooth velocity and pressure, periodicity, oddness, and divergence freedom. The result provides qualitative premises for the later Fourier cutoff, not a numerical residual bound.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ph.summary: The restricted parent supplies all qualitative approximation properties

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ph.text: If the label envelope has positive radius $\ell\le D^{-3}$ and the parent frequency satisfies $2\le\lambda_n\le D$, every nonzero value of the Eulerian oscillation on $[0,T]$ lies within distance $\lambda_n^{-1}$ of a point of $\mathbb Z^3$. Inactivity first locates the inverse-flow label in the periodic envelope; the actual parent flow converts that to spatial distance.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ph.summary: The Eulerian oscillation stays near a lattice point

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ph.text: For an activation time $0<\tau\le T$, a leading input inactive before $\tau$ or outside the support of the periodized radial envelope, and retained depth at least one, the actual Eulerian oscillation vanishes at every time in $[0,\tau]$. The support envelope is the closed support of the periodized radial cutoff. This theorem concerns the oscillatory correction, not the generally nonzero mean correction.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ph.summary: The oscillation is zero through positive activation

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ra.text: For a restricted stage with frequency at least two, the forward flow derivative and the inverse flow derivative along the forward flow are each bounded by the ninth power of that frequency. The record originally supplies the smaller deformation bound. Enlarging it puts both operators on the common parent scale used in the transverse estimates.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ra.summary: Put both flow derivatives on the common parent scale

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ra.text: For an inductive stage restricted to its slab, the physical parent velocity gradient is bounded by the ninth power of the stage frequency at every point of the restricted slab. The proof reads the actual strain from the stored geometry. Unlike the coframe enlargement lemma, this statement needs no extra lower bound on the frequency.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ra.summary: The parent strain obeys the common ninth-power bound

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.re.text: For a stage with residual $R_s$ and flow $X_s$ on $[0,T]$, a supplied mixed bound on $R_s(t,X_s(0,t,x))$ transfers to the residual profile. Under $T\le1$, nonnegative $\ell,\mathsf D,A$ with $\ell\mathsf D^p\le1$, constants $C(n)\ge0$, and that mixed bound through time order $q$ with slope $p$ and amplitude $A$, the time norm $\sum_{i\le q}\frac{T^i}{i!}\|\partial_t^i(\cdot)\|_{[n]}$ of the residual profile is bounded by the finite label cost $(q+1)W_n\sum_{j\le n}C(j)$ times $A$, $W_n$ counting multi-indices $(\alpha,j)$ with $|\alpha|+j\le n$. The theorem does not establish the residual's small amplitude.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.re.summary: The residual profile inherits its mixed time bound

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.re.text: Proves the same full-slab residual bound for the later-wave input. Besides the tail and numerical budget, it requires the exact leading-input identity, even seed, activation-primary two-jet estimate and a bound for $|\widetilde\chi'|\gamma$. The conclusion uses the selected seed and completion structure, rather than treating the switch forcing as an independent arbitrary residual.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.re.summary: The later residual includes its actual activation forcing

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.re.text: Assuming the numerical budget, coefficient caps, tail estimate and both switch sources equal to zero, proves an order-one half-Hölder residual bound of $\lambda_{i+2}^{-7/2}$ on the full slab. This is the first-wave case of the common residual estimate. It uses the actual hierarchy remainder; the bound is not inferred merely from zero activation.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.re.summary: The first residual is controlled by the expansion tail

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.sc.text: Derives all four velocity readout estimates from a numerical step budget, coefficient caps, parent Bernstein bounds and measured-level estimates through order $P+1$ at depth $P$. Inactivity controls the oscillation before activation, while the positive weight is used only on the active interval. The full-depth graph estimate and central derivative estimate refer to the same approximation and the same cost table.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.sc.summary: The measured hierarchy yields the scheduled velocity bounds

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.sm.text: The stage pressure is jointly smooth on the restricted closed slab $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3$. Smoothness is inherited by restriction from the original stage domain. This allows the endpoint mean problem to use the same pressure while temporal derivatives and momentum residuals are interpreted on the smaller interval.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.sm.summary: The parent pressure stays smooth on the smaller slab

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.sm.text: For a stage restricted to a smaller slab, the actual stage residual is jointly smooth on that closed slab. The proof uses the stage’s smooth momentum residual and the equality recorded on that interval. This gives regularity of the concrete forcing supplied to the mean equation, rather than merely of an independently chosen residual profile.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.sm.summary: The restricted momentum residual is smooth

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.sm.text: Restricting a stage to a smaller slab restricts its joint smoothness assertion for velocity to the selected endpoint slab. The proof uses inclusion of the time intervals and leaves the whole spatial domain unchanged. This is a transport of an existing regularity theorem, not a new regularity estimate for truncated data.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.sm.summary: The parent velocity stays smooth on the smaller slab

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.StageCoef.text: This proposition packages positive widths, the inverse-radius identity, carrier and deformation bounds, chart smoothness, and raw and scaled coframe jets for one restricted stage. Its final fields bound the slow rows by an order constant times $D^{a+1}$ and the fast covector by that constant times $D^2\mathrm{freq}^{3/2}$. Each field refers to the same supplied stage geometry.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.StageCoef.summary: The actual parent chart with all coefficient bounds

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.StageCoef.text: For $\mathsf D\ge1$ and $C_1\ge0$, the maximum of $\mathsf D$ and $\mathsf D^2+C_1\mathsf D^8$ is bounded by $(1+C_1)\mathsf D^8$. Although the stage coefficient caps are passed as a hypothesis, none of them is used in this numerical inequality. The result only consolidates already supplied coframe and first-derivative allowances for the cutoff tail.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.StageCoef.summary: The first coframe derivative fits one parent power

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.StageCoef.text: Given actual stage coefficient caps, $\mathsf D\ge1$, nonnegative frequency, and $b\ge a+1$ with $a\ge7$, any $K$ dominating the source-order cost at order $m$ covers both centered advection coefficients. The slow cap is at most $K\mathsf D^b$; the fast cap is at most $K\mathsf D^b\mathrm{freq}^{3/2}$. The parent exponent does not depend on the derivative order.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.StageCoef.summary: A fixed parent power covers slow and fast sources

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.StagePres.text: Collects the carrier bound, scaled inverse-deformation derivatives, adjoint, strain and longitudinal-projection derivatives, and the parent's half-Hölder gradient estimate. The constants $K$ and $K_{\rm parent}$ are fixed-order scalar costs, while parent powers of $\mathsf D=\lambda_n^9$ are explicit. This proposition is the geometric input to the higher and mean pressure bounds for one actual parent slab.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.StagePres.summary: The pressure uses fixed first and second derivative bounds

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_on.text: Chooses a parent exponent $p$, radius floor $s_0$ and order constants before the parent slab or forcing. For label radius $\lambda_j^{-9s}$ with $s\ge s_0$, parent frequency at least two, duration at most one and a force equal to its own phase average, the selected mean solver's velocity at order $n$ is bounded by its force at order $n+1$ times the explicit parent power $\lambda_j^{9(p+2+2s)}$. This estimate concerns the actual solver used by the hierarchy.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_on.summary: The actual endpoint mean inverse loses one derivative

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_on.text: There exists a threshold $N\ge4$ such that, for any inductive parameter sequence with $\lambda_0\ge N$, every stage $n$, every $T$ with $0<T\le S_n$ and every nonzero carrier $k$, the stage admits a restriction to $[0,T]$ carrying its parent coefficients and pulled-back residual. The theorem constructs the required residual and geometry certificates. The nonzero carrier and the interval inclusion $[0,T]\subseteq[0,S_n]$ are explicit and cannot be dropped.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_on.summary: A single frequency threshold builds every restricted parent

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_re.text: Let $R_j$ be the residual of a smooth periodic stage on $[0,S_j]$, with $S_j>0$ and $\lambda_j\ge0$. For every nonnegative integer $q$, the formal statement represents $\partial_t^qR_j(t)$ by a continuous field on $\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3$ whose Fourier coefficients vanish above $4\lambda_j^5$, for all $0\le t\le S_j$. Time differentiation fixes the physical point and is one-sided at the endpoints. The representation agrees with the periodic lift throughout that interval; values assigned outside it are irrelevant to this conclusion. This supplies the residual half of the Fourier-support sentence following auxiliary Lemma 1.3. The velocity band is a separate result.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_re.summary: Time differentiation does not enlarge spatial support

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_sl.text: There are constants $C_m\ge0$, chosen before the stage and time order, with the following property. On a positive stage interval, let $\lambda_j>0$. If $|\partial_t^qU_j|\le A$ everywhere, with $A\ge0$, then $\|D_x^m\partial_t^qU_j\|\le C_mA\lambda_j^{5m}$. The same implication holds for $R_j$ with any nonnegative bound $B$ in place of $A$. Both estimates include the time endpoints and use the operator norm of the full $m$th spatial derivative on the periodic lift. The paper sums coordinate partial derivatives; passing between these conventions changes only constants depending on $m$. Neither bound chooses the eventual exponent or stage in auxiliary Lemma 1.3.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_sl.summary: One spatial constant works for all time derivatives

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_sl.text: For fixed $q,A$, this selects an exponent $A\prime\ge A$ before the stage. If the stage frequency is at least two, its slab has positive length, velocity derivatives through $q$ are bounded by $\mu^A$, and the single order-$q$ residual derivative is bounded by one, then velocity derivatives through $q+1$ are bounded by $\mu^{A\prime}$. Bernstein and Hölder-Leray estimates control the differentiated advection.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_sl.summary: One more velocity time derivative costs a parent power

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_st.text: The theorem selects a nonnegative sequence $(C_m)$ uniformly before the stage and order. For a restricted stage of duration at most one, parent frequency $\mu\ge1$, and a positive child frequency equal to the length of the transported carrier at the central label at time $t_0$, it supplies the full set of stage coefficient caps (label and phase scales, carrier, deformation, coframe, slow-row and fast-coefficient bounds) with $\mathsf D=\mu^9$, $\ell=\mathsf D^{-a}$, and $h=\mathrm{freq}^{-1/2}$ whenever $a\ge7$.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_st.summary: One sequence bounds coefficients of every inductive stage

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_st.text: Selects $K\ge1$ and $K_{\rm parent}\ge0$ before the stage, carrier, frequency or radius exponent. On a slab of duration at most one, with parent frequency at least one and a carrier of positive length $\lambda$ at a slab time, every exponent $a\ge7$ gives the required pressure-geometry caps. Only fixed derivative orders one and two enter the selection.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_st.summary: One fixed pair of constants controls every stage pressure geometry

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_st.text: A single nonnegative sequence $(L_m)$ bounds relay coefficients for all restricted inductive stages and every time subset of the slab. With $a\ge16$, $\mathsf D=\mu^9$, and the selected widths, the allowance is $2L_m\mathsf D^{15+a}$. The proof obtains transported coefficient jets and absorbs the inverse label width using its exact power definition.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_st.summary: Every restricted stage has a fixed-power relay allowance

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_te.text: Fix nonnegative integers $q,A$. The formal statement chooses an integer $A'\ge A$ and constants $C_m\ge0$ before the stage. Assume $S_j>0$, $\lambda_j\ge2$, and, for every $i\le q$, the pointwise bounds $|\partial_t^iU_j|\le\lambda_j^A$ and $|\partial_t^iR_j|\le\lambda_{j+1}^{-5/2}$ on the whole stage. It then bounds velocity through time order $q+1$ by $\lambda_j^{A'}$, and its $m$th spatial derivative by $C_m\lambda_j^{A'+5m}$. Residual derivatives are bounded by $C_m\lambda_j^{5m}\lambda_{j+1}^{-5/2}$ only through time order $q$. Spatial derivatives use multilinear operator norms. Thus the velocity gains one time order without assuming the corresponding new residual derivative.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_te.summary: The momentum equation advances velocity regularity

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_ve.text: Produces nonnegative constants $K_k$ depending only on derivative order, bounding the order-$k$ spatial derivative of any certified stage velocity by $K_k\lambda_n^{5k+1}$. The frequency must satisfy $\lambda_n\ge1$ and time must lie in the closed slab $[0,S_n]$. The estimate combines velocity size $\lambda_n$ with Fourier support of radius $2\lambda_n^5$, uniformly in the stage and spatial point.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_ve.summary: Fourier support bounds every spatial derivative

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_ve.text: There exists a nonnegative sequence $C(N)$, chosen before any induction parameters or stage, such that every stage with frequency at least one satisfies a jet bound through order $N+1$. The bound is $C(N)\,\mathrm{frequency}^{5(N+1)+1}$. Summing individual Bernstein constants makes the same constant cover all lower derivative orders without depending on the chosen stage.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_ve.summary: One Bernstein constant covers every lower spatial derivative

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_ve.text: Chooses one threshold above which the actual stage gradient is bounded by the ninth power of its frequency throughout its closed slab. The Bernstein constant at order one is absorbed into one extra frequency power. The threshold concerns the frequency of the specified stage, not necessarily the global initial frequency.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_ve.summary: A uniform threshold absorbs the gradient constant

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_ve.text: For every order budget $m$, selects a uniform constant controlling all derivative orders $1\le k\le m$ at coframe scale $\mathsf D=\lambda_n^9$. The proof sums the Bernstein constants and uses $5k+1\le9k$. The exclusion of $k=0$ is essential to that power comparison; the separate velocity bound handles order zero.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_ve.summary: The parent scale controls all positive derivative orders

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_ve.text: Let $U_j$ be a smooth periodic stage on $[0,S_j]$, with $S_j>0$. For every nonnegative integer $q$, the formal statement represents $\partial_t^qU_j(t)$ as a continuous field on $\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3$ with Fourier support at most $2\lambda_j^5$, for every $0\le t\le S_j$. Its periodic lift agrees pointwise with the time derivative at fixed physical position. Endpoint derivatives are taken within the stage interval, and no agreement is asserted outside it. This proves the velocity part of the Fourier-support claim after auxiliary Lemma 1.3. It does not supply the residual's larger band or a bound on the size of either field.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_ve.summary: Every time derivative retains the stage cutoff

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.norm_mean.text: Takes a supplied order-zero half-Hölder estimate for a pressure Hessian and derives a pointwise operator-norm bound with parent exponent $6r+2(a+1)+2$ and decay $\lambda^{-5/2}$. Positivity assumptions control all scalar enlargements. The proof explicitly extracts boundedness from the Hölder predicate before using its supremum, avoiding reliance on an unchecked total supremum.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.norm_mean.summary: The mean Hessian norm follows from its closed-slab Hölder bound

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.norm_stag.text: Assuming geometry caps, measured level bounds at orders one and two, a positive bounded active weight and inactivity outside the selected support, bounds the Hessian norm of the actual higher oscillatory pressure by a fixed parent power times $\lambda^{-5/12}$. The conclusion holds on the full slab, with inactivity supplying control before activation.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.norm_stag.summary: The actual higher pressure has decay of order five twelfths

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.norm_stag.text: From pressure-geometry caps and order-two measured bounds at levels $2$ through $H$, proves a global-in-space Hessian norm bound for the actual mean pressure. It sums the mean equations, uses phase independence to control physical graph norms, and applies the periodic Poisson multiplier estimate. The result has decay $\lambda^{-5/2}$ with the explicit parent power $\mathsf D^{6r+2(a+1)+2}$.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.norm_stag.summary: The actual mean pressure has the required Hessian norm

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.ofTruncat.text: Builds the stage at index $n$ from an actual truncated child and supplied scheduled bounds. The hypotheses that the slab length equals the induction slab $T$ for stage $n$ and that the cutoff radius equals $\lambda_n^5$ identify its time slab and cutoff radius with the induction parameters. Velocity size at most $\lambda_n$, flow deformation, residual size at most $\lambda_{n+1}^{-3}$, and the cumulative upper pressure-Hessian bound $D^2\pi\le(\sum_{i<n}\lambda_i^{-1})I$ are hypotheses. Smoothness, parity, spectrum, and the Poisson equation come from the child.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.ofTruncat.summary: Use the actual cutoff child as an inductive stage

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.ofTruncat.text: The pressure of the stage built from a truncated child is exactly the child’s Poisson pressure, under the constructor’s full hypotheses. Substituting the slab and cutoff-radius equalities makes this definitional. The theorem preserves the pressure used in the child equation; it does not derive the separately supplied pressure-Hessian estimate.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.ofTruncat.summary: The stage retains the cutoff child pressure

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.ofTruncat.text: Under the same slab, radius, and scheduled-bound inputs as the stage constructor, its velocity is exactly the velocity of the truncated child. The proof substitutes the index equalities and reduces definitions. This guards against accidentally proving induction estimates for a field different from the one produced by Fourier truncation.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.ofTruncat.summary: The stage retains the cutoff child velocity

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.periodic_.text: Proves spatial periodicity of the Euclidean lift at every real time. Integer translations have the same image in the unit torus, so the result follows directly from the quotient representation. No smoothness, endpoint nesting, or equation of motion is needed for this representation fact.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.periodic_.summary: The lifted stage respects all lattice translations

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.potential.text: Combines a supplied one-sided leading-pressure estimate with operator-norm bounds for higher and mean pressures of the same approximation. If the cost and exponent budgets dominate all three contributions, the Hessian of the canonical potential is bounded above by the parent's Hessian plus the scheduled $\lambda^{-1/4}$ term. The leading contribution remains a signed quadratic-form estimate throughout.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.potential.summary: The actual pressure increment has a common upper Hessian bound

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.residual.text: Defines the physical momentum residual using the actual stage velocity and pressure, with the time derivative taken within the closed slab $[0,S_n]$. This ties the error estimate to a concrete Euler expression. The stored identity between this residual and the Leray-projected momentum residual is what permits rewriting it in projected form.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.residual.summary: The momentum error for the stored pressure

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.text: Given the scalar cost inequality and an exponent dominating the common residual exponent, bounds the tail graph factor and activation graph factor separately by $\Gamma\mathsf D^b$. Nonnegative costs justify dropping the other summand from the total, and $\mathsf D\ge1$ permits enlargement of powers. No residual field is estimated by this arithmetic lemma alone.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.summary: Each residual contribution fits the common step bound

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.text: Defines the common parent exponent as $2(\max(a,1)+1)+p$, where $p$ is the primary activation loss. The first term accounts for the two graph derivatives needed by the residual Hölder estimate. The integer maximum ensures the formula remains defined at small radius exponents, though the selected construction uses much larger ones.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.summary: Two graph derivatives add to the activation parent loss

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.text: When the radius exponent satisfies $a\ge1$, substituting the actual activation loss $a+27$ gives the common residual exponent $3a+29$. The proof simplifies the integer maximum and then uses arithmetic. It records precisely how the two derivative losses are added to the primary activation estimate.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.summary: The chosen activation loss gives exponent three a plus twenty-nine

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.text: Combines the order-two graph factor with both the measured depth-tail cost and the leading activation cost. This produces a scalar large enough for the two residual contributions once their signs are established. The remaining parent exponent and child-frequency decay are kept separate for absorption by the common numerical schedule.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.summary: The remainder and activation share one graph cost

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.text: Nonnegative hierarchy costs and nonnegative primary activation cost imply a nonnegative residual step cost. The coframe expression appears squared, so no positivity assumption on the coefficient function is needed for this sign theorem. Analytic uses of that coefficient still require their own bounds in the subsequent residual estimates.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.summary: The total residual prefactor is nonnegative

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.text: Evaluates the order-cost function $K$ at $(P+1)+3P$, combines it with the hierarchy-level constant and counts the omitted quadratic pairs. The resulting prefactor bounds the order-two expansion remainder at the selected depth $P$. Its definition preserves the actual combinatorial tail count, which is later identified with the cost produced by the profile recurrence theorem.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.summary: The tail cost uses the same derivative reserve

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.text: For depth $P\ge2$, the profile theorem's reserve $\max(P+1,3)+3P$ equals $(P+1)+3P$. Substituting this identity shows its order-two remainder prefactor is exactly the scheduled residual tail cost. This avoids choosing a second order table for the residual and keeps the velocity and residual estimates on the same schedule.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.summary: The velocity reserve already covers the order-two tail

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.text: If the hierarchy cost function $K$ is pointwise nonnegative, the selected tail prefactor is nonnegative at every depth. The squared level factor and finite pair counts introduce no negative terms. This sign is needed when multiplying the tail estimate by graph constants and comparing it with the total step budget.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.summary: The residual tail prefactor is nonnegative

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.text: Under pointwise nonnegativity of the coefficient and hierarchy cost functions, proves nonnegativity of the common velocity step cost and every mean cost. The argument uses the lower bounds for the coframe and hierarchy-level constants. These sign facts allow an individual contribution to be bounded by the larger combined step sum.

Evaluates the hierarchy-level constant at derivative reserve $(P+1)+3P$ and depth $P$. This reserves enough derivative orders to read the velocity at the cutoff depth. The definition merely selects the scalar expression from an order-cost function $K$; its useful nonnegativity follows later from assumptions on that function.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.summary: The cutoff uses the reserved hierarchy-level constant

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.text: Defines the prefactor for the mean correction's order-$m$ physical Hölder estimate at a fixed depth. The coframe and retained-level bounds enter together with the chain-rule factors for $m+1$ derivatives. The parent power and frequency decay are accounted for elsewhere, so this scalar is selected before the schedule absorbs them.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.summary: The mean correction has an explicit order cost

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.text: Multiplies the parent Bernstein constant at the chosen depth by $3(P+1)$. This is the fixed-order factor needed to bound the parent's Hölder norm from its uniform jets. The numerical schedule later ensures that this factor is small relative to the parent frequency; the definition alone gives no such absorption.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.summary: The parent Bernstein estimate has a fixed-depth prefactor

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.text: Adds four scalar contributions: the full-depth oscillatory cost, the full-depth mean cost, the supremum profile-sum cost and the central derivative cost. Each term is bounded by this sum once nonnegativity has been established. The resulting scalar becomes one part of the schedule's total step entry, alongside residual, pressure and flow costs.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.summary: One step cost covers the required velocity estimates

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.slabTimeJ.text: For a positive-length stage slab, the first fixed-point time derivative of the velocity equals its residual minus the periodic Leray projection of its advection. The proof uses the stage’s divergence-free condition to identify the tensor-divergence nonlinearity, then obtains an actual within-time derivative from projected momentum. The equality holds at both slab endpoints.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.slabTimeJ.summary: The first stage time derivative obeys the Leray equation

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.slabTimeJ.text: The order-$q+1$ velocity time derivative equals the order-$q$ residual derivative minus the Leray projection of the order-$q$ advection derivative. The stage slab must have positive length, and evaluation stays in it. The proof commutes time differentiation with the actual periodic projection. Expanding the advection into its binomial products is a separate theorem.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.slabTimeJ.summary: The next velocity derivative uses one lower residual derivative

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.slabTimeJ.text: For a smooth periodic stage on a positive interval $[0,S_j]$ and an integer $q\ge0$, the formal statement proves $\partial_t^{q+1}U_j=\partial_t^qR_j-\mathbb P\sum_{i=0}^q\binom qi((\partial_t^iU_j)\cdot\nabla)\partial_t^{q-i}U_j$. The identity holds at every spatial point and every time, with endpoint derivatives taken from within the slab. The stage equations already give incompressibility, so the advection sum is the divergence of the tensor sum in the paper. The auxiliary display is this formula with its positive time order written as $q+1$. No time derivative of the residual of order $q+1$ is required.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.slabTimeJ.summary: The next velocity derivative uses the preceding residual

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.slabTimeJ.text: At time order zero, the velocity is bounded by its stage frequency and the residual by the next frequency to the power $-5/2$, provided the stage frequency is at least one. The stage already carries a stronger residual bound with exponent $-3$; monotonicity for the next frequency, also at least one, gives the displayed weakening.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.slabTimeJ.summary: The undifferentiated stage already satisfies the base bounds

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.smooth_st.text: For an inductive Euler stage with a positive slab endpoint, its residual is jointly smooth on the closed slab. The theorem applies the closed-slab momentum-residual regularity result to the stage’s bundled velocity and pressure smoothness. It verifies the regularity of the actual residual definition before time derivatives and Fourier estimates are applied.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.smooth_st.summary: The actual stage residual is jointly smooth

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stageCoef.text: This order-only quantity multiplies the number of admissible mixed derivative words by the sum $C_0+\dots+C_m$. It converts bounds on individual parent derivatives into a bound on the exact finite seminorm. Parent powers, radius factors, and frequency are excluded from the definition and remain visible in the estimates.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stageCoef.summary: A finite allowance for every coefficient word

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stageCoef.text: If every parent coefficient constant $C_j$ is nonnegative, the finite coefficient-order allowance is nonnegative. The proof uses the nonnegative cardinality of admissible words and a sum of nonnegative constants. This sign fact is required when multiplying the allowance by parent powers or by a seminorm.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stageCoef.summary: Nonnegative parent constants give a nonnegative allowance

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stageCofr.text: The definition takes $1+C_0+\dots+C_m$. It provides a single allowance for all coframe jets up to that order when reading a profile on the Eulerian graph. The added one ensures a lower bound of one once the supplied derivative constants are nonnegative.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stageCofr.summary: A common coframe allowance through the requested order

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stageCofr.text: Under nonnegativity of the sequence $(C_j)$, adding its finite partial sum to one gives a value at least one. The proof is the direct sum inequality. This supplies a convenient positive lower bound for later coframe and flow constants without claiming that any individual derivative is nonzero.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stageCofr.summary: The common coframe allowance is at least one

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stageHigh.text: Defines the scalar prefactor for the Hessian norm of the summed higher oscillatory pressure. It depends on the number of retained higher levels, their common bound and the fixed geometry constant. The separate parent exponent and frequency decay are supplied by the later analytic theorem, not by this definition.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stageHigh.summary: The higher oscillatory pressure has a fixed-order scalar cost

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stageMean.text: Defines the scalar prefactor for the mean pressure Hessian from the norm of the pressure-Hessian multiplier, the squared coframe constant, the number of mean levels, their common bound and the parent gradient constant. The multiplier norm is retained explicitly. Parent-scale powers and the $\lambda^{-5/2}$ decay are not part of this scalar.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stageMean.summary: The mean pressure cost includes the Poisson multiplier norm

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stageMean.text: Rearranges the squared coframe factor and mean-profile bound into a scalar prefactor times one parent power and the frequency decay. The equality holds for arbitrary real scalar inputs. Its purpose is to keep the order-two geometric constant outside the exponent, preserving the required independence of the schedule's parent-loss exponent.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stageMean.summary: The mean graph constant stays outside the parent power

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stagePres.text: Adds the leading signed-Hessian coefficient to the higher oscillatory and mean-Hessian coefficients at the selected depth. Both higher costs use the number of levels from two to the depth, so they vanish for an empty higher sum. With sign assumptions, each contribution is dominated by the combined cost used in the schedule.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stagePres.summary: The leading higher and mean pressure costs are added

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stagePres.text: Nonnegative geometry, parent, level and leading coefficients imply a nonnegative total pressure cost at every natural depth. The operator norm in the mean cost and the finite level count are already nonnegative. This supports the later comparison of the sum of three parent-scaled contributions with one common step bound.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stagePres.summary: The combined pressure cost is nonnegative

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stagePres.text: Takes the maximum of the leading-pressure exponent, the higher oscillatory exponent and the mean-pressure exponent. The latter two are explicit functions of the radius exponent and recurrence loss. This number allows all three pressure contributions to be enlarged to a common parent power once the parent scale is at least one.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stagePres.summary: One parent exponent covers all three pressure terms

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stagePres.text: If $a\ge24$, $r\ge9$ and the leading-pressure exponent is no larger than $6r+2(a+1)+2$, the maximum defining the total pressure exponent equals that mean exponent. The proof compares integer expressions. It documents when the explicit maximum can be simplified, rather than assuming the leading term is automatically smaller.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stagePres.summary: The mean exponent dominates once the parameters are large enough

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stageSour.text: The source cost is $6Q_m^2$ times the coefficient-order constant. The factor covers the three spatial rows and the extra factor two from subtracting a phase average. The definition collects only order-dependent constants; the next theorem supplies the fixed parent power and the fast frequency factor.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stageSour.summary: One order constant covers both advection estimates

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stageSour.text: When the derivative-constant sequence is nonnegative, the combined slow and fast source cost is nonnegative. The proof multiplies the nonnegative squared product constant by the already nonnegative coefficient allowance. It supplies the sign required when increasing the common order cost in the recurrence.

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.velocity.text: Lifts this particular stage’s continuous torus velocity to a periodic field on $\mathbb R^3$ by composing with the quotient map $\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb T^3$. Its dependence on the stage parameters remains in the stage, while the result is an ordinary time-dependent vector field on $\mathbb R^3$. Differential operators later act on this lift, with regularity inherited only on the certified closed time slab.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.velocity.summary: The Euclidean representative of one torus velocity

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.text: Packages a single frequency schedule $\lambda_n$ with derivative orders, activation times, torus velocities, residuals and oscillatory increments. Its components certify smoothness, oddness, divergence, Fourier support and the actual projected momentum equation. The bounds on each correction hold only through the scheduled derivative order of stage $n+1$. This record supplies the limit argument; it does not itself construct a family or include the matching central waves.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.summary: One sequence of approximate Euler fields

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.HasTermi.text: For the sequence of periodic stages, this condition requires that, for every pair of nonnegative integers $(m,q)$, all sufficiently large $j$ satisfy $\|\partial_t^q(U_j-U_{j-1}-O_j)(t)\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\le\lambda_j^{-1}$ for every $t\in[0,S_j]$. The derivative fixes the spatial point and uses the closed child interval. Its starting stage may depend on both orders. The condition also requires finiteness of the spatial Hölder norm $\sum_{i\le m}(\sup|D^if|+[D^if]_{1/2})$, with $D^if$ the full $i$th derivative tensor. Unlike the full auxiliary Lemma 1.2, this condition alone contains no continuity of the time curve in that spatial norm. It records an assumption on a sequence rather than proving that the sequence satisfies it.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.HasTermi.summary: Each fixed pair of orders has a starting stage

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.StageMix.text: On the child slab, take the $q$th time derivative at fixed spatial point of $u_{n+1}-u_n-w_{n+1}$, the velocity difference minus the oscillation of stage $n+1$. This condition requires $C^{m,1/2}$ membership and $C^{m,1/2}$ norm at most the inverse child frequency at every time. The variables $q$, $m$, $n$ specify one order pair and stage; eventual quantifiers occur in later auxiliary statements.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.StageMix.summary: The exact mixed increment of two consecutive stages

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.StageTim.text: At a specified stage $j$, for nonnegative integers $q$ and $\psi$, the formal condition requires $|\partial_t^iU_j(t,x)|\le\lambda_j^\psi$ and $|\partial_t^iR_j(t,x)|\le\lambda_{j+1}^{-5/2}$ for all $i\le q$, $t\in[0,S_j]$ and $x\in\mathbb R^3$. Fields are the periodic lifts, and time derivatives are taken at fixed $x$ within the closed interval. These are uniform pointwise inequalities. The condition does not choose $\psi$, assert validity at later stages, or require continuity in the spatial supremum norm. Those additional conclusions belong to auxiliary Lemma 1.3. The exponent $\psi$ is a nonnegative integer.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.StageTim.summary: Velocity and residual share one prescribed time order

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.Terminal.text: For a fixed sequence, this condition asks for two implications at sufficiently large stages. First, bounds $|\partial_t^iU_j|\le\lambda_j^\psi$ and $|\partial_t^iR_j|\le\lambda_{j+1}^{-5/2}$ for $i\le q$ must imply the corresponding child bounds through order $q+1$, with a new integer exponent depending on $q,\psi$. Second, for every fixed $m$, those parent bounds must imply $\|\partial_t^{q+1}(U_{j+1}-U_j-O_{j+1})\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\le\lambda_{j+1}^{-1}$ on the child interval. Both starting indices may depend on the indicated orders. This packages the analytic induction hypotheses; it does not prove them or explicitly state a formula for the child's residual.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.Terminal.summary: Advancing time order requires two separate estimates

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.eventual.text: Assume that the inverse stage frequencies tend to zero and that, for every fixed $(m,q)$, the correction after removing $O_j$ eventually has formal $C^{m,1/2}$ bound $\lambda_j^{-1}$ on $[0,S_j]$. For each $c\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3$, the formal statement gives one radius $r>0$ such that $D_x^m\partial_t^q(U_j-U_{j-1})$ has operator norm at most $\lambda_j^{-1}$ on $\overline B(c,r)\times[0,S_j]$ for all sufficiently large $j$. The starting index may depend on $(m,q)$, but the ball does not. The lattice is removed because it represents the single torus origin. This is a local derivative estimate for full increments, not the compact-set support statement itself.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.eventual.summary: One spatial neighborhood works for every derivative order

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.frequenc.text: Weakens the power-288 growth estimate to the square-gap inequality needed by the abstract summability lemmas. The base-frequency hypothesis guarantees that powers are monotone in their exponent. This theorem connects the actual schedule to the generic convergence machinery without using any properties of the constructed fields.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.frequenc.summary: The frequencies grow at least quadratically

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.order_te.text: Proves that the scheduled derivative orders tend to infinity, using the greatest-admissible-order rule and divergence of the frequencies. A fixed threshold can eventually be met, so no derivative order is permanently excluded. The theorem needs the initial frequency bound $\lambda_0\ge2$; it is the schedule fact that turns finitely many estimates at each stage into all-order convergence.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.order_te.summary: Every finite derivative order is eventually available

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.paper_pr.text: Assume compatible periodic stages with their regularity, residual and increment bounds, initial frequency $\lambda_0\ge2$, and activation times tending to $T>0$. Every stage interval must contain $[0,T]$. The formal statement produces a smooth odd Euler solution $u,p$ on $[0,T)$, with mean-zero pressure, smooth odd divergence-free datum, and $U_j(0)\to u(0)$ in every spatial $C^{m,1/2}$ norm. It gives convergence in that norm uniformly on every $[0,S]$, $S<T$, and uniform velocity convergence to the same $u$ on $[0,T]$, where $u$ is continuous. Every maximal solution of finite real lifespan from $u(0)$ lasts at least to $T$ and agrees with $u$ before $T$. Equality of its lifespan with $T$ is not concluded. The spatial norm is the sum, over derivative orders $0$ through $m$, of the supremum and half-Hölder seminorm of the full spatial derivative.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.paper_pr.summary: Stage estimates imply smooth convergence before accumulation

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.periodic.text: Proves invariance of the lifted stage velocity under every integer lattice translation, for any stage and any real time. This uses the quotient map rather than the stage smoothness assumptions. It lets later estimates on a fundamental cell be transported to the whole Euclidean lift of the torus.

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.stageMix.text: Let $U_j$ and $O_j$ belong to the common stage sequence, and suppose $m\le q_j$, where $q_j$ is its retained spatial order. The formal statement gives finiteness of the spatial Hölder measurement and $\|U_j-U_{j-1}-O_j\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\le\lambda_j^{-1}$ at every time in $[0,S_j]$. This is auxiliary Lemma 1.2 at time order zero, obtained directly from the existing correction estimate. The formal indexing uses the child of stage $j-1$. Time continuity in the spatial norm is not part of this particular conclusion. That spatial norm is the $C^{m,1/2}$ norm $\sum_{i\le m}(\sup|D^if|+[D^if]_{1/2})$, with $D^if$ the full $i$th derivative tensor.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.stageMix.summary: The main induction already supplies the base case

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.stageTim.text: Suppose that at stage $j$ every time derivative through order $q$ satisfies $|\partial_t^iU_j(t,x)|\le\lambda_j^\psi$ and $|\partial_t^iR_j(t,x)|\le\lambda_{j+1}^{-5/2}$ throughout $[0,S_j]\times\mathbb R^3$. For each $i\le q$ and each time in that interval, the formal statement proves the same two bounds after taking the supremum over $x$. The derivatives are at fixed physical position and include the one-sided endpoint values. The pointwise upper bounds make these suprema finite. This supplies the spatial norm inequalities in auxiliary equation (1.3); it does not supply time continuity, choose the exponent, or prove eventual validity along the sequence.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.stageTim.summary: Taking the spatial supremum preserves both inequalities

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.stageTim.text: Assume every frequency of the common stage sequence is at least one. Then, at every stage $j$, the formal statement proves $|U_j(t,x)|\le\lambda_j$ and $|R_j(t,x)|\le\lambda_{j+1}^{-5/2}$ on $[0,S_j]\times\mathbb R^3$. The first inequality is the stage velocity bound. The second follows from the stronger existing residual bound $\lambda_{j+1}^{-3}$ because $\lambda_{j+1}\ge1$. Thus the pointwise part of auxiliary Lemma 1.3 starts with $\psi_0=1$. The paper also includes continuity in the spatial supremum norm; that assertion is supplied separately and is not proved by these two inequalities alone.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.stageTim.summary: The initial exponent can be chosen as one

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.terminal.text: Fix a common stage sequence with $\lambda_j\ge1$ and $q_j\to\infty$. Assume that, eventually at every fixed time order, the parent velocity-residual bounds imply both the next child time bounds and the mixed correction bound. Then the formal statement proves: for each $q$ there is an integer $\psi_q$ such that $|\partial_t^iU_j|\le\lambda_j^{\psi_q}$ and $|\partial_t^iR_j|\le\lambda_{j+1}^{-5/2}$ for all $i\le q$ and all sufficiently large $j$; and for every fixed $(m,q)$ the correction after removing $O_j$ eventually has spatial Hölder bound $\lambda_j^{-1}$. All bounds hold throughout the appropriate closed stage intervals. The analytic implications are hypotheses, and time continuity in the stated norms remains separate.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.terminal.summary: Two induction hypotheses give both eventual bounds

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.terminal.text: Let $T>0$ and let the stage intervals be nested with $S_j\ge T$. Assume $\lambda_0\ge2$, $\lambda_{j+1}\ge\lambda_j^2$, and the eventual mixed correction bound of size $\lambda_j^{-1}$ at every fixed pair of orders. Suppose also that $U_j$ converges uniformly to $u$ on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3$. The formal statement proves joint smoothness of $u$ on $[0,T]\times(\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3)$, interpreted with derivatives up to the time boundary. Periodic lattice translates of the origin are all removed. The result concerns this given uniform limit and does not independently construct it. It concludes smoothness; uniform convergence of its derivatives is stated in the separate local result.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.terminal.summary: Summable mixed increments yield joint boundary regularity

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.terminal.text: Assume $T>0$, nested stage intervals containing $[0,T]$, $\lambda_0\ge2$, $\lambda_{j+1}\ge\lambda_j^2$, and eventual mixed correction bounds $\lambda_j^{-1}$ at every fixed pair of orders. Let $U_j\to u$ uniformly on the closed common slab. For every $c\notin\mathbb Z^3$, the formal statement finds $r>0$ such that $u$ is jointly smooth on $[0,T]\times\overline B(c,r)$ and every joint space-time derivative of $U_j$ converges uniformly there to the corresponding derivative of $u$. Derivatives on this closed cylinder are taken within it, including at $T$. The same radius works for all orders. This supplies the local derivative convergence required before extending the velocity through the terminal time.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.terminal.summary: The same local cylinder works at every order
