TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.terminal.text: Let a sequence of approximate Euler stages $u_j$, smooth on $[0,S_j]\times\mathbb R^3$, be given with $T>0$, $T\le S_j$ and $S_{j+1}\le S_j$ for all $j$, and suppose $u_j\to u$ uniformly on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3$. Let $c\in\mathbb R^3$, $r>0$, and let $w_k(j)$ be summable in $j$ for each $k$, with, for each $k$ and all sufficiently large $j$, the $k$th joint derivative of $u_{j+1}-u_j$ within $[0,S_{j+1}]\times\mathbb R^3$ bounded by $w_k(j)$ at every point of $[0,T]\times\overline B(c,r)$. Then $u$ is jointly smooth on $S=[0,T]\times\overline B(c,r)$, and for every $k$ the $k$th derivatives of $u_j$ within $S$ converge uniformly on $S$ to the $k$th derivative of $u$ within $S$.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.terminal.summary: Summable increment bounds give the derivatives of the limit on a cylinder

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.velocity.text: Reads stage $n$ on $\mathbb R^3$ by composing its continuous torus velocity with the quotient map $\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb T^3$. This is the function used by the differential operators in the limit construction. The definition is meaningful at every real time, although smoothness and quantitative estimates are only supplied on the recorded stage slab.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.velocity.summary: The periodic lift of a stage velocity

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStep.text: Describes a successor of one exact tip. It stores the physical comparison, chosen crossing, new child and linking wave, with equalities identifying preceding and current wave pairs. The clock endpoint, gain ratio and comparison smallness bounds are also fields. These links are required before the step can be appended to a compatible prefix.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStep.summary: A new stage tied to its selected physical crossing

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStep.ofLaterWav.text: Builds a successor step from a later physical window, a selected crossing, a certified child and a wave linking the parent to that child. Two hypotheses identify the selected wave vector and amplitude with those of the linking wave. The construction assembles existing data; it does not manufacture the child estimates from a comparison alone.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStep.ofLaterWav.summary: Attach a selected comparison to its actual child

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStep.ofPhysical.text: Construction of the next inductive step from a certified prefix ending at a tip with index $n$, a later physical window and wave selection, a truncated-child stage $s$ on the slab $[0,S]$ with $S$ the scheduled slab of stage $n+2$ from the next activation $t_1$, and a stage-$(n+2)$ child whose velocity equals the cutoff velocity of $s$. The hypotheses are $e^4\le\lambda_0$; strength constant at least $18e^3$; $|w(t,x)|\le\lambda_{n+2}^{-1}$ for the oscillation $w$ on $[0,S]$; for every $m\le q_{n+2}$ the correction $u_{\rm child}-u_{\rm parent}-w$ has spatial $C^{m,1/2}$ norm at most $\lambda_{n+2}^{-1}$; $w=0$ on $[0,t_1]$; wherever $w(t,x)\ne0$ some lattice point lies within $\lambda_{n+1}^{-1}$ of $x$; the cutoff bounds of $s$ at depth at least two with $K$ times the truncation error at most $\lambda_{n+3}^{-5}$; the uncut velocity $V$ is smooth on the slab; and on $[t_1,S]$, $D_xV(t,0)=D_xu_{\rm parent}(t,0)+\chi(t)\,\mathbf a(t)\otimes k(t)+R(t)$ with the time switch $\chi$, the selected crossing wave $(k,\mathbf a)$ and $\|R(t)\|\le\lambda_{n+2}^{-1/3}$. The crossing strength and the exit coupling $\pi\le\nu\le4\pi$ are derived inside, and the resulting step uses the same wave and child throughout.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStep.ofPhysical.summary: Build the next inductive step from the same selected wave and cutoff child

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStep.parent_gra.text: On the next active slab, identifies the physical amplification gradient with the central derivative of the current parent velocity. The previous wave is fully switched on there. Rewriting its stored gradient splitting and the preceding pair and error equalities gives the identity, which is needed to interpret the next coupling physically.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStep.parent_gra.summary: The comparison gradient is the actual parent gradient

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStep.scheduledP.text: Packages the completed step as a scheduled physical crossing relation between the exit couplings of two exact pairs of stages, with their scheduled ratios. The proof uses, at the crossing time, the identity between the strain of the stored physical window and the actual parent gradient $\nabla U(t,0)$. This prevents the coupling recurrence from being applied to a comparison matrix unrelated to the retained Euler stage.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStep.scheduledP.summary: The stored successor transports the scheduled couplings

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStep.tip.text: Forms the next tip from a completed successor step. The current parent becomes the older stage, the newly constructed child becomes the parent, and the crossing supplies the next activation. Nonnegativity and slab containment come from the previous tip and lifetime estimates, retaining the exact physical objects already constructed.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStep.tip.summary: Appending a step advances the exact pair of stages

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerSuccessor.text: Abbreviates the local extension requirement: every index, exact pair of stages and certified prefix ending there admits a successor step. The statement asserts only that such a step exists, so it supplies existence rather than a preselected function. Requiring a compatible prefix is weaker and more appropriate than demanding a successor for arbitrary isolated data of a pair of stages.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerSuccessor.summary: A local successor for every compatible finite history

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.text: Holds the older stage at index $n$, its child at index $n+1$, and the completed wave that connects them. It also records the next activation selected by that wave. Nonnegative current activation and containment of the current endpoint in the older slab, $S_{n+1}\le S_n$, are explicit fields, preparing the next local construction.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.summary: Two consecutive stages and their next activation

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.LaterSelect.text: For a compatible comparison window, this abbreviation fixes the later-wave selection problem to the parent velocity, the schedule’s comparison constant and half-length, the next frequency, the following logarithmic gain, and parent scale. It keeps all those parameters tied to one tip. It does not by itself assert that such a crossing has been selected.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.LaterSelect.summary: The crossing problem with the next scheduled frequency

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.LaterWindow.text: This abbreviation fixes the later physical comparison window to the older and parent velocities, the preceding wave vector and amplitude, its error, and the next scheduled time interval at the current tip. It is a type of compatible comparison data, not a selected window. The actual window is supplied with the selected later input.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.LaterWindow.summary: The comparison window over the actual two preceding stages

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: This structure ties together a positive endpoint at most one, a sufficiently large parent frequency, a physical comparison window and crossing, a nonzero transported carrier, a restricted parent chart, and a local seed with regularity and even amplitude. Its fields ensure every subsequent physical profile uses the same wave and parent. No quantitative hierarchy bound is contained here.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: One selected wave and its compatible parent geometry

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: For selected later input with next activation time $t_*$ and physical switching rate $r$, the activation ramp is the closed interval $[t_*,\min(S,\,t_*+1/r)]$, where $S$ is the endpoint of the next stage started at $t_*$. Clipping at $S$ keeps the ramp inside the active slab.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The activation ramp clipped to the stage interval

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: The ramp attached to the selected later input is a closed subset of the real line because it is a closed interval. This topological fact is used when differentiating a field known to vanish outside the ramp: its complement is open, so the field remains zero in a neighborhood of every off-ramp time.

Every time in the activation ramp $[t_*,\min(S,t_*+1/r)]$ lies in the active interval $[t_*,S]$ from the next activation time to the stage endpoint, because the lower endpoints agree and the minimum is at most $S$.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The clipped ramp stays in the active slab

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: At a time $t$ on the selected physical slab but outside $[t_0,t_0+1/r]$, the sum of the leading and completion switch terms is zero at every label and independent phase. The selected wave supplies $r>0$. The proof uses the exact activation-source formula and vanishing of the scalar switch derivative. This declaration states a value identity, not vanishing of every higher time derivative.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The activation source vanishes outside its switch interval

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: Within the actual child slab, the sum of the leading switch profile and its completion switch profile is zero outside the selected activation ramp. The proof evaluates the exact wrapped profiles and shows their shared scalar factor, the derivative of the wave switch, is zero. This is a support statement for the selected activation residual, not a norm estimate.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The combined activation residual vanishes off the ramp

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: This definition builds the physical approximation using the selected leading input, the actual parent pressure and residual, the stored duration bound, and the scheduled depth. It does not select alternative coefficients or a second wave. The subsequent properties theorem applies the general qualitative assembly to this precise approximation.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The selected hierarchy over the same restricted parent

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: This accessor returns the carrier $k_*$ formed from the selected crossing and parent launch deformation. Its mathematical guarantees, that $k_*\ne0$, that it is transported to the wave vector, and its size bound, come from the corresponding fields of the same selected later input. Keeping this accessor avoids accidentally using a carrier from a different selection when constructing twisted profiles.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The constant label covector of the selected wave

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: The selected carrier equals the adjoint of the parent flow derivative at the origin and activation, applied to the selected crossing’s wave vector there. The equality is definitional: the selected input was built with this carrier. It identifies the frequency in the label phase with the same physical wave used in the center equations.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The carrier is the pulled-back activation covector

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: The selected crossing’s wave vector and amplitude satisfy the central wave equations, namely the covector and amplitude equations, nonvanishing and perpendicularity, transverse stability and the coupling inequality, for the parent gradient at the origin, on the active slab and with the ninth-power parent scale $\mathsf D$. The proof is the stored central-wave field of the selection. This declaration exposes existing selected data; it does not solve another differential equation or select a different pair.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The selected pair already satisfies the central wave equations

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: The same center wave satisfies the center equations written along the parent trajectory of the zero label, with its wave vector replaced by the transported carrier. The parent-flow transport theorem uses launch membership and the carrier’s adjoint formula. The amplitude and active interval remain exactly those of the original selected crossing.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The central equations use the transported label covector

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: The weight at time $t$ is $\gamma(t)=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t)|$, the norm of the selected crossing amplitude multiplied by the child frequency to power $3/4$. It is defined for every real time, while its positivity, regularity, and upper bound are proved on the active slab. This is the same center weight used in the measured hierarchy and the switching estimate.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The central amplitude determines the hierarchy weight

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: This theorem extracts continuity of the center weight $\gamma$ on the active slab from its collected properties. It supplies the exact continuity proof required when defining amplitude-weighted seminorms of the selected hierarchy. The conclusion concerns this restricted interval; it does not assert global continuity of an arbitrarily extended crossing amplitude.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The active weight has continuous time dependence

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: The selected normalized weight is at most one at every active time, directly by the packaged weight properties. This allows amplitude bounds to control ordinary profile sizes when the oscillatory profile is inactive before launch. The theorem does not provide the stronger exponentially small bound needed during the initial switching interval.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: Peak normalization bounds the active weight by one

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: At every time in the selected active interval, the center weight $\gamma$ is strictly positive. The proof projects the positivity component of the weight's collected properties; no new nonvanishing argument is carried out here. This prevents division by zero in the amplitude-weighted norms used for the selected hierarchy and leading-seed estimate.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The center weight is positive on the active slab

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: On the active slab the selected weight is continuous, strictly positive, at most one, and has a continuous within-derivative. The proof obtains continuity of the parent gradient from its joint smoothness and applies the normalized-weight theorem for the selected center solution. The derivative assertion is restricted to the closed active interval, including its endpoints.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The active weight is positive, bounded, and differentiable

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: At each time in the active slab, the selected crossing amplitude has norm at most the child frequency to power $-3/4$. The proof identifies the physical crossing’s active interval with the scheduled slab and applies its attained-peak property. This is the actual normalized crossing, rather than an independently postulated amplitude bound.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The selected peak bounds every active amplitude

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: The central error is defined as the sum of the derivative at the origin of the higher oscillatory remainder and the derivative of the mean correction. It excludes both the parent gradient and the leading rank-one wave. The following splitting theorem identifies this exact quantity inside the gradient of the untruncated approximation.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The central derivative contributed by the corrections

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: The selected child frequency is at least one because the schedule makes it a natural power of the parent frequency, already at least two. This local consequence permits monotonic comparison of its real powers. It neither changes the schedule nor supplies the stronger initial-frequency thresholds used for activation and cutoff estimates.

The stored completion switch is definitionally the finite hierarchy solver’s completion of the leading switch force. This exact equality prevents a mismatch between the activation correction and the curl operator used at later levels. It is the cancellation premise that lets the level-two relay reduce to a homogeneous relay.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The activation completion uses the hierarchy’s curl operator

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: For a certified prefix and initial frequency at least $e^4$, the parent gradient in the selected wave’s frame has its first coupling between $\pi$ and $4\pi$. The ratio of its other coupling to that first one equals the prescribed logarithmic-gain ratio. The result applies at this selected crossing time, not throughout the whole active interval.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The selected crossing has the required coupling ratio

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: The selected finite expansion keeps six times the frequency exponent associated with the next required order. This is the schedule’s concrete realization of $P=6K_{j+1}$. The depth depends only on the shared parameters and index, so all profiles and numerical budgets for this input refer to one finite truncation.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The retained depth follows the next scheduled exponent

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: The prescribed depth is at least two because it is six times a strictly positive scheduled frequency exponent. Positivity of the exponent parameter comes from the induction parameters. This establishes the minimum depth required by the finite expansion identities without making any estimate about the magnitude of its remainder.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The scheduled expansion contains at least two levels

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: Chooses a radius-exponent floor at least thirty and a nonnegative constant for all selected later inputs. Above that floor, the rescaled activation-primary profile has two-jet bound $\gamma C\mathsf D^{a+27}\lambda^{-5/4}$ throughout the active slab. The estimate keeps the positive central weight explicit; the small derivative of the temporal switch is supplied separately when estimating the residual.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The later activation profile has a uniform weighted two-jet bound

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: For a fixed strength constant at least two, one initial threshold makes $|\partial_t\chi(t)|\gamma(t)$, the selected switch derivative times the center weight, at most $\lambda_{n+1}\lambda_{n+3}^{-4}$, the parent frequency times the next frequency to power $-4$, for every time. The proof applies the actual-wave switching theorem and removes the weight’s absolute value using its global nonnegativity. The threshold is uniform over selected inputs.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The measured weight obeys the scheduled switching estimate

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: Given a certified prefix, a scheduled physical stage for this selected approximation, initial frequency at least $e^4$, and strength constant at least $18e^3$, there exists a certified next step. Its velocity and pressure are exactly the stored cutoff fields, and its oscillation is exactly this approximation’s oscillation. The proof delegates stage closure after supplying support and the bounded central split.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The measured approximation closes the same certified prefix

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: There exist a common radius exponent at least thirty and nonnegative order-dependent costs, chosen before the selected input, such that every sufficiently small selected radius gives the leading weighted velocity norm plus frequency times its pressure norm at most $\mathrm{cost}(m)D_+^{20}\lambda_+^{-5/4}$. The proof applies parent jet bounds and the same transported center wave to the localized seed.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: One radius exponent bounds every selected leading seed

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: For each spatial slope $p$ it chooses a radius floor $A\ge p$; then, for fixed orders $q,e$ and nonnegative coefficient and switch cost functions, it chooses a nonnegative cost function before the selected wave. With $\mu$ the parent frequency and $D=\mu^9$, joint smoothness and mixed jet bounds $\|D_x^n\partial_t^if\|\le C_nD^eD^{pn}$ for $i\le q$ on the slab, for the amplitude generator and the normalized pressure coefficient, are hypotheses. Switch derivatives are required through order $q+1$, with $|\chi^{(i)}|\le C_i\mu^i$. The conclusion bounds the weighted time norm of the leading velocity plus frequency times pressure, and separately the leading switch term, by $\mathrm{cost}(n)D^{e(q+1)+q+14}\lambda^{-5/4}$. It does not yet include the completion switch term.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: Time bounds for the selected leading wave

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: Specializes the uniform parent theorem to the selected input for a later wave, in which the chosen crossing, label seed and restricted parent all belong to the same verified stage of the construction. One pair of constants $A,C$ works for every stage once $a\ge A$. The parent scale becomes $\lambda_{n+1}^{9}$ and the new frequency is $\lambda_{n+2}$. The estimate holds on the selected next slab and remains a one-sided quadratic-form bound for the leading pressure $p_1$ of that stage's approximate solution.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: Leading pressure for the selected later wave

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: There are an integer $A\ge30$ and constants $c_m\ge1$ such that, for every selected later input whose radius exponent satisfies $a\ge A$, every order $m$ and every $t$ in the active interval $[t_*,S]$, all derivatives of order at most $m$ of the scaled seed amplitude $x\mapsto g(\ell x)\,\mathbf a(t,\ell x)$ are bounded by $|\mathbf a_c(t)|\,c_m\,\mathsf D^{13}$. Here $g$ is the radial envelope of radius $\ell$, $\mathbf a_c$ the selected crossing amplitude, and $\mathsf D=\lambda_{n+1}^9$. The threshold $A$ is the same for all $m$.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: One radius threshold controls the future amplitude at every order

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: For a strength constant $C_{\rm str}\ge2$, it chooses one threshold $N>1$ and nonnegative constants $C_q$ before the selected stages and all derivative orders. Assuming the initial frequency is at least $N$ and the strength constant equals $C_{\rm str}$, it proves $r\le\mu$, the center-weight bound $\gamma\le e^3\lambda_{j+1}^{-4}$ on the switch interval, and global bounds $|\chi^{(q)}|\le C_q\mu^q$. For $q>0$, multiplying by the center weight retains the factor $e^3\lambda_{j+1}^{-4}$. Positivity of the derivative order is essential to that last assertion.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: Switch derivatives retain the early growth gain

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: On the active interval, the gradient at the origin of the selected approximate velocity equals the parent gradient plus the switched rank-one tensor $\chi\,\mathbf a\otimes k$ of the selected crossing amplitude and wave vector, plus the central error, the sum of the origin gradients of the oscillatory remainder and the mean correction. The proof differentiates the actual four-part velocity decomposition and uses carrier transport. This is an exact identity before the final frequency cutoff.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The central gradient separates parent, wave, and correction

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: At activation, the label wave vector built from the selected carrier has norm equal to the child frequency. The proof first uses the selected transport identity to replace it with the physical crossing’s wave vector, then applies its launch norm. This supplies the exact normalization hypothesis of the leading-seed estimate.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The transported carrier has the prescribed launch norm

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: The selected crossing’s wave vector has norm exactly the scheduled child frequency at activation. The proof supplies positive frequency to the growing crossing’s launch-geometry theorem. This is an equality at launch, rather than a time-uniform statement about wave-vector length; later lengths follow the parent deformation and wave equations.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The launched covector has exactly the child frequency

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: The next activation belongs to the restricted parent interval $[0,T_+]$: nonnegativity comes from the inductive tip, and the strict upper bound comes from the selected seed’s regularity. This endpoint membership is passed to the parent-flow transport identity when identifying the carrier at launch. It also shows that this particular slab is nonempty.

The selected seed and its hierarchy regularity are wrapped as leading-wave input for the physical approximation, using the same restricted parent geometry. The construction also uses the parent’s actual label flow, smooth velocity, periodicity, oddness, and the stored evenness of the seed amplitude. It returns the leading wave together with the compatible pressure and activation terms.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The chosen local seed becomes the leading physical wave

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: Every time derivative of the selected leading pressure has zero normalized phase mean, at each label and every time in the child slab. The original pressure’s phase normalization is supplied by the seed’s wrapped-pressure theorem. The result follows by commuting phase averaging with time differentiation; it does not claim that the pressure itself vanishes.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The leading pressure retains zero phase mean at every time order

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: The selected approximation has zero leading-pressure phase mean, centered activation force, transverse activation force, and the exact completion-switch identity. The proof assembles previously established facts and uses phase independence of the parent covector to align the transversality statement. These four facts are the hypotheses that identify the actual first relay with the homogeneous linear relay.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The actual leading wave satisfies the relay normalization identities

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: The phase average of the selected leading switch is zero as a twisted profile. This follows from the seed’s switch construction and its centered phase profile. The result supplies the activation-mean component of the leading normalization data for the first correction; it does not claim pointwise vanishing of the force during the switching interval.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The selected activation force is centered in phase

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: At every slab point, the selected parent covector is orthogonal to the activation-force profile. The parent geometry identifies that covector with the one used by the seed, allowing the general switch-transversality result to apply. This orthogonality eliminates the force’s contribution to the phase-pressure slope in the level-two relay.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The selected activation force stays in the transverse plane

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: Defines the natural exponent $e(q+1)+q+14$ used in the common bound for the selected leading velocity, its pressure multiplied by the carrier frequency, and the leading switch source. Here $e$ is the assumed coefficient exponent in $D$, and $q$ is the time order. Spatial order and expansion depth do not occur in this exponent; their costs remain in a separate function.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: Parent exponent for the leading time derivatives

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: For a time in the parent slab no later than the next activation, the selected leading velocity is zero at every label and phase. The theorem includes the activation time itself. The proof uses the flat switch in the localized seed; it says nothing about the pressure or mean correction at this statement’s level.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The selected leading profile vanishes up to activation

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: The selected leading input is inactive before the next activation and outside the closed support of the periodized radial envelope at the selected radius. This packages the velocity, pressure, and completion-switch support facts using the same seed and parent. It does not imply that the later mean corrections vanish in that region.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The leading wave and switch share one inactive region

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: At every parent-slab time and label, the selected leading pressure has phase average zero. The proof uses the normalized twisted pressure of the same seed and carrier. This is the level-one pressure premise needed to propagate normalization to all retained oscillatory pressures and to center the linear relay.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The selected leading pressure has zero phase mean

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: Assuming the step constant is at most the child frequency to power $1/32$ and the two correction gradients have summed norm at most that constant times the frequency to power $-5/12$, the actual central error is bounded by the frequency to power $-1/3$. The proof uses the triangle inequality and weakens $1/32$ to $1/12$ before combining powers.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The central correction meets the required inverse-third power

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: Every nonzero Eulerian oscillation lies within the reciprocal parent frequency of some lattice point. The radius exponent at least six implies the envelope-size condition needed by the general support theorem. On the periodic lift this is the lattice-distance form of the paper’s ball around the torus origin, and it concerns only the oscillatory part.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The selected oscillation lies in the prescribed torus ball

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: The Eulerian oscillation of the selected approximation is zero on $[0,t₀]$, including the case $t₀=0$ arising at the second wave. The proof combines closed-envelope inactivity with the separately established zero leading profile at time zero. This extra endpoint input handles nonnegative activation without requiring it to be strictly positive.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The whole selected oscillation vanishes through activation

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: The stored lower bound of four on the selected parent frequency immediately implies the lower bound two used in support and scale estimates. This is a consequence of the data already selected, not a new threshold argument. It provides a standard hypothesis for monotonicity of parent-frequency powers.

The selected parent frequency $\lambda$ is at most its ninth power $\mathsf D=\lambda^9$, because that frequency is at least one. The proof compares natural powers with exponents one and nine. This permits replacing deformation bounds stated with the parent frequency by the coarser scale used throughout Section 5.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The ninth-power scale dominates the parent frequency

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: Combining the selected frequency’s lower bound two with its domination by the ninth-power scale proves $D_+\ge2$. The statement is a numerical consequence of the selected data. It ensures that inverse parent powers are positive and become smaller when the chosen envelope exponent increases.

The selected leading input over the restricted parent yields the qualitative properties of a physical approximation at its scheduled depth. The proof supplies the depth lower bound and invokes the parent’s qualitative assembly theorem. Smoothness, parity, periodicity, and the relevant identities concern this particular approximation; numerical smallness and cutoff estimates are proved elsewhere.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The selected approximation has all qualitative properties

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: The selected radius is $(D_+^a)^{-1}$ with $D_+=\lambda_{n+1}^9$. The input term is unused in the formula beyond its type parameters; all selections with the same schedule, index, and exponent therefore share the radius. Its positive and small size is established from the stored parent-frequency lower bound.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The envelope radius fixed by the parent scale

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: The selected radius, defined using the reciprocal of a natural power, equals $D_+^{-a}$ in real-power notation. Positivity follows from the parent-scale lower bound, allowing the real negative-power identity to apply. This converts the concrete radius definition to the notation used by the scale estimates.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The reciprocal radius formula equals a negative real power

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: The inverse of the selected radius is exactly $D_+^a$, by the double-inverse identity. This equality matches the coefficient budgets that carry an explicit inverse label width. It is algebraically valid even for a zero base, although valid selected data already guarantees the stronger positive-scale condition.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: Inverting the selected radius recovers its parent power

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: If $j\le a$, the selected radius $\mathsf D^{-a}$ is at most $\mathsf D^{-j}$. The positive parent scale is at least one, so the proof compares natural powers and reverses the inequality upon inversion. This lets one chosen radius exponent satisfy the several lower exponent requirements arising in seed and coefficient estimates.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The common radius meets every smaller exponent requirement

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: For any natural $j\le a$, the product of the selected radius with $\mathsf D^j$ is at most one. The positive scale is at least one, so increasing the exponent decreases its reciprocal. This supplies the width conditions used to absorb derivative growth in the coframe, normalized covector, and relay estimates.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The radius absorbs every lower parent power

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: If the initial frequency is at least $e$ and the common strength constant is at least $18e^3$, the product of wave-vector and amplitude lengths at the selected crossing lies between the prescribed inverse-constant quarter-power lower bound and the logarithmically enlarged upper bound. The proof uses the actual selected growing crossing and the schedule’s adjacent gain inequalities.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The selected crossing supplies the required wave strength

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: This accessor returns the prescribed phase width $\lambda_{n+2}^{-1/2}$. It depends on the schedule and index, not on a fresh choice from the input object. The hierarchy regularity in the selected data was built at exactly this width, allowing later coefficient and profile estimates to use the same normalization.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The phase width fixed by the child frequency

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.exists_late.text: Given lifetime bounds and initial frequency greater than one, constructs a physical comparison window from the actual older and parent stages in the tip. It uses nested intervals, smooth central gradients, the completed gradient splitting and positive coupling data. The result is a window object, not yet the next selected wave or child stage.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.exists_late.summary: A certified tip supplies the next physical comparison window

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.exists_sele.text: For a fixed strength constant at least two, the theorem chooses a comparison constant $C_0\ge240$, initial-frequency threshold $N\ge4$, envelope constant, and minimum radius exponent $A\ge6$ before the prefix. Every certified prefix with $\lambda_0\ge N$ then admits a selected later input for each exponent $a\ge A$. The witness combines the crossing, nonzero transported carrier, restricted parent, and symmetric local seed; it does not yet prove their quantitative approximation bounds.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.exists_sele.summary: One initial threshold selects compatible later waves for every prefix

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.exitCouplin.text: Reads the first coupling of the completed wave’s frame against the older stage gradient, evaluated at the next activation. It is the scalar propagated between consecutive tips in the coupling argument. The frame and gradient come from the same stored tip, rather than from separately supplied numerical sequences.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.exitCouplin.summary: The completed wave coupling at its selected activation

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.laterCarrie.text: The carrier is the adjoint of the parent’s forward deformation at the next activation, applied to the selected crossing wave vector at that time. It is the constant label covector whose subsequent transport reproduces the chosen central wave. The formula alone does not state a size bound or prove nonvanishing.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.laterCarrie.summary: Pulling the launch covector back to time zero

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.next_activa.text: Combines the tip’s nonnegative activation with the completed wave’s nonnegative activation increment. The resulting next activation is nonnegative without needing the lifetime certificate. This supplies the lower time bound when restricting stage regularity or residual estimates to the next comparison interval.

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.next_active.text: Shows inclusion of the next comparison interval $[t_{n+2},S_{n+2}]$ in the current wave’s active interval $[t_{n+1},S_{n+1}]$. Its left endpoint follows from nonnegative activation increments; its right endpoint follows from the strict inequality $S_{n+2}<S_{n+1}$. This ensures that the preceding wave equations and central gradient splitting remain available throughout the next comparison.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.next_active.summary: The next active interval stays within the preceding wave

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.next_slab_l.text: For a certified pair of stages and the lifetime bounds on the half-lengths $\tau_j$, combines the upper bound on the next activation increment with contraction of the half-lengths. The next endpoint $S_{n+2}$ is strictly below the current parent endpoint $S_{n+1}$. Positivity of the current half-length is essential for strictness, leaving a nonzero margin for the next endpoint problem.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.next_slab_l.summary: The next endpoint lies strictly before its parent endpoint

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.next_slab_p.text: Uses nonnegative next activation and the positive next half-length from the lifetime bounds to prove $S_{n+2}>0$ for the next stage endpoint. This prevents later closed-slab regularity arguments from being applied only to a degenerate time domain. The endpoint formula is unfolded explicitly in the proof.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.next_slab_p.summary: The next stage endpoint is positive

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerWave.text: Records the oscillatory increment and central wave linking a fixed parent to a fixed child. It includes correction norms, localization, activation, central gradient splitting, and exit strength, coupling and ratio. The child is a dependent parameter, so these claims concern that exact velocity. The early-time vanishing condition applies only when the wave index is at least two.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerWave.summary: A certified increment between two specified stages

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerWave.growingCro.text: For a growing crossing normalized with peak amplitude $\mathrm{frequency}(n+1)^{-3/4}$, derives the induction’s lower and upper strength bounds at its selected crossing. It assumes a sufficiently large initial frequency, a strength constant at least $18\exp(3)$, and the prescribed incoming ratio. Frequency monotonicity and the logarithmic gain schedule control the constants.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerWave.growingCro.summary: The scheduled gain bounds strength at the crossing

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerWave.ofGrowingC.text: Constructs an inductive wave relating an existing parent to the actual cutoff child. It retains the selected crossing’s amplitude, wave vector, and switch, and adds the cutoff derivative to the supplied central error. Oscillation size, correction bounds, support, vanishing before activation, crossing strength, and exit coupling are explicit inputs; this adapter does not derive them all from qualitative approximation.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerWave.ofGrowingC.summary: Attach the selected crossing to the cutoff child

TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.text: Packages a first-wave origin and the actual stationary parent restricted to the first slab. Its fields require envelope exponent at least six, positive duration at most one, large initial frequency, small tilt, positive logarithmic gain and small shear over the slab. Thus the type carries the analytic side conditions needed to construct the first hierarchy; it is not merely a choice of velocity and frequency.
TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.summary: The first wave on its stationary parent slab

TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.a.text: Builds the physical approximation over the selected stationary parent at the prescribed depth. The leading input is the one just constructed, and the parent residual is inherited from the restricted parent geometry. The resulting data retain the actual hierarchy profiles so that all later velocity, pressure and residual estimates refer to the same fields.
TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.a.summary: The first finite hierarchy uses the actual parent

TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.c.text: At activation time zero the parent flow from zero to zero is the identity. Its adjoint derivative therefore fixes the central covector, proving the carrier pullback identity required by the general hierarchy. This is the first-wave specialization of the later-wave construction where the pullback is no longer trivial.
TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.c.summary: The initial carrier is the covector pullback

TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.c.text: Certifies the central covector and amplitude against the derivative of the actual selected parent velocity at the origin. The parent scale is $\lambda_0^9$. The explicit stationary-shear central-wave result is transferred using the equality of gradients, so the certificate is suitable for the hierarchy over this particular parent.
TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.c.summary: The first central wave uses the actual gradient

TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.c.text: Identifies the stored completion switch with the hierarchy solver's completion of the leading switch. Although both switches were set to zero, this conclusion requires the completion operator's zero property for phase-independent geometry. It connects the explicit first input to the same selected relay used for later waves.
TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.c.summary: Zero activation has zero physical completion

TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.c.text: The selected completion switch is definitionally zero as well. This is the correction associated with the absent first activation force, not the higher oscillatory correction or the mean pressure. A subsequent theorem checks that this stored zero agrees with the actual completion operator applied to zero forcing.

TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.d.text: Sets the initial hierarchy depth to six times the frequency exponent evaluated at the next scheduled derivative order. This is the first-step implementation of $P=6K_{j+1}$. The chosen depth is a natural number; a separate lemma proves it is at least two before the hierarchy's qualitative properties are invoked.
TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.d.summary: The first expansion depth is six next exponents

TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.d.text: Proves the selected expansion depth is at least two for every admissible choice of the induction parameters. The proof uses positivity of the frequency exponent, which follows from the parameters' exponent floor and the successor derivative order. This guarantees that the first mean and oscillatory corrections required by the physical approximation are present.
TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.d.summary: The first hierarchy has at least two levels

TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.e.text: Given the lifetime bounds on the half lengths and a scheduled physical stage for the selected first approximation, constructs the base of the inductive Euler construction. Its first velocity and pressure equal the actual cutoff fields, its stationary stage is the chosen parent, and its wave oscillation is the selected hierarchy's oscillation. The numerical estimates are hypotheses stored in the scheduled stage; this theorem assembles them rather than deriving them anew.
TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.e.summary: The scheduled first cutoff supplies the initial stages

TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.e.text: Chooses a nonnegative cost for every derivative order, valid uniformly over the first-wave selections. It weakens the previous leading-profile estimate by the factor $\mathsf D^{20}\ge1$ and rewrites the first hierarchy exponent as $-5/4$. This puts the actual first profiles into the same recurrence format used for later waves.
TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.e.summary: The first profiles fit the common seed budget

TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.e.text: For each derivative order $m$, selects a nonnegative constant $C_m$ valid for every first-wave selection. The sum of the velocity amplitude seminorm and frequency times the pressure seminorm is at most $C_m\lambda_1^{-5/4}$. Both seminorms use the selected radius, width and positive time weight, so the constant is independent of the eventual schedule and envelope exponent.
TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.e.summary: The first leading profiles have uniform weighted bounds

TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.e.text: Specializes the global first-pressure estimate to the first-wave selection of the induction, the exponent $a\ge6$, the first slab, frequencies and first-wave data on the stationary parent, giving the upper Hessian bound $K(\lambda_0^9)^{2a}\lambda_1^{-1/4}$. The selected radius satisfies the stronger support condition needed for the coefficient sign. The theorem refers to the leading pressure of the approximation stored in that selection, so the signed estimate applies to the actual pressure used in the hierarchy.
TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.e.summary: The selected first pressure has the scheduled parent loss

TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.f.text: Extracts $4\le\lambda_0$ from the selection's stronger bound $1+4\pi\le\lambda_0$. This elementary consequence lets later proofs use standard monotonicity estimates for natural and real powers. It is conditional on an existing first-wave selection and does not establish a schedule or its lifetime bounds.
TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.f.summary: The selected initial frequency exceeds four

TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.f.text: Uses the frequency-step identity and the initial lower bound to prove $1\le\lambda_1$. Raising a base at least one to the scheduled natural exponent preserves this inequality. The fact is used to control negative real powers, particularly the phase width and the normalized peak amplitude.

Derives strict positivity of the first child frequency from its lower bound by one. This excludes the zero-carrier case before using reciprocals and real-power identities in the first-wave formulas. The assertion is a consequence of the selection data, not an extra hypothesis imposed on every parameter structure.

TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.g.text: Defines $\gamma(t)=\lambda_1^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|$ from the selected central amplitude. This is a real-valued global function, but its positivity and bound by one are established on the first closed slab. It is the same time weight used to measure both leading velocity and pressure profiles.
TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.g.summary: The first seed defines its normalized time weight

TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.g.text: There exists a time in the closed first slab at which the normalized weight $\gamma=1$. The origin data already include attainment of the amplitude peak; the theorem translates that equality into the normalized weight. It asserts existence of a peak time and does not identify it with activation or a later crossing.
TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.g.summary: The first weight reaches its normalized peak

TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.g.text: Continuity of the central amplitude follows from its within-interval differential equation. Taking its norm and multiplying by the constant frequency factor gives continuity of the weight $\gamma$ on the closed first slab. This is the continuity hypothesis needed by the weighted amplitude seminorms; no global-time continuity is asserted here.
TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.g.summary: The first weight is continuous on its slab

TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.g.text: Produces a continuous function $\dot\gamma$ representing the within-slab derivative of the normalized weight at every point, including the endpoints. The central-wave normalization theorem applies because the selected parent's central gradient is continuous. This supplies the time regularity needed for weighted estimates without claiming an extension of that derivative beyond the slab.
TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.g.summary: The first weight has a continuous slab derivative

TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.g.text: The initial-strength lower bound and the exact carrier length imply $\gamma(0)\ge1/2$. The proof cancels a positive frequency power after rewriting the normalization. This is stronger information at the initial time than mere positivity, and it records that the first wave begins near its prescribed peak size.

The origin amplitude is at most the selected peak $\lambda_1^{-3/4}$. Multiplying by $\lambda_1^{3/4}$ proves $\gamma\le1$ throughout the first slab. Positivity of the frequency justifies combining the real powers, and the statement leaves the weight outside that slab unconstrained.
TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.g.summary: Peak normalization bounds the first weight by one

TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.g.text: For every time in the first closed slab, the normalized weight is strictly positive. The proof uses the nonvanishing component of the central wave's transversality certificate and positivity of the frequency power. It prevents the weighted seminorm from dividing by a zero weight in the range actually measured.
TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.g.summary: The first time weight never vanishes on the slab

TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.l.text: The origin solution's covector at time zero is the first-wave launch covector at frequency $\lambda_1$. This is one of the origin data's defining properties. It identifies the carrier used in the periodic hierarchy with the covector used in the central wave equation, which is necessary before transferring normalization estimates.
TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.l.summary: The initial covector equals the chosen carrier

TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.l.text: Computes the initial norm of the origin solution's covector as $\lambda_1$. It combines its equality with the explicit launch covector and that carrier's norm calculation. This is the normalization field required when the first input is converted into a common selected physical seed.
TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.l.summary: The central covector starts at the child frequency

TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.l.text: Computes the norm of the first-wave launch covector as $\lambda_1$. The proof unfolds the coordinate vector, applies its unit norm and uses positivity of the selected frequency to remove an absolute value. It connects the Euclidean lift's explicit carrier with the paper's scalar frequency normalization.

Chooses the physical leading input over the selection's actual parent geometry, using the origin solution's scale, the scheduled radius and the scheduled width. The velocity and pressure therefore share the same normalization and carrier. The parent identities and positivity lemmas supply all constructor hypotheses; both switch terms vanish in this first-wave input.
TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.l.summary: The selected first velocity and pressure profiles

TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.l.text: Builds the relay certificate from zero phase mean of the leading pressure, zero average and transverse leading force, and compatibility of the completion switch with the selected solver. The force conditions follow from the zero leading switch. These identities ensure that the general recurrence handles the first wave with its actual pressure normalization.
TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.l.summary: The first input satisfies the relay normalizations

TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.l.text: The selected leading switch is definitionally zero. The first wave is already present at time zero, so no derivative of a temporal cutoff contributes forcing to its leading equation. This fact is used in the residual estimate to take the zero-switch branch of the common stage argument.

Shows that the selected first input is inactive outside the topological support of its periodized radial envelope. The activation time in this predicate is zero. The proof includes ordinary support in its closure and reuses the explicit first-input support theorem, so the conclusion applies to both leading velocity and phase pressure.
TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.l.summary: The selected leading wave stays in its envelope

TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.l.text: Proves zero phase average of the selected leading pressure for every label and time on the slab. The lattice periodization shifts the phase, but the profile is periodic, so the shift preserves its mean. The pressure reduces to a constant multiple of the zero-mean periodic primitive, giving the normalization required by the linear relay.

TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.o.text: For every time on the closed first slab, the actual higher oscillatory remainder is differentiable at the spatial origin. Joint slab smoothness is restricted to a spatial slice, where the spatial domain is all of Euclidean space. The conclusion includes time zero and supplies the derivative used in the central-gradient splitting.
TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.o.summary: The first higher oscillations can be differentiated at zero

TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.o.text: For a time on the first slab, any point where the selected oscillation is nonzero lies within distance $\lambda_0^{-1}$ of a lattice point. The proof transfers the label-envelope support through the parent flow and uses a sufficiently small radius. On the torus, all these lattice points represent the origin.
TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.o.summary: The first oscillation stays near the lattice

TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.p.text: Returns the stationary Euler stage at index zero, using the tilt and initial-frequency inequalities already stored in the selection. Its activation time is zero. The subsequent velocity, flow and pressure identities reveal the concrete fields of this stage; the definition itself does not choose an arbitrary parent satisfying abstract estimates.
TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.p.summary: The parent is the prescribed stationary shear

TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.p.text: Identifies the two-time parent flow with the stationary-shear flow evaluated at the time difference. This is a definitional equality of the stored flow functions. In particular, setting the terminal time to zero produces the inverse-flow expression used to evaluate the first physical wave.

The pressure stored in the first selection's parent stage is exactly the zero function. This equality concerns the stationary parent, whose self-advection vanishes; it does not say that the first wave or its corrections have zero pressure. It removes the parent pressure term when assembling the initial approximation.

Identifies the selected parent's velocity, as a function of time and position, with the stationary shear at the scheduled tilt. The equality is global in the time variable because the stage stores a global field. It serves to rewrite the hierarchy's parent term before the first-wave central estimates are applied.
TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.p.summary: The selected parent velocity is stationary

TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.p.text: Supplies the qualitative properties of a physical approximation for the selected first hierarchy. It uses the actual parent geometry, the slab-duration bound and depth at least two. This certificate covers qualitative equations and regularity; the numerical bounds needed for the inductive stage are supplied later by a scheduled physical stage.
TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.p.summary: The first approximation satisfies its qualitative equations

TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.r.text: Defines the first envelope radius as $((\lambda_0^9)^a)^{-1}$. The parent scale is $\mathsf D=\lambda_0^9$, and the natural exponent controls spatial localization. The certified parameter record already excludes a zero denominator. The subsequent selection lemmas expose positivity and prove that the envelope fits strictly inside the centered cell when its exponent meets the selected floor.
TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.r.summary: The first envelope uses a negative parent power

TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.r.text: Proves $2r<1/2$ for the selected envelope radius. The argument uses the exponent floor and the initial frequency bound to obtain a stronger numerical radius bound. This is the support-margin hypothesis required to periodize the localized profile smoothly without a discontinuity at the faces of the fundamental cell.
TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.r.summary: The envelope lies inside the centered cell

TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.r.text: Rewrites the reciprocal natural-power definition of the radius as the real power $\mathsf D^{-a}$, with $\mathsf D=\lambda_0^9$. The selected positive frequency licenses the real-power identities. This equality reconciles the arithmetic representation used in the implementation with the negative-power notation of the envelope estimates.
TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.r.summary: Natural powers give the stated radius exponent

TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.r.text: If $j\le a$, the chosen radius $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$ is at most $\mathsf D^{-j}$. The proof uses $\mathsf D\ge1$ to compare natural powers and reverses the order when taking reciprocals. Thus one selected exponent can satisfy several smaller fixed-order localization requirements simultaneously.
TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.r.summary: A larger envelope exponent gives a smaller radius

TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.r.text: For every natural $j\le a$, multiplying the radius by $\mathsf D^j$ gives at most one. This follows from the reciprocal comparison and positivity of the parent scale. The estimate is used to turn slow spatial derivative losses into dimensionless bounds at the chosen envelope scale.
TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.r.summary: The radius absorbs a bounded parent power

TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.r.text: Uses the initial frequency lower bound to show that the parent power and its reciprocal are strictly positive. No cancellation at a zero denominator is involved in the selected regime. This fact is passed to the radial-envelope and periodization constructors used by the first physical wave.

TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.v.text: Expresses the first approximation as the stationary shear, the explicit transported leading profile, the actual oscillatory remainder and the actual mean correction. The equality holds on the closed first slab. In particular, the later central-gradient estimates can differentiate the same remainder that occurs in this identity.
TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.v.summary: The selected first velocity has its actual corrections

TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.w.text: Defines the phase width as the real power $\lambda_1^{-1/2}$. The argument is a certified frequency schedule, whose constraints already force the first child frequency above one. The following lemmas expose strict positivity and the upper bound by one using the stronger first-wave selection data, ready for the smooth periodic profile and pressure primitive.
TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.w.summary: The phase width is the inverse square root

TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.w.text: Since the first child frequency is at least one, its nonpositive real power is at most one. Together with positivity of the width, this puts the phase width in the interval $(0,1]$ required by the profile estimates. It does not impose any separate lower bound independent of the frequency.
TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.w.summary: The first phase width is at most one

TorusEuler.InductiveFirstWaveSelection.w.text: The positive first child frequency makes its real power with exponent $-1/2$ strictly positive. The proof uses the selection's convenient frequency lemma to supply the lower-width hypothesis of the periodic profile and phase primitive. This is compatible with positivity already implied by the underlying certified frequency schedule.

TorusEuler.IsEulerSolution.text: For a finite real $T>0$, velocity $u(t,x)\in\mathbb R^3$ and pressure $p(t,x)\in\mathbb R$ are jointly smooth on $[0,T)\times\mathbb R^3$, and invariant under $x\mapsto x+n$ for $n\in\mathbb Z^3$. They satisfy $\partial_tu+D_xu\,u+\nabla p=0$ and $\operatorname{div}u=0$ there, with $\int_{[-1/2,1/2]^3}p(t,x)\,dx=0$. The derivative in time is taken within $[0,T)$, hence from the right at zero. The underlying functions have values at all real times, but this condition constrains only the indicated interval. It imposes neither initial data nor oddness, maximality or singularity formation.
TorusEuler.IsEulerSolution.summary: Euler holds pointwise on a half-open time interval

TorusEuler.IsEulerSolution.complexPressu.text: For an Euler solution at a time in its half-open slab, the complexified pressure is $C^2$, periodic, has zero centered-cell mean and solves $\Delta p=-\operatorname{div}\operatorname{div}(u\otimes u)$. Taking divergence of momentum removes the divergence-free time derivative. Incompressibility identifies tensor divergence with self-advection, and coordinate lemmas align the real and complex operators.
TorusEuler.IsEulerSolution.complexPressu.summary: Euler momentum gives the normalized tensor Poisson equation

TorusEuler.IsEulerSolution.contDiff_velo.text: Given a classical Euler solution $(u,p)$ on $[0,T)$ (jointly smooth, spatially periodic, with mean-zero pressure) and $t\in[0,T)$, this theorem shows that the slice $u(t,\cdot)$ is infinitely differentiable on all of $\mathbb R^3$. Its proof restricts joint smoothness on the slab $[0,T)\times\mathbb R^3$ along the map $x\mapsto(t,x)$. This is the direct bridge from the solution hypotheses to the regularity needed when interpreting the spatial derivative, divergence and curl. It proves smoothness of an existing solution; it does not construct one.

TorusEuler.IsEulerSolution.hasDerivWithi.text: Let $(u,p)$ be a classical Euler solution on $[0,T)$. For every $t\in[0,T)$ and every position $x$, the trajectory $r\mapsto u(r,x)$ has derivative within $[0,T)$ at $t$ equal to the time derivative $\partial_tu(t,x)$ computed within $[0,T)$; at $t=0$ this is the right derivative. Joint smoothness of the velocity supplies the differentiability.
TorusEuler.IsEulerSolution.hasDerivWithi.summary: The chosen time derivative is an actual derivative

TorusEuler.IsEulerSolution.hasOffOriginL.text: An actual Euler solution whose velocity and pressure gradient have spatial terminal limits also has terminal limits for its time derivative. The momentum equation identifies that derivative with negative self advection minus pressure gradient. Spatial smoothness comes from the solution being smooth on $[0,T)\times\mathbb R^3$; convergence of the pressure gradient remains an explicit assumption here.
TorusEuler.IsEulerSolution.hasOffOriginL.summary: Velocity and pressure limits determine the time derivative limit

TorusEuler.IsEulerSolution.hasOffOriginL.text: For an actual Euler solution on $[0,T)$, obtains off-origin limits of $\partial_tu$ as $t\uparrow T$ from a continuous periodic terminal velocity smooth away from the origin, uniform convergence on compact sets away from the origin of every spatial derivative, and uniform velocity convergence on the closure of a fundamental cell. The pressure Poisson equation supplied by the solution controls the nonlocal pressure gradient. Local velocity convergence alone is not the stated hypothesis.
TorusEuler.IsEulerSolution.hasOffOriginL.summary: Velocity convergence also controls the Euler acceleration

TorusEuler.IsEulerSolution.hasSmoothOffO.text: Let $u,p$ be a smooth periodic Euler solution on $[0,T)$ with $T>0$, and assume that the specified velocity field is jointly smooth on the closed punctured slab $[0,T]\times(\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3)$. The formal statement gives a periodic field $g$ smooth on $\mathbb R\times(\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3)$ and equal to $u$ for $0\le t<T$ away from the lattice. Its time domain is larger than the neighborhood required by the auxiliary theorem. Agreement is stated for $t<T$; continuity on the closed punctured slab also determines the terminal trace. No pressure extension, incompressibility after $T$, or Euler equation for the extended field is asserted.
TorusEuler.IsEulerSolution.hasSmoothOffO.summary: The extension exists at all real times

TorusEuler.IsEulerSolution.isMaximal_of_.text: Let $T>0$ and let $u,p$ be a smooth periodic incompressible Euler solution on $[0,T)$, with mean-zero pressure. If $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\to\infty$ as $t\uparrow T$, then no smooth Euler solution on $[0,S)$, $S>T$, agrees with $u$ for every $0\le t<T$. A continuation would have a continuous spatial derivative near the interior point $(T,0)$, contradicting this limit. The torus is represented by period-one fields on $\mathbb R^3$. This proves the noncontinuation step of Corollary 8.3. It neither proves nor assumes divergence of the vorticity time integral; that is a separate assertion.
TorusEuler.IsEulerSolution.isMaximal_of_.summary: Divergent central vorticity excludes a longer smooth Euler solution

TorusEuler.IsEulerSolution.velocity_eq_o.text: Let $u,p$ and $v,q$ be smooth periodic Euler solutions with mean-zero pressures on $[0,T_1)$ and $[0,T_2)$, where $T_1,T_2>0$. If $u(0)=v(0)$, the formal theorem proves $u(t,x)=v(t,x)$ for every $x\in\mathbb R^3$ and $0\le t<\min(T_1,T_2)$. Neither maximality nor oddness is assumed. The conclusion compares velocities on their common interval; it does not assert $T_1=T_2$, since one solution could simply have been restricted to a shorter interval. In Theorem 1.1, maximality is used separately to identify the lifespans. Values outside the solution intervals are irrelevant to this comparison.
TorusEuler.IsEulerSolution.velocity_eq_o.summary: Equal initial velocities give equal classical velocities

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.text: Given a velocity $U$ and a time set $I$, the formal object records maps $X(s,t,a)$ with $X(s,s,a)=a$ and $\partial_tX(s,t,a)=U(t,X(s,t,a))$ for $s,t\in I$. The paper's notation $X(t,a)$ means $X(0,t,a)$; its inverse label map is obtained from $X(t,0,x)$ once uniqueness of trajectories is established. Derivatives at interval endpoints are taken within the time interval. The maps are defined for all real times, but these equations are asserted only on $I$. Periodicity, regularity, invertibility and volume preservation are not imposed by this definition.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.summary: Particle trajectories are recorded from any starting time

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.add_latticeVect.text: Let $I=[l,r]$, suppose $X(s,t,a)$ solves the trajectory equation for $U$, and assume $U(t,\cdot)$ is periodic under every integer translation and Lipschitz with one constant valid for all $t\in I$. For any $s,t\in I$, $a\in\mathbb R^3$ and $n\in\mathbb Z^3$, the formal statement proves $X(s,t,a+n)=X(s,t,a)+n$. Thus the lifted flow descends to $\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3$. The paper uses the case $s=0$ with a smooth periodic parent, which supplies the Lipschitz bound on a compact time interval. No equation of motion for the parent beyond its prescribed velocity is required.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.add_latticeVect.summary: Periodicity of the velocity passes to equivariance of particle trajectories

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.center_coframe_.text: For a twice smooth periodic odd parent flow on a positive slab, let the prescribed central covector solve the central adjoint ODE from activation time $t_0$. Pulling its activation value back by the adjoint forward deformation defines a launch covector $k$. Its subsequent inverse-coframe transport equals the prescribed covector on $[t_0,T]$, and a nonzero activation covector gives nonzero $k$.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.center_coframe_.summary: The launch covector reproduces the prescribed central wave

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.contDiffOn_forw.text: For the same smooth periodic parent and positive slab, the spatial Fréchet derivative of the forward flow is jointly smooth in time and label. The proof differentiates the already established joint flow regularity in the spatial direction. Positivity of $T$ supplies unique differentiation on the closed time interval, so endpoint regularity is retained.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.contDiffOn_forw.summary: The forward deformation is smooth in time and label

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.contDiffOn_forw.text: A jointly smooth periodic parent velocity on a positive closed time slab has a jointly smooth supplied label flow starting at time zero. Periodicity gives a uniform spatial Lipschitz bound, while the flow’s initial map is the identity. The theorem establishes regularity of the flow map $X$ itself by parameter dependence of trajectories, including the endpoints in the within-slab sense.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.contDiffOn_forw.summary: The actual forward flow is jointly smooth

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.contDiffOn_inve.text: The derivative of the inverse label flow, evaluated along the forward flow, is jointly smooth on the closed parent slab. The two flow-derivative inverse identities identify it with the algebraic inverse of the smooth forward deformation. These identities place the operator in the unit group before smooth inversion is used; no arbitrary singular-matrix inverse is interpreted geometrically.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.contDiffOn_inve.summary: The actual inverse deformation is jointly smooth

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.contDiffOn_inve.text: For a smooth periodic parent on a positive closed slab, the map $(t,x)\mapsto X(t,0,x)$ is jointly smooth. The proof uses the time-preserving forward map $(t,a)\mapsto(t,X(0,t,a))$, establishes continuity of its actual inverse, and writes the inverse of its block derivative explicitly. Thus the result concerns the supplied inverse flow, including within-slab endpoint derivatives.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.contDiffOn_inve.summary: The actual inverse label flow is jointly smooth

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.contDiffOn_mate.text: The material gradient $M(t,a)=D_xU(t,X(0,t,a))$ is jointly smooth on the positive closed slab for a smooth periodic parent. The proof first obtains the jointly smooth spatial derivative of $U$ and then composes it with the smooth forward label flow. This provides the actual coefficient field used by the labelwise amplitude equation.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.contDiffOn_mate.summary: The parent gradient stays smooth along its flow

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.contDiffOn_tran.text: For any fixed launch covector $k$, its inverse-coframe transport is jointly smooth in time and label under the smooth periodic parent-flow hypotheses. This follows by applying the continuous linear adjoint map to the smooth inverse deformation and then evaluating on $k$. Nonzero $k$ is not needed for this regularity statement; it is required later when dividing by the transported norm.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.contDiffOn_tran.summary: Transporting a fixed covector preserves joint smoothness

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.contDiff_invers.text: Assume the forward transition has $n+1$ continuous spatial derivatives, in addition to the periodic parent-flow hypotheses. The reverse Jacobian evaluated along the forward flow then has $n$ continuous label derivatives. The result follows by identifying it with the algebraic inverse of the forward derivative, whose values are invertible.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.contDiff_invers.summary: One extra flow derivative regularizes the inverse Jacobian

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.continuousOn_la.text: For a $C^2$ periodic flow started at the left endpoint $l$, the label Jacobian $D_aX(l\to t)(a)$ is jointly continuous across the closed slab. The additional hypotheses that the velocity is spatially Lipschitz with constant $K$, and its spatial derivative Lipschitz with constant $L$, at every slab time control them uniformly in labels. These supply a uniform label-continuity estimate for the variational matrices before assembling joint continuity.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.continuousOn_la.summary: The spatial Jacobian varies continuously in time and label

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.continuousOn_ti.text: For a fixed starting time $s$ in the slab, spatial Lipschitz control of the velocity at every slab time and the trajectory equation imply joint continuity of $X(s\to t)a$ in target time $t$ and starting label $a$. The domain is the closed time interval times all of Euclidean label space. The theorem asserts continuity, without claiming joint differentiability or regularity in the starting-time parameter.

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.det_labelDeriva.text: Let $l<r$ and let $U$ be jointly $C^2$ on $[l,r]\times\mathbb R^3$, periodic in space and divergence free. Suppose $X(s,t,a)$ solves its trajectory equation with the identity at time $s$. For every $s,t\in[l,r]$ and label $a$, the formal statement proves $\det D_aX(s,t,a)=1$. This is the volume preservation used when changing variables between Eulerian and label integrals in §1.2. It requires neither oddness nor an Euler momentum equation. By itself it supplies the Jacobian factor; cancellation of the pressure term also requires periodicity and the divergence constraint on the variation.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.det_labelDeriva.summary: The deformation determinant remains one along a divergence-free flow

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.differentiableA.text: A jointly $C^2$ periodic velocity on a nondegenerate slab has label-differentiable transitions between every pair of allowed times. The theorem obtains this from the variational solution already constructed, assuming both times lie in the slab. It concludes differentiability at each arbitrary Euclidean starting label.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.differentiableA.summary: Smooth periodic flows differentiate in the label

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.even_materialGr.text: Let $U(t,\cdot)$ be odd and uniformly Lipschitz in space on a closed time interval, and let $X_{s,t}$ be its flow. Then both $a\mapsto\nabla U(t,X_{s,t}(a))$ and $a\mapsto\kappa(t,a)$ are even, where $\kappa(t,a)=D(X_{t,s})(X_{s,t}(a))^Tk_*$. This gives evenness of $M$ and $\kappa$ in the label variable for the smooth parent in §5.1. The formal result does not assume differentiability: its derivative expression is assigned zero at points where a derivative does not exist. In the smooth application it is the usual derivative. Evenness of $D_aX$ follows separately by differentiating oddness of the flow.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.even_materialGr.summary: An odd parent has even material gradient and wave vector

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.exists_bound_it.text: Assume the $n$th label derivative of the flow, $D_a^nX(0,t,a)$, is jointly continuous in $(t,a)$ through the closed slab. Spatial periodicity reduces its size to a compact label cell, producing one real bound for every time and label. The theorem uses $n\ge1$ to exclude the unbounded zeroth-order lifted transition map.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.exists_bound_it.summary: A continuous periodic derivative has a uniform bound

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.exists_lattice_.text: Let $T>0$, let $X$ be the two-time label flow of $U$ on $[0,T]$ (so $X(s,t,a)$ is the position at time $t$ of the particle at $a$ at time $s$), and assume $U$ is jointly $C^2$ on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3$ and each $U(s,\cdot)$, $s\in[0,T]$, is $\mathbb Z^3$-periodic and odd. Fix $t\in[0,T]$ and $\ell>0$. Assume $2\le\mu\le\mathsf D$, $\ell\le\mathsf D^{-3}$, and $\|D_aX(0,t,a)\|\le\mathsf D$ for every $a$. If the label $X(t,0,x)$ lies in the closed support of the periodized radial envelope $a\mapsto\chi(|c(a)|/\ell)$ (with $c(a)$ the centered representative of $a$, and $\chi$ equal to one on $[0,1]$ and zero on $[2,\infty)$), then some lattice point $n\in\mathbb Z^3$ satisfies $|n-x|\le\mu^{-1}$. It follows from the bound $2\mathsf D\ell$ and $2\mathsf D^{-2}\le\mu^{-1}$.
TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.exists_lattice_.summary: A small envelope radius confines the physical envelope within $\mu^{-1}$ of the lattice

TorusEuler.IsLabelFlowOn.exists_lattice_.text: Let $T>0$, let $X$ be the two-time label flow of $U$ on $[0,T]$ (so $X(s,t,a)$ is the position at time $t$ of the particle at $a$ at time $s$), and assume $U$ is jointly $C^2$ on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3$ and each $U(s,\cdot)$, $s\in[0,T]$, is $\mathbb Z^3$-periodic and odd. Fix $t\in[0,T]$ and $\ell>0$. Assume $\mathsf D\ge0$ and $\|D_aX(0,t,a)\|\le\mathsf D$ for every $a$.
