TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.SeedNear.text: Given functions $M(t,a)$, $\kappa(t,a)$, $\mathbf a_c(t)$ and $\mathbf a(t,a)$, and real parameters $t_0,T,\ell_*,\mathsf D,C$, this condition requires the following for $t\in[t_0,T]$ and $|a|\le2\ell_*$: $|\mathbf a(t,a)-\mathbf a_c(t)|\le C|a||\mathbf a_c(t)|$, $\tfrac12|\mathbf a_c(t)|\le|\mathbf a(t,a)|\le2|\mathbf a_c(t)|$, $(2\mathsf D)^{-1}|\kappa(t,0)||\mathbf a_c(t)|\le\kappa(t,a)\cdot M(t,a)\mathbf a(t,a)$, $\kappa(t,a)\cdot M(t,a)\mathbf a(t,a)>0$, and $(8\mathsf D)^{-1}\le\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a/(|\kappa||\mathbf a|)$. The constant $C$ is supplied, not chosen by this definition. No smoothness or seed equation is imposed here. The paper's application has $\mathsf D\ge2$ and positive radius; unrestricted reciprocals at zero are assigned zero. The condition includes more than (5.19), but does not require $C$ to be a uniform power of $\mathsf D$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.SeedNear.summary: The nearby seed obeys amplitude and coupling comparisons

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.TransverseSoluti.text: The fields are smooth phase-periodic profiles on $[0,T]$, compatible with the same label translations and with the same transported nonzero covector. Two transverse solutions with the same source, zero initial velocity and zero-mean pressure agree. The homogeneous ordinary differential equation eliminates their velocity difference; pressure normalization then removes the remaining phase-constant difference. This proves the uniqueness asserted in §5.4 and transfers bounds for the chosen solution to every solution covered by Lemma 5.3. The equation is $V_t+MV+\kappa\mathsf p_s=f$, with $\kappa\cdot V=0$, $\langle V\rangle_s=\langle\mathsf p\rangle_s=0$, and $V(0)=0$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.TransverseSoluti.summary: The source and normalization determine both unknown fields

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.TransverseSolvab.text:
Every source of zero phase mean has a solution of (5.15) from $V(0) = 0$ with pressure of zero phase mean; this is the ODE solve of the earlier library construction. The operators use the same parent inverse deformation, strain and transported covector as the paper. The selected transverse solution is determined by zero initial velocity and zero phase mean of its pressure.

Default values: The statement is quantified only over sources with zero phase average and asks for an actual transverse solution. It provides no solution for an inadmissible source and contains no default fallback. Zero start and pressure normalization are part of the solution conditions.
TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.TransverseSolvab.summary: Existence of a transverse solution for every admissible source

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.activationProfil.text:
The activation term $S = \tilde\chi'A_1$ of (3.8) as a twisted profile. A smooth compactly supported label profile is extended with the twisted lattice rule and period one in phase. The envelope fitting strictly inside the centered cell is what permits equality with the original profile there.

Default values: The constructors require a positive envelope radius fitting strictly inside the label cell, positive phase width at most one, and the stated seed/launch regularity. For time factors the vanishing-before-activation hypothesis allows smooth extension across activation. They bundle a twisted profile; equality with a raw localized expression is asserted only on the proved slab and cell domains.
TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.activationProfil.summary: The forcing introduced by switching on the wave

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.centerWaveOn_con.text: The central wave conditions (covector equation, nonvanishing and orthogonality, seed equation and transverse stability at the origin) depend only on the values of the covector on $[t_0,T]$. The bridge identifies the carrier, central seed and launch data used in Section 5 with the corresponding data of the earlier construction. Equalities are asserted on the relevant closed time slab.
TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.centerWaveOn_con.summary: Equal central covectors give the same wave conditions

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.complete_congr.text: The library completion $C[\cdot]$ only depends on the coefficient profiles. The bridge extracts only the stated consequence of those hypotheses.
TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.complete_congr.summary: Equal coefficients give equal divergence corrections

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.construct_isExpa.text: The library construction over the solvers chosen from the assumed existence of normalized mean solutions and of zero-start transverse solutions at depth $P \ge 1$, with completion switch $C[S]$, parent residual $R$ and leading pair $L$, satisfies the defining recursions of the Section 5 expansion as soon as $R = R_U\circ X$, $S = \tilde\chi'A_1$ and $L = (\tilde\chi A_1, \tilde\chi\mathsf p[A_1])$ on the label cell. At level $p$ the mean is solved before the transverse correction, because the new mean transports the leading wave. The finite recursion uses the prescribed mean pressure normalization and a zero-start transverse solution.
TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.construct_isExpa.summary: The library recursion satisfies the paper expansion equations

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.continuousOn_sli.text: A jointly continuous field of $(t,a)$ is continuous in $t$ at a fixed label. TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.cutoffSymbol_app.text: The symbol of Section 5.7 (radial, smooth, $0 \le \psi \le 1$, $\psi = 1$ on $|\zeta| \le 1$, $\psi = 0$ for $|\zeta| > 2$) satisfies the hypotheses of Appendix B. The norm is computed before phase substitution. TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.cutoffSymbol_app.summary: The selected Fourier symbol satisfies the cutoff assumptions

The transverse solver exists because every source of zero phase mean has a solution of (5.15) from $V(0)=0$ with pressure of zero phase mean. The parent is smooth, periodic, odd and divergence free on the closed time interval, with the deformation and velocity-gradient bounds of Section 5. The bridge extracts only the stated consequence of those hypotheses.
TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.exists_truncated.summary: The paper parent gives the library coefficient data

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.fieldNormFinite_.text: Every smooth twisted profile has bounded weighted jets on any time set $A \subseteq [0,T]$ with a bounded time multiplier $\tau$: the field $\tau f$ has finite norms (D.1) of every order. The norm is computed before phase substitution. Bounds for weighted profiles require a bounded inverse time weight on the active interval; continuous positivity supplies that bound for the actual central seed.
TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.fieldNormFinite_.summary: Bounded time multiplication preserves finite profile norms

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.fieldNormFinite_.text: The slices of a profile on $[0,T]$ have finite norms (D.1) of every order. The norm is computed before phase substitution. Bounds for weighted profiles require a bounded inverse time weight on the active interval; continuous positivity supplies that bound for the actual central seed.
TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.fieldNormFinite_.summary: Smooth twisted profiles have finite derivative norms

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.fieldNormFinite_.text: The field $f/\gamma$ of a profile on $[t_0,T]$ has finite norms (D.1) of every order when $\gamma$ is continuous and positive on $[t_0,T]$. TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.fieldNormFinite_.summary: Unit weighted slices have finite derivative norms

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.pressureCore.text:
$c(t) (-p_w|_{g=1}) P_h(s)$: the leading pressure without its envelope, times a time factor. A smooth compactly supported label profile is extended with the twisted lattice rule and period one in phase. The envelope fitting strictly inside the centered cell is what permits equality with the original profile there.

Default values: The pointwise formula is defined for every input, including arbitrary width and zero covector, because inverse expressions take default values (division by zero gives zero). It has its intended pressure meaning only where the transported covector is nonzero and $0<h\le1$, as supplied by the parent and launch hypotheses. The spatial envelope is omitted at this stage.
TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.pressureCore.summary: The wave pressure before spatial localization

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.pressureCore_smo.text: The pressure core is smooth on the slab. The proof uses library copies of the smoothness of the bare wave pressure and of the fact that a smooth multiplier vanishing before $t_0$ extends active smoothness across activation, with the smoothness of $M$, $\kappa$ and of the seed and $\kappa \ne 0$ on the active slab. A smooth compactly supported label profile is extended with the twisted lattice rule and period one in phase. The envelope fitting strictly inside the centered cell is what permits equality with the original profile there.
TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.pressureCore_smo.summary: A smooth time factor gives smooth leading pressure

Default values: These are restrictions along a subtype of times, with no extension or alteration of values. The time set may be empty; norm identities or finiteness statements supply the relevant slab and boundedness conditions separately. Restricting a weight does not itself prove positivity.

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.seedOnOfIsSeed.text:
A seed in the paper's sense, solving (3.2) on $[t_0,T]$ with the projected initial data $\mathbf a(t_0,a)=(I-P_{\kappa(t_0,a)})\mathbf a(t_0,0)$, becomes the localized seed carrying the quantitative conclusions of (5.22) only after the separate near-origin bounds are supplied. These bounds, for $|a|\le2\ell_*$ and $t\in[t_0,T]$, are a label-Lipschitz bound with constant $C$, the two-sided size bound $|\mathbf a(t,0)|/2\le|\mathbf a(t,a)|\le2|\mathbf a(t,0)|$, and lower bounds for $\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a$ and its ratio to $|\kappa||\mathbf a|$. The amplitude is copied unchanged. This construction must not be read as assuming (5.19) in the statement of Lemma 5.3.

Both a paper seed and the additional near-origin estimates are required. The amplitude is exactly the supplied amplitude, with no chosen replacement or zero padding. This construction does not prove the near estimates and cannot be used as a substitute for their proof.
TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.seedOnOfIsSeed.summary: Add proved near origin estimates to the seed data

Existence hypotheses for the mean and transverse equations select one solution for each admissible source. The completion operator is the actual curl correction. Separate specification theorems recover the full mean and transverse predicates from the selected outputs, including the pressure normalization.

Classical choice selects witnesses from the explicitly supplied solvability predicates. No computable solver or canonical formula is claimed. Mean and transverse pressure normalizations and uniqueness are proved separately, so an arbitrary choice is later identified with any admissible solution.

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.transverseSolvab.summary: Solve the transverse equation from zero initial data

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.transverse_homog.text: A homogeneous solution of (5.15) — $V_t + MV + \kappa\partial_s\mathsf p = 0$, $\kappa\cdot V = 0$, $V(0) = 0$, and $\mathsf p$ of zero phase mean — vanishes. Transversality eliminates the pressure slope, $\partial_s\mathsf p = -2\kappa\cdot MV/|\kappa|^2$, so that $V_t = -(\mathrm{Id} - 2P_\kappa)MV$ at each label and phase, a linear ODE with zero initial value; then $\partial_s\mathsf p = 0$, and the zero phase mean gives $\mathsf p = 0$. The operators use the same parent inverse deformation, strain and transported covector as the paper. The selected transverse solution is determined by zero initial velocity and zero phase mean of its pressure.
TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.transverse_homog.summary: Zero transverse initial data and forcing give the zero solution

abla U(t,0)^T \kappa$ transports to $\kappa$ along the origin: $\kappa(t,0) = \kappa(t)$ on $[t_0,T]$ (and $k_* 
e 0$ when $\kappa(t_0) 
e 0$). The bridge identifies the carrier, central seed and launch data used in Section 5 with the corresponding data of the earlier construction. Equalities are asserted on the relevant closed time slab.
TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.waveVector_origi.summary: Recover the transported central covector from its carrier

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.width_le_one.text: The chosen phase width is at most one. The parent is smooth, periodic, odd and divergence free on the closed time interval, with the deformation and velocity-gradient bounds of Section 5. The bridge extracts only the stated consequence of those hypotheses.

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.width_pos.text: The chosen phase width is positive. The parent is smooth, periodic, odd and divergence free on the closed time interval, with the deformation and velocity-gradient bounds of Section 5. The bridge extracts only the stated consequence of those hypotheses.

TorusEuler.Paper.Corollary83Conclusions.text: For prescribed $T,u,p$, these are the requirements of Corollary 8.3, not an existence proof. The velocity and mean-zero pressure solve smooth periodic Euler on $[0,T)$, where $0<T<\infty$, and have no smooth Euler continuation agreeing with the velocity there. Every maximal solution of finite lifespan from $u(0)$ must have the same terminal time $T$. Both $\int_0^T\|\operatorname{curl}u(t)\|_\infty\,dt$ and $\int_0^T\|\nabla u(t)\|_\infty\,dt$ are infinite. The formalization uses nonnegative Lebesgue integrals and essential suprema on $[-1/2,1/2]^3$; the gradient has its operator norm. No equation is imposed at $t=T$, and no value at that time contributes to either integral.
TorusEuler.Paper.Corollary83Conclusions.summary: Specify maximality, its time, and the two infinite integrals

TorusEuler.Paper.EndpointSystemSolution.text: On $[0,T]\times\mathbb T^3$, let $z,v$ be divergence-free $C^{0,1/2}$ fields, $c$ a time-independent field in the same space, and $G$ a vector field. The condition requires continuous $v,G$, $z_t=v$, $z(0)=z(T)=0$, and $Kv-J(\Omega v)+L=c+G$, where $Jw(t)=\int_0^tw(s)\,ds$. At each time, $G=\nabla_a\phi$ for a periodic scalar potential. Divergence is understood weakly; the spatial norm is the maximum of the supremum and half-Hölder seminorm. The functions are defined for all real times. Continuity, derivative and equation requirements concern $[0,T]$; the endpoint equalities are imposed for every $T$. The condition itself does not require $T>0$; the endpoint inverse uses a positive interval, with one-sided derivatives at its ends. No normalization or time regularity of $\phi$ is imposed. This specifies the solution class of (4.9); it proves neither existence nor uniqueness.
TorusEuler.Paper.EndpointSystemSolution.summary: Specify displacement, velocity, constant field and pressure gradient

TorusEuler.Paper.FiniteSmallness.text:
For the preceding wave, set $\sigma=|k_p(t_0)||\mathbf a_p(t_0)|$, $
u=B_{12}(t_0)>0$, $\eta=B_{32}(t_0)>0$, $r=\sqrt{2\sigma
u}$ and $\varepsilon=\eta/
u$. On a compact physical set $I$, let $\delta=\|B_{12}/
u-1\|_\infty+\|B_{32}/\eta-1\|_\infty+\|B\|_\infty/r+\|E_c\|_\infty/
u$, using Euclidean matrix operator norms. The formal condition is exactly $C_0\varepsilon\le1$ and $C_0T^{C_0}\delta\le\varepsilon$. Here $C_0$ is a nonnegative integer; the condition alone permits $C_0=0$ and does not require $T\ge2$. The lemmas separately impose a sufficiently large absolute lower bound on $C_0$ and $T\ge2$. If $I$ exceeds the physical interval corresponding to $[0,T]$, its larger suprema are used.
TorusEuler.Paper.FiniteSmallness.summary: Two inequalities quantify the required small coupling ratio and gradient error

TorusEuler.Paper.FreezingConclusion.text: Let $\mathcal R$ be a bounded projection on $C^{0,1/2}(\mathbb T^3;H)$ and $B$ a bounded operator-valued half-Hölder field. This condition says that $v\mapsto\mathcal R(Bv)$ is a bounded isomorphism on $\{v:\mathcal Rv=v\}$, with $\|v\|\le C(2+\mu^{-1}+\|B\|_\infty+L)^p\|\mathcal R(Bv)\|$, where $p$ is a nonnegative integer. For each $k\ge1$ for which $B\in C^{k,1/2}$, it requires preservation of that class in both directions and a common finite bound for the forward and inverse higher norms. Here $C,\mu,L$ are parameters: this condition does not itself impose their positivity, a Lipschitz inequality, or coercivity. Those are hypotheses of Lemma A.2, which proves the condition. Higher norms concern all spatial derivatives through the specified order; they are distinct from the base half-Hölder norm.
TorusEuler.Paper.FreezingConclusion.summary: State the base inverse and its higher regularity

TorusEuler.Paper.Lemma61Conclusions.text: For a first central wave over $B_\rho=2\pi(e_1+\rho e_3)\otimes e_2$, write $\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a|$ and $\nu=(\kappa/|\kappa|)\cdot B_\rho(\mathbf a/|\mathbf a|)$. This formal condition requires, for every $\mathsf D\ge2$, $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for every transverse amplitude solution and every $0\le t'\le t\le T$, together with $\nu(t)\ge\mathsf D^{-1}$ on $[0,T]$. It also requires $\lambda^{1/4}/2\le|\mathbf a(0)||\kappa(0)|\le\lambda^{1/4}$. These are the mathematical conclusions of Lemma 6.1. This declaration describes the three required estimates; it does not assert that an arbitrary first wave satisfies them. The short-interval and parameter hypotheses enter in the theorem proving this condition.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lemma61Conclusions.summary: Specifies weighted propagation, positive coupling and initial strength

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.CommonIncrement.text: The authors' source records this statement as not proved and outside the main argument; neither formal main theorem uses it. This proposition records the increment half of the joint auxiliary induction, uniformly over the cutoff and eligible construction choices in the statement layer. Given parent time bounds at order q, it demands eventual mixed increment bounds at order q + 1 for every spatial order m. The corresponding wrapper consumes this proposition as h. The definition itself does not discharge the analytic step.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.CommonIncrement.summary: The common increment induction step remains an input

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.CommonTime.text: The authors' source records this statement as not proved and outside the main argument; neither formal main theorem uses it. This proposition states the general time-estimate step for constructions admitted by the auxiliary statement. After a cutoff symbol, envelope-exponent floor, and majorant are chosen, it quantifies over eligible parameter records and constructions. Bounds through order q at one stage must imply bounds through order q + 1 at the next, eventually. The file explicitly leaves this proposition open; defining it supplies no witness or proof.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.CommonTime.summary: The common time induction step remains an input

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.exists_offOrigi.text: With $T>0$, decreasing stage slabs containing $T$, initial frequency at least two, and the terminal mixed increment bounds, there exists a field $w$ smooth on the punctured closed slab. At each point of that slab the stages tend to $w$. The proof selects a limit value only after local summation supplies a genuine limit; no value or smoothness at a lattice point, or outside the stated slab, is concluded.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.exists_offOrigi.summary: Assemble a smooth limit on the punctured closed slab

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.exists_threshol.text: Given any nonnegative integer $b$ and real functions $F,G$ on the nonnegative integers, the formal statement constructs a common threshold. One choice in the proof is $\mathcal B(s)=\exp(4K(s+1)^3)+\sum_{t=0}^s(|F(t)|+|G(7K(t))|)$, where $K(s)=320b(s+1)$. It is positive and nondecreasing, dominates the main majorant and $G(7K(s))$, and satisfies the required logarithmic lower bound. No monotonicity or positivity of $F,G$ is assumed. This proves that the two numerical threshold requirements can be met simultaneously. It does not establish that the prescribed majorants bound the analytic constants of a particular construction.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.exists_threshol.summary: A single function dominates both prescribed majorants

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.joint_jets_of_i.text: Assume the stages converge uniformly to $u$ on a closed time–ball cylinder, their slabs contain that cylinder and decrease, and every order of joint derivative increment has a summable eventual bound. For positive terminal time and ball radius, $u$ is smooth within the cylinder. The summable-bound hypothesis is local to the cylinder; no uniform convergence or terminal regularity at the singular origin is inferred.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.joint_jets_of_i.summary: Summable joint derivatives give a smooth local limit

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.lemma13_order.text: The input is Lemma 1.3 of the main paper, not the auxiliary lemma with the same number. Applying it to the recorded stage schedule shows that the scheduled derivative order tends to infinity with the stage index. The proof supplies the threshold, frequency recursion and order-maximum conditions from that schedule. This is the eventual-order fact needed for the zero-time-order mixed increment estimate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.lemma13_order.summary: The scheduled orders eventually exceed every fixed order

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.lemma_1_2_of_co.text: Assume the main order-growth lemma, the generalized auxiliary time bounds, and a uniform implication that advances the parent time bounds to the child's mixed correction bound. The formal statement deduces the generalized auxiliary Lemma 1.2: for each fixed $(m,q)$, the correction eventually has size at most $\lambda_j^{-1}$ in $C([0,S_j];C^{m,1/2})$, for every construction covered by the chosen threshold and step conditions. The threshold may be enlarged to satisfy all assumptions before choosing the construction. The analytic correction implication is an explicit hypothesis, as is the generalized time lemma. This declaration organizes those assumptions; it does not independently prove them or transfer the selected-construction theorem to all constructions.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.lemma_1_2_of_co.summary: The generalized estimate requires the common correction step

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.lemma_1_3_of_co.text: Assume a uniform implication that, for every qualifying construction and all sufficiently late stages, turns the parent bounds through order $q$ into child velocity and residual bounds through order $q+1$. The formal statement then obtains the generalized auxiliary Lemma 1.3, including time continuity in the spatial supremum norm. For each fixed $q$ and construction, one integer exponent and one starting stage work for all $i\le q$. The common implication is a mathematical hypothesis of this result, not a conclusion. The authors' formalization records this implication as an open input and does not prove it for every construction quantified over by the generalized lemma; the separate selected-construction argument has more specific hypotheses.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.lemma_1_3_of_co.summary: A uniform induction step gives the generalized bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.local_limit_of_.text: For stages with decreasing slabs containing the positive time $T$, initial frequency at least two, and terminal mixed increment bounds, every point $c\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3$ has a positive-radius neighborhood with a uniform smooth limit on the closed time cylinder. The proof sums the increments there and bounds joint derivatives by summable reciprocal frequencies. The excluded set $\mathbb Z^3$ consists of every lattice translate of zero in the periodic lift.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.local_limit_of_.summary: Construct the terminal limit near a nonsingular point

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.mixedIncrementB.text: For a stage index $j\ge1$, the stagewise mixed increment bound at $j-1$ yields the auxiliary bound for step $j$. The conclusions of Theorem 7.1 and its description of each step supply smoothness and the identification of the actual oscillation with its graph readout. They justify continuity in the spatial Hölder norm. The assumption $j\ge1$ makes natural-number predecessor notation agree with the intended preceding stage.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.mixedIncrementB.summary: Restore continuity and indexing to the mixed increment bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.mixedIncrement_.text: The theorem assumes divergence of the scheduled orders, the common increment step hinc, and the eventual auxiliary time bounds h13, as well as the stage conclusions and step data. It derives the mixed increment estimate for every spatial and time order eventually. For time order zero it uses the construction correction bound; higher orders use hinc after increasing the starting index beyond both required thresholds.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.mixedIncrement_.summary: Combine the time estimates with the mixed increment step

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.one_le_frequenc.text: Every frequency $\lambda_j$ of the inductive parameter schedule (exponent parameter, thresholds $\mathcal B(s)$, orders $q_j$ and frequencies with $\lambda_{j+1}=\lambda_j^{K(q_{j+1})}$) satisfies $\lambda_j\ge1$. The base case follows from the positive logarithmic threshold floor $4K(2)^3\le\log\mathcal B(1)$ with $\mathcal B(1)>0$ and the initial-threshold inequality $\mathcal B(1)\le\lambda_0$; the induction uses the frequency power law. This is an arithmetic consequence of the parameters, without an extra construction or convergence hypothesis. It justifies comparisons between natural and real powers in the auxiliary time bounds.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.one_le_frequenc.summary: Every scheduled frequency is at least one

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.smoothTerminalE.text: An existing smooth periodic extension of the velocity away from the lattice $\mathbb Z^3$ gives the terminal-extension property in the form the paper states, by choosing the neighborhood to be all times times $\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3$. Periodicity and agreement with $u$ are copied from the given extension, while smoothness is restricted to the required union. No Euler equation is imposed on the extended field after $T$, and no regularity at lattice points is asserted.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.smoothTerminalE.summary: Read a periodic extension as a terminal neighborhood

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.smoothTerminalE.text: Assume a common sequence with the lifetime, support and estimates of Theorem 7.1, and an Euler solution $u,p$ with the convergence and initial-data conclusions of Proposition 8.1. Suppose every fixed mixed derivative of $U_j-U_{j-1}-O_j$ eventually has size at most $\lambda_j^{-1}$ in its spatial Hölder norm, with time continuity on $[0,S_j]$. The formal statement proves that this same velocity $u$ has a periodic smooth extension through $T_\infty$ away from $\mathbb Z^3$. The proof first obtains a smooth limit on the closed punctured slab and identifies it with $u$ for $t<T_\infty$ by convergence. It assumes the mixed estimates; it imposes no Euler equation on the extension after the terminal time.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.smoothTerminalE.summary: Mixed correction bounds preserve the preterminal solution

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.stageTimeBounds.text: The auxiliary time bounds (1.3) at stage $j$ contain both the numerical derivative bounds, $|\partial_t^iU_j|\le\lambda_j^{\psi_q}$ and $|\partial_t^iR_j|\le\lambda_{j+1}^{-5/2}$ on $[0,S_j]\times\mathbb R^3$ for $i\le q$, and continuity in the spatial supremum norm. This theorem projects out the numerical bounds alone for the same construction, orders, and stage. It performs no induction and proves no new estimate; it lets the common induction step consume the bounds already supplied by auxiliary Lemma 1.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.stageTimeBounds.summary: Discard continuity from the auxiliary time estimate

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.stage_smooth.text: The conclusions of Theorem 7.1 supply a positive lifetime, smoothness of each stage velocity $U_j$ on $[0,S_j]\times\mathbb R^3$, and periodic velocity. Together with the smoothness of the stage pressure, the theorem proves $S_j>0$ and joint smoothness and periodicity for both the velocity $U_j$ and the residual $R_j$ on that slab. The residual is the actual momentum residual of the stage velocity and pressure. These facts provide continuity in the spatial norms used by the auxiliary estimates.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.stage_smooth.summary: Velocity and residual are smooth on every stage slab

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.timeBounds_of_s.text: Given the conclusions of Theorem 7.1 and the numerical bounds $|\partial_t^iU_j|\le\lambda_j^{\psi_q}$, $|\partial_t^iR_j|\le\lambda_{j+1}^{-5/2}$ on $[0,S_j]$ for $i\le q$, this theorem obtains the full auxiliary time bounds (1.3). The numerical estimates are inherited unchanged. Joint smoothness and periodicity of velocity and residual give continuity of each fixed-spatial-point time derivative in the supremum norm. Thus the conclusion includes the membership in the continuous-in-time function space $C([0,S_j];L^\infty)$ written in auxiliary display (1.3).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.timeBounds_of_s.summary: Restore continuity to the auxiliary time estimate

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.timeBounds_of_s.text: Assume a step hypothesis: for every $q$ and $\psi$ there is $\Psi$ such that, for all sufficiently large $n$, the numerical bounds of time order $q$ with exponent $\psi$ at stage $n$ imply those of order $q+1$ with exponent $\Psi$ at stage $n+1$. Together with the conclusions of Theorem 7.1, induction yields, for each $q$, the exponent $\psi_q$ and starting index $j_q$ required by auxiliary (1.3), including continuity, at every stage $j\ge j_q$. The zero-order estimates come from the stage record. The analytic induction step is an explicit hypothesis here, not a conclusion established by this framing theorem.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.timeBounds_of_s.summary: Iterate a supplied step to all time orders

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.witness_of_sect.text: The inputs are the conclusions of Proposition 8.1, Proposition 8.2, Corollary 8.3 and Proposition 8.4 for the same construction, time, velocity, and pressure. Their parts assemble the conclusions of Theorem 1.1 with initial data $u(0)$, together with uniqueness of the maximal velocity and its lifetime: every maximal solution $v$ on $[0,T')$ with $v(0)=u(0)$ has $T'=T$ and $v=u$ on $[0,T)$. This is a conjunction assembly: smoothness, blow-up, divergent integrals, and terminal limits are supplied by those inputs.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.witness_of_sect.summary: Assemble the singularity witness from Section Eight

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Rem12.maximal_uniqu.text: Assume hu and hv are maximal Euler solutions with identical initial velocities. Periodic Euler uniqueness gives agreement on their common interval. If either lifetime were shorter, the other solution would be a forbidden extension, so both lifetimes coincide and the velocities agree throughout the half-open interval. The theorem claims velocity uniqueness; it does not compare the pressure fields as a separate conclusion.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Rem12.maximal_uniqu.summary: Maximal solutions from the same data have equal lifetimes

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Rem12.smoothTermina.text: The off-origin extension hypothesis provides a periodic field smooth on $\mathbb R\times(\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3)$, all times away from the lattice, and agreeing with $u$ on $[0,T)\times(\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3)$. Choosing that whole punctured space–time domain as the open neighborhood of $\{T\}\times(\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3)$ yields the smooth terminal extension of Remark 1.2. This is the conversion used by the active Remark 1.2 proof. Smooth extension of a field does not assert continuation of the Euler solution beyond its maximal time.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Rem12.smoothTermina.summary: Convert the off-origin smooth extension for the active remark

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.abs_sub_le_of_h.text: On a nonnegative interval, a uniform absolute derivative bound gives variation from the initial value at most the bound times elapsed time. The statement uses within-interval derivatives, including the endpoints.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.coefficientBox.text:
Define the four-dimensional box used to compare finite-shear coefficients with the limit: bounded first and second coordinates, third coordinate between one half and three halves, and inverse shear squared between zero and one.

A negative radius can make the first two coordinate intervals empty. All compactness statements remain valid for that empty set; the application chooses a positive radius containing both the actual and reference coordinates. This set definition has no inverse or choice fallback.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.coefficientBox.summary: A compact region for coefficient comparison

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.continuousOn_sh.text: The rational coefficient map is continuous on the coefficient box because the third coordinate and the quadratic norm denominator stay strictly positive there. It does not assert continuity at singular inputs outside that box.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.continuousOn_sh.summary: Continuity of the reduced amplitude coefficients

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.cos_referenceAn.text: For any real $\varepsilon,\tau$, put $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon\tau^2/2)$. The formal identity is $\cos\varphi=(1+(\varepsilon\tau^2/2)^2)^{-1/2}$. The square root is positive because its argument is at least one; this formula therefore introduces no zero denominator. It identifies the cosine in (2.4) with the expression used in the reference estimates. No wave equation or sign condition on $\varepsilon$ is required. Restricting $\varepsilon\ge0$ additionally gives the paper’s angle range $0\le\varphi<\pi/2$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.cos_referenceAn.summary: The trigonometric cosine equals the explicit positive algebraic expression

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.driving_referen.text: For $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon\tau^2/2)$, the formal statement identifies $\cos^2\varphi(1-\varepsilon\tan\varphi)$ with $(1-\varepsilon^2\tau^2/2)/(1+(\varepsilon\tau^2/2)^2)$. This holds for every real $\varepsilon,\tau$, since the denominator is strictly positive. It is the coefficient driving the first amplitude equation in (2.5), and the constant term in the Riccati equation (2.12). The identity changes notation only; it neither supplies a solution of either equation nor proves the amplitude gain. The sign change occurs when $\varepsilon\tan\varphi=1$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.driving_referen.summary: The trigonometric driving term equals its rational expression in time

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.entry_smul.text: Scalar multiplication of a linear map scales every frame entry by the same scalar. The identity does not require the frame to be orthonormal.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.eta_div_rate.text:
At activation, let $\sigma=|k_p||\mathbf a_p|>0$, $
u=B_{12}>0$, $\eta=B_{32}>0$, and define $r=\sqrt{2\sigma
u}$, $S=\sigma/r$, $\varepsilon=\eta/
u$. The formal identity is $\eta/r=\varepsilon/(2S)$. Multiplying by $S$ gives $\eta S/r=\varepsilon/2$, one of the scalar conversions in the proof of Lemma 2.3. The quantities are frozen at $t_0$; the statement does not assert that the time-dependent coupling is constant. Positivity supplied by the amplification assumptions makes every displayed denominator nonzero.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.eta_div_rate.summary: The second coupling becomes the ratio divided by twice the shear scale

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.exists_coeffici.text: Compactness of the coefficient box turns continuity into a single input tolerance controlling all four output coefficients. The tolerance is fixed after epsilon and the box radius are fixed.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.exists_coeffici.summary: A uniform modulus for the amplitude coefficients

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.gronwallBound_e.text: Identify the general Gronwall expression for this linear system with the explicitly defined scalar factor. This is an algebraic conversion, not an additional stability theorem.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.gronwallBound_e.summary: Evaluating the wave vector Gronwall factor

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.modelEntries_ap.text: Compute all three coordinates of the model matrix applied to a vector. The only nonzero output coordinates are the first and third multiples of the second input coordinate.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.model_case_equa.text:
Assume the general frame rule $E_1'=-B_{12}E_2-B_{13}E_3$, $E_2'=B_{12}E_1-B_{32}E_3$, $E_3'=B_{13}E_1+B_{32}E_2$, $(\log\sigma_p)'=B_{33}$ for every nonzero transverse wave over trace-free $B$. Let $B,E_c$ be continuous on compact $I
i t_0$, with $\operatorname{tr}B=0$. On $I$, let $k_p,\mathbf a_p
e0$, $k_p\cdot\mathbf a_p=0$, $k_p'=-B^Tk_p$, $\mathbf a_p'=-B\mathbf a_p+2(k_p\cdot B\mathbf a_p)k_p/|k_p|^2$. Physical derivatives are relative to $I$. Put $E_1=k_p/|k_p|$, $E_2=\mathbf a_p/|\mathbf a_p|$, $E_3=E_1	imes E_2$, $B_{ij}=E_i\cdot BE_j$, $\sigma_p=|k_p||\mathbf a_p|$, $\sigma=\sigma_p(t_0)$, $
u=B_{12}(t_0)>0$, $\eta=B_{32}(t_0)>0$, $r=\sqrt{2\sigma
u}$, $S=\sigma/r$, $\varepsilon=\eta/
u$, $	au=r(t-t_0)$. Assume $[t_0,t_0+T/r]\subset I$, and $k'=-M^Tk$ on $I$, $k(t_0)=\lambda E_3(t_0)$, $\lambda>0$, where $M=B+\mathbf a_p\otimes k_p+E_c$. On $0\le	au\le T$, require $B_{12}=
u$, $B_{32}=\eta$, all other frame entries zero, and $E_c=0$. Define $\zeta=(k\cdot E_1,Sk\cdot E_2,k\cdot E_3)/\lambda$ and $\alpha=(S\mathbf a\cdot E_1,\mathbf a\cdot E_2,S\mathbf a\cdot E_3)$. Then $|k_p||\mathbf a_p|=\sigma$ and $\zeta'=(-(1+1/(2S^2))\zeta_2,-\varepsilon\zeta_3,\varepsilon\zeta_2/(2S^2))$. Every transverse amplitude solving $\mathbf a'=-M\mathbf a+2(k\cdot M\mathbf a)k/|k|^2$ satisfies $\alpha_1'=-\alpha_2+\zeta_1\Pi$, $\alpha_2'=-(1-1/(2S^2))\alpha_1+\varepsilon(\zeta_1\alpha_1+\zeta_2\alpha_2)/(2S^2\zeta_3)+\zeta_2\Pi/S^2$, where $\zeta_3
e0$ and $\Pi=[2\zeta_2\alpha_1+(\zeta_1+\varepsilon\zeta_3)\alpha_2]/[\zeta_1^2+\zeta_2^2/S^2+\zeta_3^2]$. No assumption $T\ge2$ is required. Physical derivatives are relative to $I$ and scaled derivatives to $[0,T]$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.model_case_equa.summary: The two-entry background gives constant strength and exact finite-shear equations

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.norm_le_abs_add.text: Bound the Euclidean norm of a three-vector by the sum of the absolute values of its three coordinates. This converts scalar error estimates into the norm used in the uniform limit.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.norm_le_abs_add.summary: Euclidean norm bounded by coordinate magnitudes

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.nu_div_rate.text:
Let the activation strength $\sigma$ and first coupling $
u$ be positive, and set $r=\sqrt{2\sigma
u}$ and $S=\sigma/r$. For the amplification data the formal statement proves $
u/r=1/(2S)$, equivalently $
u S/r=1/2$. This is the conversion used when the physical amplitude and wave-vector equations are written in normalized time in Lemma 2.3. It follows from $r^2=2\sigma
u$ and the nonzero denominators. It is an identity of the frozen activation values, with no claim that $B_{12}(t)$ remains constant.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.nu_div_rate.summary: The first coupling is the reciprocal of twice the shear scale

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.rate_sq.text:
For the preceding wave at activation, $\sigma=|k_p(t_0)||\mathbf a_p(t_0)|>0$ and $
u=E_1(t_0)\cdot B(t_0)E_2(t_0)>0$. The rate is defined by $r=\sqrt{2\sigma
u}$. The formal statement proves $r^2=2\sigma
u$, the scalar identity used to rescale the model equations of Lemma 2.3. Positivity is part of the supplied amplification data, so the square root is the positive one. This assertion concerns the normalization only and does not construct a new wave or assert its growth rate equals $r$ at finite shear.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.rate_sq.summary: Squaring the positive growth rate recovers twice the strength times the coupling

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.referenceSlope_.text: For any real $\varepsilon$ and function $Y$, the formal statement equates two conditions on $[0,\infty)$: $Y(0)=1$ and $Y'=\cos^2\varphi(1-\varepsilon\tan\varphi)-\varepsilon\tau\sin2\varphi\,Y-Y^2$, with $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon\tau^2/2)$, or the same equation after these trigonometric coefficients are written as rational functions of $\varepsilon\tau^2/2$. The time derivative at zero is the right derivative. The function, initial value and domain are unchanged; no existence or uniqueness assertion is included. This is the precise change of notation connecting (2.12) to the algebraic reference estimates.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.referenceSlope_.summary: The trigonometric and algebraic initial value problems are equivalent

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.referenceSystem.text: Put $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon\tau^2/2)$ and $\zeta_0=(\varepsilon\tau^2/2,-\varepsilon\tau,1)$. The formal identity evaluates the four finite-shear coefficient formulas at $(\zeta,S^{-2})=(\zeta_0,0)$ and obtains the entries $-\varepsilon\tau\sin2\varphi$, $-\cos^2\varphi(1-\varepsilon\tan\varphi)$, $-1$, $0$ of (2.5). It is an algebraic evaluation for arbitrary real parameters, not a convergence theorem. The evaluated denominator is $1+(\varepsilon\tau^2/2)^2>0$ and the third coordinate is one. Uniform convergence of actual coefficients additionally uses the model-wave estimates and continuity near these values.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.referenceSystem.summary: Evaluating the coefficient formulas at infinite shear gives the reference matrix

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.shearCoefficien.text:
Define the four rational entries of the finite-shear amplitude matrix as functions of the wave coordinates and inverse shear squared. The formula is separated from ODE solvability so that compact uniform continuity can prove coefficient convergence.

Division is total: a zero third coordinate or zero quadratic denominator gives Lean-defined values, not a valid reduced amplitude equation. Continuity and convergence are asserted only on a box with third coordinate at least one half and nonnegative inverse shear squared, which makes the denominators positive.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.shear_pos.text: The physical amplification parameters imply that the shear scale is strictly positive, allowing cancellation and division by that scale in the model equations.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.sin_referenceAn.text: Express the reference sine as the algebraic tangent parameter times its cosine factor. It translates trigonometric formulas into the rational quantities used in the scalar ODE library.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.sin_two_referen.text: Rewrite epsilon times time times sine of twice the reference angle as the library damping function. No positivity hypothesis is needed for this algebraic identity.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.smul_modelEntri.text: Scaling the model matrix scales its two nonzero entries. This identifies the physical and normalized model coefficients before the ODE calculation.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.strain_modelEnt.text: An orthonormal frame and the specified matrix entries determine the strain as the sum of the two model rank-one maps. Orthonormality is essential to reconstruct the operator from its entries.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.strongShearMatr.text: Identify the finite-shear reduced matrix with the four-entry rational coefficient map evaluated at the actual wave coordinates and inverse shear squared. The identity prepares the common continuity argument.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.strongShearMatr.summary: Finite shear coefficients in the common formula

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.strongShear_lim.text:
Assume the general frame rule $E_1'=-B_{12}E_2-B_{13}E_3$, $E_2'=B_{12}E_1-B_{32}E_3$, $E_3'=B_{13}E_1+B_{32}E_2$, $(\log\sigma_p)'=B_{33}$ for every nonzero transverse wave over trace-free $B$. Let $B,E_c$ be continuous on compact $I
i t_0$, with $\operatorname{tr}B=0$. On $I$, let $k_p,\mathbf a_p
e0$, $k_p\cdot\mathbf a_p=0$, $k_p'=-B^Tk_p$, $\mathbf a_p'=-B\mathbf a_p+2(k_p\cdot B\mathbf a_p)k_p/|k_p|^2$. Physical derivatives are relative to $I$. Put $E_1=k_p/|k_p|$, $E_2=\mathbf a_p/|\mathbf a_p|$, $E_3=E_1	imes E_2$, $B_{ij}=E_i\cdot BE_j$, $\sigma_p=|k_p||\mathbf a_p|$, $\sigma=\sigma_p(t_0)$, $
u=B_{12}(t_0)>0$, $\eta=B_{32}(t_0)>0$, $r=\sqrt{2\sigma
u}$, $S=\sigma/r$, $\varepsilon=\eta/
u$, $	au=r(t-t_0)$. Assume $T\ge2$, $[t_0,t_0+T/r]\subset I$, and $k'=-M^Tk$ on $I$, $k(t_0)=\lambda E_3(t_0)$, $\lambda>0$, where $M=B+\mathbf a_p\otimes k_p+E_c$. On $0\le	au\le T$, require $B_{12}=
u$, $B_{32}=\eta$, all other frame entries zero, and $E_c=0$. Define $\zeta=(k\cdot E_1,Sk\cdot E_2,k\cdot E_3)/\lambda$ and $\alpha=(S\mathbf a\cdot E_1,\mathbf a\cdot E_2,S\mathbf a\cdot E_3)$. For fixed $\varepsilon,T$, $\zeta	o(\varepsilon	au^2/2,-\varepsilon	au,1)$ uniformly as $S	o\infty$; all amplitude coefficients converge uniformly to $- igl( egin{smallmatrix}\varepsilon	au\sin2\varphi&\cos^2\varphi(1-\varepsilon	an\varphi)\1&0\end{smallmatrix} igr)$, $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon	au^2/2)$. One threshold precedes all configurations and times, and ensures $\zeta_3
e0$. For every tolerance $d>0$, one $S_0(\varepsilon,T,d)$ makes the Euclidean wave-vector error and each of the four coefficient errors at most $d$ whenever $S\ge S_0$. No polynomial bound for this threshold is stated.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.strongShear_lim.summary: A single shear threshold controls all model waves throughout the fixed interval

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.tan_referenceAn.text: Rewrite the tangent of the arctangent angle as epsilon times time squared divided by two. This is a notation bridge and carries no ODE or growth estimate.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.zetaBound.text:
Define the scalar Gronwall factor for the wave-vector error with epsilon and interval length fixed. Multiplication by the small parameter one over twice shear squared gives the coordinate error bound used in the strong-shear limit.

The formula is total for all real epsilon and T. At epsilon = -2 the inverse denominator is Lean zero, so it is not a meaningful Gronwall estimate there; the nonnegativity and error lemmas assume epsilon and T nonnegative. No ODE solution is selected by this definition.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.zetaBound_nonne.text: For nonnegative epsilon and interval length, the Gronwall factor is nonnegative. These sign hypotheses ensure both the denominator and the exponential increment have the required signs.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.zeta_bounds.text: Let $0\le\mu\le1$, $\varepsilon\ge0$, and let $z$ solve $z_1'=-(1+\mu)z_2$, $z_2'=-\varepsilon z_3$, $z_3'=\varepsilon\mu z_2$ on $[0,T]$, with $z(0)=(0,0,1)$. The formal statement bounds each coordinate of $z-(\varepsilon\tau^2/2,-\varepsilon\tau,1)$ in absolute value by $\mu K$, where $K=\varepsilon T(1+\varepsilon)(e^{(2+\varepsilon)T}-1)/(2+\varepsilon)$. Thus for $\mu=1/(2S^2)$ it gives uniform convergence in Lemma 2.3, with Euclidean error at most $3\mu K$. No assumption $T\ge2$ is needed. The estimate grows exponentially in $T$ and is used with $T$ fixed; it is not the polynomial comparison of Lemma 2.4.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.zeta_bounds.summary: Gronwall’s inequality bounds every coordinate error by the inverse squared shear

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.abs_apply_le_no.text: The absolute value of an individual coordinate of a three-vector is at most its Euclidean norm. This transfers a vector error bound to each denominator-sensitive coordinate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.abs_apply_le_no.summary: Each coordinate is bounded by the vector norm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.abs_div_le_self.text: Dividing a real quantity by a scale at least one does not increase its absolute value. This removes harmless inverse shear factors from residual estimates.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.abs_le_of_deriv.text: For a scalar function initially zero, a uniform derivative bound on the interval gives an absolute bound proportional to elapsed time. The result is used on the logarithm of the preceding strength ratio.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.abs_le_of_deriv.summary: A zero initial value and a bounded derivative

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.abs_threeProduc.text: If three coefficients have a common absolute bound, their products with three coordinates have sum bounded by that coefficient bound times the sum of coordinate magnitudes.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.absorb.text: Increase the universal finite-smallness threshold enough to make a specified polynomial in the horizon times delta at most one half. The constants and exponent must be fixed before choosing that threshold.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.actual_coupling.text: Turn a polynomial-in-time additive coupling error into the epsilon-scaled error required by the preceding comparison, using the finite-smallness hypothesis. The early sign of the reference slope remains an explicit input.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.actual_coupling.summary: Absorbing polynomial errors in the coupling bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.actual_coupling.text:
Let $0<\varepsilon\le1/16$, $T\ge2$, $x=\varepsilon	au^2/2$, $s=(1+x^2)^{-1/2}=\cos\varphi$ and $\varphi=\arctan x$. Suppose $Y=s(1+e)-\varepsilon	au x s^2/2$, with $0\le e\le\varepsilon/8$ on $[0,\infty)$. Also assume $Y>0$ on $[0,\sqrt2/\varepsilon]$. Define $n_0=(x+\varepsilon+2\varepsilon	au Y)s$ and $h_0=(-1+\varepsilon x+2(1+x^2)Y^2+2\varepsilon	au xY)s$. If scalar functions $n,h$ satisfy $|n-n_0|,|h-h_0|\le\varepsilon/(8T^2)$ on $[0,T]$, then $n\ge\varepsilon/2$ there. For $\sqrt2/\varepsilon\le	au\le T$, the formal statement gives $|n-1|\le\varepsilon$ and $|(h/n)/s-1|\le1/2$. In the application, $n=
u_+/
u$ and $h=\eta_+/
u$. This result assumes the additive comparison; it neither constructs a wave nor requires a differential equation for $Y$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.actual_coupling.summary: Reference comparison gives positivity and late-time ratios

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.alpha_one.text: The paper's second scaled amplitude coordinate agrees with the library coordinate V. No sign change or additional scale is needed.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.alpha_system_of.text: For the preceding wave frame $E_1,E_2,E_3$, put $r=\sqrt{2\sigma\nu}>0$, $S=\sigma/r>0$, $\varepsilon=\eta/\nu$, $t=t_0+\tau/r$, $\alpha_1(\tau)=S E_1(t)\cdot\mathbf a(t)$ and $\alpha_2(\tau)=E_2(t)\cdot\mathbf a(t)$. At a time in any prescribed set $J$, let $U=-\alpha_1$, $V=\alpha_2$, $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon\tau^2/2)$, $d=\varepsilon\tau\sin2\varphi$ and $g=\cos^2\varphi(1-\varepsilon\tan\varphi)$. Suppose $(U,V)'=(-dU+gV,U)+R(U,V)$ there. With $P=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1)$, the formal statement gives $(\alpha_1,\alpha_2)'=(-d\alpha_1-g\alpha_2,-\alpha_1)+PRP(\alpha_1,\alpha_2)$. Derivatives are relative to $J$. This is the exact change to the paper’s sign convention; it estimates neither $R$ nor the solution. The physical amplification data supply the frame and positive scales, but the calculation uses only the two displayed derivative hypotheses.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.alpha_system_of.summary: Conjugation returns the internal equations to the paper notation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.alpha_zero.text: The paper's first scaled amplitude coordinate is the negative of the library coordinate U. This sign change is why the error matrix is conjugated by a diagonal reflection.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.alpha_zero.summary: The sign convention for the first amplitude coordinate

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.amplificationPh.text: Restricting to a nonempty compact subinterval cannot increase the physical error bound, under the continuity hypotheses needed for the suprema.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.amplificationPh.summary: Physical error decreases on a smaller interval

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.amplitude_late_.text: Let $0<\varepsilon\le1$, $\tau_m\in[2/\varepsilon,3/\varepsilon]$ and $\tau_m\le\tau\le T$. Put $x(t)=\varepsilon t^2/2$, $s(t)=(1+x(t)^2)^{-1/2}$. Suppose $Y$ is continuous on $[0,\infty)$ and $Y=s(1+e)-\varepsilon t x s^2/2$, with $0\le e\le\varepsilon/8$ there. Define $a_{\rm ref}(t)=\exp\int_0^tY$. Assume also $a_{\rm ref}(\tau)/a_{\rm ref}(\tau_m)=\sqrt{s(\tau)/s(\tau_m)}\exp\int_{\tau_m}^{\tau}s(1+e)$. Assume $a_{\rm ref}(t)\le a_{\rm ref}(\tau_m)$ and $ca_{\rm ref}(t)\le A(t)\le Ca_{\rm ref}(t)$ for $0\le t\le T$, where $c,C>0$, and assume an attained maximum $M=\max_{[0,T]}A$. If $k_{\min},k_{\max}\ge0$ and $k_{\min}x(\tau)\le k\le k_{\max}x(\tau)$, then $k_{\min}(c/C)\sqrt{x(\tau)/\varepsilon}\le kA(\tau)/M\le3\exp(2)k_{\max}(C/c)\sqrt{x(\tau)/\varepsilon}$. Here $k$ is a scalar, representing $|k(\tau)|/\lambda$ in the application. The maximum and amplitude comparisons are hypotheses.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.amplitude_late_.summary: Comparison constants give an explicit late-time strength estimate

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.basis_continuou.text: Extract continuity of the preceding frame from the wave and amplitude hypotheses. The proof needs only their regularity and nonvanishing, so no invocation of Lemma 2.2 is hidden here.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.basis_orthonorm.text: Normalize the nonzero perpendicular preceding wave and amplitude vectors and complete them by the cross product to obtain an orthonormal basis.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.basis_orthonorm.summary: Orthonormality of the preceding wave frame

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.clock_continuou.text: The affine map from normalized time to physical time is continuous. Its range lies in the required time window only under the separate interval hypothesis.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.clock_mem_slab.text: A normalized time in the allowed interval maps into the physical slab between activation and the terminal clock value. Positive rate gives the order preservation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.clock_mem_slab.summary: The normalized clock stays in its physical slab

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.conjError.text:
Define the error matrix by conjugating the library error through the first-coordinate reflection. This changes coordinate convention and does not introduce a new error source.

This is ordinary composition with a fixed reflection for every time and operator, including a zero error operator. No inverse or off-domain default is introduced; continuity and size estimates remain separate hypotheses or conclusions.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.conjError.summary: The error matrix in the paper coordinates

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.continuousOn_co.text: Compose a continuous physical-time function with the normalized clock, assuming the clock maps the normalized interval into its domain.
A continuous error-operator curve remains continuous after composition with the fixed reflection on either side.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.continuousOn_co.summary: Continuity of the conjugated error matrix

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.continuousOn_cr.text: Two continuous three-vector fields have a continuous cross product. This supplies continuity of the third moving-frame vector.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.continuousOn_de.text: A continuous reference slope gives a continuous deviation after the algebraic change of variables, because the reference cosine factor never vanishes. No deviation ODE is assumed here.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.continuousOn_de.summary: Continuous deviation from a continuous reference slope

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.continuousOn_de.text: Recover the deviation as a quotient of the continuous slope plus damping by the positive cosine factor. Thus the deviation envelope is continuous on nonnegative times without appealing to an additional existence theorem.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.continuousOn_de.summary: Continuity of the bounded reference deviation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.continuousOn_fr.text: For continuous nonzero wave and amplitude vectors, all three normalized-frame vectors are continuous on the interval. This is a continuity fact; perpendicularity and orthonormality are handled separately.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.continuousOn_fr.summary: Continuity of the moving orthonormal frame

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.continuousOn_no.text: A continuous vector field that never vanishes on a set has a continuous normalized direction there. The nonvanishing assumption is necessary because normalization is totalized at zero in Lean.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.continuousOn_ph.text: Let $I$ be the compact physical observation set for a continuous gradient $M=B+\mathbf a_p\otimes k_p+E_c$, and assume $t_0+\tau/r\in I$ for $0\le\tau\le T$. If $k$ and $\mathbf a$ are continuous on $I$ and nonzero at those physical times, then $\widehat k\cdot M\widehat a$ and $(\widehat k\times\widehat a)\cdot M\widehat a$ are continuous functions of $\tau\in[0,T]$. These are the two couplings used in Proposition 2.8. This result proves continuity of each coupling, not of their quotient; continuity of $\eta_+/\nu_+$ additionally uses the positive lower bound for $\nu_+$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.continuousOn_ph.summary: Nonvanishing wave data make both frame entries continuous

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.continuous_damp.text: The quarter-damping term in the reference-slope representation is continuous. This supplies a continuous envelope when reconstructing the deviation from the paper's formula.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.coordinates_clo.text: Convert the vector comparison with the reference wave into three scalar error bounds for the moving-frame coordinates.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.coordinates_clo.summary: Coordinate errors from wave vector comparison

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.cos_referenceAn.text: Translate the paper's reference-angle cosine into the algebraic factor used in the scalar ODE library. The identity is unrestricted in epsilon and time.
Rewrite the squared reference cosine as the reciprocal of one plus the squared tangent parameter. This identifies the denominator in the relative wave-length estimate.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.coupling_budget.text: Choose a common polynomial error budget that dominates the wave-coordinate and slope errors and is at most one half. This puts the rational coupling comparison in a single admissible parameter range.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.coupling_budget.summary: One small error for all coupling estimates

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.coupling_conclu.text: Absorb the concrete error 256 times the eighth power of the horizon times the common budget, plus twice delta, and apply the coupling comparison. This packages the final numerical step of Lemma 2.7 without recreating any numbered input.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.coupling_conclu.summary: Coupling conclusions from a common error budget

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.crossing_streng.text: Assume $0<\varepsilon\le1/2$, $0<\varepsilon_+\le\varepsilon/32$, $H=2/\sqrt{\varepsilon\varepsilon_+}\le T$, and $\lambda>0$. Let $Y$ have the representation (2.13), $0\le e\le\varepsilon/8$, the amplitude formula (2.14), $Y\le1$, and a reference maximum at $\tau_m\in[2/\varepsilon,3/\varepsilon]$ with logarithmic gain at least $\varepsilon^{-1/2}-1$. Suppose continuous nonzero $\mathbf a$ satisfies $|\log(|\mathbf a|/a_{\rm ref})|\le\varepsilon$, and $||k|^2\cos^2\varphi/\lambda^2-1|\le1/2$ for $\tau\ge2/\varepsilon$. If continuous $\rho$ lies between $\cos\varphi/2$ and $3\cos\varphi/2$ for $\tau\ge\sqrt2/\varepsilon$, then a crossing lies in $(\tau_m,H)$. For $M=\max_{[0,T]}|\mathbf a|$, every crossing in $[\tau_m,H]$ has $\exp(-1)/(4\sqrt{\varepsilon\varepsilon_+})\le|\mathbf a||k|/(\lambda M)\le18\exp(3)/\sqrt{\varepsilon\varepsilon_+}$, and $|\mathbf a|\le \exp(3-\varepsilon^{-1/2})M$ on $[0,1]$. The wave equations are replaced here by these explicit comparison assumptions.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.crossing_streng.summary: A comparison argument supplies crossings, strength and early suppression

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.damping_eq.text: Identify epsilon times time times sine of twice the angle with the library damping coefficient. This allows the same derivative equation to be read in both notations.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.deviation_eq_of.text: Given the paper's ansatz for the reference slope, solve algebraically for the library deviation. Strict positivity of the cosine factor justifies the division.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.deviation_eq_of.summary: Recovering the deviation from the slope formula

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.driving_eq.text: Identify the cosine-squared driving term of the paper's scalar equation with the algebraic coefficient used by the Riccati library.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.elapsed_mem_Icc.text: A physical time in the active slab has elapsed normalized time in the prescribed interval. This is the inverse interval calculation used to restrict arbitrary propagated amplitudes.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.elapsed_mem_Icc.summary: The physical slab maps to normalized time

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.errorSize_restr.text: The error size of the active-slab restriction is bounded by the original error size. The scalar inverse-shear contribution is unchanged and the physical supremum can only decrease.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.errorSize_restr.summary: The restricted amplification error is no larger

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.finiteSmallness.text: Transfer the finite-smallness hypothesis to the active slab using the preceding error monotonicity.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.flipCLM.text:
Define the bounded linear map sending a two-coordinate state to the negative of its first coordinate and the unchanged second coordinate. It reconciles the U,V convention with the paper's alpha coordinates.

This is a globally defined bounded linear reflection on a two-dimensional real space. It involves no division, choice of representative, interval restriction, or exceptional default.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.flipCLM.summary: Reflection of the first amplitude coordinate

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.flipCLM_apply.text: Compute the reflection map as the pair consisting of minus the first coordinate and the second coordinate.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.geometry_of_clo.text: Coordinate closeness to the reference vector gives bounds on the first two scaled coordinates used in amplitude estimates. The hypotheses include the interval and epsilon bounds needed to absorb the reference polynomial terms.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.geometry_of_clo.summary: Geometry from nearby scaled wave coordinates

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.gradient_contin.text: Combine the older gradient, preceding shear, and correction to obtain continuity of the full gradient on the physical time window. This is used for amplitude ODE solvability.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.gradient_contin.summary: Continuity of the full background gradient

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.growingFactor_r.text: A uniform logarithmic amplitude comparison, positivity, and twice epsilon at most one bound the reference-amplitude ratio by exp one times the actual amplitude ratio. This closes the physical propagator estimate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.growingFactor_r.summary: Replacing the reference ratio by the actual amplitude ratio

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.hasDerivWithinA.text: Apply the first coordinate projection to a within-interval derivative of a two-coordinate curve. This is ordinary bounded-linear-map differentiation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.hasDerivWithinA.summary: The derivative of the first state coordinate

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.hasDerivWithinA.text: Apply the second coordinate projection to a within-interval derivative of a two-coordinate curve.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.hasDerivWithinA.summary: The derivative of the second state coordinate

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.mapsTo_restrict.text: The normalized clock lands in the active slab by construction. This supplies the domain hypothesis for the copied amplification data.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.mapsTo_restrict.summary: The clock maps into the restricted interval

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.nbasis.text:
Abbreviate the preceding moving frame composed with the normalized clock. The expression is defined at every time, while orthonormality and ODE conclusions are asserted only on the admissible interval.

The original frame is evaluated at every real clock value, including outside its hypothesis window. Its constituent normalizations use total real inverses, so a zero vector has a formal value; orthonormality is used only where the amplification data give nonzero perpendicular vectors.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.ne_zero_of_zeta.text: If the third scaled wave coordinate is nonzero, then the underlying wave vector is nonzero. This supports later normalization of the new wave direction.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.ne_zero_of_zeta.summary: A nonzero third coordinate excludes a zero wave

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.newWaveVector_r.text: Restrict the new wave-vector data and its initial condition to the active slab. No new wave-vector solution is constructed.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.normFactor_cos_.text: Let $T\ge2$, $S^{-2}\le2\delta$, $0\le x\le T^2/4$, $|X-x|\le e_0\le1/2$, $|Q|\le T$, and $|Z-1|\le e_0$. Then $|(X^2+Q^2/S^2+Z^2)/(1+x^2)-1|\le2T^2e_0+2T^2\delta$. For the wave, $(X,Q,Z)=\zeta$, $x=\tan\varphi$ and $|k|^2=\lambda^2(X^2+Q^2/S^2+Z^2)$, so this is the estimate for $|k|^2\cos^2\varphi/\lambda^2$ used in Lemma 2.4. It is an algebraic implication of the coordinate bounds and proves no wave evolution. The displayed real-number formula also has a defined value at $S=0$; its physical application has $S>0$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.normFactor_cos_.summary: Coordinate errors control the cosine-weighted squared norm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.norm_bounds_of_.text: At a fixed time, let $(E_1,E_2,E_3)$ be orthonormal and $k\cdot\mathbf a=0$. Write $k=\lambda(\zeta_1E_1+\zeta_2E_2/S+\zeta_3E_3)$ and $\mathbf a=\alpha_1E_1/S+\alpha_2E_2+\alpha_3E_3/S$, with $\lambda\ne0$, $S>0$. Put $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon t^2/2)$, $a_{\rm ref}(t)=\exp\int_0^tY$, $h=\alpha_2/a_{\rm ref}$ and $l=-(\alpha_1+Y\alpha_2)/(a_{\rm ref}\cos\varphi)$. Assume $T\ge1$, $|\zeta_1|\le T^2$, $|\zeta_2|\le T$, $\zeta_3\ge1/2$, $|Y(t)|\le1$, and $\max\{|h-1|,|l|\}\le d\le1/2$. The formal statement gives $\alpha_2\le|\mathbf a|\le(1+40T^4S^{-2})\alpha_2$. This pointwise estimate assumes normalized closeness; it does not derive that closeness from the wave equations. For arbitrary $Y$, the formal integral is assigned zero if it is not integrable, so $a_{\rm ref}$ remains positive.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.norm_bounds_of_.summary: Closeness to the growing state controls the physical norm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.norm_conjError_.text: The norm of the conjugated error is at most the original error norm, using the norm-one bounds for the reflection on both sides.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.norm_flipCLM_le.text: Bound the operator norm of the diagonal reflection by one. The inequality is enough to transfer the error-operator estimate through conjugation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.norm_flipCLM_le.summary: The amplitude reflection does not increase norm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.norm_movingAmpl.text: Put $x=\varepsilon t^2/2$, $s=(1+x^2)^{-1/2}=\cos\varphi$, $\varphi=\arctan x$, and $a_{\rm ref}(t)=\exp\int_0^tY$. Suppose $Y'=s^2(1-\varepsilon x)-2\varepsilon t x s^2Y-Y^2$ on $[0,T]$. Suppose $(U,V)'=(-2\varepsilon t x s^2U+s^2(1-\varepsilon x)V,U)+R(U,V)$. Set $e=(Y+\varepsilon t x s^2/2)/s-1$, $h=V/a_{\rm ref}$ and $l=(U-YV)/(sa_{\rm ref})$. Require $e\ge0$ on $[0,T]$, and continuous $R,\eta$ on $[a,T]$ with $\|R\|\le\eta$, for $0\le a\le t\le T$. On $[a,t]$, let an orthonormal frame give $k=\lambda(\zeta_1E_1+\zeta_2E_2/S+\zeta_3E_3)$, $U=-S\mathbf b\cdot E_1$, $V=\mathbf b\cdot E_2$, $k\cdot\mathbf b=0$, $\lambda\ne0$, $S\ge1$. Assume $|\zeta_1|,|\zeta_2|\le S$, $1/2\le\zeta_3\le3/2$, $|Y|\le1$, $|\zeta_1-x|\le1/2$. Then $|\mathbf b(t)|\le126S\exp(2D)a_{\rm ref}(t)|\mathbf b(a)|/a_{\rm ref}(a)$, where $D=\int_a^t(1+|Y|)^2\eta/s$. Pair operator norms use the maximum norm; physical vector norms are Euclidean. Time derivatives are relative to $[0,T]$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.norm_movingAmpl.summary: The normalized error integral controls arbitrary transverse amplitudes

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.norm_zeta_le.text: Let $T\ge2$. In the preceding wave’s orthonormal frame, write the new wave vector at physical time $t_0+\tau/r$ as $k=\lambda(\zeta_1E_1+\zeta_2E_2/S+\zeta_3E_3)$. If $|\zeta_1|\le T^2$, $|\zeta_2|\le T$, and $1/2\le\zeta_3\le3/2$, then the Euclidean norm of the scaled vector satisfies $|\zeta|\le3T^2$. The formal statement uses the scaled coordinates defined by the displayed pairings, even for arbitrary real $\lambda$; the physical wave assumes $\lambda>0$. This result only combines the three coordinate hypotheses and does not derive them from the wave equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.norm_zeta_le.summary: Three coordinate bounds give a Euclidean norm bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.norm_zeta_sub_l.text: Bound the norm of the wave-vector difference by the sum of its three scalar coordinate errors. This converts the quantitative nilpotent estimate to the statement of Lemma 2.4.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.norm_zeta_sub_l.summary: A vector error from scalar coordinate errors

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.normalizedCoupl.text: Under the moving-frame and nonvanishing assumptions, identify the algebraic normalized first and second couplings with the physical couplings divided by the preceding first coupling.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.normalizedCoupl.summary: Converting normalized couplings to physical rates

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.normalizedState.text: Put $x=\varepsilon t^2/2$, $s=(1+x^2)^{-1/2}=\cos\varphi$, $\varphi=\arctan x$, and $a_{\rm ref}(t)=\exp\int_0^tY$. Suppose $Y'=s^2(1-\varepsilon x)-2\varepsilon t x s^2Y-Y^2$ on $[0,T]$. Suppose $(U,V)'=(-2\varepsilon t x s^2U+s^2(1-\varepsilon x)V,U)+R(U,V)$. Set $e=(Y+\varepsilon t x s^2/2)/s-1$, $h=V/a_{\rm ref}$ and $l=(U-YV)/(sa_{\rm ref})$. Assume $e\ge0$ on $[0,T]$. For $0\le a\le t\le T$, suppose $R,\eta$ are continuous on $[a,T]$ and $\|R\|\le\eta$ there, using the maximum norm on pairs and its operator norm. With $D=\int_a^t(1+|Y|)^2\eta/s$, the formal statement gives $\|(h,l)(t)\|_\infty\le2\exp(2D)\|(h,l)(a)\|_\infty$. All equations use derivatives within $[0,T]$, including endpoints. The paper’s bound $4$ requires an additional estimate on $D$; this statement supplies the conditional exponential bound.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.normalizedState.summary: An integral error bound controls the normalized solution

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.normalizedStrai.text: Identify the normalized strain, including preceding shear and correction, with the full physical gradient divided by the amplification rate.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.normalized_clos.text: Put $x=\varepsilon t^2/2$, $s=(1+x^2)^{-1/2}=\cos\varphi$, $\varphi=\arctan x$, and $a_{\rm ref}(t)=\exp\int_0^tY$. Suppose $Y'=s^2(1-\varepsilon x)-2\varepsilon t x s^2Y-Y^2$ on $[0,T]$. Suppose $(U,V)'=(-2\varepsilon t x s^2U+s^2(1-\varepsilon x)V,U)+R(U,V)$. Set $e=(Y+\varepsilon t x s^2/2)/s-1$, $h=V/a_{\rm ref}$ and $l=(U-YV)/(sa_{\rm ref})$. Assume $Y(0)=U(0)=V(0)=1$, $e\ge0$, and continuous $R,\eta$ with $\|R\|\le\eta$ on $[0,T]$, using the maximum norm on pairs. Then, for $0\le t\le T$ and $D(t)=\int_0^t(1+|Y|)^2\eta/s$, the formal statement gives $\max\{|h(t)-1|,|l(t)|\}\le4\exp(2D(t))D(t)$. Derivatives are relative to $[0,T]$. The sign convention is $U=-\alpha_1$, $V=\alpha_2$, so these initial values correspond to the paper’s $(-1,1)$. No small upper bound for $D$ is part of this statement.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.normalized_clos.summary: The normalized solution stays near its initial constant state

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.normalized_fact.text:
Let $B,E_c$ be continuous on compact $I
i t_0$, with $\operatorname{tr}B=0$. On $I$, let $k_p,\mathbf a_p
e0$, $k_p\cdot\mathbf a_p=0$, $k_p'=-B^Tk_p$, $\mathbf a_p'=-B\mathbf a_p+2(k_p\cdot B\mathbf a_p)k_p/|k_p|^2$. Physical derivatives are relative to $I$. Put $E_1=k_p/|k_p|$, $E_2=\mathbf a_p/|\mathbf a_p|$, $E_3=E_1	imes E_2$, $B_{ij}=E_i\cdot BE_j$, $\sigma_p=|k_p||\mathbf a_p|$, $\sigma=\sigma_p(t_0)$, $
u=B_{12}(t_0)>0$, $\eta=B_{32}(t_0)>0$, $r=\sqrt{2\sigma
u}$, $S=\sigma/r$, $\varepsilon=\eta/
u$, $	au=r(t-t_0)$. Define $\delta=\sup_I|B_{12}/
u-1|+\sup_I|B_{32}/\eta-1|+\sup_I\|B\|/r+\sup_I\|E_c\|/
u$. If $T\ge2$, integer $C_0\ge240$, $C_0\varepsilon\le1$ and $C_0T^{C_0}\delta\le\varepsilon$, then $0<\varepsilon\le1/2$, $\delta\ge0$, $S\ge T^2$, $S^{-1},S^{-2}\le2\delta$, $240\delta T^6\le1$ and $T\delta\le1$. For every time in $I$, it also gives $\|B/r\|\le\delta$, $\|E_c/r\|\le\delta/S$, $|B_{12}/
u-1|\le\delta$, $|B_{32}/
u-\varepsilon|\le\delta$. Matrix norms are Euclidean operator norms. No new wave is part of this statement.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.normalized_fact.summary: The physical smallness assumptions supply the normalized inequalities

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.nstrain.text:
Abbreviate the older gradient divided by rate, the normalized preceding rank-one shear, and the correction divided by rate. Equality with the full rescaled gradient is proved separately.

Scalar division by the amplification rate is formally total, but physical amplification data make that rate strictly positive. The expression exists outside the active time interval without asserting the wave or frame equations there.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.nstrain.summary: The normalized strain including the preceding shear

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.ratio_error_bou.text: Control the error of a quotient after the denominator is bounded away from zero. The explicit numerical bound is used to transfer separate first and second coupling errors to their ratio.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.ratio_error_bou.summary: Converting additive errors to a relative ratio

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.raw_matrix_comp.text: Package the raw matrix comparison hypotheses from a continuous nonnegative deviation and the common amplitude error. This exposes the needed part of Lemma 2.5 at the proof boundary.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.raw_matrix_comp.summary: The normalized matrix comparison with explicit deviation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.raw_system_of_a.text: Translate the paper's alpha system into the library U,V system, conjugating the error matrix by the first-coordinate reflection. The scalar angle identities identify the reference coefficients exactly.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.raw_system_of_a.summary: The perturbed amplitude system after changing signs

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.referenceNu_low.text: Let $0<\varepsilon\le1$, $\tau\ge0$, $x=\varepsilon\tau^2/2$, and $s=(1+x^2)^{-1/2}=\cos\varphi$. If $Y(\tau)>0$, then the reference expression $n_0=(x+\varepsilon+2\varepsilon\tau Y)s$ satisfies $n_0\ge\varepsilon$. In the paper $n_0$ represents $\nu_+/\nu$ at the reference values. The formal statement needs only positivity at the time in question; it does not assume that $Y$ solves the Riccati equation or that this time lies before $\sqrt2/\varepsilon$. The reference solution supplies positivity in that early range.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.referenceNu_low.summary: Positive logarithmic growth gives the required coupling lower bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.referenceSlope_.text: Translate the reference-slope predicate into the initial condition and the library Riccati derivative equation. The equivalence imports no separate existence or uniqueness conclusion.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.referenceSystem.text: For $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon\tau^2/2)$, the formal statement identifies the four entries of the paper’s reference matrix as $-\varepsilon\tau\sin(2\varphi)$, $-\cos^2\varphi(1-\varepsilon\tan\varphi)$, $-1$, and $0$. Thus it acts on $(\alpha_1,\alpha_2)$ exactly as in (2.5). The calculation holds for arbitrary real $\varepsilon,\tau$ and asserts no existence or growth of a solution. It provides the sign conversion from the other coefficient matrix, which acts on $(-\alpha_1,\alpha_2)$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.referenceSystem.summary: The matrix entries agree with the paper equations

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.referenceV_late.text: From the supplied amplitude ratio and bounded nonnegative deviation, bound the late-time reference-amplitude ratio by absolute multiples of the peak time divided by the current time. The remaining exponential integral is bounded independently of the terminal horizon.

Combine the reference-amplitude ratio with the late quadratic wave-vector scale to obtain two-sided linear-in-time strength bounds. This remains a statement about the reference profile until physical comparison is supplied.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.referenceV_late.summary: Reference strength on the late time interval

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.referenceV_rati.text: Let $\varphi(\tau)=\arctan(\varepsilon\tau^2/2)$ and $a_{\rm ref}(\tau)=\exp\int_0^\tau Y$. Assume, for every $\tau\ge0$, $a_{\rm ref}(\tau)=\sqrt{\cos\varphi(\tau)}\exp\int_0^\tau(1+e)\cos\varphi$, and assume the integrand $(1+e)\cos\varphi$ is continuous on $[0,\infty)$. For $0\le\tau_m\le\tau$, the formal statement gives $a_{\rm ref}(\tau)/a_{\rm ref}(\tau_m)=\sqrt{\cos\varphi(\tau)/\cos\varphi(\tau_m)}\exp\int_{\tau_m}^\tau(1+e)\cos\varphi$. No peak property of $\tau_m$ is required. This version uses the amplitude formula as a hypothesis rather than deriving it from the Riccati equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.referenceV_rati.summary: The amplitude formula gives a ratio on any forward interval

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.rescale_amplitu.text: Apply the time chain rule to the amplitude equation under the normalized clock, including the rescaled pressure coefficient.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.rescale_waveVec.text: Compose the physical wave vector with the affine normalized clock and divide its derivative by the positive amplification rate to obtain the normalized wave equation.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.residualQ.text:
Define the residual in the shear-scaled second wave coordinate after subtracting the limiting coupling to the third coordinate.

The expression is total for arbitrary input coordinates and coefficients. Any divisions inherited from normalized data use Lean total inverses; the ODE interpretation and estimates are made only for positive admissible shear and rate.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.residualX.text:
Define the first coordinate of the perturbation to the limiting nilpotent wave-vector system, including frame entries, varying strength, and the physical correction.

The polynomial/rational expression is defined at all real inputs, with divisions by the shear totalized at zero. Its interpretation as a residual and the estimates require shear at least one and the stated frame/coefficient assumptions.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.residualZ.text:
Define the residual third wave-coordinate derivative, whose reference value is zero.

The explicit division by shear has a formal value even at shear zero. The residual estimate assumes shear at least one, so that value is never used in the comparison argument.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.residual_bounds.text: Under normalized coefficient bounds and a scale at least one, each residual is at most five times horizon times delta times the sum of the wave-coordinate magnitudes. The estimates keep every perturbation in the nilpotent comparison budget.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.residual_bounds.summary: Bounds for the three wave equation residuals

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.restrictSlab.text:
Build physical amplification data on the smaller interval between activation and the terminal clock value, retaining the same parameters and functions while restricting their hypotheses.

The declaration takes a nonnegative normalized horizon and a mapping hypothesis for the original window; those supply the restricted structure fields. It keeps all original functions unchanged, including their values outside the new slab, but restricts all analytic assertions to the slab.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.restrictSlab.summary: Restricting amplification data to the active slab
