TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.riccati_perturb.text: Assuming a nonnegative deviation, continuity, and a bound on the raw error matrix, control the coefficients of the normalized triangular perturbation. The nonnegative deviation is an explicit hypothesis from Lemma 2.5.

Bound propagation of the normalized state from an arbitrary earlier time by an exponential of the integrated perturbation budget. The nonnegative deviation supplies stability of the unperturbed triangular part.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.riccati_perturb.summary: A perturbed triangular propagator between two times

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.s_ratio_bounds.text: In the late range, compare the ratio of cosine factors with the squared ratio of the two times. The scalar estimates convert the amplitude formula into explicit late decay bounds.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.seven_sq_le_eps.text: Under the stated smallness of epsilon, seven times epsilon squared is at most epsilon. This numerical absorption is used only in the late coupling estimates.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.sin_referenceAn.text: Rewrite the sine of the reference angle as its tangent parameter times its cosine factor. This is a direct algebraic bridge between the two notations.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.slab_subset.text: If the normalized clock maps the interval into the original physical window, then the whole active physical slab is a subset of that window.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.slab_subset.summary: The active slab lies in the original window

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.sqrt_clock_boun.text: Let $\varepsilon,\varepsilon_+>0$ and suppose $1/(4\varepsilon_+)\le x\le3/(2\varepsilon_+)$, where $x=\varepsilon\tau^2/2$. The formal statement gives $1/(2\sqrt{\varepsilon\varepsilon_+})\le\sqrt{x/\varepsilon}\le2/\sqrt{\varepsilon\varepsilon_+}$. These are the explicit comparisons used to turn the late-time strength bound into (2.23). The hypothesis is only a bound on $x$; no coupling ratio or crossing equation is assumed in this algebraic result. The crossing argument supplies the two inequalities separately.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.sqrt_clock_boun.summary: The crossing inequalities fix the strength scale

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.strengthRatio_b.text: On $[0,T]$, let $k_p,\mathbf a_p$ be nonzero perpendicular vectors with orthonormal frame $(E_1,E_2,E_3)$. Assume $(\log\sigma_p)'=B_{33}$ for $\sigma_p=|k_p||\mathbf a_p|$, assume $\|B\|\le\delta$, and let $T\delta\le1$. Then $|\sigma_p(t)/\sigma_p(0)-1|\le2T\delta$ for every $t\in[0,T]$. The matrix norm is the Euclidean operator norm; derivatives at interval endpoints are one-sided. The time here has already been normalized. This estimate takes the logarithmic derivative identity as an assumption, rather than deriving it again from the preceding wave equations.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.strengthRatio_b.summary: A logarithmic derivative bound controls the relative shear strength

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.strengthRatio_c.text: The strength ratio in normalized time is the physical preceding strength evaluated at the clock divided by its initial strength.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.strengthRatio_c.summary: The preceding strength ratio along the clock

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.tan_referenceAn.text: Identify the tangent parameter of the reference angle with epsilon times time squared divided by two. Later geometric estimates supply the positivity hypotheses.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.waveVector_poly.text: On $[0,T]$, let $T\ge2$, $0\le\varepsilon\le1$, $\delta\ge0$, $\lambda\ne0$, $S\ge1$, and $240\delta T^6\le1$. Let $k_p,\mathbf a_p$ be nonzero perpendicular paths, $E_1=\widehat k_p$, $E_2=\widehat a_p$, $E_3=E_1\times E_2$ orthonormal, $B_{ij}=E_i\cdot BE_j$, and $\sigma_p=|k_p||\mathbf a_p|$. Assume $E_1'=-B_{12}E_2-B_{13}E_3$, $E_2'=B_{12}E_1-B_{32}E_3$, $E_3'=B_{13}E_1+B_{32}E_2$, and $(\log\sigma_p)'=B_{33}$. Suppose $k'=-M^Tk$, $k(0)=\lambda E_3(0)$, with $M=B+S(\sigma_p/\sigma_p(0))E_2\otimes E_1+E$. If $\|B\|\le\delta$, $\|E\|\le\delta/S$ and $|2SB_{32}-\varepsilon|\le\delta$, then $|\zeta_1-\varepsilon\tau^2/2|+|\zeta_2+\varepsilon\tau|+|\zeta_3-1|\le120\delta T^6\le1/2$ throughout $[0,T]$, where $\zeta=(k\cdot E_1,Sk\cdot E_2,k\cdot E_3)/\lambda$. Derivatives are relative to the interval and matrix norms are Euclidean operator norms. The frame identities are explicit assumptions; the preceding-wave ODEs themselves are not required. Here hats denote division by Euclidean length.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.waveVector_poly.summary: The frame equations give an explicit sixth-power bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.wave_norm_compa.text: Let $0<\varepsilon\le1$, $\tau\ge2/\varepsilon$, $\lambda>0$, and $K\ge0$. Put $x=\varepsilon\tau^2/2$ and $\cos\varphi=(1+x^2)^{-1/2}$. If $|K^2\cos^2\varphi/\lambda^2-1|\le1/2$, then $x/2\le K/\lambda\le3x$. Applied with $K=|k(\tau)|$, this gives the paper’s late-time wave-number comparison in a form suited to the crossing estimate. It uses only the displayed scalar inequality and the late-time range; the wave equation and the source of the norm estimate are not hypotheses of this algebraic step.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.wave_norm_compa.summary: A squared-norm comparison yields explicit linear bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.zetaRef_apply.text: Evaluate the three coordinates of the reference wave vector in terms of the algebraic tangent parameter, epsilon times time, and one.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.zeta_one.text: Identify the second coordinate of the scaled wave vector with the library coordinate containing the shear factor.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.zeta_two.text: Identify the third coordinate of the scaled wave vector with the corresponding moving-frame coordinate divided by the initial wave length.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.zeta_zero.text: Identify the first coordinate of the scaled wave vector with the normalized moving-frame coordinate used by the library.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.A1Body.text:
Package the quantified conclusion of Theorem A.1 with its universal constant and exponent fixed. This proposition is an explicit hypothesis passed to the rescaled solver, not an assumption that a solution exists by definition.

This is a proposition recording the full unit-interval conclusion with fixed C and p. It has no computational fallback; coefficients, sources, positive ellipticity/coercivity parameters, and all regularity assumptions remain quantified inside the proposition.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.A1Body.summary: The unit interval inverse after choosing constants

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.EndpointSystem.text: An endpoint solution remains a solution when coefficient and source functions are replaced by functions equal on the interval. Behavior outside the interval is irrelevant.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.EndpointSystem.summary: Transferring a solution across equal interval data

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.ae_spatialSlic.text: Almost every time slice of a joint square-integrable sum or difference agrees with the corresponding sum or difference of spatial slices. This supplies representative compatibility in the weak instantaneous equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.ae_spatialSlic.summary: Spatial slices respect sums and differences

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.budget_le_powe.text: Bound the explicit recovery expression involving the mixed inverse and instantaneous inverse by a universal constant times a power of the combined coefficient budget. The chosen exponent is twice the freezing exponent plus one.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.budget_le_powe.summary: A single polynomial bound for the two inverses

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.coefficientMul.text: A scalar multiple of a coefficient acts as the same scalar multiple of its action on a field. This is the pointwise linearity used in rescaling the vorticity term.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.coefficientMul.summary: Moving a scalar through coefficient multiplication

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.contDiffOn_cur.text: A jointly smooth periodic spatial lift on the time slab determines a smooth curve in the half-Holder space, using the supplied finite spatial jets of the lift.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.contDiffOn_cur.summary: Smooth Holder curves from smooth periodic lifts

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.contDiffOn_lif.text: If the displacement lift is smooth and its within-time derivative is the velocity, identify the velocity lift with the time derivative and obtain joint smoothness.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.contDiffOn_lif.summary: Smooth velocity from a smooth displacement

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.contDiffOn_sol.text: A solenoidal curve whose Euclidean lift is jointly smooth is smooth as a curve in the divergence-free Holder subspace.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.contDiffOn_sol.summary: Smooth curves in the divergence-free subspace

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.contDiffOn_tim.text: A jointly smooth function on the time-space slab has a jointly smooth derivative in the time direction.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.contDiffOn_tim.summary: Smoothness of the time derivative on a slab

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.continuousOn_i.text: Continuous coefficient, source, and velocity curves give a continuous integrated residual, since the vorticity-velocity product has a continuous primitive.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.continuousOn_i.summary: Continuity of the integrated momentum residual

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.endpointClosed.text: Composing a continuous curve with a clock mapping the new closed interval into the old one cannot increase its closed-time norm.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.endpointSystem.text: Suppose $Kv-J(\Omega v)+L=c+\nabla\phi$ on $[0,T_1]$, with divergence-free $z_t=v$, $z(0)=z(T_1)=0$, and time-continuous half-Hölder velocity and pressure gradient. If $\sigma>0$ and $\sigma T_2=T_1$, then $Z(\tau)=\sigma^{-1}z(\sigma\tau)$ and $V(\tau)=v(\sigma\tau)$ solve the same system on $[0,T_2]$. Replace $K$ by $K(\sigma\tau)$, $\Omega$ by $\sigma\Omega(\sigma\tau)$, and compose $L,\phi$ and its gradient with the time change; $c$ is unchanged. Theorem 4.2 uses $\sigma=T$ and $T_2=1$. Here $Jw(t)=\int_0^tw(s)\,ds$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.endpointSystem.summary: Preserve both endpoint conditions under a positive time change

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.eval_sourceDer.text: Evaluation at a label commutes with the time primitive, so the source derivative is the negative forcing integrand. Continuity supplies the fundamental theorem of calculus on the closed interval.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.exists_instant.text: Choose the pointwise compressed inverses on the time interval and use smooth inversion of operator curves to obtain the asserted time regularity and uniform bound. The selected family is assigned the identity outside the interval, where no regularity is claimed.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.exists_instant.summary: Continuous instantaneous inverses from pointwise inverses

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.exists_isometr.text: Conjugate a continuous linear equivalence through a linear isometry equivalence while preserving its stated inverse bound. This changes the representation of the solenoidal space.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.exists_isometr.summary: Transporting an inverse through an isometry

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.exists_mixedSo.text: Assuming the mixed solution already has the required spatial derivative words, differentiate the projected equation and use the product rule and commuting projection to obtain every differentiated equation with its lower-order Leibniz correction. Regularity itself comes from the supplied higher-order freezing conclusion, not this differentiation lemma.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.exists_mixedSo.summary: Differentiated mixed equations for spatial derivative words

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.exists_mixedTi.text: Given a mixed projected solution, ellipticity, and a continuous bounded instantaneous inverse family, construct a continuous solenoidal representative with both primitive endpoints zero. Recover the constant by time averaging and identify almost-everywhere representatives by testing the difference against the positive coefficient.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.exists_mixedTi.summary: Recovering a continuous velocity from the mixed solution

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.exists_mixed_r.text: Represent the continuous endpoint solution in the mixed Holder-in-label and square-integrable-in-time space, preserving both constraints and its projected residual equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.exists_mixed_r.summary: A mixed representation of an endpoint solution

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.exists_smoothS.text: Apply the mixed higher-order clause of Lemma A.2 to obtain every finite spatial derivative hierarchy, differentiate the mixed equation to expose its commutators, and recover time-smooth representatives through base-space instantaneous inverses. Joint smoothness follows from matched finite spatial jets; this differs from the paper's use of instantaneous inverses on each higher Holder class.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.exists_smoothS.summary: A smooth solution from mixed spatial regularity

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.exists_solenoi.text: Suppose the conclusion of Lemma A.2 has already been established for $\mathcal R=\mathbb P$ and coefficient $B$ on $\mathbb T^3$, with $C\ge0$, $\mu>0$, Lipschitz bound $L\ge0$, and integer exponent $p\ge0$. Then $v\mapsto\mathbb P(Bv)$ is an isomorphism on divergence-free $C^{0,1/2}$ fields and its inverse norm is at most $C(2+\mu^{-1}+\|B\|_\infty+L)^p$. The norm is the maximum of the supremum and half-Hölder seminorm. This transfers an assumed inverse estimate to the precise space used by the endpoint problem; it does not establish coercivity or time dependence.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.exists_solenoi.summary: Transfer the freezing estimate to divergence-free Hölder fields

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.exists_spatial.text: For a finite spatial derivative hierarchy satisfying the differentiated mixed equations, recover time-smooth representatives using the supplied instantaneous inverse family and induction on word length. All permitted time derivatives retain the spatial derivative relations and the endpoint primitive conditions.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.exists_spatial.summary: Time regularity of the spatial derivative words

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.exists_unitSol.text: Given the mixed inverse and the continuous bounded family of instantaneous inverses, construct the unique continuous solenoidal velocity with zero time mean and constant projected residual. The explicit norm estimate combines the two inverse bounds; coercivity is used to identify its almost-everywhere mixed representative.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.exists_unitSol.summary: The unit interval solution from two inverses

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.fixedTime42.text: On $I=[0,T]$, $0<T\le1$, let $U$ be smooth, unit-periodic and divergence free, $X$ its flow from time zero, $F=D_aX$, $M=(DU)\circ X$, $K=F^TF$, $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$, and $H^\#=-(M_t+M^2)\le I$ as quadratic forms. Assume $\|F^{-1}\|\le D\ge1$, $\|M\|\le L$, $\|K\|\le K_0$ and $\|D_aK\|\le K_1$ uniformly. If the spatial inverse assertion of Lemma A.2 holds with $C_2\ge0$ and integer $p_2\ge0$, then $w\mapsto\mathbb P(K(t)w)$ is invertible on solenoidal $C^{0,1/2}$ fields and $\|(\mathbb PK(t))^{-1}\mathbb P\|\le C_2(2+D^2+K_0+2K_1)^{p_2}\|\mathbb P\|$ for every $t\in[0,T]$. The forward matrix and gradient in this assertion come from the actual flow; the input inverse assertion permits general coercive Lipschitz coefficients.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.fixedTime42.summary: Bound the inverse after the spatial Leray projection

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.freezingConclu.text: Let $e:v\mapsto\mathcal R(Bv)$ already be an isomorphism on the range of a bounded projection in $C^{0,1/2}(\mathbb T^3;H)$. Fix an integer $k\ge0$. Assume that the forward map preserves $C^{k,1/2}$, that every datum in that class has a unique preimage there, and that forward and inverse norm bounds have already been proved. Then $v\in C^{k,1/2}$ if and only if $ev\in C^{k,1/2}$, and one nonnegative constant controls both norm inequalities. This is an assembly step for Lemma A.2; it makes no deduction of those analytic premises from coercivity.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.freezingConclu.summary: Assemble the forward and inverse Hölder estimates

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.hasDerivWithin.text: The scalar map taking a new time to T times that time has within-set derivative T on every set. This supplies the clock derivative for the later chain rule and needs no interval-mapping hypothesis.
Evaluate a joint derivative on the pure time direction to obtain the derivative of a time slice at a fixed spatial point, with the time-interval boundary treated by within derivatives.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.hasDerivWithin.summary: Time derivatives of jointly smooth spatial slices

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.hasSpatialDeri.text: Directional differentiation on torus lines distributes over the sum of two Holder fields.
Differentiate pointwise application of an operator-valued Holder coefficient to a field, obtaining the derivative of the coefficient times the field plus the coefficient times the field derivative.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.hasSpatialDeri.summary: The spatial product rule for a coefficient

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.hasSpatialDeri.text: Negating a Holder field negates its directional derivative along every torus line.
Two Holder fields representing the same directional derivative on every torus line agree pointwise. This identifies derivatives after differentiating a projected equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.hasSpatialDeri.summary: Uniqueness of a spatial directional derivative

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.hasSpatialHold.text: A hierarchy of coordinate derivative words through order N plus one restricts to a hierarchy through order N.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.hasSpatialHold.summary: Discarding the highest spatial derivative order

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.integral_norm_.text: Let $0<T\le1$, $F_t=MF$, $GF=I$, $\|G\|\le D$, and $\|M\|\le L$, with $D,L\ge0$, continuous $M$ and differentiable $F$ on $[0,T]$. For any $v\in L^2$ with zero integral, set $z=Jv$ and $\xi=Fz$. Then $\|v\|_{L^2}^2\le D^2(1+L)^2\int_0^T|M\xi+Fv|^2\,dt$. The last integrand is $|\xi_t|^2$ almost everywhere. This is (4.6) for every Sobolev displacement, with the exact constant. The formal statement works in any complete real Hilbert space and does not require $F$ to arise from a particle flow. Here $Jw(t)=\int_0^tw(s)\,ds$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.integral_norm_.summary: Extend the displacement estimate to square-integrable velocities

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.integratedMome.text: If coefficients and sources agree throughout the time interval, their integrated momentum residuals agree at every time of that interval.
An interval-integral substitution identifies the momentum residual for rescaled coefficients and velocity with the original residual at the scaled time.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.integratedMome.summary: The integrated residual under time rescaling

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.lifts42.text: Construct the smooth kinetic and vorticity coefficient lifts from the smooth deformation and velocity gradient of the parent flow.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.mapsTo_scale.text: A positive scale taking the new terminal time to the old one maps the entire new closed interval into the old closed interval.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.mapsTo_scale.summary: Scalar time rescaling maps the required intervals

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.meanDeformatio.text: The inverse deformation of the rescaled flow is the original inverse deformation evaluated at the rescaled time.
The deformation matrix of the rescaled flow is the original deformation evaluated at the rescaled time.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.meanGradientRa.text: The time derivative of the rescaled gradient acquires two factors of T, one from velocity scaling and one from the clock.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.meanGradientRa.summary: The gradient derivative after time rescaling

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.meanGradient_s.text: The gradient of the rescaled parent velocity is T times the original gradient at the rescaled time.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.meanGradient_s.summary: The velocity gradient after time rescaling

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.meanHsharp_sca.text: The rescaled H-sharp is T squared times the original H-sharp at the rescaled time, because both the gradient derivative and its square have that factor.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.meanHsharp_sca.summary: The quadratic-form coefficient after time rescaling

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.meanHsharp_sca.text: For positive T at most one, the upper bound H-sharp at most the identity passes to the scaled parent. The proof treats negative quadratic values separately; multiplication by T squared need not decrease a negative value in the order needed for a naive argument.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.meanHsharp_sca.summary: The quadratic upper bound survives rescaling

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.meanKinetic_sc.text: The kinetic coefficient of the rescaled flow is K evaluated at the rescaled time, without an additional power of T.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.meanKinetic_sc.summary: The kinetic coefficient after time rescaling

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.meanParentFlow.text: For positive T at most one, the rescaled velocity and flow satisfy the mean-parent assumptions on the unit interval, including derivatives, periodicity, divergence freedom, and inverse flow identities.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.meanParentFlow.summary: The rescaled parent satisfies the flow hypotheses

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.meanVorticity_.text: The pulled-back skew vorticity coefficient acquires one factor of T under the unit-interval rescaling.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.meanVorticity_.summary: The vorticity coefficient after time rescaling

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.mixedPathCoeff.text: Spatial derivatives of K and Omega give the corresponding derivative of the path operator K minus J Omega. The time primitive is a fixed bounded operator and commutes with this spatial differentiation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.mixedPathCoeff.summary: Spatial differentiation of the mixed path coefficient

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.mixed_fixed.text: A continuous solenoidal velocity with zero terminal primitive has a mixed representative fixed by the combined spatial and temporal projection. The zero time mean encodes the second endpoint condition.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.mixed_fixed.summary: The mixed representative satisfies both constraints

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.mixed_projecti.text: If the spatial projection of a continuous residual is a time-independent field, then its mixed representative has zero combined spatial and time-mean projection. This links the integrated equation to the mixed equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.mixed_projecti.summary: The mixed projection removes the constant field

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.mixed_solution.text: Two mixed fields fixed by the projection and solving the same compressed equation agree because the supplied mixed operator is an isomorphism. This is uniqueness conditional on that inverse, not a new freezing theorem.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.mixed_solution.summary: Uniqueness from the supplied mixed inverse

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.norm_symm_le_o.text: For a continuous linear equivalence, a lower bound controlling the input norm by the output norm gives the corresponding operator norm bound for its inverse.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.parent42.text: Convert the paper's smooth mean-parent flow into the older inverse library's parent structure, transporting gradient bounds from labels to Eulerian points through the inverse flow.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.pow_le_of_le_s.text: Let $x,c\ge0$, $S\ge1$, and let $n,m$ be nonnegative integers with $n\le m$. If $x\le cS^4$, then $x^n\le c^nS^{4m}$. Both exponents are integer powers, including exponent zero. In Theorem 4.2 this elementary inequality combines the endpoint and fixed-time estimates into a common polynomial in the parent controls. It does not establish any inverse or estimate for the differential equation; the analytic bounds are inputs.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.pow_le_of_le_s.summary: Raise a scale estimate to a controlled integer power

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.scaledFlow.text:
Define the two-time parent flow with both time arguments multiplied by T. Spatial variables are unchanged.

Defined by composition for every real T, without division. At T = 0 both time arguments are zero; the theorem giving the required rescaled parent flow assumes positive T at most one.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.scaledFlow_bac.text: Setting the terminal time of the rescaled two-time flow to zero gives the original backward map from T times the new time. This is an evaluation identity, not a separate proof of the inverse-flow relation.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.scaledFlow_zer.text: Setting the initial time of the rescaled two-time flow to zero gives the original forward flow evaluated at T times the new time. This is an evaluation identity and uses no flow equation.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.scaledVelocity.text:
Define the parent velocity after time rescaling by multiplying its value at T times time by T. This is the velocity whose flow follows the original trajectories at the rescaled clock.

Defined for every real scaling factor T, including zero or negative T. The factor-zero velocity is zero; the parent-flow theorem is only used for positive T at most one, which maps the desired interval correctly.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.scaledVelocity.summary: The parent velocity on the unit time interval

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.smooth42.text:
On $I=[0,T]$, $0<T\le1$, let $U$ be smooth, unit-periodic and divergence free, $X$ its flow from time zero, $F=D_aX$, $M=(DU)\circ X$, $K=F^TF$, $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$, and $H^\#=-(M_t+M^2)\le I$ as quadratic forms. Assume finite bounds for $F^{-1},M$ and an endpoint solver which is unique in $z,v,c,G_\phi$ and returns smooth $z$ whenever its rescaled source is smooth. For smooth periodic Eulerian $f$, take $g=F^T(f\circ X)$ and $L_{m src}=-Jg$. The formal statement constructs smooth $z$ and a smooth periodic label pressure $\mathsf q$ of spatial mean zero, with $Kv_t+
abla_a\mathsf q=g-2F^TF_t v$. Then $b=(Fv)\circ X^{-1}$ and $q=\mathsf q\circ X^{-1}$ are smooth, $\operatorname{div}b=0$, and $b_t+U\cdot
abla b+b\cdot
abla U+
abla q=f$, with $b(0)=c$. The fields $z,v,c$ in the integrated system are solenoidal, and $z_t=v$, $z(0)=z(T)=0$. Uniqueness concerns the pressure gradient, not its scalar potential.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.smooth42.summary: Convert the endpoint solution into the linearized Euler solution

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.smoothData_con.text: Once the velocity is jointly smooth and the coefficients and source are smooth, obtain joint smoothness of its primitive, the spatial constant field, and the pressure gradient. The constant is recovered by projecting a fixed-time residual, while the gradient is the residual minus that constant.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.smoothData_con.summary: Smooth displacement constant and pressure gradient

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.sobolevEnergy_.text: On $I=[0,T]$, $0<T\le1$, let $U$ be smooth, unit-periodic and divergence free, $X$ its flow from time zero, $F=D_aX$, $M=(DU)\circ X$, $K=F^TF$, $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$, and $H^\#=-(M_t+M^2)\le I$ as quadratic forms. Assume $\|F^{-1}\|\le D\ge1$ and $\|M\|\le L\ge0$. Taking Lemma 4.1 as a premise, the formal statement gives $\int_0^1(\langle K(T\tau)v,v\rangle+\langle T\Omega(T\tau)v,Z\rangle)\,d\tau\ge[2D^2(1+L)^2]^{-1}\|v\|_{L^2(0,1)}^2$ for every zero-mean $L^2$ velocity, with $Z(\tau)=\int_0^\tau v$. Equivalently the tests are all $Z\in H^1_0(0,1;\mathbb R^3)$. This is the rescaled Sobolev coercivity needed for the endpoint inverse, including its exact constant.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.sobolevEnergy_.summary: Obtain the normalized displacement energy lower bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.solve42.text: Assume Lemma 4.1 and Theorem A.1. Let $u$ be smooth, periodic and divergence free on $[0,T]$, $0<T\le1$, with $H^\#\le I$. Bound the inverse flow derivative by $D\ge1$, the transported gradient by $M_0$, and $K,\Omega$ and their first spatial derivatives by $K_0,\Omega_0,K_1,\Omega_1$. For every continuous half-Hölder source $L$, there is a unique solution of $Kv-J(\Omega v)+L=c+\nabla\phi$, $z_t=v$, $z(0)=z(T)=0$, with weakly divergence-free $z,c$. Here $K=F^TF$, $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$ and $F=D_aX$. Its velocity bound is $C_1(2+D^2+2D^2(1+M_0)^2+K_0+K_1+\Omega_0+\Omega_1)^{p_1}\|L\|_{C_tC^{0,1/2}}$. Smooth source gives smooth displacement. Smooth physical velocity and pressure are additional conclusions established elsewhere. Here $Jw(t)=\int_0^tw(s)\,ds$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.solve42.summary: Apply the normalized inverse to the parent flow

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.spatialFixedIs.text:
Define a linear isometry between the fixed space of the strong Leray projection and the divergence-free Holder subspace. Both descriptions contain the same underlying field; this is a type-level identification without an analytic inversion.

Both directions preserve the same underlying Holder field and merely exchange equivalent subspace membership proofs. The zero field is handled ordinarily; there is no coefficient inverse, arbitrary representative, or exceptional value.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.spatialFixedIs.summary: Identifying the two solenoidal Holder spaces

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.spatialFixedIs.text: The forward isometry leaves the underlying Holder vector field unchanged.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.spatialFixedIs.summary: The fixed space identification preserves the field

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.spatialFixedIs.text: The inverse isometry likewise leaves the underlying Holder field unchanged, so estimates transfer without changing norms.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.spatialFixedIs.summary: The inverse identification preserves the field

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.spatiallyPerio.text: Evaluating a torus-valued Holder field on the Euclidean covering map gives a spatially periodic field.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.srcDeriv42.text: For the prescribed integrated force source, differentiate its Holder-space primitive to obtain minus the deformation transpose applied to the pulled-back force. Pointwise evaluation agrees with this derivative.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.srcDeriv42.summary: The derivative of the pulled back force source

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.strongMixedLer.text: Translation invariance and the Haar-space norm bound imply that the combined Leray and time-mean projection preserves the given spatial directional derivative.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S34A.strongMixedLer.summary: The mixed projection commutes with spatial differentiation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.Asub.text:
The linear space of bounded coefficient derivatives. These linear spaces encode the hypotheses of D.3 for an ODE with an initial datum. Permutation symmetry makes the derivative shifts commute; the equation uses the negative Leibniz expansion of coefficient multiplication.

Each word of the symmetric coefficient family has its own finite uniform bound on the slab. No common bound over all words, continuity in time, or realization as actual derivatives is built into this space. These additional facts are supplied where the smooth ODE is inserted.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.Asub.summary: The linear space of bounded coefficient derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.DA.text:
Shift the derivative family of a coefficient. These linear spaces encode the hypotheses of D.3 for an ODE with an initial datum. Permutation symmetry makes the derivative shifts commute; the equation uses the negative Leibniz expansion of coefficient multiplication.

The maps are restrictions of word-index shifts, with closure in the relevant subspaces proved in the definition. They encode already-weighted directions supplied elsewhere, rather than inserting an extra scalar weight here. Symmetry gives commutation; no new spatial differentiability is inferred merely from the shift.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.DA.summary: Shift the derivative family of a coefficient

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.DA_apply.text: Evaluate a shifted coefficient derivative. These linear spaces encode the hypotheses of D.3 for an ODE with an initial datum. Permutation symmetry makes the derivative shifts commute; the equation uses the negative Leibniz expansion of coefficient multiplication.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.DA_comm.text: The weighted derivative maps on coefficient families commute, as required by Lemma D.3. These linear spaces encode the hypotheses of D.3 for an ODE with an initial datum. Permutation symmetry makes the derivative shifts commute; the equation uses the negative Leibniz expansion of coefficient multiplication.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.DE.text:
The weighted derivative in the direction $i$ on solution jets. These linear spaces encode the hypotheses of D.3 for an ODE with an initial datum. Permutation symmetry makes the derivative shifts commute; the equation uses the negative Leibniz expansion of coefficient multiplication.

Default values: The maps are restrictions of word-index shifts, with closure in the relevant subspaces proved in the definition. They encode already-weighted directions supplied elsewhere, rather than inserting an extra scalar weight here. Symmetry gives commutation; no new spatial differentiability is inferred merely from the shift.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.DE.summary: Shift the derivative family of a solution

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.DE_apply.text: Evaluate a shifted solution derivative. These linear spaces encode the hypotheses of D.3 for an ODE with an initial datum. Permutation symmetry makes the derivative shifts commute; the equation uses the negative Leibniz expansion of coefficient multiplication.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.DE_comm.text: The weighted derivative maps on solution families commute, as required by Lemma D.3. These linear spaces encode the hypotheses of D.3 for an ODE with an initial datum. Permutation symmetry makes the derivative shifts commute; the equation uses the negative Leibniz expansion of coefficient multiplication.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.DF.text:
Shift both forcing and initial derivative families. These linear spaces encode the hypotheses of D.3 for an ODE with an initial datum. Permutation symmetry makes the derivative shifts commute; the equation uses the negative Leibniz expansion of coefficient multiplication.

The maps are restrictions of word-index shifts, with closure in the relevant subspaces proved in the definition. They encode already-weighted directions supplied elsewhere, rather than inserting an extra scalar weight here. Symmetry gives commutation; no new spatial differentiability is inferred merely from the shift.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.DF.summary: Shift both forcing and initial derivative families

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.DF_apply_fst.text: The forcing component of the shift prepends the selected direction to its word index. The same shift acts simultaneously on the initial-value component.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.DF_apply_snd.text: The initial-value component of the shift prepends the selected direction to its word index. This ensures that spatial differentiation commutes with prescribed initial data.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.DF_comm.text: The weighted derivative maps on forcing and initial-data families commute, as required by Lemma D.3. These linear spaces encode the hypotheses of D.3 for an ODE with an initial datum. Permutation symmetry makes the derivative shifts commute; the equation uses the negative Leibniz expansion of coefficient multiplication.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.DF_comm.summary: Forcing and initial derivative shifts commute

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.EP.text:
Admissible time regularity of a solution derivative family. These linear spaces encode the hypotheses of Lemma D.3 for an ODE with an initial datum. Permutation symmetry makes the derivative shifts commute; the equation uses the negative Leibniz expansion of coefficient multiplication.

An element is a family of functions indexed by words, unchanged when a word is permuted, each differentiable within the slab $[l,r]$ with continuous within-derivatives. This is weaker than being the derivative family of a single spatial function. Values outside the slab are unconstrained; later constructions from the data of the linear equation $x'=Ax+f$ supply the actual finite derivative family.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.EP.summary: Admissible time regularity of a solution derivative family

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.Esub.text:
The linear space of solution derivative families. These linear spaces encode the hypotheses of Lemma D.3 for an ODE with an initial datum. Permutation symmetry makes the derivative shifts commute; the equation uses the negative Leibniz expansion of coefficient multiplication.

An element is a family of functions indexed by words, unchanged when a word is permuted, each differentiable within the slab $[l,r]$ with continuous within-derivatives. This is weaker than being the derivative family of a single spatial function. Values outside the slab are unconstrained; later constructions from the data of the linear equation $x'=Ax+f$ supply the actual finite derivative family.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.Esub.summary: The linear space of solution derivative families

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.Fsub.text:
The linear space of forcing and initial derivatives. These linear spaces encode the hypotheses of D.3 for an ODE with an initial datum. Permutation symmetry makes the derivative shifts commute; the equation uses the negative Leibniz expansion of coefficient multiplication.

Only the forcing part has a weighted boundedness condition; the second component is an arbitrary symmetric family of initial values. No continuity of the forcing is included here. The combined seminorm separately measures the initial component and the forcing component.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.Fsub.summary: The linear space of forcing and initial derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.text: The actual selected velocity and pressure satisfy the quantitative inverse estimate in the measured active-slab seminorm. The positive coefficient-word bound enters only through its dimensionless budget. The selected solution has zero initial data, zero phase mean and support inherited from the forcing. Positive weight and covector hypotheses make the measured velocity and frequency-weighted pressure estimates meaningful.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.summary: Bound the selected transverse velocity and pressure

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.text: Smooth strain and a smooth everywhere nonzero covector give smooth pressure coefficients for the amplitude and source terms. Nonvanishing is essential for the factors involving the inverse squared covector norm.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.summary: Nonvanishing covectors give smooth pressure coefficients

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.text: Lemma 5.3(i)–(ii) (cc:uf:tower:lem:inverse) for arbitrary smooth supported launch data and for the selected zero-start transverse solve. The frequency-weighted active seminorms are the actual Appendix D norms. This passes pointwise word estimates to the finite weighted norms used in Section 5. Constants may depend on the derivative order but the final power of the parent bound does not.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.summary: The supported transverse inverse preserves every derivative order

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.text: Derivative-order constants control the actual coframe, generator and pressure coefficient words. The measured oscillatory inverse budget retains a single power $D ^ 20$ at every order. The supported labels lie within twice the envelope radius of a lattice point. The parent bounds and central weighted stability supply the near-origin propagator estimate; smallness of the label radius absorbs differentiated coefficients.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.summary: Coframe and pressure constants have uniform parent cost

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.text: The parent deformation and velocity bounds determine a radius exponent for the selected fixed-plane forward propagator. The supported labels lie within twice the envelope radius of a lattice point. The parent bounds and central weighted stability supply the near-origin propagator estimate; smallness of the label radius absorbs differentiated coefficients.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.summary: The transverse propagator is controlled near the origin

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.text: The finite launch seminorm controls each admissible derivative word of the initial profile. This supplies the individual initial-data bound required by the ODE recurrence from the paper's summed launch norm.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.summary: The launch norm bounds each derivative word

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.text: A bound $C \ell D^27$ on the rescaled jets of positive order of a phase-independent coefficient gives the bound $C D^{-3}$ on its weighted derivative words of positive length, since $\ell \le D^{-30}$. The supported labels lie within twice the envelope radius of a lattice point. The parent bounds and central weighted stability supply the near-origin propagator estimate; smallness of the label radius absorbs differentiated coefficients.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.summary: A small envelope absorbs differentiated coefficients

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.text: For a smooth function of labels alone and nonnegative label scale, any mixed label-phase word is bounded by the label scale to the word length times the corresponding Fréchet derivative norm. A phase derivative annihilates such a coefficient; the bound is sufficient without separating that zero case in later estimates.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.summary: Label derivatives control phase independent derivative words

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.text: For a smooth label field and a nonnegative scale, the $j$th derivative norm of $a\mapsto f(\ell a)$ equals $\ell^j$ times the $j$th derivative norm of $f$ at $\ell a$. This turns a rescaled-label estimate into the weighted derivatives of Appendix D, including $j=0$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.summary: Rescaling labels inserts the derivative weights

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.text: Positive frequency, nonvanishing smooth covector, and finite derivative bounds for κ/λ and λ²/|κ|² give a finite derivative bound for the normalized pressure-source coefficient. The result isolates the coefficient multiplying the forcing in the zero-mean pressure primitive.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.summary: The normalized pressure source has bounded derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.text:
The selected oscillatory inverse constant in the sum of velocity and carrier-weighted pressure seminorms. The constants collect the fixed-plane inverse, the two coframes and the pressure primitive. Their use requires the displayed nonnegative bounds; the eventual estimate has a single power of the parent scale at every derivative order.

These are total real-valued expressions for arbitrary scalar arguments. A negative duration or a negative coefficient bound does not have the intended estimate interpretation. The application theorems impose nonnegative budgets and a positive time slab. No division occurs here; the selected amplification factor is controlled only at its nonnegative argument.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.summary: The constant for transverse velocity and pressure

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.text: The velocity part has degree thirteen in $D$. Its pressure contribution has degree twenty, while the direct forcing contribution has degree six. The constants collect the fixed-plane inverse, the two coframes and the pressure primitive. Their use requires the displayed nonnegative bounds; the eventual estimate has a single power of the parent scale at every derivative order.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.summary: One parent exponent bounds velocity and pressure

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.text:
The per-word velocity constant from the fixed-plane solve and the two coframes. The constants collect the fixed-plane inverse, the two coframes and the pressure primitive. Their use requires the displayed nonnegative bounds; the eventual estimate has a single power of the parent scale at every derivative order.

These are total real-valued expressions for arbitrary scalar arguments. A negative duration or a negative coefficient bound does not have the intended estimate interpretation. The application theorems impose nonnegative budgets and a positive time slab. No division occurs here; the selected amplification factor is controlled only at its nonnegative argument.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.summary: The constant for transverse velocity derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.text: A solve on an interval of length at most one has a common coefficient for its initial-data and source bounds. The constants collect the fixed-plane inverse, the two coframes and the pressure primitive. Their use requires the displayed nonnegative bounds; the eventual estimate has a single power of the parent scale at every derivative order.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.HierarchyTwiste.summary: A unit time interval gives a common constant

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.IsSymm.text:
Derivative families invariant under permutations. These linear spaces encode the hypotheses of D.3 for an ODE with an initial datum. Permutation symmetry makes the derivative shifts commute; the equation uses the negative Leibniz expansion of coefficient multiplication.

This is only invariance of a family under permutations of its list index. It does not assert existence of an underlying smooth field or derivative relations. The empty word is allowed and its symmetry condition is automatic.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.JetPower.text:
Pointwise power bound $\|\partial^m f x\| \le C_m D^{a(m+1)}$ (the pointwise form of (D.6)). The bridge converts between coordinate word norms in Appendix D and Fréchet derivative bounds used by the fixed-plane construction. The conversion changes constants depending on the order, not the absolute parent exponent.

Default values: The predicate includes smoothness and an inequality at every order, including zero. It does not itself assert $D\ge1$ or nonnegative constants. Monotonicity and product/rescaling theorems supply their own sign hypotheses, so the formula at a nonpositive scale is not silently interpreted as a parent estimate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.JetPower.summary: Pointwise derivatives bounded by powers of the parent scale

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.JetPower.comp_l.text: A fixed contraction applied on the left preserves the power bound. Here the lift is the deformation restricted to the fixed carrier plane, and the pullback is the inverse deformation followed by the transverse projection and orthogonal projection onto that plane. This avoids a separate Gram-matrix inverse estimate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.JetPower.comp_l.summary: A contraction preserves polynomial derivative bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.JetPower.const_.text: Multiplying the coefficient field by a constant scalar multiplies its derivative constants by the absolute value of that scalar. The power of the parent scale is unchanged.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.JetPower.const_.summary: Scale a coefficient and its derivative constants

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.JetPower.mono_c.text: Pointwise enlargement of the nonnegative derivative constants preserves the same smooth coefficient power bound. The field, parent scale and exponent stay fixed.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.JetPower.mono_c.summary: Increase the constants in a derivative bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.JetPower.mono_e.text: When the parent scale is at least one, increasing the absolute exponent weakens every derivative bound. This permits several coefficient estimates to share one exponent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.JetPower.mono_e.summary: Increase the parent exponent in a derivative bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.L0.text:
Time differentiation together with the initial value. These linear spaces encode the hypotheses of D.3 for an ODE with an initial datum. Permutation symmetry makes the derivative shifts commute; the equation uses the negative Leibniz expansion of coefficient multiplication.

The forcing component is the within-interval derivative multiplied by the interval indicator, hence zero outside the slab. The data component evaluates at the actual left endpoint. The admitted solution-family regularity makes the derivative legitimate on the slab; no differentiability of the zero extension across its boundary is claimed.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.L0.summary: Time differentiation together with the initial value

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.L0_comm.text: The derivative shift commutes with the map sending a solution family to its time derivative within the interval and its initial value, as required by Lemma D.3. These linear spaces encode the hypotheses of D.3 for an ODE with an initial datum. Permutation symmetry makes the derivative shifts commute; the equation uses the negative Leibniz expansion of coefficient multiplication.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.L0_comm.summary: Spatial shifts commute with time differentiation and initial evaluation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.L0_fst.text: On the closed interval the forcing component of L₀ is the within-interval time derivative of the solution family. Outside the interval this component is explicitly zero by the indicator in the definition.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.L0_fst.summary: Recover the time derivative in the forcing component

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.L0_snd.text: The data component of L₀ evaluates every word of the solution family at the left endpoint. It is the initial datum that accompanies the forcing in the inverse estimate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.L0_snd.summary: Recover the initial value in the data component

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.Leaf2.text:
The leaf jets hold at a base scale $D_0$ with $D_0^{64} \le D$, where $D$ is the scale of the chain. The bridge converts between coordinate word norms in Appendix D and Fréchet derivative bounds used by the fixed-plane construction. The conversion changes constants depending on the order, not the absolute parent exponent.

Default values: The witness $D_0$ is explicitly at least one and satisfies $D_0^{64}\le D$, so the comparison cannot use a zero or negative base scale. The statement stores coefficient bounds at $D_0$, not at an unspecified smaller positive number. It does not construct new parent data.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.Leaf2.summary: Coefficient estimates at a smaller parent scale

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.Leaf2.toLeaf.text: The two-scale leaf jets give the leaf jets at the chain scale. The bridge converts between coordinate word norms in Appendix D and Fréchet derivative bounds used by the fixed-plane construction. The conversion changes constants depending on the order, not the absolute parent exponent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.Leaf2.toLeaf.summary: Transfer coefficient bounds to the larger parent scale

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.Leaves.text:
The facts of Lemmas 3.1, D.1, D.2, D.3 that the library chain consumes. This module passes supplied proofs of Lemmas 3.1, D.1 and D.2, and a derivative recurrence obtained from D.3, into the copied transverse argument. The local class is a bundle of hypotheses, not an additional axiom.

The class stores proofs of the cited statements and a weighted ODE estimate; declaring the class does not assert that an instance exists. The entry theorem explicitly constructs an instance from its hypotheses. The factor Φ is constrained only on nonnegative arguments, which is the domain used by the estimates.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.Leaves.summary: The cited estimates needed for the transverse inverse

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.LocalizedAmplit.text: Localized homogeneous seed estimates in normalized spatial coordinates. The ODE estimate is used only on the support of the envelope. Initial data are the projected center amplitude, including every derivative of the envelope. The leading profile is built from a seed, a compact label envelope and the one-dimensional phase wave. All derivative orders use the same sufficiently small envelope radius; the estimates are on the active time interval.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.LocalizedAmplit.summary: Bound the enveloped seed in rescaled labels

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.LocalizedAmplit.text: Smooth deformation and covector data give a smooth longitudinal coframe in the stated parameter domain. The construction uses the supplied nonvanishing hypotheses wherever inverse covector lengths occur.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.LocalizedAmplit.summary: The longitudinal coframe depends smoothly on its coefficients

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.LocalizedAmplit.text: A single natural exponent is chosen large enough to enforce the finite list of smallness requirements for the transverse coframe. It is independent of the derivative order; the constants at each order remain separate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.LocalizedAmplit.summary: Choose one envelope exponent for the coframe bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.LocalizedAmplit.text: Lemma 5.3(iii) for the unswitched leading velocity and its normalized primitive pressure on the active slab. The norm is taken in the independent label and phase, before taking the physical graph. This passes pointwise word estimates to the finite weighted norms used in Section 5. Constants may depend on the derivative order but the final power of the parent bound does not.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.LocalizedAmplit.summary: Bound the leading oscillation and its pressure

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.LocalizedAmplit.text: On the actual closed parent slab, the same radius exponent serves all orders of the initial leading velocity and pressure estimates. The leading profile is built from a seed, a compact label envelope and the one-dimensional phase wave. All derivative orders use the same sufficiently small envelope radius; the estimates are on the active time interval.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.LocalizedAmplit.summary: One envelope exponent controls every leading derivative order

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.LocalizedAmplit.text: The scaled leading velocity and pressure estimates obtained from the same seed and parent coefficients. The leading profile is built from a seed, a compact label envelope and the one-dimensional phase wave. All derivative orders use the same sufficiently small envelope radius; the estimates are on the active time interval.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.LocalizedAmplit.summary: Retain the leading profile derivative estimates

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.LocalizedAmplit.text: The coframe coefficients of the actual parent flow satisfy the power bound (D.6), by Lemma D.2(a) applied to the transverse coframe, as used in the proof of Lemma 5.3. The leaf jets hold at the base scale $D_0$; the geometric bounds on the flow hold at the scale $D$. The fields are $F = D_a X$, $G Q$ with $Q$ the projection orthogonal to $G^T k$, and $-2 (G Q)(M F)$; the lift $J$, the pullback $R$ and the generator $A$ are fixed contractions of them ($J = F \iota$, $R = \pi (G Q)$, $A = \pi (-2 (G Q)(M F)) \iota$ with the inclusion $\iota$ and the orthogonal projection $\pi$ of the transverse plane). The leading profile is built from a seed, a compact label envelope and the one-dimensional phase wave. All derivative orders use the same sufficiently small envelope radius; the estimates are on the active time interval.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.LocalizedAmplit.summary: The transverse coframe has polynomial derivative bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.LocalizedAmplit.text: The physical enveloped seed has polynomial cost ($D^{13}$) at every fixed order. The restriction on the label radius uses only the first derivative of the generator. The leading profile is built from a seed, a compact label envelope and the one-dimensional phase wave. All derivative orders use the same sufficiently small envelope radius; the estimates are on the active time interval.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.LocalizedAmplit.summary: The enveloped seed has one fixed parent exponent

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.LocalizedAmplit.text: A bound for each derivative of the rescaled leading field gives a bound for the finite weighted raw norm. The number of admissible words and the inverse positive amplitude weight are accounted for explicitly.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.LocalizedAmplit.summary: Rescaled derivatives control the weighted finite norm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeData.text:
The data of the linear ODE $x' = A x + f$ on $[l, r]$ at a fixed point $p$. Smooth parameter derivatives of the actual solution supply the abstract families used for D.3. Only derivatives through the fixed order and times in the closed interval are retained; time differentiation is taken within that interval.

Default values: The record requires $l<r$, smooth coefficient/source/solution and a strictly positive differentiable weight on the slab. The homogeneous stability estimate is only at the stored parameter point p; it is not an unstated uniform estimate at every parameter. Sign assumptions on K are provided by downstream estimates, not by this record alone.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeData.summary: A smooth linear equation with a positive weight

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeData.Rw.text:
The differentiated right side of the equation. Smooth parameter derivatives of the actual solution supply the abstract families used for Lemma D.3. Only derivatives through the fixed order and times in the closed interval are retained; time differentiation is taken within that interval.

The word derivative of $Ax+f$ is defined for every input, but the smooth ODE interpretation is used only on the stored slab $[l,r]$ where the data of the linear equation supply regularity. Unlike the retained derivative families of the solution $x$ and the coefficient $A$, this expression is not padded by a time or order cutoff.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeData.Rw.summary: The differentiated right side of the equation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeData.aE.text:
The coefficient jets as an element of the space of coefficients. Smooth parameter derivatives of the actual solution supply the abstract families used for D.3. Only derivatives through the fixed order and times in the closed interval are retained; time differentiation is taken within that interval.

Default values: The bundled family uses the deliberately zero-padded finite jets. Membership proves only symmetry and the required within-slab regularity or boundedness. It does not identify the padded family with all higher derivatives of the original field. For the coefficient family the positive-order bound is an explicit input, and compactness bounds the zero-order coefficient.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeData.aE.summary: Place coefficient derivatives in the bounded linear space

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeData.aj.text:
The jets $\partial^w A(t, p)$ of order $\le n$ (zero otherwise and outside the slab). Smooth parameter derivatives of the actual solution supply the abstract families used for D.3. Only derivatives through the fixed order and times in the closed interval are retained; time differentiation is taken within that interval.

Default values: The definition sets entries to zero both above the retained derivative order and outside the closed time slab. It represents actual derivatives only when the word length and slab membership conditions hold. The zero extension need not be smooth across the time boundary; all time-regularity results are within the slab.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeData.aj.summary: The coefficient derivatives through a fixed order

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeData.aj_of_m.text: For a retained word and a time in the closed interval, the padded coefficient family equals the actual parameter derivative of the ODE coefficient. Outside those conditions the definition makes no derivative claim.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeData.aj_of_m.summary: Recover an included coefficient derivative on the time interval

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeData.aj_symm.text: The jets are symmetric under permutations of the derivative words. Smooth parameter derivatives of the actual solution supply the abstract families used for D.3. Only derivatives through the fixed order and times in the closed interval are retained; time differentiation is taken within that interval.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeData.aj_symm.summary: Coefficient derivatives are invariant under permutations

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeData.continu.text: Smoothness of coefficient, solution and source makes the differentiated right-hand side continuous in time on the slab. This supplies the time-regularity requirement of the abstract solution space.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeData.continu.summary: The differentiated right side is continuous in time

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeData.derivWi.text: The within-interval time derivative of a retained solution word is identified with the differentiated right-hand side. The result rewrites the time operator L₀ in the abstract equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeData.derivWi.summary: Identify the time derivative on the closed interval

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeData.equatio.text: The differentiated equation: $L \tilde x$ consists of the jets of the forcing. Smooth parameter derivatives of the actual solution supply the abstract families used for D.3. Only derivatives through the fixed order and times in the closed interval are retained; time differentiation is taken within that interval.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeData.equatio.summary: The residual of the derivative family is the forcing

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeData.hasDeri.text: A retained parameter derivative of the smooth solution has time derivative equal to the same parameter word applied to Ax+f. The time derivative is within the nonempty closed interval, including its endpoints.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeData.hasDeri.summary: Solution derivatives satisfy the differentiated time equation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeData.slab.text:
Retain the time interval and weight of the equation. Smooth parameter derivatives of the actual solution supply the abstract families used for Lemma D.3. Only derivatives through the fixed order and times in the closed interval are retained; time differentiation is taken within that interval.

This projection retains the same $l$, $r$ and weight $g$ from the data of the linear equation and proves continuity of $g$ from its stored derivative property. The strict interval $l<r$ and positive weight are preserved; no new interval or arbitrary extension is selected.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeData.slab.summary: Retain the time interval and weight of the equation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeData.xE.text:
The solution jets as an element of the space of solutions. Smooth parameter derivatives of the actual solution supply the abstract families used for D.3. Only derivatives through the fixed order and times in the closed interval are retained; time differentiation is taken within that interval.

Default values: The bundled family uses the deliberately zero-padded finite jets. Membership proves only symmetry and the required within-slab regularity or boundedness. It does not identify the padded family with all higher derivatives of the original field. For the coefficient family the positive-order bound is an explicit input, and compactness bounds the zero-order coefficient.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeData.xE.summary: Place solution derivatives in the admissible linear space

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeData.xj.text:
The jets $\partial^w x(t, p)$ of order $\le n$ (zero otherwise and outside the slab). Smooth parameter derivatives of the actual solution supply the abstract families used for D.3. Only derivatives through the fixed order and times in the closed interval are retained; time differentiation is taken within that interval.

Default values: The definition sets entries to zero both above the retained derivative order and outside the closed time slab. It represents actual derivatives only when the word length and slab membership conditions hold. The zero extension need not be smooth across the time boundary; all time-regularity results are within the slab.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeData.xj.summary: The solution derivatives through a fixed order

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeData.xj_big.text: Every word longer than the retained order is the identically zero time function by definition. This padding supplies an infinite indexed family while retaining only a finite amount of derivative data.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeData.xj_big.summary: Derivatives above the retained order are set to zero

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeData.xj_of_m.text: For a retained word and a time in the closed interval, the padded solution family equals the actual parameter derivative of the solution. Both hypotheses are necessary because other entries were defined to be zero.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeData.xj_of_m.summary: Recover an included solution derivative on the time interval

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeData.xj_symm.text: The jets are symmetric under permutations of the derivative words. Smooth parameter derivatives of the actual solution supply the abstract families used for D.3. Only derivatives through the fixed order and times in the closed interval are retained; time differentiation is taken within that interval.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeData.xj_symm.summary: Solution derivatives are invariant under permutations

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeData.zeroOrd.text: The homogeneous weighted stability hypothesis yields the forced zero-order estimate by variation of constants. The source is measured by interval length times its weighted supremum plus the weighted initial datum, matching the forcing space of D.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeData.zeroOrd.summary: Variation of constants gives the required zero order estimate

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeWordBound.text:
Lemma D.3 for the ODE: some monotone nonnegative factor $\Phi$ satisfies the weighted derivative estimate with that factor. A separate theorem derives this from the assumed Lemma D.3. The formalization passes supplied proofs of Lemmas 3.1, D.1 and D.2, and a derivative recurrence obtained from D.3, into the copied transverse argument. The bundle of these facts is a set of hypotheses, not an additional axiom.

Default values: Existence is of a factor $\Phi$ that is nonnegative and monotone only for nonnegative scalar arguments. Its value at negative arguments is deliberately unrestricted. All subsequent uses pass $K(r-l)C$ with $K,C\ge0$ and $l<r$, so no uncontrolled branch is used.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeWordBound.summary: Existence of a monotone derivative amplification factor

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeWordBoundWit.text:
The weighted derivative recurrence on a slab (the library form of Lemma D.3 for the linear ODE $x' = A x + f$ with weight $g$, (5.18)-(5.23)): for the amplification factor $\Phi$, which depends only on the order $N$ and on a bound of $K (r - l) C$, all derivative words of order $\le N$ of the solution are bounded by $\Phi(N, K (r - l) C) \cdot K (B + (r - l) H)$. The original library's word bound for the linear ODE on a closed interval has an explicit recursively defined factor; Lemma D.3 only provides some factor $\Phi$. The formalization passes supplied proofs of Lemmas 3.1, D.1 and D.2, and a derivative recurrence obtained from D.3, into the copied transverse argument. The bundle of these facts is a set of hypotheses, not an additional axiom.

Default values: The interval is explicitly nonempty, the weight is strictly positive on it, and the stability and derivative bounds are nonnegative. The parameter set may be empty, in which case the pointwise conclusion is vacuous. The derivative order may be zero, in which case there are no positive coefficient-word hypotheses. The statement assumes a smooth solution rather than selecting one.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.OdeWordBoundWit.summary: The weighted derivative estimate with a specified amplification factor

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.Slab.text:
A nonempty time interval with positive continuous weight. These linear spaces encode the hypotheses of D.3 for an ODE with an initial datum. Permutation symmetry makes the derivative shifts commute; the equation uses the negative Leibniz expansion of coefficient multiplication.

The strict inequality l<r makes the closed interval nonempty and supplies unique within-interval derivatives at endpoints. The weight is continuous and strictly positive there, so compactness controls its reciprocal. Nothing is asserted about its sign outside the slab.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.Slab.summary: A nonempty time interval with positive continuous weight

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.Tmap.text:
$T(a)u = -(a u)$ with the Leibniz rule for words, and zero initial data. These linear spaces encode the hypotheses of D.3 for an ODE with an initial datum. Permutation symmetry makes the derivative shifts commute; the equation uses the negative Leibniz expansion of coefficient multiplication.

Default values: This is a finite negative Leibniz sum with initial component identically zero. The coefficient family is bounded and the solution family continuous on the slab, proving weighted boundedness of each forcing word. It is a linear-algebra encoding of multiplication, not an assumed solution of the ODE.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.Tmap.summary: Subtract coefficient multiplication in the differentiated equation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.Tmap_fst.text: The forcing component of coefficient multiplication is minus the Leibniz sum over all splits of the word. Thus L₀+T corresponds to x′−Ax together with the initial value.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.Tmap_fst.summary: The product term is the negative Leibniz sum

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.Tmap_leibniz.text: Shifting the product term splits into a shifted coefficient times the original solution and the original coefficient times the shifted solution. This is the Leibniz compatibility required by D.3.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.Tmap_snd.text: Coefficient multiplication contributes zero to the initial-data component. The prescribed data are carried entirely by L₀.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.Tmap_snd.summary: Coefficient multiplication contributes no initial datum

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.WBdd.text:
A time function bounded relative to the weight. These linear spaces encode the hypotheses of D.3 for an ODE with an initial datum. Permutation symmetry makes the derivative shifts commute; the equation uses the negative Leibniz expansion of coefficient multiplication.

The predicate asks for some real bound relative to the positive slab weight. It does not require the witness to be explicitly nonnegative; on the nonempty positive-weight slab any valid witness is forced to be nonnegative by its inequality. No global bound outside the slab is implied.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.WBdd.summary: A time function bounded relative to the weight

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.WBdd.add.text: Two functions bounded relative to the same positive weight have a weighted bound for their sum, obtained by adding their constants. The statement asserts existence of a bound, not a sharp norm equality.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.WBdd.add.summary: Add two bounds relative to the same weight

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.WBdd.congr.text: Equality of two functions on the slab transfers an existing weighted bound from one to the other. Values outside the slab are irrelevant to this predicate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.WBdd.congr.summary: Equality on the interval preserves a weighted bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.WBdd.smul.text: Scalar multiplication preserves weighted boundedness, with the constant multiplied by the scalar's absolute value. This establishes closure under scalars for the forcing space.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.WBdd.smul.summary: Scale a bound relative to the same weight

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.coefficientPowe.text: Pointwise jets with a power bound give the coefficient power bound of Appendix D (the size $|c|_m$ is a sum over the nondecreasing coordinate words, each of whose terms is a pointwise jet). The bridge converts between coordinate word norms in Appendix D and Fréchet derivative bounds used by the fixed-plane construction. The conversion changes constants depending on the order, not the absolute parent exponent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.coefficientPowe.summary: Pointwise derivatives give the coefficient power bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.contDiff_cofram.text: Restriction to the transverse plane preserves smoothness. Here the lift is the deformation restricted to the fixed carrier plane, and the pullback is the inverse deformation followed by the transverse projection and orthogonal projection onto that plane. This avoids a separate Gram-matrix inverse estimate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.contDiff_cofram.summary: Restriction to the transverse plane preserves smoothness

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.contDiff_slabSl.text: Joint smoothness on a time slab times all spatial parameters gives smoothness in the parameters at each allowed time. No extension of the time variable beyond the slab is asserted.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.contDiff_slabSl.summary: A smooth time slab has smooth spatial slices

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.d2Scale.text:
The power of the base scale: the chain scale $D$ dominates $D_0^{64}$. The bridge converts between coordinate word norms in Appendix D and Fréchet derivative bounds used by the fixed-plane construction. The conversion changes constants depending on the order, not the absolute parent exponent.

Default values: This is the fixed natural number 64. There is no choice, denominator or degenerate branch; it deliberately provides slack between a base parent scale and the scale of the copied chain.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.d2Scale.summary: The fixed exponent separating the two parent scales

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.derivWithin_add.text: The derivative within the closed interval of a sum equals the sum of the two derivatives when both summands are differentiable there. The nonempty interval supplies the local uniqueness of the derivative at its endpoints.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.derivWithin_add.summary: Time differentiation distributes over addition on the interval

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.derivWithin_smu.text: Constant scalar multiplication commutes with the time derivative within the interval for a differentiable function. This proves linearity of the time operator in the solution-family space.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.derivWithin_smu.summary: Time differentiation respects constant scaling on the interval

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.evA.text:
Evaluation of a coefficient at the empty word and the time $t$. The seminorms measure the empty word on the closed interval. They become norms of higher derivatives only after applying the commuting shifts; positivity of the weight and explicit boundedness justify the suprema.

Default values: These linear evaluations are defined at the empty word and (except the initial-datum evaluation) at any specified real time. They ignore higher-word entries and make no assertion about that time lying in the slab. The seminorm definitions index their time argument by the slab to enforce the intended domain.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.evA.summary: Evaluate the undifferentiated coefficient at one time

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.evA_apply.text: Identify evaluation of the coefficient family. The seminorms measure the empty word on the closed interval. They become norms of higher derivatives only after applying the commuting shifts; positivity of the weight and explicit boundedness justify the suprema.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.evA_apply.summary: Identify evaluation of the coefficient family

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.evE.text:
Evaluation of a solution jet at the empty word and the time $t$. The seminorms measure the empty word on the closed interval. They become norms of higher derivatives only after applying the commuting shifts; positivity of the weight and explicit boundedness justify the suprema.

Default values: These linear evaluations are defined at the empty word and (except the initial-datum evaluation) at any specified real time. They ignore higher-word entries and make no assertion about that time lying in the slab. The seminorm definitions index their time argument by the slab to enforce the intended domain.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.evE.summary: Evaluate the undifferentiated solution at one time

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.evE_apply.text: Identify evaluation of the solution family. The seminorms measure the empty word on the closed interval. They become norms of higher derivatives only after applying the commuting shifts; positivity of the weight and explicit boundedness justify the suprema.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.evE_apply.summary: Identify evaluation of the solution family

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.evF.text:
Evaluation of the forcing at the empty word and the time $t$. The seminorms measure the empty word on the closed interval. They become norms of higher derivatives only after applying the commuting shifts; positivity of the weight and explicit boundedness justify the suprema.

Default values: These linear evaluations are defined at the empty word and (except the initial-datum evaluation) at any specified real time. They ignore higher-word entries and make no assertion about that time lying in the slab. The seminorm definitions index their time argument by the slab to enforce the intended domain.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.evF.summary: Evaluate the undifferentiated forcing at one time

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.evF_apply.text: Identify evaluation of the forcing family. The seminorms measure the empty word on the closed interval. They become norms of higher derivatives only after applying the commuting shifts; positivity of the weight and explicit boundedness justify the suprema.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.evF_apply.summary: Identify evaluation of the forcing family

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.evI.text:
Read the undifferentiated initial datum at the empty word. The seminorms measure the empty word on the closed interval. They become norms of higher derivatives only after applying the commuting shifts; positivity of the weight and explicit boundedness justify the suprema.

Default values: These linear evaluations are defined at the empty word and (except the initial-datum evaluation) at any specified real time. They ignore higher-word entries and make no assertion about that time lying in the slab. The seminorm definitions index their time argument by the slab to enforce the intended domain.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.evI_apply.text: Identify evaluation of the initial datum. The seminorms measure the empty word on the closed interval. They become norms of higher derivatives only after applying the commuting shifts; positivity of the weight and explicit boundedness justify the suprema.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.exists_const_ge.text: A constant bounding the finitely many rescaling constants $R m$, $m \le N$. Here the lift is the deformation restricted to the fixed carrier plane, and the pullback is the inverse deformation followed by the transverse projection and orthogonal projection onto that plane. This avoids a separate Gram-matrix inverse estimate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.exists_const_ge.summary: Bound finitely many derivative constants at once

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.exists_leading_.text: The initial velocity and frequency-scaled pressure in (5.22) follow from the scaled envelope-amplitude and pressure operator jets on a time slice.
