The weighted derivations are ℓ times restricted word shifts and are total even for negative or zero ℓ. The norm-identification and lifting results require ℓ≥0; the actual envelope radius is positive. They preserve the explicit subspace constraints by construction.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.dF.summary: The radius weighted derivative on forcing families

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.dF_val.text: On underlying forcing families, the forcing derivation is exactly ℓ times the coordinate shift. This relates the abstract derivation to the weighted word norm.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.endpointC.text: Time families equal on the closed interval have equal closed-time norms. The equality does not require their arbitrary values outside that interval to coincide.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.endpointC.summary: Agreement on the interval gives equal time suprema

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.eq_of_der.text: Two derivative towers with the same base and derivative relations coincide. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.eq_of_der.summary: The base field and derivative relations determine the family

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.exactNorm.text: For nonnegative label radius, the abstract exact-order coefficient norm equals the sum of the corresponding wordwise closed-time norms with factor $\ell^m$. This identifies the commutator hypothesis in D.3 with (5.13).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.exactNorm.summary: Read the weighted exact order coefficient norm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.exactNorm.text: The exact-order norm of Lemma D.3 is the weighted word norm (D.1). The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.exactNorm.summary: The abstract exact order norm is the weighted derivative sum

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.exists_sy.text: A jointly smooth periodic field on the slab has a symmetric derivative tower (jets of the sorted word; the paper's remark that label derivatives preserve the constraints). The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.exists_sy.summary: Construct all periodic spatial derivatives in the Hölder space

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.exists_ve.text: The symmetric tower of a smooth divergence-free velocity $v = z_t$ with $z(0) = z(T) = 0$ lies in the space of towers of solenoidal velocities $u_w$ with $\int_0^T u_w = 0$ (the endpoint and divergence constraints are preserved by label derivatives, as the paper notes). The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.exists_ve.summary: The velocity derivative family satisfies both endpoint constraints

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.finiteNor.text: For nonnegative label radius, the abstract solution norm through order n equals the sum of the solution-family word norms weighted by ℓ to their lengths. The family remains in the solenoidal endpoint-constrained space.

For nonnegative label radius, the abstract forcing norm through order n equals the weighted sum of its wordwise closed-time norms. This is the forcing-side identification used in the lifted mean estimate.

The finite norm of Lemma D.3 is the weighted word norm (D.1) (scaling of derivations; TeX 52-58). The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.finiteNor.summary: The abstract finite norm is the weighted derivative sum

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.hSA.text: The coefficient-family space is stable under every coordinate shift. This supplies the invariant domain for the coefficient derivations in D.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.hSA.summary: Coefficient families are closed under label shifts

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.hSE.text: The constrained solenoidal solution-family space is stable under every coordinate shift. Zero total time integral is imposed at every word, so the endpoint condition survives the shift.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.hSE.summary: Endpoint solution families are closed under label shifts

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.hSF.text: The forcing-family space is stable under every coordinate shift. This supplies the target-space derivations that commute with the integrated operators.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.hSF.summary: Forcing families are closed under label shifts

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.hasSD_coe.text: The spatial derivative of coefficient multiplication is the derivative of the coefficient times the field plus the coefficient times the derivative of the field. The hypotheses are actual spatial-derivative relations in the torus Hölder spaces.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.hasSD_coe.summary: Spatial differentiation obeys the coefficient product rule

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.hasSD_neg.text: Negating a field negates its specified torus spatial derivative. This handles the sign convention for the integrated source and vorticity primitive.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.hasSD_pjL.text: The fixed Leray projection commutes with a specified spatial derivative. This preserves the projected equation when label derivatives are taken.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.hasSD_pjL.summary: Spatial differentiation commutes with the Leray projection

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.hasSD_uni.text: Two proposed half-Hölder spatial derivatives of the same field in the same direction agree. This lets an abstract derivative family be identified with the family constructed from the smooth field.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.hasSD_uni.summary: A spatial derivative in the Hölder space is unique

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.leibnizK.text: Applying a weighted coordinate shift to the kinetic action differentiates its coefficient or its solution factor. The subtraction at time zero commutes with that shift, giving the D.3 Leibniz identity on the constrained spaces.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.leibnizK.summary: The weighted kinetic action obeys the Leibniz rule

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.leibnizOm.text: Applying a weighted coordinate shift to the integrated vorticity action differentiates its coefficient or solution factor. Time integration and projection are fixed linear operations, so they preserve the Leibniz identity.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.leibnizOm.summary: The weighted vorticity action obeys the Leibniz rule

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.main_towe.text: Let $T>0$, $Jg(t)=\int_0^tg$, and let smooth unit-periodic $K,\Omega,v,z,g$ satisfy $z_t=v$, $z(0)=z(T)=0$, $\operatorname{div}v=0$ and $\mathbb P(Kv)-\mathbb P(K(0)v(0))-\mathbb PJ(\Omega v)=\mathbb PJg$. Assume the continuous half-Hölder endpoint problem has a unique solution for every source with velocity bound $A$. Write $N_m(f)=\sum_{|\alpha|=m}\ell^m\|\partial^\alpha f\|_{C_tC^{0,1/2}}$. If $\ell,C_0\ge0$, $A\le C_0$, and $C_0\|\mathbb P\|(4N_m(K)+2TN_m(\Omega))\le c_m$ for $1\le m\le n$, Lemma D.3 gives $\sum_{m\le n}N_m(v)\le C_nC_0\|\mathbb P\|T\sum_{m\le n}N_m(g)$. Here $C_n\ge0$ depends on $n$ and the supplied $c_m$. The formal statement also requires bounded, compatible derivative families for the coefficients, fields and time primitives. It assumes Lemma D.3; it does not establish the low-order inverse.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.main_towe.summary: The endpoint estimate lifts while preserving its constraints

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.mem_solen.text: If the base entry of a genuine derivative family is solenoidal, every higher entry is solenoidal as well. The result uses the derivative relations, not permutation symmetry alone.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.mem_solen.summary: Spatial derivatives preserve the solenoidal constraint

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.norm_S_eq.text: Inclusion of a solenoidal half-Hölder field into the ambient half-Hölder space preserves its norm. The constrained space has the inherited norm.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.norm_S_eq.summary: The solenoidal subspace inherits the Hölder norm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.norm_prim.text: On a positive closed interval the primitive norm is at most T times the closed-time norm of its continuous integrand. This is the source of the factor T in the vorticity-action bound.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.norm_prim.summary: Interval length controls the time primitive norm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.phaseOper.text: All coordinate derivative words of the zero vector field vanish. In the endpoint argument this carries the zero initial and terminal displacement identities to every derivative order.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.phaseOper.summary: Every spatial derivative of the zero field vanishes

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.pjL.text:
The Leray projection $P$ of Theorem 4.2 as an endomorphism of $C^{0,1/2}$. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.

Default values: This is the fixed continuous Leray projection followed by inclusion of its solenoidal image into the ambient Hölder space. Its operator norm is carried explicitly in the estimates; no norm-one assertion is smuggled into the definition.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.pjL.summary: Leray projection in the spatial Hölder space

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.primC.text:
The time primitive restricted to the parent interval. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.

The integral ends at the clamped time and therefore only uses the physical interval when T≥0. Integral notation remains total outside integrability hypotheses, but continuity supplies integrability in all analytic uses. The operation is used as a continuous primitive on the slab, not as a globally smooth function across the clamp endpoints.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.primC.summary: The time primitive restricted to the parent interval

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.primC_add.text: For continuous functions on a nonnegative closed interval, the clamped time primitive distributes over addition. Continuity supplies the integrability needed for linearity of the integral.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.primC_add.summary: The time primitive distributes over addition

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.primC_con.text: On a positive time interval, the primitive of a continuous family is continuous. Only continuity on the closed physical interval is required for the tower construction.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.primC_eq.text: At an allowed time, the clamped primitive equals the ordinary integral from zero to that time. Thus clamping changes only the auxiliary values outside the interval.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.primC_eq.summary: The clamped primitive agrees with ordinary integration inside

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.primC_smu.text: Constant scalar multiplication commutes with the clamped time primitive. This is the scalar linearity needed to construct the bilinear vorticity action.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.primC_smu.summary: The time primitive respects constant scaling

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.shift.text:
Add one label derivative to a family. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.

This is a total linear reindexing by prepending a coordinate letter. It is meaningful for arbitrary families and is not by itself a differentiation theorem. Preservation of constraints and commutation are established separately from symmetry and the derivative-family hypotheses.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.shiftOn.text:
The derivation $\partial_i$ on a submodule of towers that is closed under it. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.

Default values: A proof that every coordinate shift preserves the submodule is an explicit argument. The definition restricts that already-defined shift and does not infer closure or actual differentiability from the submodule alone.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.shiftOn.summary: Restrict a derivative shift to an invariant subspace

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.shiftOn_c.text: Weighted shifts commute on any shift-stable subspace of symmetric families. The proof uses permutation symmetry and multiplication of the common scalar weight, so it does not require the entries to be realized as derivatives first.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.shift_mem.text: Prepending one coordinate direction preserves permutation symmetry and continuity in time. Thus the shift remains inside the space of symmetric families, without yet asserting that its entries are derivatives of a field.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.shift_mem.summary: A label shift preserves the continuous derivative family

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.shift_mem.text: A shift of a solenoidal family whose every word has zero total time integral still has both properties. This expresses preservation of the mean endpoint and divergence constraints under differentiation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.shift_mem.summary: A label shift preserves the terminal displacement constraint

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.srt.text:
Put coordinate derivative letters in increasing order. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.

Merge sort returns a canonical ordering of the finite coordinate list. It preserves multiplicities, including repeated directions and the empty word. The sorting operation is combinatorial; equality of mixed derivatives uses the separate smoothness results.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.srt.summary: Put coordinate derivative letters in increasing order

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.srt_eq_of.text: Two permutation-equivalent coordinate words have identical sorted representatives. This is the combinatorial equality used when constructing a symmetric derivative family.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.srt_eq_of.summary: Permuted derivative words have the same sorted form

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.srt_perm.text: Sorting a coordinate word preserves its letters with multiplicity. This supplies a canonical representative of the derivative multi-index.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.srt_perm.summary: Sorting preserves the multiset of derivative directions

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.tower.text:
Permutation-invariant towers, continuous in time on $[0,T]$. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.

Default values: The subspace records permutation symmetry and continuity in time for every word. It does not require actual spatial-derivative relations. When $T<0$ the continuity domain is empty; applications explicitly use $T\ge0$ or $T>0$, and the separate derivative-tower conditions supply the missing derivative interpretation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.tower.summary: Symmetric derivative families continuous in time

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.tower_lif.text: Apply the cited derivative estimate to endpoint families. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.tower_lif.summary: Apply the cited derivative estimate to endpoint families

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.word_appl.text: A word of shift maps evaluates the family at the reversed shift word followed by the original word. Permutation symmetry later removes the reversal when passing to the derivative norm.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.word_appl.summary: A sequence of shifts reads the corresponding derivative

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.word_norm.text: For a symmetric continuous family and nonnegative terminal time, the empty-word seminorm after a word of shifts equals the closed-time norm of that word's entry. This is the identification between D.3's operator notation and the concrete derivative family.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.word_norm.summary: Read the supremum after a sequence of derivative shifts

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.zeroSemi.text:
The zero-order seminorm $\sup_{t \in [0,T]} \|u_\varnothing(t)\|$, the supremum of the empty-word entry, on a submodule of towers. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.

Default values: The supplied inclusion in the continuous-family space and $T\ge0$ make the closed-time supremum well behaved. It measures only the empty word and can vanish for a nonzero whole family. Higher-order estimates arise by shifting the family before this seminorm is applied.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.zeroSemi.summary: The undifferentiated supremum seminorm of a family

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.zeroSemi_.text: The zero-order seminorm of a family is exactly the supremum-in-time norm of its empty-word entry. Higher words are invisible until the shifts are applied.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.zero_orde.text: The first clause of the supplied Theorem 4.2 gives existence, uniqueness and a bound for the integrated endpoint problem. Applying it to the residual of any constrained family and using uniqueness yields the zero-order inverse estimate for that family, which is the hypothesis required by D.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.zero_orde.summary: The endpoint theorem bounds the undifferentiated velocity family

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.adjL.text:
Matrix transpose $A\mapsto A^T$ on linear maps of $\mathbb R^3$ as a fixed linear operator. The coefficient bookkeeping separates constants depending on the derivative order from powers of the parent bound. The numbers $\Omega$ and $\Theta$ in the two-parameter bound $\Omega^a\Theta^i$ are bounds, not the vorticity coefficient $\Omega$ of the mean equation.

These fixed continuous linear or bilinear maps are defined everywhere on the finite-dimensional coefficient spaces and use no inverse or choice. They remain meaningful at zero inputs. The later estimates include their actual operator norms; this packaging does not assume every such norm is one.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.adjL.summary: Matrix transpose as a fixed linear operator

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.adjL_apply.text: Evaluation of the fixed continuous linear adjoint map gives the transpose of the matrix coefficient. Its operator norm is then an order-independent factor in the relay budget.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.adjL_apply.summary: Recover matrix transpose from its operator form

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.appL.text:
The application $(A, v) \mapsto A v$ of a field of linear maps to a field. The coefficient bookkeeping separates constants depending on the derivative order from powers of the parent bound. The numbers $\Omega$ and $\Theta$ in the monotone-weight bound are bounds, not the vorticity coefficient $\Omega$ of the mean equation.

Default values: These fixed continuous linear or bilinear maps are defined on all of the finite-dimensional coefficient spaces and use no inverse or choice. They remain meaningful at zero inputs. The later estimates include their actual operator norms; this packaging does not assume every such norm is one.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.appL.summary: Apply a continuous linear operator to a vector

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.average_transve.text: The transverse source $f_p + f_p^S$ of (5.27), (5.28) has zero phase mean when the means $B_i$, $2 \le i \le p$, are phase independent. The inactive set consists of times before activation or labels outside the periodized envelope support. The induction concerns oscillatory profiles and their sources; the means may already be nonzero before activation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.average_transve.summary: The transverse source has zero phase average

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.boundedWeightSe.text: For phase-independent inverse deformation and nonvanishing covector, the actual curl completion of a zero-mean profile has the stated weighted estimate. The scalar time multiplier is only required to be bounded on the measured set; positive frequency and label/phase scales are separate assumptions.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.boundedWeightSe.summary: Transfer the divergence correction estimate to profile seminorms

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.boundedWeightSe.text: If a twisted residual profile agrees on the measured time set with the explicit relay formula, D.1 and the coefficient budget bound its weighted seminorm by inverse frequency times the order n+1 seminorms of velocity and forcing. A bounded scalar time multiplier is permitted; the application uses the inverse central amplitude weight.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.boundedWeightSe.summary: Transfer the linear residual estimate to profile seminorms

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.centerWaveOn_mo.text: The conditions $(5.5)$ on the centre wave only weaken when the scale $D$ is increased. This transfers the supplied coefficient estimates to the derivative conventions used by the seed construction. Increasing constants or the parent scale changes no field and imposes no new equation on the parent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.centerWaveOn_mo.summary: Increasing the parent scale weakens the central wave assumptions

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.coefficientNorm.text: Converse of the statement that a finite coefficient norm gives a finite lifted norm: if the lift $(t, a, s) \mapsto c(t, a)$ has finite norm (D.1) for some $\ell > 0$ and $h$, the coefficient $c$ has a finite norm. The mean is measured in unweighted label norms over the entire time interval. The comparison with half-Hölder norms is where one derivative of the source is lost.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.coefficientNorm.summary: Finite lifted norms imply finite coefficient norms

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.coefficientNorm.text: (D.6) bounds every coefficient norm: all jet suprema of all orders are finite. Positive-order coefficient derivatives retain a factor of the envelope radius. The supremum-to-Hölder comparison uses half of that gain, leaving its square root to absorb the zero-order endpoint constant A.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.coefficientNorm.summary: Polynomial derivative estimates make coefficient norms finite

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.coefficientNorm.text: The finite norm (D.1) of a coefficient is bounded by the (5.8)-type sums of spatial suprema: if $\sum_{j \le n} \ell^j \|\partial^j c(t)\|_\infty \le S$ for every $t$ (and $S \ge 0$), then $\|c\|_{[n]} \le \big(\sum_{m \le n} \#\{\text{words of order } m\}\big) \cdot S$. Positive-order coefficient derivatives retain a factor of the envelope radius. The supremum-to-Hölder comparison uses half of that gain, leaving its square root to absorb the zero-order endpoint constant $A$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.coefficientNorm.summary: Spatial suprema bound the sum of coordinate derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.coefficientNorm.text: The finite coefficient norm is nonnegative. The mean is measured in unweighted label norms over the entire time interval. The comparison with half-Hölder norms is where one derivative of the source is lost.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.coefficientNorm.summary: The finite coefficient norm is nonnegative

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.coefficientPowe.text: Operator-norm jet bounds $\|D^m c(t,x)\| \le K_m \mathsf D^{a(m+1)}$ of a field smooth in the label give the power bound (D.6) in the form of Appendix D, with constants $\#\{\text{words of order } m\} \cdot K_m$. This transfers the supplied coefficient estimates to the derivative conventions used by the seed construction. Increasing constants or the parent scale changes no field and imposes no new equation on the parent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.coefficientPowe.summary: Full derivative bounds give coordinate coefficient estimates

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.coefficientPowe.text: (D.6) from operator-norm jet bounds with arbitrary (possibly negative) constants. The two coefficients are K=FᵀF and Ω=Fᵀ(Mᵀ−M)F, with F the deformation. Their derivative bounds are obtained by finite products of the parent coefficients before choosing the small label radius.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.coefficientPowe.summary: Replace derivative constants by nonnegative upper bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.contDiffOn_seed.text: Smooth strain and covector with no covector zero make both the seed operator −(Id−2Pκ)M and the projection Id−Pκ jointly smooth on the given set. This supplies regularity for the parameter-dependent linear seed ODE.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.contDiffOn_seed.summary: Nonzero transported covectors give smooth seed coefficients

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.contDiff_phaseP.text: The zero-mean phase primitive of a jointly smooth family is jointly smooth. This gives the regularity needed to commute parameter derivative words with the primitive in the relay calculation.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.contDiff_slice.text: A velocity slice of a field smooth on the slab is smooth. Bernstein bounds the truncated parent derivatives, and the differentiated flow equation controls the deformation. Lemma D.2 supplies coefficient products, inverses and the small-radius absorption; the final absolute exponent need not be sharp.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.contDiff_slice.summary: Smooth parent velocities have smooth spatial slices

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.contDiff_slice'.text: A slice of a field that is jointly smooth on the slab is smooth. The completion and relay gain one inverse carrier frequency and cost one spatial derivative. The pressure and vector-potential formulas eliminate the dangerous fast derivative without differentiating the mean or the forcing in time.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.contDiff_slice'.summary: Joint smoothness gives smooth coefficient slices

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.continuousOn_in.text: Continuity of the pointwise inverse of a coframe family given by a left inverse. The first label derivatives of the parent coefficients make the fixed-plane ODE a small perturbation of its value at the origin. A common envelope exponent controls both amplitude comparison and positivity of the physical coupling.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.continuousOn_in.summary: A given left inverse gives continuous coframe inverses

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.crossL.text:
The cross product $\kappa \mapsto \kappa \times \cdot$ as a continuous linear map of $\kappa$. The coefficient bookkeeping separates constants depending on the derivative order from powers of the parent bound. The numbers $\Omega$ and $\Theta$ in the monotone-weight bound are bounds, not the vorticity coefficient $\Omega$ of the mean equation.

Default values: These fixed continuous linear or bilinear maps are defined on all of the finite-dimensional coefficient spaces and use no inverse or choice. They remain meaningful at zero inputs. The later estimates include their actual operator norms; this packaging does not assume every such norm is one.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.crossL.summary: The cross product as a linear map of its first factor

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.crossL_apply.text: Evaluation of the packaged continuous linear map gives the ordinary cross product κ×v. This identifies the fixed bilinear operation whose norm is included in the relay coefficient bound.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.crossL_apply.summary: Recover the cross product from its operator form

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.curlCorrection_.text: The divergence correction $C[V] = \mathbf d \times Q[V]$ of a profile vanishing on the inactive region vanishes there (it centres its input and acts pointwise in time and label). The inactive set consists of times before activation or labels outside the periodized envelope support. The induction concerns oscillatory profiles and their sources; the means may already be nonzero before activation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.curlCorrection_.summary: Taking the divergence correction preserves the inactive region

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.deriv_leadingPr.text: The phase derivative of $\mathsf p[A_1]$, copying a private lemma of the earlier library construction for a seed given by its defining conditions. The unswitched seed is initially available only on the active slab. A smooth extension supplies global representatives, and only their equality with the unswitched leading profiles on that slab enters Lemma 5.5.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.deriv_leadingPr.summary: Differentiate the explicit leading pressure in the phase

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.envelopeSupport.text: The support $\operatorname{supp} g$ of the periodized envelope is invariant under lattice translations. The inactive set consists of times before activation or labels outside the periodized envelope support. The induction concerns oscillatory profiles and their sources; the means may already be nonzero before activation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.envelopeSupport.summary: Envelope support is invariant under lattice translations

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.envelopeWrapped.text:
This packages the twisted extension of g(a)z(s)u(t,a) as a smooth profile of phase period one. Smoothness of both factors, phase periodicity and the fitting-radius hypothesis are supplied explicitly.

Positive radius and strict fitting inside the centered cell are explicit, as are global smoothness of the extension and periodicity of the phase function. The choice of extension before activation is auxiliary; only its stated active-slab agreement is later used. The constructor does not identify every off-cell value with the raw compact profile.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.envelopeWrapped.summary: Extend an amplitude times its phase profile periodically

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.envelopeWrapped.text: The preceding pointwise zero phase-mean identity gives zero for the bundled phase-average operator on the wrapped vector profile. This makes it admissible for the transverse solve and primitive estimates.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.envelopeWrapped.summary: The wrapped velocity has zero phase average

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.envelopeWrapped.text: Evaluation of the packaged profile equals the chosen twisted periodization on the slab. This is an equality of representatives there, with no additional estimate or global equality outside the recorded time slab.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.envelopeWrapped.summary: Read the localized twisted profile at a point

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.envelopeWrapped.text: A zero-mean periodic phase factor makes the phase mean of the localized twisted product vanish. Translation of the phase caused by the lattice extension does not change that mean.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.envelopeWrapped.summary: The wrapped profile preserves zero phase mean

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.envelopeWrapped.text: If the slow field and the periodic phase function are smooth and the positive envelope fits strictly inside the centered cell, their localized twisted periodization is smooth on the profile slab. The compact label support removes boundary discrepancies between neighboring cells.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.envelopeWrapped.summary: The localized twisted extension is jointly smooth

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.eq_of_gradient_.text: Two smooth periodic functions with the same gradient and the same mean over the label cell coincide. Endpoint uniqueness fixes the mean velocity. Equality of pressure gradients fixes pressure only after the two pressures have the same cell mean; the pressure normalization cannot be dropped from the full pair uniqueness claim.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.eq_of_gradient_.summary: Equal gradients and means determine the scalar function

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_A_bound.text: Fix a real prefactor $C$, a nonnegative integer $p$, real sequences $C_K,C_\Omega$, and nonnegative integers $a_K,a_\Omega$. There exists an integer $C_A\ge0$, chosen before $\mathsf D\ge2$ and the four nonnegative coefficient bounds, such that $C(2\mathsf D+K_0+K_1+\Omega_0+\Omega_1)^p\le\mathsf D^{C_A}$ whenever $K_0\le C_K(0)\mathsf D^{a_K}$, $K_1\le3C_K(1)\mathsf D^{2a_K}$, $\Omega_0\le C_\Omega(0)\mathsf D^{a_\Omega}$ and $\Omega_1\le3C_\Omega(1)\mathsf D^{2a_\Omega}$. This is an arithmetic implication. It does not identify these numbers with coefficient norms or prove that the left side bounds an endpoint inverse.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_A_bound.summary: Low-order coefficient bounds control the endpoint inverse constant

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_KOmega_p.text: Let $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$, $\lambda\ge1$. Let $U$ be smooth, odd, solenoidal and unit-periodic, with flow $X$ and smooth periodic pressure $p_U$. Require Fourier radii $2\mathsf D$ for $U$ and $4\mathsf D$ for the odd residual $R_U=U_t+U\cdot\nabla U+\nabla p_U$, $\|DU\|_\infty,\|DX\|_\infty,\|DX^{-1}\|_\infty\le\mathsf D$, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$, and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$ as quadratic forms. Write $F=D_aX$, $G=F^{-1}$, $M=(DU)\circ X$, $K=F^TF$ and $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$. Assuming Proposition 5.1 and Lemma D.2, there are nonnegative sequences $C_K(m),C_\Omega(m)$ and nonnegative integers $a_K,a_\Omega$, fixed before the parent, such that $\|D_a^mK\|_\infty\le C_K(m)\mathsf D^{a_K(m+1)}$ and $\|D_a^m\Omega\|_\infty\le C_\Omega(m)\mathsf D^{a_\Omega(m+1)}$ for every $m\ge0$. Spatial derivatives are measured in multilinear operator norm. No Poisson equation or mean normalization of $p_U$ is imposed.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_KOmega_p.summary: Products of deformation coefficients control the endpoint system

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_common_e.text: One absolute envelope exponent enforces both the fixed-coordinate Duhamel perturbation budget and the physical coupling budget. The first label derivatives of the parent coefficients make the fixed-plane ODE a small perturbation of its value at the origin. A common envelope exponent controls both amplitude comparison and positivity of the physical coupling.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_common_e.summary: Choose an envelope satisfying both comparison requirements

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_halfHold.text: A smooth periodic field on the slab is realized, at each time of $[0,T]$, by an element of $C^{0,1/2}(\mathbb T^3; E)$ (the empty word of the generic slab jets). The supplied Theorem 4.2 solves the smooth endpoint problem for a phase-independent source. Its velocity and pressure are transported to twisted profiles satisfying the mean equation, with zero displacement at both endpoints.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_halfHold.summary: Realize each periodic slice in the Hölder space

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_isSeed.text: Existence of the seed of §5.1: over a parent with launch data and a central seed (5.5), the solution $\mathbf a$ of the seed equation (3.2) on $[t_0,T]$ with the initial value (5.4) $\mathbf a(t_0,a) = (\mathrm{Id} - P_{\kappa(t_0,a)}) \mathbf a(t_0,0)$ exists, is jointly smooth, transverse to $\kappa$, and equals the central seed at the origin. Existence and smoothness here come from the linear seed ODE with projected initial data. No small-envelope estimate or conclusion of Lemma 5.3 is assumed for this existence step.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_isSeed.summary: Solve the seed equation from its projected initial amplitude

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_launch.text: Every parent with $\lambda \ge 1$ admits a launch ($t_0 = 0$, $k_* \ne 0$ with $|\kappa(0,0)| = \lambda$). The mean equation itself is independent of the carrier. This auxiliary launch allows the statement of Proposition 5.1, which is packaged with launch data, to be used for the mean coefficients.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_launch.summary: Supply auxiliary launch data for any parent

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_leading_.text: A smooth extension of the active seed gives smooth twisted velocity and pressure profiles on the entire slab. On the active interval they agree with A₁ and its prescribed pressure, and their phase means are zero. Their values before activation are auxiliary representatives and are not claimed to be the physical switched wave.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_leading_.summary: Represent the unswitched wave by smooth full interval profiles

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_meanCoef.text: Finite bounds for $K$, $\Omega$ of (4.1) and their first label derivatives on $[0,T] \times \mathbb R^3$ (continuity on the compact $[0,T] \times [-1/2,1/2]^3$ and periodicity). Their values do not enter: Theorem 4.2 is used here only for existence. The supplied Theorem 4.2 solves the smooth endpoint problem for a phase-independent source. Its velocity and pressure are transported to twisted profiles satisfying the mean equation, with zero displacement at both endpoints.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_meanCoef.summary: Compactness bounds the mean coefficients and first derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_monotone.text: A nondecreasing coordinate word of length $m$ is the word of a monotone map $\{0,\dots,m-1\} \to \{0,1,2\}$. This transfers the supplied coefficient estimates to the derivative conventions used by the seed construction. Increasing constants or the parent scale changes no field and imposes no new equation on the parent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_monotone.summary: A sorted word determines a monotone coordinate sequence

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_seedOn_o.text: With the Section 5 parent, launch, central stability and first coefficient jets, one absolute radius exponent gives a library seed carrying quantitative near-origin bounds. The seed is built by the fixed-coordinate Duhamel argument, and the radius threshold controls both the ODE perturbation and the physical coupling.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_seedOn_o.summary: Construct a seed with the required near origin bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_smoothMe.text: A solution $(B, \bar q)$ of (5.11) is a smooth mean solution in label coordinates (the phase-0 slices; $B = D_aX\, v$, $v = z_t$, $\mathrm{div}_a v = 0$, $B_t + MB + (D_aX)^{-T}\nabla_a \bar q = \bar f$), for the parent data of Theorem 4.2 built from the coefficients of the flow. Endpoint uniqueness fixes the mean velocity. Equality of pressure gradients fixes pressure only after the two pressures have the same cell mean; the pressure normalization cannot be dropped from the full pair uniqueness claim.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_smoothMe.summary: Translate a profile solution into a smooth endpoint solution

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_smooth_h.text: A smooth periodic field on the slab is realized by a curve in $C^{0,1/2}$ that is smooth in time (the empty word of the generic slab jets; the smooth variant of the library's half-Hölder curve construction). Endpoint uniqueness fixes the mean velocity. Equality of pressure gradients fixes pressure only after the two pressures have the same cell mean; the pressure normalization cannot be dropped from the full pair uniqueness claim.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_smooth_h.summary: Realize a smooth periodic field as a smooth Hölder curve

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_sortedWo.text: Symmetry of the derivatives of a smooth function: every coordinate component $D^m f(x)(e_{\beta 0}, \dots, e_{\beta (m-1)})$ is the value of one nondecreasing coordinate word of length $m$ (the sorted word of the letters of $\beta$). This transfers the supplied coefficient estimates to the derivative conventions used by the seed construction. Increasing constants or the parent scale changes no field and imposes no new equation on the parent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_sortedWo.summary: Smoothness allows coordinate derivatives to be sorted

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_velocity.text: Assuming Bernstein’s inequality in Lemma B.1, a nonnegative sequence $V_n$ can be chosen before the field and $\mathsf D$. Let $g$ be a continuous field on $\mathbb T^3=\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3$ whose periodic lift is smooth, whose Fourier coefficients vanish for $|k|>4\mathsf D$, and whose gradient has operator norm at most $\mathsf D\ge1$. Then $\|D^kg\|_\infty\le V_n\mathsf D^k$ whenever $1\le k\le n$. The statement controls positive spatial derivatives and makes no estimate for $g$ itself. Its frequency radius $4\mathsf D$ includes the $2\mathsf D$ velocity band used in Proposition 5.1.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.exists_velocity.summary: Frequency support controls every positive velocity derivative

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.expansionPressu.text: The expansion pressure to order $P$ is unchanged by truncating at $P$. This is an exact finite algebraic identity. The final curl completion $C_{P+1}$ is retained while the top velocity and mean profiles are set to zero; no assertion about convergence of an infinite expansion is involved.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.expansionPressu.summary: Removing unused levels leaves the pressure unchanged

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.expansion_trunc.text: The expansion to order $P$ is unchanged by truncating at $P$. This is an exact finite algebraic identity. The final curl completion $C_{P+1}$ is retained while the top velocity and mean profiles are set to zero; no assertion about convergence of an infinite expansion is involved.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.expansion_trunc.summary: Removing unused levels leaves the velocity unchanged

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.halfHolder_lift.text: The lift of an element of a space of torus fields is periodic. The supplied Theorem 4.2 solves the smooth endpoint problem for a phase-independent source. Its velocity and pressure are transported to twisted profiles satisfying the mean equation, with zero displacement at both endpoints.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.halfHolder_lift.summary: Lifting a torus field gives a periodic function

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.hasDerivWithinA.text: The time derivative of the leading oscillation $A_1$ of a seed on $[t_0,T]$: by the seed equation (3.2), $\partial_tA_1 = -MA_1 - \partial_s\mathsf p[A_1] \kappa$. This is the step of the leading homogeneous equation (3.4), kept as a derivative statement. The seed equation cancels the homogeneous part of the time derivative. The remaining derivative of the time cutoff is the activation error retained in the exact finite-expansion identity.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.hasDerivWithinA.summary: Differentiate the leading oscillation using the seed equation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.holderFieldNorm.text: The finite Hölder norm is nonnegative. The mean is measured in unweighted label norms over the entire time interval. The comparison with half-Hölder norms is where one derivative of the source is lost.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.inactiveVP.text:
The inactive region $\{t < t_0\} \cup \{a \notin \operatorname{supp} g\}$ of the slab, as a submodule of profiles. The inactive set consists of times before activation or labels outside the periodized envelope support. The induction concerns oscillatory profiles and their sources; the means may already be nonzero before activation.

Default values: This is the submodule of profiles vanishing on the indicated open inactive region. Its definition does not assert that a given profile belongs to it. In particular, the means are not automatically members; the support induction proves membership only for the relevant oscillatory profiles.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.inactiveVP.summary: Profiles vanishing before activation and outside the envelope

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.innerL.text:
The inner product $(u, v) \mapsto \langle u, v\rangle$ on $\mathbb R^3$ as a continuous bilinear map. The coefficient bookkeeping separates constants depending on the derivative order from powers of the parent bound. The numbers $\Omega$ and $\Theta$ in the monotone-weight bound are bounds, not the vorticity coefficient $\Omega$ of the mean equation.

Default values: These fixed continuous linear or bilinear maps are defined on all of the finite-dimensional coefficient spaces and use no inverse or choice. They remain meaningful at zero inputs. The later estimates include their actual operator norms; this packaging does not assume every such norm is one.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.innerL.summary: Inner product as a fixed bilinear operator

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.innerL_apply.text: Evaluation of the fixed bilinear map gives the Euclidean inner product. It is used for the contractions in the normalized pressure and vector-potential coefficients.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.innerL_apply.summary: Recover the inner product from its bilinear form

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.integratedSolut.text: A smooth mean solution solves the integrated endpoint problem (the paper's remark that (4.9) is (4.11) integrated once in time): for the curves $K$, $\Omega$ of (4.1) in $C^{0,1/2}$ (smooth in time, with lifts given by the parent's kinetic and vorticity coefficients) and the integrated source of a smooth force, the label velocity of a smooth solution of the mean equation is the velocity of a solution of the integrated endpoint system. This copies the corresponding library statement, with its parent data replaced by the four fields it uses. Multiplying the smooth mean equation by the transpose deformation and integrating in time gives the equation used by Theorem 4.2. The Leray projection removes the label pressure gradient; endpoint displacement supplies the zero total velocity integral.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.integratedSolut.summary: Integrating a smooth mean solution gives the endpoint system

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.inv_sqrt_mul_se.text: Half a radius factor remains after Hölder conversion. Positive-order coefficient derivatives retain a factor of the envelope radius. The supremum-to-Hölder comparison uses half of that gain, leaving its square root to absorb the zero-order endpoint constant A.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.inv_sqrt_mul_se.summary: Half a radius factor remains after Hölder conversion

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.isClosed_envelo.text: The periodic envelope has closed support. The inactive set consists of times before activation or labels outside the periodized envelope support. The induction concerns oscillatory profiles and their sources; the means may already be nonzero before activation.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.isExpansion_ide.text: The identities of Proposition 5.4 for every expansion of depth $P \ge 2$, given the leading switch $(\partial_t+M)V_1 + \kappa\partial_s\mathsf p_1 = \tilde\chi'A_1$ (from (3.4) and (3.7)). Each conclusion is a clause of the identities in the formal statement of Proposition 5.4, in the same order, and the proof follows the steps of the paper's proof. This is an exact finite algebraic identity. The final curl completion $C_{P+1}$ is retained while the top velocity and mean profiles are set to zero; no assertion about convergence of an infinite expansion is involved.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.isExpansion_ide.summary: The finite expansion satisfies its exact residual identity

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.jetValues_nonne.text: Every derivative size in the supremum is nonnegative. The mean is measured in unweighted label norms over the entire time interval. The comparison with half-Hölder norms is where one derivative of the source is lost.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.jetValues_nonne.summary: Every derivative size in the supremum is nonnegative

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.kinetic_derivat.text: Along a smooth mean solution, the time derivative of Kv is expressed using the smooth momentum equation and the deformation identities. This is the differential identity subsequently integrated and projected to obtain the endpoint equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.kinetic_derivat.summary: Differentiate kinetic momentum along a mean solution

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.labelDirection_.text: The unit label directions of Appendix D are the coordinate directions. This transfers the supplied coefficient estimates to the derivative conventions used by the seed construction. Increasing constants or the parent scale changes no field and imposes no new equation on the parent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.labelDirection_.summary: Unit label derivatives use the coordinate directions

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.labelLipschitz_.text: First-order power bounds for deformation, inverse deformation, strain, normalized covector and projection give uniform label differences for the coframe and generator coefficients. These bounds are supplied by the power clause of Proposition 5.1, not obtained by calling the old library's global coefficient estimate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.labelLipschitz_.summary: The parent derivative estimate gives local coefficient comparison

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.labelWord_eq_it.text: The value of a coordinate word is the iterated derivative on the coordinate directions of its letters. This transfers the supplied coefficient estimates to the derivative conventions used by the seed construction. Increasing constants or the parent scale changes no field and imposes no new equation on the parent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.labelWord_eq_it.summary: A coordinate word evaluates the iterated Fréchet derivative

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.leadingSwitch.text: Assume a seed solving the transverse homogeneous equation, a smooth time cutoff and an expansion whose first profiles equal the cutoff times that seed wave and its pressure. The switched leading wave satisfies $V_{1,t}+MV_1+\kappa\partial_s\mathsf p_1=\widetilde\chi^{\prime}A_1$. This follows by differentiating the cutoff times the homogeneous leading solution, including times before activation. It is the first identity in the proof of Proposition 5.4; the activation contribution of the curl correction is added separately in the full residual. The phase width is restricted to $0<h\le1$, and the switched identity holds on all of $[0,T]$, including before activation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.leadingSwitch.summary: Differentiating the time cutoff produces the leading forcing

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.leading_homogen.text: The leading equation (3.4) for a seed given by its defining conditions, copying the corresponding lemmas of the earlier library construction and reading only the seed equation (3.2) and the transversality in the paper's seed conditions: on $[t_0,T]$, $\partial_tA_1 + MA_1 + \partial_s\mathsf p[A_1] \kappa = 0$, $\kappa\cdot A_1 = 0$, and $A_1$, $\mathsf p[A_1]$ have zero phase mean. The unswitched seed is initially available only on the active slab. A smooth extension supplies global representatives, and only their equality with the unswitched leading profiles on that slab enters Lemma 5.5.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.leading_homogen.summary: The leading oscillation solves the homogeneous transverse equation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.leafBounds_of_h.text: The jets (D.6) of the coefficients of Proposition 5.1 (assumed, with the absolute exponent $C_0$) give the library form of the seven coefficient jet bounds at the scale $D^{C_0}$, with constants independent of the data: $K_n D^{C_0 (n+1)} \le \max(K_n,0) (D^{C_0})^e$ for every $e \ge n+1$ since $D \ge 1$. This transfers the supplied coefficient estimates to the derivative conventions used by the seed construction. Increasing constants or the parent scale changes no field and imposes no new equation on the parent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.leafBounds_of_h.summary: The parent proposition supplies the seed coefficient estimates

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.lemma55_main.text: Assuming Proposition 5.1 and Lemma D.1, the formal implication proves the following. Let the parent be smooth, odd, unit-periodic and solenoidal, with smooth periodic pressure on $0<T\le1$, with bands $2\mathsf D$ for velocity and $4\mathsf D$ for its odd residual, gradient and both deformation bounds $\mathsf D\ge2$, residual bound $\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. Put $M=DU\circ X$, $\kappa=DX^{-T}k_*$, $\lambda=|\kappa(t_0,0)|\ge1$ and $0\le t_0<T$. The nonzero central seed solves $\mathbf a_t=-(I-2P_\kappa)M\mathbf a$, is transverse, has $\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a\ge\mathsf D^{-1}|\kappa||\mathbf a|$, and satisfies $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$. Every transverse homogeneous solution $\mathbf b$ obeys $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$. For small fixed $\ell_*$ and $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, transverse $V$ satisfies $\|C[V]\|_{[n],\gamma}\le C_n\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-1}\|V\|_{[n+1],\gamma}$. If $V_t+MV+\kappa\mathsf p_s=f$, the same factor bounds $(\partial_t+M)C[V]+\mathbf d\mathsf p$ by the sum of the next-order norms of $V,f$. The profiles are smooth and $V,f$ have zero phase mean on all $[0,T]$; transversality, the equation and pressure normalization concern $[t_0,T]$. Smooth representatives of the homogeneous leading wave also exist. Thus full-interval assumptions accompany broader pressure and amplitude hypotheses.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.lemma55_main.summary: Derive both inverse-frequency bounds from coefficient control

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.levelSource_tru.text: The level source of order $p \ge 2$ is unchanged by truncation. This is an exact finite algebraic identity. The final curl completion $C_{P+1}$ is retained while the top velocity and mean profiles are set to zero; no assertion about convergence of an infinite expansion is involved.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.levelSource_tru.summary: Removing unused levels leaves the preliminary source unchanged

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.mFourierCoeff_c.text: Fourier coefficients commute with complex-linear maps. This copies a private lemma of the earlier library construction, for a map into $\mathbb C$ from the complex Euclidean space, with the same proof. This transfers the supplied coefficient estimates to the derivative conventions used by the seed construction. Increasing constants or the parent scale changes no field and imposes no new equation on the parent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.mFourierCoeff_c.summary: Fourier coefficients commute with complex linear evaluation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanHsharp_le_o.text: The coercivity (5.2) of the parent of §5.1 gives the hypothesis $H^\# \le \mathrm{Id}$ of Theorem 4.2, by (4.3) along each trajectory $t \mapsto X(t,a)$. The coercivity assumption on the parent pressure and residual is transported along the flow to the quadratic-form hypothesis of Theorem 4.2. This is the bridge that permits the endpoint inverse over the Section 5 parent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanHsharp_le_o.summary: Parent pressure coercivity gives the endpoint curvature bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanInt_slice_s.text: A jointly smooth field on the slab is smooth in the label at each time of $[0,T]$. This copies a private lemma of the earlier library construction. Multiplying the smooth mean equation by the transpose deformation and integrating in time gives the equation used by Theorem 4.2. The Leray projection removes the label pressure gradient; endpoint displacement supplies the zero total velocity integral.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanInt_slice_s.summary: A smooth mean field has smooth spatial slices

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanInt_slice_t.text: A jointly smooth field on the slab is smooth in time at each label. This copies a private lemma of the earlier library construction. Multiplying the smooth mean equation by the transpose deformation and integrating in time gives the equation used by Theorem 4.2. The Leray projection removes the label pressure gradient; endpoint displacement supplies the zero total velocity integral.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanInt_slice_t.summary: A smooth mean field has smooth time slices

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanKinetic_smo.text: Joint smoothness of the kinetic coefficient $K = (D_aX)^T D_aX$ of (4.1). The supplied Theorem 4.2 solves the smooth endpoint problem for a phase-independent source. Its velocity and pressure are transported to twisted profiles satisfying the mean equation, with zero displacement at both endpoints.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanKinetic_smo.summary: The kinetic coefficient is jointly smooth

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanParentFlow_.text: The selected parent satisfies the endpoint flow assumptions. The coercivity assumption on the parent pressure and residual is transported along the flow to the quadratic-form hypothesis of Theorem 4.2. This is the bridge that permits the endpoint inverse over the Section 5 parent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanParentFlow_.summary: The selected parent satisfies the endpoint flow assumptions

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanProfile_per.text: A phase-independent twisted profile is periodic in the label at fixed phase. The supplied Theorem 4.2 solves the smooth endpoint problem for a phase-independent source. Its velocity and pressure are transported to twisted profiles satisfying the mean equation, with zero displacement at both endpoints.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanProfile_per.summary: A phase independent twisted profile is spatially periodic

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanSlice_contD.text: A jointly smooth field on the slab is smooth in the label at each time of $[0,T]$. The supplied Theorem 4.2 solves the smooth endpoint problem for a phase-independent source. Its velocity and pressure are transported to twisted profiles satisfying the mean equation, with zero displacement at both endpoints.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanSlice_contD.summary: A smooth slab field has smooth label slices

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanSolvable_of.text:
On $[0,T]	imes\mathbb T^3$, $0<T\le1$, let $U,p_U$ be smooth, $U$ odd and solenoidal, $X$ its flow, and $R_U=U_t+U\cdot
abla U+
abla p_U$ odd. Assume $\mathsf D\ge2,\lambda\ge1$, Fourier radii $2\mathsf D,4\mathsf D$ for $U,R_U$, $\|
abla U\|_\infty,\|DX\|_\infty,\|DX^{-1}\|_\infty\le\mathsf D$, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. Assume Theorem 4.2, the endpoint solvability theorem. For every smooth periodic phase-independent forcing $f(t,a)$, the formal statement supplies smooth phase-independent $B,q$ satisfying $B_t+MB+\mathbf dq=f$, where $M=DU\circ X$ and $\mathbf d=DX^{-T}
abla_a$. There are smooth periodic $z,v$ with $z_t=v$, $\operatorname{div}_av=0$, $z(0)=z(T)=0$, and $B=DX\,v$. The pressure is normalized by zero spatial mean. Thus the endpoint condition is on the displacement, not on $B$ or $v$. This is existence of the mean solution used by the recursion; uniqueness is a separate assertion.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanSolvable_of.summary: Every smooth phase-independent forcing has a mean solution

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanTimeSlice_c.text: A jointly smooth field on the slab is smooth in time on $[0,T]$ at each label. The supplied Theorem 4.2 solves the smooth endpoint problem for a phase-independent source. Its velocity and pressure are transported to twisted profiles satisfying the mean equation, with zero displacement at both endpoints.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanTimeSlice_c.summary: A smooth slab field has smooth time slices

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanUnique_of_t.text: The normalized solution of the mean equation (5.11) is unique, for the parent of Section 5.1. Theorem 4.2 enters through the uniqueness clause of its first item: a normalized solution $(B, \bar q)$ of (5.11) gives (by integrating once in time, "(4.11) integrated once in time") a solution of the integrated system (4.9) with source $L = -\int_0^t (D_aX)^T \bar f$, whose velocity is unique; this fixes $B = D_aX\, v$, then $\nabla_a \bar q$ by (5.11), and $\bar q$ by its normalization. Endpoint uniqueness fixes the mean velocity. Equality of pressure gradients fixes pressure only after the two pressures have the same cell mean; the pressure normalization cannot be dropped from the full pair uniqueness claim.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanUnique_of_t.summary: Endpoint uniqueness fixes the mean velocity and normalized pressure

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanVorticity_s.text: Joint smoothness of the vorticity coefficient $\Omega = (D_aX)^T (M^T - M) D_aX$ of (4.1). The supplied Theorem 4.2 solves the smooth endpoint problem for a phase-independent source. Its velocity and pressure are transported to twisted profiles satisfying the mean equation, with zero displacement at both endpoints.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.meanVorticity_s.summary: The vorticity coefficient is jointly smooth

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.mem_inactive_of.text: A twisted profile vanishes on the inactive region as soon as it vanishes at its inactive points over the label cell (the lattice twist and the periodicity of $\operatorname{supp} g$). The inactive set consists of times before activation or labels outside the periodized envelope support. The induction concerns oscillatory profiles and their sources; the means may already be nonzero before activation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.mem_inactive_of.summary: Vanishing on the cell extends by twisted periodicity

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.momentum_eval.text: (5.11) at a point of the slab, with $B$, $\bar q$ replaced by their phase-0 values: $f = \partial_tB + MB + (D_aX)^{-T}\nabla_a \bar q$. Consequently the source is independent of the phase. Endpoint uniqueness fixes the mean velocity. Equality of pressure gradients fixes pressure only after the two pressures have the same cell mean; the pressure normalization cannot be dropped from the full pair uniqueness claim.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.momentum_eval.summary: Evaluate the mean equation on its phase zero slice

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.norm_iteratedFD.text: $\| D^m c(t,x)\| \le 3^m |c|_m$: the operator norm of the $m$-th label derivative is bounded by the coefficient size $|c|_m = \sum_{|\beta|=m} \sup |\partial^\beta c|$ of Appendix D. This transfers the supplied coefficient estimates to the derivative conventions used by the seed construction. Increasing constants or the parent scale changes no field and imposes no new equation on the parent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.norm_iteratedFD.summary: The coordinate derivative sum bounds the full derivative norm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.norm_iteratedFD.text: The power bound (D.6) in the form of Appendix D gives operator-norm jet bounds with the same exponent: $\| D^m c(t,x)\| \le 3^m C_m \mathsf D^{a(m+1)}$. This transfers the supplied coefficient estimates to the derivative conventions used by the seed construction. Increasing constants or the parent scale changes no field and imposes no new equation on the parent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.norm_iteratedFD.summary: Coefficient power estimates control full derivative norms

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.norm_linearMap_.text: A linear map on $\mathbb R^3$ whose values on the coordinate directions are at most $M$ has operator norm at most $3M$. This copies a private lemma of the earlier library construction, for any target space, with the same proof. This transfers the supplied coefficient estimates to the derivative conventions used by the seed construction. Increasing constants or the parent scale changes no field and imposes no new equation on the parent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.norm_linearMap_.summary: Three coordinate bounds control a spatial linear map

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.ofFnWord_eq_ite.text: The word of the letters $\beta 0, \dots, \beta (m-1)$ is the iterated derivative on $e_{\beta 0}, \dots, e_{\beta (m-1)}$. This transfers the supplied coefficient estimates to the derivative conventions used by the seed construction. Increasing constants or the parent scale changes no field and imposes no new equation on the parent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.ofFnWord_eq_ite.summary: A finite coordinate sequence specifies a derivative word

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.opNorm_le_coord.text: The operator norm of a multilinear map on $\mathbb R^3$ is at most the sum of its values on coordinate directions. This copies a private lemma of the earlier library construction, stated for any normed target space instead of a normed algebra, with the same proof. This transfers the supplied coefficient estimates to the derivative conventions used by the seed construction. Increasing constants or the parent scale changes no field and imposes no new equation on the parent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.opNorm_le_coord.summary: Coordinate evaluations bound the multilinear operator norm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.parent_deformat.text: The deformation $D_aX(t,\cdot)$ of the parent of §5.1 is periodic in the label. The supplied Theorem 4.2 solves the smooth endpoint problem for a phase-independent source. Its velocity and pressure are transported to twisted profiles satisfying the mean equation, with zero displacement at both endpoints.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.parent_deformat.summary: The parent deformation is periodic in the label

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.parent_flow_lat.text: The flow of the parent of §5.1 commutes with the lattice translations. The supplied Theorem 4.2 solves the smooth endpoint problem for a phase-independent source. Its velocity and pressure are transported to twisted profiles satisfying the mean equation, with zero displacement at both endpoints.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.parent_flow_lat.summary: The parent flow respects lattice translations

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.parent_flow_lef.text: The backward flow inverts the forward flow. The supplied Theorem 4.2 solves the smooth endpoint problem for a phase-independent source. Its velocity and pressure are transported to twisted profiles satisfying the mean equation, with zero displacement at both endpoints.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.parent_flow_lef.summary: The backward flow inverts the forward flow

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.parent_strain_p.text: The velocity gradient along the flow $M(t,\cdot)$ of the parent is periodic in the label. The supplied Theorem 4.2 solves the smooth endpoint problem for a phase-independent source. Its velocity and pressure are transported to twisted profiles satisfying the mean equation, with zero displacement at both endpoints.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.parent_strain_p.summary: The strain along the parent flow is periodic

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.pressure_phase_.text: The pressure of a solution of (5.11) is independent of the phase: $\kappa\partial_s \bar q = 0$ with $\kappa \ne 0$. Endpoint uniqueness fixes the mean velocity. Equality of pressure gradients fixes pressure only after the two pressures have the same cell mean; the pressure normalization cannot be dropped from the full pair uniqueness claim.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.pressure_phase_.summary: Zero fast gradient forces the mean pressure to be phase independent

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.productConstant.text:
The constant of the product rule on word bounds: the factor of (D.4) times the two conversions between word bounds and the norm (D.1) (each costing the number of admissible words). The coefficient bookkeeping separates constants depending on the derivative order from powers of the parent bound. The numbers $\Omega$ and $\Theta$ in the monotone-weight bound are bounds, not the vorticity coefficient $\Omega$ of the mean equation.

Default values: This is an explicit nonnegative finite combinatorial expression in the number of admissible words and powers of two. It is defined also at order zero, where the empty word remains present. No asymptotic or sharp growth claim is attached to it.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.productConstant.summary: Count the factors in the derivative product estimate

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.productConstant.text: The derivative product constant of order $m$, the factor of (D.4) times the two conversions between word bounds and the norm (D.1), is nonnegative. The coefficient bookkeeping separates constants depending on the derivative order from powers of the parent bound. The numbers $\Omega$ and $\Theta$ in the two-parameter bound $\Omega^a\Theta^i$ are bounds, not the vorticity coefficient $\Omega$ of the mean equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.productConstant.summary: The derivative product constant is nonnegative

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.product_le_rela.text: The common constant absorbs each bilinear operation: if $\|B\|$ is at most the fixed operation bound $N$, then the product constant $c_m$ times $\|B\|$ is at most $\Omega_m=(c_m+1)(N+1)$. The coefficient bookkeeping separates constants depending on the derivative order from powers of the parent bound. The numbers $\Omega$ and $\Theta$ in the two-parameter bound $\Omega^a\Theta^i$ are bounds, not the vorticity coefficient $\Omega$ of the mean equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.product_le_rela.summary: The common constant absorbs each bilinear operation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.radialEnvelope_.text: On the label cell, the envelope vanishes outside $\operatorname{supp} g$ ($2\ell_* < 1/2$). The inactive set consists of times before activation or labels outside the periodized envelope support. The induction concerns oscillatory profiles and their sources; the means may already be nonzero before activation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.radialEnvelope_.summary: The local envelope vanishes outside its periodic support

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.rankOneBilinear.text:
The bilinear map $(u, v) \mapsto u \otimes v$, where $u\otimes v$ is the rank-one map $w \mapsto \langle v, w\rangle u$, of norm at most one: the product of Lemma D.2(a) that builds $\kappa \otimes \kappa$ in $P_\kappa$. Bernstein bounds the truncated parent derivatives, and the differentiated flow equation controls the deformation. Lemma D.2 supplies coefficient products, inverses and the small-radius absorption; the final absolute exponent need not be sharp.

Default values: These fixed continuous linear or bilinear maps are defined on all of the finite-dimensional coefficient spaces and use no inverse or choice. They remain meaningful at zero inputs. The later estimates include their actual operator norms; this packaging does not assume every such norm is one.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.rankOneBilinear.summary: The rank one operator as a bounded bilinear product

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.rankOneBilinear.text: Evaluate the rank one product on a vector. Bernstein bounds the truncated parent derivatives, and the differentiated flow equation controls the deformation. Lemma D.2 supplies coefficient products, inverses and the small-radius absorption; the final absolute exponent need not be sharp.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.rankOneBilinear.summary: Evaluate the rank one product on a vector

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.realNormedTorus.text: A continuous real vector field on the torus whose complexified Fourier coefficients vanish at the frequencies $|k| > R$ is supported on frequencies at most $R$ in the sense of the statement of Lemma B.1: every real linear measurement of it has vanishing Fourier coefficients at those frequencies. This transfers the supplied coefficient estimates to the derivative conventions used by the seed construction. Increasing constants or the parent scale changes no field and imposes no new equation on the parent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.realNormedTorus.summary: Vector Fourier support gives the scalar testing condition

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.relayBudget.text: The coefficient budget of the relay: from word bounds $\Theta$ at order $n+1$ for $(D_aX)^{-1} = G$, $M$, $\kappa/\lambda$ and $\lambda^2/|\kappa|^2 = \nu = |\kappa/\lambda|^{-2}$, and $\|\ell_*^{-1}\| \le \Theta$, every coefficient of the relay has word bound $\omega^{10} \Theta^6$, where $\omega$ is the relay constant of order $n+1$. Products use (D.4) of the supplied Lemma D.1. The coefficient bookkeeping separates constants depending on the derivative order from powers of the parent bound. The numbers $\Omega$ and $\Theta$ in the monotone-weight bound are bounds, not the vorticity coefficient $\Omega$ of the mean equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.relayBudget.summary: Assemble coefficient bounds for the divergence correction residual

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.relayNorms.text:
A bound for the norms of the fixed linear maps used to build the relay coefficients, and for the numbers $2$ and $1$. The coefficient bookkeeping separates constants depending on the derivative order from powers of the parent bound. The numbers $\Omega$ and $\Theta$ in the monotone-weight bound are bounds, not the vorticity coefficient $\Omega$ of the mean equation.

Default values: These are explicit finite expressions in norms and nonnegative combinatorial constants, and the subsequent lemmas prove their positive lower bounds. There are no chosen inverses or asymptotic limits. Their order dependence is allowed in $C_n$ and is separated from the parent-scale exponent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.relayNorms.summary: A common bound for the fixed coefficient operations

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.relayNorms_boun.text: The norms of the fixed linear maps are at most the common bound for the fixed coefficient operations. The coefficient bookkeeping separates constants depending on the derivative order from powers of the parent bound. The numbers $\Omega$ and $\Theta$ in the monotone-weight bound are bounds, not the vorticity coefficient $\Omega$ of the mean equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.relayNorms_boun.summary: The chosen constant bounds every fixed coefficient operation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.relayNorms_ge.text: The fixed operation bound, three plus the operator norms of the fixed linear maps (evaluations, composition, scalar multiplication, inner product, cross product, transpose and the others) used to build the relay coefficients, is at least three. The coefficient bookkeeping separates constants depending on the derivative order from powers of the parent bound. The numbers $\Omega$ and $\Theta$ in the two-parameter bound $\Omega^a\Theta^i$ are bounds, not the vorticity coefficient $\Omega$ of the mean equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.relayNorms_ge.summary: The fixed operation bound is at least three

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.relayOmega.text:
The constant $\Omega$ of order $m$: $(c^{\rm prod}_m + 1)(N_{\rm rel} + 1)$, where $c^{\rm prod}_m$ is the product-rule constant of order $m$ and $N_{\rm rel}$ the common bound for the fixed coefficient operations. The coefficient bookkeeping separates constants depending on the derivative order from powers of the parent bound. The numbers $\Omega$ and $\Theta$ in the monotone-weight bound are bounds, not the vorticity coefficient $\Omega$ of the mean equation.

Default values: These are explicit finite expressions in norms and nonnegative combinatorial constants, and the subsequent lemmas prove their positive lower bounds. There are no chosen inverses or asymptotic limits. Their order dependence is allowed in $C_n$ and is separated from the parent-scale exponent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.relayOmega.summary: A common constant for products at each derivative order

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.relayOmega_ge.text: The relay constant of order $m$ dominates the common bound for the fixed coefficient operations. The coefficient bookkeeping separates constants depending on the derivative order from powers of the parent bound. The numbers $\Omega$ and $\Theta$ in the monotone-weight bound are bounds, not the vorticity coefficient $\Omega$ of the mean equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.relayOmega_ge.summary: The product constant dominates all fixed operation bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.relayWordBound_.text: The sum of two smooth fields with word bounds has the sum of those constants as a word bound. It is the two-term case needed by the polynomial relay formulas.

A nonnegative uniform bound on every admissible derivative word supplies boundedness of the corresponding sets of derivative norms. This justifies taking the real suprema used by the finite field norm.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.relayWordBound_.summary: A derivative bound makes the defining supremum finite

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.relayWordBound_.text: A bounded continuous bilinear map applied to two smooth fields with word bounds has a word bound with the usual Leibniz combinatorial factor. This is the local product calculation used when building the relay coefficients.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.relayWordBound_.summary: Bilinear products obey the derivative word bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.relayWordBound_.text: Constant scalar multiplication changes the word bound by the scalar's absolute value. Derivatives still act only on the field, not on the scalar.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.relayWordBound_.summary: Constant multiplication preserves the derivative word bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.relayWordBound_.text: The primitive clause of the supplied D.1 bounds the zero-mean phase primitive after multiplication by a phase-independent linear coefficient. Smoothness, period one and zero phase mean are explicit hypotheses; the derivative order is preserved.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.relayWordBound_.summary: Bound a phase primitive of two linear terms

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.relayWordBound_.text: Increasing a word-bound constant preserves the bound for the same field and derivative order. This permits coefficients with different estimates to share a common nonnegative budget.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.relayWordBound_.summary: Lower derivative orders inherit a larger common bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.relayWordBound_.text: The primitive estimate (D.5) of Lemma D.1 on word bounds. It replaces a private lemma of the earlier library construction, whose proof calls the library's own proof of the phase-primitive bound: here the bound $\|\partial_s^{-1} f\|_{[n]} \le 2 \|f\|_{[n]}$ and the finiteness of the left side are the (D.5) clause of the supplied Lemma D.1, with $\gamma \equiv 1$. The primitive estimate is taken from the supplied Lemma D.1. Its use, together with coefficient word bounds, yields the inverse-frequency gain in the curl correction and relay without a time derivative of the source.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.relayWordBound_.summary: The cited primitive estimate preserves derivative order
