TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.relayWordBound_.text: Summing finitely many fields with uniform word bounds gives the sum of their constants as a word bound. All summands are smooth in the label and phase parameters.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.relayWordBound_.summary: Sum the bounds for finitely many profiles

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.relayWordBound_.text: The zero field has word bound zero at every order. This is used for the leading-wave relay where the transverse forcing is zero.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.relayWordBound_.summary: The zero profile has zero derivative bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.relay_phaseOper.text: A derivative word of a finite sum of smooth fields equals the sum of their derivative words. The identity lets the finitely many relay terms be estimated separately.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.relay_phaseOper.summary: Derivative words commute with finite sums

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.remainder_eq_li.text: The two groupings of the remainder agree: $R_P$ of (5.30) is the library remainder, when the transverse levels do not differentiate the phase and $C_1 = B_1 = 0$. This is an exact finite algebraic identity. The final curl completion $C_{P+1}$ is retained while the top velocity and mean profiles are set to zero; no assertion about convergence of an infinite expansion is involved.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.remainder_eq_li.summary: The two groupings of the uncanceled terms agree

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.remainder_trunc.text: The remainder is unchanged by truncating at $P$ when the top profiles vanish. This is an exact finite algebraic identity. The final curl completion $C_{P+1}$ is retained while the top velocity and mean profiles are set to zero; no assertion about convergence of an infinite expansion is involved.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.remainder_trunc.summary: Removing unused levels leaves the remainder unchanged

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.seedNear_of_h51.text: Assume $0\le t_0<T\le1$, the parent coefficient, residual and coercivity bounds, and a nonzero central transverse seed with relative forward growth at most $\mathsf D$ and coupling at least $\mathsf D^{-1}$. Proposition 5.1 allows one sufficiently small envelope on which every seed with initial data (5.4) satisfies the quantitative near-origin estimates. Uniqueness identifies that seed with the separately constructed local solution. The conclusion includes more than (5.19), but its relative-error constant is only specified as a function of $\mathsf D$; this statement does not expose a polynomial bound for that constant. The transverse stability assumption is $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for every transverse homogeneous solution $\mathbf b$ and $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.seedNear_of_h51.summary: The prescribed seed inherits quantitative bounds near the origin

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.slice0_contDiff.text: The phase-0 slice of a jointly smooth profile is jointly smooth in $(t, a)$. Endpoint uniqueness fixes the mean velocity. Equality of pressure gradients fixes pressure only after the two pressures have the same cell mean; the pressure normalization cannot be dropped from the full pair uniqueness claim.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.smoothMeanSolut.text: If two smooth solutions of the mean equation (5.11) in label coordinates have the same velocity, their pressures have the same gradient: $(D_aX)^T (D_aX)^{-T} = \mathrm{Id}$. Endpoint uniqueness fixes the mean velocity. Equality of pressure gradients fixes pressure only after the two pressures have the same cell mean; the pressure normalization cannot be dropped from the full pair uniqueness claim.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.smoothMeanSolut.summary: Equal mean velocities give equal pressure gradients

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.sum_coordinateD.text: A vector of $\mathbb R^3$ is the sum of its coordinates times the coordinate directions. This transfers the supplied coefficient estimates to the derivative conventions used by the seed construction. Increasing constants or the parent scale changes no field and imposes no new equation on the parent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.sum_coordinateD.summary: Coordinate vectors reconstruct every spatial vector

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.suppSource_trun.text: The support source of order $p \le P$ is unchanged by truncation. This is an exact finite algebraic identity. The final curl completion $C_{P+1}$ is retained while the top velocity and mean profiles are set to zero; no assertion about convergence of an infinite expansion is involved.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.suppSource_trun.summary: Removing unused levels leaves the mean transport source unchanged

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.toSpanL.text:
The map sending a vector $v$ to scalar multiplication by it, $v \mapsto (r \mapsto r v)$, as a continuous linear map of $v$. The coefficient bookkeeping separates constants depending on the derivative order from powers of the parent bound. The numbers $\Omega$ and $\Theta$ in the monotone-weight bound are bounds, not the vorticity coefficient $\Omega$ of the mean equation.

Default values: These fixed continuous linear or bilinear maps are defined on all of the finite-dimensional coefficient spaces and use no inverse or choice. They remain meaningful at zero inputs. The later estimates include their actual operator norms; this packaging does not assume every such norm is one.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.toSpanL.summary: Turn a vector into scalar multiplication by that vector

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.toSpanL_apply.text: The map obtained from a vector sends a scalar r to r times that vector. This identifies scalar multiplication as a fixed bilinear map for the product bound.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.toSpanL_apply.summary: Evaluate the vector to scalar multiplication map

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.totalDivergence.text: Here $\kappa=(D_aX)^{-T}k_*\ne0$, the parent is smooth, periodic and volume preserving, and all constraints hold throughout $[0,T]$. A zero-mean transverse profile satisfies $\widetilde{\mathbf d}\cdot(V+C[V])=0$. The proof uses the identity $V+C[V]=\widetilde{\mathbf d}\times Q[V]$ in the transported parent geometry. Proposition 5.4 sums these completed oscillations and the separately divergence-free means to obtain the divergence constraint for the entire finite correction.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.totalDivergence.summary: The curl correction restores the full divergence constraint

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.totalDivergence.text: The parent is smooth and volume preserving on $[0,T]$, and the smooth periodic displacement satisfies $z(0)=z(T)=0$. The endpoint mean solution has $B=D_aXz_t$ with divergence-free label velocity $z_t$. Volume preservation and the Piola identity give $\mathbf d\cdot B=0$, and phase independence makes this the full divergence constraint as well. This supplies the mean terms in the divergence calculation for $W$ in Proposition 5.4.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.totalDivergence.summary: Transfer the divergence constraint through the parent flow

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.transverseSolut.text: A solution of (5.15) from $V(0) = 0$ whose source has zero phase mean and vanishes on the inactive region vanishes there, together with its pressure. By uniqueness of transverse solutions it coincides with the ODE solve of the earlier library construction, and that solve is known to vanish on the inactive region. The inactive set consists of times before activation or labels outside the periodized envelope support. The induction concerns oscillatory profiles and their sources; the means may already be nonzero before activation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.transverseSolut.summary: The transverse solve preserves the inactive region

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.transverseSourc.text: The transverse source $f_p + f_p^S$ of level $p \ge 2$ vanishes on the inactive region when the lower levels do: $Y_j = V_j + C_j$ for $1 \le j < p$, $C_p$, $\mathsf p_{p-1}$ and (at $p = 2$) the activation correction $C[\tilde\chi'A_1]$ vanish there, and the means $B_j$, $1 \le j < p$, are phase independent (the statement holds for every $p$; it is used for $2 \le p \le P$). On the inactive region $H_p$ reduces to the slow products of means, which the centring removes, and every term of $f_p^S$ has an inactive second factor. The inactive set consists of times before activation or labels outside the periodized envelope support. The induction concerns oscillatory profiles and their sources; the means may already be nonzero before activation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.transverseSourc.summary: The next transverse source preserves the inactive region

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.truncProfiles.text:
The profiles of an expansion of depth $P$ with the levels outside $1 \le p \le P$ and the library corrections $u.C q$ outside $q \le P$ (that is, $C_{q+1}$ outside $1 \le q + 1 \le P + 1$) set to zero. Only these levels enter $W$, $\mathsf P$, $R_P$ and the sources of Proposition 5.4. This is an exact finite algebraic identity. The final curl completion $C_{P+1}$ is retained while the top velocity and mean profiles are set to zero; no assertion about convergence of an infinite expansion is involved.

Default values: Levels outside the specified ranges are intentionally set to zero. The stored completion C is indexed with an offset: retaining C through P retains the physical completion $C_{P+1}$. The preservation theorems state exactly which V,B,p,q and derived C,Y,Z entries agree; no all-level equality with the original family is claimed.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.truncProfiles.summary: Retain precisely the levels of a finite expansion

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.trunc_B.text: Truncating the profiles at $P$ does not change $B i$ for $1 \le i \le P$. This is an exact finite algebraic identity. The final curl completion $C_{P+1}$ is retained while the top velocity and mean profiles are set to zero; no assertion about convergence of an infinite expansion is involved.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.trunc_B_top.text: The extra mean velocity is zero. This is an exact finite algebraic identity. The final curl completion C_{P+1} is retained while the top velocity and mean profiles are set to zero; no assertion about convergence of an infinite expansion is involved.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.trunc_Cd.text: Truncating the expansion at $P$ does not change the paper's correction $C_i$ for $i \le P + 1$. This is an exact finite algebraic identity. The final curl completion $C_{P+1}$ is retained while the top velocity and mean profiles are set to zero; no assertion about convergence of an infinite expansion is involved.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.trunc_Cd.summary: Truncation keeps the corrections through level P+1

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.trunc_V.text: Truncating the profiles at $P$ does not change $V i$ for $1 \le i \le P$. This is an exact finite algebraic identity. The final curl completion $C_{P+1}$ is retained while the top velocity and mean profiles are set to zero; no assertion about convergence of an infinite expansion is involved.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.trunc_V_top.text: The extra transverse velocity is zero. This is an exact finite algebraic identity. The final curl completion C_{P+1} is retained while the top velocity and mean profiles are set to zero; no assertion about convergence of an infinite expansion is involved.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.trunc_Yd.text: Truncating the expansion at $P$ does not change $Y_i = V_i + C_i$ for $1 \le i \le P + 1$. This is an exact finite algebraic identity. The final curl completion $C_{P+1}$ is retained while the top velocity and mean profiles are set to zero; no assertion about convergence of an infinite expansion is involved.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.trunc_Zd.text: Truncating the expansion at $P$ does not change $Z_i = Y_i + B_i$ for $1 \le i \le P + 1$. This is an exact finite algebraic identity. The final curl completion $C_{P+1}$ is retained while the top velocity and mean profiles are set to zero; no assertion about convergence of an infinite expansion is involved.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.trunc_p.text: Truncating the profiles at $P$ does not change $p i$ for $1 \le i \le P$. This is an exact finite algebraic identity. The final curl completion $C_{P+1}$ is retained while the top velocity and mean profiles are set to zero; no assertion about convergence of an infinite expansion is involved.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.trunc_q.text: Truncating the profiles at $P$ does not change $q i$ for $1 \le i \le P$. This is an exact finite algebraic identity. The final curl completion $C_{P+1}$ is retained while the top velocity and mean profiles are set to zero; no assertion about convergence of an infinite expansion is involved.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.two_le_relayOme.text: The common product constant $\Omega_m=(c_m+1)(N+1)$ is at least two for every order $m$. The coefficient bookkeeping separates constants depending on the derivative order from powers of the parent bound. The numbers $\Omega$ and $\Theta$ in the two-parameter bound $\Omega^a\Theta^i$ are bounds, not the vorticity coefficient $\Omega$ of the mean equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.two_le_relayOme.summary: The common product constant is at least two

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.wNorm_zero.text: The zero profile has zero weighted norm. The completion and relay gain one inverse carrier frequency and cost one spatial derivative. The pressure and vector-potential formulas eliminate the dangerous fast derivative without differentiating the mean or the forcing in time.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.waveCompletion_.text: Positive spatial and phase scales, nonzero frequency and the specified coefficient word bounds imply an estimate for the curl completion. The result gains one inverse frequency and uses one additional derivative of the zero-mean input, with the primitive bound supplied by D.1.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.waveCompletion_.summary: The divergence correction gains one inverse frequency

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.waveLinearRelay.text: For smooth periodic zero-mean velocity and forcing, the specified potential, pressure and curl coefficient bounds control the four terms of the linear relay. The estimate gains one inverse frequency and costs one derivative. The source is used through its spatial words, never through a time derivative.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.waveLinearRelay.summary: Bound the four terms after differentiating the vector potential

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.wb_bilinear_of_.text: The product rule (D.4) of Lemma D.1 on word bounds: if every weighted mixed derivative of order at most $m$ of $f$ is at most $A$ and of $g$ at most $C$, those of $B(f, g)$ are at most $c^{\rm prod}_m \|B\| A C$, with $c^{\rm prod}_m$ the product-rule constant of order $m$. The norm of the product and its finiteness are the (D.4) clause of the supplied Lemma D.1, with weight $\gamma \equiv 1$. The coefficient bookkeeping separates constants depending on the derivative order from powers of the parent bound. The numbers $\Omega$ and $\Theta$ in the monotone-weight bound are bounds, not the vorticity coefficient $\Omega$ of the mean equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.wb_bilinear_of_.summary: The cited product rule bounds each derivative word

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.wb_congr.text: Equal fields satisfy the same derivative bound: a uniform bound on every weighted mixed derivative of order at most $m$. The coefficient bookkeeping separates constants depending on the derivative order from powers of the parent bound. The numbers $\Omega$ and $\Theta$ in the two-parameter bound $\Omega^a\Theta^i$ are bounds, not the vorticity coefficient $\Omega$ of the mean equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.wb_congr.summary: Equal fields satisfy the same derivative bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.wb_const.text: Constant fields have uniform derivative bounds: the constant field $v$ has every weighted mixed derivative of order at most $m$ bounded by $|v|$. The coefficient bookkeeping separates constants depending on the derivative order from powers of the parent bound. The numbers $\Omega$ and $\Theta$ in the two-parameter bound $\Omega^a\Theta^i$ are bounds, not the vorticity coefficient $\Omega$ of the mean equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.wb_const.summary: Constant fields have uniform derivative bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.weighted_one.text: Dividing by the unit weight changes nothing. The primitive estimate is taken from the supplied Lemma D.1. Its use, together with coefficient word bounds, yields the inverse-frequency gain in the curl correction and relay without a time derivative of the source.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.weighted_one.summary: Dividing by the unit weight changes nothing

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.wrapped_eq_on_c.text: On the centered label cell, the twisted periodization agrees with a field supported in the ball of radius 2ℓ when 2ℓ<1/2. The support and strict fitting condition are what prevent an additional translated copy from contributing.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.wrapped_eq_on_c.summary: The localized extension agrees with its cell data

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.CoefficientPowe.text: The power bound (D.6) is monotone in the exponent, since $\mathsf D \ge 1$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.CoefficientPowe.summary: Increasing the parent exponent preserves coefficient bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.coefficientPowe.text: Operator-norm jet bounds $\|D^m c(t,x)\| \le K_m \mathsf D^{a(m+1)}$ of a field smooth in the label give the power bound (D.6) in the form of Appendix D, with constants $\#\{\text{words of order } m\} \cdot K_m$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.coefficientPowe.summary: Full coefficient jets imply the required power bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.exists_monotone.text: A nondecreasing coordinate word of length $m$ is the word of a monotone map from $\{0,\dots,m-1\}$ to the three coordinate indices $\{0,1,2\}$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.exists_monotone.summary: Sorted derivative words have monotone index maps

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.exists_sortedWo.text: Symmetry of the derivatives of a smooth function: every coordinate component $D^m f(x)(e_{\beta 0}, \dots, e_{\beta (m-1)})$ is the value of one nondecreasing coordinate word of length $m$ (the sorted word of the letters of $\beta$).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.exists_sortedWo.summary: Symmetry permits sorting the derivative directions

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.labelDirection_.text: The unit label directions of Appendix D are the coordinate directions.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.labelDirection_.summary: Unit label directions are coordinate directions

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.labelWord_eq_it.text: The value of a coordinate word is the iterated derivative on the coordinate directions of its letters.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.labelWord_eq_it.summary: Ordered label words evaluate Fréchet derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.mFourierCoeff_c.text: A continuous complex linear map commutes with Fourier coefficients of a continuous torus field. Here the map takes a complex Euclidean vector to a scalar, permitting coordinate projections of a vector frequency-support bound.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.mFourierCoeff_c.summary: Linear maps commute with Fourier coefficients

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.norm_iteratedFD.text: $\| D^m c(t,x)\| \le 3^m |c|_m$: the operator norm of the $m$-th label derivative is bounded by the coefficient size $|c|_m = \sum_{|\beta|=m} \sup |\partial^\beta c|$ of Appendix D.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.norm_iteratedFD.summary: Coefficient norms control full label derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.norm_iteratedFD.text: The power bound (D.6) in the form of Appendix D gives operator-norm jet bounds with the same exponent: $\| D^m c(t,x)\| \le 3^m C_m \mathsf D^{a(m+1)}$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.norm_iteratedFD.summary: Power bounds control full coefficient jets

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.norm_linearMap_.text: If a linear map on ℝ³ has norm at most M on each coordinate vector, then its operator norm is at most 3M. The codomain is an arbitrary real normed space; the proof expands an input in its three coordinates.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.norm_linearMap_.summary: Three coordinate bounds control a linear map

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.ofFnWord_eq_ite.text: The word of the letters $\beta 0, \dots, \beta (m-1)$ is the iterated derivative on $e_{\beta 0}, \dots, e_{\beta (m-1)}$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.ofFnWord_eq_ite.summary: Indexed coordinate words evaluate Fréchet derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.opNorm_le_coord.text: The operator norm of a multilinear map on ℝ³ is bounded by the sum of the norms of its values on coordinate directions. The target may be any normed space, so this applies to coefficient operators as well as scalar fields.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.opNorm_le_coord.summary: Bounding multilinear norms by coordinate values

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.realNormedTorus.text: A continuous real vector field on the torus whose complexified Fourier coefficients vanish at the frequencies $|k| > R$ is supported on frequencies at most $R$ in the sense of the statement of Lemma B.1: every real linear measurement of it has vanishing Fourier coefficients at those frequencies.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.realNormedTorus.summary: Vector Fourier support bounds scalar projections

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.sum_coordinateD.text: A vector of $\mathbb R^3$ is the sum of its coordinates times the coordinate directions.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.sum_coordinateD.summary: Expanding vectors in the three coordinate directions

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.CentralReturnCl.text:
Packages the error estimate for the velocity gradient at the origin after subtracting the parent gradient and the switched rank one seed contribution. The eventual smallness assumption absorbs the $D$ power and the $\lambda^{-5/12}$ intermediate error into the stated $\lambda^{-1/3}$ error.

This is a quantified estimate for valid expansion data, not an independently chosen pressure or velocity. It may be vacuous without admissible data; the subsequent proof supplies it under the cited hypotheses and Proposition 5.4 supplies expansion existence. Natural finite sums use the stated retained level range.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.CutBand.text:
Lemma B.1, real block, band clause at the frequency $\Lambda$: for every continuous field $g$ on $\mathbb T^3$, $S_\Lambda g$ has vanishing Fourier coefficients at every integer vector $k$ with $|k|>2\Lambda$.

This is a proposition stating one analytic property with chosen constants or cutoff parameters; the definition alone does not prove it. The application obtains it from Lemma B.1 or (5.59), with an admissible cutoff, nonnegative constants and $\Lambda\ge1$. Empty or degenerate intervals do not replace the explicit strict time-length hypothesis where it is needed.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.CutBand.summary: The Fourier cutoff confines the frequency support

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.CutDivergence.text:
Lemma B.1, real block, divergence clause at the frequency $\Lambda$: if a continuous field $g$ on $\mathbb T^3$ has a smooth lift with zero divergence everywhere, then $S_\Lambda g$ also has zero divergence everywhere.

This is a proposition stating one analytic property with chosen constants or cutoff parameters; the definition alone does not prove it. The application obtains it from Lemma B.1 or (5.59), with an admissible cutoff, nonnegative constants and $\Lambda\ge1$. Empty or degenerate intervals do not replace the explicit strict time-length hypothesis where it is needed.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.CutDivergence.summary: The Fourier cutoff preserves zero divergence

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.CutParity.text:
Lemma B.1, real block, parity clause at the frequency $\Lambda$: whenever $g(-z)=c\,g(z)$ for all $z$, also $S_\Lambda g(-z)=c\,S_\Lambda g(z)$ for all $z$.

This is a proposition stating one analytic property with chosen constants or cutoff parameters; the definition alone does not prove it. The application obtains it from Lemma B.1 or (5.59), with an admissible cutoff, nonnegative constants and $\Lambda\ge1$. Empty or degenerate intervals do not replace the explicit strict time-length hypothesis where it is needed.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.CutParity.summary: The Fourier cutoff preserves reflection parity

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.CutSpaceDeriv.text:
Lemma B.1, real block, commutation with the first-order coordinate derivatives.

This is a proposition stating one analytic property with chosen constants or cutoff parameters; the definition alone does not prove it. The application obtains it from Lemma B.1 or (5.59), with an admissible cutoff, nonnegative constants and Λ ≥ 1. Empty or degenerate intervals do not replace the explicit strict time-length hypothesis where it is needed.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.CutSpaceDeriv.summary: The Fourier cutoff commutes with spatial derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.CutTail.text:
(B.2) of Lemma B.1 for the real vector cutoff $S_\Lambda$ at the frequency $\Lambda$, with constants $C_t(M)$: for $s\le M$ and every continuous field $g$ on $\mathbb T^3$ of class $C^{M,1/2}$, the tail $g-S_\Lambda g$ is $C^{s,1/2}$ with $\|g-S_\Lambda g\|_{C^{s,1/2}}\le C_t(M)\Lambda^{s-M}\|g\|_{C^{M,1/2}}$.

This is a proposition stating one analytic property with chosen constants or cutoff parameters; the definition alone does not prove it. The application obtains it from Lemma B.1 or (5.59), with an admissible cutoff, nonnegative constants and $\Lambda\ge1$. Empty or degenerate intervals do not replace the explicit strict time-length hypothesis where it is needed.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.CutTail.summary: The tail estimate (B.2) for the real Fourier cutoff

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.CutTailComplex.text:
(B.2) of Lemma B.1 for the complex smooth Fourier cutoff $S_\Lambda$ with symbol $\psi$, acting on fields with values in a complete complex normed space $E$, with the constants $C_t(M)$.

This is a proposition stating one analytic property with chosen constants or cutoff parameters; the definition alone does not prove it. The application obtains it from Lemma B.1 or (5.59), with an admissible cutoff, nonnegative constants and $\Lambda\ge1$. Empty or degenerate intervals do not replace the explicit strict time-length hypothesis where it is needed.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.CutTailComplex.summary: The tail estimate (B.2) for the complex Fourier cutoff

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.CutTimeDeriv.text:
Lemma B.1, real block, commutation with the time derivative on a closed slab.

This is a proposition stating one analytic property with chosen constants or cutoff parameters; the definition alone does not prove it. The application obtains it from Lemma B.1 or (5.59), with an admissible cutoff, nonnegative constants and Λ ≥ 1. Empty or degenerate intervals do not replace the explicit strict time-length hypothesis where it is needed.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.CutTimeDeriv.summary: The Fourier cutoff commutes with closed slab time derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.EulerMean.text:
The Eulerian form of a solution $(B,\bar q)$ of (5.11) with source $\bar f$: $b=B\circ X^{-1}$, $q=\bar q\circ X^{-1}$ and $f=\bar f\circ X^{-1}$ are smooth and periodic, $\operatorname{div}b=0$, and the linearized Euler equation (4.12) holds, with the material derivative $\partial_t+U\cdot\nabla$ taken on the closed slab.

This is a conjunction recording smoothness, periodicity, divergence freeness and an Eulerian equation on the closed slab. It is not a chosen solution. The within-slab material derivative is interpreted through the supplied smoothness and positive time interval.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.EulerMean.summary: The Eulerian form of a mean solution

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.HigherHessianCl.text:
On $[0,T]	imes\mathbb T^3$, $0<T\le1$, let $U,p_U$ be smooth, $U$ odd and solenoidal, $X$ its flow, and $R_U=U_t+U\cdot
abla U+
abla p_U$ odd. Assume $\mathsf D\ge2$, Fourier radii $2\mathsf D,4\mathsf D$ for $U,R_U$, $\|
abla U\|_\infty,\|DX\|_\infty,\|DX^{-1}\|_\infty\le\mathsf D$, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. Write $M=
abla U\circ X$, $\kappa=DX^{-T}k_*$, $|\kappa(t_0,0)|=\lambda\ge1$, $0\le t_0<T$. At the origin, a nonzero transverse seed solves $\mathbf a_t=-(I-2P_\kappa)M\mathbf a$, with $P_\kappa=\kappa\otimes\kappa/|\kappa|^2$, $\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a|\le1$, and $\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a\ge\mathsf D^{-1}|\kappa||\mathbf a|$. Every transverse solution $\mathbf b$ of that homogeneous equation must satisfy $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$. For a depth-$P\ge2$ expansion with sufficiently small $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$ and $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, the conclusion is $\|D^2\sum_{p=2}^P\mathsf p_p^
atural\|_\infty\le K_P\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-5/12}$ on $[0,T]$. It assumes $\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$; the exponent and constants are selected before the parent and expansion. This declaration formulates the claim; it does not prove it.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.HigherHessianCl.summary: State the decay of the sum of higher oscillatory pressures

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.Icc_subset_Icc_.text: Time domains: for $0\le t_0$, the active interval is contained in the full slab, $[t_0,T]\subseteq[0,T]$, so estimates on the slab apply on the active interval.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.Icc_subset_Icc_.summary: The active interval lies within the full time slab

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.IsExpansion.ina.text: Supports of the expansion, given the support of the sources. If the sources $f_p+f_p^S$ ($2\le p\le P$) lie in the inactive subspace, then so do $V_p$, $\mathsf p_p$ ($1\le p\le P$) and $C_p$ ($1\le p\le P+1$). The leading pair and the activation term vanish there by their cell values (3.7), (3.8); for $p\ge2$ the transverse equation (5.15) with the zero initial datum is solved by the general transverse ODE solve, which keeps the inactive region, and $C_{p+1}=C[V_p]$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.IsExpansion.ina.summary: Inactive sources force every oscillatory level to vanish

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.IsExpansion.lea.text: The leading pressure vanishes on the inactive region (no use of Proposition 5.4): on the label cell $\mathsf p_1=\tilde\chi\cdot(-c_{\mathbf a})\mathsf p_h$ by the leading pressure clause of the expansion, $\tilde\chi=0$ for $t<t_0$ (the cutoff) and $c_{\mathbf a}=0$ off $\operatorname{supp}g$ (the radial envelope).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.IsExpansion.lea.summary: The first pressure vanishes in the inactive region

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.LeadingHessianC.text:
Packages the leading pressure estimate as a quadratic-form upper bound for every vector $v$, with size $C D^C \lambda^{-1/4}\lVert v\rVert^2$. It deliberately does not bound the absolute value or operator norm of the leading Hessian; the large signed phase tensor is controlled only on its unfavorable side.

This is a quantified estimate for valid expansion data, not an independently chosen pressure or velocity. It may be vacuous without admissible data; the subsequent proof supplies it under the cited hypotheses and Proposition 5.4 supplies expansion existence. Natural finite sums use the stated retained level range.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.LeadingHessianC.summary: The signed leading pressure Hessian bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.MeanHessianClai.text:
On $[0,T]	imes\mathbb T^3$, $0<T\le1$, let $U,p_U$ be smooth, $U$ odd and solenoidal, $X$ its flow, and $R_U=U_t+U\cdot
abla U+
abla p_U$ odd. Assume $\mathsf D\ge2$, Fourier radii $2\mathsf D,4\mathsf D$ for $U,R_U$, $\|
abla U\|_\infty,\|DX\|_\infty,\|DX^{-1}\|_\infty\le\mathsf D$, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. Write $M=
abla U\circ X$, $\kappa=DX^{-T}k_*$, $|\kappa(t_0,0)|=\lambda\ge1$, $0\le t_0<T$. At the origin, a nonzero transverse seed solves $\mathbf a_t=-(I-2P_\kappa)M\mathbf a$, with $P_\kappa=\kappa\otimes\kappa/|\kappa|^2$, $\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a|\le1$, and $\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a\ge\mathsf D^{-1}|\kappa||\mathbf a|$. Every transverse solution $\mathbf b$ of that homogeneous equation must satisfy $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$. For a depth-$P\ge2$ expansion with sufficiently small $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$ and $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, the conclusion is $\|D^2\sum_{p=2}^P ar q_p^
atural\|_\infty\le K_P\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-5/2}$ on $[0,T]$. It assumes $\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$; the exponent and constants are selected before the parent and expansion. This declaration formulates the claim; it does not prove it.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.MeanHessianClai.summary: State the decay of the pressure attached to the mean corrections

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.ProductBound.text:
The product inequality (5.59) with chosen constants $C_m$: each $C_m\ge0$, and for every bounded bilinear map $B$ and fields $f,g$ of class $C^{m,1/2}$, the field $B(f,g)$ is $C^{m,1/2}$ with $\|B(f,g)\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\le C_m\|B\|\,\|f\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\|g\|_{C^{m,1/2}}$. It is the formal statement of (5.59) with its constants fixed.

This is a proposition stating one analytic property with chosen constants or cutoff parameters; the definition alone does not prove it. The application obtains it from Lemma B.1 or (5.59), with an admissible cutoff, nonnegative constants and $\Lambda\ge1$. Empty or degenerate intervals do not replace the explicit strict time-length hypothesis where it is needed.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.ProductBound.summary: Chosen constants for the physical Hölder product estimate

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.adjL.text:
The transpose $A\mapsto A^{\mathsf T}$ on linear maps of $\mathbb R^3$, as a continuous linear map; it repeats the transpose map used in Section 5.

This is a total algebraic or continuous-linear construction with no division or noncanonical choice. Zero inputs have their literal algebraic values. Any geometric identification or differentiability property is supplied separately by the consuming theorem.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.adjL.summary: Transposition as a continuous linear operator

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.adjL_apply.text: Applying the continuous linear transposition map to a linear map $A$ of $\mathbb R^3$ gives its transpose $A^{\mathsf T}$; this is the evaluation rule for that map.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.average_transve.text: The transverse source $f_p+f_p^S$ of (5.27), (5.28) has zero phase mean when the means $B_i$, $2\le i\le p$, are phase independent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.average_transve.summary: The full transverse source has zero phase average

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.centralReturnCl.text:
On $[0,T]	imes\mathbb T^3$, $0<T\le1$, let $U,p_U$ be smooth, $U$ odd and solenoidal, $X$ its flow, and $R_U=U_t+U\cdot
abla U+
abla p_U$ odd. Assume $\mathsf D\ge2$, Fourier radii $2\mathsf D,4\mathsf D$ for $U,R_U$, $\|
abla U\|_\infty,\|DX\|_\infty,\|DX^{-1}\|_\infty\le\mathsf D$, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. Write $M=
abla U\circ X$, $\kappa=DX^{-T}k_*$, $|\kappa(t_0,0)|=\lambda\ge1$, $0\le t_0<T$. At the origin, a nonzero transverse seed solves $\mathbf a_t=-(I-2P_\kappa)M\mathbf a$, with $P_\kappa=\kappa\otimes\kappa/|\kappa|^2$, $\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a|\le1$, and $\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a\ge\mathsf D^{-1}|\kappa||\mathbf a|$. Every transverse solution $\mathbf b$ of that homogeneous equation must satisfy $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$. For a depth-$P\ge2$ expansion with sufficiently small $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$ and $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, the conclusion is $\|DV(t,0)-DU(t,0)-\widetilde\chi(t)\mathbf a(t,0)\otimes\kappa(t,0)\|\le\lambda^{-1/3}$ on $[t_0,T]$. It assumes $\Gamma_P\mathsf D^b\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$ for sufficiently large $b,\Gamma_P$. The formal implication assumes Lemma 3.1, Proposition 5.4, Theorem 5.6, and Lemma 5.7.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.centralReturnCl.summary: Prove the central error bound from profile and evaluation estimates

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.centralReturn_e.text:
The central error. For an expansion of depth $P\ge1$ over a parent, $V=U+W^
atural$ and $t\in[t_0,T]$, the difference $
abla V(t,0)-
abla U(t,0)-	ilde\chi(t)\,\mathbf a(t,0)\otimes\kappa(t,0)$ equals $D_x(W_{m osc}-V_1)^
atural(t,0)+D_x ar W^
atural(t,0)$. The profile facts $F_h(0)=0$ and $F_h'(0)=1$ enter through the chain-rule computation of the leading wave's derivative at the origin.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.centralReturn_e.summary: The central gradient equals the prescribed rank one part

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.closedSlabLeray.text: Applying the real cutoff and the periodic Leray projection to the approximate momentum equation on a closed slab $[a,b]$ with $a<b$ gives (5.58). The commutation of $S_\Lambda$ with the time derivative and with the first spatial derivatives, and the preservation of divergence freeness, are hypotheses (the corresponding clauses of Lemma B.1).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.closedSlabLeray.summary: Deriving the projected residual identity on the slab

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.coefC.text:
The number of words of length at most one in the three label directions.

The definition uses finite word counts and total real arithmetic. Maxima or absolute values, where present, ensure the chosen majorants remain nonnegative; the formula itself is not a proof that an arbitrary input constant bounds a field. The analytic estimates provide the corresponding coefficient or level bounds.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.coefC.summary: Counting the label words through order one

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.coefC_nonneg.text: The constant of (D.6) at order one, the number of derivative words of length at most one in the three label directions, is nonnegative.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.coefC_nonneg.summary: Nonnegative counts of label derivative words

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.coefK.text:
The constant $\kappa_0=\#W_1\cdot\max(K_1(1),0)$, where $\#W_1$ counts the label derivative words of length at most one, bounding the order-one norms of the coefficients $(D_aX)^{-1}$, $M$, $P_\kappa$ by $\kappa_0\mathsf D^{C_1}$ ((D.6), (5.8) of Proposition 5.1).

The definition uses finite word counts and total real arithmetic. Maxima or absolute values, where present, ensure the chosen majorants remain nonnegative; the formula itself is not a proof that an arbitrary input constant bounds a field. The analytic estimates provide the corresponding coefficient or level bounds.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.coefK.summary: The coefficient constant from the parent geometry bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.coefNorm.text: The norm of a phase-independent coefficient $L(c(t,a))$ on a time domain mapped into $[0,T]$, from the bounds (D.6) (finiteness of the jets) and (5.8) of Proposition 5.1, both taken as hypotheses: it is finite, and at most $\#W_n\|L\|B$, where $\#W_n$ counts the derivative words of order at most $n$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.coefNorm.summary: Finite coefficient norms from the parent estimates

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.coef_bounds.text: Norms of a phase-independent coefficient, the Section 5 coefficient bound restated here with a vector-valued linear map $L$. For a smooth $G$ with uniformly bounded jets and $\ell^m|\nabla^mG(t,a)|\le B$ for $m\le n$, the field $(t,a,s)\mapsto L(G(t,a))$ has a finite norm (D.1) of order $n$, at most $\#W_n\,\|L\|\,B$, where $\#W_n$ is the number of admissible derivative words of order at most $n$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.coef_bounds.summary: Profile norms of phase independent coefficients

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.contDiff_slice.text: A jointly smooth field on a closed time slab has a smooth spatial slice at each time belonging to that slab. The proof composes with the constant-time inclusion, so the slab endpoints cause no spatial differentiability problem.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.contDiff_slice.summary: Spatial smoothness of a closed slab field

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.contDiff_slice_.text: A jointly smooth field on [a,b] × ℝ³ has a smooth spatial slice for every t in [a,b], including both endpoints. This supplies the cutoff argument with spatial regularity without extending time derivatives beyond the slab.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.curlCorrection_.text: The divergence correction $C[V]=\mathbf d\times Q[V]$ of a profile vanishing on the inactive region vanishes there (it centres its input and acts pointwise in time and label).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.curlCorrection_.summary: The divergence correction preserves the inactive region

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.cutoffPressureT.text: For $\Lambda\ge1$, $P\ge2$ and a field $V$ of class $C^{P,1/2}$ with cutoff $u=S_\Lambda V$, the product $\|u-V\|_{C^{1,1/2}}(\|u\|_{C^{1,1/2}}+\|V\|_{C^{1,1/2}})$ is at most $C(2+C)\Lambda^{2-P}(1+\|V\|_{C^{P,1/2}})^2$ with $C=C_t(P)$; the tail estimate (B.2) is a hypothesis.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.cutoffPressureT.summary: The quadratic velocity tail in the pressure estimate

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.cutoffVelocityD.text: For $m\le P$ and a field $V$ of class $C^{P,1/2}$, the difference $S_\Lambda V-V$ is $C^{m,1/2}$ with $\|S_\Lambda V-V\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\le C_t(P)\Lambda^{m-P}\|V\|_{C^{P,1/2}}$; the tail estimate (B.2) is a hypothesis.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.cutoffVelocityD.summary: The velocity change under Fourier truncation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.divergence_add_.text: The divergence is additive on differentiable fields.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.divergence_add_.summary: Divergence distributes over differentiable vector fields

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.envelopeSupport.text: The support $\operatorname{supp}g$ of the periodized radial envelope is invariant under translations by integer lattice vectors: $a\in\operatorname{supp}g$ exactly when $a+n\in\operatorname{supp}g$ for $n\in\mathbb Z^3$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.envelopeSupport.summary: The envelope support is invariant under lattice shifts

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.exists_closedSl.text: Continuous spatially periodic slices on a closed time interval descend to continuous functions on the unit torus. The selected family agrees with the original velocity at every time in the interval; no agreement outside that interval is claimed.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.exists_closedSl.summary: Representing every periodic time slice on the torus

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.exists_cutoffBo.text: Assume the cutoff tails satisfy $\|(I-S_\Lambda)f\|_{C^{s,1/2}}\le C_M\Lambda^{s-M}\|f\|_{C^{M,1/2}}$ for every $s\le M$, with $C_M\ge0$, for real vector fields and for complex matrix-valued fields, and assume the bilinear Hölder product inequality at every order. Let $P\ge2$, $\Lambda\ge1$, and let $V,R_V$ be jointly smooth periodic fields on $[0,T]$, $T>0$, with $\operatorname{div}V=0$. At each time let $\Pi$ be smooth and periodic and satisfy $V_t+V\cdot\nabla V+\nabla\Pi=R_V$. For an already constructed cutoff velocity $u=S_\Lambda V$ and its zero-mean Poisson pressure $p$, set $\varepsilon(t)=\Lambda^{2-P}(1+\|V(t)\|_{C^{P,1/2}})^2$. A constant $C$ chosen first and a constant $K_P$ chosen after $P$, both before $T,\Lambda,V$, give $\|u(t)-V(t)\|_{C^{2,1/2}}\le K_P\varepsilon(t)$. Each of $\|R_u(t)\|_{C^{1,1/2}}$ and $\|D^2(p-\Pi)(t)\|_{C^{0,1/2}}$ is separately at most $C\|R_V(t)\|_{C^{1,1/2}}+K_P\varepsilon(t)$, for each $t\in[0,T]$. The summed bound follows after enlarging constants. No time regularity of $\Pi$ and no radiality or range restriction on the symbol is a premise here; its tail bounds are supplied directly.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.exists_cutoffBo.summary: Control the velocity tail, residual, and pressure difference together

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.exists_mean_eul.text: The mean equation (5.11) is solvable, with the Eulerian form (4.12). This repeats the Section 5 solvability argument from Theorem 4.2, keeping the conjunct of its smooth-force item that the earlier version discarded: for a phase-independent source $\bar f$ there is a normalized solution $(B,\bar q)$ of (5.11) for which $b=B\circ X^{-1}$, $q=\bar q\circ X^{-1}$ and $f=\bar f\circ X^{-1}$ satisfy $\operatorname{div}b=0$ and the linearized Euler equation (4.12), the latter two being conclusions of Theorem 4.2 (a hypothesis) for the solution of (4.9) that gives $(B,\bar q)$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.exists_mean_eul.summary: Solving the mean equation through linearized Euler evolution

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.exists_realFour.text: For $T>0$, the cutoff velocity has a smooth, periodic, zero-mean Poisson pressure, $\Delta p=-\operatorname{tr}((Du)^2)$, whose momentum residual is (5.58). The band and divergence properties of the cutoff, and its commutation with time and space derivatives, are hypotheses (Lemma B.1).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.exists_realFour.summary: Constructing the zero mean pressure of the cutoff velocity

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.exists_torusVec.text: For a continuous torus vector field whose lift is C¹, its ith coordinate derivative is itself the lift of a continuous torus vector field. This supplies the input needed by the spatial derivative commutation clause of Lemma B.1.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.exists_torusVec.summary: A periodic coordinate derivative descends to the torus

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.expansionPressu.text: For profiles with $\bar q_1=0$, the expansion pressure splits as $\mathsf P=\mathsf p_1+\sum_{p\ge2}\mathsf p_p+\sum_{p\ge2}\bar q_p$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.expansionPressu.summary: Splitting the pressure into three contributions

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.expansion_eq_sp.text: For profiles with $B_1=0$, $W=V_1+(W_{\rm osc}-V_1)+\bar W$, where $W_{\rm osc}-V_1=\sum_{p=2}^PV_p+\sum_{p=1}^PC_{p+1}$ and $\bar W=\sum_{p=2}^PB_p$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.expansion_eq_sp.summary: Splitting the velocity into leading and remainder terms

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.fderivWithin_sl.text: The material derivative of (4.12) on the closed slab: for $b$ smooth on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3$, the derivative of $b$ in the space-time direction $(1,u)$ is $\partial_tb(t,x)+(Db)(t,x)u$, with the time derivative taken within $[0,T]$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.fderivWithin_sl.summary: Splitting the material derivative on a closed slab

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.fderiv_graphFie.text: The chain rule for the readout $y\mapsto G(Yy,k\cdot Yy)$ of a vector-valued field $G$ of label and phase, where $Y$ is the inverse flow at a fixed time.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.fderiv_graphFie.summary: Differentiating a vector field on the physical graph

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.fderiv_inverseF.text: The spatial derivative of the inverse flow $Y$ is $D_xY=G\circ Y$, where $G(t,a)=(D_aX(t,a))^{-1}=D_xY(X(t,a))$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.fderiv_inverseF.summary: The inverse deformation along the inverse flow

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.fderiv_left_com.text: At a point where f is differentiable, applying a fixed continuous linear map L commutes with taking the Fréchet derivative: the derivative is L composed with Df. It is used to move tensor-column projections through derivatives.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.fderiv_tensorCo.text: For a differentiable momentum-tensor field, differentiating its ith column in the ith coordinate direction equals taking the ith column of the tensor derivative in that direction. This permits the cutoff commutation argument to act column by column.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.fderiv_tensorCo.summary: Differentiation commutes with selecting a tensor column

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.fieldNormFinite.text: Finite norms (D.1) are closed under addition.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.fieldNormFinite.summary: Finite derivative norms persist under addition

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.fieldNormFinite.text: Finite norms (D.1) are closed under finite sums.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.fieldNormFinite.summary: Finite sums retain finite derivative norms

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.fieldNormFinite.text: The zero field has finite norms.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.fieldNormFinite.summary: The zero profile has finite derivative norms

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.fieldNorm_add_l.text: The norm (D.1) is subadditive on fields with finite norms.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.fieldNorm_add_l.summary: The triangle inequality for profile norms

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.fieldNorm_sum_l.text: The norm (D.1) of a finite sum of fields with finite norms is at most the sum of the norms.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.fieldNorm_sum_l.summary: Bounding the derivative norm of a finite sum

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.fieldNorm_zero.text: The zero field has norm zero.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.fieldNorm_zero.summary: The zero profile has zero derivative norm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.gradient_graphR.text:
The chain rule (3.1) for the gradient of the physical readout of a scalar profile $f$: $
abla_xf^
atural=(\mathbf df+\kappa\partial_sf)^
atural$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.gradient_graphR.summary: The pressure gradient along the physical graph

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.graphRead_slice.text: The Eulerian readout $f^\natural(t)$ of a twisted profile, obtained by evaluating the profile at the label $X(t\to0)(x)$ and the phase $k_*\cdot X(t\to0)(x)$, is smooth on $\mathbb R^3$ at each time of the slab.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.graphRead_slice.summary: Smoothness of a physical graph evaluation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.hessianSub.text: For two C² scalar pressures p and q, the Hessian of p−q is the difference of their Hessians. This algebraic identity separates the cutoff pressure error from the approximate pressure before the one-sided comparison is added.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.hessianSub.summary: Taking the Hessian of a pressure difference

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.higherHessianCl.text:
On $[0,T]	imes\mathbb T^3$, $0<T\le1$, let $U,p_U$ be smooth, $U$ odd and solenoidal, $X$ its flow, and $R_U=U_t+U\cdot
abla U+
abla p_U$ odd. Assume $\mathsf D\ge2$, Fourier radii $2\mathsf D,4\mathsf D$ for $U,R_U$, $\|
abla U\|_\infty,\|DX\|_\infty,\|DX^{-1}\|_\infty\le\mathsf D$, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. Write $M=
abla U\circ X$, $\kappa=DX^{-T}k_*$, $|\kappa(t_0,0)|=\lambda\ge1$, $0\le t_0<T$. At the origin, a nonzero transverse seed solves $\mathbf a_t=-(I-2P_\kappa)M\mathbf a$, with $P_\kappa=\kappa\otimes\kappa/|\kappa|^2$, $\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a|\le1$, and $\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a\ge\mathsf D^{-1}|\kappa||\mathbf a|$. Every transverse solution $\mathbf b$ of that homogeneous equation must satisfy $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$. For a depth-$P\ge2$ expansion with sufficiently small $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$ and $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, the conclusion is $\|D^2\sum_{p=2}^P\mathsf p_p^
atural\|_\infty\le K_P\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-5/12}$ on $[0,T]$. It assumes $\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$; the exponent and constants are selected before the parent and expansion. The formal implication assumes Propositions 5.1 and 5.4, Theorem 5.6, and Lemmas 5.7 and D.1.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.higherHessianCl.summary: Replace one phase derivative using the transverse pressure equation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.idB.text:
The identity of the space of linear maps of $\mathbb R^3$, viewed as the bilinear map $(A,v)\mapsto Av$.

This is a total algebraic or continuous-linear construction with no division or noncanonical choice. Zero inputs have their literal algebraic values. Any geometric identification or differentiability property is supplied separately by the consuming theorem.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.idB.summary: Applying a coefficient operator to a vector

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.inactiveVP.text:
The inactive region $\{t<t_0\}\cup\{a\notin\operatorname{supp}g\}$ of the slab, as the linear subspace of profiles vanishing there.

The vanishing submodule is defined by pointwise equalities before activation or outside the periodized envelope support. It imposes no condition on active points inside the support. Derivative closure uses the open complementary region and profile smoothness.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.inactiveVP.summary: Profiles vanishing before activation or outside the envelope

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.inactive_of_pro.text: Proposition 5.4 gives support of the sources and completed oscillatory sum, rather than all separate pressures. This lemma recovers the vanishing of $V_p$, $\mathsf p_p$ and $C_p$ individually by starting with the leading pair and applying uniqueness of the zero-initial transverse solve at each level. The inactive region combines $t<t_0$ with labels outside the periodized envelope support.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.inactive_of_pro.summary: Recovering individual supports from the hierarchy support theorem

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.inner_carrier_f.text: The phase gradient is the transported wave vector: for every vector $v$, $k_*\cdot D_xY\,v=\kappa(t,Y(x))\cdot v$, where $Y$ is the inverse flow.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.inner_carrier_f.summary: The carrier pulls back to the transported wave vector

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.inverseDeformat.text: The inverse deformation $G(t,\cdot)=(D_aX(t,\cdot))^{-1}$ of the parent flow is a smooth function of the label at each time.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.inverseDeformat.summary: Smoothness of the inverse deformation field

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.inverseFlow_lat.text: The inverse label flow is lattice equivariant.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.inverseFlow_lat.summary: The inverse flow respects lattice translations

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.inverseFlow_ori.text: The inverse label flow fixes the origin.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.inverseFlow_ori.summary: Oddness fixes the origin under the inverse flow

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.inverseFlow_rig.text: For the inverse flow $Y=X(t\to0)$ one has $X(t,Y(x))=x$ for every point $x$: following a physical point back to its label and then forward again returns the point.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.inverseFlow_rig.summary: The inverse flow is a right inverse of the flow

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.inverseFlow_smo.text: The inverse label flow $Y(t)=X(t\to0)$ of a parent, sending a physical point at time $t$ back to its label, is jointly smooth in time and space on the slab.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.inverseFlow_smo.summary: Smoothness of the inverse parent flow

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.isClosed_envelo.text: The support $\operatorname{supp}g$ of the periodized radial envelope is a closed subset of the label space $\mathbb R^3$.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.jet_one_le.text: The first derivative of a smooth function $Q$ of label and phase, applied to a direction $(\alpha,\sigma)$, is at most $A(|\alpha|/\ell+|\sigma|/h)$ when the scaled jets of $Q$ up to an order $n\ge1$ are bounded by $A$, for positive $\ell,h$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.jet_one_le.summary: Bounding a directional derivative from scaled jets

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.labelB.text:
For each coordinate index $j$, the bilinear map $(A,r)\mapsto rA^{\mathsf T}e_j$ on pairs of a linear map of $\mathbb R^3$ and a real number.

This is a total algebraic or continuous-linear construction with no division or noncanonical choice. Zero inputs have their literal algebraic values. Any geometric identification or differentiability property is supplied separately by the consuming theorem.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.labelB.summary: A scalar coefficient times a transposed coframe column

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.labelB_apply.text: Evaluation formula for the bilinear label map with index $j$: applied to a linear map $A$ and a real number $r$ it gives $rA^{\mathsf T}e_j$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.labelB_apply.summary: Evaluating the label gradient bilinear map

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.labelFlow_eq.text: Two label flows of a velocity field that is uniformly Lipschitz in space on $[0,T]$ agree on $[0,T]$.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.labelGrad_mem_i.text: The label gradient $\mathbf dq$ of a profile $q$ vanishing on the inactive region also vanishes there.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.labelGrad_mem_i.summary: Label gradients preserve vanishing in the inactive region

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.labelPaths_eqOn.text: Two particle paths with the same initial value and the same uniformly spatially Lipschitz velocity agree on the specified closed interval. The proof uses uniqueness for the time-dependent ODE, then extends equality from the initial point across the interval.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.labelPaths_eqOn.summary: Uniqueness of uniformly Lipschitz particle paths

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.labelPhaseUnsca.text:
The inverse of the label-phase scaling $(x,s)\mapsto(\ell x,hs)$, that is the linear map $(x,s)\mapsto(\ell^{-1}x,h^{-1}s)$.

This linear map uses the total reciprocals $\ell^{-1}$ and $h^{-1}$; if either scale is zero its corresponding component collapses. The cancellation theorem explicitly assumes nonzero scales, and the analytic applications use positive $\ell$ and $h$.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.le_abs_rpow_of_.text: For $\lambda\ge1$ and real exponents with $e_1+e_2\le e$, one has $K\mathsf D^C\lambda^{e_1}\lambda^{e_2}\le|K|\mathsf D^C\lambda^e$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.le_abs_rpow_of_.summary: Absorbing smaller frequency powers into a common bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.leadingHessianC.text:
On $[0,T]	imes\mathbb T^3$, $0<T\le1$, let $U,p_U$ be smooth, $U$ odd and solenoidal, $X$ its flow, and $R_U=U_t+U\cdot
abla U+
abla p_U$ odd. Assume $\mathsf D\ge2$, Fourier radii $2\mathsf D,4\mathsf D$ for $U,R_U$, $\|
abla U\|_\infty,\|DX\|_\infty,\|DX^{-1}\|_\infty\le\mathsf D$, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. Write $M=
abla U\circ X$, $\kappa=DX^{-T}k_*$, $|\kappa(t_0,0)|=\lambda\ge1$, $0\le t_0<T$. At the origin, a nonzero transverse seed solves $\mathbf a_t=-(I-2P_\kappa)M\mathbf a$, with $P_\kappa=\kappa\otimes\kappa/|\kappa|^2$, $\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a|\le1$, and $\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a\ge\mathsf D^{-1}|\kappa||\mathbf a|$. Every transverse solution $\mathbf b$ of that homogeneous equation must satisfy $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$. For a depth-$P\ge2$ expansion with sufficiently small $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$ and $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, the conclusion is $D^2\mathsf p_1^
atural\le K\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-1/4}I$ on $[0,T]$. It assumes $\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$; the exponent and constants are selected before the parent and expansion. The formal implication assumes Lemmas 3.1, 5.3 and D.1, Proposition 5.1, and Theorem 5.6.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.leadingHessianC.summary: Positive coupling controls the only large pressure tensor by sign

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.leading_graph_h.text: The chain rule (3.1) at the origin for the leading oscillation: if $V_1$ has the cell values $\tilde\chi A_1=\tilde\chi g\,\mathbf a F_h$ of (3.7), then, for $t\in[t_0,T]$, $D_xV_1^\natural(t,0)=\tilde\chi(t)\,\mathbf a(t,0)\otimes\kappa(t,0)$. The inputs are $g(0)=1$ (from $0<\ell_*$), $F_h(0)=0$ and $F_h'(0)=1$ (Lemma 3.1, here hypotheses), the fixed origin of the inverse flow, and $\kappa(t,0)=(D_xX(t\to0)(0))^{\mathsf T}k_*$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.leading_graph_h.summary: The leading wave gives the exact central rank one derivative

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.leading_hess_po.text: The Hessian (5.51) at one point. For the vector fields $G_1=\mathbf dq$, $G_2=\kappa\partial_sq$ of the label and phase gradient, read on the graph $\Phi(y)=(Yy,k\cdot Yy)$, the quadratic form of the derivative of $y\mapsto G_1(\Phi y)+G_2(\Phi y)$ is the phase term $c\sigma^2$ of $G_2$ (with $\partial_sG_2=c\,\kappa$ and $\sigma=\kappa\cdot v=k\cdot D_xY\,v$: the first tensor of (5.51)) plus the terms bounded by the scaled jets of order one of $G_1$ (all components) and of $G_2$ (label components only): the remaining tensors of (5.51).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.leading_hess_po.summary: Separating the signed leading pressure Hessian tensor

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.lemma59_of_clai.text: Lemma 5.9 from its four parts. Estimate (5.49) is the sum of the three Hessian bounds; (5.50) is the central return claim. The constants are $a_0$, the maximum of the four exponents; $b_0=\max(C_1+C_2+C_3,\,b_0^{(5.50)})$; and $\Gamma_0(P)=\max\big(1+|K_1|+|K_2(P)|+|K_3(P)|,\,\Gamma_0^{(5.50)}(P)\big)$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.lemma59_of_clai.summary: Combining the three pressure bounds and central return

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.levelK.text:
The level constant of (5.52): $3c_1\kappa_0|K_6(2,p)|+(c_1\kappa_0+c_1c_4\kappa_0^2)|K_6(1,p)|$, where $c_1,c_4$ are the order-one product constants of (D.4) and $\kappa_0$ is the coefficient constant.

The definition uses finite word counts and total real arithmetic. Maxima or absolute values, where present, ensure the chosen majorants remain nonnegative; the formula itself is not a proof that an arbitrary input constant bounds a field. The analytic estimates provide the corresponding coefficient or level bounds.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.levelK.summary: The constant in one higher pressure estimate

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.levelK_nonneg.text: For all input constants $K_1,K_6$ and every level $p$, the level constant $3c_1\kappa_0|K_6(2,p)|+(c_1\kappa_0+c_1c_4\kappa_0^2)|K_6(1,p)|$ of (5.52) is nonnegative.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.levelK_nonneg.summary: Nonnegative constants for the higher pressure levels

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.level_estimate.text: Real arithmetic for one level: with $B_c\ell_*^{-1}\le\kappa_0Z$, $B_c\le\kappa_0Z$ and $B_c^2\le\kappa_0^2Z$, the level term in the bound for the summed higher pressure gradient profile is at most $(3c_L\kappa_0|K_2|+(c_P\kappa_0+c_Pc_M\kappa_0^2)|K_1|)ZX$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.level_estimate.summary: The frequency powers of one higher pressure level

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.meanHessianClai.text:
On $[0,T]	imes\mathbb T^3$, $0<T\le1$, let $U,p_U$ be smooth, $U$ odd and solenoidal, $X$ its flow, and $R_U=U_t+U\cdot
abla U+
abla p_U$ odd. Assume $\mathsf D\ge2$, Fourier radii $2\mathsf D,4\mathsf D$ for $U,R_U$, $\|
abla U\|_\infty,\|DX\|_\infty,\|DX^{-1}\|_\infty\le\mathsf D$, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. Write $M=
abla U\circ X$, $\kappa=DX^{-T}k_*$, $|\kappa(t_0,0)|=\lambda\ge1$, $0\le t_0<T$. At the origin, a nonzero transverse seed solves $\mathbf a_t=-(I-2P_\kappa)M\mathbf a$, with $P_\kappa=\kappa\otimes\kappa/|\kappa|^2$, $\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a|\le1$, and $\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a\ge\mathsf D^{-1}|\kappa||\mathbf a|$. Every transverse solution $\mathbf b$ of that homogeneous equation must satisfy $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$. For a depth-$P\ge2$ expansion with sufficiently small $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$ and $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, the conclusion is $\|D^2\sum_{p=2}^P ar q_p^
atural\|_\infty\le K_P\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-5/2}$ on $[0,T]$. It assumes $\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$; the exponent and constants are selected before the parent and expansion. The formal implication assumes Theorem 4.2, Theorem 5.6, and Lemmas 5.7 and B.1.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.meanHessianClai.summary: Use the summed mean equation and the periodic Poisson estimate

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.meanSolution_ad.text: Sums of two solutions of (5.11) are solutions with the summed source.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.meanSolution_so.text: The source of a solution of (5.11) is independent of the phase.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.meanSolution_so.summary: A mean solution has a phase independent source

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.meanSolution_su.text: Finite sums of solutions of (5.11) are solutions with the summed source.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.meanSolution_su.summary: Summing the mean equations over all retained levels

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.meanSolution_ze.text: Taking the source, the mean velocity and the mean pressure all equal to $0$ gives a solution of the mean equation (5.11): the zero pair solves it with source $0$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.meanSolution_ze.summary: The zero solution of the mean equation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.mem_inactive_of.text: A twisted profile vanishes on the inactive region as soon as it vanishes at its inactive points over the label cell (by the lattice twist of the profile and the periodicity of $\operatorname{supp}g$).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.mem_inactive_of.summary: Vanishing on one cell implies vanishing everywhere

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.mixedDirection_.text: The weighted directions of (D.1) are constant, hence smooth.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.mixedDirection_.summary: The scaled coordinate directions are smooth

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.momentum_realFo.text: The unprojected momentum identity behind (5.58): for the cutoff velocity $u=S_\Lambda V$, the sum $u_t+(u\cdot\nabla)u+S_\Lambda(\nabla p)$ equals the truncated residual expression, assuming the commutation of $S_\Lambda$ with first spatial derivatives (a clause of Lemma B.1) and zero divergence of $u$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.momentum_realFo.summary: The momentum identity before the Leray projection

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.negB.text:
The bilinear map sending a linear map $A$ and a vector $v$ to $-(Av+Av)=-2Av$.

This is a total algebraic or continuous-linear construction with no division or noncanonical choice. Zero inputs have their literal algebraic values. Any geometric identification or differentiability property is supplied separately by the consuming theorem.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.negB.summary: Twice the negative strain action on a vector

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.nonempty_trunca.text: The truncation of §5.7 exists as a child stage. The cutoff of each time slice is constructed directly; oddness, divergence freeness and the band $2\Lambda$ of the cutoff velocity come from the parity, divergence and band clauses of Lemma B.1, taken as hypotheses, and the Poisson pressure from the zero-mean pressure construction for the cutoff velocity.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.nonempty_trunca.summary: Constructing the smooth truncated child stage

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_adjL_le.text: The transposition map $A\mapsto A^{\mathsf T}$, as a continuous linear map on linear maps of $\mathbb R^3$, has operator norm at most one.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_adjL_le.summary: Transposition has operator norm at most one

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_carrier_le.text: The carrier satisfies $|k_*|\le\mathsf D\lambda$: indeed $k_*=D_aX(t_0,0)^{\mathsf T}\kappa(t_0,0)$ with $|\kappa(t_0,0)|=\lambda$, and (5.1) bounds the deformation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_carrier_le.summary: The carrier size is controlled by the parent deformation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_fderiv2_in.text: The second spatial derivative of the inverse flow satisfies $|D_x^2Y|\le\mathsf D B$ when the label derivative of $G=(D_aX)^{-1}$ is bounded by $B$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_fderiv2_in.summary: Bounding the second derivative of the inverse flow

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_fderiv_gra.text: (5.44) at $m=1$, left side: the operator norm of $D_xf^\natural(t,0)$ is at most the sum, over the three coordinate directions, of the suprema of the first coordinate derivatives of $f^\natural(t)$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_fderiv_gra.summary: Profile words bound the derivative on the graph

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_fderiv_inv.text: The spatial derivative of the inverse flow satisfies $|D_xY|\le\mathsf D$, which is the bound (5.1) for $(D_aX)^{-1}$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_fderiv_inv.summary: The parent bound controls the inverse deformation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_fderiv_le_.text: For a field with a bounded first derivative, the operator norm of the derivative at a point is at most the sum, over the coordinate derivatives of order one, of the suprema appearing in (5.44) at $m=1$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_fderiv_le_.summary: First coordinate words control the derivative norm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_idB_le.text: The evaluation bilinear map $(A,v)\mapsto Av$ on linear maps and vectors of $\mathbb R^3$ has norm at most one.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_idB_le.summary: Operator evaluation has bilinear norm at most one

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_iteratedFD.text: The iterated derivatives of a smooth function $Q$ of label and phase from those of its scaled form: if the scaled jets up to order $n$ are bounded by $A$, then for $j\le n$ the $j$th derivative applied to directions $(\alpha_i,\sigma_i)$ is at most $A\prod_i(|\alpha_i|/\ell+|\sigma_i|/h)$, for positive $\ell,h$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_iteratedFD.summary: Unscaled derivatives from scaled jet bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_labelB_le.text: For each coordinate index $j$, the bilinear label map $(A,r)\mapsto rA^{\mathsf T}e_j$ has norm at most one.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_labelB_le.summary: The label gradient bilinear map is contractive

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_labelPhase.text: Norm bound for the unscaling of the label-phase jet.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_labelPhase.summary: Bounding the inverse label and phase scaling

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_labelWord_.text: A weighted label derivative word of length $|w|$ applied to a smooth phase-independent field is at most $r^{|w|}$ times the norm of the full spatial derivative (Fréchet jet) of the same order.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_labelWord_.summary: Scaled label words are bounded by Fréchet jets

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_negB_le.text: The bilinear map $(A,v)\mapsto-2Av$ on linear maps and vectors of $\mathbb R^3$ has norm at most two.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_negB_le.summary: Twice the strain action has norm at most two

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_waveVector.text: The transported wave vector satisfies $|\kappa(t,a)|\le\mathsf D^2\lambda$, from (5.3) together with (5.1).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_waveVector.summary: The transported wave vector obeys the parent bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.odd_lift_of_cut.text: The parity clause of Lemma B.1 makes the cutoff of an odd lifted field odd: if $g(-x)=-g(x)$ on $\mathbb R^3$, then $S_\Lambda g(-x)=-S_\Lambda g(x)$. This replaces the corresponding direct oddness statement for the real vector cutoff.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.opNorm_le_sum_c.text: The operator norm of a derivative is at most the sum of its values on the coordinate vectors.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.opNorm_le_sum_c.summary: Coordinate values control the derivative operator norm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.parentGradient_.text: $\|\nabla U\|_{C^{0,1/2}}\le C\mathsf D^2$ for a smooth field with frequencies at most $4\mathsf D$ and $\|\nabla U\|_\infty\le\mathsf D$, from Bernstein's inequality (B.1), taken as a hypothesis; this repeats the earlier parent-gradient Hölder bound with its Bernstein step drawn from that hypothesis.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.parentGradient_.summary: Bernstein controls the parent gradient Hölder norm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.periodic_sliceT.text: If every time slice of a velocity is spatially periodic on a closed interval, then its time derivative taken within that interval is spatially periodic at every time in the interval. The statement accommodates the endpoint derivative used by the cutoff momentum equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.periodic_sliceT.summary: Closed slab time differentiation preserves spatial periodicity

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.phaseGrad_mem_i.text: The phase gradient $\kappa\partial_sq$ of a profile $q$ vanishing on the inactive region vanishes there (the inactive region does not depend on the phase).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.phaseGrad_mem_i.summary: Phase gradients preserve vanishing in the inactive region

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.phaseGrad_phase.text: On a phase line $q(a,s)=cP(s)$ with $P'=F$, the phase derivative of the gradient field $G_2=\kappa\partial_sq$ is $(cF'(s))\kappa$ (the first tensor $c_{\mathbf a}F_h'\kappa\otimes\kappa$ of (5.51)).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.phaseGrad_phase.summary: The phase derivative of the leading pressure gradient

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.phaseGrad_trans.text: The transverse equation (5.16): $\kappa\partial_s\mathsf p=P_\kappa(F-2MV)$ for a solution $(V,\mathsf p)$ of (5.15) with source $F$ of zero phase mean, where $P_\kappa=|\kappa|^{-2}\kappa\otimes\kappa$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.phaseGrad_trans.summary: Eliminating a pressure derivative with the transverse equation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.phaseMean_eq_av.text: The phase mean of a profile $W$, that is $\int_0^1W(t,a,s)\,ds$, is its average $\langle W\rangle$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.phaseMean_eq_av.summary: Identifying the pulled back mean velocity

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.phaseOscillatio.text: The oscillatory part of the pulled-back field $c=(D_aX)^{-1}(W+v\circ X)$ is $(D_aX)^{-1}(W-\langle W\rangle)$: the perturbation $v\circ X$ and the coefficient $(D_aX)^{-1}$ are independent of the phase, and the phase mean of the profile is the average $\langle W\rangle$ of the operators of the parent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.phaseOscillatio.summary: Identifying the pulled back oscillatory velocity

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.prodC1.text:
The constant $\#W_1\cdot2\cdot2$ of (D.4) at order one for a bilinear map of norm at most one (the factor $2\|B\|\le2$), where $\#W_1$ counts derivative words of length at most one in the label and phase directions.

The definition uses finite word counts and total real arithmetic. Maxima or absolute values, where present, ensure the chosen majorants remain nonnegative; the formula itself is not a proof that an arbitrary input constant bounds a field. The analytic estimates provide the corresponding coefficient or level bounds.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.prodC1.summary: The order one product constant for contractions

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.prodC1_nonneg.text: The order-one product constant $\#W_1\cdot2\cdot2$ of (D.4), used for bilinear maps of norm at most one, is nonnegative.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.prodC4.text:
The constant $\#W_1\cdot2\cdot4$ of (D.4) at order one for a bilinear map with $\|B\|\le2$, where $\#W_1$ counts derivative words of length at most one in the label and phase directions.

The definition uses finite word counts and total real arithmetic. Maxima or absolute values, where present, ensure the chosen majorants remain nonnegative; the formula itself is not a proof that an arbitrary input constant bounds a field. The analytic estimates provide the corresponding coefficient or level bounds.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.prodC4.summary: The order one product constant for twice an evaluation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.prodC4_nonneg.text: The order-one product constant $\#W_1\cdot2\cdot4$ of (D.4), used for bilinear maps of norm at most two, is nonnegative.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.prodC4_nonneg.summary: Nonnegative product constants for doubled evaluation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.profileDivergen.text: The vanishing of the total divergence $\tilde{\mathbf d}\cdot W$ of a profile, read along the parent flow: $\operatorname{div}_yW(t,X(t,0)y,s)+((D_aX)^{-\mathsf T}k_*)\cdot\partial_sW=0$ at $y=X(0,t)a$. This is the same computation as in the physical approximation of the hierarchy, carried out for an arbitrary twisted profile.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.profileDivergen.summary: The profile divergence identity along the parent flow

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.profile_slice_s.text: A slice of a twisted profile is smooth in label and phase.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.profile_slice_s.summary: Smoothness of every label and phase slice

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.profile_sum_app.text: Evaluation of a finite sum of profiles.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.profile_sum_app.summary: Evaluating finite sums of hierarchy profiles

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.profile_sum_eva.text: Evaluation of a finite sum of twisted profiles.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.projectedMoment.text: The projected momentum identity after truncation: if the projection removes the cut-off pressure gradient, then the projected momentum $u_t+(u\cdot\nabla)u$ of $u=S_\Lambda V$ equals the projected truncated residual. The commutation of $S_\Lambda$ with first spatial derivatives (Lemma B.1) is a hypothesis.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.projectedMoment.summary: The projected momentum identity after truncation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.quarter_pow.text: Power identity for the exponent $1/4$: for $\lambda\ge0$ and a natural number $n$, the real power $\lambda^{n/4}$ equals the $n$th power of $\lambda^{1/4}$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.quarter_pow.summary: The fourth root representation of the frequency

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.quarter_pow_neg.text: Negative-exponent form of the fourth-root power identity: for $\lambda\ge0$, the real power $\lambda^{-n/4}$ is the reciprocal of the $n$th power of $\lambda^{1/4}$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.quarter_pow_neg.summary: Inverse frequency powers through the fourth root

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.radialEnvelope_.text: On the label cell, the radial envelope vanishes outside $\operatorname{supp}g$, using $2\ell_*<1/2$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.radialEnvelope_.summary: The radial envelope vanishes outside its support

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.realTensorCutof.text: The tail of the real tensor cutoff $R\circ S_\Lambda\circ J$, obtained from the complex estimate (B.2) (a hypothesis, Lemma B.1) by composing with the bounded maps $J$ and $R$ with $R\circ J=\mathrm{id}$: for $\Lambda>0$ and $s\le M$ the tail is bounded by $\|R\|\|J\|C_t(M)\Lambda^{s-M}$ times the $C^{M,1/2}$ norm.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.realTensorCutof.summary: Transferring the complex cutoff tail to real tensors

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.realVectorFouri.text: The cutoff commutes with the tensor divergence appearing in (5.58): the divergence of the cut-off momentum tensor equals the cutoff of the divergence. The commutation of the real cutoff with the coordinate derivatives is a hypothesis (the corresponding clause of Lemma B.1).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.realVectorFouri.summary: The cutoff commutes with tensor divergence

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.remainder_bound.text: Real arithmetic for the remaining tensors of (5.51): with $D,r\ge1$, $\ell^{-1}=D^a$, $h^{-1}=r^2$, $\lambda=r^4$ and the coefficient norms $B_c=c_ck_BD^{C_1}$, $B_\kappa=c_cDr^4k_BD^{C_1}$, the sum of the two terms is at most $28c_1c_ck_BD^Nr^6W\|v\|^2$ for $C_1+2a+2\le N$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.remainder_bound.summary: Estimating the two remaining leading Hessian tensors

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.scaledJets_appl.text: Scaled jets of $G(a)F(a,s)$: Leibniz' rule for the evaluation of a label-dependent operator $G$ on a profile $F$, with $|\ell|\le1$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.scaledJets_appl.summary: Leibniz bounds for the inverse deformation times a profile

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.scaledJets_of_u.text: The scaled jets of a twisted profile at a time $t\in[0,T]$, that is its derivatives in the scaled variables $(\ell a,hs)$, are bounded by its unweighted norm (D.1).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.scaledJets_of_u.summary: Unweighted profile norms bound the scaled jets

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.scaledJets_of_w.text: The scaled jets of a twisted profile at a time $t\in[t_0,T]$ are bounded by its weighted norm (D.1), for a weight satisfying $0<\gamma\le1$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.scaledJets_of_w.summary: Weighted profile norms bound the scaled jets

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.scaled_unscale.text: Scaling then unscaling a jet is the identity.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.slice_smooth_c.text: A jointly smooth field on the slab is smooth at each time.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.slice_smooth_c.summary: Spatial smoothness of a coefficient slice

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.slices_labelGra.text: On a time set $A\subseteq[0,T]$, the label gradient of a scalar profile expands as $\mathbf dq=\sum_j(\partial_{a_j}q)\,G^{\mathsf T}e_j$, with $G=(D_aX)^{-1}$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.slices_labelGra.summary: Expanding the label gradient into coefficient products

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.slices_phaseGra.text: For a transverse solution, $\kappa\partial_s\mathsf p=P_\kappa(F-2MV)$ on a time set $A\subseteq[0,T]$, written as the evaluation of the operator $P_\kappa$ on the vector $F+(-2MV)$, so that it is a product of a coefficient with a profile.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.slices_phaseGra.summary: The phase pressure gradient from the transverse equation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.spatialHolderHa.text: For a field with finite $C^{m,1/2}$ norm, sums the nonnegative derivative-level contributions. The finiteness hypothesis is retained because the norm uses real-valued suprema.
