Bernstein at order one, the band $2\lambda_n^5$ and the velocity bound give the estimate after absorbing a fixed constant into the growing frequency.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.eventually_ce.summary: Older central gradients satisfy the ninth-power bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.eventually_fi.text: Assume Lemmas 1.3, 2.2 and B.1 as hypotheses. For a fixed construction and any natural constant $C_0$, all sufficiently late physical waves satisfy the smallness condition (2.7) with that constant, namely $C_0\varepsilon\le1$ and $C_0T^{C_0}\delta\le\varepsilon$. The threshold may depend on $C_0$; there is no single stage asserted to work for every constant simultaneously. This exports comparison hypotheses needed by Proposition 8.2.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.eventually_fi.summary: Every fixed comparison constant works for sufficiently late waves

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.eventually_st.text: From Lemma B.1 and a construction, the central gradient and its time derivative satisfy $\lambda_n^9$ and $\lambda_n^{18}$ bounds for all sufficiently large $n$. The proof applies the stage-level derivative bounds from the residual identity after the frequency passes its threshold, reading smoothness, frequency support, divergence and residual identity from the construction's stages. No separate appeal to the conclusions of Theorem 7.1 is required.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.eventually_st.summary: Large stages satisfy both central gradient bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.exists_induct.text: Given positive $T$, all stage slabs covering it, square-separated frequencies, orders tending to infinity, and activation times converging to $T$, the stated increment and residual hypotheses produce a velocity limit. It is continuous on the closed slab and smooth with the actual projected Euler equation on $[0,T)$. Spatial derivatives converge uniformly only on strict prefixes. Periodicity, oddness and zero divergence pass from the stages.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.exists_induct.summary: The tower yields a continuous terminal velocity and preterminal Euler flow

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.exists_induct.text: Under the tower, oscillation, residual and schedule hypotheses, and the product estimate (5.59), there exist a velocity $u$ and pressure $p$ forming a classical Euler solution on $[0,T)$. The velocity is odd before $T$, extends continuously to the closed slab, and is the uniform stage limit there. Every finite spatial derivative and every Hölder norm converges on positive strict prefixes. The proof recovers pressure from the projected equation; it does not claim smoothness at $T$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.exists_induct.summary: The limit has an Euler pressure and Hölder convergence

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.firstWaveCove.text: The explicit covector is $\kappa(t)=\lambda(e_1-2\pi te_2)$. The definition allows any real $\lambda$, including zero; it does not itself assert a nonzero wave vector. The following nonvanishing and ODE lemmas supply the conditions needed when this formula is installed in the first wave's data at the origin.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.firstWaveCove.summary: The first covector along the stationary shear

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.firstWaveCove.text: This expands the explicit covector at each of the three axes into scalar coordinates. The first coordinate is $\lambda$, the second is $-2\pi t\lambda$ and the third is zero. The formula imposes no positivity condition; such conditions enter only when nonvanishing is required.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.firstWaveCove.summary: Coordinates of the initial shear covector

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.firstWaveCove.text: The inner product of the explicit covector and seed is zero for every frequency, tilt and time. The first two coordinate products cancel and the covector’s third coordinate vanishes. This calculation establishes perpendicularity directly; it does not invoke the propagation result of Lemma 2.1.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.firstWaveCove.summary: The explicit first pair stays perpendicular

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.firstWaveCove.text: Assuming $0<\lambda$, the explicit covector is nonzero at every time. Its first coordinate remains equal to the positive frequency, so a zero-vector equality would contradict $0<\lambda$. This hypothesis is required here even though the underlying formula is defined for zero frequency.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.firstWaveCove.summary: Positive frequency prevents a zero covector

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.firstWaveGaug.text: The scalar factor is $g(t)=(1+(2\pi t)^2)^{-1}$. It controls the first two coordinates of the explicit unnormalized seed and is defined for every real time. Positivity of its denominator will establish that the seed’s second coordinate never vanishes, which avoids a degenerate moving frame.

The scalar gauge is strictly positive at every real time, because its denominator is one plus a square. In the explicit seed this gauge is exactly the second coordinate. The theorem therefore supplies the nonvanishing argument without a restriction to the construction’s time interval.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.firstWaveGaug.summary: The first seed keeps a positive second coordinate

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.firstWaveOrig.text: For every real $\rho$, every $T\ge0$ and every $\lambda>0$, the formal theorem constructs nonzero perpendicular paths $\kappa,\mathbf a$ solving the central wave equations over $B_\rho=2\pi(e_1+\rho e_3)\otimes e_2$ on $[0,T]$. They start with $\kappa(0)=\lambda e_1$ and $\mathbf a(0)=c e_2$, $c>0$, and attain $\max_{[0,T]}|\mathbf a|=\lambda^{-3/4}$. The proof verifies explicit paths and rescales their positive maximum. The mathematical existence conclusion agrees with the other first-wave existence theorem; using explicit formulas is a difference of proof, not of statement. No short-interval condition is needed for existence, and $T=0$ is permitted. At $T=0$, derivatives within the singleton interval impose no evolution equation beyond the stipulated values.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.firstWaveOrig.summary: Constructs and normalizes the first wave for any positive frequency

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.firstWaveSeed.text: For tilt $s$, the seed is $g(t)(2\pi te_1+e_2)-s\arctan(2\pi t)e_3$. Its value at time zero is $e_2$. It is not yet normalized to the peak $\lambda^{-3/4}$: a later existence proof multiplies it by a positive constant obtained from its maximum on the chosen interval.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.firstWaveSeed.summary: An explicit seed before peak normalization

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.firstWaveSeed.text: The seed’s three coordinates are $2\pi tg(t)$, $g(t)$ and $-s\arctan(2\pi t)$. Tests on the coordinate index select each coordinate. This scalar form is used to verify orthogonality, nonvanishing and the differential equation directly for the first wave.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.firstWaveSeed.summary: Coordinates of the unnormalized first seed

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.firstWaveSeed.text: The explicit seed is nonzero for every real tilt and time. Its second coordinate is the gauge $g(t)>0$, so equality to the zero vector is impossible. This holds before normalization and supplies the positive maximum used when rescaling to the prescribed peak amplitude.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.first_couplin.text: Assume the frame identities of Lemma 2.2. Let the first central wave over $B_\rho=2\pi(e_1+\rho e_3)\otimes e_2$ start with $\kappa(0)=\lambda e_1$ and amplitude in the positive $e_2$ direction, and remain nonzero and transverse on $[0,T]$. If $\lambda>0$, $|\rho|\le1$ and $T\|B_\rho\|\le1/8$, then $E_1(t)\cdot B_\rho E_2(t)\ge\pi$ for every $t\in[0,T]$. The proof obtains $|E_1'|,|E_2'|\le\|B_\rho\|$ and a coupling variation of at most $2t\|B_\rho\|^2$. Only the final positivity bound is stated as the conclusion. The formal assumption on $\rho$ allows negative values and zero as well as the paper's range.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.first_couplin.summary: Uses the frame identities to preserve the first coupling

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.frame_axis_de.text: Under Lemma 2.2, a transverse wave pair over a trace-free gradient has a derivative for each frame axis on $J$. At any $t\in J$, one may choose its derivative vector with norm at most $2\|B(t)\|$. The proof uses the frame equations and orthonormality supplied by the lemma, retaining a uniform bound for all three axes.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.frame_axis_de.summary: Each moving axis turns at a controlled speed

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.hasDerivAt_fi.text: The formula for the first covector satisfies $\kappa_t=-B_s^T\kappa$ at every real time. The proof differentiates the affine formula and substitutes the explicit adjoint shear. No frequency positivity is needed for this equality, though a nonzero covector is required when constructing the moving frame.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.hasDerivAt_fi.summary: The explicit covector solves its transport equation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.hasDerivAt_fi.text: Assuming $0<\lambda$, the unnormalized seed has derivative given by the amplitude operator of (3.2), $\mathbf a\mapsto-B\mathbf a+2\frac{\kappa\cdot B\mathbf a}{|\kappa|^2}\kappa$, for the stationary shear and explicit covector. The calculation differentiates the gauge and arctangent, then clears the nonzero denominators. This verifies the seed equation directly and supplies the derivative identity used in the existence conjunct of Lemma 6.1.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.hasDerivAt_fi.summary: The explicit seed solves the amplitude equation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.increment_jet.text: From the increment clause of the conclusions of Theorem 7.1, this extracts a pointwise bound for the $m$th derivative of $U_{n+1}-U_n-O_{n+1}$. The assumptions include $m\le q_{n+1}$ and time membership in the new stage’s closed slab. Its bound is $\lambda_{n+1}^{-1}$, obtained by dropping the other terms of the Hölder norm.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.increment_jet.summary: Each corrected increment has small spatial derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.inner_vec3.text: For vectors $x$ and $y$ in $\mathbb R^3$, the real inner product is the sum of the three coordinate products. The finite-coordinate identity introduces no wave assumptions. It is the elementary calculation used to verify that the explicit first covector and seed remain perpendicular.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.inner_vec3.summary: The Euclidean inner product in three coordinates

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.lemma13_sched.text: Given the statement of Lemma 1.3 as a hypothesis, every parameter record has orders tending to infinity and satisfies $4\log\lambda_{i+3}\le(\log\lambda_i)^2$. The proof supplies the record fields to Lemma 1.3 and converts the paper index $j\ge1$ to $i+1$. It uses the lemma as a hypothesis rather than calling the formalization's own proof of it.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.lemma13_sched.summary: Slow orders control the later logarithmic gain

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.limit_agreeme.text: Assume the conclusions of Theorem 7.1, the conclusions of Proposition 8.1, and uniform convergence of the stage velocities to a field $w$ on the closed slab. Then $u(t)=w(t)$ for $0\le t<T$. The argument compares two pointwise limits, using order-zero Hölder convergence from Proposition 8.1; it does not identify the values of $u$ at or after $T$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.limit_agreeme.summary: The continuous terminal limit agrees before the endpoint

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.mFourierCoeff.text: For a continuous complex-linear map $L$ between complete normed complex spaces, the Fourier coefficient of $L\circ g$ equals $L$ applied to the coefficient of $g$. Compactness gives integrability and permits the map to pass through the integral. This allows vector Fourier-band information to be tested by scalar measurements.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.mFourierCoeff.summary: Fourier coefficients commute with linear measurements

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.nonneg_period.text: For every order $m$ and every witness of the product estimate (5.59), the combined momentum bound is nonnegative. The selected Hölder-product constant has a nonnegativity proof and the other factors are norms, a square root or a square. The theorem does not assert strict positivity or a sharp operator norm.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.nonneg_period.summary: The momentum jet bound is nonnegative

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.norm_advectio.text: Let $A$ be a half-Hölder field on the torus whose values are $Du\,u$. If the velocity, gradient and second derivative are bounded by nonnegative $M$, $B$ and $H$, then $\|A\|_{C^{0,1/2}}\le2(BM+B^2+HM)$. The proof combines a Lipschitz estimate at short distances with a sup-norm estimate at long distances.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.norm_advectio.summary: Velocity jets control the Hölder norm of self-advection

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.norm_fderiv_s.text: For a $C^2$ vector field, the derivative of $Du\,u$ is bounded by $\|Du\|^2+\|D^2u\|\,\|u\|$. The proof applies the product rule to evaluating the derivative map on the velocity. No periodicity or Euler equation is assumed; this is the local estimate used to control the parent’s projected momentum.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.norm_fderiv_s.summary: Differentiating self-advection costs two spatial derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.norm_periodic.text: For smooth periodic $u$ and $v$, the order-$m$ jet norm of their signed projected momentum $-\mathbb P\operatorname{div}(u\otimes v)$ is bounded by the momentum jet bound of order $m$ times their two order-$(m+2)$ jet norms. The proof explicitly obtains the product estimate from (5.59), then applies tensor divergence and Leray bounds. It is conditional on the cited estimate (5.59).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.norm_periodic.summary: Two extra spatial derivatives control the projected momentum

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.norm_realHalf.text: For a bounded half-Hölder vector field $f$ on the torus, the underlying continuous field has sup norm at most the endpoint half-Hölder norm of $f$. The Hölder norm already controls pointwise values, so the proof passes that bound through the characterization of the sup norm of continuous maps. This is used for the Leray-projected advection in the parent time-derivative estimate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.norm_realHalf.summary: The supremum norm is bounded by the Hölder norm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.norm_signed_t.text: Unit orthogonal axes $x$ and $y$ and coefficients $a$, $b$ are given. If their squared magnitudes match the corresponding squared components of $z$, then $\|ax+by\|\le\|z\|$. The signs may differ from the actual components. This estimate bounds the moving-frame derivative in the first-coupling proof.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.norm_signed_t.summary: Two orthogonal components cannot exceed the full length

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.norm_sq_vec3.text: For every vector $x\in\mathbb R^3$, its squared Euclidean norm equals the sum of its three squared coordinates. The proof reduces this identity to the preceding inner-product formula. The seed-equation calculation uses it to turn the pressure correction denominator into an explicit positive scalar expression.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.norm_sq_vec3.summary: The squared norm in three coordinates

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.opNorm_le_sum.text: The operator norm of a continuous real-linear map from $\mathbb R^3$ is at most the sum of its values on the three unit axes. The codomain is any real normed space. Expanding an input vector in coordinates and bounding each coordinate by its length supplies the conversion used after Bernstein’s coordinate estimates.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.opNorm_le_sum.summary: Coordinate directions bound the full operator norm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.parent_derive.text: Given Lemma B.1, choose a frequency threshold $N$. Smooth periodic parent data with velocity bound $\lambda$, band $2\lambda^5$, a small residual and the represented projected evolution satisfy gradient bounds $\lambda^9$ and $\lambda^{18}$ in space and time. The hypotheses include $0<T$, $N\le\lambda$, $1\le\lambda'$ for the next frequency $\lambda'$, and the projected equation on the closed slab. The time derivative is taken within the slab.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.parent_derive.summary: The projected equation bounds the parent gradient in time

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.periodicMomen.text: Given the formal statement of the product estimate (5.59), this chooses its product-estimate constant at order $m+1$ and combines it with the Leray, tensor-divergence and jet-to-Hölder bounds. The result is a scalar bound for projected momentum from order $m+2$ jets to order $m$ jets. Its value depends on the witness selected from (5.59).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.periodicMomen.summary: The product estimate supplies a momentum bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.periodicProje.text: On a positive closed prefix, assume smooth periodic stages, smooth limiting spatial slices, uniform convergence of every spatial derivative, uniformly vanishing residuals and the stage projected equation. The theorem returns the integrated limit equation, its time derivative and joint smoothness. The product estimate (5.59) is used in the momentum map; no symbolic residual replacement is used to assert the equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.periodicProje.summary: Vanishing residuals give an actual smooth projected Euler limit

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.periodicProje.text: With the product estimate (5.59), the signed projected momentum becomes a continuous bilinear map from two completed compatible jet spaces of order $m+2$ into the order-$m$ space. It is obtained by extending the bounded map on smooth jet tuples along their dense isometric inclusion. Later evaluation lemmas identify its values on smooth inputs with the actual spatial derivatives.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.periodicProje.summary: Projected momentum extends to compatible limiting jets

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.periodicProje.text: For smooth periodic inputs, the $i$th component of the completed momentum map at $x$ is $D^i[-\mathbb P\operatorname{div}(u\otimes v)](x)$. Here $i$ ranges over $0,\dots,m$, which restricts the output order. The equality identifies component values, rather than only matching norms or giving an abstract existence result.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.periodicProje.summary: Each output jet is the actual momentum derivative

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.periodicProje.text: Apply the completed momentum map to the compatible jets of smooth periodic fields $u$ and $v$. The result is exactly the order-$m$ jet tuple of their signed projected momentum $-\mathbb P\operatorname{div}(u\otimes v)$. Density-based extension therefore preserves the original operator, which is essential before using the jet-space evolution to infer regularity of the physical velocity.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.periodicProje.summary: The extended momentum agrees with smooth Euler momentum

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.preceding_str.text: Assume Lemma 2.2, a transverse nonzero wave solving the covector and amplitude equations over a trace-free gradient, and $\|B(t)\|\le\mu^{1/32}$. If $\mu\ge1$ and the interval length is at most $\mu^{-1/16}$, the strength stays above $e^{-1}$ times its left-endpoint strength. The log-strength equation from Lemma 2.2 controls the loss.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.preceding_str.summary: The preceding wave loses at most one exponential factor

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.proposition82.text: Assume Lemmas 1.3, 2.2, 2.4 and B.1, a common construction satisfying Theorem 7.1, and its smooth odd Euler limit $u$ from Proposition 8.1. Then $\sup_{0\le t<T_\infty}\|u(t)\|_\infty<\infty$ and $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\to\infty$. More precisely, there are fixed real $c>0,C$ such that, for every sufficiently large $j$ and every $t\in[t_j,t_{j+1})$, $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\ge c\lambda_{j-1}^{1/8}-C\lambda_{j-1}^{1/32}-C$. The constants precede the choice of $j$ and $t$. This estimate concerns the limiting solution, whereas (8.2) concerns $U_j$ and retains $\lambda_{j-2}^9$. The extra conclusion is used with crossing-time bounds to prove integral divergence. The supremum norm is the essential supremum over one spatial period.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.proposition82.summary: Retain a quantitative bound on each late activation interval

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.realHalfHolde.text: This definition regards a bounded half-Hölder field on the torus as a continuous torus field. It preserves every pointwise value while dropping the extra Hölder information. The conversion allows the projected advection term to be combined with a continuous residual when estimating the parent’s time derivative in the proof of (7.6).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.realHalfHolde.summary: Forget Hölder control while retaining the same field

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.realNormedBan.text: If the complexified vector Fourier coefficients of $g$ vanish above radius $R$, then every real continuous linear measurement of $g$ has the same frequency bound. The proof builds the corresponding complex-linear coordinate map and commutes it with Fourier coefficients. This converts the stage’s band condition into the normed-space band condition required by Lemma B.1.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.realNormedBan.summary: The vector frequency bound controls scalar measurements

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.slab_pos.text: Each slab endpoint in a construction is strictly positive. The zeroth slab is one; a later slab is its nonnegative activation time plus twice a positive half length from the construction's lifetime bounds. This prevents the closed-slab derivative arguments from being applied on an interval with zero or negative length.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.slab_pos.summary: Every stage slab has positive length

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.slab_succ_le.text: For every $i$, the endpoint $S_{i+2}$ is at most $S_{i+1}$. The activation increment is at most the old half length, while four times the next half length is at most the old one. The statement starts with the first positive-index slab and does not assert a separate comparison between $S_1$ and $S_0$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.slab_succ_le.summary: Later stage endpoints are nested from the first stage

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.stage_derived.text: Assuming Lemma B.1, a smooth periodic stage with bounded velocity, frequency support, zero divergence and Leray-projected momentum on the closed slab equal to its residual $R$ has central gradient and time-gradient bounds $\lambda_{\rm old}^9$ and $\lambda_{\rm old}^{18}$. The old frequency exceeds a chosen threshold and the next scale $\mu$ is at least one. The proof constructs the Hölder advection representative and torus residual needed by the parent-level derivative bound from the projected equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.stage_derived.summary: The stage residual identity yields the central derivative bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.stationaryShe.text: For every real tilt $s$, the adjoint shear maps $y$ to $2\pi\langle e_1+se_3,y\rangle e_2$. The proof identifies it through inner products rather than matrix entries. This is the operator that drives the covector equation $\kappa_t=-B_\rho^T\kappa$ in the explicit first-wave construction.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.stationaryShe.summary: The transposed shear points along the second axis

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.stationaryShe.text: The stationary shear gradient sends a vector $x$ to $2\pi x_2(e_1+se_3)$. Here $s$ is an arbitrary real tilt, and $x_2$ is the second coordinate. The identity expands the rank-one map used in (6.1), making the first-wave ODE calculation an explicit coordinate calculation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.stationaryShe.summary: The shear acts through the second coordinate

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.tendstoUnifor.text: Assume the product estimate (5.59), uniform convergence of compatible velocity jets through order two, and continuity of the limiting tuple on $[0,S]$. The projected quadratic momenta then converge uniformly in time at each fixed spatial point $x$. The proof applies the bounded bilinear momentum map and evaluates the zeroth output jet.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.tendstoUnifor.summary: Second-order jet convergence passes through the projected momentum

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.trace_station.text: The rank-one shear gradient has trace zero for every real tilt $s$. Its action is along the first and third axes and depends only on the second coordinate, so all diagonal entries vanish. The first-coupling proof supplies this identity to the trace-free hypothesis of Lemma 2.2.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.trace_station.summary: The stationary shear gradient is trace free

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.two_le_freque.text: For a parameter record, the initial frequency satisfies $2\le\lambda_0$. The logarithmic floor at order one and the stored bound $\mathcal B(1)\le\lambda_0$ supply the lower bound; the exponent parameter is already positive in the record. This is a consequence of the chosen schedule, not an additional assumption about a stage.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.two_le_freque.summary: The initial frequency is at least two

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.unitAxis.text: This abbreviation gives the coordinate vector $e_{i+1}$ in $\mathbb R^3$. The formalization indexes the axes from zero, so indices zero, one and two correspond to the paper’s first, second and third coordinates. It supplies the concrete vectors used to verify the first wave at the origin.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.wave_geometry.text: From Lemma 2.4, choose the lemma’s threshold $N$. A growing crossing with $N\le C_0$, $1\le C_0$, normalized length $T\ge2$, positive scale and the smallness condition (2.7) with constant $C_0$ has $|X|\le(2T)^2$, $|Q|\le2T$ and $|Z-1|\le1/2$ on its active slab. The equality of the observation set $I$ with the active slab of length $T$ is required to match the two domains.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678b.wave_geometry.summary: The new wave keeps a substantial third component

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.admissible_jet_.text: The hypothesis hb bounds the value sets of every admissible word through order n. For a word w in that set, its pointwise norm is bounded by the finite word norm; when holder holds, its spatial difference is bounded by the same norm times the square root of the distance. The case of equal points is separated before division by that square root.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.admissible_jet_.summary: Bound one derivative word by the finite norm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.appendSorted'.text: The definition appends the index i to a derivative word and sorts the resulting list. It supplies a canonical representative of the enlarged multi-index for display (D.2). The input word may be arbitrary; preservation of admissibility and injectivity are separate results with the required sorted-word hypotheses. Sorting itself is a finite combinatorial operation and asserts no commutation of derivatives.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.appendSorted'.summary: Insert one derivative direction into a sorted word

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.appendSorted'_i.text: For a fixed letter i, adjoining and sorting is injective on the admissible words through order n. The domain restriction matters: arbitrary differently ordered lists could have the same sorted output. Cancellation of the added letter gives a permutation of the old words, and their nondecreasing order upgrades that permutation to equality. The result controls multiplicities when summing the interpolation estimate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.appendSorted'_i.summary: Adding a fixed derivative direction preserves distinct words

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.appendSorted'_m.text: If w is an admissible nondecreasing word of length at most n, appending a letter and sorting yields an admissible word of length at most n + 1. The proof checks the new length and its sorted order separately. This lets the Hölder interpolation argument use one additional label derivative without leaving the supplied finite set of derivative bounds.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.appendSorted'_m.summary: The enlarged word remains admissible one order higher

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.appendSorted'_p.text: The sorted word obtained by adjoining i is a permutation of the original word followed by i. This is a combinatorial statement about lists, valid without a sortedness hypothesis on the input. It is later combined with commutation of constant-direction derivatives to identify the new word with a derivative of the old one.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.appendSorted'_p.summary: Sorting preserves the enlarged derivative multi-index

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.coefficientPowe.text: Assume $f$ is spatially smooth at every time, each $K_m$ is nonnegative, $\mathsf D$ is nonnegative, and $\|D^mf(t,x)\|\le K_m\mathsf D^{a(m+1)}$ bounds every derivative operator norm. The theorem obtains the power bound (D.6) with constants $K_m$ multiplied by the number of sorted coordinate words of length $m$. It proves boundedness of the sets whose suprema define the coefficient sizes before applying the supremum estimates, so those real-valued suprema carry their intended meaning.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.coefficientPowe.summary: Recover coefficient bounds from derivative operator bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.coefficientPowe.text: The hypothesis hc includes smoothness, bounded coordinate jets, and the coefficient estimate (D.6). It yields a pointwise operator bound for the mth derivative with an additional factor $3^m$. Sorting an ordered coordinate word preserves its derivative because the directions commute; the sum over all ordered tuples then accounts for that factor. The conclusion is a conversion of hc, not an independent construction of coefficient bounds.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.coefficientPowe.summary: Turn coefficient bounds into derivative operator bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.hierarchyJetVal.text: For a continuous bilinear map B, the smooth fields f and g have bounded derivatives for every admissible word up to n. The result proves boundedness for the product word, including half-Hölder quotients when holder is true. Leibniz bounds use all subwords of w, and admissibility of those subwords follows from their sorted order. This establishes finiteness separately from the product norm inequality.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.hierarchyJetVal.summary: Bound the derivative values of a bilinear product

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.hierarchyLabelD.text: Setting the label weight to one makes each hierarchy direction the corresponding constant coordinate vector. This function equality removes the weighting convention before ordinary coordinate calculus is applied. It does not assert a derivative bound or any property of a field; it identifies the two direction families used in the coefficient norms of Appendix D.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.hierarchyLabelD.summary: Unit weights give the coordinate directions

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.holderWord_le.text: For $0<\ell\le1$, the supremum values of one word and its three enlarged coordinate words control every half-Hölder quantity of that word by their sum divided by $\sqrt\ell$. The assumptions hbw and hbi provide the bounded suprema explicitly. The proof combines a uniform-value bound with a gradient bound and treats coincident points separately. Summing this per-word estimate gives display (D.2).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.holderWord_le.summary: One extra derivative gives a half Hölder word bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.jetValues_bdd_a.text: For one fixed word w, smoothness of f, g, and the directions combines with hbf and hbg to show that the derivative values of f + g are bounded above. The bound is the sum of the two existing suprema. The holder flag is fixed to False, so this lemma supplies supremum control only; the Hölder difference quotients are not part of its conclusion.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.jetValues_bdd_a.summary: Preserve bounded derivative values under addition

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.jetValues_bdd_d.text: Bounded weighted derivatives through order n + 1 give smoothness and bounded weighted derivatives through order n of the unweighted derivative in direction d i. The hypothesis hr requires the weight r i to be strictly positive. The proof first differentiates in the weighted direction, then multiplies by its reciprocal; this explicit hypothesis prevents the inverse at zero from being used as a derivative rescaling.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.jetValues_bdd_d.summary: Remove a direction weight from derivative bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.jetValues_bdd_s.text: Multiplying a smooth family by the real scalar c preserves boundedness of the quantities measured for a fixed derivative word. The proposition holder can include half-Hölder quotients as well as supremum values. The proof identifies the new set with the old set scaled by $|c|$, which is nonnegative. No positivity or nonzero condition on c is needed.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.jetValues_bdd_s.summary: Preserve bounded derivative values under scalar multiplication

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.list_eq_castSuc.text: A word in the four letters (three label directions and the phase direction) that contains no phase letter can be written as a word in the three label letters, each viewed as one of the first three of the four. Thus every mixed derivative word without the phase letter is a label word. This is a finite combinatorial helper; it asserts no differentiation, regularity, or norm bound.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.list_eq_castSuc.summary: Words without a phase letter use only label directions

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.norm_labelLinea.text: For a continuous linear map $A$ from three-dimensional Euclidean space to a real normed space, its operator norm is bounded by the sum $|Ae_1|+|Ae_2|+|Ae_3|$ of the three coordinate-direction values. The coordinate expansion and triangle inequality supply the bound. It turns the three extra word bounds in the Hölder word estimate into control of the full gradient required by Hölder interpolation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.norm_labelLinea.summary: Control a linear norm by coordinate derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.norm_sub_sqrt_o.text: Let $v:\mathbb R^3\to X$ be differentiable, where $X$ is a real normed space. Suppose $A,B\ge0$, $|v(x)|\le A$, and $\|Dv(x)\|\le B$ for every $x$, with the operator norm on the derivative. The formal statement proves $|v(x)-v(y)|\le\sqrt{2AB}\,|x-y|^{1/2}$ for all $x,y$. It combines the bounds $2A$ and $B|x-y|$ and yields the interpolation inequality preceding (D.2). The domain here is all of $\mathbb R^3$; periodicity and a time variable are unnecessary. The hypotheses are actual pointwise bounds, so no unproved supremum finiteness is implicit.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.norm_sub_sqrt_o.summary: Interpolates a uniform bound with a derivative bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.opNorm_le_coord.text: For a continuous multilinear map with $m$ arguments in three-dimensional space, the operator norm is at most the sum of its norms on all ordered coordinate tuples. The target $X$ is any real normed space, not necessarily an algebra. Expanding each argument in coordinates gives the estimate used for the pointwise bound on coefficient powers; all ordered tuples appear here, before any sorting.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.opNorm_le_coord.summary: Control a multilinear norm by coordinate values

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.phaseAverage_je.text: Assume each field is smooth, each phase slice is one-periodic, and the supremum value sets for every admissible word through n are bounded. The phase average is then smooth with bounded value sets for the same words. The proof commutes each word with averaging and bounds the integral by the original supremum. The flag is False, so no half-Hölder estimate is asserted here.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.phaseAverage_je.summary: Preserve smoothness and bounded jets under phase averaging

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.phaseMeanTransl.text: At a point x in label–phase space, this definition integrates f at x + (0,r) over one phase period. It retains the starting phase in x until periodicity is supplied by a later theorem. Smoothness permits differentiation under the integral, and periodicity then identifies this translated mean with the phase-independent average used in Lemma D.1.

For a smooth f and any fixed direction d in label–phase space, the directional derivative of the translated phase average equals the translated average of the directional derivative. The proof first differentiates the parameter integral, then moves evaluation at d through the integral. Both arguments use continuity on the integration interval, while phase periodicity is unnecessary for this identity.

If each phase slice of f is one-periodic, averaging f after an arbitrary phase translation gives its ordinary phase mean at the same label. The result identifies the two integral representations used in Lemma D.1. It makes no smoothness claim and does not establish the derivative or norm estimates; those follow from the separate smoothness and boundedness lemmas.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.phaseMeanTransl.summary: Remove the starting phase from a periodic average

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.phaseMeanTransl.text: A smooth field f on label–phase space has a smooth translated phase average. The target is a complete real normed space, so integration of its values is available with the usual smooth-parameter integral theorem. This statement does not require phase periodicity: smoothness follows from integrating translations over the fixed compact interval alone.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.phaseMeanTransl.summary: Smoothness passes through the translated phase average

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.phaseMeanTransl.text: For a family of constant directions d and a finite word w, applying that word to the translated phase average equals averaging the corresponding derivative word of f. Smoothness hf lets the one-derivative commutation theorem be reapplied at each stage. The index type J is arbitrary, and the statement does not impose an order on the word.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.phaseMeanTransl.summary: Commute every derivative word with phase averaging

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.phaseOperatorWo.text: A word of directional derivatives applied to the sum of two smooth fields is the sum of their words. The direction fields themselves must be smooth, by hypothesis; they need not be constant or commuting for this additive identity. Induction on the word uses the derivative of a sum at each step. The result supplies finiteness estimates in Lemma D.1.

For a smooth spatial field $f$ and an ordered tuple $\beta$ of $m$ coordinate indices, the unweighted derivative word equals the $m$th Fréchet derivative evaluated on those coordinate vectors $e_{\beta_1},\dots,e_{\beta_m}$. Smoothness of $f$ is a hypothesis, and the tuple is turned into the list $(\beta_1,\dots,\beta_m)$ expected by the derivative-word notation. This identifies the word notation with the coordinate derivatives used in Lemma D.2.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.phaseOperatorWo.summary: Read coordinate words as iterated derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.spatialHolderHa.text: A continuous linear map $L$ satisfying the pointwise contraction bound $\|Lv\|\le\|v\|$ preserves spatial $C^{m,1/2}$ regularity and does not increase the $C^{m,1/2}$ norm. The proof moves $L$ through each derivative and each spatial increment. In Lemma B.1 this transfers cutoff estimates through complexification and the real-part map. No Fourier-support or cutoff assumption belongs to this general composition lemma.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.sumCoordinateDi.text: Every vector in the Euclidean model of the torus is the sum of its three coordinates times the coordinate directions. The proof evaluates each coordinate after moving the projection through the finite sum. This supplies the elementary expansion used to compare derivative operator norms with coordinate partial derivatives in Lemma D.2.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.sumCoordinateDi.summary: Resolve a vector into coordinate directions

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.word_eq_zero_of.text: If a word contains a letter whose entire direction field is zero, its iterated directional derivative is the zero function. The statement needs no smoothness: any continuous-linear derivative applied to the zero vector is zero, including a totalized derivative value. In the phase-independent reduction the phase direction becomes the zero label direction.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.word_eq_zero_of.summary: A zero direction annihilates the derivative word

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.word_fst_of_con.text: For a smooth label field $f$, a family of constant directions $d_i$ in label × phase space and any word $w$, differentiating $(a,s)\mapsto f(a)$ along the $d_i$ equals differentiating $f$ along their label components and then composing with the projection $(a,s)\mapsto a$. Time and norms do not enter this identity. It supplies the chain rule used to remove the phase variable from a phase-independent field.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.word_fst_of_con.summary: Constant mixed derivatives restrict to the label directions

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.word_map_letter.text: For any direction family D, letter map e, word w and function f, applying the word w after replacing every direction by D(e i) equals applying the mapped word to D. No smoothness is assumed because this is a definitional rearrangement of the same total derivative operators. It is bookkeeping for derivative words, not a separate analytical estimate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.SBD.word_map_letter.summary: Renaming derivative directions leaves their composition unchanged

TorusEuler.Paper.MeanParentFlow.text: The setting is $0<T\le1$ and a velocity $u$ smooth on the closed slab $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3$, periodic under integer translations and divergence free. A supplied family $X_{s,t}$ is the particle flow of $u$. The paper's map is $X(t,a)=X_{0,t}(a)$, while $X_{t,0}$ is the reverse map. Thus the domain is $\mathbb T^3=\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3$, represented by periodic lifts. This precisely records the standing setting of §4; no Euler equation or bound on $H^\#$ is included here.
TorusEuler.Paper.MeanParentFlow.summary: Specify a smooth incompressible parent and its flow

TorusEuler.Paper.ModelCase.text: For the preceding wave’s moving frame and its positive activation couplings $\nu=B_{12}(t_0)$ and $\eta=B_{32}(t_0)$, the formal condition requires $B_{12}(t_0+\tau/r)=\nu$, $B_{32}(t_0+\tau/r)=\eta$, all other frame entries zero, and $E_c(t_0+\tau/r)=0$ for every $0\le\tau\le T$. These are the model assumptions of Lemma 2.3, in a frame that may itself rotate. The condition does not mean that $B$ is constant in fixed spatial coordinates. It neither constructs a new wave nor asserts that the physical interval lies in the compact set where the preceding wave equations are assumed; both are separate hypotheses.
TorusEuler.Paper.ModelCase.summary: Only two entries of the older gradient survive in the model case

TorusEuler.Paper.NewWaveVector.text: The formal condition requires $\lambda>0$, $k(t_0)=\lambda E_3(t_0)$ and $k'=-M^Tk$ throughout the compact physical time set $I$, where $M=B+\mathbf a_p\otimes k_p+E_c$ and $E_3$ is the preceding wave’s third unit direction. Derivatives are taken relative to $I$. This matches the wave-vector data in §2.2.1. No amplitude or amplitude initial value is specified. The path $k$ is formally defined for all real times, but the equation is required only on $I$; the amplification theorems separately require $[t_0,t_0+T/r]\subseteq I$.
TorusEuler.Paper.NewWaveVector.summary: The new wave vector solves its transport equation with a prescribed direction

TorusEuler.Paper.ProfileFamily.text: This condition on two real families $F_h,P_h$ states all properties in Lemma 3.1. For $0<h\le1$, $F_h$ is smooth, odd and period one, while $P_h$ is smooth, period one, has mean zero over $[0,1]$, and satisfies $P_h'=F_h$. A single positive $C$, independent of $h$ and phase, gives $F_h'(0)=1$, $-Ch\le F_h'\le1$ and $|F_h|\le Ch$. For each integer $j\ge2$, a positive $C_j$ independent of $h,s$ gives $|\partial_s^jF_h|\le C_jh^{1-j}$. The exponent is an integer, so it is negative when $j\ge2$. Pointwise phase bounds encode the supremum bounds. This condition does not itself assert that such a family exists.
TorusEuler.Paper.ProfileFamily.summary: Uniform constants describe the profiles and their normalized primitives

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.Text.eq_5_13_of.text: This theorem assumes the formal statements labelled Proposition 5.1, Lemma D.2 and (D.2). In the parent-flow setting of §5.1, put $F=D_aX$, $M=(D_xU)\circ X$, $K=F^TF$ and $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$. Given a nonnegative integer $C_A$, the formal conclusion selects $a_0$; for every integer $a\ge a_0$ it selects $C,C_m$ before the parent, $\mathsf D$ and $A$. With $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$ and $0<A\le\mathsf D^{C_A}$, it proves, for every $m\ge1$, finite coefficient Hölder quantities on $[0,T]$ and $\ell_*^m(|K|_{m,1/2}+|\Omega|_{m,1/2})\le C_m\mathsf D^C\sqrt{\ell_*}\le C_m/A$. The Hölder norm uses the maximum of uniform norm and seminorm. The parent hypotheses are the standing hypotheses of §5.1: $T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$, $\lambda\ge1$, $U$ smooth, periodic, odd and divergence free with frequencies at most $2\mathsf D$, the bounds (5.1), $R_U$ odd with frequencies at most $4\mathsf D$ and $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$, and the coercivity (5.2); the pressure may be any smooth periodic pressure whose residual has these properties. The result assumes the polynomial bound on $A$; it does not identify $A$ with an inverse norm.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.Text.eq_5_13_of.summary: Radius weights absorb the endpoint inverse cost

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.Text.eq_5_14_of.text:
Let $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$, $\lambda\ge1$. Let $U$ be smooth, odd, solenoidal and unit-periodic, with flow $X$ and smooth periodic pressure $p_U$. Require Fourier radii $2\mathsf D$ for $U$ and $4\mathsf D$ for the odd residual $R_U=U_t+U\cdot
abla U+
abla p_U$, $\|DU\|_\infty,\|DX\|_\infty,\|DX^{-1}\|_\infty\le\mathsf D$, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$, and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$ as quadratic forms. Write $F=D_aX$, $G=F^{-1}$, $M=(DU)\circ X$, $K=F^TF$ and $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$. Let smooth periodic $B,z, ar q, ar f$ satisfy $B_t+MB+F^{-T}
abla_a ar q= ar f$, $B=Fz_t$, $\operatorname{div}_az_t=0$ and $z(0)=z(T)=0$. Put $v=F^{-1}B=z_t$ and $g=F^T ar f$. For sufficiently large fixed $a$, $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$, and finite scaled source half-Hölder norm, the formal statement gives finiteness of the velocity norm and $\|v\|_{[n],1/2}\le C_n\mathsf D^C\|g\|_{[n],1/2}$ for all $n\ge0$. The norms sum scaled label derivatives on the whole interval, with the maximum of the supremum and half-Hölder seminorm at each order. The exponent $C$ is chosen after $a$ but before the parent and derivative order. This implication assumes Theorem 4.2, Proposition 5.1, Lemmas D.2–D.3 and (5.13).
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.Text.eq_5_14_of.summary: Endpoint control lifts without losing a source derivative

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.Text.eq_5_59.text: For an integer $m\ge0$, let $f:\mathbb R^3\to E$ and $g:\mathbb R^3\to F$ have finite $C^{m,1/2}$ norms, where $E,F,G$ are real normed spaces. If $B:E\times F\to G$ is continuous and bilinear, then $x\mapsto B(f(x),g(x))$ belongs to $C^{m,1/2}$ and its norm is at most $3(m+1)2^m\|B\|\|f\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\|g\|_{C^{m,1/2}}$. This proves (5.59) for scalar and tensor products and also covers other bilinear operations. The factor $\|B\|$ is necessary when the operation is rescaled. Periodicity is not required for this estimate on $\mathbb R^3$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.Text.eq_5_59.summary: Prove the estimate for every bounded bilinear operation

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.Text.eq_D_2.text: Let $0<\ell_*\le1$ and let $c:I\times\mathbb R^3\to X$ be smooth in the label variable, where $X$ is any real normed space. Assume all derivatives through order $n+1$ are uniformly bounded in time and label. The formal statement proves $\|c\|_{[n]}\le\|c\|_{[n],1/2}\le4\ell_*^{-1/2}\|c\|_{[n+1]}$ and establishes finiteness of the Hölder quantities. At an order $m$ with derivatives bounded through $m+1$, it also proves $\ell_*^m|c|_{m,1/2}\le4\ell_*^{-1/2}(\ell_*^m|c|_m+\ell_*^{m+1}|c|_{m+1})$. Each multi-index is counted once. The Hölder norm uses the maximum of supremum and seminorm; their sum is equivalent within a factor two. Thus the explicit constant four yields the paper's unspecified constant after the chosen norm convention is accounted for.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.Text.eq_D_2.summary: Costs one derivative and half a power of the radius

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.Text.section8_set.text: Assuming Theorem 7.1, the formal statement selects admissible parameters, an inductive construction, a strength constant and a finite positive time $T_\infty$. The construction has the smooth periodic approximate velocities, residual and central-wave estimates, shrinking supports, summable increments and activation times converging to $T_\infty$ required by that theorem. Every stage is defined beyond this common time. The conclusion establishes the existence of this setting; it contains neither a velocity $w$ nor a convergence assertion. Thus it supports the opening choice in Section 8, while the next claim, uniform convergence on the closed terminal interval, needs a separate theorem.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.Text.section8_set.summary: Theorem 7.1 supplies one sequence and a common positive time

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.corollary_8_3.text: Assume the common construction of Theorem 7.1, its smooth odd Euler limit $u,p$ from Proposition 8.1, and the formal conclusions of Proposition 8.2. These include fixed $c>0,C$ with $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\ge c\lambda_{j-1}^{1/8}-C\lambda_{j-1}^{1/32}-C$ on every sufficiently late interval $[t_j,t_{j+1})$. Then $u$ is maximal at $T_\infty>0$, every maximal solution of finite lifespan from the same data has that lifespan, and both integrals in (1.2) are infinite. The proof combines the displayed lower bound with lower bounds for the crossing durations. It does not infer integral divergence from pointwise blow-up alone. The paper instead invokes the periodic Beale–Kato–Majda criterion; the formal proof establishes this construction-specific conclusion without proving that general criterion.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.corollary_8_3.summary: Quantitative vorticity bounds and crossing lengths give infinite integrals

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_1_3.text: Let $b\ge1$ be an integer, $K(s)=320b(s+1)$, and $\mathcal B(s)>0$ satisfy $\log\mathcal B(s)\ge4K(s+1)^3$ for $s\ge1$. Suppose $\lambda_0\ge\mathcal B(1)$, $q_1=1$, $\lambda_j=\lambda_{j-1}^{K(q_j)}$, and $q_{j+1}=\max\{1\le s\le q_j+1:\mathcal B(s)\le\lambda_{j-1}\}$. Then $q_j\le q_{j+1}\le q_j+1$, $q_j\to\infty$, and $4\log\lambda_{j+2}\le(\log\lambda_{j-1})^2$ for $j\ge1$. Thus the last expression is exactly (1.15), since $L_{j+1}=4\log\lambda_{j+2}$. The formal statement omits threshold monotonicity and analytic-cost domination from §1.5; the arithmetic result therefore applies under fewer assumptions.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_1_3.summary: The schedule yields order growth and logarithmic control

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_2_1.text: Let $J$ be a time interval on which relative derivatives are uniquely determined. Suppose $D$ is differentiable, $\operatorname{tr}D=0$, $D'+D^2$ is symmetric, and $k'=-D^Tk$, $\mathbf a'=-D\mathbf a+p_{\rm w}k$, where $p_{\rm w}=2k\cdot D\mathbf a/|k|^2$. For differentiable $F$ and any $P$ with $P'=F$, transverse data give an Euler velocity $u=Dx+\mathbf aF(k\cdot x)$ on $\mathbb R^3$, with pressure $-x\cdot(D'+D^2)x/2-p_{\rm w}P(k\cdot x)$ and zero divergence. Nonzero perpendicular data at any $t_0\in J$ remain so throughout $J$, including earlier times. Unlike the paper, the formal statement requires neither a smooth odd periodic profile nor its normalization; the Euler identity also allows $k=0$, using zero for division by zero. The interval derivative includes one-sided endpoint derivatives.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_2_1.summary: The affine wave solves Euler and preserves nonzero transverse data

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_2_2.text: Let nonzero perpendicular paths $k,\mathbf a\in\mathbb R^3$ satisfy $k'=-B^Tk$ and $\mathbf a'=-B\mathbf a+2(k\cdot B\mathbf a)k/|k|^2$ on a time set $J$, with $\operatorname{tr}B=0$. Put $E_1=k/|k|$, $E_2=\mathbf a/|\mathbf a|$, $E_3=E_1\times E_2$, $B_{ij}=E_i\cdot BE_j$ and $\sigma=|k||\mathbf a|$. The formal statement gives orthonormality and $E_1'=-B_{12}E_2-B_{13}E_3$, $E_2'=B_{12}E_1-B_{32}E_3$, $E_3'=B_{13}E_1+B_{32}E_2$, $(\log\sigma)'=B_{33}$. Derivatives are relative to $J$. These are (2.2), with no regularity assumption on $B$ beyond the supplied wave derivatives and no symmetry assumption on $B'+B^2$. All normalizations and the logarithm have nonzero positive denominators or arguments under the stated hypotheses.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_2_2.summary: The three unit vectors and wave strength satisfy the frame equations

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_2_5.text: For $0<\varepsilon\le1$, let $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon\tau^2/2)$ and consider $Y'=\cos^2\varphi(1-\varepsilon\tan\varphi)-\varepsilon\tau\sin(2\varphi)Y-Y^2$, $Y(0)=1$, on $[0,\infty)$. The same deviation $e$ occurs in both displayed representations, as in Lemma 2.5.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_2_5.summary: The global Riccati solution has the stated representation and gain

In physical time, the new wave solves $k'=-M^Tk$, $\mathbf a'=-M\mathbf a+2(k\cdot M\mathbf a)k/|k|^2$, $k\cdot\mathbf a=0$, with $M=B+\mathbf a_p\otimes k_p+E_c$, $k(t_0)=\lambda E_3(t_0)$, $\lambda>0$, and $\mathbf a(t_0)=-E_1(t_0)/S+E_2(t_0)$. TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_2_6_of.summary: The additive comparison and reference lemma imply the wave bounds

Let $B,E_c$ be continuous on compact $I\supset[t_0,t_0+T/r]$, with $\operatorname{tr}B=0$ and nonzero perpendicular preceding wave data satisfying $k_p\prime=-B^Tk_p$, $\mathbf a_p\prime=-B\mathbf a_p+2(k_p\cdot B\mathbf a_p)k_p/|k_p|^2$. TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_3_1.text: The formal result proves that the selected bump-based families $F_h,P_h$ satisfy Lemma 3.1 for every $0<h\le1$. They are smooth and period one; $F_h$ is odd, $P_h'=F_h$, and $\int_0^1P_h=0$. One positive constant independent of $h,s$ bounds the negative slope and amplitude by $Ch$, with $F_h'(0)=1$ and $F_h'\le1$. For every integer $j\ge2$, a width-independent $C_j$ bounds $|\partial_s^jF_h|$ by $C_jh^{1-j}$. The integer exponent preserves the negative powers of $h$. Thus the result specifies witnesses for the paper's existential assertion, not merely a condition an unknown family would need to satisfy.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_3_1.summary: The bump construction supplies a family satisfying Lemma 3.1

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_4_1.text: Let $u$ be a smooth periodic divergence-free parent with flow $X$ on $[0,T]$, $0<T\le1$. Set $F=D_aX$, $M=(\nabla u)\circ X$, $H^\#=-(M_t+M^2)$, $K=F^TF$, and $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$. If $H^\#\le I$ as quadratic forms, then for each label and every $z\in H^1_0$, with $\xi=Fz$, $\int H^\#\xi\cdot\xi\le\frac12\int|\xi_t|^2$ and $\int(Kz_t\cdot z_t+\Omega z_t\cdot z)\ge\frac12\int|\xi_t|^2$. The formal statement represents $z$ by $Jv$ with $v\in L^2$ and $\int v=0$, so no test paths are lost. Symmetry of $H^\#$ is unnecessary. Here $Jw(t)=\int_0^tw(s)\,ds$.

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_5_10_of.text: Assume the parent coefficient bounds, the finite hierarchy estimates, and existence and uniqueness of the expansion. For the smooth odd periodic parent and its depth-$P\ge2$ expansion, with $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$, central stability and positive coupling, and $C_{\rm step}=\Gamma_P\mathsf D^b$ and $C_{\rm step}\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, take a smooth periodic divergence-free perturbation $v$ whose derivatives of orders zero, one and two are each at most $\lambda^{-5/2}$. Then a flow $Y$ of $V+v$ exists and every such flow satisfies $\|D Y_{0,t}\|,\|D Y_{t,0}\|\le C_{\rm step}\lambda^{1/4}$ on $[0,T]$. The proof estimates the pulled back oscillation through order two and its mean through order one. It does not prove the stronger intermediate second-order mean bound printed in the paper, although these estimates suffice for the same flow conclusion. The transverse stability assumption is $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for every transverse homogeneous solution $\mathbf b$ and $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_5_10_of.summary: Derive the perturbed flow bound from finite hierarchy estimates

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_5_3_of.text: Assuming Lemma 3.1, Proposition 5.1 and Lemmas D.1–D.3, the formal implication proves all parts of Lemma 5.3 for a smooth periodic parent with the band, deformation, residual and coercivity bounds and a nonzero central transverse seed with controlled relative growth and positive coupling. It gives the near-origin seed comparison, weighted transverse estimates with initial data, the zero-initial velocity-pressure estimate, and leading-wave size $C_n\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-5/4}$. The weight is $\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|$ on $[t_0,T]$. The first estimate requires full-interval smooth profiles; the paper allows fields supplied only after activation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_5_3_of.summary: Coefficient bounds and derivative lifting prove Lemma 5.3

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_5_5_of.text: Assuming Proposition 5.1 and Lemma D.1, the formal implication proves the following. Let the parent be smooth, odd, unit-periodic and solenoidal, with smooth periodic pressure on $0<T\le1$, with bands $2\mathsf D$ for velocity and $4\mathsf D$ for its odd residual, gradient and both deformation bounds $\mathsf D\ge2$, residual bound $\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. Put $M=DU\circ X$, $\kappa=DX^{-T}k_*$, $\lambda=|\kappa(t_0,0)|\ge1$ and $0\le t_0<T$. The nonzero central seed solves $\mathbf a_t=-(I-2P_\kappa)M\mathbf a$, is transverse, has $\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a\ge\mathsf D^{-1}|\kappa||\mathbf a|$, and satisfies $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$. Every transverse homogeneous solution $\mathbf b$ obeys $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$. For small fixed $\ell_*$ and $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, transverse $V$ satisfies $\|C[V]\|_{[n],\gamma}\le C_n\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-1}\|V\|_{[n+1],\gamma}$. If $V_t+MV+\kappa\mathsf p_s=f$, the same factor bounds $(\partial_t+M)C[V]+\mathbf d\mathsf p$ by the sum of the next-order norms of $V,f$. The profiles are smooth and $V,f$ have zero phase mean on all $[0,T]$; transversality, the equation and pressure normalization concern $[t_0,T]$. Smooth representatives of the homogeneous leading wave also exist. Thus full-interval assumptions accompany broader pressure and amplitude hypotheses.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_5_5_of.summary: Obtain the general estimate and the homogeneous leading case

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_5_7_of.text: Assuming Proposition 5.1 and Lemma D.1, the formal implication proves the following. For a smooth odd divergence-free periodic parent on $0<T\le1$ with deformation and gradient bounds $\mathsf D\ge2$, velocity and residual Fourier radii $2\mathsf D,4\mathsf D$, residual size $\lambda^{-5/2}$ and coercivity $D^2p-\nabla R_U\le I$, require a transverse nonzero central solution $\mathbf a_t=-(I-2P_\kappa)M\mathbf a$, $\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a\ge\mathsf D^{-1}|\kappa||\mathbf a|$, and $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for every transverse homogeneous solution and $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$, $|\kappa(t_0,0)|=\lambda\ge1$ and $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$. Take $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$ sufficiently small and $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$. A smooth profile with the combined lattice translation law, independent of phase outside the envelope, satisfies $\|D^mf^\natural\|\le C_m(\mathsf D^C\lambda^{3/2})^m\gamma(t)\|f\|_{[m],\gamma}$ and the $C^{m,1/2}$ bound using $m+1$. Here the derivative norm sums ordered coordinate sequences. The weighted estimates hold on $[t_0,T]$. Both estimates hold unweighted on $[0,T]$, and phase-independent fields omit $\lambda^{3/2}$. The target is any real normed space; constants precede the parent. The profile incorporates continuation across cells.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_5_7_of.summary: Iterate the label and phase chain rule with uniform constants

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_5_8_of.text:
Assume the localized seed estimate, existence and uniqueness of the finite expansion, the oscillatory inverse estimate, the hierarchy bounds and the physical evaluation estimates. For a smooth odd divergence-free periodic parent and a depth-$P\ge2$ expansion with stable positive central coupling, $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$ and $C_{m step}=\Gamma_P\mathsf D^b$ and $C_{m step}\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, the formal statement proves Lemma 5.8: $V=U+W^
atural$ is smooth, odd and divergence free, $\Pi=p+\mathsf P^
atural$ is smooth, and $V_t+V\cdot
abla V+
abla\Pi=R_P^
atural+R_{\widetilde\chi}^
atural$. It also gives the velocity estimates with oscillatory scale $\lambda^{-5/4}$ and mean scale $\lambda^{-5/2}$, and $\|R_V\|_{C_tC^{1,1/2}}\le C_{m step}\lambda^2(\lambda^{-2P/3}+\|\widetilde\chi\,{}^{\prime}\gamma\|_\infty)$. Reflection symmetry is derived from uniqueness. This theorem is conditional on the stated preceding results; the numbered theorem supplies those results. The transverse stability assumption is $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for every transverse homogeneous solution $\mathbf b$ and $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_5_8_of.summary: Combine exact cancellation, symmetry, and physical estimates

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_5_9_of.text: Assuming Lemma 3.1, Theorem 4.2, Proposition 5.1, Lemmas 5.3 and 5.7, Theorem 5.6, Proposition 5.4, and Lemmas B.1 and D.1, the formal implication proves the following. For a smooth odd divergence-free periodic parent on $0<T\le1$, require deformation and gradient bounds $\mathsf D\ge2$, Fourier radii $2\mathsf D,4\mathsf D$ for $U,R_U$, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p-\nabla R_U\le I$. Take a nonzero transverse seed of $\mathbf a_t=-(I-2P_\kappa)M\mathbf a$, with $\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a\ge\mathsf D^{-1}|\kappa||\mathbf a|$ and $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for every transverse homogeneous solution $\mathbf b$ and $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$, $|\kappa(t_0,0)|=\lambda\ge1$, $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$, and a depth-$P\ge2$ finite expansion with sufficiently small envelope. Under $C_{\rm step}=\Gamma_P\mathsf D^b$ and $C_{\rm step}\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, the assertion gives $D_x^2\mathsf P^\natural\le C_{\rm step}\lambda^{-1/4}I$ on $[0,T]$ and $\|D V(t,0)-D U(t,0)-\widetilde\chi\mathbf a\otimes\kappa\|\le\lambda^{-1/3}$ on $[t_0,T]$. The first is a quadratic-form upper bound, the second an operator-norm bound. Constants precede the parent and expansion. Neither zero-mean Poisson normalization of $p$ nor attainment of $\max\gamma=1$ is required.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_5_9_of.summary: Assemble the four estimates used in Lemma 5.9

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_6_1_of.text: Assuming the frame equations of Lemma 2.2, the formal theorem proves the following. For $0<\rho\le1$, $\lambda\ge1$, $T>0$ and $T\|B_\rho\|\le1/8$, a first central wave exists with initial covector $\lambda e_1$, positive initial amplitude along $e_2$ and attained peak $\lambda^{-3/4}$. Every such wave satisfies, for all $\mathsf D\ge2$, the transverse propagation bound $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ and coupling bound $\nu(t)\ge\mathsf D^{-1}$ on $0\le t'\le t\le T$, where $\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a|$. Its initial strength lies in $[\lambda^{1/4}/2,\lambda^{1/4}]$. The dependence on Lemma 2.2 is explicit here; the final numbered theorem supplies that already proved result.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_6_1_of.summary: Derives the complete first-wave lemma from Lemma 2.2

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_A_2.text: For $H=\mathbb R^3$ take $\mathcal R=\mathbb P$; for $H=L^2([0,1];\mathbb R^3)$ take $\mathcal R=\mathbb P\mathcal Q$, where $\mathcal Q$ removes the time average. Suppose $B:\mathbb T^3\to\mathcal L(H)$ is Lipschitz with constant $L\ge0$ and $\langle B(a)w,w\rangle\ge\mu\|w\|^2$, $\mu>0$, for all vectors in the first case and zero-time-mean paths in the second. Then $\mathcal RB$ is invertible on its projected half-Hölder space with bound $C(2+\mu^{-1}+\|B\|_\infty+L)^p$. The constants are chosen before $B$, with integer $p\ge0$. If $B\in C^{k,1/2}$, $k\ge1$, the same inverse preserves that class. The paper requires the stronger base hypothesis $B\in C^{1,1/2}$.

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_B_1.text: Let $S_\Lambda$ act on $\mathbb T^3=\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3$ with symbol $\psi(\xi/\Lambda)$. Assume $\psi$ is smooth and even, $0\le\psi\le1$, equals one on the unit ball and vanishes outside radius two, and $\Lambda>0$. The formal statement gives parity, support $|\xi|\le2\Lambda$, divergence preservation for smooth real velocities, and uniform $L^\infty$ and $C^{0,1/2}$ bounds. For frequencies at most $4\Lambda$ it proves $\sum_{|\beta|=m}\|\partial^\beta f\|_\infty\le C_m\Lambda^m\|f\|_\infty$; for $f\in C^{M,1/2}$ and $s\le M$, $\|(I-S_\Lambda)f\|_{C^{s,1/2}}\le C_M\Lambda^{s-M}\|f\|_{C^{M,1/2}}$. Constants precede frequencies, targets and fields. Bernstein permits any real normed target. The $L^\infty$ input is essentially bounded and almost-everywhere strongly measurable in a complex Banach target; real velocities are continuous. Spatial commutation covers all complex orders, one real coordinate derivative and one time derivative on smooth closed slabs. Higher real orders require iteration. Each Hölder norm sums, over the orders through the indicated one, the supremum and half-Hölder seminorm of the full derivative tensor. The paper assumes radiality and $\Lambda\ge1$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_B_1.summary: Collects commutation, support, boundedness, Bernstein and tail estimates

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_D_1.text: Fix a time set $I$, positive scales $\ell_*,h$ and $\gamma:I\to(0,\infty)$. For fields smooth in $(a,s)\in\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, $\|f\|_{[n]}$ sums $\ell_*^{|\beta|}h^j\sup_{t,a,s}|\partial_a^\beta\partial_s^jf|$ over $|\beta|+j\le n$, once per multi-index. Assume the derivative families entering each right side below are bounded. The formal statement proves $\sum_i\|\partial_{a_i}f\|_{[n],\gamma}\le3\ell_*^{-1}\|f\|_{[n+1],\gamma}$, $\|\partial_sf\|_{[n],\gamma}\le h^{-1}\|f\|_{[n+1],\gamma}$, and $\|B(f,g)\|_{[n],\gamma}\le C_n\|B\|\|f\|_{[n]}\|g\|_{[n],\gamma}$ for every continuous bilinear $B$. Weighted boundedness concerns derivatives of $f/\gamma$ or $g/\gamma$, not merely the unnormalized fields. For period-one Banach-valued fields, averaging, subtraction of the average and the zero-mean periodic primitive have respective bounds $1,2,2$ in the same norm; the primitive requires zero phase mean. All output derivative families are bounded. For phase-independent fields, the product estimate also holds with half-Hölder norms using the maximum of the uniform norm and seminorm. There is no time differentiation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_D_1.summary: Controls differentiation, products, averaging and the periodic primitive

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_D_2.text: Assume $\mathsf D\ge1$ and smooth phase-independent coefficients with $|c|_m\le C_m\mathsf D^{q(m+1)}$. The formal statement uses nonnegative integer exponents. For inputs with exponents $q,r$, a bilinear product of norm at most one has exponent $2\max(q,r)$. In a complete real normed algebra, pointwise invertibility and $\|c^{-1}\|_\infty\le\mathsf D^e$ give exponent $3\max(q,e)$. Output constants are selected after the input constants and value spaces, but before $\mathsf D$, the time set and fields. Finally, $0<\ell_*\le\mathsf D^{-q}$ gives $\|c\|_{[n]}\le C'_n\mathsf D^q$ and $\ell_*^m|c|_m\le C'_m\mathsf D^{2q}\ell_*$ for $m\ge1$. Rounding the paper's fixed real exponent upward changes both this radius condition and its concluding powers; it does not reproduce that clause literally.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_D_2.summary: Preserves polynomial growth under products, inverses and weighting

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_D_3.text:
Let $A,E,F$ be real vector spaces with seminorms $p_A,p_E,p_F$ and a finite ordered family of linear derivative maps. Put $\mathcal Lv=L_0v+\sum_
u B_
u(c_
u,v)$. Assume principal commutation, the product rule for each $B_
u$, and commuting coefficient and forcing derivatives. Require $b_
u,C_{m low}\ge0$, $p_F(B_
u(a,u))\le b_
u p_A(a)p_E(u)$, and $p_E(u)\le C_{m low}p_F(\mathcal Lu)$ for every $u\in E$. Let $|c|_m$ and $\|u\|_{[n]}$ sum derivative seminorms at order $m$ and through order $n$, counting each nondecreasing sequence once. If $C_{m low}\sum_
u b_
u|c_
u|_m\le C_m$ for $1\le m\le n$, the formal statement proves $\|v\|_{[n]}\le C_nC_{m low}\|f\|_{[n]}$ whenever $\mathcal Lv=f$. The constant depends only on $n$, the coefficient bounds and the number of derivative directions. Taking derivatives $\ell_*\partial_{a_i},h\partial_s$ and the appropriate zero-order seminorms gives the paper's weighted setting. Constraints, quotient equations and prescribed data must be included in $E,F$. No existence assertion is made.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.lemma_D_3.summary: Retains one zero-order inverse factor at higher orders

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_2_8_o.text:
Let $B,E_c$ be continuous on compact $I\supset[t_0,t_0+T/r]$, with $\operatorname{tr}B=0$ and nonzero perpendicular preceding wave data satisfying $k_p\prime=-B^Tk_p$, $\mathbf a_p\prime=-B\mathbf a_p+2(k_p\cdot B\mathbf a_p)k_p/|k_p|^2$. Set $E_1=\widehat{k_p}$, $E_2=\widehat{\mathbf a_p}$ and $E_3=E_1	imes E_2$; $B_{ij}=E_i\cdot BE_j$. Physical derivatives are relative to $I$; for interval $I$, endpoint derivatives are one-sided. Put $\sigma=|k_p(t_0)||\mathbf a_p(t_0)|$, $
u=B_{12}(t_0)>0$, $\eta=B_{32}(t_0)>0$, $r=\sqrt{2\sigma
u}$, $S=\sigma/r$, $\varepsilon=\eta/
u$, and $\delta=\sup_I|B_{12}/
u-1|+\sup_I|B_{32}/\eta-1|+\sup_I\|B\|/r+\sup_I\|E_c\|/
u$. Assume $T\ge2$ and $C_0\varepsilon\le1$, $C_0T^{C_0}\delta\le\varepsilon$ for sufficiently large integer $C_0$. In physical time, the new wave solves $k'=-M^Tk$, $\mathbf a'=-M\mathbf a+2(k\cdot M\mathbf a)k/|k|^2$, $k\cdot\mathbf a=0$, with $M=B+\mathbf a_p\otimes k_p+E_c$, $k(t_0)=\lambda E_3(t_0)$, $\lambda>0$, and $\mathbf a(t_0)=-E_1(t_0)/S+E_2(t_0)$. Use $	au=r(t-t_0)$, $\alpha_1=S\mathbf a\cdot E_1$, $\alpha_2=\mathbf a\cdot E_2$, $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon	au^2/2)$, and $a_{m ref}=\exp\int_0^	au Y$ with $Y\prime=\cos^2\varphi(1-\varepsilon	an\varphi)-\varepsilon	au\sin(2\varphi)Y-Y^2$, $Y(0)=1$, on $[0,\infty)$. Assume $0<\varepsilon_+\le\varepsilon/32$ and $H=2/\sqrt{\varepsilon\varepsilon_+}\le T$. Given Lemmas 2.4–2.7, the formal statement proves a crossing $\eta_+/
u_+=\varepsilon_+$ in $[	au_m,H]$. For $A=\max_{[0,T]}|\mathbf a|$, every crossing there satisfies $\exp(-1)/(4\sqrt{\varepsilon\varepsilon_+})\le|\mathbf a||k|/(\lambda A)\le18\exp(3)/\sqrt{\varepsilon\varepsilon_+}$. It also gives $|\mathbf a|\le\exp(3-\varepsilon^{-1/2})A$ on $[0,1]$. Here $
u_+=\widehat k\cdot M\widehat a$, $\eta_+=(\widehat k	imes\widehat a)\cdot M\widehat a$, and $	au_m$ is the reference peak.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_2_8_o.summary: The reference and comparison lemmas imply the crossing conclusions

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_5_11_.text: Assume Lemmas 5.8 and 5.9, the Fourier cutoff estimates and the Hölder product inequality. For a depth-$P\ge2$ approximation $V,\Pi,R_V$ on $[0,T]$ satisfying those lemmas, take a smooth radial symbol $0\le\psi\le1$, equal to one on $|\xi|\le1$ and zero on $|\xi|>2$. For $\Lambda\ge1$, set $u=S_\Lambda V$ and choose the periodic zero-mean $p$ solving $\Delta p=-\operatorname{tr}((\nabla u)^2)$. This proves Proposition 5.11: $u,R_u$ are odd and divergence free with Fourier radii $2\Lambda,4\Lambda$, and $\|u-V\|_{C_tC^{2,1/2}}\le K_P\varepsilon_\Lambda$. The sum of residual and pressure-Hessian errors is at most $e=C\|R_V\|_{C_tC^{1,1/2}}+K_P\varepsilon_\Lambda$, where $\varepsilon_\Lambda=\Lambda^{2-P}(1+\|V\|_{C_tC^{P,1/2}})^2$. Moreover $D^2(p-p_U)\le(C_{\rm step}\lambda^{-1/4}+e)I$, with $C_{\rm step}=\Gamma_P\mathsf D^b$ from the approximation. Existence and uniqueness of the normalized Poisson pressure identify the constructed pressure.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_5_11_.summary: Transfer the approximation estimates to a Fourier truncated parent

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_5_1_o.text: Let $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$, $\lambda\ge1$. Let $U$ be smooth, odd, solenoidal and unit-periodic, with flow $X$ and smooth periodic pressure $p_U$. Require Fourier radii $2\mathsf D$ for $U$ and $4\mathsf D$ for the odd residual $R_U=U_t+U\cdot\nabla U+\nabla p_U$, $\|DU\|_\infty,\|DX\|_\infty,\|DX^{-1}\|_\infty\le\mathsf D$, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$, and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$ as quadratic forms. Put $F=DX$, $M=DU\circ X$, $\kappa=F^{-T}k_*$ and $|\kappa(t_0,0)|=\lambda$. For $\mathcal C=\{F,F^{-1},M,\kappa/\lambda,\lambda^2/|\kappa|^2,P_\kappa\}$, one exponent $C$ gives $\|D^m\Phi\|_\infty\le C_m\mathsf D^{C(m+1)}$. If $\|D^mf\|_\infty\le C'_mA_f\mathsf D^m$, $A_f\ge0$, then $\|D^m(f\circ X)\|_\infty\le C_mA_f\mathsf D^{Cm}$. For $0<\ell_*\le\mathsf D^{-C}$, the sums $\sum_{j\le n}\ell_*^j\|D^j\Phi\|_\infty$ and $\sum_{j\le n}\ell_*^j\|D^j(f\circ X)\|_\infty$ are bounded by $C_n\mathsf D^C$ and $C_nA_f$, respectively. Derivatives use operator norms; constants precede the parent. Pressure normalization is not required. This implication assumes Bernstein’s inequality and Lemma D.2.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_5_1_o.summary: Bernstein and flow estimates control the six coefficient families

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_5_2_o.text:
Let $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$ and $\lambda\ge1$. Assume a smooth odd solenoidal unit-periodic parent $U$ and flow $X$, Fourier bands $2\mathsf D$ for $U$ and $4\mathsf D$ for the odd residual $R_U=U_t+U\cdot
abla U+
abla p_U$, bounds $\|DU\|,\|DX\|,\|DX^{-1}\|\le\mathsf D$, $\|R_U\|\le\lambda^{-5/2}$, and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. The pressure may be any smooth periodic choice satisfying these conditions. Put $M=DU\circ X$, $\mathbf d=DX^{-T}
abla_a$. For a smooth periodic phase-independent solution $B_t+MB+\mathbf d ar q= ar f$, require $B=DXz_t$, $\operatorname{div}_az_t=0$ and $z(0)=z(T)=0$. At sufficiently small fixed $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$, $\|B\|_{[n]}\le C_n\mathsf D^C\| ar f\|_{[n+1]}$ for every $n$. These are scaled label-derivative suprema on all of $[0,T]$. The exponent is chosen before the parent and order. This estimates existing solutions; it does not set $B(0)=0$. This implication assumes Proposition 5.1, Lemma D.1, (D.2) and (5.14).
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_5_2_o.summary: Hölder comparison costs exactly one source derivative

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_5_4_o.text: Assuming Theorem 4.2, the formal implication proves the following. Let the parent be smooth, odd, unit-periodic and solenoidal, with smooth periodic pressure on $0<T\le1$, with bands $2\mathsf D$ for velocity and $4\mathsf D$ for its odd residual, gradient and both deformation bounds $\mathsf D\ge2$, residual bound $\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. Put $M=DU\circ X$, $\kappa=DX^{-T}k_*$, $\lambda=|\kappa(t_0,0)|\ge1$ and $0\le t_0<T$. The nonzero central seed solves $\mathbf a_t=-(I-2P_\kappa)M\mathbf a$, is transverse, has $\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a\ge\mathsf D^{-1}|\kappa||\mathbf a|$, and satisfies $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$. Every transverse homogeneous solution $\mathbf b$ obeys $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$. For sufficiently small fixed $\ell_*$, the projected seed exists, and every depth $P\ge2$ admits a unique family of retained velocities and normalized pressures satisfying the mean and transverse recursions. For $W=\sum_{p=1}^P(V_p+C_{p+1}+B_p)$ and $\mathsf P=\sum_{p=1}^P(\mathsf p_p+\bar q_p)$, $\widetilde{\mathbf d}\cdot W=0$ and the momentum residual is $R_P+R_{\widetilde\chi}$. The oscillations and their sources vanish before activation and, at all times, outside the envelope; outside the envelope the remainder $R_P$ is also phase independent. Means need not vanish before activation. Smoothness concerns the closed slab.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_5_4_o.summary: The endpoint theorem supplies the mean solves and uniqueness

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_8_1_o.text: Assume the frequency conclusions of Lemma 1.3 and the product estimate (5.59). For any common construction satisfying Theorem 7.1, the formal statement produces smooth periodic $u,p$ solving incompressible Euler on $[0,T_\infty)$, with mean-zero pressure and odd velocity. The data $U_j(0)$ converge to the smooth odd divergence-free $u(0)$ in every $C^{m,1/2}$, and $U_j\to u$ uniformly in that spatial norm on each $[0,S]$, $S<T_\infty$. Every maximal solution of finite lifespan from $u(0)$ lasts at least to $T_\infty$ and agrees with $u$ before it. General maximal-solution existence is not a conclusion here. The spatial $C^{m,1/2}$ norm is $\sum_{i\le m}(\sup|D^if|+[D^if]_{1/2})$, where $D^if$ is the full $i$th derivative tensor in operator norm.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_8_1_o.summary: Construct a smooth limit and compare finite maximal lifespans

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_8_2_o.text: Assume the schedule, moving-frame, amplification and cutoff conclusions of Lemmas 1.3, 2.2, 2.4 and B.1. For a common construction satisfying Theorem 7.1 and its smooth Euler limit from Proposition 8.1, the formal statement proves uniformly bounded velocity and $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\to\infty$ as $t\uparrow T_\infty$. It also supplies fixed $c>0,C$ with $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\ge c\lambda_{j-1}^{1/8}-C\lambda_{j-1}^{1/32}-C$ for every sufficiently late $[t_j,t_{j+1})$. These are period-one fields on $\mathbb R^3$ representing the torus. The quantitative estimate is an additional conclusion beyond the printed statement of Proposition 8.2 and applies to the limit $u$, rather than only to an approximation $U_j$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_8_2_o.summary: The wave estimates yield both terminal conclusions and a lower bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_8_4_o.text: Assume Lemma 1.3, a common construction satisfying Theorem 7.1, and its smooth periodic Euler limit from Proposition 8.1. For every compact $K\subset\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3$ and every integer $m\ge0$, both $u(t)$ and $\partial_tu(t)$ converge as $t\uparrow T_\infty$, uniformly on $K$ with all spatial derivatives through order $m$. Each limit extends to a $C^m$ field on an open neighbourhood of $K$. Removing the integer lattice represents removal of the torus origin. The time derivative is taken within $[0,T_\infty)$, including the right derivative at zero. Shrinking oscillation supports give the velocity limits; a separated pressure kernel handles the time derivative. The conclusion is not a smooth Euler continuation through the terminal time.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_8_4_o.summary: Velocity and its time derivative have local spatial derivative limits

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.remark_1_2.text: The formal proof chooses smooth odd divergence-free periodic data and a maximal Euler solution on $[0,T_*)$, where $0<T_*<\infty$. Velocity is bounded, central vorticity tends to infinity, both gradient and vorticity time integrals diverge, and velocity and its time derivative have all spatial limits away from the origin. In addition, the velocity has a smooth periodic extension through $T_*$ away from that point.
