Every other maximal solution of finite real lifespan from the chosen data has the same lifespan and velocity. The proof uses an auxiliary existence theorem with selected parameters. It does not establish the auxiliary note’s broader assertion for every admissible threshold, and imposes no Euler equation after $T_*$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.remark_1_2.summary: An existential auxiliary result supplies Remark 1.2

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.remark_1_2_of.text: The authors' source records this statement as not proved and outside the main argument; neither formal main theorem uses it. Assuming the generalized auxiliary Theorem 1.1, this wrapper chooses a cutoff symbol, takes the envelope floor to be zero, obtains an admissible threshold and a sufficiently large frequency, and projects a singularity witness with its smooth extension. This route is kept in the formalization but no longer used. The main proof obtains the remark from the auxiliary terminal-smoothness theorem instead; the generalized auxiliary theorem is assumed here, not proved.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.remark_1_2_of.summary: Obtain the remark from the generalized auxiliary theorem

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_1_1_of.text: Assume existence of the common approximate sequence selected in Section 8, its smooth Euler limit and initial-data convergence from Proposition 8.1, bounded velocity and central-vorticity blow-up from Proposition 8.2, finite maximality and both divergent integrals from Corollary 8.3, and the local spatial limits from Proposition 8.4. The formal statement then proves existence of smooth odd divergence-free periodic data and an odd maximal Euler solution on $[0,T_*)$, $0<T_*<\infty$. Velocity stays bounded, $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\to\infty$, and the time integrals of both $\|\nabla u\|_\infty$ and $\|\operatorname{curl}u\|_\infty$ are infinite. On each compact set off the torus origin, $u$ and $\partial_tu$ have limits with all spatial derivatives. Every maximal solution of finite real lifespan from those data has the same lifespan and velocity before it. The inputs are hypotheses of this assembly; separate numbered theorems establish them.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_1_1_of.summary: Five earlier assertions imply all of Theorem 1.1

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_4_2_of.text: On $I=[0,T]$, $0<T\le1$, let $U$ be smooth, unit-periodic and divergence free, $X$ its flow from time zero, $F=D_aX$, $M=(DU)\circ X$, $K=F^TF$, $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$, and $H^\#=-(M_t+M^2)\le I$ as quadratic forms. Assume $\|F^{-1}\|_\infty\le D\ge1$, $\|M\|_\infty\le L$, $\|K\|_\infty\le K_0$, $\|D_aK\|_\infty\le K_1$, $\|\Omega\|_\infty\le\Omega_0$, $\|D_a\Omega\|_\infty\le\Omega_1$, with nonnegative bounds. For $L_{\rm src}\in C(I;C^{0,1/2}(\mathbb T^3))$, solve $Kv-J(\Omega v)+L_{\rm src}=c+G_\phi$, $z_t=v$, $z(0)=z(T)=0$, where $Jw(t)=\int_0^tw(s)\,ds$. The fields $z,v,c$ are weakly divergence free; $z\in C^1_tC^{0,1/2}$, $v,G_\phi\in C_tC^{0,1/2}$, and $G_\phi=\nabla_a\phi$ for a periodic potential at each time. There are absolute $C\ge0$ and an integer $p\ge0$ such that $A=C(D+L+K_0+K_1+\Omega_0+\Omega_1)^p$ gives $\|v\|_{C_tC^{0,1/2}}\le A\|L_{\rm src}\|_{C_tC^{0,1/2}}$ and $\|(\mathbb PK(t))^{-1}\mathbb P\|\le A$ uniformly on $I$. This is conditional on Lemma 4.1, Theorem A.1 and Lemma A.2. It also supplies smooth Eulerian corrections for smooth force sources $L_{\rm src}=-J(F^T(f\circ X))$, with a reconstructed smooth label pressure. The coefficient inputs use first derivative suprema.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_4_2_of.summary: Combine coercivity with both Hölder inverse results

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_5_6_of.text: Assuming Propositions 5.1, 5.2, 5.4, Lemmas 5.3, 5.5, D.1 and B.1 (the Fourier cutoff lemma, including Bernstein’s inequality), the formal implication proves Theorem 5.6 for each depth-$P$ expansion. Under the smooth parent bounds, central transverse stability and $\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, level-$p$ oscillations decay as $\lambda^{-5/4-2(p-1)/3}$, means as $\lambda^{-5/2-2(p-2)/3}$ and $C_{p+1}$ as $\lambda^{-9/4-2(p-1)/3}$, up to $C_{n,p}\mathsf D^C$. The remainder is bounded by $C_{m,P}\lambda^{-5/4-2P/3}$. All derivative orders apply to the same profiles; the parent exponent is independent of order, level and depth. The transverse stability assumption is $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for every transverse homogeneous solution $\mathbf b$ and $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_5_6_of.summary: Close the level induction with one fixed parent exponent

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_7_1_of.text: Assuming Lemmas 1.3, 2.2, 2.5–2.7, 5.8–5.10, 6.1 and B.1 and Propositions 2.8, 5.4 and 5.11, the formal theorem derives Theorem 7.1. For each admissible radial cutoff and integer floor $a_0$, it chooses integers $b\ge1$, $a\ge a_0$ and a majorant of the fixed-order constants. Every admissible threshold $\mathcal B$ above that majorant then permits the construction for all sufficiently large initial frequencies $N$. The resulting smooth odd periodic velocities have the residual, flow, pressure, central-wave and increment bounds of (T1)–(T4), with positive common time and $C=18e^3$. It also supplies the actual expansion and truncation of each step. The central covector is still not identified with the localized step's transported covector; the first-wave direction and attained normalization are not part of this exported conclusion.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_7_1_of.summary: Assembles one sequence after fixing the cutoff and parameter majorants

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_A_1_of.text: Assume the two inverse assertions of Lemma A.2. On $I=[0,1]\times\mathbb T^3$, let $K$ be symmetric and $\Omega$ skew-symmetric, continuous in time in $C^{0,1/2}$, spatially differentiable, and uniformly bounded with their first spatial derivatives. Suppose $K\ge\kappa I$, $\kappa>0$, and $\int_0^1(Kz_t\cdot z_t+\Omega z_t\cdot z)\,dt\ge\mu\int_0^1|z_t|^2\,dt$ at every label for every $z\in H^1_0$, with $\mu>0$. For every $L\in C_tC^{0,1/2}$, the formal statement proves unique $z,v=z_t,c,G$ satisfying $Kv-J(\Omega v)+L=c+G$, $z(0)=z(1)=0$, with solenoidal $z,c$ and periodic $G=\nabla\phi$. It gives a polynomial velocity bound and smoothness of $z,c,G$ for smooth data. Here $Jw(t)=\int_0^tw(s)\,ds$; uniqueness concerns the closed interval and the gradient. The proof first solves for square-integrable time paths, then recovers time continuity.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_A_1_of.summary: Recover the endpoint solution from the freezing lemma

TorusEuler.Paper.Proposition81Conclusion.text: For a prescribed common construction and $T,u,p$, the formal statement requires the data $U_j(0)$ to converge to smooth odd divergence-free $u(0)$ in every $C^{m,1/2}$. It requires smooth periodic Euler evolution on $[0,T)$ with $T>0$, mean-zero pressure, odd velocity, and convergence $U_j\to u$ uniformly in the same spatial norm on every earlier $[0,S]$, $S<T$. Every maximal solution of finite lifespan with initial velocity $u(0)$ must last at least to $T$ and agree with $u$ on $[0,T)$. This is a list of required properties, not a theorem that such a solution exists. It does not quantify over an infinite maximal lifespan. The spatial $C^{m,1/2}$ norm is $\sum_{i\le m}(\sup|D^if|+[D^if]_{1/2})$, where $D^if$ is the full $i$th derivative tensor in operator norm.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proposition81Conclusion.summary: Record convergence, smooth Euler evolution, and conditional maximal agreement

TorusEuler.Paper.Proposition82Conclusion.text: For prescribed $T,u$ and a frequency and activation schedule, the formal statement records three conditions: a single finite bound for $\|u(t)\|_\infty$ on $0\le t<T$; $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\to\infty$ as $t\uparrow T$ within that interval; and fixed real $c>0,C$ such that $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\ge c\lambda_{j-1}^{1/8}-C\lambda_{j-1}^{1/32}-C$ on every sufficiently late $[t_j,t_{j+1})$. The last condition is stronger than the printed statement of Proposition 8.2. Positivity of $T$, the Euler equations and identification of $T$ with $T_\infty$ are supplied separately. The velocity norm is an essential supremum over the unit cell. Since only sufficiently large indices occur, subtraction in the index $j-1$ has its usual meaning.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proposition82Conclusion.summary: Require bounded velocity, full blow-up, and uniform interval lower bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Proposition84Conclusion.text: Given $T$ and a field $u$, the formal statement requires the following for each of $u$ and its time derivative. For every compact $K\subset\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3$ and integer $m\ge0$, there is a $C^m$ field on an open neighbourhood of $K$ whose spatial derivatives through order $m$ are the uniform limits on $K$ as $t\uparrow T$ within $[0,T)$. This is the meaning of the two $C^m(K)$ limits in Proposition 8.4. The local limiting field may depend on $K$ and $m$. The time derivative is taken within the half-open lifespan. The condition itself neither proves existence of $u$ nor supplies a single jointly smooth extension in space and time.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proposition84Conclusion.summary: Require local limits for velocity and its first time derivative

TorusEuler.Paper.ReferenceSlope.text: For a real parameter $\varepsilon$, the formal condition says $Y(0)=1$ and $Y'=\cos^2\varphi(1-\varepsilon\tan\varphi)-\varepsilon\tau\sin2\varphi\,Y-Y^2$ for every $\tau\ge0$, where $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon\tau^2/2)$. This is (2.12). At zero the derivative is taken from the right. Although $Y$ is a function on all real numbers, its values at negative times are unrestricted. The condition places no sign restriction on $\varepsilon$ and proves no existence, uniqueness or growth bound. Lemma 2.5 obtains those conclusions under $0<\varepsilon\le1$.
TorusEuler.Paper.ReferenceSlope.summary: The condition specifies the scalar initial value problem on the forward half-line

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Cd.text: The correction attached to $V_p$ is stored alongside that oscillation, but the paper denotes it by $C_{p+1}$. This definition recovers the paper's $C_q$ by reading the stored correction at index $q-1$. Indices are nonnegative integers: subtraction at $q=0$ gives zero rather than a negative index. Consequently $C_0$ and $C_1$ refer to the same stored entry, although only the paper's levels $q\ge1$ are used in the expansion. The condition $C_1=0$ must still be imposed or proved; it does not follow from this change of indexing.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Cd.summary: The correction of an oscillation carries the next paper index

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.CutoffSymbol.text:
This is the fixed symbol $\psi$ from Appendix B. It is smooth on $\mathbb R^3$, depends only on $|\xi|$, lies between zero and one, equals one on the unit ball, and vanishes when $|\xi|>2$. Smoothness makes the support inclusion agree with the compact-support formulation in the paper. The zero symbol cannot satisfy the unit-ball condition.

This condition contains no numerical derivative, integral, quotient, supremum, conversion from extended nonnegative reals or square root. Smoothness is a regularity assertion, not the value of a derivative. The condition $\psi=1$ on a nonempty ball excludes a trivial zero cutoff. The boundary $|\xi|=2$ is handled by smoothness and continuity together with vanishing outside the closed ball.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.CutoffSymbol.summary: Smooth radial Fourier cutoff equal to one near zero

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.IsExpansion.text: On $[0,T]$, profiles are smooth, one-periodic in $s$, and obey $f(t,a+n,s+k_*\cdot n)=f(t,a,s)$. Put $M=DU\circ X$, $\kappa=DX^{-T}k_*$, $\mathbf d=DX^{-T}\nabla_a$, $A_1=g\mathbf aF_h$, and $S=\widetilde\chi'A_1$ in the centered cell. The requirements include $R=R_U\circ X$, $V_1=\widetilde\chi A_1$, $\mathsf p_1=\widetilde\chi\mathsf p[A_1]$, and $C_1=B_1=\bar q_1=0$. For $1\le p\le P$, $C_{p+1}=\mathbf d\times[-\partial_s^{-1}(\kappa\times V_p/|\kappa|^2)]$. For $2\le p\le P$, require $B_{p,t}+MB_p+\mathbf d\bar q_p=-\langle H_p\rangle_s-\mathbf1_{p=2}R$ and $V_{p,t}+MV_p+\kappa\mathsf p_{p,s}=-(H_p-\langle H_p\rangle_s)+f_p^S$. Here $H_p$ is the sum of the preceding linear correction and all lower-level quadratic interactions, with the activation correction subtracted at level two; $f_p^S=-\sum_{i=2}^p(B_i\cdot\kappa)\partial_s(V_{p+1-i}+C_{p+1-i})$. Means satisfy $B_p=DX\,z_{p,t}$, $\operatorname{div}_az_{p,t}=0$, $z_p(0)=z_p(T)=0$ and zero spatial pressure mean. Transverse velocities are perpendicular to $\kappa$, centered and initially zero, with centered pressure. Finally $V_{P+1}=B_{P+1}=0$. This condition asserts no existence or estimates.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.IsExpansion.summary: The definition specifies every equation through the retained depth

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.IsSeed.text: Let $M(t,a)=\nabla U(t,X_{0,t}(a))$ and $\kappa(t,a)=D(X_{t,0})(X_{0,t}(a))^Tk_*$. A seed is a smooth field $\mathbf a$ on $[t_0,T]\times\mathbb R^3$ which agrees with the central seed at $a=0$, starts from $(I-P_{\kappa(t_0,a)})\mathbf a(t_0,0)$, and solves $\partial_t\mathbf a=-M\mathbf a+2\kappa(\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a)/|\kappa|^2$ while satisfying $\kappa\cdot\mathbf a=0$. The differential equation uses derivatives within $[t_0,T]$ at its endpoints. This records the seed equation and (5.4), not the amplitude and coupling estimates on nearby labels. Those are later conclusions. Nonvanishing of $\kappa$ comes from the parent flow and nonzero carrier, not from this declaration alone.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.IsSeed.summary: Specify smooth transverse evolution from projected initial data

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.IsTruncation.text: This condition identifies $u$ with $S_\Lambda V$ on $[0,T]$ by requiring the cutoff formula for every continuous function on $\mathbb T^3=\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3$ representing $V$. At each time, $p$ must be smooth, periodic, have zero integral over the centered unit cell, and solve $\Delta p=-\operatorname{tr}((\nabla u)^2)$. Existence of a continuous periodic representative of $V$ is not included in this condition: without one, its cutoff clause alone imposes no restriction. Proposition 5.11 supplies such a representative by proving $V$ smooth and periodic. The condition specifies the pressure spatially at each time; joint time smoothness is proved for the constructed truncation.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.IsTruncation.summary: Specify a Fourier cutoff and its normalized periodic Poisson pressure

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Launch.text: The conditions are $0\le t_0<T$, $k_*\ne0$, and $|\kappa(t_0,0)|=\lambda$, with $\kappa(t,a)=D(X_{t,0})(X_{0,t}(a))^Tk_*$. They specify the activation time and the frequency convention in §5.1. Thus $\lambda$ is the length of the transported vector at the origin when the wave is activated, not automatically $|k_*|$. These conditions do not themselves assert that $X$ is a differentiable flow or that $\lambda\ge1$; those requirements are supplied by the parent hypotheses. Together with the bounds for the forward and inverse deformation, they give (5.3).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Launch.summary: Measure frequency after transport at the activation point

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.MeanSolution.text: On $[0,T]$, let $X$ be the parent flow, $M=DU\circ X$ and $\mathbf d=(D_aX)^{-T}\nabla_a$. The formal condition on smooth phase-independent $B,\bar q$ is $B_t+MB+\mathbf d\bar q=\bar f$, with smooth periodic fields $z,v$ satisfying $z_t=v$, $\operatorname{div}_a v=0$, $z(0)=z(T)=0$ and $B=D_aXv$. Volume preservation converts this to $\mathbf d\cdot B=0$, as in (5.11). The pressure’s spatial mean is not fixed here. The conditions select $B(0)$ through both displacement endpoints; they do not require zero initial velocity or vanishing before activation.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.MeanSolution.summary: Zero displacement at both ends selects the mean velocity

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Origin.text: On $[t_0,T]$, put $M=DU\circ X$, $\kappa=DX^{-T}k_*$, and $\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|c|$. The formal conditions require $\kappa,c\ne0$, $\kappa\cdot c=0$, $\kappa_t=-M^T\kappa$ and $c_t=-(I-2P_\kappa)Mc$. For every transverse solution $b$ of the same amplitude equation and $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$, require $|b(t)|/|c(t)|\le\mathsf D|b(t')|/|c(t')|$, and require $\kappa\cdot Mc\ge\mathsf D^{-1}|\kappa||c|$. Finally $\gamma\le1$. These are hypotheses, not an existence theorem. With $\lambda\ge1$ supplied separately, $\gamma>0$ and the stability inequality is unchanged when its denominators are replaced by $\gamma$. The paper’s stronger normalization $\max\gamma=1$ is not required.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Origin.summary: Allow a smaller peak while retaining the central growth conditions

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Parent.text:
The domain is represented by periodic fields on $\mathbb R^3$. Require $T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$, $\lambda\ge1$, smooth odd divergence-free $U$ with flow $X$, and Fourier support $|\xi|\le2\mathsf D$. Operator norms of $
abla U$, $D_aX$ and its inverse are at most $\mathsf D$. The pressure $p$ is smooth and periodic; $R_U=U_t+U\cdot
abla U+
abla p$ is odd, supported in $|\xi|\le4\mathsf D$, and has supremum norm at most $\lambda^{-5/2}$. Finally $D^2p-
abla R_U\le I$ as quadratic forms. The time derivative is within $[0,T]$. Unlike §5.1, this condition imposes neither $\int p=0$ nor $\Delta p=-\operatorname{tr}((
abla U)^2)$, and it does not assume $\operatorname{div}R_U=0$. The numbered results separately add $T>0$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Parent.summary: Record the parent bounds without imposing the Poisson normalization

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.TransverseSolution.text: Given the parent flow, its gradient $M$, transported covector $\kappa$ and forcing profile $f$, a transverse solution on $[0,T]$ satisfies $V_t+MV+\kappa\partial_s\pi=f$, $\kappa\cdot V=0$, $\langle V\rangle_s=0$ and $V(0,a,s)=0$. The phase pressure is also normalized by $\langle\pi\rangle_s=0$. These are smooth profiles with phase period one and the simultaneous label-phase translation law giving a periodic physical field. Time derivatives hold the label fixed. This is the problem used for (1.12) after its specified forcing is inserted. The definition describes a solution; it does not assert existence, uniqueness or a bound.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.TransverseSolution.summary: The correction starts from zero and remains perpendicular to the covector

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Yd.text: The paper’s $C_p$ is stored at index $p-1$; the physical expansion sets $C_1=0$. The field $Y_p=V_p+C_p$ groups the new transverse velocity with the divergence correction produced by $V_{p-1}$. This is the convention at the start of §5.5, reflecting the extra frequency gain of the correction. The sum itself imposes no equation; its size and constraints follow from the expansion equations and Theorem 5.6.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Yd.summary: Group the velocity with the preceding divergence correction

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Zd.text: For an indexed family of profiles, the formal definition gives $Z_p=V_p+C_p+B_p$ in the paper's notation. Here $C_p$ is generated by the preceding oscillation $V_{p-1}$: the stored correction index is one smaller than the paper index. The formula defines the level field used in the quadratic interactions of §1.3 and §5.5. It does not impose that $B_p$ is phase independent or that $V_p$ is transverse; these belong to the expansion equations. At index zero, subtraction is truncated to zero, so the intended mathematical use is at levels $p\ge1$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Zd.summary: Each level combines its oscillation, inherited correction and mean

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.curlCorrection.text: Profiles are smooth on $[0,T]$, with phase period one and $F(t,a+n,s+k_*\cdot n)=F(t,a,s)$. Nonvanishing of the transported covector is supplied by the parent geometry. The correction is $C[V]=\mathbf d\times Q[V]$, with $Q[V]=-\partial_s^{-1}((\kappa\times V)/|\kappa|^2)$. For zero-mean transverse profiles it gives $V+C[V]=\widetilde{\mathbf d}\times Q[V]$, as used in §5.5. The formal operation acts on the oscillatory part of a general profile; the divergence identity requires the zero-mean and transversality assumptions.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.curlCorrection.summary: Take the label curl of the vector potential

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.envelopeSupport.text:
This takes the topological support of the envelope after periodic extension from the centered cell. The raw envelope is $g(a)=\chi(|a|/\ell)$, using the fixed smooth cutoff $\chi$ of the activation profiles. The periodization selects a representative in the half-open centered label cell, so this support is repeated across all lattice translates. Outside this set the oscillatory profiles and their sources vanish. It is not just one Euclidean ball when viewed on $\mathbb R^3$.

The radial envelope divides by $\ell$. At $\ell=0$ the quotient is zero everywhere, so the envelope is identically one and its support is all space, not a localized ball. The radius hypothesis with $\mathsf D\ge2$ gives $\ell>0$. A sufficiently large exponent additionally keeps the support away from the cell boundary, making periodic extension smooth. The topological support is a closure, not a numerical supremum; no fallback value for an unbounded supremum is involved. No integral or conversion from extended nonnegative reals occurs.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.envelopeSupport.summary: Spatial support repeated over the label lattice

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.expansion.text: For depth $P\ge0$, the formal definition is $W=\sum_{p=1}^P(V_p+C_{p+1}+B_p)$, using the paper's indices. Thus the correction of $V_P$ remains even though the next oscillation is absent. When $C_1=0$ and $P\ge1$, regrouping gives $W=\sum_{p=1}^PZ_p+C_{P+1}$; when $P=0$, the sum is empty and equals zero. The definition accepts arbitrary additive families. To obtain the approximate velocity, one evaluates the profiles at $s=k_*\cdot a$, passes to physical coordinates and adds the parent. Differential equations, divergence cancellation and size estimates are additional facts.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.expansion.summary: Every oscillation is kept together with its own curl correction

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.expansionPressure.text: The depth $P$ is a nonnegative integer; an empty sum is zero, while Proposition 5.4 uses $P\ge2$. The profile pressure is $\mathsf P=\sum_{p=1}^{P}(\mathsf p_p+\bar q_p)$, as in Proposition 5.4. In an admissible expansion the oscillatory pressures have zero phase mean, the mean pressures are phase independent, and $\bar q_1=0$. Those equations and normalizations belong to the construction; this expression simply adds the selected pressure components.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.expansionPressure.summary: Sum the mean and oscillatory pressures through the depth

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.fieldNorm.text: For a field $f(t,a,s)$ and time set $I$, the expression sums $\sup_{t\in I,a,s}\ell_*^{|\alpha|}h^j|\partial_a^\alpha\partial_s^j(\tau(t)f)|$ over $|\alpha|+j\le n$, counting each multi-index once. Only label and phase variables are differentiated. Each supremum is implemented as a real supremum of a set that also contains zero; if that set is unbounded above, that term of the sum takes the default value zero. Thus a finite numerical value alone does not establish boundedness. Analytic estimates separately require or prove boundedness of the derivative sets. With $\tau=\gamma^{-1}$ this gives the weighted norm of Appendix D when $\gamma>0$; at a time where $\gamma(t)=0$ the multiplier $\gamma(t)^{-1}$ is zero by the convention for division by zero, so that time contributes zero. These conventions do not assert any estimate for an unbounded field or a vanishing weight.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.fieldNorm.summary: Label and phase derivatives carry their natural scales

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.launchNorm.text:
This is the finite norm of $f(t_0,a,s)$ with time restricted to the singleton $\{t_0\}$. It supplies the initial-data term in (5.20). The singleton restricts only which slice is sampled; the differentiated variables remain $a$ and $s$, so this is not a derivative within a singleton time set.

A time outside $[0,T]$ reads the smooth profile’s stipulated zero extension, giving a zero slice irrespective of the interior data. The launch hypotheses put $t_0$ inside $[0,T]$; smoothness and the compact periodic quotient then bound all sampled jets. The real supremum must still be read with these guards, and zero $\ell$ or $h$ suppresses the corresponding derivatives. There is no reciprocal weight, integration, conversion from extended nonnegative reals or square root here.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.launchNorm.summary: The finite norm of the initial slice

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.leading.text: For a seed field $\mathbf a(t,a)$, define $A_1(t,a,s)=g(a)\mathbf a(t,a)F_h(s)$ with $g(a)=\chi(|a|/\ell_*)$. The formalization selects a particular smooth radial cutoff $\chi$ and the periodic phase profile $F_h$ constructed earlier. This is the unswitched leading wave in §5.1; the time cutoff is introduced later as $V_1=\widetilde\chi A_1$. The formula itself assumes no differential equation for the seed and no positive radius or width. Its intended smooth localized interpretation uses $\ell_*>0$, $0<h\le1$, and the seed regularity on $[t_0,T]$ supplied in the application.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.leading.summary: Multiply the seed by the spatial envelope and phase profile

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.leadingPressure.text:
This is $-2g(a)(\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a)/|\kappa|^2$ times $P_h(s)$, where $P_h$ is the zero-mean periodic primitive of $F_h$. The minus sign is part of the pressure formula. The parent velocity $U$ and flow $X$ provide the actual strain and transported covector; the amplitude is the proposed seed. It is the unswitched pressure paired with $A_1$, not the parent pressure $p_U$ and not the sum of all hierarchy pressures.

The coefficient divides by $|\kappa|^2$, so $\kappa=0$ would silently force that coefficient to zero. The parent hypotheses, positive slab length and the launch hypotheses exclude this. The envelope and phase primitives inherit the requirements $\ell>0$, $0<h\le1$ described for the leading oscillation; with these guards the phase integrals are over smooth real functions and cannot vanish merely because they are undefined. The raw definition accepts bad data and gives no nonzero or regularity certificate itself. There is no real supremum or conversion from extended nonnegative reals here.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.levelSource.text: This defines the source for $p\ge2$ using $Y_i=V_i+C_i$ and $Z_i=Y_i+B_i$; subtraction of natural-number indices is truncated at zero outside that range. The source $H_p$ contains $(\partial_t+M)C_p+\mathbf d\mathsf p_{p-1}$ and the two interaction sums of (5.26). At level two it subtracts the activation contribution of the curl correction, recovering (5.25). The correction $C_p$ is already known from $V_{p-1}$, so the source does not depend on the new transverse velocity.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.levelSource.summary: Collect lower-level terms before choosing the new mean

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.meanSource.text: At level $p$, the formal definition is $\overline f_p=-\langle H_p\rangle_s-\mathbf1_{p=2}R$, where $H_p$ is the source assembled before solving for the new mean and $R$ is the supplied parent residual. In the geometric application $R=R_U\circ X$ is independent of phase. The negative sign makes the mean correction cancel the averaged error, and level two is the only place where the previous parent's residual is inserted. This is the right side of the equation described in §1.3. The definition does not solve that equation or impose the endpoint conditions selecting its initial velocity.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.meanSource.summary: Only the first mean equation contains the parent residual

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.ops.text:
This abbreviation packages the actions $\partial_t+M$, the label gradient $\mathbf d$, the phase gradient $\kappa\partial_s$, label advection, phase advection and phase averaging. Its argument is a parent geometry for the actual parent $U$, flow $X$ and carrier $k$; it carries smooth coefficient profiles and identifications with the inverse deformation, strain and covector. It acts on smooth lattice-twisted profiles. An equation using its material operator $\partial_t+M$ is therefore an equation in the profile space, including the inherited zero extension outside $[0,T]$.

The operators contain derivatives within the positive-length slab and phase integrals. The hypothesis $0<T$ and smooth profile types ensure genuine derivatives on the slab; finite-dimensional vector and scalar values and smooth phase-periodic slices make the phase means integrable. Outside the slab the representative is intentionally zero and carries no physical claim. No inverse of a possibly singular matrix is selected here: the parent geometry supplies the actual coefficient identities. No conversion from extended nonnegative reals is used in this abbreviation.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.ops.summary: The operators of the parent geometry

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.oscSource.text: For an arbitrary preliminary source $H_p$, phase averaging is the integral over one period; centering is an algebraic operation, not an existence statement. The forcing $f_p=-(H_p-\langle H_p\rangle_s)$ is the centered term in (5.27). Its sign cancels the oscillatory part of $H_p$ in the momentum equation. The additional forcing $f_p^S$ is formed only after the mean solve, and the transverse equation uses their sum; centering the preliminary source alone does not include that transport.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.oscSource.summary: Negate the oscillatory part of the preliminary source

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.radius.text: The formal radius is $\ell_*=(\mathsf D^a)^{-1}$, where $a$ is a nonnegative integer. In the parent regime $\mathsf D\ge2$, this is positive; choosing $a\ge3$ gives the paper’s $\ell_*\le\mathsf D^{-3}$. The later estimates first fix a sufficiently large threshold for $a$, then quantify over all larger integer exponents. The radius does not change with derivative order or expansion depth. The definition also accepts $\mathsf D=0$: since the reciprocal of zero is zero, it then gives zero for $a>0$ and one for $a=0$. Those values are excluded by the parent assumptions.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.radius.summary: Use one integer exponent to choose the spatial scale

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.remainder.text: The stored correction is indexed by its generating velocity, so the paper’s $C_{P+1}$ is the stored correction with index $P$. The expression is (5.30): the two final linear terms, label interactions with $i+j\ge P+1$, and phase interactions with $i+j\ge P+2$. Both indices run through $P+1$, where only the final correction remains. The activation error is separate. The expansion equations are needed to identify this expression with the uncanceled momentum residual.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.remainder.summary: Keep precisely the interactions beyond the canceled levels

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.strainField.text:
This is $M(t,a)=(D_xU)(t,X(t,a))$. Its value is a continuous linear map on Euclidean three-space, so subsequent norms are operator norms. The flow used is the transition $X(0\to t)$ from time zero to $t$; the direction of these two time arguments matters.

The spatial derivative of $U(t)$ can equal its default zero on a nonsmooth slice. The parent's velocity smoothness clause gives genuine spatial derivatives for every $t\in[0,T]$, which is where the estimates use $M$. No regularity is claimed for values outside that slab. There is no division, integration, supremum, conversion from extended nonnegative reals or square root in this definition.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.strainField.summary: Parent velocity gradient along a trajectory

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.suppSource.text: The formal definition gives $f_p^S=-\sum_{i=2}^{p}(B_i\cdot\kappa)\partial_sY_{p+1-i}$, with $Y_j=V_j+C_j$ in paper notation. In particular, at $p=2$ it is $-(B_2\cdot\kappa)\partial_sV_1$ when $C_1=0$, the extra term in (1.12). The sum is empty below level two. At every included index $p+1-i\ge1$, so nonnegative-integer subtraction agrees with ordinary subtraction. For phase-independent $B_i,\kappa$ and differentiable periodic $Y_j$, its phase average vanishes. These properties are not imposed by the formula alone; they come from the geometric profiles and expansion equations.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.suppSource.summary: The newly solved mean transports the leading wave phase

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.totalDivergence.text:
This is $\tilde{\mathbf d}\cdot W=(\mathbf d+\kappa\partial_s)\cdot W$, expressed as the sum of the label divergence determined by the inverse deformation $(D_aX)^{-1}$ and the phase derivative contracted with the covector $\kappa$. The output is a smooth scalar profile. A zero output in Proposition 5.4 is the divergence cancellation needed before graph evaluation produces an Eulerian incompressible velocity.

The underlying derivatives are applied to smooth profile slices and along a slab with $T>0$, so they do not use the zero derivative of a nonsmooth field on that domain. The zero extension of the profile space outside the slab is intentional and carries no assertion about Eulerian regularity there. The definition has no division, integration, supremum, conversion from extended nonnegative reals or square root.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.totalDivergence.summary: Divergence with label and phase derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.uNorm.text:
This measures all label and phase derivatives through order $n$ on $[0,T]$, with scales $\ell$ and $h$ and multiplier one. It is the norm used for the mean corrections, which need not vanish before activation. Smoothness and both periodicity conditions are carried by the profile space. The norm contains no time derivatives.

For an arbitrary $T<0$ the time set is empty and the value is zero. At positive $T$, smooth lattice-twisted profiles have bounded spatial and phase jets on the compact quotient; a companion lemma supplies the required boundedness above of the weighted mixed derivative values. Thus the fallback value for an unbounded supremum is excluded in the stated theorems. The definition by itself does not require $\ell,h>0$, so zero scales can suppress higher derivatives. The parent hypotheses with radius and width supply positive scales. No division, integral, conversion from extended nonnegative reals or square root occurs in this specialization.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.uNorm.summary: The unweighted profile norm on the full slab

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.wNorm.text: For a smooth profile $f$ on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, define $\|f\|_{[n],\gamma}=\sum_{|\alpha|+j\le n}\ell_*^{|\alpha|}h^j\sup_{t\in[t_0,T],a,s}|\partial_a^\alpha\partial_s^jf(t,a,s)|/\gamma(t)$ for positive scales and positive $\gamma$. Each multi-index occurs once; time is not differentiated. Profiles are one-periodic in phase and obey $f(t,a+z,s+k_*\cdot z)=f(t,a,s)$ for lattice vectors $z$. In the application $0\le t_0<T$ and $\gamma$ is continuous and positive, so these suprema are finite. The unrestricted expression instead uses $|\gamma(t)^{-1}|$: division by zero is assigned zero, and an unbounded set of real derivative values has real supremum assigned zero. Consequently the unrestricted formula alone does not certify boundedness; the positivity and regularity hypotheses in the estimates are essential.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.wNorm.summary: Oscillatory corrections are measured against the central seed

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.waveVector.text: The formal vector is $\kappa(t,a)=D(X_{t,0})(X_{0,t}(a))^Tk_*$, with reference time zero. When $X$ is the smooth parent flow, the inverse derivative identity makes this $(D_aX(t,a))^{-T}k_*$, exactly the transported field in §5.1. The argument $a$ is a parent label, not the physical point. The formula alone does not require $k_*\ne0$ or guarantee invertibility: these enter through the parent and activation hypotheses. Likewise, nonvanishing and the frequency comparisons (5.3) are proved separately. Outside differentiability, the formal derivative expression is assigned its default value zero.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.waveVector.summary: Apply the transpose of the inverse deformation to the carrier

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.weight.text: Given a frequency $\lambda$ and central seed $\mathbf a(t,0)$, define $\gamma(t)=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|$. This is the weight used in the active-interval profile norms: $\|f\|_{[n],\gamma}$ measures spatial and phase derivatives of $f/\gamma$ on $[t_0,T]$. Because $\gamma$ depends only on time, those derivatives do not act on it. The definition itself proves neither positivity nor an upper bound. The parent frequency $\lambda\ge1$, nonzero central seed, and normalization imposed elsewhere give $0<\gamma\le1$. It does not impose the paper’s stronger equality $\max_{[t_0,T]}\gamma=1$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.weight.summary: Measure corrections relative to the amplitude of the central seed

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.width.text: The formal width is the real power $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$. Under the parent condition $\lambda\ge1$, this gives $0<h\le1$, as required for the chosen periodic profile $F_h$. In the finite profile norms, every phase derivative carries a factor $h$; converting to a physical derivative introduces $|k_*|h^{-1}$. With $|k_*|\le\mathsf D\lambda$ this is at most $\mathsf D\lambda^{3/2}$. The width definition does not assert these inequalities without their frequency assumptions. Combined with central amplitude scale $\lambda^{-3/4}$ and $\|F_h\|_\infty=O(h)$, it yields the leading velocity scale $\lambda^{-5/4}$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.width.summary: Set the narrow periodic profile scale from the frequency

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.Cd_reflFamily.text: Unfolding the completed-family component gives the divergence correction as the negated reflection of the original correction. This is a definitional identity, not a new estimate.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.CoefBounds.text:
Bounds $N_G(n)$, $N_\kappa(n)$ for the norms (D.1) of the coefficients $(D_aX)^{-1}$ and $\kappa$ on every time set in $[0,T]$.

Default values: The statement includes finite coefficient norms on every allowed time subset and their stated upper bounds. An empty subset is allowed but is not used to infer a nontrivial slab bound; the application supplies the actual slab and positive scales.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.CoefBounds.summary: Uniform bounds for the coframe and wave vector

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.EvenGeometry.text:
The parities of the coefficient profiles of an odd parent: $(D_aX)^{-1}$, $M$, $\kappa$ are even.

Default values: A structure containing three parity equalities. It is not a new geometric construction and does not imply existence of an odd parent; a separate theorem proves it from the parent data.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.EvenGeometry.summary: Even coefficients for the reflected hierarchy

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.NormSetting.text:
The standing data of the norms: $T, \ell, h > 0$, $0 \le t_0 \le T$, and the weight $\gamma$ continuous, positive and at most one on $[t_0,T]$.

Default values: The setting explicitly excludes zero or negative scales and time length, requires $0 \le t_0 \le T$, and imposes continuous positive weights at most one on the active interval. These conditions rule out degenerate reciprocal weights in subsequent norm comparisons.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.NormSetting.summary: Positive scales and weights on the time slab

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.NormSetting.active.text: In the standing norm setting the active interval $[t_0,T]$ lies in the full interval $[0, T]$, since $t_0 \ge 0$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.NormSetting.active.summary: The active interval lies in the full slab

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.NormSetting.finP.text: In the standing norm setting, the unweighted finite profile norm $\|f\|_{[n]}$ on the active interval $[t_0,T]$ is finite for every smooth twisted profile $f$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.NormSetting.finP.summary: Finiteness of the active unweighted profile norms

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.NormSetting.finU.text: In the standing norm setting, the unweighted finite profile norm $\|f\|_{[n]}$ on the full interval $[0,T]$ is finite for every smooth twisted profile $f$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.NormSetting.finU.summary: Finiteness of the full unweighted profile norms

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.NormSetting.finW.text: In the standing norm setting, the weighted norm $\|f\|_{[n],\gamma}$ on $[t_0,T]$ is finite for every smooth twisted profile $f$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.NormSetting.finW.summary: Finiteness of the weighted profile norms

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.NormSetting.invBoun.text: The inverse bound of a norm setting.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.NormSetting.invBoun.summary: The reciprocal weight is bounded on the active interval

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.NormSetting.weight_.text: The weight of a norm setting is positive.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.OddExpansions.text:
This statement asks for a threshold in $a$ above which the physical perturbation of every permitted expansion is odd. It isolates the symmetry input needed by the quantitative approximation argument. A separate theorem establishes it from the parity of the construction and the uniqueness clause of Proposition 5.4.

Default values: A statement over permitted expansions, not a choice of an expansion. It can be vacuous if there are no admissible expansions; later uses combine it with the existence clause of Proposition 5.4.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.OddExpansions.summary: Oddness of every sufficiently separated expansion

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.P_le_U.text: The unweighted norm $\|f\|_{[n]}$ on $[t_0,T]$ is at most the unweighted norm $\|f\|_{[n]}$ on the full interval $[0,T]$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.P_le_U.summary: The full slab norm controls the active unweighted norm

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.P_le_W.text: The unweighted norm $\|f\|_{[n]}$ on $[t_0,T]$ is at most the weighted norm $\|f\|_{[n],\gamma}$ on $[t_0,T]$ in the standing norm setting.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.P_le_W.summary: The weighted norm controls the active unweighted norm

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.PhaseIndep.text:
A field is independent of the phase.

A universal equality predicate, meaningful for every field. It does not supply differentiability; the derivative consequences add smoothness hypotheses.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.PhaseIndep.eq_comp.text: A phase-independent field is its own composition with $(a, s) \mapsto (a, 0)$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.PhaseIndep.eq_comp.summary: A phase independent field ignores the phase coordinate

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.PhaseIndep.fderiv_e.text: The derivative of a phase-independent smooth field only sees the label component of the increment.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.PhaseIndep.fderiv_e.summary: Only label increments affect phase independent fields

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.PhaseIndep.labelPar.text: Label derivatives of a phase-independent smooth field are phase independent.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.PhaseIndep.phasePar.text: The phase derivative of a phase-independent smooth field vanishes.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.PhaseIndep.phasePar.summary: Phase derivatives vanish for phase independent fields

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.S_eq_smul.text: For a twisted profile $V$ equal to the leading field on the active cell, the activation term satisfies $S = \tilde\chi' V$ on the slab, as for the first velocity with $\tilde\chi$ replaced by $\tilde\chi'$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.S_eq_smul.summary: Activation is the derivative of the switch

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.U_le_W.text: The $U$ seminorm is at most the $W$ seminorm for profiles vanishing before $t0$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.U_le_W.summary: The weighted norm controls an initially vanishing profile

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.U_mono.text: For derivative orders n ≤ m, the unweighted seminorm of order n is at most that of order m. The statement compares derivative orders of one profile and makes no monotonicity assertion in the hierarchy index.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.U_mono.summary: Unweighted norms increase with derivative order

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.Un.text:
The unweighted norm $\|f\|_{[n]}$ on $[0,T]$ as a seminorm on profiles.

Default values: The standing norm setting supplies a positive time slab and smooth twisted profiles, which make the unweighted seminorm finite. It includes the whole slab; controlling it by an active weighted norm additionally requires vanishing before activation.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.Un.summary: The unweighted norm as a seminorm

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.V1_eq_smul.text: $V_1 = \tilde\chi V$: for a twisted profile $V$ equal to $A_1$ on $[t_0,T] \times [-1/2,1/2]^3$, the first velocity $V_1 = \tilde\chi A_1$ (on the cell) is $\tilde\chi V$ on the whole slab (lattice twist; before $t_0$ both vanish).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.V1_eq_smul.summary: The first velocity is the switched leading wave

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.V1_transverse.text: $V_1 = \tilde\chi A_1$ is transverse: $\kappa\cdot V_1 = 0$ on the slab.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.V1_transverse.summary: The leading velocity is transverse to the wave vector

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.VanishBefore.text:
A profile vanishing for $t < t_0$.

Default values: A universal vanishing condition restricted to $[0,T]$ and $t < t_0$. At $t_0 = 0$ it is vacuous; equality at the activation time is obtained from the relevant smoothness or cutoff data when needed.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.VanishBefore.summary: A profile vanishes before the activation time

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.W_mono.text: For derivative orders n ≤ m, the weighted seminorm of order n is at most that of order m. The variables being compared are derivative orders, not hierarchy levels; this corrects the loose use of “level” in the source docstring.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.W_mono.summary: Weighted norms increase with derivative order

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.Wn.text:
The weighted norm $\|\cdot\|_{[n],\gamma}$ as a seminorm.

The standing norm data ($T,\ell_*,h>0$, $0\le t_0\le T$, and $\gamma$ continuous, positive and at most one on $[t_0,T]$) supply continuous positive weights and a compact nonempty active interval, so the amplitude seminorm is finite. The weighted norm is meaningful at every permitted derivative order; controlling the whole slab additionally requires preactivation vanishing.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.Wn.summary: Weighted active profile norms as seminorms

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.Yd_reflFamily.text: The level sum $Y_i = V_i + C_i$ commutes with the reflection of a family: the sums of the reflected family are the reflections $\varrho Y_i$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.Yd_reflFamily.summary: Reflection of the completed oscillatory velocity

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.Zd_reflFamily.text: The level sum $Z_i = Y_i + B_i$ commutes with the reflection of a family: the sums of the reflected family are the reflections $\varrho Z_i$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.Zd_reflFamily.summary: Reflection of the completed level sums $Z_i$

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.activation_average.text: The activation term has zero phase mean.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.activation_average.summary: The activation source has zero phase mean

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.activation_eval.text: The activation term on the slab: $S = \tilde\chi' \cdot A_1^{\rm tw}$, where $A_1^{\rm tw}$ is the twisted extension of the leading oscillation $A_1$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.activation_eval.summary: Activation is the differentiated time cutoff

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.activation_holder.text: Assumes an active-interval $C^{1,1/2}$ bound $B\gamma(t)$ for the extended leading profile together with its divergence correction. At a fixed time, the activation source and its correction are $\tilde\chi'$ times this pair, so homogeneity gives the bound $B$ times $\sup_{t\in[t_0,T]}|\tilde\chi'(t)|\gamma(t)$. Before activation both terms vanish. The estimates for $B$ are supplied by the caller from Lemmas 5.3 and 5.5 and Lemma 5.7; this helper does not itself take those numbered hypotheses.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.activation_holder.summary: Bounding the activation error in physical space

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.approx_divergence.text:
On $[0,T]	imes\mathbb T^3$, $0<T\le1$, let $U,p_U$ be smooth, $U$ odd and solenoidal, $X$ its flow, and $R_U=U_t+U\cdot
abla U+
abla p_U$ odd. Assume $\mathsf D\ge2,\lambda\ge1$, Fourier radii $2\mathsf D,4\mathsf D$ for $U,R_U$, $\|
abla U\|_\infty,\|DX\|_\infty,\|DX^{-1}\|_\infty\le\mathsf D$, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. Profiles are smooth on the closed slab, one-periodic in phase, and satisfy $f(t,a+n,s+k_*\cdot n)=f(t,a,s)$. Write $f^
atural(t,x)=f(t,X_{t,0}(x),k_*\cdot X_{t,0}(x))$. Let $\widetilde{\mathbf d}=DX^{-T}(
abla_a+k_*\partial_s)$. If $\widetilde{\mathbf d}\cdot W=0$, then $\operatorname{div}(U+W^
atural)=0$ at every $t\in[0,T]$ and position. This is the divergence implication used for the approximate velocity. It assumes the profile constraint and the actual transported coefficients; it does not derive that constraint from the finite recursion.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.approx_divergence.summary: The full profile divergence becomes ordinary spatial divergence

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.approx_residual.text:
On $[0,T]	imes\mathbb T^3$, $0<T\le1$, let $U,p_U$ be smooth, $U$ odd and solenoidal, $X$ its flow, and $R_U=U_t+U\cdot
abla U+
abla p_U$ odd. Assume $\mathsf D\ge2,\lambda\ge1$, Fourier radii $2\mathsf D,4\mathsf D$ for $U,R_U$, $\|
abla U\|_\infty,\|DX\|_\infty,\|DX^{-1}\|_\infty\le\mathsf D$, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. Profiles are smooth on the closed slab, one-periodic in phase, and satisfy $f(t,a+n,s+k_*\cdot n)=f(t,a,s)$. Write $f^
atural(t,x)=f(t,X_{t,0}(x),k_*\cdot X_{t,0}(x))$. Set $M=DU\circ X$ and $\widetilde{\mathbf d}=DX^{-T}(
abla_a+k_*\partial_s)$. If $W_t+MW+(W\cdot\widetilde{\mathbf d})W+\widetilde{\mathbf d}\mathsf P+R=F$ with $R=R_U\circ X$, then $V=U+W^
atural$, $\Pi=p_U+\mathsf P^
atural$ satisfy $V_t+V\cdot
abla V+
abla\Pi=F^
atural$ on $[0,T]$. Thus the parent's residual cancels exactly. The profile equation is a premise; this implication does not construct its profiles.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.approx_residual.summary: Evaluate the profile equation and cancel the parent residual

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.approx_smooth.text:
On $[0,T]	imes\mathbb T^3$, $0<T\le1$, let $U,p_U$ be smooth, $U$ odd and solenoidal, $X$ its flow, and $R_U=U_t+U\cdot
abla U+
abla p_U$ odd. Assume $\mathsf D\ge2,\lambda\ge1$, Fourier radii $2\mathsf D,4\mathsf D$ for $U,R_U$, $\|
abla U\|_\infty,\|DX\|_\infty,\|DX^{-1}\|_\infty\le\mathsf D$, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. Profiles are smooth on the closed slab, one-periodic in phase, and satisfy $f(t,a+n,s+k_*\cdot n)=f(t,a,s)$. Write $f^
atural(t,x)=f(t,X_{t,0}(x),k_*\cdot X_{t,0}(x))$. For any velocity and pressure profiles $W,\mathsf P$, the physical fields $U+W^
atural$ and $p_U+\mathsf P^
atural$ are jointly smooth on $[0,T]	imes\mathbb R^3$ and spatially periodic. No profile momentum equation is a premise of this regularity statement. The conclusion concerns the closed slab; assigning a profile zero outside it does not assert smooth continuation through its time endpoints.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.approx_smooth.summary: Global profile translation laws give smooth periodic Eulerian fields

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.average_first.text: $\langle V_1\rangle = 0$: on the cell, $V_1$ agrees with the twisted leading velocity profile of $\tilde\chi A_1$ built in the bridge to the earlier construction, whose phase average vanishes.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.average_first.summary: The first oscillatory velocity has zero phase mean

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.average_le.text: (D.5) of Lemma D.1 (the phase average and the centered part).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.average_le.summary: Phase averaging and centering preserve derivative bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.average_material_ze.text: For a profile $V$ with zero phase average, the material derivative also has zero phase average: $\langle(\partial_t+M)V\rangle = 0$ when $\langle V\rangle = 0$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.average_material_ze.summary: Material evolution preserves a vanishing phase average

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.average_phaseGrad_z.text: $\langle\kappa\partial_s q\rangle = 0$ for every pressure profile (the phase derivative of a periodic function has mean zero, and $\kappa$ does not depend on the phase).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.average_phaseGrad_z.summary: A periodic phase gradient has zero average

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.average_reflection.text: The phase average commutes with the reflection.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.average_sourceBefor.text: Averages the pre-mean source and rewrites the fast phase products by periodic integration by parts, using transversality and the divergence correction identity. The resulting formula contains averaged label products, a label divergence product and the mean–mean label product. This is the mechanism by which the mean source avoids paying a fast phase derivative.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.average_sourceBefor.summary: Integration by parts rewrites the mean source

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.average_vrefl.text: Taking the phase average commutes with the velocity reflection: $\langle\varrho f\rangle = \varrho\langle f\rangle$, where $\varrho f(t,a,s) = -f(t,-a,-s)$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.average_vrefl.summary: Velocity reflection commutes with phase averaging

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.band_jets.text: Bernstein's inequality in operator norm (B.1): a real vector field on the torus with frequencies at most $4\Lambda$ satisfies $\|\nabla^m g(x)\| \le C_m \Lambda^m \|g\|$. The coordinate sums of (B.1) are converted to operator norms by writing each coordinate word in sorted order and bounding the operator norm of a multilinear map by the sum of its coordinate values.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.band_jets.summary: Bernstein bounds for the parent residual jets

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.bilinear_abstract.text: The splitting argument for a bilinear map, over an abstract module with an involution $r$: if $r(B f g) = -\sigma(f)\sigma(g) B f g$ whenever $r f = \sigma(f) f$, $r g = \sigma(g) g$ with $\sigma = \pm1$, then $r(B f g) = -B(r f)(r g)$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.bilinear_abstract.summary: Extending parity identities to all profile pairs

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.bilinear_neg_neg.text: A bilinear map is even under $(f,g) \mapsto (-f,-g)$: changing the sign of both arguments leaves its value unchanged.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.bilinear_neg_neg.summary: Two sign changes cancel in bilinear terms

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.coefBounds_of_h5_1.text: The coefficient norms $\|(D_aX)^{-1}\|_{[n]} \le N_G(n)$, $\|\kappa\|_{[n]} \le N_\kappa(n)$ on every time set in $[0,T]$, from (D.6) and (5.8) of the assumed Proposition 5.1, when $\ell_* \le \mathsf D^{-C}$; here $N_G(n) = K_n \mathsf D^C$ and $N_\kappa(n) = K_n \mathsf D^C \lambda$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.coefBounds_of_h5_1.summary: Parent geometry controls the advection coefficients

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.coefField.text:
The coefficient field $(t,a,s) \mapsto c(t,a)$.

Default values: This is a total algebraic or continuous-linear construction with no division or noncanonical choice. Zero inputs have their literal algebraic values. Any geometric identification or differentiability property is supplied separately by the consuming theorem.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.coefField.summary: A label coefficient extended independently of phase

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.coefField_bounds.text: Norms of a phase-independent coefficient from bounds on its Fréchet jets ($\ell^m |\nabla^m c(t,a)| \le B$ for $m \le n$, uniformly bounded jets): the field $(t,a,s) \mapsto c(t,a)$ has a finite norm (D.1) of order $n$, at most $\#W_n B$. This is the argument of the coefficient bound for a linear functional of a matrix field, without the functional.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.coefField_bounds.summary: Label jet bounds control coefficient profile norms

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.coef_bounds.text: Norms of a phase-independent coefficient. For a smooth coframe $G$ with uniformly bounded jets and $\ell^m |\nabla^m G(t,a)| \le B$ for $m \le n$, and a continuous linear functional $L$, the field $(t,a,s) \mapsto L(G(t,a))$ has a finite norm (D.1) of order $n$, at most $\#W_n \| L\| B$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.coef_bounds.summary: Profile norms of phase independent coefficients

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.coframeC.text:
The coframe $(D_aX)^{-1}(t,a) = D(X(t,\cdot)^{-1})(X(t,a))$ on a time set.

Default values: Uses the Fréchet derivative of a supplied flow map, which is defined for every map. For arbitrary nonsmooth maps that derivative can take its default zero value; the parent geometry and the parent estimates ensure it is the actual derivative in every analytic application.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.coframeC.summary: The inverse deformation as a coefficient field

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.compl_exp_split.text: Exponent splitting for the completion terms of (5.37), (5.38).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.compl_exp_split.summary: Separating the divergence correction decay powers

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.complete_smul_time_.text: $C[\cdot]$ acts at fixed time: if $W(t,\cdot,\cdot) = c V(t,\cdot,\cdot)$ at one time $t$ (for a constant $c$), then $C[W](t,\cdot,\cdot) = c C[V](t,\cdot,\cdot)$ (the curl completion is linear and uses only the profile at the time $t$).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.complete_smul_time_.summary: Time multiplication commutes with divergence completion

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.continuous_phase_sl.text: The phase slices of a twisted profile are continuous.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.curlCorrection_acti.text: The divergence correction $C[\cdot]$ acts at fixed time: at $t \in [t_0,T]$, $C[S](t,\cdot) = \tilde\chi'(t) C[V_0](t,\cdot)$ for the extended leading profile $V_0$, by the corresponding fact for scalar multiples of twisted profiles in the earlier library construction.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.curlCorrection_acti.summary: Time factors pass through the divergence correction

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.curlCorrection_extL.text: $C[V_0]$ vanishes at labels outside $\operatorname{supp} g$ (it is a label derivative of the wave potential of $V_0$, which vanishes on the open complement of $\operatorname{supp} g$).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.curlCorrection_extL.summary: The correction preserves the envelope support

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.curlCorrection_vref.text: $C[\varrho V] = \varrho C[V]$ for $\langle V\rangle = 0$ (even coframe and wave vector): the phase primitive of $-V(t,-a,-s)$ is $Q[V](t,-a,-s)$, and the slow curl of a reflected potential is minus the reflected slow curl.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.deformation_even.text: For an odd parent, the deformation gradient $D_aX(t,\cdot)$ of its flow is an even function of the label at each time.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.deformation_even.summary: The deformation of an odd parent is even

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.deriv_le.text: (D.3) of Lemma D.1 (label and phase derivatives).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.deriv_le.summary: The costs of label and phase differentiation

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.divProd.text:
$(\mathbf d\cdot V) Y$.

Default values: The expression is total as an algebraic combination of Fréchet derivatives, including their default value at nondifferentiable points. The estimates assume smooth fields and coefficients so those derivatives have the intended meaning. Empty derivative words act as the identity; empty coordinate sums or zero inputs cause no inverse operation.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.divProd.summary: The label divergence times a vector field

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.divergence_add'.text: The divergence is additive on differentiable vector fields: the divergence of a sum is the sum of the divergences. This copies a private lemma of the earlier library construction.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.divergence_add'.summary: Adding divergences of smooth vector fields

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.domain_bounds.text: For a time domain contained in $[0,T]$, a positive time weight, and a smooth profile with finite weighted derivative norms, the graph readout satisfies the integer and half Hölder estimates with $\Lambda = D^{C_1+a+1} \lambda^{3/2}$. If the field is independent of the phase, the same argument uses $\Lambda = D^{C_1+a+1}$. The proof iterates the coefficient estimate for one physical derivative and then bounds the full Fréchet derivatives by coordinate words.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.evalLM.text:
Evaluation of a twisted profile at a point as a linear map.

This is a total algebraic or continuous-linear construction with no division or noncanonical choice. Zero inputs have their literal algebraic values. Any geometric identification or differentiability property is supplied separately by the consuming theorem.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.eval_add.text: Evaluation of a sum of profiles.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.eval_add.summary: Evaluation distributes over sums of profiles

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.eval_sub.text: Evaluation of a difference of profiles.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.eval_sub.summary: Evaluation distributes over differences of profiles

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.evenGeometry.text: The coefficient profiles $(D_aX)^{-1}$, $M$ and $\kappa$ of an odd parent are even, by the reflection symmetry of the parent geometry in the earlier library construction.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.evenGeometry.summary: Parent symmetry supplies even hierarchy coefficients

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.exists_seed_extensi.text: The seed extends to a jointly smooth field on $\mathbb R \times \mathbb R^3$ that agrees with it on $[t_0,T] \times \mathbb R^3$ (library Seeley extension in time).

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.expansion_average_C.text: $\langle u.C i\rangle = 0$ for the corrections of an expansion ($C_{p+1} = C[V_p]$; $C_1 = 0$).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.expansion_average_C.summary: Every divergence correction has zero phase average

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.extLeading.text:
The twisted profile on $[0,T]$ of the leading field built from an extended seed amplitude, that is, a seed extended smoothly to the whole time interval.

Default values: The constructor takes positive scales, a support-fit inequality, and smoothness of the extended seed. Its extension can differ from the original seed before the active interval; no analytic bound on an arbitrary extension there is inferred from the active estimate.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.extLeading.summary: The twisted leading profile of an extended seed

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.extLeading_active_e.text: On $[t_0,T]$ the extended leading profile is the twisted extension of $A_1$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.extLeading_active_e.summary: Recovering the leading field after activation

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.extLeading_average.text: The extended leading profile has zero phase mean ($F_h$ has zero mean).

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.extLeading_eq_zero_.text: The extended leading profile vanishes at labels outside the support $\operatorname{supp} g$ of the periodized envelope, at every time and phase.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.extLeading_eq_zero_.summary: The extended seed stays inside the envelope

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.extLeading_eval.text: Evaluation of the extended leading term.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.extLeading_jets.text: Jets of the twisted extension versus jets of $A_1$ at a time $t \in [t_0,T]$, for the fields scaled by a constant $c$ (the weight $\gamma(t)^{-1}$): every jet of one is a jet of the other or zero.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.extLeading_jets.summary: Twisted extension preserves the leading jets

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.extLeading_transver.text: On $[t_0,T]$ the extended leading profile is transverse to $\kappa$ (the seed is).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.extLeading_transver.summary: The extended leading velocity is transverse

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.extLeading_wNorm_le.text: The norm comparison: on $[t_0,T]$, $\|V_0\|_{[n],\gamma} \le \|A_1\|_{[n],\gamma}$ (the latter the norm (D.1) of the raw leading field of Section 5 on $[t_0,T] \times \mathbb R^3 \times \mathbb R$), and the raw field has bounded jets (so its norm is a genuine finite norm).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.extLeading_wNorm_le.summary: The extended profile retains the weighted bound

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fastAdv.text:
$(f\cdot\kappa)\partial_s g$.

Default values: The expression is total as an algebraic combination of Fréchet derivatives, including their default value at nondifferentiable points. The estimates assume smooth fields and coefficients so those derivatives have the intended meaning. Empty derivative words act as the identity; empty coordinate sums or zero inputs cause no inverse operation.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fastAdv.summary: Advection through the fast phase derivative

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fastAdv_eq.text: The fast advection term as a product of the given factors.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fastAdv_eq.summary: Phase advection expressed as bilinear products

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fastAdv_eq_flip.text: The fast advection term with the factors flipped.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fastAdv_eq_flip.summary: Reordering the factors in phase advection

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fastAdv_left.text: Phase advection, weight on the advecting field.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fastAdv_left.summary: Putting the weight on the advecting phase field

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fastAdv_right.text: Phase advection, weight on the advected field (the second line of (5.39)): $\|(f\cdot\kappa)\partial_s g\|_{[n],\gamma} \le c_n (c_n N_\kappa \|f\|_{[n]}) (h^{-1} \|g\|_{[n+1],\gamma})$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fastAdv_right.summary: Putting the weight on the advected phase field

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fderiv_comp_neg'.text: The derivative of $b \mapsto f(-b)$ at $a$ is minus the derivative of $f$ at $-a$. No differentiability hypothesis on $f$ is needed for this identity.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fderiv_comp_neg'.summary: Differentiating spatial reflection with total derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fieldNormFinite_add.text: Finite norms (D.1) are closed under addition.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fieldNormFinite_add.summary: Finite derivative norms persist under addition

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fieldNormFinite_sum.text: Finite norms (D.1) are closed under finite sums.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fieldNormFinite_sum.summary: Finite sums retain finite derivative norms

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fieldNormFinite_zer.text: The zero field has finite norms.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fieldNormFinite_zer.summary: The zero profile has finite derivative norms

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fieldNorm_add_le.text: The norm (D.1) is subadditive on fields with finite norms.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fieldNorm_add_le.summary: The triangle inequality for profile norms

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fieldNorm_congr_on.text: The norm (D.1) of a field on a time set only depends on the field on that set.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fieldNorm_congr_on.summary: Identical time slices have identical derivative norms

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fieldNorm_nonneg'.text: Every norm (D.1) is nonnegative (a supremum of norms, with $0$ among the values).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fieldNorm_nonneg'.summary: Nonnegative sums of scaled derivative norms

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fieldNorm_smul_time.text: A time multiplier of modulus at most one does not increase the norm (D.1) of a field whose jets are bounded.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fieldNorm_smul_time.summary: Time multiplication preserves spatial derivative estimates

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fieldNorm_sum_le.text: The norm (D.1) of a finite sum of fields with finite norms is at most the sum of the norms.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fieldNorm_sum_le.summary: Bounding the derivative norm of a finite sum

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fieldNorm_zero.text: The zero field has norm zero.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.fieldNorm_zero.summary: The zero profile has zero derivative norm

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.final_bounds.text: Conversion of the bounds obtained from derivative words of the graph readout into the form of the statement, $C_m \Lambda^m \gamma(t) N_m$ and $C_m \Lambda^{m+1} \gamma(t) N_{m+1}$, when the word constants are at most $(\prod_{l<j} \kappa_{0,l}) \Lambda^j$ with $\Lambda \ge 1$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.final_bounds.summary: Converting derivative words to physical bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.flow_odd.text: For an odd parent, the flow map $X(t,\cdot)$ from time $0$ to time $t$ is an odd function of the label at each time.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.flow_odd.summary: The flow of an odd parent is odd

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.frequency_pow.text: Raising $\mathsf D^{C} \lambda^{3/2}$ to the integer power $j$ gives $(\mathsf D^{C} \lambda^{3/2})^{j} = \mathsf D^{Cj} \lambda^{3j/2}$, with real exponents on the right.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.frequency_pow.summary: Expand a power of the frequency factor

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.graphPoint.text:
The graph point $x \mapsto (A(x), k\cdot A(x))$ at a fixed time, with $A = X(t,\cdot)^{-1}$.

Default values: This is a total algebraic or continuous-linear construction with no division or noncanonical choice. Zero inputs have their literal algebraic values. Any geometric identification or differentiability property is supplied separately by the consuming theorem.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.graphPoint.summary: The label and phase on the physical graph

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.graphPoint_smooth.text: The graph point is smooth for a smooth inverse map.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.graphRead_eq_zero_b.text: The physical field read off the graph of a profile vanishing before $t_0$ also vanishes at every time before $t_0$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.graphRead_eq_zero_b.summary: Vanishing before activation survives graph evaluation

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.graph_from_words.text: (5.44), (5.45) at a fixed time from the word estimate. Let $A = X(t,\cdot)^{-1}$ be smooth with $G(A(x)) = D A(x)$ for the coframe $G$ at time $t$, and suppose the $\tilde d$-words of $f$ satisfy $\sum_{|w|=m} \|\tilde d_w f\|_{[0],\gamma} \le P_m \| f\|_{[m],\gamma}$ with finite norms. Then the graph $F = f(t) \circ (A, k\cdot A)$ satisfies $\sum_{|w|=m} \sup |\partial_w F| \le \gamma(t) P_m \| f\|_{[m],\gamma}$ and $\| F\|_{C^{m,1/2}} \le 3(m+1) \gamma(t) (\sum_{j\le m+1} P_j) \| f\|_{[m+1],\gamma}$ (the chain rule (3.1), $\sup |g(t)| \le \gamma(t)\| g\|_{[0],\gamma}$, and the Hölder bound by one more derivative).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.graph_from_words.summary: From coordinate words to physical Hölder norms

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.graph_norm_le_wNorm.text: Let a smooth profile $g(t,a,s)$ vanish for $t<t_0$ within $[0,T]$, and let $\gamma$ be positive continuous with $\gamma\le1$ on $[t_0,T]$. For any map $Y(t,x)$, $|g(t,Y(t,x),k_*\cdot Y(t,x))|\le\|g\|_{[0],\gamma}$ for all $t\in[0,T]$ and $x\in\mathbb R^3$. The order-zero weighted norm is the supremum of $|g|/\gamma$ over active times, labels and phases. No smoothness or invertibility of $Y$ is needed for this pointwise comparison. Lemma 5.8 uses $Y=X_{t,0}$ and $g=W_{\rm osc}$; the additional scale $\lambda^{-5/4}$ comes from the separate hierarchy estimate.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.graph_norm_le_wNorm.summary: The weighted order zero norm bounds every physical value

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.holder_of_active.text: A half-Hölder bound for the graph of a profile vanishing before $t_0$, known on $[t_0,T]$, holds on $[0,T]$.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.holder_smul.text: The half-Hölder norm is homogeneous: $\| c f\|_{C^{m,1/2}} = |c| \| f\|_{C^{m,1/2}}$.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.holder_zero.text: The zero field has every half-Hölder norm zero.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.innerCLM.text:
$(u, v) \mapsto u \cdot v$.

Default values: This is a total algebraic or continuous-linear construction with no division or noncanonical choice. Zero inputs have their literal algebraic values. Any geometric identification or differentiability property is supplied separately by the consuming theorem.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.innerCLM.summary: The scalar product as a continuous bilinear map

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.integral_centeredCe.text: The integral over the closed label cell $[-1/2,1/2]^3$ is invariant under $a \mapsto -a$. This copies a private lemma of the earlier library construction.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.integral_centeredCe.summary: Cell integration is invariant under reflection

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.isExpansion_reflFam.text: The reflected family is an expansion with the same data ($R \mapsto \varrho R$, $S \mapsto \varrho S$): every clause of the defining recursions of the Section 5 expansion is preserved by the symmetry $(a,s) \mapsto (-a,-s)$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.isExpansion_reflFam.summary: The reflected family satisfies the same hierarchy

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.iterate_words.text: Iteration of a one-step estimate $\sum_i N_n(d_i f) \le \kappa_n N_{n+1}(f)$ over all words of length $m$ : the words keep an invariant $Q$ and finite norms, and $\sum_{|w| = m} N_n(d_w f) \le (\prod_{j<m} \kappa_{n+j}) N_{n+m}(f)$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.iterate_words.summary: Iterating the estimate for one derivative

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.jets_of_bounds.text: Pointwise jet bounds $\|\nabla^m c\| \le K_m \mathsf D^{C(m+1)}$ (D.6) and the sup bounds (5.8) give uniform jets and $\ell^m \|\nabla^m c\| \le \max(K_n,0) \mathsf D^C$ for $m \le n$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.jets_of_bounds.summary: Scaled coefficient bounds from the parent estimates

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.labelAdv_vrefl.text: Label advection commutes with the velocity reflection: $(\varrho Z\cdot\mathbf d)\varrho Z' = \varrho((Z\cdot\mathbf d)Z')$ for velocity profiles $Z$, $Z'$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.labelAdv_vrefl.summary: Reflection preserves the label advection term

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.labelCoef.text:
The coefficient $G_{ji} = (G e_i)_j$ of $\partial_{a_j}$ in $\tilde d_i$.

Default values: This is a total algebraic or continuous-linear construction with no division or noncanonical choice. Zero inputs have their literal algebraic values. Any geometric identification or differentiability property is supplied separately by the consuming theorem.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.labelCoef_eq.text: Label coefficient as the evaluation of the label functional.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.labelCoef_eq.summary: Expressing the label coefficient as a linear functional

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.labelConst.text:
The constant of the label products, $c_n^2 N_G \cdot 3\ell^{-1}$.

Default values: The reciprocal $\ell^{-1}$ is defined for every real $\ell$ and equals zero at $\ell = 0$, which would invalidate its interpretation as a derivative cost. Every estimate uses $\ell > 0$ from the standing norm setting and nonnegative coefficient bounds.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.labelConst.summary: The coefficient in the label product estimate

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.labelConst_nonneg.text: Nonnegativity of the label constant from coefficient bounds.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.labelConst_nonneg.summary: The label product coefficient is nonnegative

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.labelFunctional.text:
The linear functional $A \mapsto (A e_i)_j$ on matrices, so that the label coefficient of the coframe is $G_{ji}(t,a) = (G(t,a) e_i)_j$.

Default values: This is an algebraic or continuous-linear construction defined for every input, with no division or noncanonical choice. Zero inputs have their literal algebraic values. Any geometric identification or differentiability property is supplied separately by the consuming theorem.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.labelFunctional.summary: Extracting a coframe entry as a linear functional

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.labelGrad_reflectio.text: For a pressure profile $q$ and the reflection $(t,a,s)\mapsto(t,-a,-s)$, the label gradient satisfies $\mathbf d(q \circ \text{reflection}) = \varrho\, \mathbf d q$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.labelGrad_reflectio.summary: A reflected pressure has a reflected label gradient

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.labelGrad_time_smul.text: $\mathbf d$ acts at fixed time: if $q_1(r,\cdot,\cdot) = c(r) q(r,\cdot,\cdot)$ on $[0,T]$ for a smooth $c$, then $(\mathbf d q_1)(t,a,s) = c(t) (\mathbf d q)(t,a,s)$ (the label gradient has no time derivative).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.labelGrad_time_smul.summary: Label gradients ignore a pure time factor

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.labelPartial_slices.text: The label partial of the slices of a profile.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.labelPartial_slices.summary: Label partials of a twisted profile slice

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.labelPhase_decomp.text: A label-phase increment in the coordinate directions of Appendix D.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.le_pos.text: A real number is at most its positive part.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.le_pos.summary: A constant is bounded by its positive part

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.leadingPressure_neg.text: $\mathsf p[A_1] = -p_w g P_h$ is even in $(a,s)$ on $[t_0,T]$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.leadingPressure_neg.summary: The leading pressure is even in label and phase

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.leading_neg.text: The leading velocity $A_1 = g\mathbf a F_h$ is odd in $(a,s)$ on $[t_0,T]$: reflecting both label and phase changes its sign.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.leading_neg.summary: The leading velocity is odd in label and phase

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.lemma57Const.text:
The constants $C_m$ of Lemma 5.7: $\prod_{l<m} \kappa_{0,l} + 3(m+1) \sum_{j\le m+1} \prod_{l<j} \kappa_{0,l}$.

Default values: Finite products include the empty product 1, so the order-zero case is meaningful. The formula chooses convenient nonnegative constants; it asserts no estimates unless the preceding word bounds hold.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.lemma_5_8_of_odd.text:
Assume the localized seed, finite expansion, transverse inverse, hierarchy and physical evaluation results, together with oddness of all admissible expansions. For a depth-$P\ge2$ expansion over the smooth odd divergence-free periodic parent of §5.1, with stable positive central coupling, $0<\gamma\le1$ and $C_{m step}\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, the formal statement derives the full assertions of Lemma 5.8. These are smooth periodic $V=U+W^
atural$ and $\Pi=p+\mathsf P^
atural$, odd divergence-free $V$, the exact residual $R_P^
atural+R_{\widetilde\chi}^
atural$, and the velocity and residual estimates (5.47)–(5.48). The residual bound retains $\sup_{[t_0,T]}|\widetilde\chi\,{}^{\prime}|\gamma$ alongside $\lambda^{-2P/3}$. This is a conditional assembly theorem; the separate symmetry result supplies the assumed oddness from uniqueness of the expansion. The transverse stability assumption is $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for every transverse homogeneous solution $\mathbf b$ and $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.lemma_5_8_of_odd.summary: Prove the physical bounds after reflection symmetry has been supplied

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.levelConstant_indep.text: Fix $P'\le P$ and the same numerical recurrence coefficient $K$ in both depths. The equality holds for every $q\le P'$. The numerical constant for a level is unchanged when the surrounding expansion is extended to a larger depth. The interaction pairs at the earlier levels are identical, so induction gives equality of their constants. This justifies the dependence $C_{n,p}$ in Theorem 5.6; it does not assert a bound uniform in $p$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.levelConstant_indep.summary: Extending the expansion leaves earlier level constants unchanged

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.levelPairs_indep.text: The index pairs at level $p \le P'$ do not depend on the depth $P \ge P'$, when the index shift of the pairs is at most one.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.levelPairs_indep.summary: Fixed convolution levels do not depend on the depth

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.levelPairs_le.text: The indices of a pair at level $p$, with index shift at most one, are both at most $p$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.levelPairs_le.summary: Both convolution indices precede the total level

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.levelPairs_spec.text: Index facts of the pairs $(i,j)$ at level $p$ with index shift $\delta$: $\delta + 1 \le i$, $1 \le j$, $i + j = p + \delta$. This copies a private lemma of the earlier library construction.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.levelPairs_spec.summary: Index facts for the pairs at one level

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.levelSource_vrefl.text: The level forcing $H_p$ of (5.25)–(5.26), computed for the reflected family, is the reflection of the level forcing $H_p$ of the original family.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.master_recurrence.text:
On $[0,T]	imes\mathbb T^3$, $0<T\le1$, let $U,p_U$ be smooth, $U$ odd and solenoidal, $X$ its flow, and $R_U=U_t+U\cdot
abla U+
abla p_U$ odd. Assume $\mathsf D\ge2$, Fourier radii $2\mathsf D,4\mathsf D$ for $U,R_U$, $\|
abla U\|_\infty,\|DX\|_\infty,\|DX^{-1}\|_\infty\le\mathsf D$, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. Write $M=
abla U\circ X$, $\kappa=DX^{-T}k_*$, $|\kappa(t_0,0)|=\lambda\ge1$, $0\le t_0<T$.
