At the origin, a nonzero transverse seed solves $\mathbf a_t=-(I-2P_\kappa)M\mathbf a$, with $P_\kappa=\kappa\otimes\kappa/|\kappa|^2$, $\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a|\le1$, and $\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a\ge\mathsf D^{-1}|\kappa||\mathbf a|$. Every transverse solution $\mathbf b$ of that homogeneous equation must satisfy $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$. For every depth-$P\ge2$ finite expansion, the formal implication supplies a nonnegative majorant for $\|V_1\|_{[n],\gamma}+\lambda\|\mathsf p_1\|_{[n],\gamma}$ and, for every finite derivative reserve $H$, the numerical mean, transverse, correction and product recurrence with loss $L=\mathsf D^c$ and constant $K_H\ge1$. All other entries are the actual profile norms. The same $c$ is chosen before $H,P$ and the parent. Under $L^6\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, it also gives $\|R_P\|_{[m]}\le K_{m,P}\lambda^{-5/4-2P/3}$ for every $m$. The implication assumes Propositions 5.1, 5.2 and 5.4, Lemmas 5.3 and 5.5, and Lemmas D.1 (finite-norm products) and B.1 (the Fourier cutoff lemma, including Bernstein’s inequality).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.master_recurrence.summary: Combine the analytic estimates into one level recurrence

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.material_reflection.text: The material operator $(\partial_t + M)$ of the parent commutes with the reflection $(t,a,s)\mapsto(t,-a,-s)$ of profiles, for this parent.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.material_reflection.summary: Reflection commutes with the material equation

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.material_vrefl.text: The material operator commutes with the velocity reflection: $(\partial_t + M)\varrho f = \varrho(\partial_t + M)f$ for every velocity profile $f$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.material_vrefl.summary: Velocity reflection commutes with material evolution

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.meanSolution_vrefl.text: (5.11) is preserved: if $(B, \bar q)$ solves the mean equation with source $\bar f$, then $(\varrho B, \bar q \circ \text{reflection})$ solves it with source $\varrho\bar f$ (displacement $-z(t,-a)$, velocity $-v(t,-a)$).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.meanSolution_vrefl.summary: Reflection preserves the mean evolution equation

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.meanSource_vrefl.text: $\bar f_p$ of the reflected family (with $\varrho R_U\circ X$) is the reflection of $\bar f_p$, (5.27).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.meanSource_vrefl.summary: Reflection preserves the phase averaged source

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.mean_constant_bound.text: The exponent bookkeeping of the second bound of (5.48).

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.mean_exp_split.text: Exponent splitting for the mean terms of (5.37), (5.38).

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.measuredLevels'.text:
Keeps every component of an existing numerical hierarchy except its oscillatory measurement at p = 1, which is replaced by the prescribed nonnegative function osc₁. In the proof of Theorem 5.6 this is the bound for the unswitched leading pair. It permits the cancellation of χ̃′ in the level-two relay without changing any profile or any higher-level measurement.

Only the oscillatory numerical component at index 1 is overwritten. The supplied h₁ proves its nonnegativity. No physical field is changed, and comparison with the original measurements requires the separate domination hypothesis.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.measuredLevels'.summary: Replacing the first oscillatory bound by the unswitched bound

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.measuredLevels'_osc.text: Oscillation bound for the reindexed measured levels.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.measuredLevels'_osc.summary: The unswitched bound dominates the measured first level

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.measuredLevels'_osc.text: Oscillation of the reindexed measured levels away from the distinguished index.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.measuredLevels'_osc.summary: Higher oscillatory bounds survive the first level replacement

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.measuredOf.text:
Builds the nonnegative numerical measurements of an actual finite expansion: weighted norms for oscillatory sources, velocities, pressures and completions, and unweighted norms for mean fields and their sources. The pressure contribution is scaled by $\lambda$. The standing norm data ($T,\ell_*,h>0$, $0\le t_0\le T$, $\gamma$ continuous with $0<\gamma\le1$ on $[t_0,T]$) supply the positivity and finiteness facts needed to use these quantities as seminorm measurements.

The measured data are built from norms of actual profiles, with the standing norm data certifying positive parameters and finite seminorms. The pressure factor $\lambda$ is used in the theorem only for $\lambda\ge1$. Exterior velocity indices come from the separate truncation convention.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.measuredOf.summary: Measuring each source and velocity in its natural norm

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.mixedDirection_cons.text: The mixed directions of (D.1) are constant.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.mixedDirection_cons.summary: The scaled derivative directions are constant

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.mixedDirection_smoo.text: The weighted directions of (D.1) are constant, hence smooth.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.mixedDirection_smoo.summary: The scaled coordinate directions are smooth

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.neg_mem_centeredCel.text: If a label $a$ lies in the closed cell $[-1/2,1/2]^3$, then $-a$ also lies in that cell.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.neg_mem_centeredCel.summary: The label cell is closed under negation

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.neg_preimage_center.text: The closed label cell $[-1/2,1/2]^3$ is symmetric: its preimage under $a\mapsto -a$ is itself. This copies a private lemma of the earlier library construction.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.neg_preimage_center.summary: The label cell is symmetric under negation

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.normRecurrence'.text: Packages the seed estimate, bounds for the mean and oscillatory sources, the mean and transverse solves, completion, and the level-one triangle inequality into the hierarchy norm recurrence used in the proof of Theorem 5.6. Its first oscillatory measurement is the auxiliary unswitched bound, while all other measured components are unchanged. The subsequent abstract induction is therefore applicable to the actual expansion after comparing that one measurement.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.normRecurrence'.summary: From individual term bounds to the hierarchy recurrence

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.normSetting_of.summary: The standing hypotheses supply positive norm parameters

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.norm_apply_coordina.text: The coordinate functional has norm at most one.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.norm_apply_coordina.summary: A coordinate of a vector respects its norm

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.norm_innerCLM_le.text: The inner product map has norm at most one.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.norm_innerCLM_le.summary: The scalar product has bilinear norm at most one

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.norm_iteratedFDeriv.text: The Fréchet jet of order $m$ of a smooth field on $\mathbb R^3$ is at most the sum of its ordered coordinate derivative words.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.norm_iteratedFDeriv.summary: Derivative words control the full Fréchet derivative

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.norm_labelFunctiona.text: The label functional has norm at most one.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.norm_labelFunctiona.summary: The coframe coordinate functional is contractive

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.norm_labelWord_le.text: A weighted label word of a smooth phase-independent field is at most $r^{|w|}$ times the Fréchet jet of the same order.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.norm_labelWord_le.summary: Scaled label words are bounded by Fréchet jets

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.norm_le_norm_sub_la.text: A label in the closed cell is at least as close to the origin as any of its lattice translates.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.norm_le_norm_sub_la.summary: The centered cell minimizes distance to the origin

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.norm_le_sum_coordin.text: The operator norm of a multilinear map on $\mathbb R^3$ is at most the sum of the norms of its values on the coordinate words. This is adapted from a private lemma of the earlier library construction, with a sum in place of a uniform bound.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.norm_le_sum_coordin.summary: Coordinate components control a multilinear operator norm

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.norm_le_weight_mul_.text: The supremum of a field at a fixed time is at most the weight times its weighted norm of order zero: $\sup |f(t)| \le \gamma(t) \| f\|_{[0],\gamma}$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.norm_le_weight_mul_.summary: Recovering pointwise amplitudes from a weighted norm

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.norm_phaseFunctiona.text: The phase functional has norm at most the norm of the wavevector.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.norm_phaseFunctiona.summary: The phase coefficient is bounded by the carrier

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.norm_rowCLM_le.text: The row functional has norm at most one.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.norm_smulCLM_flip_l.text: The flipped scalar multiplication map has norm at most one.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.norm_smulCLM_flip_l.summary: Reversing scalar multiplication retains its norm bound

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.norm_smulCLM_le.text: The scalar multiplication map has norm at most one.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.norm_smulCLM_le.summary: Scalar multiplication has bilinear norm at most one

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.oddExpansions_of.text: Assume Proposition 5.4, including uniqueness of the retained profiles. Over the smooth odd periodic parent of §5.1, take a seed with even dependence on the label and an admissible depth-$P\ge2$ expansion. Reflect $(a,s)$ to $(-a,-s)$, reverse the sign of velocity profiles and preserve the sign of pressure profiles. The reflected family satisfies the same defining equations and prescribed data. Uniqueness therefore makes the retained velocity expansion odd under this reflection. After composition with the odd inverse parent flow, its Eulerian perturbation is odd. This statement proves symmetry of the expansion; it does not derive its quantitative estimates or bound its residual.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.oddExpansions_of.summary: Reflect the finite expansion and use uniqueness of its retained levels

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.opWord.text:
The word $d_{w_1} \cdots d_{w_m} f$ of a family of operators (first letter outermost).

Default values: A finite fold of a supplied family of operators. The empty word is the identity on the input field. The definition itself asserts no linearity, smoothness or differential interpretation of those operators; the iteration theorem supplies the required invariant and seminorm estimates.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.opWord.summary: An ordered succession of differential operators

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.opWord_cons.text: Unfolding an ordered derivative word with one more leading letter.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.ops_labelGrad_eval.text: The label gradient on the slab: $(\mathbf d q)(x) = \sum_i \partial q(x)(0, (D_aX)^{-1} e_i, 0) e_i$.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.oscForcing_gen.text: The oscillatory source bound: the source of level $p$ is the centered sum of the linear term, the label products and the completion phase products, plus the mean phase products, with a bound $K L R$ for the linear term. This is adapted from the corresponding assembly step of the earlier library construction, where $R$ is fixed to the inverse frequency times the sum of the oscillatory bound and the oscillatory source bound at level $p - 1$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.oscForcing_gen.summary: Assembling the centered oscillatory source estimate

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.oscSource_vrefl.text: The centered oscillatory source $f_p$ of (5.27), computed for the reflected family, is the reflection of $f_p$ for the original family.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.oscSource_vrefl.summary: Reflection preserves the centered oscillatory source

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.osc_constant_bound.text: The exponent bookkeeping of the first bound of (5.48).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.osc_constant_bound.summary: The powers in the oscillatory physical bound

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.osc_exp_split.text: Exponent splitting for the oscillatory terms of (5.37), (5.38).

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.p1_eq_smul.text: For a pressure profile $q$ equal to the leading pressure on the active cell, the first pressure satisfies $\mathsf p_1 = \tilde\chi q$ on the slab, as for the first velocity.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.p1_eq_smul.summary: The first pressure is the switched leading pressure

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.p1_phaseMean.text: $\mathsf p_1 = \tilde\chi\mathsf p[A_1]$ has zero phase mean ($P_h$ has zero mean).

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.pairs_mem.text: The indices of the pairs entering the sources are levels of the expansion.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.pairs_mem.summary: Hierarchy convolutions stay inside the finite index set

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.parity_of_even.text: A profile that is even under the reflection used in the parity argument has parity $1$ when profiles are split into reflection-even and reflection-odd parts.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.parity_of_even.summary: Even profiles have positive reflection parity

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.parity_of_odd.text: A profile that is odd under the reflection used in the parity argument has parity $-1$ when profiles are split into reflection-even and reflection-odd parts.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.parity_of_odd.summary: Odd profiles have negative reflection parity

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.phaseAdv_vrefl.text: Phase advection commutes with the velocity reflection: $(\varrho Z\cdot\kappa)\partial_s\varrho Y = \varrho((Z\cdot\kappa)\partial_sY)$ for profiles $Z$ and $Y$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.phaseAdv_vrefl.summary: Reflection preserves the phase advection term

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.phaseCoef.text:
The coefficient $\sum_j G_{ji} k_j = k \cdot G e_i$ of $\partial_s$ in $\tilde d_i$.

Default values: This is a total algebraic or continuous-linear construction with no division or noncanonical choice. Zero inputs have their literal algebraic values. Any geometric identification or differentiability property is supplied separately by the consuming theorem.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.phaseCoef_eq.text: Phase coefficient as the evaluation of the phase functional.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.phaseCoef_eq.summary: Expressing the phase coefficient as a linear functional

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.phaseConst.text:
The constant of the phase products, $c_n^2 N_\kappa h^{-1}$.

Default values: The reciprocal $h^{-1}$ is defined for every real $h$ and equals zero at $h = 0$. All phase derivative estimates require $h > 0$, and the nonnegativity lemma obtains the coefficient sign from the coefficient bounds for $(D_aX)^{-1}$ and $\kappa$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.phaseConst.summary: The coefficient in the phase product estimate

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.phaseConst_nonneg.text: Nonnegativity of the phase constant from coefficient bounds.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.phaseConst_nonneg.summary: The phase product coefficient is nonnegative

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.phaseDrop.text:
The projection $(a, s) \mapsto (a, 0)$ of label and phase to the label with zero phase.

Default values: A linear projection, defined everywhere, setting the phase to zero. It loses phase information; only the fact that a phase-independent field equals its composition with this projection justifies the replacement.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.phaseFunctional.text:
The linear functional $A \mapsto k \cdot A e_i$ on matrices, so that the phase coefficient of the coframe and carrier is $k \cdot G(t,a) e_i$.

Default values: This is an algebraic or continuous-linear construction defined for every input, with no division or noncanonical choice. Zero inputs have their literal algebraic values. Any geometric identification or differentiability property is supplied separately by the consuming theorem.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.phaseFunctional.summary: Pairing the carrier with a coframe column

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.phaseGrad_reflectio.text: For a pressure profile $q$ and the reflection $(t,a,s)\mapsto(t,-a,-s)$, the phase gradient satisfies $\kappa\partial_s(q \circ \text{reflection}) = \varrho\, \kappa\partial_s q$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.phaseGrad_reflectio.summary: A reflected pressure has a reflected phase gradient

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.phaseMean_comp_neg.text: The phase mean of a $1$-periodic function is invariant under $s \mapsto -s$, for values in any normed space. This copies a private lemma of the earlier library construction.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.phaseMean_comp_neg.summary: The periodic phase mean is reflection invariant

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.phasePartial_slices.text: The phase partial of the slices of a profile.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.phasePartial_slices.summary: Phase partials of a twisted profile slice

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.plain.text:
The unweighted finite profile norm $\|f\|_{[n]}$ on $[t_0,T]$.

Default values: This is a real-valued derivative norm on the active interval, with the same convention for real suprema as the Section 5 field norm. Theorems invoking it provide profile smoothness, positive scales and the compact valid time interval to ensure genuine finiteness.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.plain.summary: Unweighted profile norms on the active time interval

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.plain_le_uNorm.text: The unweighted norm on $[t_0,T]$ is at most the one on $[0,T]$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.plain_le_uNorm.summary: The full slab norm bounds the active norm

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.plain_le_wNorm.text: The unweighted norm on $[t_0,T]$ is at most the weighted norm when $0 < \gamma \le 1$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.plain_le_wNorm.summary: Weights bounded by one dominate the active norm

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.pos.text:
The positive part $\max(x,0)$ of a real number $x$, used to make chosen constants nonnegative.

Default values: The maximum with zero is defined for every real number. It changes a negative input to zero; estimates using it remain justified by $x \le \max(x,0)$, not by an assumption that the original constant was positive.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.prod_le.text: (D.4) of Lemma D.1 for a bilinear map of norm at most one, with the weight on the second factor.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.prod_le.summary: Weighted products of scaled derivative norms

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.prod_le_one.text: The product estimate (D.4) of the assumed Lemma D.1 without weight ($\gamma \equiv 1$), for a bilinear map of norm at most one and fields of finite norm.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.prod_le_one.summary: Unweighted products of scaled derivative norms

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.productConst.text:
The constant of (D.4) in Lemma D.1 for a bilinear map of norm at most one, $\#W_n \cdot 2^n \cdot 2$, where $\#W_n$ is the number of admissible words of order at most $n$.

Default values: The definition uses finite word counts and ordinary real arithmetic. Maxima or absolute values, where present, ensure the chosen majorants remain nonnegative; the formula itself is not a proof that an arbitrary input constant bounds a field. The analytic estimates provide the corresponding coefficient or level bounds.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.productConst.summary: The product constant for scaled derivative words

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.productConst_nonneg.summary: Nonnegative constants in the product estimate

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.profile_sum_eval.text: A finite sum of twisted profiles is evaluated pointwise.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.ptpc_eq_zero_off_su.text: The twisted extension of a field with the envelope factor vanishes at labels outside $\operatorname{supp} g$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.ptpc_eq_zero_off_su.summary: Twisted extension preserves the envelope support

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.ptpc_smul_time.text: Pulling a time factor out of the twisted extension.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.ptpc_smul_time.summary: Time factors pass through twisted extension

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.rawLeading.text:
The raw leading field $g(a) F_h(s) \mathbf a(t,a)$ for a field $\mathbf a$ on all times.

Default values: This product is defined for every real scale and seed field. Smoothness, envelope support and the intended wave normalization are used only with positive phase width and a smooth seed; the later constructors impose these conditions.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.rawLeading_eq_leadi.text: The raw leading term agrees with the leading term of Lemma 5.8.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.reflFamily.text:
The reflected family: $\varrho V_p$, $\varrho C_p$, $\varrho B_p$, $\mathsf p_p \circ \text{reflection}$, $\bar q_p \circ \text{reflection}$.

Default values: Every component is transformed algebraically at every natural index, including zero. Velocity, mean and completion components are negated after reflection; pressure components are only reflected. Validity as an expansion is a separate theorem.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.reflFamily.summary: The reflected family of an expansion

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.reflFamily_B.text: Unfolding the reflected family gives its mean velocity $B_p$ as the negated reflection of the original mean velocity. This is a definitional identity used in checking the reflected mean equation.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.reflFamily_V.text: The $V$ component of the reflected family at each level is the velocity reflection $\varrho V_p$ of the original component.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.reflFamily_p.text: Unfolding the reflected family gives its oscillatory pressure as the ordinary reflection of the original pressure, with no velocity sign. This sign convention makes its gradient transform as a velocity.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.reflFamily_q.text: Unfolding the reflected family gives its mean pressure as the ordinary reflection of the original mean pressure. The mean velocity receives the minus sign separately.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.reflection_of_parit.text: The reflection of a profile of parity $\sigma$ is $\sigma$ times the profile.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.reflection_split.text: Splitting. An additive map $M$ that agrees with $L$ on reflection-even profiles and with $-L$ on reflection-odd profiles is $L \circ \text{reflection}$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.reflection_split.summary: Recovering reflection from the even and odd parts

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.relay_two_eq.text: At level two the differentiated switch in the material derivative of C[V₁] cancels the correction of the activation source S. What remains is χ̃ times the completion/pressure relay for the unswitched leading pair. This identity is why the numerical recurrence uses an unswitched level-one bound instead of estimating χ̃′ separately.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.relay_two_eq.summary: The activation derivative cancels in the second relay

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.relay_vanish_before.text: The linear term vanishes before $t_0$: if $C$ and $p$ vanish at all times $< t_0$, so does $(\partial_t+M)C + \mathbf d p$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.relay_vanish_before.summary: The linear relay vanishes before activation

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.residual_uNorm.text: The pulled-back residual satisfies $\|R_U\circ X\|_{[n]} \le K_n \lambda^{-5/2}$ when $\ell_* \le \mathsf D^{-C}$, from the assumed Bernstein inequality (B.1) and the bound (5.7) of the assumed Proposition 5.1.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.residual_uNorm.summary: The pulled back parent residual in profile norms

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.rowCLM.text:
$(M, v) \mapsto (M v)_j$.

Default values: This is a total algebraic or continuous-linear construction with no division or noncanonical choice. Zero inputs have their literal algebraic values. Any geometric identification or differentiability property is supplied separately by the consuming theorem.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.rowCLM_apply.text: Action of the row functional on a vector.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.rpow_three_halves.text: For the frequency $\lambda$, the real power splits as $\lambda^{3/2} = \lambda \cdot \lambda^{1/2}$, used when converting derivative counts into powers of $\lambda$.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.seed_even.text: The seed is even in the label: $\mathbf a(t,-a) = \mathbf a(t,a)$ on $[t_0,T]$, since $\mathbf a(t,-a)$ solves (3.2) with (5.4) (the coefficients $M$, $\kappa$ are even) and the seed is unique.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.seed_even.summary: Uniqueness makes the seed even in the label

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.seminorm_finset_le.text: A seminorm of a finite sum is at most the sum of the seminorms of its terms. This copies a private lemma of the earlier library construction.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.seminorm_finset_le.summary: A seminorm bounds a finite sum by its terms

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slab_fderiv_slice.text: The derivative within the slab in a direction without time component is the derivative of the time slice.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slab_fderiv_slice.summary: Spatial directions ignore the boundary of the time slab

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slice_contDiff.text: A function jointly smooth on $[0,T] \times \mathbb R^3$ is smooth in space at each time of $[0,T]$.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slice_fderiv_label.text: The derivative of a slice in a label direction.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slice_fderiv_label.summary: Label derivatives agree with derivatives of slices

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slices_average.text: The phase average as a field.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slices_average.summary: Phase averaging commutes with taking time slices

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slices_divProduct.text: The divergence product $(\mathbf d\cdot V)Y$ written as a field on the time slices of the profiles, for use in the finite norm estimates.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slices_divProduct.summary: The divergence product written on profile slices

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slices_labelAdv.text: The label advection as a field: $(f\cdot\mathbf d)g = \sum_j ((D_aX)^{-1} f)_j \partial_{a_j} g$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slices_labelAdv.summary: Label advection written as a field product

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slices_mono.text: The unweighted norm on a smaller time set is smaller.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slices_mono.summary: Restricting the time interval reduces the norm

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slices_phaseAdv.text: The phase advection $(f\cdot\kappa)\partial_s g$ written as a field on the time slices of the profiles, for use in the finite norm estimates.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slices_phaseAdv.summary: Phase advection written as a field product

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slices_phasePeriodi.text: The slices of a twisted profile, taken at the times of a time set, are $1$-periodic in the phase at every label.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slices_phasePeriodi.summary: Profile slices are periodic in the phase

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slowAdv.text:
$(f\cdot\mathbf d)g = \sum_j (G f)_j \partial_{a_j} g$ for the coframe $G$.

Default values: The expression is total as an algebraic combination of Fréchet derivatives, including their default value at nondifferentiable points. The estimates assume smooth fields and coefficients so those derivatives have the intended meaning. Empty derivative words act as the identity; empty coordinate sums or zero inputs cause no inverse operation.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slowAdv_eq.text: The slow advection term as a product of the given factors.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slowAdv_eq.summary: Label advection expressed as bilinear products

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slowAdv_eq_flip.text: The slow advection term with the factors flipped.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slowAdv_eq_flip.summary: Reordering the factors in label advection

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slowAdv_left.text: Label advection with the weight on the advecting field: the first line of (5.39), with the weight placed on the advecting profile $Z$ rather than on the advected one.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slowAdv_left.summary: Putting the weight on the advecting label field

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slowAdv_right.text: Label advection, weight on the advected field (the first line of (5.39)): $\|(f\cdot\mathbf d)g\|_{[n],\gamma} \le c_n (c_n N_G \|f\|_{[n]}) (3\ell^{-1} \|g\|_{[n+1],\gamma})$, by (D.4) for the coefficient $(G f)_j$ and for its product with $\partial_{a_j} g$, and (D.3) for $\sum_j \|\partial_{a_j} g\|$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slowAdv_right.summary: Putting the weight on the advected label field

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slowDiv.text:
$\mathbf d\cdot V = \sum_i (G \partial_{a_i} V)_i$.

Default values: The expression is total as an algebraic combination of Fréchet derivatives, including their default value at nondifferentiable points. The estimates assume smooth fields and coefficients so those derivatives have the intended meaning. Empty derivative words act as the identity; empty coordinate sums or zero inputs cause no inverse operation.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slowDiv_eq.text: The slow divergence term as a product of the given factors.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slowDiv_eq.summary: Label divergence expressed through coframe rows

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slowDiv_le.text: The label divergence: $\|\mathbf d\cdot V\|_{[n],\gamma} \le c_n N_G 3\ell^{-1} \| V\|_{[n+1],\gamma}$.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.slowDiv_le_one.summary: Unweighted control of the label divergence

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.smooth_of_weighted.text: A field whose weighted field is smooth is smooth (the weight is a nonzero constant at each time).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.smooth_of_weighted.summary: A positive time weight preserves spatial smoothness

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.smulCLM.text:
$(r, v) \mapsto r v$.

Default values: This is a total algebraic or continuous-linear construction with no division or noncanonical choice. Zero inputs have their literal algebraic values. Any geometric identification or differentiability property is supplied separately by the consuming theorem.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.smulCLM.summary: Scalar multiplication as a continuous bilinear map

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.spatialDerivativeWo.text: The spatial chain rule (3.1), iterated: with $A = X(t,\cdot)^{-1}$ and the coframe $G$ with $G(A(x)) = D A(x)$, every Eulerian derivative word of the graph $g \circ (A, k\cdot A)$ is the graph of the $\tilde d$-word of $g$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.spatialDerivativeWo.summary: Repeated chain rule along the physical graph

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.spatialHolderHalfNo.summary: Nonnegative norms for physical Hölder estimates

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.strainField_neg.text: For an odd parent, the label strain $M(t,\cdot)$ is an even function of the label at each time.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.strainField_neg.summary: The strain of an odd parent is even

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.sum_coordinate.text: A vector is the sum of its coordinates times the coordinate directions.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.sum_coordinate.summary: Expanding a vector in coordinate directions

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.suppSource_vrefl.text: The supplementary mean source $f_p^S$ of (5.28), computed for the reflected family, is the reflection of $f_p^S$ for the original family.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.suppSource_vrefl.summary: Reflection preserves the supplementary mean source

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.term_BB.text: For any two profiles $B,B'$, assuming Lemma D.1 and the coefficient bounds of the parent, the label product satisfies $\|(B\cdot\mathbf d)B'\|_{[n]}\le\Lambda_n\|B\|_{[n+1]}\|B'\|_{[n+1]}$, where $\Lambda_n$ is the label-product constant of order $n$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.term_BB.summary: Bounding the product of two mean velocities

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.term_YY.text: For profiles $f,g$ vanishing before $t_0$, the phase average of their label product satisfies $\|\langle(f\cdot\mathbf d)g\rangle\|_{[n]}\le\Lambda_n\|f\|_{[n+1],\gamma}\|g\|_{[n+1],\gamma}$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.term_YY.summary: Bounding the averaged oscillatory label product

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.term_divY.text: For profiles $V,Y$ vanishing before $t_0$, the phase average of the label divergence product satisfies $\|\langle(\mathbf d\cdot V)Y\rangle\|_{[n]}\le\Lambda_n\|V\|_{[n+1],\gamma}\|Y\|_{[n+1],\gamma}$.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.term_fastB.text: The mean phase product: for profiles $B,Y$, $\|(B\cdot\kappa)\partial_sY\|_{[n],\gamma}\le\Lambda'_n\|B\|_{[n]}\|Y\|_{[n+1],\gamma}$, with $\Lambda'_n$ the phase-product constant of order $n$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.term_fastB.summary: Bounding the mean against an oscillatory phase derivative

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.term_fastC.text: The centered completion phase product: for any two profiles $C$ and $Y$, assuming Lemma D.1 and the coefficient bounds of the parent, $\|(C\cdot\kappa)\partial_sY-\langle(C\cdot\kappa)\partial_sY\rangle\|_{[n],\gamma}\le2\Lambda'_n\|C\|_{[n],\gamma}\|Y\|_{[n+1],\gamma}$, with $\Lambda'_n$ the phase-product constant of order $n$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.term_fastC.summary: Bounding the centered completion phase product

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.term_fastU.text: $\|(f\cdot\kappa)\partial_s g\|_{[n]} \le \Lambda'_n \| f\|_{[n]} \| g\|_{[n+1]}$ on $[0,T]$, $\Lambda'_n = c_n^2 N_\kappa h^{-1}$.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.term_slow.text: The centered label product of $Z=Y+B$ and $Z'=Y'+B'$ (with $Y,Y'$ vanishing before $t_0$ and $B,B'$ phase independent): $\|(Z\cdot\mathbf d)Z'-\langle(Z\cdot\mathbf d)Z'\rangle\|_{[n],\gamma}\le2\Lambda_n(\|Y\|_\gamma+\|B\|)(\|Y'\|_\gamma+\|B'\|)$, the norms on the right taken at order $n+1$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.term_slow.summary: Centering removes the product of two means

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.tildeDirection.text:
The direction field of $\tilde d_i = \sum_j G_{ji}(\partial_{a_j} + k_j \partial_s)$ at a fixed time: $(a, s) \mapsto (G(a) e_i, k \cdot G(a) e_i)$. For $G = (D_aX)^{-1}$ this is $\tilde d = (D_aX)^{-T}(\nabla_a + k_*\partial_s)$ of.

Default values: A total algebraic direction built from a supplied coframe G and carrier k, without taking an inverse or derivative. If G is not the inverse flow deformation, the direction remains defined but need not represent an Eulerian derivative; the graph chain rule requires that geometric identification.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.tildeDirection.summary: The physical derivative in label and phase variables

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.tildeDirection_smoo.text: The direction fields of $\tilde d$ are smooth for a smooth coframe.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.tildeDirection_smoo.summary: Smooth coefficients give smooth physical derivative directions

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.tildeWord.text:
The $\tilde d$-word $\tilde d_{w_1} \cdots \tilde d_{w_m} f$ of a field, time by time (the first letter is the outermost derivative).

Default values: The expression is total as an algebraic combination of Fréchet derivatives, including their default value at nondifferentiable points. The estimates assume smooth fields and coefficients so those derivatives have the intended meaning. Empty derivative words act as the identity; empty coordinate sums or zero inputs cause no inverse operation.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.tildeWord.summary: Ordered physical derivatives of a profile

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.tildeWord_cons.text: One letter of a $\tilde d$-word applied to a word is the word with one more letter.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.tildeWord_cons_eq.text: $\tilde d_i g = \sum_j G_{ji} \partial_{a_j} g + (k\cdot G e_i) \partial_s g$: one letter of a $\tilde d$-word is a sum of products of phase-independent coefficients with the label and phase derivatives of Lemma D.1.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.tildeWord_cons_eq.summary: One physical derivative splits into label and phase terms

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.tildeWord_eq_opWord.text: The $\tilde d$-words are the operator words of the one-letter $\tilde d$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.tildeWord_eq_opWord.summary: Physical derivative words as operator compositions

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.tilde_step.text: One letter of $\tilde d$, by Lemma D.1. For a coframe $G$ and a carrier $k$, whose coefficients $G_{ji}$ and $k\cdot G e_i$ (fields independent of the phase) have finite norms (D.1) bounded by $N_c$ and $N_k$, and a field $f$ with $\|f\|_{[n+1],\gamma}$ finite: $\tilde d_i f$ has a finite weighted norm and $\sum_i \|\tilde d_i f\|_{[n],\gamma} \le c_n (3 N_c (3\ell^{-1} \|f\|_{[n+1],\gamma}) + 3 N_k \|\partial_s f\|_{[n],\gamma})$. The proof assumes Lemma D.1 and uses (D.4) for each of the four products in the expansion $\tilde d_i f=\sum_j G_{ji}\partial_{a_j}f+(k\cdot Ge_i)\partial_sf$, and (D.3) for $\sum_j \|\partial_{a_j} f\|_{[n],\gamma} \le 3\ell^{-1}\|f\|_{[n+1],\gamma}$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.tilde_step.summary: Bounding one physical derivative of a profile

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.tilde_step_general.text: The one-step estimate for a general field: $\sum_i \|\tilde d_i f\|_{[n],\gamma} \le c_n (9 N_c \ell^{-1} + 3 N_k h^{-1}) \|f\|_{[n+1],\gamma}$. It assumes Lemma D.1, through the one-letter estimate, and uses the phase bound $\|\partial_s f\|_{[n],\gamma} \le h^{-1}\|f\|_{[n+1],\gamma}$ of (D.3).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.tilde_step_general.summary: The full phase cost of one physical derivative

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.tilde_step_phaseInd.text: The one-step estimate for a phase-independent field: $\tilde d_i f$ is again phase independent, and $\sum_i \|\tilde d_i f\|_{[n],\gamma} \le 9 c_n N_c \ell^{-1} \|f\|_{[n+1],\gamma}$, since $\partial_s f = 0$. It assumes Lemma D.1, through the one-letter estimate.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.tilde_step_phaseInd.summary: Phase independent fields avoid the fast derivative cost

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.transverseSolution_.text: (5.15) is preserved: if $(V, \mathsf p)$ solves the transverse equation from zero with source $f$, then $(\varrho V, \mathsf p \circ \text{reflection})$ solves it with source $\varrho f$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.transverseSolution_.summary: Reflection preserves the transverse evolution equation

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.transverse_average_.text: A solution of the transverse equation (5.15) has a source of zero phase mean: $f = (\partial_t+M)V + \kappa\partial_s\mathsf p$ with $\langle V\rangle = 0$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.transverse_average_.summary: The transverse equation forces zero source average

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.truncate.text:
The levels of $u$ restricted to $1\le i\le P$ ($C_i$ for $i \le P$), zero elsewhere.

Default values: The natural-index condition sets $V$ and $B$ to zero outside $1 \le p \le P$, and $C$ to zero outside $p \le P$. It leaves both pressure families untouched. No estimate for these exterior pressures follows from the definition; later tail arguments use only the truncated velocity components.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.truncate.summary: Extending the finite velocity hierarchy by zero

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.twisted_jets.text: Jets of a twisted profile versus jets of a raw field at one time: every jet of one is a jet of the other or zero.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.twisted_jets.summary: Twisted extension preserves local derivative bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.twisted_wNorm_le.text: Norm of a twisted profile versus the raw field: on $[t_0,T]$, $\|V_0\|_{[n],\gamma}\le\|F\|_{[n],\gamma}$, the latter being the norm (D.1) of the raw field on $[t_0,T]\times\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.twisted_wNorm_le.summary: Twisted extension preserves weighted leading norms

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.uNorm_average.text: The bound (D.5): on $[0,T]$, the phase average does not increase the unweighted norm, $\|\langle f\rangle\|_{[n]} \le \| f\|_{[n]}$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.uNorm_average.summary: Phase averaging does not increase the unweighted norm

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.uNorm_divProduct.summary: An unweighted bound for the divergence product

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.uNorm_labelAdv.text: The estimate (5.39) for the label advection term, without weight, in the unweighted norm on the full interval $[0,T]$.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.uNorm_le_plain.text: For a field vanishing before $t_0$, the unweighted norm on $[0,T]$ is the one on $[t_0,T]$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.uNorm_le_plain.summary: Vanishing before activation reduces the full slab norm

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.uNorm_le_wNorm.text: The profile is smooth and phase periodic, with the coupled label-translation law; the weight is continuous on the compact active interval. For a profile vanishing before $t_0$, its unweighted norm on $[0,T]$ is at most its weighted norm on $[t_0,T]$ when $0<\gamma\le1$. The vanishing assumption matters because the time intervals differ. The remainder proof applies this to terms containing oscillations; products of two means are estimated directly in the unweighted norm.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.uNorm_le_wNorm.summary: Preactivation vanishing extends control to the whole interval

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.uNorm_phaseAdv.text: The second line of (5.39), in the unweighted norm on $[0,T]$: $\|(f\cdot\kappa)\partial_s g\|_{[n]} \le c_n (c_n N_\kappa \|f\|_{[n]}) (h^{-1} \|g\|_{[n+1]})$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.uNorm_phaseAdv.summary: Unweighted control of the phase advection term

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.vrefl.text:
The symmetry of the construction on velocity profiles: $\varrho f(t,a,s) = -f(t,-a,-s)$.

Default values: Reflection and negation are algebraic operations on already smooth twisted profiles. No reciprocal, partial inverse or arbitrary choice is introduced; pressures use ordinary reflection, without the minus sign, in the reflected family.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.vrefl.summary: Reflection of velocity profiles with a minus sign

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.vrefl_apply.text: Unfolding of the velocity reflection $\varrho$, the negated reflection $\varrho f(t,a,s) = -f(t,-a,-s)$, into its defining formula.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.vrefl_eval.text: Evaluation formula for the velocity reflection: at time $t$, label $a$ and phase $s$, $(\varrho f)(t,a,s) = -f(t,-a,-s)$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.vrefl_eval.summary: Evaluating velocity reflection at a label and phase

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.vrefl_vrefl.text: The velocity reflection $\varrho f(t,a,s) = -f(t,-a,-s)$ is an involution: applying it twice gives back $f$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.vrefl_vrefl.summary: Reflecting the velocity twice changes nothing

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wNorm_center.text: The bound (D.5) for centering: $\| f - \langle f\rangle\|_{[n],\gamma} \le 2 \| f\|_{[n],\gamma}$, with the phase average $\langle f\rangle$ subtracted.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wNorm_center.summary: Centering at most doubles the weighted norm

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wNorm_labelAdv_left.text: (5.39) for the label advection with the weight on the advecting field.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wNorm_labelAdv_left.summary: Weighted label advection of the first factor

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wNorm_labelAdv_righ.text: $\|(f\cdot\mathbf d)g\|_{[n],\gamma} \le c_n (c_n N_G \| f\|_{[n]}) (3\ell^{-1} \| g\|_{[n+1],\gamma})$, (5.39) with the weight on the advected field.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wNorm_labelAdv_righ.summary: Weighted label advection of the second factor

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wNorm_phaseAdv_left.text: (5.39), second line, with the weight on the advecting field.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wNorm_phaseAdv_left.summary: Weighted phase advection of the first factor

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wNorm_phaseAdv_righ.text: Phase advection with the weight on the advected field: $\|(f\cdot\kappa)\partial_s g\|_{[n],\gamma} \le c_n (c_n N_\kappa \|f\|_{[n]}) (h^{-1} \|g\|_{[n+1],\gamma})$, the second line of (5.39).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wNorm_phaseAdv_righ.summary: Weighted phase advection of the second factor

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wNorm_smul_time_le.text: A time multiplier of modulus at most one does not increase the weighted norm: if $F = c G$ on $[t_0,T]$ and $|c| \le 1$ there, then $\| F\|_{[n],\gamma} \le \| G\|_{[n],\gamma}$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wNorm_smul_time_le.summary: A bounded time factor preserves the weighted estimate

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.waveC.text:
The wave vector $\kappa(t,a)$ on a time set.

Default values: The wave vector is defined from the supplied flow derivative for every input. The parent-flow hypotheses are what identify it with the transported nonzero covector; the definition alone does not establish those geometric facts.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.waveC.summary: The transported wave vector as a coefficient field

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wavePotential_smul_.text: For any fixed wave vector $K$, scalar $c$ and phase profile $V$, the wave potential of $cV$ equals $c$ times the wave potential of $V$. Linearity of the cross product and phase primitive proves the identity, even at $K = 0$, where the reciprocal is assigned the value zero. The consuming completion estimate works at each fixed time.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wavePotential_smul_.summary: Time multiplication commutes with the wave potential

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wavePotential_zero.text: The wave potential of the zero profile vanishes.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.waveVector_neg.text: For an odd parent, the transported covector $\kappa(t,\cdot)$ is an even function of the label at each time.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.waveVector_neg.summary: The transported covector of an odd parent is even

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.weighted_add.text: The time weight distributes over sums of fields.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.weighted_sum.text: The time weight distributes over finite sums of fields.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.weighted_zero.text: The time weight of the zero field is zero.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.width_inv.text: For the profile width $h = \lambda^{-1/2}$, its reciprocal is $h^{-1} = \lambda^{1/2}$, so each phase derivative costs a factor $\lambda^{1/2}$.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wordConst.text:
The one-step constant $\kappa_{0,n} = 12 c_n \#W_n \max(K_n, 0)$ of the proof of Lemma 5.7, for the constants $K_n$ of (5.8) in Proposition 5.1.

Default values: Finite sums, products and max are total. The max clips any supplied negative coefficient constant to zero; analytic use still requires that it bounds the coefficient jets. The order-zero word set is nonempty.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wordConst_nonneg.text: The word constant of Lemma 5.7 is nonnegative.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wordNorm_le_of_valu.text: A word norm is at most another one when every value of the first is dominated by a value of the second.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wordNorm_le_of_valu.summary: Dominating every derivative value bounds the word norm

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.word_add.text: Derivative words are additive on smooth functions.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.word_comp_add.text: Words in constant directions commute with translations.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.word_comp_add.summary: Translations commute with constant directional derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.word_eventuallyEq.text: Words of functions that agree near a point agree near that point.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.word_smul_const.text: A derivative word of a constant multiple.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.word_smul_const.summary: Constants pass through ordered derivative words

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.word_zero.text: Derivative words vanish on the zero function.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.word_zero.summary: Derivative words annihilate the zero field

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.words_general.text: Let $\ell_*,h>0$ and let the time weight $\gamma$ be positive. Suppose all finite norms of $f/\gamma$ exist, and the coefficients of label and phase differentiation have finite order-$j$ bounds $N_c(j)$ and $N_k(j)$. Assuming the finite-norm product estimate, the sum over all ordered sequences of $m$ physical coordinate derivatives is bounded by $\prod_{j=0}^{m-1}[C_j(9N_c(j)\ell_*^{-1}+3N_k(j)h^{-1})]\,\|f\|_{[m],\gamma}$. The formal conclusion also includes finiteness of these differentiated norms. With inverse-flow coefficients and $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, this gives the derivative cost in Lemma 5.7. The product for $m=0$ is one; its order constants are those of the product estimate, not new assumptions on the parent.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.words_general.summary: Iterate the weighted chain rule with separate coefficient costs

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.words_phaseIndep.text: Let $f$ be independent of phase, $\ell_*,h>0$, and $\gamma>0$. Assume finite weighted profile norms at every order and finite order-$j$ coefficient bounds $N_c(j),N_k(j)$ for the label and phase parts of the derivative operator. Given the finite-norm product estimate, the sum of the weighted norms after all ordered sequences of $m$ physical coordinate derivatives is at most $\prod_{j=0}^{m-1}[C_j9N_c(j)\ell_*^{-1}]\,\|f\|_{[m],\gamma}$. The phase-coefficient bounds remain formal premises, but no $N_k(j)h^{-1}$ factor appears in the conclusion because phase derivatives vanish. This is the improved mean estimate used in Lemma 5.7. The conclusion includes finiteness of all differentiated order-zero norms.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.words_phaseIndep.summary: Only inverse label coefficients remain for phase independent profiles

TorusEuler.Paper.Schedule.L.text: For a real-valued frequency sequence $\lambda_j$, the formal definition is $L_j=4\log\lambda_{j+1}$. This is the gain parameter in (1.14); in particular $L_{j+1}$ uses $\lambda_{j+2}$, which matters in Lemma 1.3. The formula is defined even without a positive-frequency hypothesis. The logarithm is assigned the value zero at zero and is extended to negative arguments using their absolute value. In the paper’s schedule all frequencies exceed one, so this convention is inactive and $L_j>0$. The formula alone provides neither that positivity nor any bound on the gain.
TorusEuler.Paper.Schedule.L.summary: The gain uses the next frequency in the sequence

TorusEuler.Paper.Schedule.ε.text: For the frequency sequence $\lambda_j$, put $L_j=4\log\lambda_{j+1}$. The formal definition assigns $\varepsilon_j=1/L_{j+1}^2$, agreeing with $\varepsilon_{j-1}=L_j^{-2}$ for $j\ge2$ in (1.14). Consequently $\varepsilon_j$ depends on $\lambda_{j+2}$, not $\lambda_{j+1}$. The formal formula also assigns a value at index zero, which this part of the paper does not use. Division by zero is assigned the value zero, so a zero gain would give a zero ratio, not an infinite one. The positive-frequency schedule supplies positive gains; separate estimates make these positive ratios small enough for amplification.
TorusEuler.Paper.Schedule.ε.summary: The ratio is the inverse square of the following gain

TorusEuler.Paper.Schedule.τ.text: For a positive frequency sequence $\lambda_j$, put $L_j=4\log\lambda_{j+1}$. At each wave index $j\ge1$, the formal definition is $\tau_j=\lambda_{j-1}^{-1/8}L_{j+1}^3$, the half-length used in $S_j=t_j+2\tau_j$. The formula uses a real exponent $-1/8$ and an integer cube. It is also assigned a value at index zero: subtraction of one from a nonnegative integer gives zero there, so it uses $\lambda_0$. The paper does not use that extra value. Positivity, decay of $\tau_j$, and the endpoint relation require separate assertions; this formula alone supplies none of them.
TorusEuler.Paper.Schedule.τ.summary: Defines the time available before each endpoint condition

TorusEuler.Paper.SmoothTerminalExtension.text: The formal condition asks for an open set containing $\{T\}\times(\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3)$ and a field $g$ smooth jointly on its union with $[0,T)\times(\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3)$. The field is periodic under every integer spatial translation and equals $u$ on that entire preterminal punctured slab. Thus it descends to a smooth extension through the terminal slice of the punctured torus. The field is defined everywhere, but smoothness is required only on the stated union; its other values are unconstrained. This condition neither asserts an Euler equation after $T$ nor extends a pressure. It specifies what an extension means and does not prove one exists.
TorusEuler.Paper.SmoothTerminalExtension.summary: One periodic field agrees with the preterminal velocity

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.eq_5_13.text: Let $F=D_aX$, $M=(D_xU)\circ X$, $K=F^TF$ and $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$ for the parent flow on $[0,T]$. The formal condition assumes $T>0$ and the standing hypotheses of §5.1: $T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$, $\lambda\ge1$, $U$ smooth, periodic, odd and divergence free with frequencies at most $2\mathsf D$, the bounds (5.1), $R_U$ odd with frequencies at most $4\mathsf D$ and $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$, and the coercivity (5.2); the pressure may be any smooth periodic pressure whose residual has these properties. For each nonnegative integer $C_A$, the assertion selects $a_0$; for every integer $a\ge a_0$ it selects $C$ and $C_m$, independently of the parent and derivative order. For $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$ and every $0<A\le\mathsf D^{C_A}$, it asserts finiteness and $\ell_*^m(|K|_{m,1/2}+|\Omega|_{m,1/2})\le C_m\mathsf D^C\sqrt{\ell_*}\le C_m/A$ for all $m\ge1$. Each Hölder norm is the maximum of its uniform norm and seminorm, over all labels and times in $[0,T]$. This defines the proposed assertion; the linked proof establishes it from Proposition 5.1, Lemma D.2 and (D.2).
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.eq_5_13.summary: The radius suppresses positive-order Hölder coefficient norms

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.eq_5_14.text:
Let $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$, $\lambda\ge1$. Let $U$ be smooth, odd, solenoidal and unit-periodic, with flow $X$ and smooth periodic pressure $p_U$. Require Fourier radii $2\mathsf D$ for $U$ and $4\mathsf D$ for the odd residual $R_U=U_t+U\cdot
abla U+
abla p_U$, $\|DU\|_\infty,\|DX\|_\infty,\|DX^{-1}\|_\infty\le\mathsf D$, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$, and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$ as quadratic forms. Write $F=D_aX$, $G=F^{-1}$, $M=(DU)\circ X$, $K=F^TF$ and $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$. Let smooth periodic $B,z, ar q, ar f$ satisfy $B_t+MB+F^{-T}
abla_a ar q= ar f$, $B=Fz_t$, $\operatorname{div}_az_t=0$ and $z(0)=z(T)=0$. Put $v=F^{-1}B=z_t$ and $g=F^T ar f$. For sufficiently large fixed $a$, $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$, and finite scaled source half-Hölder norm, the formal statement gives finiteness of the velocity norm and $\|v\|_{[n],1/2}\le C_n\mathsf D^C\|g\|_{[n],1/2}$ for all $n\ge0$. The norms sum scaled label derivatives on the whole interval, with the maximum of the supremum and half-Hölder seminorm at each order. The exponent $C$ is chosen after $a$ but before the parent and derivative order.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.eq_5_14.summary: The endpoint inverse preserves the derivative order

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.eq_5_59.text: For each integer $m\ge0$, the assertion asks for a nonnegative constant $C_m$ such that every continuous bilinear map $B:E\times F\to G$ between real normed spaces satisfies $\|B(f,g)\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\le C_m\|B\|\|f\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\|g\|_{C^{m,1/2}}$ whenever $f:\mathbb R^3\to E$ and $g:\mathbb R^3\to F$ belong to $C^{m,1/2}$. The output’s Hölder regularity is also asserted. The constant is chosen before the spaces, fields and bilinear map. This states a generalization of (5.59); scalar multiplication and the tensor products used in §5.7 are particular cases. It does not require periodicity.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.eq_5_59.summary: State the product estimate uniformly in the target spaces

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.eq_D_2.text: Let $0<\ell_*\le1$ and let $c:I\times\mathbb R^3\to X$ be smooth in the label variable, where $X$ is any real normed space. Assume all derivatives through order $n+1$ are uniformly bounded in time and label. The formal statement asserts $\|c\|_{[n]}\le\|c\|_{[n],1/2}\le4\ell_*^{-1/2}\|c\|_{[n+1]}$ and establishes finiteness of the Hölder quantities. At an order $m$ with derivatives bounded through $m+1$, it also proves $\ell_*^m|c|_{m,1/2}\le4\ell_*^{-1/2}(\ell_*^m|c|_m+\ell_*^{m+1}|c|_{m+1})$. Each multi-index is counted once. The Hölder norm uses the maximum of supremum and seminorm; their sum is equivalent within a factor two. Thus the explicit constant four yields the paper's unspecified constant after the chosen norm convention is accounted for. The proof is supplied separately.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.eq_D_2.summary: Costs one derivative and half a power of the radius

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.section8.text: The formal statement asks for parameters, an inductive construction, a constant and a real time $T$ satisfying the conclusions of Theorem 7.1. These include smooth odd divergence-free periodic stage velocities, the residual and central-wave bounds, summable corrections, shrinking oscillation supports, and $0<T<S_j$ for every stage, with $t_j\to T$. Thus $T$ is the paper’s common accumulation time. This declaration specifies an existence assertion; the adjoining proof establishes it from Theorem 7.1. Its conclusion contains no limiting field and no uniform convergence on $[0,T]$. It represents only the initial choice in Section 8, not the whole opening paragraph.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.section8.summary: Specify a common construction without yet asserting its limit

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.corollary_8_3.text: Given a common construction satisfying Theorem 7.1 and its smooth Euler limit $u,p$ from Proposition 8.1, assume bounded velocity, central vorticity blow-up, and fixed $c>0,C$ with $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\ge c\lambda_{j-1}^{1/8}-C\lambda_{j-1}^{1/32}-C$ throughout every sufficiently late $[t_j,t_{j+1})$. The formal statement concludes maximality at $T_\infty>0$, equality with the lifespan of every other maximal solution of finite lifespan from $u(0)$, and divergence of both integrals in (1.2). The quantitative bound is included in the formal Proposition 8.2, although not in its printed statement. This declaration specifies the implication; its proof uses crossing durations instead of a general continuation criterion. The integrals are nonnegative Lebesgue integrals over the half-open lifespan.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.corollary_8_3.summary: Assume the construction and quantitative terminal conclusions to obtain maximality

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_1_3.text: Let $b\ge1$ be an integer, $K(s)=320b(s+1)$, and $\mathcal B(s)>0$ satisfy $\log\mathcal B(s)\ge4K(s+1)^3$ for $s\ge1$. Suppose $\lambda_0\ge\mathcal B(1)$, $q_1=1$, $\lambda_j=\lambda_{j-1}^{K(q_j)}$, and $q_{j+1}=\max\{1\le s\le q_j+1:\mathcal B(s)\le\lambda_{j-1}\}$. Then $q_j\le q_{j+1}\le q_j+1$, $q_j\to\infty$, and $4\log\lambda_{j+2}\le(\log\lambda_{j-1})^2$ for $j\ge1$. Thus the last expression is exactly (1.15), since $L_{j+1}=4\log\lambda_{j+2}$. The formal statement omits threshold monotonicity and analytic-cost domination from §1.5; the arithmetic result therefore applies under fewer assumptions.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_1_3.summary: The schedule has slowly increasing unbounded derivative orders

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_2_1.text: Let $J$ be a time interval on which relative derivatives are uniquely determined. Suppose $D$ is differentiable, $\operatorname{tr}D=0$, $D'+D^2$ is symmetric, and $k'=-D^Tk$, $\mathbf a'=-D\mathbf a+p_{\rm w}k$, where $p_{\rm w}=2k\cdot D\mathbf a/|k|^2$. For differentiable $F$ and any $P$ with $P'=F$, transverse data give an Euler velocity $u=Dx+\mathbf aF(k\cdot x)$ on $\mathbb R^3$, with pressure $-x\cdot(D'+D^2)x/2-p_{\rm w}P(k\cdot x)$ and zero divergence. Nonzero perpendicular data at any $t_0\in J$ remain so throughout $J$, including earlier times. Unlike the paper, the formal statement requires neither a smooth odd periodic profile nor its normalization; the Euler identity also allows $k=0$, using zero for division by zero. The interval derivative includes one-sided endpoint derivatives.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_2_1.summary: The Euler identity needs weaker profile hypotheses than the paper assumes

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_2_2.text: Let nonzero perpendicular paths $k,\mathbf a\in\mathbb R^3$ satisfy $k'=-B^Tk$ and $\mathbf a'=-B\mathbf a+2(k\cdot B\mathbf a)k/|k|^2$ on a time set $J$, with $\operatorname{tr}B=0$. Put $E_1=k/|k|$, $E_2=\mathbf a/|\mathbf a|$, $E_3=E_1\times E_2$, $B_{ij}=E_i\cdot BE_j$ and $\sigma=|k||\mathbf a|$. The formal statement gives orthonormality and $E_1'=-B_{12}E_2-B_{13}E_3$, $E_2'=B_{12}E_1-B_{32}E_3$, $E_3'=B_{13}E_1+B_{32}E_2$, $(\log\sigma)'=B_{33}$. Derivatives are relative to $J$. These are (2.2), with no regularity assumption on $B$ beyond the supplied wave derivatives and no symmetry assumption on $B'+B^2$. All normalizations and the logarithm have nonzero positive denominators or arguments under the stated hypotheses.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_2_2.summary: Wave derivatives and zero trace suffice for the frame equations

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_2_4.text:
Let $B,E_c$ be continuous on compact $I
i t_0$, with $\operatorname{tr}B=0$. On $I$, let $k_p,\mathbf a_p
e0$, $k_p\cdot\mathbf a_p=0$, $k_p'=-B^Tk_p$, $\mathbf a_p'=-B\mathbf a_p+2(k_p\cdot B\mathbf a_p)k_p/|k_p|^2$. Physical derivatives are relative to $I$. Put $E_1=k_p/|k_p|$, $E_2=\mathbf a_p/|\mathbf a_p|$, $E_3=E_1	imes E_2$, $B_{ij}=E_i\cdot BE_j$, $\sigma_p=|k_p||\mathbf a_p|$, $\sigma=\sigma_p(t_0)$, $

u-1|+\sup_I|B_{32}/\eta-1|+\sup_I\|B\|/r+\sup_I\|E_c\|/

With $\zeta=(k\cdot E_1,Sk\cdot E_2,k\cdot E_3)/\lambda$ and $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon	au^2/2)$, the formal statement gives $|\zeta-(	an\varphi,-\varepsilon	au,1)|$, $||k|^2\cos^2\varphi/\lambda^2-1|\le CT^p\delta\le1/2$, $1/2\le\zeta_3\le3/2$, $|\zeta|\le3T^2$, and $|\sigma_p/\sigma-1|\le2T\delta$. One continuous $\mathcal E$ satisfies $\|\mathcal E\|\le CT^p\delta$ and $\alpha'=[- igl( egin{smallmatrix}\varepsilon	au\sin2\varphi&\cos^2\varphi(1-\varepsilon	an\varphi)\1&0\end{smallmatrix} igr)+\mathcal E]\alpha$ for every $\mathbf a'=-M\mathbf a+2(k\cdot M\mathbf a)k/|k|^2$, $k\cdot\mathbf a=0$ on $I$, where $\alpha=(S\mathbf a\cdot E_1,\mathbf a\cdot E_2)$. Absolute $C$ and integers $p,N$ precede $C_0\ge N$ and all data. Bounds concern $[0,T]$; vector norms are Euclidean, pair operator norms use the maximum norm.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_2_4.summary: A common small error controls the wave vector and every transverse amplitude

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_2_5.text: For $0<\varepsilon\le1$, let $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon\tau^2/2)$ and consider $Y'=\cos^2\varphi(1-\varepsilon\tan\varphi)-\varepsilon\tau\sin(2\varphi)Y-Y^2$, $Y(0)=1$, on $[0,\infty)$. There is a unique solution on that half-line, with $|Y|\le1$ and $Y=(1+e)\cos\varphi-\varepsilon\tau\sin(2\varphi)/4$ for one function $0\le e\le\varepsilon/8$. Its amplitude $a_{\rm ref}=\exp\int_0^\tau Y$ equals $\sqrt{\cos\varphi}\exp\int_0^\tau(1+e)\cos\varphi$. It has its global maximum at the unique zero $\tau_m$ of $Y$, with $2\le\varepsilon\tau_m\le3$, positive $Y$ before and negative $Y$ after, and $\log a_{\rm ref}(\tau_m)\ge\varepsilon^{-1/2}-1$. This declaration specifies the complete assertion of Lemma 2.5; a separate theorem proves it. The functions are defined on all real times, but the equation, bounds and uniqueness concern only $\tau\ge0$, with a right derivative at zero.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_2_5.summary: The assertion includes uniqueness on the nonnegative time axis

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_2_6.text:
Let $B,E_c$ be continuous on compact $I\supset[t_0,t_0+T/r]$, with $\operatorname{tr}B=0$ and nonzero perpendicular preceding wave data satisfying $k_p\prime=-B^Tk_p$, $\mathbf a_p\prime=-B\mathbf a_p+2(k_p\cdot B\mathbf a_p)k_p/|k_p|^2$. Set $E_1=\widehat{k_p}$, $E_2=\widehat{\mathbf a_p}$ and $E_3=E_1	imes E_2$; $B_{ij}=E_i\cdot BE_j$. Physical derivatives are relative to $I$; for interval $I$, endpoint derivatives are one-sided. Put $\sigma=|k_p(t_0)||\mathbf a_p(t_0)|$, $
u=B_{12}(t_0)>0$, $\eta=B_{32}(t_0)>0$, $r=\sqrt{2\sigma
