TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_2_7.summary: The first coupling stays positive throughout amplification

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_3_1.text: For the selected bump construction and every $0<h\le1$, the formal theorem establishes smooth period-one functions $F_h,P_h$, with $F_h$ odd, $P_h'=F_h$ and $\int_0^1P_h=0$. A positive constant independent of width and phase gives $F_h'(0)=1$, $-Ch\le F_h'\le1$ and $|F_h|\le Ch$. For each integer $j\ge2$, a positive $C_j$ independent of $h,s$ gives $|\partial_s^jF_h|\le C_jh^{1-j}$. The power uses an integer exponent, including negative values. The paper asserts existence of some such family; this result asserts all those properties of the particular family subsequently used for the wave and its pressure.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_3_1.summary: The selected profiles realize the paper’s existence assertion

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_4_1.text: Let $u$ be a smooth periodic divergence-free parent with flow $X$ on $[0,T]$, $0<T\le1$. Set $F=D_aX$, $M=(\nabla u)\circ X$, $H^\#=-(M_t+M^2)$, $K=F^TF$, and $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$. If $H^\#\le I$ as quadratic forms, then for each label and every $z\in H^1_0$, with $\xi=Fz$, $\int H^\#\xi\cdot\xi\le\frac12\int|\xi_t|^2$ and $\int(Kz_t\cdot z_t+\Omega z_t\cdot z)\ge\frac12\int|\xi_t|^2$. The formal statement represents $z$ by $Jv$ with $v\in L^2$ and $\int v=0$, so no test paths are lost. Symmetry of $H^\#$ is unnecessary. Here $Jw(t)=\int_0^tw(s)\,ds$.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_4_1.summary: Prove Lemma 4.1 for every Sobolev test path

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_10.text: Let $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$, $\lambda\ge1$. Let $U$ be smooth, odd, solenoidal and unit-periodic, with flow $X$ and smooth periodic pressure $p_U$. Require Fourier radii $2\mathsf D$ for $U$ and $4\mathsf D$ for the odd residual $R_U=U_t+U\cdot\nabla U+\nabla p_U$, $\|DU\|_\infty,\|DX\|_\infty,\|DX^{-1}\|_\infty\le\mathsf D$, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$, and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$ as quadratic forms. Let $P\ge2$, $0\le t_0<T$, $M=DU\circ X$, $\kappa=DX^{-T}k_*$, $\lambda=|\kappa(t_0,0)|$, and $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$. The central seed is nonzero, transverse and homogeneous; require $\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a\ge\mathsf D^{-1}|\kappa||\mathbf a|$ and $|b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for every transverse homogeneous $b$ and $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$. For sufficiently small envelope and $C_{\rm step}=\Gamma_P\mathsf D^b$ with $C_{\rm step}\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, every smooth periodic solenoidal perturbation $v$ satisfying $\|D^jv\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$, $j=0,1,2$, has a flow of $V+v$; every such flow satisfies $\|DY_{0,t}\|,\|DY_{t,0}\|\le C_{\rm step}\lambda^{1/4}$. These are separate derivative bounds, and $V$ is the depth-$P$ approximate velocity. Homogeneous means $b_t=-(I-2P_\kappa)Mb$, with $P_\kappa=\kappa\otimes\kappa/|\kappa|^2$.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_10.summary: Every permitted perturbed flow has the same polynomial deformation bound

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_3.text: Assume a smooth odd solenoidal parent and smooth periodic pressure on $0<T\le1$, bands $2\mathsf D$ for $U$ and $4\mathsf D$ for its odd residual $R_U$, bounds $\|DU\|,\|DX\|,\|DX^{-1}\|\le\mathsf D$, $\mathsf D\ge2$, $\|R_U\|\le\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. Let $0\le t_0<T$, $\lambda=|\kappa(t_0,0)|\ge1$, and a nonzero transverse central seed satisfy $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$ and $\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a\ge\mathsf D^{-1}|\kappa||\mathbf a|$. Every transverse homogeneous solution $\mathbf b$ must obey $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$. For small fixed $\ell_*$ and $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, nearby seeds obey $|\mathbf a(t,a)|\le2|\mathbf a(t,0)|$ and positive coupling. Supported transverse solutions obey $\|V\|_{[n],\gamma}\le C_n\mathsf D^C(\gamma(t_0)^{-1}\|V(t_0)\|_{[n]}+\|f\|_{[n],\gamma})$. Zero-initial centered forcing gives $\|V\|_{[n],\gamma}+\lambda\|\mathsf p\|_{[n],\gamma}\le C_n\mathsf D^C\|f\|_{[n],\gamma}$; the leading wave has bound $C_n\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-5/4}$. The first estimate requires full-interval profiles; the paper permits active-interval data. Pressure and amplitude assumptions are broader; the envelope is fixed.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_3.summary: Seed localization and correction bounds hold together

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_3_of_ode.text: This assembles the cited estimates of Lemmas 3.1, D.1 and D.2 and the assumed weighted ODE derivative estimate into one bundle of inputs, then invokes the form of Lemma 5.3 that takes this bundle. A separate theorem derives that ODE estimate from the cited Lemma D.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_3_of_ode.summary: Pass the supplied estimates to the transverse argument

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_5.text: Assume a smooth odd unit-periodic solenoidal parent and smooth periodic pressure on $0<T\le1$, with bands $2\mathsf D$ for velocity and $4\mathsf D$ for its odd residual, gradient and both deformation bounds $\mathsf D\ge2$, residual bound $\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. Put $M=DU\circ X$, $\kappa=DX^{-T}k_*$, $\lambda=|\kappa(t_0,0)|\ge1$ and $0\le t_0<T$. The nonzero central seed solves $\mathbf a_t=-(I-2P_\kappa)M\mathbf a$, is transverse, has $\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a\ge\mathsf D^{-1}|\kappa||\mathbf a|$, and satisfies $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$. Every transverse homogeneous solution $\mathbf b$ obeys $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$. For small fixed $\ell_*$ and $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, transverse $V$ satisfies $\|C[V]\|_{[n],\gamma}\le C_n\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-1}\|V\|_{[n+1],\gamma}$. If $V_t+MV+\kappa\mathsf p_s=f$, the same factor bounds $(\partial_t+M)C[V]+\mathbf d\mathsf p$ by the sum of the next-order norms of $V,f$. The profiles are smooth and $V,f$ have zero phase mean on all $[0,T]$; transversality, the equation and pressure normalization concern $[t_0,T]$. Smooth representatives of the homogeneous leading wave are also proved to exist. Thus full-interval assumptions accompany broader pressure and amplitude hypotheses.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_5.summary: The curl correction gains one inverse frequency

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_7.text: On $[0,T]\times\mathbb T^3$, for a smooth odd divergence-free periodic parent on $0<T\le1$ with deformation and gradient bounds $\mathsf D\ge2$, velocity and residual Fourier radii $2\mathsf D,4\mathsf D$, residual size $\lambda^{-5/2}$ and coercivity $D^2p-\nabla R_U\le I$, require a transverse nonzero central solution $\mathbf a_t=-(I-2P_\kappa)M\mathbf a$, $\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a\ge\mathsf D^{-1}|\kappa||\mathbf a|$, and $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for every transverse homogeneous solution and $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$, $|\kappa(t_0,0)|=\lambda\ge1$ and $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$. Take $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$ sufficiently small and $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$. A profile smooth on $[0,T]$ and defined for all labels and phases, with the combined lattice translation law, independent of phase outside the envelope, satisfies $\|D^mf^\natural\|\le C_m(\mathsf D^C\lambda^{3/2})^m\gamma(t)\|f\|_{[m],\gamma}$ and the $C^{m,1/2}$ bound using $m+1$. Here the derivative norm sums ordered coordinate sequences. The weighted estimates hold on $[t_0,T]$. Both estimates hold unweighted on $[0,T]$, and phase-independent fields omit $\lambda^{3/2}$. The target is any real normed space; constants precede the parent. The formal profile already incorporates continuation across cells.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_7.summary: The physical derivative estimates are proved for all derivative orders

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_8.text:
Let a smooth odd divergence-free periodic parent on $0<T\le1$ have gradient and deformation bounds $\mathsf D\ge2$, Fourier radii $2\mathsf D,4\mathsf D$ for $U,R_U$, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p-
abla R_U\le I$. For $\lambda\ge1$, take a nonzero transverse seed of $\mathbf a_t=-(I-2P_\kappa)M\mathbf a$, with $\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a\ge\mathsf D^{-1}|\kappa||\mathbf a|$ and $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for every transverse homogeneous solution $\mathbf b$ and $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$, $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$, a sufficiently small envelope and a depth-$P\ge2$ expansion. Under $C_{m step}=\Gamma_P\mathsf D^b$ and $C_{m step}\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, this theorem proves smooth periodic $V=U+W^
atural$, $\Pi=p+\mathsf P^
atural$, odd divergence-free $V$, and residual $R_P^
atural+R_{\widetilde\chi}^
atural$. The oscillatory supremum is $O(\mathsf D^b\lambda^{-5/4})$; its $C^{m,1/2}$ bound has factor $\mathsf D^{b(m+2)}\lambda^{3(m+1)/2-5/4}$, while the mean has $\mathsf D^{b(m+2)}\lambda^{-5/2}$. The residual $C_tC^{1,1/2}$ norm is bounded by $C_{m step}\lambda^2(\lambda^{-2P/3}+\|\widetilde\chi\,{}^{\prime}\gamma\|_\infty)$. Constants precede the parent; the cutoff supremum is over $[t_0,T]$.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_8.summary: Prove exact residual decomposition and all physical norm estimates

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_9.text: For a smooth odd divergence-free periodic parent on $0<T\le1$, require deformation and gradient bounds $\mathsf D\ge2$, Fourier radii $2\mathsf D,4\mathsf D$ for $U,R_U$, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p-\nabla R_U\le I$. Take a nonzero transverse seed of $\mathbf a_t=-(I-2P_\kappa)M\mathbf a$, with $\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a\ge\mathsf D^{-1}|\kappa||\mathbf a|$ and $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for every transverse homogeneous solution $\mathbf b$ and $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$, $|\kappa(t_0,0)|=\lambda\ge1$, $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$, and a depth-$P\ge2$ finite expansion with sufficiently small envelope. Under $C_{\rm step}=\Gamma_P\mathsf D^b$ and $C_{\rm step}\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, the assertion gives $D_x^2\mathsf P^\natural\le C_{\rm step}\lambda^{-1/4}I$ on $[0,T]$ and $\|D V(t,0)-D U(t,0)-\widetilde\chi\mathbf a\otimes\kappa\|\le\lambda^{-1/3}$ on $[t_0,T]$. The first is a quadratic-form upper bound, the second an operator-norm bound. Constants precede the parent and expansion. Neither zero-mean Poisson normalization of $p$ nor attainment of $\max\gamma=1$ is required.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_9.summary: Prove the signed Hessian bound and central rank one approximation

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_6_1.text: Let $B_\rho=2\pi(e_1+\rho e_3)\otimes e_2$, $0<\rho\le1$, $\lambda\ge1$, $T>0$, and $T\|B_\rho\|\le1/8$. The formal statement asserts existence of nonzero perpendicular paths $\kappa,\mathbf a$ on $[0,T]$ solving $\kappa_t=-B_\rho^T\kappa$ and $\mathbf a_t=-(I-2P_\kappa)B_\rho\mathbf a$, with $\kappa(0)=\lambda e_1$, $\mathbf a(0)=ce_2$, $c>0$, and attained maximum $\lambda^{-3/4}$. Here $P_\kappa$ projects onto $\mathbb R\kappa$. Every such pair satisfies $\lambda^{1/4}/2\le|\kappa(0)||\mathbf a(0)|\le\lambda^{1/4}$. With $\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a|$ and $\nu=(\kappa/|\kappa|)\cdot B_\rho(\mathbf a/|\mathbf a|)$, it also gives $\nu\ge\mathsf D^{-1}$ and $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for every $\mathsf D\ge2$, every transverse solution of the same amplitude equation, and $0\le t'\le t\le T$. Derivatives are within the closed interval; the matrix norm is the Euclidean operator norm. This is the proved numbered assertion.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_6_1.summary: Proves existence, propagation, coupling and the initial strength interval

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_A_2.text: For $H=\mathbb R^3$ take $\mathcal R=\mathbb P$; for $H=L^2([0,1];\mathbb R^3)$ take $\mathcal R=\mathbb P\mathcal Q$, where $\mathcal Q$ removes the time average. Suppose $B:\mathbb T^3\to\mathcal L(H)$ is Lipschitz with constant $L\ge0$ and $\langle B(a)w,w\rangle\ge\mu\|w\|^2$, $\mu>0$, for all vectors in the first case and zero-time-mean paths in the second. Then $\mathcal RB$ is invertible on its projected half-Hölder space with bound $C(2+\mu^{-1}+\|B\|_\infty+L)^p$. The constants are chosen before $B$, with integer $p\ge0$. If $B\in C^{k,1/2}$, $k\ge1$, the same inverse preserves that class. The paper requires the stronger base hypothesis $B\in C^{1,1/2}$.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_A_2.summary: Prove the base inverse and preservation of higher regularity

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_B_1.text: Let $S_\Lambda$ act on $\mathbb T^3=\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3$ with symbol $\psi(\xi/\Lambda)$. Assume $\psi$ is smooth and even, $0\le\psi\le1$, equals one on the unit ball and vanishes outside radius two, and $\Lambda>0$. The formal statement gives parity, support $|\xi|\le2\Lambda$, divergence preservation for smooth real velocities, and uniform $L^\infty$ and $C^{0,1/2}$ bounds. For frequencies at most $4\Lambda$ it proves $\sum_{|\beta|=m}\|\partial^\beta f\|_\infty\le C_m\Lambda^m\|f\|_\infty$; for $f\in C^{M,1/2}$ and $s\le M$, $\|(I-S_\Lambda)f\|_{C^{s,1/2}}\le C_M\Lambda^{s-M}\|f\|_{C^{M,1/2}}$. Constants precede frequencies, targets and fields. Bernstein permits any real normed target. The $L^\infty$ input is essentially bounded and almost-everywhere strongly measurable in a complex Banach target; real velocities are continuous. Spatial commutation covers all complex orders, one real coordinate derivative and one time derivative on smooth closed slabs. Higher real orders require iteration. The $C^{m,1/2}$ norm is the sum over orders $j\le m$ of the supremum and the half-Hölder seminorm of the $j$th derivative tensor. The paper assumes radiality and $\Lambda\ge1$.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_B_1.summary: Collects commutation, support, boundedness, Bernstein and tail estimates

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_D_1.text: Fix a time set $I$, positive scales $\ell_*,h$ and $\gamma:I\to(0,\infty)$. For fields smooth in $(a,s)\in\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, $\|f\|_{[n]}$ sums $\ell_*^{|\beta|}h^j\sup_{t,a,s}|\partial_a^\beta\partial_s^jf|$ over $|\beta|+j\le n$, once per multi-index. Assume the derivative families entering each right side below are bounded. The formal statement proves $\sum_i\|\partial_{a_i}f\|_{[n],\gamma}\le3\ell_*^{-1}\|f\|_{[n+1],\gamma}$, $\|\partial_sf\|_{[n],\gamma}\le h^{-1}\|f\|_{[n+1],\gamma}$, and $\|B(f,g)\|_{[n],\gamma}\le C_n\|B\|\|f\|_{[n]}\|g\|_{[n],\gamma}$ for every continuous bilinear $B$. Weighted boundedness concerns derivatives of $f/\gamma$ or $g/\gamma$, not merely the unnormalized fields. For period-one Banach-valued fields, averaging, subtraction of the average and the zero-mean periodic primitive have respective bounds $1,2,2$ in the same norm; the primitive requires zero phase mean. All output derivative families are bounded. For phase-independent fields, the product estimate also holds with half-Hölder norms using the maximum of the uniform norm and seminorm. There is no time differentiation.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_D_1.summary: Controls differentiation, products, averaging and the periodic primitive

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_D_2.text: Assume $\mathsf D\ge1$ and smooth phase-independent coefficients with $|c|_m\le C_m\mathsf D^{q(m+1)}$. The formal statement uses nonnegative integer exponents. For inputs with exponents $q,r$, a bilinear product of norm at most one has exponent $2\max(q,r)$. In a complete real normed algebra, pointwise invertibility and $\|c^{-1}\|_\infty\le\mathsf D^e$ give exponent $3\max(q,e)$. Output constants are selected after the input constants and value spaces, but before $\mathsf D$, the time set and fields. Finally, $0<\ell_*\le\mathsf D^{-q}$ gives $\|c\|_{[n]}\le C'_n\mathsf D^q$ and $\ell_*^m|c|_m\le C'_m\mathsf D^{2q}\ell_*$ for $m\ge1$. Rounding the paper's fixed real exponent upward changes both this radius condition and its concluding powers; it does not reproduce that clause literally.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_D_2.summary: Preserves polynomial growth under products, inverses and weighting

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_D_3.text:
Let $A,E,F$ be real vector spaces with seminorms $p_A,p_E,p_F$ and a finite ordered family of linear derivative maps. Put $\mathcal Lv=L_0v+\sum_
u B_
u(c_
u,v)$. Assume principal commutation, the product rule for each $B_
u$, and commuting coefficient and forcing derivatives. Require $b_
u,C_{m low}\ge0$, $p_F(B_
u(a,u))\le b_
u p_A(a)p_E(u)$, and $p_E(u)\le C_{m low}p_F(\mathcal Lu)$ for every $u\in E$. Let $|c|_m$ and $\|u\|_{[n]}$ sum derivative seminorms at order $m$ and through order $n$, counting each nondecreasing sequence once. If $C_{m low}\sum_
u b_
u|c_
u|_m\le C_m$ for $1\le m\le n$, the formal statement proves $\|v\|_{[n]}\le C_nC_{m low}\|f\|_{[n]}$ whenever $\mathcal Lv=f$. The constant depends only on $n$, the coefficient bounds and the number of derivative directions. Taking derivatives $\ell_*\partial_{a_i},h\partial_s$ and the appropriate zero-order seminorms gives the paper's weighted setting. Constraints, quotient equations and prescribed data must be included in $E,F$. No existence assertion is made.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_D_3.summary: Retains one zero-order inverse factor at higher orders

TorusEuler.Paper.meanDeformation.text: For the two-time flow notation $X(s,t,a)$, this definition is $F(t,a)=D_aX(0,t,a)$, a linear map on Euclidean $\mathbb R^3$. It is the paper's deformation $D_aX(t,a)$ and sends label variations to spatial variations. No smoothness or flow equation is assumed by the definition itself. Where a spatial derivative does not exist, the formal derivative operation returns zero; under the smooth-parent hypotheses used in the paper it is the ordinary derivative. Invertibility follows from the reverse-flow identities, rather than from this formula alone.
TorusEuler.Paper.meanDeformation.summary: Differentiate particle position with respect to its initial label

TorusEuler.Paper.meanDeformationInv.text: The formal definition is $G(t,a)=D_xX(t,0,x)|_{x=X(0,t,a)}$. For the smooth parent flow, $X(t,0,\cdot)$ is the inverse of $X(0,t,\cdot)$, and differentiating their compositions gives $G=(D_aX)^{-1}$. This is the inverse deformation in §3.1 and the coefficient of the derivative $\mathbf d=G^T\nabla_a$. The displayed definition accepts arbitrary maps and does not itself prove the inverse identity. Derivatives are assigned zero at points where they do not exist; regularity and the trajectory uniqueness hypotheses rule out that case in the application.
TorusEuler.Paper.meanDeformationInv.summary: Differentiate the reverse flow at the current particle position

TorusEuler.Paper.meanGradient.text: For a velocity $U$ and two-time maps $X$, the formal definition is $M(t,a)=D_xU(t,X(0,t,a))$. The derivative is a linear map on Euclidean $\mathbb R^3$, with matrix entries $M_{ij}=\partial_jU_i$. For the smooth parent and its flow, this is the coefficient driving both $\kappa_t=-M^T\kappa$ and the Craik–Criminale seed equation in §3.1. The definition alone imposes no Euler equation, incompressibility or trajectory equation. At a spatial nondifferentiability point the formal derivative is assigned zero; the paper's smoothness assumptions ensure the usual gradient is used.
TorusEuler.Paper.meanGradient.summary: The parent gradient is evaluated at the particle’s current position

TorusEuler.Paper.meanGradientRate.text: For a parent velocity $u$ and particle flow $X$, set $M(t,a)=D_xu(t,X_{0,t}(a))$. This expression defines its time derivative with the label $a$ fixed, taken within $[0,T]$. At $t=0$ and $t=T$ it is the corresponding one-sided derivative. This is the $M_t$ in (4.1), not the derivative at fixed Eulerian position. If the derivative within the interval does not exist, the formal expression is assigned zero. This convention is irrelevant under the smooth-parent assumptions of §4 with $T>0$, which ensure the ordinary one-sided derivative at the endpoints and the usual derivative in the interior.
TorusEuler.Paper.meanGradientRate.summary: Differentiate the transported velocity gradient at fixed label

TorusEuler.Paper.meanHsharp.text: For $M(t,a)=D_xu(t,X_{0,t}(a))$, define $H^\#(t,a)=-(M_t(t,a)+M(t,a)^2)$, with time differentiation at fixed label within $[0,T]$. This is precisely the coefficient in (4.1). No symmetry is built into the definition. If $u$ solves Euler, (4.3) identifies it with the pressure Hessian along the flow; for a parent with residual $R$, the additional term is $-(\nabla R)\circ X$. The inverse requires the upper quadratic-form bound $H^\#\le I$, which is a separate assumption.
TorusEuler.Paper.meanHsharp.summary: Define the coefficient governing the displacement energy

TorusEuler.Paper.meanKinetic.text: For a differentiable particle map $a\mapsto X_{0,t}(a)$, write $F=D_aX_{0,t}(a)$. The coefficient is $K=F^TF$, so $Kw\cdot w=|Fw|^2$. It is the kinetic matrix in (4.1), and the quadratic part of the label energy in (4.7). The transpose is the Euclidean adjoint and norms are operator norms. This definition gives nonnegativity, not a positive lower bound. If $F$ has inverse norm at most $D_->0$, the separate ellipticity estimate gives $K\ge D_-^{-2}I$.
TorusEuler.Paper.meanKinetic.summary: Define the kinetic coefficient from the flow deformation

TorusEuler.Paper.meanVorticity.text: With $F=D_aX_{0,t}(a)$ and $M=D_xu(t,X_{0,t}(a))$, the coefficient is $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$. It is the pulled-back vorticity in (4.1) and supplies the term $\Omega z_t\cdot z$ in the endpoint energy. The matrix convention is $(D_xu)_{ij}=\partial_ju_i$, fixing the sign of $M^T-M$. The formula does not require Euler or incompressibility. Its relation $K_t-\Omega=2F^TF_t$ uses the separately established flow identity $F_t=MF$.
TorusEuler.Paper.meanVorticity.summary: Pull the skew velocity gradient back by the flow

TorusEuler.Paper.modelEntries.text:
The formal matrix is $ igl( egin{smallmatrix}0&
u&0\0&0&0\0&\eta&0\end{smallmatrix} igr)$, so its only possibly nonzero entries are $B_{12}=
u$ and $B_{32}=\eta$. In Lemma 2.3 these are entries in the preceding wave’s moving orthonormal frame, not fixed spatial components. The definition permits arbitrary real $
u,\eta$ and contains no time variable. The model hypothesis separately requires the actual gradient to have these constant frame entries throughout $[0,T]$, with positive activation couplings and vanishing error gradient $E_c$.
TorusEuler.Paper.modelEntries.summary: The model matrix has precisely the two prescribed couplings

TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_2_8.text:
Let $B,E_c$ be continuous on compact $I
i t_0$, with $\operatorname{tr}B=0$. On $I$, let $k_p,\mathbf a_p
e0$, $k_p\cdot\mathbf a_p=0$, $k_p'=-B^Tk_p$, $\mathbf a_p'=-B\mathbf a_p+2(k_p\cdot B\mathbf a_p)k_p/|k_p|^2$. Physical derivatives are relative to $I$. Put $E_1=k_p/|k_p|$, $E_2=\mathbf a_p/|\mathbf a_p|$, $E_3=E_1	imes E_2$, $B_{ij}=E_i\cdot BE_j$, $\sigma_p=|k_p||\mathbf a_p|$, $\sigma=\sigma_p(t_0)$, $
u=B_{12}(t_0)>0$, $\eta=B_{32}(t_0)>0$, $r=\sqrt{2\sigma
u}$, $S=\sigma/r$, $\varepsilon=\eta/
u$, $	au=r(t-t_0)$. Assume $T\ge2$, $[t_0,t_0+T/r]\subset I$, and $k'=-M^Tk$ on $I$, $k(t_0)=\lambda E_3(t_0)$, $\lambda>0$, where $M=B+\mathbf a_p\otimes k_p+E_c$. Define $\delta=\sup_I|B_{12}/
u-1|+\sup_I|B_{32}/\eta-1|+\sup_I\|B\|/r+\sup_I\|E_c\|/
u$. For sufficiently large integer $C_0$, assume $C_0\varepsilon\le1$ and $C_0T^{C_0}\delta\le\varepsilon$. On $I$, require $\mathbf a'=-M\mathbf a+2(k\cdot M\mathbf a)k/|k|^2$, $k\cdot\mathbf a=0$, and $\mathbf a(t_0)=-E_1(t_0)/S+E_2(t_0)$. Assume $0<\varepsilon_+\le\varepsilon/32$, $H=2/\sqrt{\varepsilon\varepsilon_+}\le T$. Define $
u_+=\widehat k\cdot M\widehat a$ and $\eta_+=(\widehat k	imes\widehat a)\cdot M\widehat a$. There is a crossing $\eta_+/
u_+=\varepsilon_+$ in $[	au_m,H]$. Here $	au_m\ge2/\varepsilon$ is the unique nonnegative zero of every solution $Y'=\cos^2\varphi(1-\varepsilon	an\varphi)-\varepsilon	au\sin2\varphi\,Y-Y^2$, $Y(0)=1$, on $[0,\infty)$, with $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon	au^2/2)$. An attained $A=\max_{[0,T]}|\mathbf a|$ exists. At every crossing there, $e^{-1}/(4\sqrt{\varepsilon\varepsilon_+})\le|\mathbf a||k|/(\lambda A)\le18e^3/\sqrt{\varepsilon\varepsilon_+}$. On $[0,1]$, $|\mathbf a|\le e^{3-1/\sqrt\varepsilon}A$. The absolute threshold for integer $C_0$ precedes all data. Crossing uniqueness is not asserted. Here hats denote division by Euclidean length.
TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_2_8.summary: Every crossing in the prescribed interval retains the strength bound

TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_5_1.text: Let $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$, $\lambda\ge1$. Let $U$ be smooth, odd, solenoidal and unit-periodic, with flow $X$ and smooth periodic pressure $p_U$. Require Fourier radii $2\mathsf D$ for $U$ and $4\mathsf D$ for the odd residual $R_U=U_t+U\cdot\nabla U+\nabla p_U$, $\|DU\|_\infty,\|DX\|_\infty,\|DX^{-1}\|_\infty\le\mathsf D$, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$, and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$ as quadratic forms. Put $F=DX$, $M=DU\circ X$, $\kappa=F^{-T}k_*$ and $|\kappa(t_0,0)|=\lambda$. For $\mathcal C=\{F,F^{-1},M,\kappa/\lambda,\lambda^2/|\kappa|^2,P_\kappa\}$, one exponent $C$ gives $\|D^m\Phi\|_\infty\le C_m\mathsf D^{C(m+1)}$. If $\|D^mf\|_\infty\le C'_mA_f\mathsf D^m$, $A_f\ge0$, then $\|D^m(f\circ X)\|_\infty\le C_mA_f\mathsf D^{Cm}$. For $0<\ell_*\le\mathsf D^{-C}$, the sums $\sum_{j\le n}\ell_*^j\|D^j\Phi\|_\infty$ and $\sum_{j\le n}\ell_*^j\|D^j(f\circ X)\|_\infty$ are bounded by $C_n\mathsf D^C$ and $C_nA_f$, respectively. Derivatives use operator norms; constants precede the parent. Pressure normalization is not required.
TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_5_1.summary: Bernstein estimates yield the uniform coefficient bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_5_11.text:
Let $V,\Pi$ be a depth-$P\ge2$ approximation over a smooth odd divergence-free periodic parent on $0<T\le1$, with gradient and deformation bounds $\mathsf D\ge2$, velocity and residual Fourier radii $2\mathsf D,4\mathsf D$, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p_U-
abla R_U\le I$. Put $M=DU\circ X$, $\kappa=DX^{-T}k_*$, $|\kappa(t_0,0)|=\lambda$, $0\le t_0<T$. Require $|b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for every transverse homogeneous $b$, $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$, and $\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a\ge\mathsf D^{-1}|\kappa||\mathbf a|$. Assume $\lambda\ge1$, $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$, small envelope and $C_{m step}\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, where $C_{m step}=\Gamma_P\mathsf D^b$. For every smooth radial $0\le\psi\le1$ equal to one on $|\xi|\le1$ and zero on $|\xi|>2$, and $\Lambda\ge1$, the theorem constructs $u=S_\Lambda V$ and its normalized Poisson pressure $p$. With $\varepsilon=\Lambda^{2-P}(1+\|V\|_{C_tC^{P,1/2}})^2$ and $e=C\|R_V\|_{C_tC^{1,1/2}}+K_P\varepsilon$, $\|u-V\|_{C_tC^{2,1/2}}\le K_P\varepsilon$ and $\|R_u\|_{C_tC^{1,1/2}}+\|D^2(p-\Pi)\|_{C_tC^{0,1/2}}\le e$, and $D^2(p-p_U)\le(C_{m step}\lambda^{-1/4}+e)I$. Both $u,R_u$ are odd and solenoidal with bands $2\Lambda,4\Lambda$. Homogeneous means $b_t=-(I-2P_\kappa)Mb$, with $P_\kappa=\kappa\otimes\kappa/|\kappa|^2$. Take a nonzero transverse homogeneous central seed. Here $p_U$ is smooth periodic, $R_U=U_t+DU\,U+
abla p_U$ is odd, and $R_V=V_t+DV\,V+
abla\Pi$.
TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_5_11.summary: Prove the cutoff error bounds with the normalized Poisson pressure

TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_5_2.text:
Let $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$ and $\lambda\ge1$. Assume a smooth odd solenoidal unit-periodic parent $U$ and flow $X$, Fourier bands $2\mathsf D$ for $U$ and $4\mathsf D$ for the odd residual $R_U=U_t+U\cdot
abla U+
abla p_U$, bounds $\|DU\|,\|DX\|,\|DX^{-1}\|\le\mathsf D$, $\|R_U\|\le\lambda^{-5/2}$, and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. The pressure may be any smooth periodic choice satisfying these conditions. Put $M=DU\circ X$, $\mathbf d=DX^{-T}
abla_a$. For a smooth periodic phase-independent solution $B_t+MB+\mathbf d ar q= ar f$, require $B=DXz_t$, $\operatorname{div}_az_t=0$ and $z(0)=z(T)=0$. At sufficiently small fixed $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$, $\|B\|_{[n]}\le C_n\mathsf D^C\| ar f\|_{[n+1]}$ for every $n$. These are scaled label-derivative suprema on all of $[0,T]$. The exponent is chosen before the parent and order. This estimates existing solutions; it does not set $B(0)=0$.
TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_5_2.summary: The endpoint mean bound loses one source derivative

TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_5_4.text: Assume a smooth odd unit-periodic solenoidal parent and smooth periodic pressure on $0<T\le1$, with bands $2\mathsf D$ for velocity and $4\mathsf D$ for its odd residual, gradient and both deformation bounds $\mathsf D\ge2$, residual bound $\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. Put $M=DU\circ X$, $\kappa=DX^{-T}k_*$, $\lambda=|\kappa(t_0,0)|\ge1$ and $0\le t_0<T$. The nonzero central seed solves $\mathbf a_t=-(I-2P_\kappa)M\mathbf a$, is transverse, has $\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a\ge\mathsf D^{-1}|\kappa||\mathbf a|$, and satisfies $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$. Every transverse homogeneous solution $\mathbf b$ obeys $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$. For sufficiently small fixed $\ell_*$, the projected seed exists, and every depth $P\ge2$ admits a unique family of retained velocities and normalized pressures satisfying the mean and transverse recursions. For $W=\sum_{p=1}^P(V_p+C_{p+1}+B_p)$ and $\mathsf P=\sum_{p=1}^P(\mathsf p_p+\bar q_p)$, $\widetilde{\mathbf d}\cdot W=0$ and the momentum residual is $R_P+R_{\widetilde\chi}$. The oscillations and their sources vanish before activation and, at all times, outside the envelope; outside the envelope the remainder $R_P$ is also phase independent. Means need not vanish before activation. Smoothness is on the closed slab; no continuation across its endpoints is asserted.
TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_5_4.summary: Construct unique retained profiles and their exact remainder

TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_8_1.text: For every common construction satisfying Theorem 7.1, this theorem constructs smooth periodic velocity $u$ and mean-zero pressure $p$ solving Euler on $[0,T_\infty)$. The datum $u(0)$ is smooth, odd and divergence free, with $U_j(0)\to u(0)$ in every $C^{m,1/2}$. The velocity stays odd, and $U_j\to u$ uniformly in each such spatial norm on every $[0,S]$, $S<T_\infty$. Every maximal solution of finite lifespan from the same data lasts at least to $T_\infty$ and agrees with $u$ there. This is a conditional comparison, not general maximal-solution existence; Corollary 8.3 later proves maximality of the constructed solution. The spatial $C^{m,1/2}$ norm is $\sum_{i\le m}(\sup|D^if|+[D^if]_{1/2})$, where $D^if$ is the full $i$th derivative tensor in operator norm.
TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_8_1.summary: Prove existence and convergence without a general maximal-existence theorem

TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_8_2.text: For a common construction satisfying Theorem 7.1 and its smooth Euler limit from Proposition 8.1, this theorem proves $\sup_{0\le t<T_\infty}\|u(t)\|_\infty<\infty$ and $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\to\infty$. In addition, fixed real $c>0,C$ give $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\ge c\lambda_{j-1}^{1/8}-C\lambda_{j-1}^{1/32}-C$ for every sufficiently large $j$ and all $t\in[t_j,t_{j+1})$. Thus the blow-up is not restricted to a sequence of times. The spatial domain is the unit torus, represented by periodic fields on $\mathbb R^3$; the velocity norm is its essential supremum. The quantitative estimate is stronger than the printed Proposition 8.2 and is used with crossing lengths for the later integral argument.
TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_8_2.summary: Prove bounded velocity and a full terminal vorticity limit

TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_8_4.text: For the smooth periodic Euler limit of any common construction satisfying Theorem 7.1, this theorem proves the two limits in Proposition 8.4. Given a compact $K\subset\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3$ and an integer $m\ge0$, $u(t)$ and $\partial_tu(t)$ converge uniformly on $K$ with every spatial derivative through order $m$, as $t\uparrow T_\infty$. The limits extend to $C^m$ fields near $K$. Removing the lattice means removing the torus origin, and the time derivative is taken inside $[0,T_\infty)$. The conclusion supplies spatial limits of the velocity and one time derivative; it does not require convergence of all higher time derivatives. The auxiliary note proves a stronger extension assertion for a suitably chosen construction.
TorusEuler.Paper.proposition_8_4.summary: Prove both local limits away from the torus origin

TorusEuler.Paper.referenceAmplitude.text: For a real function $Y$ and time $\tau$, the formal expression is $a_{\rm ref}(\tau)=\exp(\int_0^\tau Y(s)\,ds)$, using the interval integral with its orientation when $\tau<0$. This defines a positive number for every input function. If the integral is not defined by an integrable function on the interval, the formal integral is assigned zero, giving amplitude one; this is not a claim of integrability. In the application, $Y$ solves (2.12) on $[0,\infty)$, hence is continuous there, and the ordinary integral gives the reference amplitude with $a_{\rm ref}(0)=1$ and $a_{\rm ref}'=Ya_{\rm ref}$.
TorusEuler.Paper.referenceAmplitude.summary: Exponentiating the integral of the logarithmic slope defines the reference amplitude

TorusEuler.Paper.referenceAngle.text: The formal angle is $\varphi(\tau)=\arctan(\varepsilon\tau^2/2)$ for every real $\varepsilon,\tau$. It satisfies $\tan\varphi=\varepsilon\tau^2/2$, and for $\varepsilon\ge0$ lies in $[0,\pi/2)$. These specify the branch in (2.4); there is no ambiguity by integer multiples of $\pi$. The angle parametrizes the limiting direction $\tan\varphi E_1+E_3$ as the preceding shear tends to infinity. The definition does not claim that it is the actual angle of a finite-shear or perturbed wave, whose components must be estimated separately.
TorusEuler.Paper.referenceAngle.summary: The arctangent chooses a fixed branch for the limiting wave-vector angle

TorusEuler.Paper.referenceAngle_mem.text: For every $\varepsilon\ge0$ and every real $\tau$, the formal statement proves $0\le\arctan(\varepsilon\tau^2/2)<\pi/2$. This is the branch requirement for $\varphi$ in (2.4), extended to all real times. In particular the cosine is positive at every finite time. The result concerns the explicitly defined reference angle only; it does not constrain the actual wave vector of a finite-shear configuration. Neither an evolution equation nor the smallness condition (2.7) is a hypothesis.
TorusEuler.Paper.referenceAngle_mem.summary: A nonnegative coupling ratio keeps the reference angle below a right angle

TorusEuler.Paper.referenceSystemMatrix.text: Put $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon\tau^2/2)$. The formal matrix acting on $(\alpha_1,\alpha_2)$ is $-\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}\varepsilon\tau\sin2\varphi&\cos^2\varphi(1-\varepsilon\tan\varphi)\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$. Its second row therefore gives $\alpha_2'=-\alpha_1$, exactly as in (2.5). This definition uses the paper’s signs, unlike the intermediate matrix in coordinates $(-\alpha_1,\alpha_2)$. It is defined for all real parameters and times and is only a coefficient matrix: it neither constructs a solution nor proves that a particular amplitude satisfies the equation. Those assertions require separate differential-equation hypotheses or theorems.
TorusEuler.Paper.referenceSystemMatrix.summary: The matrix is written in the paper’s two scaled amplitude coordinates

TorusEuler.Paper.remark_1_2.text: There exist smooth odd divergence-free data $u_0$ on $\mathbb T^3$ and a smooth odd maximal Euler solution on $[0,T_*)$, with $0<T_*<\infty$, bounded velocity, $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\to\infty$, and divergent time integrals of both gradient and vorticity norms. Velocity and its time derivative converge in every spatial $C^m$ norm on compact sets away from the origin. The velocity also extends smoothly in space and time through $T_*$ away from that point. Any maximal solution of finite real lifespan from $u_0$ has the same lifespan and velocity. The extension is periodic and need not solve Euler after $T_*$. This is the existential assertion of Remark 1.2, not an extension theorem for every singular solution.
TorusEuler.Paper.remark_1_2.summary: The chosen singular solution extends smoothly away from the origin

TorusEuler.Paper.scaledNormSq.text: For a real scale $S$ and vector $\zeta\in\mathbb R^3$, the formal expression is $m=\zeta_1^2+\zeta_2^2/S^2+\zeta_3^2$. When $S\ne0$ and $k=\lambda(\zeta_1E_1+\zeta_2E_2/S+\zeta_3E_3)$ in an orthonormal frame, it satisfies $|k|^2=\lambda^2m$. This is the factor after (2.3), not the ordinary Euclidean squared norm of $\zeta$. The definition also permits $S=0$: division by zero is assigned zero, so the middle term vanishes. To use $m$ as a nonzero pressure denominator, the amplitude equations impose positive $S$ and nonzero $\zeta_3$.
TorusEuler.Paper.scaledNormSq.summary: The scaled squared norm has a different weight in the second direction

TorusEuler.Paper.statementsS34ASolenoida.text:
This makes the existing normed additive group structure on the subspace of divergence-free bounded half-Hölder fields available to the formal statements. It introduces no new norm formula and no additional regularity assertion about a field. The paper uses the inherited $C^{0,1/2}$ norm on divergence-free fields without spelling out this step. It is implementation support for the endpoint statements, not a separately numbered mathematical claim.

No analytic operation is defined here: the declaration reuses the bundled normed additive-group structure. Finiteness of the half-Hölder norm is part of the ambient bundled space, rather than a fresh real supremum over an arbitrary unbounded function. This declaration does not by itself prove coefficient continuity, integrability, or differentiability.
TorusEuler.Paper.statementsS34ASolenoida.summary: The inherited norm on divergence free fields

TorusEuler.Paper.statementsS34ASolenoida.text:
This local declaration supplies the inherited real normed-space structure on the subspace of divergence-free half-Hölder fields on $\mathbb T^3$. It lets the endpoint statements use continuous linear maps, scalar multiplication and derivatives in that subspace. No solution is constructed and no coefficient estimate is proved. It is the explicit elaboration support for the paper’s use of a normed linear space of divergence-free fields.

The declaration only reuses an existing normed-space structure. It introduces no derivative, integral, division, supremum, conversion to extended nonnegative reals or square root. The presence of a normed-space structure is not a substitute for any field’s regularity hypotheses.
TorusEuler.Paper.statementsS34ASolenoida.summary: Scalar multiplication on divergence free Hölder fields

TorusEuler.Paper.strongShearMatrix.text: For scale $S$, ratio $\varepsilon$ and scaled wave vector $\zeta$, put $m=\zeta_1^2+\zeta_2^2/S^2+\zeta_3^2$ and $\Pi=(2\zeta_2\alpha_1+(\zeta_1+\varepsilon\zeta_3)\alpha_2)/m$. The formal matrix is the linear map whose first component is $-\alpha_2+\zeta_1\Pi$ and whose second is $-(1-1/(2S^2))\alpha_1+\varepsilon(\zeta_1\alpha_1+\zeta_2\alpha_2)/(2S^2\zeta_3)+\zeta_2\Pi/S^2$. These are the finite-shear right-hand sides in Lemma 2.3. The definition asserts no differential equation. Its use for a model amplitude requires $S>0$, $\zeta_3\ne0$ and transversality. At zero denominators the formal divisions are assigned zero, so existence of the matrix alone does not establish that this reduction is valid.
TorusEuler.Paper.strongShearMatrix.summary: Eliminating the third amplitude component gives the two finite-shear equations

TorusEuler.Paper.strongShearMatrix_mulVe.text: Let $m=\zeta_1^2+\zeta_2^2/S^2+\zeta_3^2$ and $\Pi=(2\zeta_2\alpha_1+(\zeta_1+\varepsilon\zeta_3)\alpha_2)/m$. The formal statement proves that the finite-shear matrix applied to $(\alpha_1,\alpha_2)$ has components $-\alpha_2+\zeta_1\Pi$ and $-(1-1/(2S^2))\alpha_1+\varepsilon(\zeta_1\alpha_1+\zeta_2\alpha_2)/(2S^2\zeta_3)+\zeta_2\Pi/S^2$. This verifies the algebra connecting the coefficient matrix to Lemma 2.3. The identity holds for arbitrary real inputs, including zero denominators because every division by zero is assigned zero. It is not an assertion that an amplitude solves this system; that requires the model wave hypotheses and $\zeta_3\ne0$.
TorusEuler.Paper.strongShearMatrix_mulVe.summary: Matrix multiplication gives the two displayed finite-shear right-hand sides

TorusEuler.Paper.strongShearPressure.text: For $S,\varepsilon\in\mathbb R$ and $\zeta\in\mathbb R^3$, the formal formula is $\Pi=(2\zeta_2\alpha_1+(\zeta_1+\varepsilon\zeta_3)\alpha_2)/(\zeta_1^2+\zeta_2^2/S^2+\zeta_3^2)$. In the two-entry model, with positive $S$, nonzero wave vector and the scaling (2.3), this is $\lambda S p_{\rm w}/r$. It is the pressure term in Lemma 2.3, linear in the two remaining amplitude components. The definition itself does not assume the model equations or positivity of the denominator. Division by zero is assigned zero; the lemma’s condition $\zeta_3\ne0$ ensures the ordinary pressure interpretation.
TorusEuler.Paper.strongShearPressure.summary: The reduced pressure depends linearly on the first two amplitude coordinates

TorusEuler.Paper.tan_referenceAngle.text: For all real $\varepsilon,\tau$, the formal statement proves $\tan(\arctan(\varepsilon\tau^2/2))=\varepsilon\tau^2/2$. This is the first relation in (2.4) with the explicitly chosen arctangent branch. It imposes no sign condition on $\varepsilon$ and involves no wave equation. The additional paper condition $0\le\varphi<\pi/2$ uses $\varepsilon\ge0$. Because arctangent always lies strictly between $-\pi/2$ and $\pi/2$, the tangent here does not encounter a pole at any finite real input.
TorusEuler.Paper.tan_referenceAngle.summary: The chosen arctangent has exactly the required tangent

TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_1_1.text: There exist smooth odd divergence-free periodic data $u_0$ and a smooth odd maximal Euler solution $u,p$ on $[0,T_*)$, with finite $T_*>0$. Velocity remains uniformly bounded, $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\to\infty$, and the time integrals of $\|\nabla u(t)\|_\infty$ and $\|\operatorname{curl}u(t)\|_\infty$ both diverge. For every compact set away from the torus origin and every $m\ge0$, velocity and its time derivative converge in $C^m$. The formal statement further spells out the classical uniqueness implicit in the paper: every maximal solution from $u_0$ has endpoint $T_*$ and agrees with $u$ before it. Fields are periodic functions on $\mathbb R^3$; pressure has zero spatial mean.
TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_1_1.summary: The formal theorem proves the stated periodic singularity

TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_4_2.text: On $I=[0,T]$, $0<T\le1$, let $U$ be smooth, unit-periodic and divergence free, $X$ its flow from time zero, $F=D_aX$, $M=(DU)\circ X$, $K=F^TF$, $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$, and $H^\#=-(M_t+M^2)\le I$ as quadratic forms. Assume $\|F^{-1}\|_\infty\le D\ge1$, $\|M\|_\infty\le L$, $\|K\|_\infty\le K_0$, $\|D_aK\|_\infty\le K_1$, $\|\Omega\|_\infty\le\Omega_0$, $\|D_a\Omega\|_\infty\le\Omega_1$, with nonnegative bounds. For $L_{\rm src}\in C(I;C^{0,1/2}(\mathbb T^3))$, solve $Kv-J(\Omega v)+L_{\rm src}=c+G_\phi$, $z_t=v$, $z(0)=z(T)=0$, where $Jw(t)=\int_0^tw(s)\,ds$. The fields $z,v,c$ are weakly divergence free; $z\in C^1_tC^{0,1/2}$, $v,G_\phi\in C_tC^{0,1/2}$, and $G_\phi=\nabla_a\phi$ for a periodic potential at each time. There are absolute $C\ge0$ and an integer $p\ge0$ such that $A=C(D+L+K_0+K_1+\Omega_0+\Omega_1)^p$ gives $\|v\|_{C_tC^{0,1/2}}\le A\|L_{\rm src}\|_{C_tC^{0,1/2}}$ and $\|(\mathbb PK(t))^{-1}\mathbb P\|\le A$ uniformly on $I$. The solution is unique in $z,v,c,G_\phi$ on $I$, not in the potential. Smooth force sources $L_{\rm src}=-J(F^T(f\circ X))$ also give smooth solutions of the linearized Euler equation. The coefficient bound uses first derivative suprema rather than full $C^{1,1/2}$ norms.
TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_4_2.summary: Prove existence and estimates for the selected correction

TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_5_6.text: On $0<T\le1$, assume smooth odd periodic solenoidal $U$ with flow $X$, smooth periodic $p_U$, Fourier bands $2\mathsf D,4\mathsf D$ for $U,R_U=U_t+DU\,U+\nabla p_U$, odd $R_U$, $\|DU\|,\|DX\|,\|DX^{-1}\|\le\mathsf D\ge2$, $\|R_U\|\le\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. Put $M=DU\circ X$, $\kappa=DX^{-T}k_*$, $|\kappa(t_0,0)|=\lambda\ge1$, $0\le t_0<T$. Require a nonzero transverse homogeneous seed, $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$, $\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a\ge\mathsf D^{-1}|\kappa||\mathbf a|$, and $|b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for every transverse homogeneous $b$ and $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$. At fixed sufficiently small $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$, if $\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, a depth-$P\ge2$ expansion obeys: $V_1,\lambda\mathsf p_1=O(\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-5/4})$; $V_p,f_p+f_p^S,\lambda\mathsf p_p=O(\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-5/4-2(p-1)/3})$ and $B_p,\bar f_p=O(\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-5/2-2(p-2)/3})$ for $2\le p\le P$; $C_{p+1}=O(\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-9/4-2(p-1)/3})$ for $1\le p\le P$. These hold in every finite scaled derivative norm, weighted by $\gamma^{-1}$ on the active interval for oscillations and unweighted on $[0,T]$ for means. Constants may depend on order and level or depth, but are uniform in the parent; one exponent works throughout. Homogeneous means $b_t=-(I-2P_\kappa)Mb$, with $P_\kappa=\kappa\otimes\kappa/|\kappa|^2$. Also $W_{\rm osc}=O(\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-5/4})$, $\sum_{p=2}^PB_p,\sum_{p=2}^P\bar f_p=O(\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-5/2})$, and $\|R_P\|_{[m]}\le C_{m,P}\lambda^{-5/4-2P/3}$.
TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_5_6.summary: The full hierarchy estimates hold with uniform parent powers

TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_7_1.text: For each smooth radial Fourier cutoff and integer $a_0$, the theorem chooses $b\ge1$, an envelope exponent $a\ge a_0$ and fixed-order majorants. Every admissible threshold $\mathcal B$ above them permits construction for all sufficiently large $N$. It gives smooth odd divergence-free periodic velocities on $[0,S_j]\times\mathbb R^3$, starting from $\sin(2\pi x_2)(e_1+\varepsilon_1e_3)$, with $\|U_j\|_\infty,\|(D_aX_j)^{\pm1}\|_\infty\le\lambda_j$, $\|R_j\|_\infty\le\lambda_{j+1}^{-3}$ and $D^2\pi_j\le(\sum_{i<j}\lambda_i^{-1})I$. The central splitting has error $\le\lambda_j^{-1/4}$; at $t_{j+1}$, $\eta_j/\nu_j=\varepsilon_j$, $\pi\le\nu_j\le4\pi$ and $C^{-1}\lambda_j^{1/4}\le\sigma_j\le C\lambda_j^{1/4}L_{j+1}^2$, with $C=18e^3$. Also $t_j\to T_\infty\in(0,S_j)$ and $\|O_j\|_\infty,\|U_j-U_{j-1}-O_j\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\le\lambda_j^{-1}$ for $m\le q_j$. Each step equals its finite expansion and Fourier cutoff. The central seed is identified, but equality of central and transported covectors and first-wave initial directions and normalization are absent. Hölder bounds are pointwise in time, in the spatial norm $\sum_{i\le m}(\sup|D^if|+[D^if]_{1/2})$, with $D^if$ the full $i$th derivative tensor. The exponent can be chosen arbitrarily large; the assertion does not cover every sufficiently large exponent.
TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_7_1.summary: Proves one common sequence with its actual localized steps

TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_A_1.text: There are constants $C\ge0$ and $p\in\mathbb N$, chosen before the data. On $[0,1]\times\mathbb T^3$, let symmetric $K$ and skew-symmetric $\Omega$ be time-continuous in $C^{0,1/2}$ and spatially differentiable, with uniform value and first derivative bounds $K_0,K_1,\Omega_0,\Omega_1$. Assume $K\ge\kappa I$, $\kappa>0$, and $\int_0^1(Kz_t\cdot z_t+\Omega z_t\cdot z)\,dt\ge\mu\int_0^1|z_t|^2\,dt$ for every $H^1_0$ path at every label, with $\mu>0$. Each $L\in C_tC^{0,1/2}$ gives unique $z,v=z_t,c,G$ on this interval satisfying $Kv-J(\Omega v)+L=c+G$, $z(0)=z(1)=0$, with solenoidal $z,c$ and periodic $G=\nabla\phi$. Moreover $\|v\|_0\le CQ^p\|L\|_0$, where $Q=2+\kappa^{-1}+\mu^{-1}+K_0+K_1+\Omega_0+\Omega_1$ and $Jw(t)=\int_0^tw$. Smooth data give smooth $z,c,G$. The norm is the time supremum of the spatial half-Hölder norm. The paper assumes stronger coefficient regularity; the scalar potential is not unique.
TorusEuler.Paper.theorem_A_1.summary: Prove Theorem A.1 on the normalized time interval

TorusEuler.Paper.zeta.text: At physical time $t=t_0+\tau/r$, the formal vector is $\zeta=((E_1\cdot k)/\lambda,S(E_2\cdot k)/\lambda,(E_3\cdot k)/\lambda)$, where $r=\sqrt{2\sigma\nu}$ and $S=\sigma/r$ use the positive activation strength and coupling of the preceding wave. In an orthonormal frame and for $\lambda\ne0$, this is exactly the wave-vector expansion (2.3). No new wave equation or initial frequency condition is imposed by this definition. It accepts $\lambda=0$, in which case all three divisions are assigned zero. The amplification theorems separately require $\lambda>0$ and physical times inside the compact set on which the frame assumptions hold.
TorusEuler.Paper.zeta.summary: Frequency and shear rescale the three moving-frame projections

TorusEuler.Paper.zetaRef.text: For real $\varepsilon,\tau$, the formal vector is $\zeta_0=(\tan\varphi,-\varepsilon\tau,1)=(\varepsilon\tau^2/2,-\varepsilon\tau,1)$, with $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon\tau^2/2)$. This defines the reference coordinates in (2.4), and its initial value is $(0,0,1)$. The third component is identically one. The definition does not by itself state its differential equations or convergence of an actual wave to it. Those are separate calculations. Its norm is the Euclidean norm of these three coordinates; it is not the physical wave vector, whose second component also carries $S^{-1}$ in (2.3).
TorusEuler.Paper.zetaRef.summary: The reference coordinates give the trajectory of the triangular limiting system

TorusEuler.PaperAffine.WaveOn.text: For functions $k,\mathbf a$ and a prescribed spatial linear map $D(t)$ on a time set $J$, the formal condition requires $k'=-D^Tk$ and $\mathbf a'=-D\mathbf a+2(k\cdot D\mathbf a)k/|k|^2$ throughout $J$. The second equation is expressed as a linear operator applied to $\mathbf a$. Derivatives are relative to $J$, including one-sided derivatives when $J$ is an interval with endpoints. Transversality, nonzero vectors and the background Euler conditions are absent from this condition and must be imposed separately. Division by zero is assigned zero, so the displayed right-hand side is formally defined even when $k=0$.
TorusEuler.PaperAffine.WaveOn.summary: The wave vector and amplitude obey the prescribed linear evolution equations

Put $E_1=k_p/|k_p|$, $E_2=\mathbf a_p/|\mathbf a_p|$, $E_3=E_1	imes E_2$, $B_{ij}=E_i\cdot BE_j$, $\sigma_p=|k_p||\mathbf a_p|$, $\sigma=\sigma_p(t_0)$, $

The formal statement bounds both $|\zeta-\zeta_0|$ and $\sum_i|\zeta_i-\zeta_{0,i}|$ by $CT^p\delta\le1/2$ on $[0,T]$. Every $\mathbf a'=-M\mathbf a+2(k\cdot M\mathbf a)k/|k|^2$, $k\cdot\mathbf a=0$ on $I$, gives $U=-S\mathbf a\cdot E_1$, $V=\mathbf a\cdot E_2$ satisfying $(U,V)'=(-\varepsilon	au\sin2\varphi\,U+\cos^2\varphi(1-\varepsilon	an\varphi)V,U)+R(U,V)$, $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon	au^2/2)$. One continuous $R$ works for all amplitudes, with maximum operator norm at most $CT^p\delta$. Absolute $C$, integer $p$ and threshold $N\ge240$ precede $C_0\ge N$ and all data. The paper uses $(-U,V)$ and additionally bounds the relative squared wave norm.
TorusEuler.PaperAffine.additiveCompariso.summary: One continuous error matrix controls every transverse amplitude in signed coordinates

TorusEuler.PaperAffine.exactWave.text: Let $J$ be a time interval on which relative derivatives are uniquely determined. Suppose $D$ is differentiable, $\operatorname{tr}D=0$, $D'+D^2$ is symmetric, and $k'=-D^Tk$, $\mathbf a'=-D\mathbf a+p_{\rm w}k$, where $p_{\rm w}=2k\cdot D\mathbf a/|k|^2$. For differentiable $F$ and any $P$ with $P'=F$, transverse data give an Euler velocity $u=Dx+\mathbf aF(k\cdot x)$ on $\mathbb R^3$, with pressure $-x\cdot(D'+D^2)x/2-p_{\rm w}P(k\cdot x)$ and zero divergence. Nonzero perpendicular data at any $t_0\in J$ remain so throughout $J$, including earlier times. Unlike the paper, the formal statement requires neither a smooth odd periodic profile nor its normalization; the Euler identity also allows $k=0$, using zero for division by zero. The interval derivative includes one-sided endpoint derivatives.
TorusEuler.PaperAffine.exactWave.summary: The prescribed wave and background give an exact incompressible Euler velocity

u,\eta$. Set $r=\sqrt{2\sigma
u}$, $S=\sigma/r$, $\varepsilon=\eta/
u$, $	au=r(t-t_0)$ and $\delta=\|B_{12}/
u-1\|_\infty+\|B_{32}/\eta-1\|_\infty+\|B\|_\infty/r+\|E_c\|_\infty/
u$, measured on a compact physical set containing $[t_0,t_0+T/r]$. Assume $T\ge2$, sufficiently large integer $C_0$, $C_0\varepsilon\le1$, $C_0T^{C_0}\delta\le\varepsilon$. Launch the new wave over $M=B+\mathbf a_p\otimes k_p+E_c$ at $k=\lambda E_3$, $\lambda>0$, $\mathbf a=E_2-E_1/S$. Supply $Y(0)=1$, $Y'=\cos^2\varphi(1-\varepsilon	an\varphi)-\varepsilon	au\sin2\varphi\,Y-Y^2$ on $[0,\infty)$, where $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon	au^2/2)$; put $a_{m ref}=e^{\int_0^	au Y}$. The formal statement gives $|\log(|\mathbf a|/a_{m ref})|\le\varepsilon$, $
u_+\ge\varepsilon
u/2$. For $	au\ge\sqrt2/\varepsilon$, it gives $|
u_+/
u-1|\le\varepsilon$ and $|(\eta_+/
u_+)/\cos\varphi-1|\le1/2$. The couplings are $
u_+=E_{1,+}\cdot ME_{2,+}$, $\eta_+=E_{3,+}\cdot ME_{2,+}$ with $E_{1,+}=k/|k|$, $E_{2,+}=\mathbf a/|\mathbf a|$, $E_{3,+}=E_{1,+}	imes E_{2,+}$. Between $u\le v$ in $[0,T]$, invertible transverse transport has Euclidean operator norm at most $252eS|\mathbf a(v)|/|\mathbf a(u)|$. Existence of $Y$ is an input. The paper assumes smoother backgrounds.
TorusEuler.PaperAffine.finiteComparison.summary: Growing initial data give amplitude, coupling and transverse-transport bounds

TorusEuler.PaperAffine.finiteReturn.text:
Let $B,E_c$ be continuous on compact $I
i t_0$, with $\operatorname{tr}B=0$. On $I$, let $k_p,\mathbf a_p
e0$, $k_p\cdot\mathbf a_p=0$, $k_p'=-B^Tk_p$, $\mathbf a_p'=-B\mathbf a_p+2(k_p\cdot B\mathbf a_p)k_p/|k_p|^2$. Physical derivatives are relative to $I$. Put $E_1=k_p/|k_p|$, $E_2=\mathbf a_p/|\mathbf a_p|$, $E_3=E_1	imes E_2$, $B_{ij}=E_i\cdot BE_j$, $\sigma_p=|k_p||\mathbf a_p|$, $\sigma=\sigma_p(t_0)$, $
u=B_{12}(t_0)>0$, $\eta=B_{32}(t_0)>0$, $r=\sqrt{2\sigma
u}$, $S=\sigma/r$, $\varepsilon=\eta/
u$, $	au=r(t-t_0)$. Assume $T\ge2$, $[t_0,t_0+T/r]\subset I$, and $k'=-M^Tk$ on $I$, $k(t_0)=\lambda E_3(t_0)$, $\lambda>0$, where $M=B+\mathbf a_p\otimes k_p+E_c$. Define $\delta=\sup_I|B_{12}/
u-1|+\sup_I|B_{32}/\eta-1|+\sup_I\|B\|/r+\sup_I\|E_c\|/
u$. For sufficiently large integer $C_0$, assume $C_0\varepsilon\le1$ and $C_0T^{C_0}\delta\le\varepsilon$. On $I$, assume $\mathbf a'=-M\mathbf a+2(k\cdot M\mathbf a)k/|k|^2$ and $\mathbf a(t_0)=-E_1(t_0)/S+E_2(t_0)$. Supply $Y(0)=1$ and $Y'=\cos^2\varphi(1-\varepsilon	an\varphi)-\varepsilon	au\sin2\varphi\,Y-Y^2$ on $[0,\infty)$, $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon	au^2/2)$. Assume $0<\varepsilon_+\le\varepsilon/32$, $H=2/\sqrt{\varepsilon\varepsilon_+}\le T$. With $
u_+=\widehat k\cdot M\widehat a$, $\eta_+=(\widehat k	imes\widehat a)\cdot M\widehat a$, the formal statement supplies $	au_m\in[2/\varepsilon,3/\varepsilon]$, $Y(	au_m)=0$, an attained $A=\max_{[0,T]}|\mathbf a|$, and a crossing $\eta_+/
u_+=\varepsilon_+$ in $(	au_m,H)$. Every crossing in $[	au_m,H]$ satisfies $1/(18e^3\sqrt{\varepsilon\varepsilon_+})\le|\mathbf a||k|/(\lambda A)\le18e^3/\sqrt{\varepsilon\varepsilon_+}$. On $[0,1]$, $|\mathbf a|\le e^{3-1/\sqrt\varepsilon}A$. One integer threshold $N\ge240$ precedes all data. Transversality on the active interval is derived, not separately assumed. Here hats denote division by Euclidean length.
TorusEuler.PaperAffine.finiteReturn.summary: A successor crossing occurs after the reference peak with controlled strength

TorusEuler.PaperAffine.finiteWindowNorma.text: For a valid amplification window, positive carrier, sufficiently large $C_0$, both smallness conditions, prescribed growing-wave initial data, wave equations and Riccati hypotheses, this theorem adds transverse transport to the normalized comparison theorem. For $u\in[0,T]$ and $v\in[u,T]$, it produces a continuous linear equivalence between the corresponding perpendicular planes, with norm at most $252eS\|A(v)\|/\|A(u)\|$. The action agrees with every transverse amplitude solution. It also retains the logarithmic and coupling bounds.

TorusEuler.PaperAffine.movingFrameDeriva.text: Let nonzero perpendicular paths $k,\mathbf a\in\mathbb R^3$ satisfy $k'=-B^Tk$ and $\mathbf a'=-B\mathbf a+2(k\cdot B\mathbf a)k/|k|^2$ on a time set $J$, with $\operatorname{tr}B=0$. Put $E_1=k/|k|$, $E_2=\mathbf a/|\mathbf a|$, $E_3=E_1\times E_2$, $B_{ij}=E_i\cdot BE_j$ and $\sigma=|k||\mathbf a|$. The formal statement gives orthonormality and $E_1'=-B_{12}E_2-B_{13}E_3$, $E_2'=B_{12}E_1-B_{32}E_3$, $E_3'=B_{13}E_1+B_{32}E_2$, $(\log\sigma)'=B_{33}$. Derivatives are relative to $J$. These are (2.2), with no regularity assumption on $B$ beyond the supplied wave derivatives and no symmetry assumption on $B'+B^2$. All normalizations and the logarithm have nonzero positive denominators or arguments under the stated hypotheses.
TorusEuler.PaperAffine.movingFrameDeriva.summary: The preceding wave frame and logarithmic strength satisfy the four identities

TorusEuler.PaperAffine.referenceModel.text: For $0<\varepsilon\le1$, put $\varphi(\tau)=\arctan(\varepsilon\tau^2/2)$. The formal statement constructs $Y,e$ on $[0,\infty)$ satisfying $Y(0)=1$, $Y'=\cos^2\varphi(1-\varepsilon\tan\varphi)-\varepsilon\tau\sin2\varphi\,Y-Y^2$ and $Y=(1+e)\cos\varphi-\varepsilon\tau\sin2\varphi/4$, with $0\le e\le\varepsilon/8$ and $|Y|\le1$. It gives exactly one zero $\tau_m$, with $2\le\varepsilon\tau_m\le3$, $Y>0$ before it and $Y<0$ afterwards. Moreover $\int_0^{\tau_m}Y\ge1/\sqrt\varepsilon-1$, so $a_{\rm ref}(\tau)=\exp(\int_0^\tau Y)$ reaches a maximum at $\tau_m$ with that logarithmic gain. The derivative at zero is from the right. This constructs one solution; it does not assert uniqueness among all solutions or the amplitude representation with a common deviation in (2.14), both included in the full numbered lemma.
TorusEuler.PaperAffine.referenceModel.summary: One Riccati solution has the prescribed deviation and a unique amplitude peak

TorusEuler.PaperFirstWaveConclusion.text: For a first central wave over $B_\rho=2\pi(e_1+\rho e_3)\otimes e_2$ on $[0,T]$, set $\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a|$ and $\nu=(\kappa/|\kappa|)\cdot B_\rho(\mathbf a/|\mathbf a|)$. The formal condition requires $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for every transverse amplitude solution, every $\mathsf D\ge2$ and $0\le t'\le t\le T$. It also requires $\nu(t)\ge\mathsf D^{-1}$ throughout the interval and $\lambda^{1/4}/2\le|\kappa(0)||\mathbf a(0)|\le\lambda^{1/4}$. This is a description of the conclusions, not a proof or a new wave construction. The estimates are proved when $0<\rho\le1$, $\lambda>0$ and $T\|B_\rho\|\le1/8$.
TorusEuler.PaperFirstWaveConclusion.summary: Collects precisely the three conclusions needed for the first wave

TorusEuler.PaperLimitAgreement.text: For specified approximate velocities $U_j$, a finite real $T>0$ and fields $u,p$, this condition requires a smooth odd periodic Euler solution on $[0,T)$ with mean-zero pressure and smooth odd divergence-free datum $u(0)$. It requires $U_j(0)\to u(0)$ in every spatial $C^{m,1/2}$ norm and convergence in those norms uniformly on every $[0,S]$, $S<T$. The same field $u$ must be continuous on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3$ and be the uniform velocity limit there. Every maximal solution of finite real lifespan from $u(0)$ must last at least to $T$ and agree with $u$ before $T$. This specifies properties; it does not prove existence. The closed-interval convergence exceeds the printed Proposition 8.1. The spatial norm is the sum of the supremum and half-Hölder seminorm of the full derivatives through order $m$.
TorusEuler.PaperLimitAgreement.summary: The same velocity is the closed-interval limit and Euler solution

TorusEuler.PaperMeanIntegratedSolution.text: On $[0,T]$, a solution here consists of a continuous curve $v$ of weakly divergence-free $C^{0,1/2}(\mathbb T^3)$ fields and a fixed divergence-free field $c$, satisfying $\mathbb P(Kv-J(\Omega v)+L)=c$ and $Jv(T)=0$. Since $Jv(0)=0$, its displacement has both zero endpoint values. The half-Hölder norm is the maximum of the supremum and seminorm. This is the projected form of (4.9); it does not yet supply a scalar pressure or prove existence. All asserted equations concern the designated interval, despite the functions being defined for every real time. Here $Jw(t)=\int_0^tw(s)\,ds$.
TorusEuler.PaperMeanIntegratedSolution.summary: Encode the velocity and its time-independent solenoidal part

TorusEuler.PaperMeanIntegratedSolution.c.text: Suppose a continuous divergence-free half-Hölder velocity $v$ satisfies $\mathbb P(Kv-J(\Omega v)+L)=c$ on $[0,T]$, with $T\ge0$, $K(0)=I$ and $L(0)=0$. Then $c=v(0)$, since the primitive vanishes at zero and the Leray projection fixes $v(0)$. These are the initial conditions used in §4.3 for a source obtained by integrating a force. The additional identification $c=b(0)$ uses the actual flow normalization $X_{0,0}=I$ and $D_aX_{0,0}=I$; it is not part of this algebraic conclusion. Here $Jw(t)=\int_0^tw(s)\,ds$.
TorusEuler.PaperMeanIntegratedSolution.c.summary: Identify the constant removed by the time projection

TorusEuler.PaperMeanIntegratedSolution.e.text: Let $T\ge0$, and let divergence-free $z,v,c$ be half-Hölder fields with continuous $v$, $z_t=v$ on $[0,T]$, and $z(0)=z(T)=0$. Suppose $Kv-J(\Omega v)+L=c+G$, where $G$ is the gradient of a differentiable periodic potential at each time. Then the same $v,c$ solve the projected endpoint equation and $z=Jv$ throughout the interval. This is a conversion of an already supplied solution, not an existence theorem for a prescribed source. Periodicity is essential for the Leray projection to remove the gradient. Here $Jw(t)=\int_0^tw(s)\,ds$.
TorusEuler.PaperMeanIntegratedSolution.e.summary: Preserve the displacement when removing its pressure gradient

TorusEuler.PaperMeanIntegratedSolution.e.text: Let $K,\Omega,L$ be time-continuous half-Hölder fields on $[0,T]\times\mathbb T^3$. Suppose continuous divergence-free $v$ and constant $c$ satisfy $\mathbb P(Kv-J(\Omega v)+L)=c$ and $Jv(T)=0$. Then there is a periodic potential $\phi(t,\cdot)$ of zero spatial mean whose gradient $G$ is continuous in time in $C^{0,1/2}$ and satisfies $Kv-J(\Omega v)+L=c+G$. Mean zero is integration over the unit torus. This recovers the pressure gradient in (4.9). The conclusion does not assert time differentiability of the scalar potential. Here $Jw(t)=\int_0^tw(s)\,ds$.
TorusEuler.PaperMeanIntegratedSolution.e.summary: Choose a periodic potential with zero spatial mean

TorusEuler.PaperMeanIntegratedSolution.o.text: Packages a continuous solenoidal velocity and constant as an integrated solution when the terminal primitive vanishes and the original equation holds with a periodic continuously differentiable potential $\varphi$. The represented gradient $\nabla\varphi$ is annihilated by the spatial projection. Thus the original pressure formulation supplies the exact projected field required by the inverse’s uniqueness theorem.
TorusEuler.PaperMeanIntegratedSolution.o.summary: A periodic pressure solution satisfies the projected equation

TorusEuler.PaperMeanIntegratedSolution.p.text: Suppose two integrated equations on $[0,T]$ use the same coefficients and source, their velocities agree on this interval, and their time-independent fields agree. If their remaining terms are $G_1$ and $G_2$, so that $Kv-J(\Omega v)+L=c+G_i$, then $G_1=G_2$ throughout $[0,T]$. This is the final algebraic step in pressure-gradient uniqueness for Theorems 4.2 and A.1. It assumes velocity uniqueness rather than proving it, and does not identify scalar potentials without a normalization. Here $Jw(t)=\int_0^tw(s)\,ds$.
TorusEuler.PaperMeanIntegratedSolution.p.summary: Subtract two integrated equations with identical velocities

TorusEuler.PaperMeanParent.text: On $[0,T]\times\mathbb T^3$, supply smooth matrix fields $F,M$, an inverse $G$ with $GF=FG=I$, and a continuous time derivative $M_t$. Require $F_t=MF$, $\|G\|\le D$, $\|M\|\le L$, and $\langle-(M_t+M^2)w,w\rangle\le|w|^2$ for every $w$. In §4 these are $F=D_aX$, $G=F^{-1}$ and $M=(\nabla u)\circ X$. The formal data themselves need not arise from any velocity or volume-preserving flow. They isolate the identities needed by the endpoint inverse; positivity of $T$ and bounds such as $D\ge1$ are imposed by theorems using them.
TorusEuler.PaperMeanParent.summary: Record the deformation equations and coercivity assumptions

TorusEuler.PaperMeanParent.exists_coeffi.text: For a physical parent with $0<T\le1$, $D\ge1$, and $L\ge0$, constructs the Hölder and path-space representations of its kinetic and vorticity coefficients. The parent provides inverse deformation, derivative identities, and the Hessian upper bound. Spatial ellipticity comes from the inverse-deformation bound; mixed coercivity comes from the displacement energy with both endpoint traces.
TorusEuler.PaperMeanParent.exists_coeffi.summary: Build both coefficient representations from the parent

TorusEuler.PaperMeanParent.exists_integr.text: Let $T>0$ and suppose smooth periodic $F,M$ satisfy $F_t=MF$, with inverse $G$, bounds $\|G\|\le D$, $\|M\|\le L$, and $-(M_t+M^2)\le I$. For a smooth periodic label force $f_{\mathrm{lab}}(t,a)$, there is a smooth curve $L:[0,T]\to C^{0,1/2}(\mathbb T^3)$ whose values are $L(t,a)=-\int_0^tF(s,a)^Tf_{\mathrm{lab}}(s,a)\,ds$. In Theorem 4.2 one first sets $f_{\mathrm{lab}}=f\circ X$. This construction does not itself perform that composition or solve the endpoint problem.
TorusEuler.PaperMeanParent.exists_integr.summary: Integrate a smooth force already written in particle labels

TorusEuler.PaperMeanParent.kinetic.text:
The kinetic coefficient in physical label coordinates.

The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.
TorusEuler.PaperMeanParent.kinetic.summary: The kinetic coefficient of the physical parent

TorusEuler.PaperMeanParent.vorticity.text:
The vorticity coefficient in physical label coordinates.

The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.
TorusEuler.PaperMeanParent.vorticity.summary: The vorticity coefficient of the physical parent

TorusEuler.PaperMeanPhysicalCoefficients.text: Packages Hölder time curves for the kinetic and vorticity coefficients, their mixed path operators, and exact evaluation and almost-everywhere action identities. It also records spatial and zero-time-mean coercivity with the physical constants determined by $D$ and $L$. These fields are obligations on the record: the structure is not itself an existence theorem, and all regularity claims are restricted to the closed slab.
TorusEuler.PaperMeanPhysicalCoefficients.summary: Represent the kinetic and vorticity coefficients

TorusEuler.PaperPhysicalStepBudget.text: Packages the inequalities needed to use the same step coefficient $\Gamma$ and exponent in the oscillation, residual, central-gradient, pressure and flow estimates. It requires $\Gamma\ge1$ and several explicit bounds built from the supplied costs and depth. This is a proposition of numerical compatibility, not a choice of $\Gamma$; the later existence theorem proves such a budget from its parameter hypotheses.
TorusEuler.PaperPhysicalStepBudget.summary: One numerical budget for all physical estimates

TorusEuler.PaperPhysicalStepBudget.hiera.text: Let $\mathsf D,\lambda\ge1$ and suppose the common step coefficient has been chosen to dominate all the specified costs, including $\Gamma_P\ge1$ and an exponent $b\ge6r$. If $\Gamma_P\mathsf D^b\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, then $(\mathsf D^r)^6\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$. This is the precise implication supplied by the formal statement behind the sentence after (5.43). The hierarchy uses loss $\mathsf D^r$ and hence its sixth power here. The assertion is a numerical consequence of the coefficient choice; it does not independently prove any hierarchy estimate or select the frequency.
TorusEuler.PaperPhysicalStepBudget.hiera.summary: The common coefficient dominates the sixth power of the hierarchy loss

TorusEuler.PaperSmoothMeanSolution.text: On $[0,T]$, let $F,M$ be smooth unit-periodic matrix fields, and let $G$ satisfy $GF=FG=I$. Assume $F_t=MF$, $\|G\|\le D$, $\|M\|\le L$, and $-(M_t+M^2)\le I$. Put $K=F^TF$, $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$. For a supplied label force $f_{\rm lab}$, a smooth mean solution consists of smooth unit-periodic fields $v,z,B,\mathsf q$ satisfying $z_t=v$, $z(0)=z(T)=0$, $\operatorname{div}_av=0$, $B=Fv$ and $B_t+MB+G^T\nabla_a\mathsf q=f_{\rm lab}$ on the closed interval. These are defining conditions, not an existence assertion. No spatial mean normalization of $\mathsf q$ is imposed. An actual flow is not part of these data. Only after separately identifying $F=D_aX$, $M=DU\circ X$ and $f_{\rm lab}=f\circ X$ may one interpret $Fz$ as particle displacement and $B\circ X^{-1}$ as the Eulerian correction.
TorusEuler.PaperSmoothMeanSolution.summary: The label displacement has zero values at both endpoints

TorusEuler.PaperSmoothMeanSolution.euler.text:
Let $u$ be a smooth periodic divergence-free parent on $[0,T]$, $T>0$, with flow $X$. Suppose a smooth periodic label solution has $z_t=v$, $z(0)=z(T)=0$, $\operatorname{div}_av=0$, $B=Fv$, and $B_t+MB+F^{-T}
abla_a\mathsf q=f_{\mathrm{lab}}$, with $F=D_aX$, $M=(
abla u)\circ X$. Its coefficient data also carry the inverse, gradient and $H^\#\le I$ bounds. Then $b=B\circ X^{-1}$ and $q=\mathsf q\circ X^{-1}$ are smooth periodic fields, $\operatorname{div}b=0$, and $b_t+u\cdot
abla b+b\cdot
abla u+
abla q=f_{\mathrm{lab}}\circ X^{-1}$. Recovering the paper's $f$ requires $f_{\mathrm{lab}}=f\circ X$.
TorusEuler.PaperSmoothMeanSolution.euler.summary: Push a smooth label solution through the actual flow

TorusEuler.PaperSmoothMeanSolution.exist.text: Let $T>0$. Suppose smooth periodic matrix fields $F,M$ satisfy $F_t=MF$, have a bounded inverse, and satisfy the gradient and upper displacement-Hessian bounds used by the mean inverse. Let a smooth periodic label solution satisfy $z_t=v$, $z(0)=z(T)=0$, $\operatorname{div}_av=0$ and $B_t+MB+F^{-T}\nabla_a\mathsf q=f_{\mathrm{lab}}$, with $B=Fv$. For a smooth half-Hölder source equal to $-J(F^Tf_{\mathrm{lab}})$, this solution satisfies $\mathbb P(Kv-J(\Omega v)+L)=c$ for some time-independent solenoidal $c$, with exactly the same label velocity. The coefficient representatives must equal $F^TF$ and $F^T(M^T-M)F$. This is a compatibility result for an existing solution. Here $Jw(t)=\int_0^tw(s)\,ds$.
TorusEuler.PaperSmoothMeanSolution.exist.summary: Identify its velocity with the projected endpoint solution

TorusEuler.PaperSmoothMeanSolution.mean_.text: Let $0<T\le1$ and suppose the smooth periodic parent coefficients satisfy $F_t=MF$, $G=F^{-1}$, $\|G\|\le D$ with $D\ge1$, $\|M\|\le L$ with $L\ge0$, and $-(M_t+M^2)\le I$ as quadratic forms. For the same smooth periodic forcing, take two smooth mean solutions with label displacements zero at both $0$ and $T$. The formal statement proves equality of their pulled-back physical means $B=Fz_t$ for every time in $[0,T]$. Hence their initial corrections agree. It compares existing solutions on the same interval; it does not establish existence or identify scalar pressures, whose additive time-dependent constants remain free.
TorusEuler.PaperSmoothMeanSolution.mean_.summary: Two smooth mean solutions have the same pulled-back velocity

TorusEuler.PaperSmoothMeanSolution.stron.text: Suppose smooth periodic $F,M$ obey $F_t=MF$, $G=F^{-1}$, the inverse and gradient bounds, and $-(M_t+M^2)\le I$ on $[0,T]$, $T>0$. Let a smooth periodic mean solution have $B=Fv$, zero endpoint displacement, divergence-free $v$, and $B_t+MB+G^T\nabla_a\mathsf q=f_{\mathrm{lab}}$. Then $Kv_t+\nabla_a\mathsf q=F^Tf_{\mathrm{lab}}-2F^TMFv$, with $K=F^TF$. Taking $f_{\mathrm{lab}}=f\circ X$ gives (4.11), since $2F^TMF=2F^TF_t$. The equation holds at each time, using derivatives from within the closed interval at its endpoints.
TorusEuler.PaperSmoothMeanSolution.stron.summary: Write the differentiated equation in the label velocity

TorusEuler.PaperTerminalOffOrigin.text: For a field $u$ and terminal time $T$, this condition requires a local $C^m$ limit for each of $u(t)$ and its time derivative, for every integer $m\ge0$ and compact $K\subset\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3$. A local limit means a $C^m$ field on an open neighbourhood of $K$ and uniform convergence on $K$ of every spatial derivative through order $m$ as $t\uparrow T$ within $[0,T)$. The lattice is the set of representatives of the torus origin. The time derivative is defined relative to the half-open lifespan. Positivity of $T$ and the Euler equations are imposed elsewhere. This condition states the two limits of Proposition 8.4 without supplying existence or a smooth continuation.
TorusEuler.PaperTerminalOffOrigin.summary: Define both local terminal limits without asserting time extension

TorusEuler.PaperTerminalTime.text: For prescribed $T,u,p$, this condition requires a smooth periodic Euler solution on $[0,T)$, with $0<T<\infty$ and mean-zero pressure, admitting no longer smooth Euler solution whose velocity agrees there. It also requires $\int_0^T\|\operatorname{curl}u(t)\|_\infty\,dt=\infty$ and $\int_0^T\|\nabla u(t)\|_\infty\,dt=\infty$. These are nonnegative Lebesgue integrals; spatial norms are essential suprema over the unit cell, and the gradient uses its operator norm. The condition does not itself identify $T$ with a limit of activation times or prove its existence. Those identifications are made when all Section 8 conclusions are established for one construction.
TorusEuler.PaperTerminalTime.summary: Require maximal Euler evolution and divergence of both time integrals

TorusEuler.PaperTerminalVelocityCurl.text: For a given field $u$ and real time $T$, this condition records a single finite bound for the essential supremum of $|u(t,x)|$ over $x\in[-1/2,1/2]^3$, valid for every $0\le t<T$. It also records $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\to\infty$ as $t\uparrow T$ within that interval: every prescribed threshold is exceeded at all sufficiently late times. In the periodic Euler application the cell represents $\mathbb T^3$ and $T=T_\infty>0$. The condition alone supplies neither positivity of $T$, periodicity, nor the Euler equations. Unlike the enlarged formal Proposition 8.2 conclusions, it contains no quantitative lower bound indexed by activation intervals.
TorusEuler.PaperTerminalVelocityCurl.summary: Specify a uniform velocity bound and full central vorticity blow-up

TorusEuler.PaperTheorem71Conclusions.text: For a given scheduled construction, this condition records smooth odd divergence-free periodic velocities $U_j$ on $[0,S_j]$, starting from the stationary sine shear. Residuals are bounded by $\lambda_{j+1}^{-3}$, Fourier support by $2\lambda_j^5$, and pressure Hessians above by $\sum_{i<j}\lambda_i^{-1}$ times the identity. It records the central gradient as the preceding gradient plus a switched rank-one wave and an error bounded by $\lambda_j^{-1/4}$. Crossing times have the prescribed coupling ratios and shear bounds and tend to a finite positive $T<S_j$. Oscillations are supported within distance $\lambda_{j-1}^{-1}$ of lattice points and bounded by $\lambda_j^{-1}$; the remaining increments are small in spatial $C^{m,1/2}$ for $m\le q_j$. This specifies conclusions for a construction; it does not assert existence.
TorusEuler.PaperTheorem71Conclusions.summary: One sequence satisfies support, error, crossing and lifetime bounds

TorusEuler.PaperWaveCutoff.text: The formal object is a real function $\widetilde\chi$ that is smooth on $[0,T]$, takes values in $[0,1]$ there, and vanishes at times $t<t_0$ within that interval. It encodes the cutoff in (3.7). The function is defined at all real times, but no restriction is imposed outside $[0,T]$, and no condition says that it eventually reaches one. For $0<t_0<T$, smoothness and vanishing to the left give flatness at activation. The first wave is treated separately by choosing $t_0=0$ and the constant function one.
TorusEuler.PaperWaveCutoff.summary: The cutoff is constrained only on the construction interval

TorusEuler.PaperWaveCutoff.abs_le_one.text: At every time in the slab, the absolute value of a time cutoff in the sense of the paper is at most one. Its bundled range already gives both nonnegativity and an upper bound by one, so this theorem is a convenient consequence. It does not prove that the cutoff ever reaches one or has a nonzero derivative.
TorusEuler.PaperWaveCutoff.abs_le_one.summary: The cutoff has absolute value at most one

TorusEuler.PaperWaveCutoff.derivative.text: Defines the cutoff derivative as the derivative within $[0,T]$. This is the time domain on which the cutoff has bundled smoothness. It therefore includes a consistent endpoint derivative when $T>0$, rather than requiring any arbitrary continuation outside the slab to be differentiable.
TorusEuler.PaperWaveCutoff.derivative.summary: The activation derivative on the closed slab

TorusEuler.PaperWaveCutoff.derivativeSiz.text: For a smooth cutoff $\widetilde\chi$ on $[0,T]$, define the real supremum $\sup_{t\in[t_0,T]}|\widetilde\chi\,{}^{\prime}(t)|\gamma(t)$. The derivative is taken within $[0,T]$, including its one-sided values at the endpoints. If $0\le t_0\le T$, $T>0$, and $\gamma$ is continuous and nonnegative, compactness makes this a finite nonnegative number, equal to the quantity $\|\widetilde\chi\,{}^{\prime}\gamma\|_\infty$ in (5.48). The definition alone does not assume those properties of $\gamma$; with signed weights it is a supremum of the displayed product, not its absolute value. The formal real supremum has a default value when the set is empty or unbounded, so boundedness is established before using it as a norm.
TorusEuler.PaperWaveCutoff.derivativeSiz.summary: Take the activation supremum on the active time interval

TorusEuler.PaperWaveCutoff.derivativeSiz.text: For $T>0$ and $0\le t_0\le T$, a continuous nonnegative weight $\gamma$ makes the weighted supremum $\sup_{t\in[t_0,T]}|\chi'(t)|\gamma(t)$ nonnegative and bounds every $|\chi'(t)|\gamma(t)$ on the active interval. Compactness supplies boundedness and the interval is nonempty. These conditions make the real supremum a genuine maximum-type bound instead of relying on a default value.
TorusEuler.PaperWaveCutoff.derivativeSiz.summary: The activation supremum bounds every weighted derivative

TorusEuler.PaperWaveCutoff.derivative_fi.text: The within-time derivative of the first-wave cutoff is identically zero for every real $T$ and evaluation time. That cutoff is the constant function one, so the derivative convention, which assigns a value even where no unique derivative exists, gives zero even for a degenerate slab. This is the scalar reason that the first wave has no activation residual.
TorusEuler.PaperWaveCutoff.derivative_fi.summary: The first wave has no activation derivative

TorusEuler.PaperWaveCutoff.derivative_sm.text: For $T>0$, the cutoff’s within-time derivative is infinitely smooth on $[0,T]$. Smoothness of the cutoff is bundled, and the nondegenerate interval supplies unique differentiation. The conclusion is restricted to the closed slab; it does not assert that the chosen total derivative function is smooth across its exterior endpoints.
