Pressure is normalized to have zero mean. The numbered version of Theorem 1.1 additionally states uniqueness of the maximal velocity and its lifespan. That comparison is not an explicit conjunct of this shorter assertion.
TorusEuler.Theorem11.summary: The shorter assertion collects the singularity conclusions

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.text: A truncated stage supplies continuous torus representatives of $V$ and $R_V$, a velocity $u=S_\Lambda V$, and a smooth periodic pressure $p$ of zero spatial mean on $[0,T]$. It requires $u$ smooth, odd and divergence free, with Fourier support $|\xi|\le2\Lambda$, and $\Delta p=-\operatorname{tr}((\nabla u)^2)$. Its actual momentum residual is identified both with $u_t+\mathbb P\operatorname{div}(u\otimes u)$ and with the cutoff expression in (5.58). These are conditions on the supplied objects, not an existence proof. A separate theorem constructs them from an approximate solution. No vanishing residual or quantitative cutoff error is part of this declaration.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.summary: Record the cutoff fields and their exact residual relation

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.CutoffBou.text: Bundles all spatial tail estimates $\|u-V\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\le K\Lambda^{m-P}\|V\|_{C^{P,1/2}}$ for $m\le P$, the order-two tail estimate, the order-one true residual estimate, and the order-zero pressure-Hessian difference estimate. All are pointwise in time on the child slab. A common pair of constants $C,K$ controls the residual and pressure; the error $\Lambda^{2-P}(1+\|V(t)\|_{C^{P,1/2}})^2$ uses the spatial norm of that time slice.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.CutoffBou.summary: The cutoff tail residual and pressure estimates together

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.PulledBac.text: Records joint smoothness of the parent-coframe pullback after adding the actual cutoff tail. The oscillatory part has a scaled jet bound through order two of size $B \cdot  D^p \cdot  \mathrm{freq}^{-5/4}$; the phase mean has a bound through order one of size $B \cdot  D^p \cdot  \mathrm{freq}^{-5/2}$. These measured hypotheses feed the child-flow estimate.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.PulledBac.summary: Measured jets of the corrected pulled back profile

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.PulledBac.text: Let $s$ be a truncated-child stage on $[0,T]$ with uncut velocity $V$ and cutoff bounds at depth $P\ge2$ with constants $C,K$; let $X$ be the label flow of a smooth periodic $U$ on $[0,T]$ with $T>0$, $V$ and the profile $W(t,x,r)$ smooth, $|\ell|\le1$, $\|D X(0,t,\cdot)\|,\|DX(t,0,\cdot)\|\le\mathsf D$, the first derivative of $x\mapsto D X(t,0,X(0,t,x))$ bounded by $D_1$, and $K$ times the truncation error at most $\varepsilon$. Suppose the uncut pulled-back profile $DX(t,0,X(0,t,x))\,W(t,x,r)$ has scaled phase oscillation with derivatives of order at most two bounded by $B\mathsf D^p\lambda^{-5/4}$, scaled phase mean with derivatives of order at most one bounded by $M$, and $M+\max\{\mathsf D,\mathsf D^2+D_1\}\varepsilon\le B\mathsf D^p\lambda^{-5/2}$. Then the profile corrected by the cutoff tail $s(t)-V(t)$ is smooth and satisfies the same oscillation bound and the mean bound $B\mathsf D^p\lambda^{-5/2}$. The tail is phase independent, so it changes only the mean.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.PulledBac.summary: The cutoff tail changes only the pulled-back mean

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.cutoffTai.text: Combines certified cutoff bounds with smooth solenoidal approximate velocity to show that the actual tail is jointly smooth, periodic and solenoidal on the slab. Its order-two half-Hölder norm is at most the current frequency to power minus five-halves, provided the next-frequency error budget and frequency ordering hold. The smallness is an assumption-backed estimate on the actual difference field.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.cutoffTai.summary: The cutoff tail satisfies the child flow assumptions

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.divergenc.text: For a positive slab and a time in it, shows that the actual child residual has zero divergence at every spatial point. The child record supplies the Poisson equation, smoothness and velocity solenoidality needed by the general cancellation theorem. This is a derived property of the constructed pressure and velocity.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.divergenc.summary: The constructed pressure cancels residual divergence

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.exists_ch.text: Produces a flow for the actual cutoff velocity with deformation bounded by $\Gamma \cdot  D^b \cdot  \mathrm{freq}^{1/4}$. Its hypotheses include the physical profile identity, incompressible parent and profile, cutoff-tail control, corrected profile jet bounds, and the scale smallness condition $\Gamma \cdot  D^b \cdot  \mathrm{freq}^{-1/12} \le  1$. The proof applies the scaled-flow theorem to the same cutoff tail, then rewrites the velocity identity.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.exists_ch.summary: The actual cutoff velocity has controlled deformation

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.exists_cu.text: For a fixed smooth normalized cutoff symbol, chooses a nonnegative constant $C$ before choosing the depth. For each $P\ge2$ it then chooses a nonnegative $K$, uniformly over all positive slabs, scales $\Lambda\ge1$ and admissible approximate stages. The actual approximate momentum equation and solenoidality supply the pressure estimate. These quantifiers prevent the residual constant from secretly depending on expansion depth.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.exists_cu.summary: One residual constant works across all expansion depths

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.exists_de.text: Chooses one threshold independent of the child. Above it, a child cut off at the fifth power of its frequency, with the prescribed velocity and residual bounds on a positive slab, has spatial derivative norm at most frequency to the ninth power and within-slab time derivative of that spatial derivative at most frequency to the eighteenth power.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.exists_de.summary: Large cutoff parents satisfy the two low derivative estimates

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.odd_resid.text: On a positive slab with nonnegative cutoff radius, derives oddness of the true child residual at every slab time. The proof first obtains the matching finite-band projected data and then applies the parity theorem. Thus the residual symmetry follows from the same child velocity and pressure that define its momentum equation.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.odd_resid.summary: The actual truncated child has an odd residual

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.periodic_.text: For a time belonging to the child slab, proves spatial periodicity of its actual momentum residual. The within-slab time derivative respects the velocity periodicity throughout the interval, while spatial derivatives use smooth periodic slices. Pressure periodicity is taken from the same stage record at that time.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.periodic_.summary: The child residual is periodic on its slab

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.periodic_.text: Proves spatial periodicity of the physical child velocity for every real time, including times outside the certified slab. This follows from the quotient map and the stored torus field. The unconditional periodicity statement should not be extended to smoothness or the momentum equation outside the slab.

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.phaseJetB.text: Add two first-order bounds for differentiable profiles.

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.pressureH.text: Let $p,q$ be smooth periodic scalar functions on $\mathbb R^3$ and suppose $\|D^2(p-q)\|_{C^{0,1/2}}\le B$. Then at every point and for every vector $v$, $v\cdot D^2p\,v\le v\cdot D^2q\,v+B|v|^2$. Thus $D^2p\le D^2q+BI$ as quadratic forms. Periodicity ensures the relevant Hölder norm is finite. This is the passage used in §5.7 to add the cutoff pressure error to the upper bound for the approximate pressure. The statement does not itself bound $D^2q$, choose either pressure, or assert a two-sided bound on $D^2p$.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.pressureH.summary: A norm estimate transfers an upper quadratic form bound

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.residual.text: For the truncated velocity $u$ and its smooth periodic zero-mean Poisson pressure $p$, define $R_u(t,x)=\partial_tu(t,x)+(u(t,x)\cdot\nabla)u(t,x)+\nabla p(t,x)$. The time derivative is taken within $[0,T]$, so the values at $0$ and $T$ use one-sided derivatives on that interval. This is the residual in Proposition 5.11. The same chosen fields carry identities expressing it through the Leray projection and cutoff tensors. The definition alone does not assert $R_u=0$, a norm bound, or a Fourier support bound; those are separate properties or estimates of the truncated stage.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.residual.summary: Use the actual momentum error of the chosen truncated fields

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.residual_.text: For a positive slab and nonnegative cutoff radius, constructs torus representatives of the child residual and its advection at a slab time. It records residual Fourier support within $4\Lambda$, exact physical representation, and the projected within-slab derivative equation. These same representatives feed the later Bernstein and low-derivative estimates.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.residual_.summary: The child exposes its actual finite-band evolution data

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.scheduled.text: Under the listed schedule inequalities, exact child-flow deformation, parent and oscillation bounds, correction and cutoff budgets, and approximate-pressure comparison, proves the child velocity and flow bounds, the next-frequency residual bound, and the cumulative one-sided pressure-Hessian bound. The pressure conclusion controls quadratic forms from above; it is not a two-sided operator-norm estimate.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.scheduled.summary: The actual child inherits velocity residual and pressure bounds

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.scheduled.text: Assumes an exact split of the approximate velocity into parent, oscillation and mean, together with scheduled mean bounds and the cutoff error budget. Through each order $m\le q$, bounds the child minus parent minus oscillation in $C^{m,1/2}$ by the inverse child frequency. The depth must cover $q$, and frequency and constant inequalities are explicit hypotheses.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.scheduled.summary: The remaining child increment fits the inverse frequency budget

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.slabTimeJ.text: Let $T>0$, $\lambda\ge2$, and let $V$ be smooth and periodic on the closed slab. Use the fixed cutoff of the selected construction at $\Lambda=\lambda^5$. At a given time, assume $\|\partial_t^iV\|_{C^{0,1/2}}\le\lambda^{2+\psi}$ and that one plus the order-zero cutoff constant is at most $\lambda$. The formal statement proves $|\partial_t^i(S_\Lambda V)(t,x)|\le\lambda^{\psi+3}$ for every $x$. The exponent $\psi$ may be any real number. Endpoint derivatives are taken within the slab. This is the velocity estimate used to finish auxiliary Lemma 1.3, conditional on the approximate-velocity bound; it does not establish the residual estimate.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.slabTimeJ.summary: The cutoff loses one additional frequency power

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.slabTimeJ.text: For a truncated child with positive $T,\Lambda$, assume the slab identity $V=U+O+M$, smooth $V,M$, and periodic $V$. At a slab time, $m\le d$ and spatial $C^{m,1/2}$ regularity of $\partial_t^qM$ give the child's omitted increment $\partial_t^q(u-U-O)$ spatial $C^{m,1/2}$ regularity and a norm bound $\|\partial_t^qM\|_{C^{m,1/2}}+C_d\Lambda^{m-d}\|\partial_t^qV\|_{C^{d,1/2}}$, the mean time-derivative norm plus the order-$d$ Fourier tail bound for $V$. The exact time derivative within the slab is used at the endpoints. Separate smoothness of $U,O$ is unnecessary because the combined difference is rewritten first.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.slabTimeJ.summary: Split the omitted increment into mean and cutoff tail

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.slabTimeJ.text: Let $V=U+O+M$ on $[0,T]$, where $T>0$, $V$ is smooth and periodic, and $M$ is smooth. Use the selected cutoff at $\Lambda=\lambda^5$, with $\lambda\ge2$. Fix integers $q,m,P$ with $m\le P$, and assume $5m+5+\psi\le3P$, the order-$P$ cutoff constant is at most $\lambda$, and $\|\partial_t^qV\|_{C^{P,1/2}}\le\lambda^{2(P+1)+\psi}$. If $\partial_t^qM$ has finite spatial Hölder norm at most $\tfrac12\lambda^{-1}$, the formal statement proves finiteness and the bound $\|\partial_t^q(S_\Lambda V-U-O)\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\le\lambda^{-1}$. This is a pointwise-in-time estimate on the closed slab. Continuity in the spatial norm is a separate assertion in the full auxiliary lemma.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.slabTimeJ.summary: Two half-size bounds give the required increment

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.slabTimeJ.text: Let $V,R_V$ be smooth on a positive closed time slab and let every time derivative have the specified continuous periodic representative. Fix a spatial cutoff $S_\Lambda$ independent of time. The formal statement gives $\partial_t^qR_j=\mathbb P[S_\Lambda\partial_t^qR_V+\operatorname{div}\sum_{i=0}^q\binom qi E_\Lambda(\partial_t^iV,\partial_t^{q-i}V)]$, where $E_\Lambda(f,g)=(S_\Lambda f)\otimes(S_\Lambda g)-S_\Lambda(f\otimes g)$. Time derivatives fix the physical point and are taken within the slab. This formula includes all nonnegative orders, and at order zero its tensor difference rearranges into the three terms displayed in the auxiliary note. It is an identity, not a bound on the residual. The theorem does not assume that the cutoff commutes with an arbitrary time-dependent symbol.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.slabTimeJ.summary: The quadratic cutoff error differentiates by the binomial rule

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.slabTimeJ.text: Let $V$ be smooth on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3$, with $T>0$, and suppose each time derivative is represented by the specified continuous field on $\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3$. For a fixed cutoff symbol and fixed scale $\Lambda$, the formal statement proves $\partial_t^q(S_\Lambda V)=S_\Lambda(\partial_t^qV)$ at every time of the closed interval and every spatial point. It applies to all nonnegative integers $q$. The derivative is taken within the slab, so the endpoint values are one-sided. The paper writes the corresponding identity for $(S_\Lambda-\operatorname{Id})V$; that form also requires subtracting $\partial_t^qV$. No estimate or Fourier-tail decay is part of this identity.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.slabTimeJ.summary: A fixed spatial cutoff commutes with time derivatives

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.slabTimeJ.text: Let $V$ be smooth and periodic on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3$, with $T>0$, and use the fixed cutoff of the selected construction at any scale $\Lambda>0$. For integers $q,m,P\ge0$ with $m\le P$, the formal statement proves $\|\partial_t^q(S_\Lambda-\operatorname{Id})V(t)\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\le C_P\Lambda^{m-P}\|\partial_t^qV(t)\|_{C^{P,1/2}}$ at every time in the closed interval, together with finiteness of the output norm. The exponent $m-P$ is an integer difference and may be negative. The fixed constant depends on $P$ and the chosen cutoff, not the time derivative order. The spatial $C^{m,1/2}$ norm is $\sum_{i\le m}(\sup|D^if|+[D^if]_{1/2})$, where $D^if$ is the full $i$th derivative tensor in operator norm.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.slabTimeJ.summary: A higher spatial norm controls the truncation error

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.smooth_re.text: On a positive closed slab, the child record supplies joint smoothness of velocity and pressure, and the actual momentum formula then gives joint smoothness of its residual. Positivity permits differentiation within the time interval at endpoints. This statement certifies the true residual rather than an independently chosen smooth proxy.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.smooth_re.summary: The true child residual is jointly smooth

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.truncatio.text:
The slice form of the truncation error in (5.56).

Negative integer powers of Λ are totalized at zero. The actual truncation estimates use positive Λ, finite spatial norms and the required order P.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.truncatio.summary: The velocity error caused by Fourier truncation

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.truncatio.text: At cutoff radius equal to the fifth power of the child frequency, uses depth six times the following exponent to bound the weighted truncation error by the next frequency to power minus five. It requires base scale at least two, positive exponent parameter, $K\le\mu$ for the base scale $\mu$, half-Hölder regularity of the input through that full depth and the explicit full-depth size bound.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.truncatio.summary: Full expansion depth absorbs the cutoff constants

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.velocity.text: Defines the child velocity on Euclidean space by lifting its stored continuous torus velocity. This is the physical function on which gradients, material acceleration and the true momentum residual are evaluated. The definition exists at all real times, while the stage record certifies its analytic properties only on the closed slab.

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.velocity_.text: Identifies the Euclidean child velocity with the real Fourier cutoff of its own stored approximate torus velocity. This equality holds at every real time because the cutoff identity is a field of the stage record. Agreement of the approximate torus field with the original physical velocity is separately restricted to the slab.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.velocity_.summary: The physical child is the cutoff of its input

TorusEuler.UniformPhysicalEstimates.text: States that for every strength constant at least two, nonnegative envelope constant and requested radius floor, one can choose exponents, costs and an initial-frequency floor. Those choices then produce scheduled dyadic-cutoff stages for every admissible first or later input satisfying its numerical budget. This quantifier order is essential: the costs are uniform before the parameter schedule and stage are supplied.
TorusEuler.UniformPhysicalEstimates.summary: Uniform stage estimates are chosen before the schedule

TorusEuler.Vec3.text:
The paper’s real vector space $\mathbb R^3$ is the Euclidean space of real vectors indexed by the three-element set $\{0,1,2\}$. A vector has coordinates indexed by 0, 1 and 2, while the paper numbers coordinates 1, 2 and 3. The Euclidean norm and inner product are built into this space; a space vector, a velocity value and a wave vector use the same space. This abbreviation does not impose periodicity or encode a quotient torus.

No partial analytic operation occurs. The three dimensional space is nonempty and has its usual nondegenerate Euclidean norm; there is no empty index set or variable dimension.

This is a concrete Euclidean space abbreviation. It contains zero vectors as well as nonzero ones; nonvanishing is always a separate wave hypothesis.

TorusEuler.Velocity.text:
A velocity field is a function $u:\mathbb R\to(\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3)$ defined at every input. The first argument is time and the second is position, so $u\,t\,x$ means $u(t,x)$. Values outside the physical time interval exist but are unconstrained by this abbreviation. Periodicity, smoothness and the Euler equation are supplied separately by the conditions for a classical Euler solution on $[0,T)$.

The function type is unrestricted. It admits discontinuous, nonperiodic and zero fields. No derivative or norm is evaluated here; interpreting an arbitrary velocity field as a classical Euler solution would require hypotheses not present in the abbreviation.

This is a completely unrestricted function type. It alone provides no regularity, periodicity, incompressibility or solution property.
TorusEuler.Velocity.summary: Velocity as a function of time and position

TorusEuler.abs_fixedOrderCost_le_thresho.text: Let $c_k(m,p)$ be any finite family of real numbers depending on nonnegative integer derivative order $m$ and expansion depth $p$. Put $K(s)=320b(s+1)$ and let $\mathcal B(s)$ be the maximum of $e^{4K(s+1)^3}$ and the sum of $|c_k(m,p)|$ over all indices with $m,p\le7K(s)$. The formal theorem proves $|c_k(m,p)|\le\mathcal B(s)$ for every entry in those ranges. No positivity or monotonicity of the cost table is assumed. This gives the arithmetic domination used in §1.5, including order and depth zero. Identification of the table entries with the paper’s analytic estimates remains a separate requirement.
TorusEuler.abs_fixedOrderCost_le_thresho.summary: The finite cost sum bounds every required entry

TorusEuler.abs_oscillatoryPressureSlope_.text: For nonzero $\kappa$, the pressure-slope magnitude is bounded by $(\|f\|+2\|M\|\|V\|)/\|\kappa\|$. Cauchy–Schwarz bounds the two inner products in its numerator, cancelling one factor of the wave-vector norm. This is a pointwise algebraic estimate; integrating the slope and imposing phase normalization require additional hypotheses.
TorusEuler.abs_oscillatoryPressureSlope_.summary: The phase pressure slope loses one wave-vector factor

TorusEuler.abs_terminalGraphCost_le_enve.text: For any cost table, row and orders $q,A,m,d$, $|\mathrm{cost}(\mathrm{row},q,A,m,d)|\le\sum_{q'=0}^{s}\sum_{A'=0}^{s}|\mathrm{cost}(\mathrm{row},q',A',m,d)|$ with $s=\max(q,A)$. The comparison involves no construction, frequency or regularity.
TorusEuler.abs_terminalGraphCost_le_enve.summary: A graph cost fits the envelope at its largest order

TorusEuler.absolutelyContinuousOnInterva.text: On a nonnegative-length interval, the anchored primitive of an interval-integrable velocity is absolutely continuous. This is stronger than ordinary continuity and permits integration by parts with other absolutely continuous paths. No pointwise continuity of the velocity is assumed, which is necessary for the weak endpoint formulation.
TorusEuler.absolutelyContinuousOnInterva.summary: An integrable velocity produces an absolutely continuous displacement

TorusEuler.activationGrowthRate_bounds.text: Let $\mu>0$, $L\ge0$, and let $c,C>0$ satisfy $c\mu^{1/4}\le\sigma\le C\mu^{1/4}L^2$ and $\pi\le\nu\le4\pi$. The formal statement proves $\sqrt{2c\pi}\,\mu^{1/8}\le r\le\sqrt{8C\pi}\,\mu^{1/8}L$, where $r=\sqrt{2\sigma\nu}$. Thus the unspecified constants in the growth-rate bound of §7.2 can be expressed in terms of the constants in the strength bounds. This is an inequality for positive real parameters; it does not establish that a particular wave has those strength and coupling bounds. Those must already be supplied at activation.
TorusEuler.activationGrowthRate_bounds.summary: Converts strength and coupling bounds into an activation rate

TorusEuler.activationLifetime_tail.text: If a nonnegative lifetime sequence satisfies $4\tau_{j+1}\le\tau_j$, each shifted sequence is summable and its sum is at most $4\tau_j/3$. Strict positivity is unnecessary, so the conclusion includes zero lifetimes. The theorem bounds tails of the supplied sequence; it neither constructs activation times nor proves that individual increments equal these lifetimes.
TorusEuler.activationLifetime_tail.summary: Geometric lifetime decay controls every remaining lifetime

TorusEuler.activationTimes_converge.text: Let $t_j$ be real times with $t_0\ge0$, and let $\tau_j>0$ satisfy $4\tau_{j+1}\le\tau_j$. Assume $0\le t_{j+1}-t_j\le\tau_j$ and that, after every index $j$, some time is strictly larger than $t_j$. Then there is $T_\infty>0$ with $t_j\to T_\infty$, $0<T_\infty-t_j\le4\tau_j/3$ and $T_\infty<t_j+2\tau_j$ for every $j$. Strict increase at every step is not required; the last hypothesis excludes an eventually constant sequence. The statement is an abstract result about times and needs no Euler fields. The explicit comparison with $\sum_{p\ge j}\tau_p$ occurs in the proof, not in its conclusion.
TorusEuler.activationTimes_converge.summary: Geometrically decreasing gaps leave room before every endpoint

TorusEuler.activation_interval_weight_lo.text: For positive $L$, $C$, and rate $r$, the bounds $2L^2\le r(t_{stop}-t_{start})$ and $r\le C\mu^{1/8}L$ imply $t_{start}<t_{stop}$ and $(2/C)L\le\mu^{1/8}(t_{stop}-t_{start})$. Positivity of $\mu$ is not an explicit hypothesis; the conclusion follows from the stated positive constants and compatible inequalities.
TorusEuler.activation_interval_weight_lo.summary: The clock and rate bounds force positive weighted duration

TorusEuler.activeTimeJet.text: For a field $f(t,x)$ with $x$ in any parameter space, an interval $[a,b]$ and an order $i$, this is the $i$th time derivative within $[a,b]$ of $u\mapsto f(u,x)$ at time $t$, with $x$ held fixed. No smoothness is assumed by the definition itself.
TorusEuler.activeTimeJet.summary: Time derivatives with label and phase held fixed

TorusEuler.activeTimeJet_bilinear_phaseJ.text: Let $B$ be a continuous bilinear map with $\|B\|\le1$, $a<b$, $t\in[a,b]$, and $f,g$ jointly smooth on $[a,b]\times X$. If for every $j\le i$ the $j$th time derivatives of $f$ and $g$ at $t$ have all parameter derivatives through order $n$ bounded by $A\ge0$ and $C\ge0$, then the $i$th time derivative of $B(f,g)$ at $t$ has all parameter derivatives through order $n$ bounded by $2^i\,2^n\,AC$. The bounds may depend on $t$.
TorusEuler.activeTimeJet_bilinear_phaseJ.summary: Time and parameter product derivatives have binomial bounds

TorusEuler.activeTimeJet_homogeneous_pha.text: Let $a<b$, $t\in[a,b]$, let $f$ and $A$ be jointly smooth on $[a,b]\times X$, and suppose $\partial_tf(u,x)=A(u,x)f(u,x)$ within $[a,b]$ for all $u\in[a,b]$ and $x$. If $B,C\ge0$, the time derivatives of $A$ through order $q$ at $t$ have parameter derivatives through order $n$ bounded by $B$, and $f(t)$ has them bounded by $C$, then for each $i\le q$ the $i$th time derivative of $f$ at $t$ has parameter derivatives through order $n$ bounded by $C(1+2^q2^nB)^i$.
TorusEuler.activeTimeJet_homogeneous_pha.summary: A homogeneous equation bounds all chosen time derivatives

TorusEuler.activeTimeJet_zero.text: The order-zero active time derivative is exactly the original field, as an equality of functions. No structure on the parameter space or interval is needed beyond the displayed function types. This algebraic identity starts the regularity and homogeneous-equation inductions for the leading wave; it is not a claim about any positive derivative order.
TorusEuler.activeTimeJet_zero.summary: Zero active time derivatives give the original field

TorusEuler.actualJetValues_add_le.text: Summing two smooth fields adds the supremum bounds of the same derivative word.
TorusEuler.actualJetValues_add_le.summary: Derivative suprema obey the triangle inequality

TorusEuler.actualJetValues_smul.text: For smooth directions and smooth time slices, multiplying the field by a real scalar sends its entire measurement set to the scalar norm times the original set. This includes the zero sample, pointwise jet norms, and optional half-Hölder quotients. The equality also handles the zero scalar.
TorusEuler.actualJetValues_smul.summary: Scaling a field scales every measured derivative value

TorusEuler.add_gradient_truncatedParentS.text: For a finite-band torus field with smooth Euclidean lift, identifies the lift plus the constructed pressure gradient with its actual periodic Leray projection. The proof shows the sum is solenoidal and uses that the projection fixes solenoidal fields and kills periodic gradients. This is an exact field identity, not merely equality of Fourier support.
TorusEuler.add_gradient_truncatedParentS.summary: Adding the pressure gradient gives the Leray projection

TorusEuler.add_hierarchyLatticeShift.text: Adding the lattice-shift vector preserves time, translates the label by an integer vector and translates phase by its pairing with k. This is the coordinate formula for twisted periodicity.

TorusEuler.add_hierarchyLatticeShift_mem.text: Adding the carrier-dependent lattice shift preserves membership in the profile slab, because its time component is zero. Both label and phase coordinates may change. The equivalence is used to transfer twisted periodicity across zero-extension representatives and to keep derivative evaluations in the same closed domain.
TorusEuler.add_hierarchyLatticeShift_mem.summary: A twisted translation preserves the time-slab condition

TorusEuler.add_hierarchyPhasePeriod.text: Adding the unit phase vector $(0,0,1)$ to a joint point leaves time and label unchanged and adds one to the phase. This coordinate identity converts periodicity of the whole representative into unit periodicity of a phase slice. It is an algebraic statement independent of the slab or any profile.
TorusEuler.add_hierarchyPhasePeriod.summary: A period changes only the phase coordinate

TorusEuler.add_hierarchyPhasePeriod_mem_.text: A point belongs to the profile slab $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ exactly when the point translated by one phase period does. The slab restricts time alone, so phase translation cannot change membership. This equivalence allows periodicity proofs to use the same zero-extension branch at both points.
TorusEuler.add_hierarchyPhasePeriod_mem_.summary: A phase period preserves the time-slab condition

TorusEuler.adjoint_vorticityForm.text: The adjoint of the pulled-back vorticity coefficient is its negative. This algebraic fact holds for arbitrary deformation and gradient operators.
TorusEuler.adjoint_vorticityForm.summary: Skew symmetry of the vorticity coefficient

TorusEuler.ae_endpointMixedCoefficient_s.text: When joint, mixed and fixed-time coefficient descriptions agree almost everywhere and satisfy the stated measurability and bound hypotheses, a spatial slice of the embedded mixed product equals the weak spatial coefficient applied to the slice. The theorem preserves equality only almost everywhere in time, which is the correct input to continuous representative recovery.
TorusEuler.ae_endpointMixedCoefficient_s.summary: Coefficient multiplication survives the change of slices

TorusEuler.ae_endpointMixedCoefficient_s.text: Assuming the mixed coefficient acts as the specified continuous strong coefficient on each temporal path almost everywhere, its product with a mixed field has the expected weak-coefficient action on almost every spatial slice.
TorusEuler.ae_endpointMixedCoefficient_s.summary: Coefficient action agrees on almost every spatial slice

TorusEuler.ae_endpointSpatialSlice_coeff.text: Assume the jointly measurable bounded coefficient $\Omega_{\rm joint}$ agrees almost everywhere with the evaluated strong coefficient family $\Omega$, and $g$ represents the spatial slices of $v$. Then the embedding of the strong product agrees almost everywhere in time with the slice of the joint product multiplier. The explicit representative compatibility is necessary to connect the two constructions.
TorusEuler.ae_endpointSpatialSlice_coeff.summary: The recovered coefficient product matches the joint weak product

TorusEuler.ae_endpointSpatialSlice_l2Mul.text: For a jointly measurable, essentially bounded coefficient $K$, slicing its product with $v$ agrees almost everywhere in time with multiplying the spatial slice of $v$. The conclusion supplies, for each time slice of $K$, its measurability and its almost-everywhere bound. It compares $L^2$ classes and does not choose values at exceptional times.
TorusEuler.ae_endpointSpatialSlice_l2Mul.summary: Spatial slicing respects a bounded coefficient multiplier

TorusEuler.ae_endpointSpatialSlice_solen.text: A weakly solenoidal joint field has solenoidal spatial slices on a single full-measure time set for all potential tests. The proof reduces the family of open failure sets to a countable subcover using second countability of spatial L2.
TorusEuler.ae_endpointSpatialSlice_solen.summary: One full measure set of solenoidal slices

TorusEuler.ae_endpointTimeSlice_congr.text: If two fields agree almost everywhere for the product of time measure and label measure, then for almost every label they agree for almost every time along that label's path. The quantified outer variable is the label $a$. This is the precise Fubini statement needed to integrate chosen $L^2$ representatives in time.
TorusEuler.ae_endpointTimeSlice_congr.summary: Product equality descends to almost every label path

TorusEuler.ae_endpointTimeSlice_of_conti.text: For nonnegative $T$, suppose $f$ is continuous in the spatial half-Hölder norm and its $L^2$ embeddings agree with the spatial slices of $v$ almost everywhere in time. Then, for almost every label, evaluating $f$ gives the same time path as the joint representative. This is a Fubini compatibility statement, not equality at every exceptional space-time point.
TorusEuler.ae_endpointTimeSlice_of_conti.summary: Recover the time path representative from continuous spatial slices

TorusEuler.ae_hasDerivAt_endpointPrimiti.text: For an interval-integrable velocity with values in a complete normed space, its primitive has ordinary derivative equal to that velocity almost everywhere in the restricted time measure. This is the almost-everywhere fundamental theorem of calculus. It does not assert a derivative at every time or at either endpoint.
TorusEuler.ae_hasDerivAt_endpointPrimiti.summary: The primitive differentiates to velocity almost everywhere

TorusEuler.ae_memLp_endpointTimeSlice.text: A square-integrable field on the time-label product has a square-integrable time slice at almost every label. The label measure is assumed s-finite by the surrounding section. This justifies using the one-dimensional time integration estimates on product-space representatives, while keeping the exceptional set explicitly almost everywhere in labels.

TorusEuler.ae_real_inner_angularTimeLera.text: Apply the angular/time-mean projection to a time L² path; its values are orthogonal to the frequency vector almost everywhere in time. The proof uses its representative formula and the finite-dimensional angular identity. This statement imposes transversality only; the separate time-integral theorem supplies the zero-mean condition.
TorusEuler.ae_real_inner_angularTimeLera.summary: The combined time path projection is transverse almost everywhere

TorusEuler.ae_sub_angularTimeLeray_eq.text: The complement of the combined symbol is the constant time mean plus the frequency-parallel part of the mean-free path. The formula holds almost everywhere and is valid with the convention $x/0=0$. If $\xi=0$, the longitudinal term vanishes, matching the zero-frequency identity convention; positive $T$ is required when interpreting the first term as an average.
TorusEuler.ae_sub_angularTimeLeray_eq.summary: The discarded part is a mean plus a longitudinal path

TorusEuler.affineWaveAmplitudeOperator.text: For a bounded linear map $D$ on a real inner-product space and a vector $k$, the formal operator is $\mathbf a\mapsto-D\mathbf a+2(k\cdot D\mathbf a)k/|k|^2$. Its specialization to Euclidean $\mathbb R^3$ is the amplitude equation (2.1). Linearity in $\mathbf a$ is built into this expression and is used for nonvanishing and propagation. No hypothesis $k\ne0$ is imposed by the definition: division by zero is assigned zero, so at $k=0$ the operator is $-D$. Continuity as a function of a varying $k$ requires separate hypotheses; the physical wave arguments use a nonvanishing wave vector.
TorusEuler.affineWaveAmplitudeOperator.summary: For fixed wave vector, the amplitude equation is linear in the amplitude

TorusEuler.affineWaveAmplitudeOperator_a.text: For $M:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ linear and $\kappa,V,f\in\mathbb R^3$, put $P_\kappa w=\kappa(\kappa\cdot w)/|\kappa|^2$ and $q=(\kappa\cdot f-2\kappa\cdot MV)/|\kappa|^2$. The identity is $-(I-2P_\kappa)MV+(I-P_\kappa)f=f-MV-q\kappa$. It is valid for arbitrary vectors, without assuming $\kappa\cdot V=0$. The scalar $q$ is an algebraic expression here, not an asserted pressure derivative. When $\kappa\ne0$ and $\mathsf p_s=q$, the identity converts the projected velocity equation into $V_t+MV+\kappa\mathsf p_s=f$. At $\kappa=0$, the formal reciprocal is zero, so $P_0=0$ and $q=0$ and both sides still equal $f-MV$.
TorusEuler.affineWaveAmplitudeOperator_a.summary: Pressure recovery identifies the two forms of the equation

TorusEuler.affineWaveAmplitudeOperator_a.text: For any bounded linear map $D$ and vectors $k,\mathbf a$ in a real inner-product space, the formal identity evaluates the amplitude operator as $-D\mathbf a+2(k\cdot D\mathbf a)k/|k|^2$. In $\mathbb R^3$ this is the second equation of (2.1); with $D=M$ and $k=\kappa$ it also supplies the right-hand side of (3.2) along a particle path. It is an algebraic identity, not existence of an amplitude solution. No nonzero or transversality hypothesis is required. When $k=0$, division by zero is assigned zero and both expressions reduce to $-D\mathbf a$.
TorusEuler.affineWaveAmplitudeOperator_a.summary: The operator gives exactly the wave amplitude’s pressure-corrected acceleration

TorusEuler.affineWavePressure.text: At a fixed time, for a linear map $S$ on $\mathbb R^3$, scalar $p_{\rm w}$, vector $k$ and function $P$, the formal pressure is $p(x)=-x\cdot Sx/2-p_{\rm w}P(k\cdot x)$. It is a function on all of $\mathbb R^3$. In Lemma 2.1 one substitutes $S=D'+D^2$ and a primitive $P'=F$. Those identities and symmetry of $S$ are not imposed by the definition. Neither is periodicity or zero phase average of $P$. The formula alone therefore specifies a candidate pressure; the exact-wave theorem proves its gradient cancels the acceleration under the stated background and wave hypotheses.
TorusEuler.affineWavePressure.summary: A quadratic background pressure is combined with a primitive of the wave profile

TorusEuler.affineWavePressureCoeff.text: For a spatial linear map $D$ and vectors $k,\mathbf a\in\mathbb R^3$, the formal coefficient is $p_{\rm w}=2k\cdot D\mathbf a/|k|^2$, as in (1.4) and (2.1). Here the norm and inner product are Euclidean. The definition imposes no wave equation, transversality or nonvanishing. Division by zero is assigned zero, so its value at $k=0$ is zero. For a nonzero wave vector satisfying the wave equations, substituting this coefficient gives $(k\cdot\mathbf a)'=0$; interval persistence of perpendicularity additionally uses an initial zero pairing.
TorusEuler.affineWavePressureCoeff.summary: The pressure coefficient is determined by the wave vector and amplitude

TorusEuler.affineWaveVelocity.text: For arbitrary time-dependent $D,k,\mathbf a$ and scalar profile $F$, the formal velocity is $u(t,x)=D(t)x+F(k(t)\cdot x)\mathbf a(t)$ on $\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3$. It is the full velocity $Dx+w$ of §1.1, not merely the perturbation $w$. The definition imposes no differentiability, periodicity, transversality or Euler equation. In particular a nonzero linear background is generally not a periodic velocity on the torus. Lemma 2.1 obtains the Euler conclusion after imposing the background compatibility and wave equations, while the later construction localizes these waves to obtain periodic fields.
TorusEuler.affineWaveVelocity.summary: A linear background and a plane wave define the velocity ansatz

TorusEuler.affineWave_exists_Icc.text: For a continuous operator path $D$ on $[l,r]$, constructs both affine-wave paths from nonzero perpendicular data at any $t_0$ in that interval. It solves for $k$ first, proves $k$ never vanishes, then solves the linear amplitude equation. The returned paths stay nonzero and perpendicular. Only within-interval derivatives are asserted, including endpoints; neither trace freeness nor an Euler background is assumed.
TorusEuler.affineWave_exists_Icc.summary: Affine waves exist throughout the closed interval

TorusEuler.affineWave_materialAccelerati.text: At a space-time point, suppose $D,k,\mathbf a$ have time derivatives $D',k',\mathbf a'$ relative to a time set with unique derivatives, $k'=-D^Tk$, $k\cdot\mathbf a=0$, and $F$ is differentiable at $k\cdot x$. For $u=Dx+\mathbf aF(k\cdot x)$, the formal identity is $\partial_tu+(u\cdot\nabla)u=(D'+D^2)x+(\mathbf a'+D\mathbf a)F(k\cdot x)$. This is the acceleration calculation in Lemma 2.1. It does not yet impose the amplitude equation, trace zero or symmetry of $D'+D^2$; those hypotheses are needed subsequently for the pressure cancellation and incompressibility.
TorusEuler.affineWave_materialAccelerati.summary: Phase transport and transversality cancel the nonlinear wave self-interaction

TorusEuler.affineWave_propagation.text: On an order-connected time set, a continuous background and solutions of the two wave ODEs preserve nonzero wave and amplitude vectors and their perpendicularity from one initial time. This holds throughout the interval, including earlier times and endpoints, and requires neither trace zero nor symmetry of the background acceleration.
TorusEuler.affineWave_propagation.summary: Propagation of nonzero perpendicular wave data

TorusEuler.affineWave_solvesEulerOn.text: On a time set with unique derivatives, a trace-free background with self-adjoint acceleration matrix and perpendicular wave data satisfying the two ODEs gives the exact Euler momentum and divergence identities. The primitive need only have derivative equal to the profile; oddness, periodicity, and unit central slope are not required for this local identity.
TorusEuler.affineWave_solvesEulerOn.summary: The affine wave solves the Euler equations

TorusEuler.angularLeray.text: For a spatial frequency $\xi\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$, the symbol is $r(\xi)=I-\widehat\xi\otimes\widehat\xi$, where $\widehat\xi=\xi/|\xi|$. Thus it projects vectors orthogonally onto $\xi^\perp$. The formal definition assigns zero to the normalized vector at $\xi=0$, giving $r(0)=I$ rather than removing the spatial mean. This is the spatial symbol in Lemma A.2. In the time-path case it must be combined with the separate projection subtracting the time average.
TorusEuler.angularLeray.summary: Project nonzero frequencies onto their transverse planes

TorusEuler.angularLeray_apply.text: For any real frequency vector, the angular Leray symbol sends $v$ to $v-(\langle\xi,v\rangle/\|\xi\|^2)\xi$. The identity includes zero frequency because real division is totalized there. This formula identifies the normalized rank-one definition with the familiar orthogonal projection onto the perpendicular plane.
TorusEuler.angularLeray_apply.summary: The real Leray symbol removes the frequency component

TorusEuler.angularLeray_isSymmetricProje.text: The angular Leray map is both symmetric and idempotent for every real frequency. Nonzero frequencies use projection away from the normalized frequency direction; zero frequency uses the identity. The result supplies the exact projection hypothesis required by the frozen-symbol coercivity and inverse theorems.
TorusEuler.angularLeray_isSymmetricProje.summary: Every real frequency gives a symmetric projection

TorusEuler.angularLeray_neg.text: The angular Leray operator is unchanged by replacing its frequency by its negative. The longitudinal numerator and vector both change sign, leaving the rank-one correction unchanged. This holds also at zero and supplies the parity needed to relate real symbols to complex Fourier multipliers.
TorusEuler.angularLeray_neg.summary: The real Leray symbol is even in frequency

TorusEuler.angularLeray_pos_smul.text: If $c>0$, replacing the frequency $\xi$ by $c\xi$ leaves the angular Leray operator $I-\widehat\xi\otimes\widehat\xi$ unchanged. The frequency itself may be zero. This degree-zero homogeneity is the starting point for the scaling law of higher derivatives on the punctured frequency space.
TorusEuler.angularLeray_pos_smul.summary: Positive frequency rescaling leaves the Leray symbol unchanged

TorusEuler.angularLeray_zero.text: The spatial Leray symbol equals the identity at frequency zero. Its definition uses $I-\widehat\xi\otimes\widehat\xi$, with the normalized zero vector assigned value zero, so this conclusion includes the exceptional frequency explicitly. In Appendix A.1, a constant spatial vector field therefore survives the Leray projection. Subtracting the time mean is a different operation: the mixed endpoint projection also applies that time projection, even in the spatial zero mode.
TorusEuler.angularLeray_zero.summary: Leave the spatial mean unchanged under Leray projection

TorusEuler.angularTimeLeray.text: This path operator first subtracts the time average, then applies the spatial angular Leray symbol at each time. It represents the combined projection used for endpoint velocities. Its projection and zero-integral properties require a positive interval in the subsequent theorems; the definition itself accepts arbitrary real duration.
TorusEuler.angularTimeLeray.summary: Projecting paths onto transverse zero mean velocities

TorusEuler.angularTimeLeray_apply_ae.text: The projected path agrees almost everywhere with the angular Leray operator applied to the mean-subtracted path value. The order of the two operations is fixed in this definition, though they commute. The theorem gives representative-level meaning without asserting equality at every chosen time.

TorusEuler.angularTimeLeray_eq_self_iff.text: For $T>0$, a path is fixed by the combined symbol exactly when its time integral is zero and it is almost everywhere perpendicular to $\xi$. The forward direction reads the two projection properties; the reverse uses the mean-subtraction formula and the angular projection formula. Zero frequency leaves only the time-mean condition.
TorusEuler.angularTimeLeray_eq_self_iff.summary: Fixed paths have zero mean and no longitudinal component

TorusEuler.angularTimeLeray_isSymmetricP.text: On a positive interval, the combined angular-time operator is a symmetric projection. Its factors are the lifted spatial orthogonal projection and time mean subtraction, and the previous commutation theorem allows their product to remain orthogonal. This supplies the projection input for frozen operators on whole time paths.
TorusEuler.angularTimeLeray_isSymmetricP.summary: The two commuting path projections form a symmetric projection

TorusEuler.angularTimeLeray_pos_smul.text: For a positive real scale, rescaling the spatial frequency leaves the angular-time projection unchanged. The duration is arbitrary in this algebraic statement. Only the spatial angular symbol depends on frequency, so its degree-zero homogeneity passes directly to the mixed path operator.
TorusEuler.angularTimeLeray_pos_smul.summary: The mixed symbol is homogeneous in spatial frequency

TorusEuler.angularTimeLeray_zero.text: At zero spatial frequency, the combined operator is exactly the time-mean subtraction $v\mapsto v-T^{-1}\int_0^Tv$. The spatial Leray factor becomes the identity, but the terminal-displacement constraint still removes the time average. This prevents confusing the zero mode of the mixed symbol with the identity on all time paths.
TorusEuler.angularTimeLeray_zero.summary: At zero spatial frequency only the time projection remains

TorusEuler.annularLocalize.text: Multiply the operator symbol by the scalar difference $\psi(\xi)-\psi(2\xi)$. With a unit cutoff near zero and compact outer support, this confines the product to an annulus. The definition itself accepts arbitrary functions; vanishing, compact support, and smoothness are proved under separate cutoff and symbol hypotheses.
TorusEuler.annularLocalize.summary: Remove low frequencies before inverting the Fourier transform

TorusEuler.annularLocalize_compact.text: The outer cutoff condition alone ensures that the localized symbol has compact support within the closed ball of radius two. The original operator symbol may be arbitrary. This is a support statement; global smoothness still needs a smooth cutoff, local cancellation near zero, and smoothness of the symbol away from zero.

TorusEuler.annularLocalize_smooth.text: A smooth cutoff equal to one near zero turns a symbol smooth on the punctured space into a globally smooth annular product. Away from zero, multiplication preserves smoothness; near zero the product is identically zero. The theorem does not require the original symbol to have a limit at zero.
TorusEuler.annularLocalize_smooth.summary: Localization removes the origin from the symbol regularity problem

TorusEuler.annularLocalize_zero_of_large.text: If the cutoff is zero at norms at least two, its annular localization of any operator symbol is also zero there. Both cutoff evaluations vanish because doubling the frequency stays outside the same radius. No smoothness or boundedness of the original symbol is required for this support statement.
TorusEuler.annularLocalize_zero_of_large.summary: The localized symbol vanishes beyond the outer radius

TorusEuler.annularLocalize_zero_of_small.text: If the cutoff equals one on the closed unit ball, its difference at $\xi$ and $2\xi$ vanishes whenever $\|\xi\|\le1/2$. Therefore the localized symbol is zero throughout that inner region, regardless of the original symbol. This removes any singular or discontinuous behavior at the origin before Fourier inversion.
TorusEuler.annularLocalize_zero_of_small.summary: The localized symbol vanishes on the inner half ball

TorusEuler.appendixCoefficientCoordinate.text: Defines the exact-order coordinate quantity by summing over all ordered coordinate words of length $m$. Each term is the real supremum of the corresponding derivative norm over the index and space, with zero inserted. This is not yet a guaranteed analytic norm: the separate coefficient condition includes boundedness of every supremum set.
TorusEuler.appendixCoefficientCoordinate.summary: The sum of coordinate derivative suprema

TorusEuler.appendixCoefficientMultiIndex.text: For a phase-independent coefficient $c:I\times\mathbb R^3\to A$ in a real normed algebra, this expression is $|c|_m=\sum_{|\beta|=m}\sup_{t,a}|\partial_a^\beta c(t,a)|$. Each multi-index occurs once, represented by its coordinate differentiations in increasing order. The time set $I$ is arbitrary and is included in the supremum; there are no time derivatives. This is the coefficient specialization of the notation introduced in Appendix D. Smoothness and boundedness are additional hypotheses in the coefficient estimates. The real-valued expression itself does not imply either of them.
TorusEuler.appendixCoefficientMultiIndex.summary: Sums the uniform norms of all exact-order coordinate derivatives

TorusEuler.appendixCoefficientOrderWords.text:
The set of nondecreasing coordinate words of length $m$ in the three spatial directions; each such word represents one spatial multi-index of order $m$.

Finite sums and index sets are defined at zero order or empty ranges as well. The paper use supplies the intended order and level restrictions.

TorusEuler.appendixCutoffKernel.text: Defines the torus kernel by summing $\psi(k/\Lambda)e_k(x)e_{-k}(z)$ over the finite band of radius $2\Lambda$. It is defined for every real scale and arbitrary real symbol. Identifying this expression with the intended smooth frequency cutoff, and obtaining a uniform kernel norm, require the support and positivity hypotheses of subsequent theorems.

TorusEuler.appendixDerivativeWord.text:
Apply coordinate derivative maps in word order, with the outermost derivative first. The maps can already include coordinate weights.

The derivative maps are supplied linear maps. Their identification with actual coordinate derivatives and their commutation must be established in each application.
TorusEuler.appendixDerivativeWord.summary: Coordinate derivatives applied in ordered words

TorusEuler.appendixDerivativeWord_coeffi.text: For a bilinear coefficient action $B$ satisfying the stated first-order product rule, differentiating along a word gives the unchanged coefficient acting on the differentiated unknown plus a finite sum of correction terms. Those terms run over the pairs of complementary subwords in which at least one derivative falls on the coefficient. This is the algebraic source of the triangular derivative recursion.

TorusEuler.appendixDerivativeWord_cons.text: Adding a letter at the front of a derivative word applies that coordinate derivative to the previously evaluated word. This is the recursive convention for order in the finite derivative calculus.
TorusEuler.appendixDerivativeWord_cons.summary: The first letter is the outermost derivative

TorusEuler.appendixDerivativeWord_equati.text:
Suppose $\mathcal L_0v+\sum_
u T_
u(c_
u v)=f$, the derivative maps commute with $\mathcal L_0$, and each coefficient action obeys the product rule. The formal statement gives the equation satisfied by any specified sequence of derivatives of $v$. Its correction sums over all ways to place a nonempty part of that sequence on a coefficient, leaving fewer derivatives on $v$. No estimate, inverse bound or existence assertion is used. The paper groups equal terms into multi-indices and binomial coefficients; the formal identity retains each distribution of derivatives separately. For commuting spatial and phase derivatives, grouping those repeated terms gives the multiplicities in the display following Lemma D.3.
TorusEuler.appendixDerivativeWord_equati.summary: Separates derivatives on coefficients from derivatives on the solution

TorusEuler.appendixDerivativeWord_nil.text: Applying the derivative word built from the empty list returns the original vector. This is the zero-order convention in the abstract derivative calculus. It supplies the base case for permutation and Leibniz arguments and ensures that finite derivative norms include the undifferentiated field.
TorusEuler.appendixDerivativeWord_nil.summary: An empty derivative word leaves the field unchanged

TorusEuler.appendixDerivativeWord_perm.text: If every pair of linear derivative maps commutes on every vector, permutation-equivalent words have identical action. The proof uses the generators of list permutation. The commutation hypothesis is necessary here: a word is not treated as a multi-index for an arbitrary collection of noncommuting operators.

TorusEuler.appendixDerivativeWord_scaled.text: Multiplying each coordinate derivative by its weight multiplies the whole derivative by the product of its letter weights.
TorusEuler.appendixDerivativeWord_scaled.summary: Each coordinate weight contributes one factor

TorusEuler.appendixExactOrderDerivativeN.text:
The coefficient size at one order sums its distinct coordinate derivatives of that order. The derivative maps carry the scale factors.

Only finitely many words of the specified exact order are included. The derivative maps and base seminorm are parameters, so the definition alone is algebraic.
TorusEuler.appendixExactOrderDerivativeN.summary: The coefficient norm at one exact derivative order

TorusEuler.appendixFiniteDerivativeNorm.text:
The exact finite norm consists of one word for each mixed multi-index. The zeroth-order seminorm can be the weighted sup norm or the Hölder norm.

This is a finite sum of a supplied zeroth seminorm applied to supplied derivative maps. Its analytic interpretation depends on those maps being the actual derivatives; it does not infer differentiability.
TorusEuler.appendixFiniteDerivativeNorm.summary: The exact finite norm over mixed multi-indices

TorusEuler.appendixFiniteDerivativeNorm_.text: Let $D_i$ be finitely many linear derivative maps, let $r_i\ge0$, and let $p$ be a seminorm. The formal statement says that summing $p$ of all increasing-order compositions of at most $n$ maps $r_iD_i$ equals the corresponding sum for the unweighted maps, each term multiplied by the product of its weights. With $r_i=\ell_*$ for label directions and $r_s=h$ for phase differentiation, the weight is $\ell_*^{|\beta|}h^j$, as in (D.1). This algebraic identity explains the weighting step in Lemma D.3. It does not itself estimate the differentiated equation or prove the subsequent sum inequality.
TorusEuler.appendixFiniteDerivativeNorm_.summary: Identifies scaling of derivatives with weights on each term

TorusEuler.appendixSlowCoefficient_word_.text:
Let the coefficient derivatives commute, let $b_
u\ge0$, and let $C_{m low}\ge0$. Assume the sum of all order-$m$ coefficient derivative seminorms satisfies $C_{m low}\sum_
u b_
u|c_
u|_m\le S$. Then the formal statement proves the same bound with each $|c_
u|_m$ replaced by the seminorm of any one prescribed sequence of $m$ derivatives. Commutation allows that sequence to be put in the increasing order used to count multi-indices. Taking $S=C_m$ supplies the individual derivative bounds needed from (D.7). The statement derives those bounds from the full sum; it does not establish (D.7) for any coefficient family.
TorusEuler.appendixSlowCoefficient_word_.summary: Passes from exact-order coefficient sums to individual derivatives

TorusEuler.auxiliaryLemma12.text: The formal theorem chooses an exponent parameter, a nondecreasing threshold $\mathcal B$, and $N_1$ such that every initial frequency $N\ge N_1$ admits a selected common construction with $\lambda_0=N$. In that one construction, every fixed pair $(m,q)$ eventually satisfies $\|\partial_t^q(U_j-U_{j-1}-O_j)\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\le\lambda_j^{-1}$ throughout $[0,S_j]$, and the differentiated correction is continuous in that spatial norm. The starting stage may depend on both orders and the construction. This is a proved selected-construction version of auxiliary Lemma 1.2. It does not quantify over all cutoff symbols, all admissible thresholds or all constructions having the Section 7 conclusions. The spatial $C^{m,1/2}$ norm is $\sum_{i\le m}(\sup|D^if|+[D^if]_{1/2})$, where $D^if$ is the full $i$th derivative tensor in operator norm.
TorusEuler.auxiliaryLemma12.summary: One threshold supplies every fixed pair of orders

TorusEuler.auxiliaryLemma13.text: The formal theorem chooses an exponent parameter, a nondecreasing threshold and an initial-frequency lower bound before constructing the sequence. Every sufficiently large initial frequency then admits a selected construction in which each $q$ has an integer $\psi_q$ and a starting stage such that $|\partial_t^iU_j|\le\lambda_j^{\psi_q}$ and $|\partial_t^iR_j|\le\lambda_{j+1}^{-5/2}$ for all $i\le q$ and all later stages. Both time curves are continuous in the spatial supremum norm on $[0,S_j]$. This proves the stated time estimates with a more specific, nonnegative integer exponent. It is existential in the selected construction and does not prove the separate generalized assertion for every qualifying construction.
TorusEuler.auxiliaryLemma13.summary: One construction supports all finite time orders

TorusEuler.auxiliaryTerminalSmoothness.text: The formal statement chooses an integer $b$, a nondecreasing threshold $\mathcal B$ and $N_1$ before $N$. For every $N\ge N_1$ it supplies stages with $\lambda_0=N$, the eventual time and mixed correction estimates, and activation times tending to a finite $T>0$ below every stage endpoint. It also supplies an odd smooth maximal periodic Euler solution on $[0,T)$ with bounded velocity, central vorticity tending to infinity, and infinite time integrals of gradient and vorticity supremum norms. Both velocity and its first time derivative have all local spatial derivative limits off the torus origin. The velocity extends periodically and smoothly to all real times off that point; Euler is not imposed after $T$. The exported conclusion does not state $U_j\to u$, although the supplied assembly proof constructs and uses that limit. It selects one threshold, rather than treating every admissible threshold.
TorusEuler.auxiliaryTerminalSmoothness.summary: Selected parameters yield the auxiliary extension conclusion

TorusEuler.auxiliaryTerminalSmoothness_o.text: Fix a cost table depending on a radius exponent, a reserve function, a real $N_{\rm aux}$ and an integer radius floor. Assume: for every scheduled Euler construction with $N_{\rm aux}\le\lambda_0$, radius exponent at least the floor, strength constant $18e^3$, and graph costs fitting the scheduled threshold, the construction satisfies the terminal graph-step estimates. Then the auxiliary terminal smoothness conclusion holds: there are an exponent $b$, a monotone threshold function and $N_1$ such that for every $N\ge N_1$ some scheduled construction with $\lambda_0=N$ has eventual stage time bounds at every time order, the terminal mixed increment bounds, and a limit Euler singularity on $[0,T)$, $T>0$, with a smooth extension through $T$ away from the origin. The graph estimates themselves remain the hypothesis.
TorusEuler.auxiliaryTerminalSmoothness_o.summary: Graph estimates and cutoff costs share one schedule

TorusEuler.auxiliaryTerminalSmoothness_o.text: Fix a cost function depending on a radius exponent, a reserve function, a real $N_{\rm aux}$ and an integer radius floor. Assume: for every scheduled Euler construction with $N_{\rm aux}\le\lambda_0$, radius exponent at least the floor, strength constant $18e^3$, and fixed-order costs bounded as above by the previous frequency, the stages satisfy the local terminal time-step estimates. Then there are an exponent $b$, a monotone threshold function and $N_1$ such that for every $N\ge N_1$ there are parameters with that $b$ and threshold and $\lambda_0=N$, and a scheduled construction, for which: every time-derivative order has eventual stage time bounds; the terminal mixed increment bounds hold; and there are $T>0$, a velocity $u$ and pressure $p$ with activation times tending to $T$, $T$ below every stage slab end, $u$ an Euler singularity witness on $[0,T)$ with initial data $u(0)$, and $u$ admitting a smooth extension through $T$ away from the origin.
TorusEuler.auxiliaryTerminalSmoothness_o.summary: Local time-step estimates give smooth terminal extension

TorusEuler.bddAbove_endpointLabelWord_of.text: Every spatial derivative word of a smooth periodic field on a nondegenerate closed slab has bounded jet-value sets in both the supremum and half-Hölder measurements. The assumptions include a nonnegative label scale $\ell$. Bounds on one additional derivative control the Hölder differences, making subsequent uses of the real supremum mathematically justified.
TorusEuler.bddAbove_endpointLabelWord_of.summary: Smooth periodic words have finite uniform bounds

TorusEuler.bernstein_lift_coordinate_sum.text: Sum the supremum norms of order-$j$ derivatives over all sequences $\beta=(\beta_1,\dots,\beta_j)$ of coordinate directions. For a field supported below $4\Lambda$, the result is bounded by an explicit kernel-dependent constant times $\Lambda^j\|g\|_\infty$. The sequence indexing counts ordered coordinate directions, which can include repeated representations of the same multi-index derivative.
TorusEuler.bernstein_lift_coordinate_sum.summary: Summing coordinate derivatives gives a Bernstein constant

TorusEuler.bernstein_lift_finiteFourierS.text: If a finite synthesis is supported in the band of radius $4\Lambda$, with $\Lambda>0$, its order-$j$ directional derivative is bounded by $(4\Lambda)^j$ times the corresponding undilated kernel derivative $L^1$ norm and the supplied supremum bound $M$. The cutoff must be smooth, supported in radius two, and equal one on the unit ball.
TorusEuler.bernstein_lift_finiteFourierS.summary: Band limited Fourier polynomials satisfy the directional Bernstein bound

TorusEuler.bernstein_lift_of_band.text: A continuous torus field whose coefficients vanish beyond $4\Lambda$ satisfies the same directional derivative bound as a Fourier polynomial. The positive-scale and cutoff hypotheses are explicit. Finite synthesis first proves that the field’s lift is smooth; the derivative estimate then uses the supremum norm of the original continuous field.
TorusEuler.bernstein_lift_of_band.summary: Continuous band limited fields satisfy directional Bernstein estimates

TorusEuler.bernstein_lift_of_real_band.text: For a smooth cutoff symbol supported in the radius-two ball and equal to one on the unit ball, bounds the $j$th derivative of a real band-limited lift in any specified directions $v_1,\dots,v_j$. The factor is $(4\Lambda)^j$ times the integral of the corresponding kernel derivative times $\|g\|$. It requires $\Lambda>0$ and band radius $4\Lambda$.
TorusEuler.bernstein_lift_of_real_band.summary: Bernstein bound for a band-limited lift in given directions

TorusEuler.centeredCell.text: The formal domain is the closed cube $\{x\in\mathbb R^3:-1/2\le x_i\le1/2\text{ for }i=1,2,3\}$. Lebesgue integration over this cube defines the pressure normalization and the torus essential-supremum norms. The cube itself does not identify opposite faces; that identification is represented by imposing integer-translation invariance on the fields. Both boundary faces are included, but they have zero three-dimensional measure and therefore do not change these integrals or essential suprema. This is precisely the fundamental-cell convention in the introduction, not an additional boundary condition of vanishing velocity.
TorusEuler.centeredCell.summary: Torus integrals use the unit cube centered at zero

TorusEuler.centeredCell_fourier_coordina.text: Let $f:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb C$ be $C^1$ and $\mathbb Z^3$-periodic, $k\in\mathbb Z^3$ and $i\in\{1,2,3\}$. Then $\int_{[-1/2,1/2]^3}e^{-2\pi ik\cdot x}\,\partial_if(x)\,dx=2\pi ik_i\int_{[-1/2,1/2]^3}e^{-2\pi ik\cdot x}f(x)\,dx$. Periodicity removes the boundary terms, and both integrands are continuous on the compact cell, so the integrals are ordinary integrals.
TorusEuler.centeredCell_fourier_coordina.summary: Periodic integration by parts gives the Fourier derivative factor $2\pi ik_i$

TorusEuler.centeredCell_fourier_coordina.text: For a periodic $C^2$ complex field, the Fourier integral of the mixed coordinate derivative has the product of the two derivative symbols. The proof applies the first-derivative identity twice, using regularity and periodicity of the inner derivative. It keeps the derivative order explicit and holds at zero frequency as well.
TorusEuler.centeredCell_fourier_coordina.summary: Two coordinate derivatives give two Fourier factors

TorusEuler.centeredCell_fourier_laplacia.text: Summing the diagonal second derivatives of a periodic $C^2$ complex field gives the Laplacian Fourier factor times the field’s coefficient. Each summand is integrable on the centered cell, which permits exchange of the finite sum and integral. The result supplies the scalar equation inverted at nonzero frequencies.
TorusEuler.centeredCell_fourier_laplacia.summary: The Laplacian has its scalar Fourier symbol

TorusEuler.centeredLabel.text: The representative of $x$ with each coordinate in the half-open centered cell $[-1/2,1/2)$, given coordinatewise by $\operatorname{frac}(x_i+1/2)-1/2$. The centered representative uses fractional parts and is discontinuous across cell faces. It selects a half-open cell even though the integration cell $[-1/2,1/2]^3$ is closed; boundary agreement is handled by support or periodicity.
TorusEuler.centeredLabel.summary: Choosing the centered representative of a spatial point

TorusEuler.centralSplit_error_continuous.text: If the older and child gradients, cutoff, wave vector, and amplitude are continuous, an exact rank-one gradient splitting forces the remaining correction $E$ to be continuous. The proof solves the splitting for $E$. It avoids needing an independent regularity assumption for an error already defined by continuous physical data.
TorusEuler.centralSplit_error_continuous.summary: The central correction is continuous because the split is exact

TorusEuler.child_flow_deformation_scale_.text: Assume the envelope reciprocal is bounded by $\mathsf D^a$, the phase width equals the inverse square root of the frequency $\lambda$, and the displacement bound has size at most $K\mathsf D^c\lambda^{-5/4}$. With the exponent budget $\max(a,1)+c+1\le b$ and constant budget $1+2K\le\Gamma$, the parent factor times the graph deformation is bounded by $\Gamma\mathsf D^b\lambda^{1/4}$.
TorusEuler.child_flow_deformation_scale_.summary: Absorbing graph scales into a quarter-frequency bound

TorusEuler.child_flow_deformation_scale_.text: For frequency $\lambda\ge1$, the step condition bounds a coefficient times $\lambda^{-1/12}$ by one. It then bounds the coefficient times the quarter power $\lambda^{1/4}$ by the full frequency $\lambda$. This scalar implication converts the sharper child-flow deformation estimate into the next parent's allowed coframe bound.

TorusEuler.child_flow_pullback_profile_s.text: The oscillatory size $K\mathsf D^p\lambda^{-5/4}$ and the smaller mean size $K\mathsf D^p\lambda^{-5/2}$ satisfy two common bounds after the envelope and phase costs are included. Positivity of the envelope and the frequency relation $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$ are explicit. The scalar inequality records the cancellation that charges the large wave number only to the mean.
TorusEuler.child_flow_pullback_profile_s.summary: Only the smaller mean pays the full wave number

TorusEuler.child_flow_scaled_gradient_le.text: Let $\mathsf D,\lambda\ge1$, let $a,c$ be nonnegative integers, and suppose $\ell_*^{-1}\le\mathsf D^a$ and $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$. If nonnegative quantities $A,B$ satisfy $A,B\le K\mathsf D^c\lambda^{-5/4}$, then $\ell_*^{-1}A+h^{-1}B\le2K\mathsf D^{a+c}\lambda^{-3/4}$. In Lemma 5.10 these quantities bound derivatives of the label velocity and its longitudinal component. The theorem is a scalar inequality: it does not prove the input derivative estimates or identify the left side with the actual gradient. Positivity of the physical radius is imposed elsewhere; the formal inequality only needs the displayed reciprocal bound.
TorusEuler.child_flow_scaled_gradient_le.summary: Combine inverse spatial and phase scales in one numerical bound

TorusEuler.child_flow_scaled_gradient_sm.text: Let $\mathsf D,\lambda\ge1$, $C,\delta\ge0$, and nonnegative integer exponents $p\le b$. Suppose $C\le\delta\Gamma_P$, $\Gamma_P\mathsf D^b\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, and a quantity $G$ satisfies $G\le C\mathsf D^p\lambda^{-3/4}$. Then $G\le\delta$. This is the numerical absorption used before the Gronwall estimate in Lemma 5.10. It applies once $G$ has been identified with a bound for the scaled gradient; no differentiability or flow assertion is part of this lemma. The weaker frequency exponent $-1/12$ is sufficient because $\lambda\ge1$.
TorusEuler.child_flow_scaled_gradient_sm.summary: The step condition turns frequency decay into any prescribed bound

TorusEuler.closedSlabLerayMomentum.text:
The actual periodic Leray projection of the closed-slab time derivative and Euler advection.

This combines totalized time and spatial derivatives with a projection that itself defaults to zero off its periodic Hölder domain. The cutoff proof establishes smoothness and periodicity before using the expression as projected momentum.
TorusEuler.closedSlabLerayMomentum.summary: The projected momentum on the closed time slab

TorusEuler.closedSlabLerayMomentum_realF.text: On a nondegenerate closed slab, a jointly smooth periodic divergence-free parent satisfying the momentum equation with a smooth periodic pressure has the claimed truncated projected residual at every slab time. The time derivative is the actual within-interval derivative, including endpoints. The symbol must be even. The proof verifies coefficient differentiation, incompressibility, and pressure removal for the actual lifted Leray projection.
TorusEuler.closedSlabLerayMomentum_realF.summary: Identify the actual closed slab projected momentum

TorusEuler.closedSlabLerayMomentum_restr.text: Applies the fixed periodic Leray lift to the material-acceleration restriction identity. Thus projected momentum computed on a positive smaller closed slab agrees with the original expression at times in that slab. The function is unchanged; the result only validates the different within-time derivative domain used by the next endpoint problem.
TorusEuler.closedSlabLerayMomentum_restr.summary: Projected momentum agrees after restricting the time interval

TorusEuler.closure_smooth_meanZero_L2.text: For positive duration, smooth velocities with zero time integral are dense in the kernel of time integration in L2. Subtracting the mean from a smooth approximation preserves smoothness and imposes the endpoint constraint.

TorusEuler.compactMultiplierKernel.text: A smooth compactly supported Banach-valued symbol is first bundled as a Schwartz function, then transformed inversely to obtain its Schwartz kernel. Completeness of the target and the support and smoothness proofs are explicit parameters. This construction supplies an actual rapidly decaying kernel for a localized multiplier.
TorusEuler.compactMultiplierKernel.summary: The inverse Fourier transform of a localized smooth symbol

TorusEuler.compactMultiplierKernel_halfM.text: The kernel integral weighted by $\sqrt{\|y\|}$ is bounded by an explicit multiple of the derivative mass $\sum_{p\le1,\,j\le5}\int\|\xi\|^p\|D^j\sigma(\xi)\|\,d\xi$ times the finite radial integral of $(1+\|y\|)^{-4}$. The proof uses fifth-order kernel decay in dimension three. This turns qualitative Schwartz integrability into a quantitative constant for the dyadic half-Hölder estimate.
TorusEuler.compactMultiplierKernel_halfM.summary: Five symbol derivative masses control the kernel half moment

TorusEuler.compactSymbolDyadicBlocks.text: For a smooth compact symbol vanishing at zero and supported within radius four, construct a block family with supremum decay $2^{-j/2}$ and Lipschitz growth $2^{j/2}$. A normalized smooth cutoff supplies Bernstein estimates. The common bound combines the kernel half-moment with a first-derivative kernel constant.
TorusEuler.compactSymbolDyadicBlocks.summary: A cancelled compact symbol supplies certified dyadic blocks

TorusEuler.complexDivergence.text: This is the sum of the matching coordinate components of the real Fréchet derivative of a complex vector field. The spatial variables remain real. Differentiability is not stored in the definition; subsequent smooth finite-synthesis theorems identify it with the expected Fourier multiplier.
TorusEuler.complexDivergence.summary: Divergence of a complex field on the Euclidean lift

TorusEuler.complexDivergence_lift_finite.text: The divergence of a lifted vector Fourier polynomial equals the scalar Fourier synthesis of its divergence-mode coefficients. The finite sum is smooth, so the differential definition has its classical meaning. This calculation supplies the passage from algebraic transversality to a divergence-free spatial field.
TorusEuler.complexDivergence_lift_finite.summary: Divergence of a finite polynomial is computed modewise

TorusEuler.complexDivergence_lift_finite.text: A finite vector Fourier polynomial is divergence free at every Euclidean label exactly when each included coefficient has zero divergence symbol. The forward direction uses uniqueness of finite Fourier coefficients, not cancellation between different modes. The reverse direction follows by summing zero scalar coefficients.
TorusEuler.complexDivergence_lift_finite.summary: Divergence freedom is equivalent to modewise transversality

TorusEuler.complexDivergence_lift_lerayM.text: Synthesizing the Leray-projected coefficients gives a field with zero Euclidean divergence at every label. The theorem follows from modewise zero divergence and finite differentiation. It establishes a classical statement for smooth trigonometric polynomials, before extending the projection to completed function spaces.
TorusEuler.complexDivergence_lift_lerayM.summary: The projected finite Fourier field is divergence free

TorusEuler.complexDivergence_lift_smooth.text: If the original finite vector Fourier polynomial has zero divergence everywhere, applying the Fourier cutoff preserves that property. The proof checks each frequency after real scalar multiplication. No support, parity, positivity, or smoothness assumption on the cutoff symbol is needed for this finite algebraic preservation result.
TorusEuler.complexDivergence_lift_smooth.summary: The cutoff preserves divergence freedom of polynomials

TorusEuler.complexFrequency.text: The integer wave vector is cast coordinatewise into the complex coefficient space. This lets the same vector appear in complex-linear contractions and projections. Its entries remain real in the sense of complex conjugation, a fact used later to identify the contraction with a Hermitian inner product.
TorusEuler.complexFrequency.summary: The integer frequency viewed in complex coordinates

TorusEuler.complexFrozenInverseSymbol.text: At a frequency $\xi$, takes the ring inverse of the real frozen operator $P(\xi)BP(\xi)+I-P(\xi)$ and extends it to the chosen complexification. This packages the inverse symbol used by the Fourier construction. The definition accepts arbitrary $P,B$; invertibility and quantitative bounds are separate theorems obtained from projection and coercivity hypotheses.

TorusEuler.complexFrozenInverseSymbol_po.text: If the projection family satisfies $P(c\xi)=P(\xi)$ for the particular scalar and frequency under consideration, then the complex frozen inverse has the same value at those frequencies. The declaration itself does not assume $c>0$ despite its name; positive homogeneity is one way callers provide the required equality of projection values.
TorusEuler.complexFrozenInverseSymbol_po.summary: Frequency invariance of the inverse symbol

TorusEuler.complexFrozenMode_identity.text: For a symmetric projection $r$ and an operator $B$ coercive on its range with constant $\mu>0$, consider complex vectors satisfying $rv=v$, $f=rw$, and $s=Bv-w$ after complexification. Then $A_0^{-1}f+A_0^{-1}rs=v$. The source sign is fixed by the hypothesis $s=Bv-w$; the result is a single-mode algebraic identity, with genuine invertibility obtained from coercivity.
TorusEuler.complexFrozenMode_identity.summary: The frozen decomposition at one Fourier mode

TorusEuler.complexFrozenProjectedInverse.text: Defines the complex extension of the real operator $A_0(\xi)^{-1}P(\xi)$, where $A_0(\xi)=P(\xi)BP(\xi)+I-P(\xi)$. This is the symbol that acts on the coefficient-difference source in the frozen identity. The projection is applied first, so the multiplication order matters even when the coefficient operator $B$ is not symmetric.
TorusEuler.complexFrozenProjectedInverse.summary: Complexify the projected frozen inverse symbol

TorusEuler.complexFrozenProjectedInverse.text: Shows that complexifying $A_0(\xi)^{-1}P(\xi)$ gives the product of the complexified inverse with the complexified projection. This is an algebraic consequence of the fact that complexification of operators preserves multiplication. It holds for arbitrary $P,B,\xi$, even before the ring inverse, which is assigned zero at a noninvertible operator, has been shown to be a genuine inverse.
TorusEuler.complexFrozenProjectedInverse.summary: Factor the complex projected inverse symbol

TorusEuler.complexFrozenProjectedInverse.text: A supplied equality $P(c\xi)=P(\xi)$ makes both factors in the projected frozen inverse unchanged, hence the complex symbol also agrees at $c\xi$ and $\xi$. No positivity condition on $c$ or invertibility hypothesis is required for this equality. Homogeneity of an actual projection family is established separately before using it for Fourier identification.
TorusEuler.complexFrozenProjectedInverse.summary: Frequency invariance of the projected inverse

TorusEuler.complexFrozenSymbols_fiveJets.text: Let $r(\xi)$ be a smooth family of orthogonal projections on an open subset of $\mathbb R^3$, and let $B$ be a bounded operator on a real Hilbert space with a compatible complexification.
