The conclusion is a stage $n+1$ with the given activation whose velocity and pressure are exactly those of the truncated stage, such that $|w(t,x)|\le\lambda_{n+1}^{-1}$ on $[0,T_c]$ and, for every $m\le q_{n+1}$ and $t\in[0,T_c]$, the correction $u_{\rm child}(t)-u_{\rm parent}(t)-w(t)$ has bounded derivatives and half-Hölder quotients through order $m$ and spatial $C^{m,1/2}$ norm at most $\lambda_{n+1}^{-1}$.
TorusEuler.exists_inductiveEulerChild_of.summary: Derive the child flow from the profile jets and close the stage

TorusEuler.exists_inductiveEulerStages_o.text: Given lifetime bounds, an inhabited base and existence of successors for every compatible finite prefix, constructs an infinite stage family with exactly the prescribed frequency and order sequences. It also supplies matching central waves. Classical choice selects the base and local extension function once; recursion then preserves all earlier choices.
TorusEuler.exists_inductiveEulerStages_o.summary: Local compatible extensions produce a common infinite family

TorusEuler.exists_inductiveEulerStep_of_.text: Constructs a full later step from the retained hierarchy and the preceding selected comparison. In addition to the quantitative stage inputs, it requires the oscillation’s support and early-time vanishing, and the central rank-one decomposition with scale $-1/3$ error. The conclusion identifies the child velocity, child pressure, and step oscillation with the actual constructed fields.
TorusEuler.exists_inductiveEulerStep_of_.summary: Close a later induction step from actual hierarchy fields

TorusEuler.exists_inductiveEulerTip_late.text: For a fixed strength constant $C\ge2$, chooses a comparison constant at least $240$ and a base-frequency threshold. Any certified pair of stages with $\lambda_0$ above that threshold, satisfying the lifetime bounds and with parameter constants equal to the selected ones, admits a later window and wave selection. No compatible-prefix argument is required. The conclusion supplies comparison data before constructing the truncated child.
TorusEuler.exists_inductiveEulerTip_late.summary: Uniform constants select the next amplified wave

TorusEuler.exists_inductiveEulerTip_olde.text: Produces a uniform frequency threshold which, together with the lifetime bounds, ensures $|\nabla U_n(t,0)|\le\lambda_n^9$ and $|\partial_t\nabla U_n(t,0)|\le\lambda_n^{18}$ for a certified pair’s older central gradient and its time derivative within the slab, on the next comparison interval. It also provides the derivative witness. The proof uses the actual projected momentum equation and Fourier support of the stored velocity.
TorusEuler.exists_inductiveEulerTip_olde.summary: The older gradient and its time derivative are controlled

TorusEuler.exists_inductiveEulerTip_sche.text: Above one threshold depending on the strength constant, the derivative of the actual later-wave switch times its normalized center amplitude is bounded by the parent frequency times the next frequency to power $-4$. The statement holds for every real time: the early-amplitude estimate handles the switching interval, and support of the switch derivative handles its complement.
TorusEuler.exists_inductiveEulerTip_sche.summary: The actual switch costs four inverse frequency powers

TorusEuler.exists_inductiveEulerTip_swit.text: For fixed strength constant at least two and nonnegative switch constant, one initial-frequency threshold controls every compatible tip, physical window, and selected later wave. It gives positivity of the next frequency, absorbs the physical growth rate into the parent frequency, and bounds the child’s normalized early amplitude by the logarithmic gain at the next frequency. All conclusions concern the same selection.
TorusEuler.exists_inductiveEulerTip_swit.summary: One threshold controls both rate and early amplitude

TorusEuler.exists_inductiveFirstWaveSele.text: Produces a single threshold $N\ge4$ such that every parameter schedule with $\lambda_0\ge N$ satisfying the lifetime bounds on its half lengths admits a first-wave selection for every exponent $a\ge6$. The proof combines the geometry threshold, gain and shear inequalities, and an origin-wave existence result. The quantifier order makes the threshold independent of the chosen envelope exponent.
TorusEuler.exists_inductiveFirstWaveSele.summary: One frequency threshold supplies the first wave

TorusEuler.exists_inductive_periodicEule.text: Given the complete stage hypotheses, including growing frequencies, increasing derivative order, activation convergence, increment bounds, and small actual projected residuals, this theorem constructs a continuous closed slab velocity. It is jointly smooth, periodic, odd, solenoidal, and satisfies projected Euler before $T$. Every spatial jet converges on strict positive prefixes. The terminal time itself is only covered by continuity.
TorusEuler.exists_inductive_periodicEule.summary: The inductive tower yields an unforced projected velocity limit

TorusEuler.exists_inductive_periodicEule.text: All the stage increment, activation, smoothness, parity, frequency, and projected residual hypotheses produce an actual Euler velocity and normalized pressure before $T$. The velocity extends continuously to the closed slab; its spatial jets and Hölder norms converge on strict positive prefixes. The theorem is conditional on the supplied tower and does not itself prove terminal blow-up or maximality.
TorusEuler.exists_inductive_periodicEule.summary: The tower produces an actual Euler solution before accumulation

TorusEuler.exists_inductive_velocity_lim.text: Quadratically growing frequencies, derivative orders tending to infinity, and the supplied oscillatory and correction bounds produce a continuous velocity limit on the common closed slab. On any open spatial region and time set where late oscillations vanish, all actual spatial jets converge uniformly, remain continuous, and have tail bound $2/\mathrm{freq}(n+1)$. No Euler equation is concluded here.
TorusEuler.exists_inductive_velocity_lim.summary: Stage increments converge wherever late oscillations vanish

TorusEuler.exists_isEulerSolution_of_per.text: A positive-time, jointly smooth periodic solenoidal velocity satisfying the actual projected momentum equation admits a pressure $p$ making $(u,p)$ a classical Euler solution on $[0,T)$: jointly smooth, periodic, with mean-zero pressure, satisfying the momentum equation and incompressibility. The pressure is periodic and mean zero, and its gradient equals minus time derivative minus self advection. Joint pressure smoothness is proved from the smooth gradient and normalization, not assumed.
TorusEuler.exists_isEulerSolution_of_per.summary: Projected dynamics recovers a smooth normalized Euler pressure

TorusEuler.exists_isEulerSolution_of_pre.text: Assume a jointly smooth limit velocity, uniform prefix convergence of velocities, spatial derivatives and periodic pressure gradients, approximation symmetries and divergence, and the limiting dynamics. The theorem constructs a jointly smooth mean-zero pressure and an Euler solution with odd velocity. It first recovers spatial pressure slices, then uses momentum to prove joint gradient smoothness and normalization to control the time-dependent gauge.
TorusEuler.exists_isEulerSolution_of_pre.summary: Recover a smooth normalized pressure for the limiting velocity

TorusEuler.exists_iteratedDeriv_waveProf.text: For every integer $j\ge2$, the formal statement chooses a positive constant $C_j$ such that $|\partial_s^jF_h(s)|\le C_jh^{1-j}$ for all $0<h\le1$ and all real phases $s$. The family $F_h$ is the particular normalized bump construction. The order $j$ is chosen before the constant, and the constant is chosen before $h$ and $s$; no uniform bound in $j$ is asserted. The power uses the integer exponent $1-j$, rather than subtraction of nonnegative integers, so it means $h^{-(j-1)}$. This is the derivative scaling stated in Lemma 3.1.
TorusEuler.exists_iteratedDeriv_waveProf.summary: Each derivative order has a constant independent of the profile width

TorusEuler.exists_jet_majorant_dyadicPer.text: For any derivative order, bounded points uniformly separated from the lattice admit a summable majorant for the corresponding derivative of every translated dyadic kernel. The sequence is indexed by scale and lattice point together. This is the quantitative convergence input for smoothness of the full periodic kernel.
TorusEuler.exists_jet_majorant_dyadicPer.summary: Separated regions have one summable bound for all kernel terms

TorusEuler.exists_jointSmooth_oscillator.text: For finite-dimensional parameters and state, smooth periodic zero-mean forcing and a smooth transported wave vector nonzero initially produce a jointly smooth zero-start velocity and its normalized pressure. Both profiles remain periodic with zero phase mean. The velocity is transverse, and the pressure's phase derivative gives the exact momentum equation at every label, phase and closed-slab time.
TorusEuler.exists_jointSmooth_oscillator.summary: Construct the smooth periodic transverse velocity and pressure

TorusEuler.exists_jointSmooth_oscillator.text: Assume $0<T$, $\kappa(0,a)\ne0$, $\kappa_t=-M^T\kappa$, periodic smooth coefficients, and $f(t,a+n,s+k_*\cdot n)=f(t,a,s)$ with phase period one. Smooth coefficients and a smooth source with zero phase mean produce a jointly smooth solution of (5.15), with zero initial velocity and normalized pressure. Periodicity and the compatibility of label and phase translations are retained. When the coefficients and source have the required reflection symmetry or support, the solution inherits it. This existence result leaves uniqueness to a separate argument.
TorusEuler.exists_jointSmooth_oscillator.summary: The transverse equation preserves support and symmetry

TorusEuler.exists_jointSmooth_oscillator.text: In finite-dimensional parameter and inner-product state spaces, smooth strain, wave vector and forcing, with nonzero initial wave vector and its adjoint transport equation, produce a jointly smooth zero-start velocity on the closed slab. The velocity stays transverse and satisfies both the projected ODE and the equation using the pressure slope. Phase periodicity and averaging are not included here.
TorusEuler.exists_jointSmooth_oscillator.summary: Construct a jointly smooth transverse velocity from zero data

TorusEuler.exists_jointly_continuous_par.text: For continuous-in-time coefficients and forcing with uniform size and parameter Lipschitz bounds, construct solutions for all parameters in one complete normed space. The initial family $x_0$ is bounded and Lipschitz. The output satisfies the ODE within the closed interval, has an explicit Grönwall size bound, and is jointly continuous with a uniform parameter Lipschitz constant.
TorusEuler.exists_jointly_continuous_par.summary: A jointly continuous family of linear ODE solutions

TorusEuler.exists_labelFlow_on_Icc.text: Joint continuity of $U$ on $[l,r]\times\mathbb R^3$, a uniform velocity bound, and a uniform spatial Lipschitz bound give a two-time label flow $X(s,t,a)$ on the closed interval. The produced function is defined for all real arguments, but its initial and trajectory laws are constrained only when the start and evaluation times lie in the interval.
TorusEuler.exists_labelFlow_on_Icc.summary: Bounded Lipschitz velocities admit flows on the whole closed interval

TorusEuler.exists_labelFlow_on_Icc_of_co.text: For a nondegenerate interval $l<r$, a jointly $C^1$ periodic velocity on $[l,r]\times\mathbb R^3$ yields both a uniform spatial Lipschitz constant and a two-time label flow. The regularity is within the closed slab, including its endpoints. The theorem supplies pointwise trajectories; higher label smoothness is proved in later parts of the formalization.
TorusEuler.exists_labelFlow_on_Icc_of_co.summary: A periodic C1 velocity gives the closed slab flow

TorusEuler.exists_labelFlow_on_Icc_of_pe.text: Given joint continuity, spatial periodicity, and a uniform Lipschitz bound on the closed time interval, there exists a label flow throughout that interval. Compactness of the centered cell supplies a velocity bound, which periodicity extends to every label. The result asserts the flow laws only on the prescribed slab.
TorusEuler.exists_labelFlow_on_Icc_of_pe.summary: Spatial periodicity supplies the boundedness needed for a full flow

TorusEuler.exists_lattice_dist_le_of_mem.text: Let $\ell>0$ and consider the periodized radial envelope $a\mapsto\chi(|c(a)|/\ell)$, where $c(a)$ is the representative of $a$ with every coordinate in $[-1/2,1/2)$ and $\chi$ equals one on $[0,1]$ and zero on $[2,\infty)$. Every point $a$ of its closed support has some lattice point $n\in\mathbb Z^3$ with $|n-a|\le2\ell$. Thus the closed support lies in the union of the closed balls of radius $2\ell$ about the lattice points.
TorusEuler.exists_lattice_dist_le_of_mem.summary: The periodized envelope is supported within $2\ell$ of the lattice

TorusEuler.exists_lattice_separation_of_.text: A compact subset of $\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3$ has a common positive lower bound on its distance to every lattice vector. Here the punctured Euclidean lift excludes all integer translates of the torus origin. The proof uses an open thickening of the compact set; excluding only the single Euclidean point zero would be insufficient.
TorusEuler.exists_lattice_separation_of_.summary: A compact punctured set has a uniform lattice gap

TorusEuler.exists_leading_scaledJetBound.text: At each order, chooses a constant before the frequency and slow-amplitude budgets. With frequency at least one, phase scale $\mathrm{freq}^{-1/2}$, and weight $\gamma = \mathrm{freq}^{3/4}\cdot g$, supplied smooth scaled amplitude and pressure-coefficient jets imply leading velocity and frequency-weighted pressure bounds proportional to $\gamma\cdot \mathrm{freq}^{-5/4}$. The amplitude hypothesis already includes the fixed-time switch, so no separate switch bound is assumed.
TorusEuler.exists_leading_scaledJetBound.summary: Slow seed jets produce the leading frequency decay

TorusEuler.exists_leading_scaledJetBound.text: Fix a derivative order $N$ and constants $B\ge1$, $P\ge1$. Then there is $C\ge1$ with the following property, for all real $\lambda,\ell,\chi,\mathsf D,g$, all vector fields $a,\kappa$ on $\mathbb R^3$ and every matrix field $M$, provided $\lambda\ge1$, $\mathsf D\ge1$, $|\chi|\le1$ and $g\ge0$. Put $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, $\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}g$, let $g_\ell$ be the radial envelope of radius $\ell$, and set $A(x)=g_\ell(\ell x)\,a(\ell x)$ and $Q(x)v=-2|\lambda^{-1}\kappa(\ell x)|^{-2}\,\lambda^{-1}\kappa(\ell x)\cdot M(\ell x)v$. Assume $A$ and $Q$ are smooth, every derivative of $A$ of order at most $N$ is bounded everywhere by $B\mathsf D^{13}g$, and every derivative of $Q$ of order at most $N$ by $P\mathsf D^{7}$. Let $w_h$ be the wave profile of width $h$. Then, after the rescaling $(x,s)\mapsto(\ell x,hs)$, both the switched leading velocity $\chi g_\ell(x)w_h(s)a(x)$ and $\lambda$ times its oscillatory phase pressure, the zero-mean phase primitive of $s\mapsto-2\kappa(x)\cdot M(x)V(s)/|\kappa(x)|^2$ with $V(s)=\chi g_\ell(x)w_h(s)a(x)$ and zero forcing, have all derivatives in $(x,s)$ of order at most $N$ bounded by $\gamma\,C\,\mathsf D^{20}\lambda^{-5/4}$. The constant $C$ is chosen before $\lambda,\ell,\chi,\mathsf D,g$ and the fields.
TorusEuler.exists_leading_scaledJetBound.summary: Switched leading velocity and pressure cost twenty powers of $\mathsf D$

TorusEuler.exists_lipschitzWith_of_contD.text: A jointly ($C^1$) periodic velocity on a nondegenerate closed slab has a uniform spatial Lipschitz bound, including at the temporal endpoints.
TorusEuler.exists_lipschitzWith_of_contD.summary: A smooth periodic velocity is uniformly Lipschitz in space

TorusEuler.exists_nearestTorusLift.text: Given Euclidean representatives $x,a$, constructs another representative $x'$ of the same torus point as $x$ whose distance to $a$ equals the auxiliary torus Euclidean distance. Coordinatewise integer translations realize the minimum. The result gives existence of a shortest lifted segment, which is enough for the local estimate, without requiring a unique lift.

TorusEuler.exists_norm_endpointStrongMix.text: There is one nonnegative constant bounding the operator norm of the mixed half-Hölder Leray projection for every positive duration $T$. The proof uses five angular derivatives of the multiplier and treats the zero mode separately. The conclusion is a spatial half-Hölder operator bound independent of the changing temporal $L^2$ target, not an assertion that this norm is one.
TorusEuler.exists_norm_endpointStrongMix.summary: The mixed Leray bound is uniform in duration

TorusEuler.exists_norm_homogeneousHalfHo.text: For a fixed cutoff and fixed complex value spaces, a nonnegative constant bounds the constructed multiplier norm by the derivative mass of its annular localization plus $\|A(0)\|$. The proof combines kernel half-moment and block-summation estimates. It does not require homogeneity for this bound on the constructed operator.
TorusEuler.exists_norm_homogeneousHalfHo.summary: Derivative mass and the mean bound control the operator norm

TorusEuler.exists_norm_iteratedFDeriv_pe.text: Let $K,S\subset\mathbb R^3$ be compact and suppose $x-y\notin\mathbb Z^3$ for every $x\in K,y\in S$. There is an open $U\supset K$ such that, for each integer $d\ge0$, a constant $C\ge0$ bounds the difference of the $d$th spatial derivatives of two far pressure gradients on $U$ by $C\int_{S\cap Q}|P-Q_1|$. Here $Q$ is a unit cell and $P,Q_1$ are integrable complex matrix fields; the pressure is the real-valued integral against the periodic pressure kernel. The constant is chosen before these fields and the observation point. This proves smoothing across separation on the torus. Identifying this pressure gradient with the localized Leray-divergence term in Proposition 8.4 requires the adjoining representation theorem.
TorusEuler.exists_norm_iteratedFDeriv_pe.summary: Separated source and observation sets give bounds for every derivative

TorusEuler.exists_norm_iteratedFDeriv_pe.text: For compact periodically separated target and source sets, one open target neighborhood supports a nonnegative constant at every derivative order bounding pressure-jet differences by the integral tensor difference norm. Both densities must be integrable on the source portion of the fundamental cell. The constants are independent of those densities.
TorusEuler.exists_norm_iteratedFDeriv_pe.summary: Each far pressure derivative is controlled by the source integral error

TorusEuler.exists_norm_iteratedFDeriv_ra.text: For each derivative order $m$ there is a constant $C>0$ such that, for every radius $\ell>0$ and every label $x\in\mathbb R^3$, the $m$-th derivative of the radial envelope $g_\ell$ of radius $\ell$ satisfies $\|D^mg_\ell(x)\|\le C\,\ell^{-m}$. The constant depends on $m$ only, not on $\ell$ or $x$; the proof bounds the derivatives of the unit envelope on the closed ball of radius two, outside which they vanish.
TorusEuler.exists_norm_iteratedFDeriv_ra.summary: Envelope derivatives cost inverse powers of the radius

TorusEuler.exists_norm_realHomogeneousHa.text: For a fixed complexification, chooses $C\ge0$ that works for every symbol smooth away from zero. The real multiplier norm is bounded by $C$ times the derivative mass of its fixed annular localization, plus $\|A(0)\|$ for the mean mode. This separates the nonzero-frequency kernel estimate from the independently specified zero mode; no homogeneity assumption is used for the norm bound.
TorusEuler.exists_norm_realHomogeneousHa.summary: Bound the real multiplier by localized symbol mass

TorusEuler.exists_norm_universal_homogen.text: A single cutoff-dependent nonnegative constant bounds the constructed multiplier by its localized derivative mass plus its zero-mode norm for all complete complex value spaces. The existential constant precedes the space parameters. This is the uniform estimate needed when the value space varies with the time interval in the mixed endpoint problem.
TorusEuler.exists_norm_universal_homogen.summary: The multiplier norm constant is uniform across Banach spaces

TorusEuler.exists_offOrigin_compact_neig.text: Every compact set contained in $\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3$ has a positive radius whose closed thickening remains compact and avoids the integer lattice. The theorem also gives strict separation from every lattice point. Here $\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3$ is the punctured periodic lift, so excluding only the Euclidean point zero would be insufficient.
TorusEuler.exists_offOrigin_compact_neig.summary: A compact region stays away from the singular lattice

TorusEuler.exists_older_central_gradient.text: For sufficiently large older frequency, a smooth torus parent with the supplied Fourier band, amplitude bound, small residual, and actual projected momentum equation satisfies the small central gradient powers required by amplification. The schedule relation converts the raw powers of the older frequency to powers of $\mu$. The advection representative $A$ is explicitly identified in the hypotheses.
TorusEuler.exists_older_central_gradient.summary: Fourier and momentum estimates control the older central strain

TorusEuler.exists_older_central_gradient.text: The raw central bounds derived from the projected residual become the amplification bounds $\mu^{1/32}$ and $\mu^{1/16}$ after imposing the scheduled relation between the older frequency and $\mu$. The conclusion includes the actual within derivative on the comparison interval. Smoothness, band limitation, divergence freedom, and residual smallness remain explicit assumptions.
TorusEuler.exists_older_central_gradient.summary: The actual parent supplies the amplification gradient powers

TorusEuler.exists_older_central_gradient.text: The parent projected momentum identity, frequency band, divergence condition, and small pointwise residual imply the actual central gradient bounds with exponents nine and eighteen on any contained later interval. The theorem constructs the required torus representatives internally through the preceding result. A uniform initial frequency threshold is quantified before the parent data.
TorusEuler.exists_older_central_gradient.summary: The actual residual identity yields raw central derivative bounds

TorusEuler.exists_open_farPressureSource.text: If a compact target is periodically separated from the support of $1-\chi$, it has an open neighborhood separated from the compact far source set. The proof first obtains a positive uniform separation radius, then uses a thickening of the target. The conclusion excludes equality modulo every lattice vector for all target-source pairs.
TorusEuler.exists_open_farPressureSource.summary: Compact separation persists on an open target neighborhood

TorusEuler.exists_oscillatoryPhaseSolve_.text: On $[l,r]$, $l\le r$, assume continuous $M$, a transported covector satisfying $\kappa_t=-M^T\kappa$ and $\kappa(l)\ne0$. Let $f(t,s)$ be period one with zero phase mean and continuous in time in the supremum norm on bounded continuous phase functions. The formal statement constructs a continuous period-one velocity $V$ with $V(l)=0$, $\kappa\cdot V=0$ and $\langle V\rangle_s=0$. Its normalized periodic pressure satisfies $V_t+MV+\kappa\partial_s\pi=f$, with $\langle\pi\rangle_s=0$. Derivatives are asserted pointwise in phase and within the time interval. This solves (1.12) at one particle label after inserting its forcing; regularity in the label and the specific hierarchy source are additional ingredients.
TorusEuler.exists_oscillatoryPhaseSolve_.summary: A zero-mean periodic forcing produces a zero-initial transverse solution

TorusEuler.exists_oscillatoryTransverse_.text: Let $t_0\in[l,r]$, with continuous coefficients $M,f$, and suppose $\kappa_t=-M^T\kappa$ with $\kappa(t_0)\ne0$. For any initial amplitude $V_0\perp\kappa(t_0)$, the formal statement constructs $V$ on $[l,r]$ with $V(t_0)=V_0$, $\kappa\ne0$ and $\kappa\cdot V=0$. It satisfies $V_t+MV+p_s\kappa=f$, where $|\kappa|^2p_s=\kappa\cdot f-2\kappa\cdot MV$. The conclusion extends to times before $t_0$ as well as after it. Setting $f=0$ recovers the seed equation (3.2) along a single label. No smooth dependence on labels or periodic phase pressure is asserted by this one-path theorem.
TorusEuler.exists_oscillatoryTransverse_.summary: Any transverse initial value gives an amplitude on the full interval

TorusEuler.exists_paperA1_smoothSolution.text: On $[0,1]\times\mathbb T^3$, let $K,\Omega,L$ be jointly smooth. Require $K,\Omega$ to be time-continuous in $C^{0,1/2}$, with uniform bounds on values and first spatial derivatives. Assume $K\ge\kappa I$ as quadratic forms, $\kappa>0$, and $\int_0^1(Kz_t\cdot z_t+\Omega z_t\cdot z)\,dt\ge\mu\int_0^1|z_t|^2\,dt$ at every label for every $z\in H^1_0$, with $\mu>0$. Then there exist a continuous divergence-free half-Hölder velocity $v$ and a time-independent divergence-free field $c$ such that $Jv(1)=0$ and $\mathbb P(Kv-J(\Omega v)+L)=c$. The periodic lift of $v$ is jointly smooth. Here $Jw(t)=\int_0^tw(s)\,ds$. Symmetry of $K$ and skew-symmetry of $\Omega$ are not hypotheses. This intermediate result constructs the smooth velocity; the full theorem supplies the other recovered smooth fields.
TorusEuler.exists_paperA1_smoothSolution.summary: Construct a jointly smooth label velocity from smooth data

TorusEuler.exists_paperMeanParent_of_flo.text: Let $T>0$ and let $u$ be smooth and periodic on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3$, with particle flow $X$. Assume $\|D_xX_{t,0}(X_{0,t}(a))\|\le D$, $\|D_xu\|\le L$, and $-(M_t+M^2)\le I$ along each trajectory. Then the periodic matrix fields $F=D_aX$, $G=F^{-1}$, $M=(D_xu)\circ X$ and $M_t$ satisfy the smoothness, inverse and evolution requirements of the mean inverse. This supplies their exact identification with the actual flow. Neither incompressibility nor an Euler equation is assumed in this coefficient construction; those enter the later Eulerian conclusion.
TorusEuler.exists_paperMeanParent_of_flo.summary: Construct the matrix data from an actual particle flow

TorusEuler.exists_paperPhysicalStepBudge.text: Fix nonnegative integer exponents for the envelope, hierarchy loss and mean estimates, a finite depth $P$, and nonnegative constants for the coefficient, remainder, leading-wave, pressure and flow bounds. There exists $\Gamma_P$ such that the common expression $\Gamma_P\mathsf D^b$ dominates every listed cost simultaneously for all $\mathsf D\ge1$, with $b=6r+5a+2a_{\rm mean}+160$. In particular $\Gamma_P\ge1$. This is a finite numerical choice of constants before the parent scale, as required for $C_{\rm step}$ in §5.6. Its coefficient may depend on the supplied estimates and depth. The result does not prove those estimates or assert the smallness condition involving $\lambda$.
TorusEuler.exists_paperPhysicalStepBudge.summary: A single coefficient dominates every fixed order cost uniformly

TorusEuler.exists_paper_hierarchy_invers.text: Assume $0\le t_0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$, $\lambda=|\kappa(t_0,0)|\ge1$, smooth periodic $U$, gradient and both deformation bounds $\mathsf D$, velocity derivative bounds $R_n\mathsf D^j$, and central transverse stability and coupling bounds $\mathsf D,\mathsf D^{-1}$. Put $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, $\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|$ and choose a sufficiently small radius. Smooth transverse solutions on $[t_0,T]$ satisfy $\|V\|_{[n],\gamma}\le C_n\mathsf D^{20}(\gamma(t_0)^{-1}\|V(t_0)\|_{[n]}+\|f\|_{[n],\gamma})$. Initial data and source are supported within $2\ell_*$ of lattice points and satisfy phase period one and the coupled label translations. Unlike the numbered lemma’s first clause, this theorem assumes no smooth extension before activation. The transverse stability assumption is $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for every transverse homogeneous solution $\mathbf b$ and $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$.
TorusEuler.exists_paper_hierarchy_invers.summary: Transverse data need only exist after activation

TorusEuler.exists_parameter_differentiab.text: For uniformly bounded, parameter-Lipschitz coefficients and forcing with the stated parameter derivatives, constructs a jointly continuous solution whose spatial parameter slices are differentiable. The initial family $x_0$ is assumed differentiable. Adjoining a constant scalar coordinate turns the forced system into a homogeneous one; the conclusion does not include higher parameter derivatives.
TorusEuler.exists_parameter_differentiab.summary: A forced solution varies differentiably with its parameter

TorusEuler.exists_parameter_differentiab.text: Under uniform coefficient bounds, parameter Lipschitz bounds and a coefficient derivative continuous in time, constructs a jointly continuous fundamental solution. At every parameter it has a Fréchet derivative satisfying the forced variational equation and vanishing initially. The time interval may have zero length; infinite smoothness in the parameter is not asserted here.
TorusEuler.exists_parameter_differentiab.summary: The fundamental solution varies differentiably with its parameter

TorusEuler.exists_parentDerivedLowBounds.text:
There is an absolute lower frequency threshold such that the following holds on $[0,T]$, $T>0$. Let $u$ be a smooth periodic velocity, $\|u(t)\|_\infty\le\mu$, with Fourier support at most $2\mu^5$, and let a continuous periodic residual satisfy $\|R(t)\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-3}$, where $\lambda\ge1$. Assume $u_t=-\mathbb P((u\cdot
abla)u)+R$, with the advective term represented in the spatial one-half Hölder space. For $\mu$ above the threshold, the formal statement gives $\|
abla u(t,x)\|\le\mu^9$ and $\|\partial_t
abla u(t,x)\|\le\mu^{18}$ for every point and time in the closed interval. Time derivatives at the endpoints are taken from within the interval; matrix norms are operator norms. This supplies (7.6) without requiring oddness.
TorusEuler.exists_parentDerivedLowBounds.summary: Derives spatial and time derivative bounds from projected momentum

TorusEuler.exists_parentGradient_halfHol.text: One nonnegative universal constant controls every torus field with bandwidth at most $4D$, $D\ge1$, and physical first-gradient norm at most $D$. Its lifted gradient has half-Hölder norm at most $CD^2$. The bandwidth hypothesis supplies the additional spatial variation control; a first-gradient supremum bound alone would not imply this estimate.
TorusEuler.exists_parentGradient_halfHol.summary: Bandwidth controls the parent gradient Hölder norm

TorusEuler.exists_parentMeanCoefficientJ.text: For a smooth periodic parent with controlled flow, inverse flow, and velocity jets on a slab of length at most one, this constructs uniform constants for the deformation, its adjoint, $K$, and $\Omega$. It proves their spatial smoothness and derivative bounds with powers $5n+1$, $5n+1$, $5n+2$, and $6n+3$ of $D$, respectively.
TorusEuler.exists_parentMeanCoefficientJ.summary: The actual mean coefficients have uniform jet bounds

TorusEuler.exists_parentMeanWeightedCoef.text: Let $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge1$, and let $X$ be the flow of a smooth unit-periodic $U$. Assume $\|D_aX\|,\|(D_aX)^{-1}\|\le\mathsf D$ and $\|D^jU\|_\infty\le R_n\mathsf D^j$ for every $1\le j\le n$, where the nonnegative sequence $R_n$ is fixed before the flow. Write $F=D_aX$, $G=F^{-1}$, $M=(DU)\circ X$, $K=F^TF$ and $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$. Let $\ell_*>0$ and $\ell_*\mathsf D^6\le1$. All spatial half-Hölder derivative sets of $F,F^T,K,\Omega$ are bounded. Nonnegative sequences $C_n,H_m$, chosen before the flow, satisfy $\|F\|_{[n],1/2},\|F^T\|_{[n],1/2}\le C_n\mathsf D/\sqrt{\ell_*}$. For every individual word $\alpha$ of $m\ge1$ coordinate derivatives, $\ell_*^m(\|\partial^\alpha K\|_{C_tC^{0,1/2}}+\|\partial^\alpha\Omega\|_{C_tC^{0,1/2}})\le H_m\mathsf D^9\sqrt{\ell_*}$. Summing the finitely many words changes only the order-dependent constant.
TorusEuler.exists_parentMeanWeightedCoef.summary: Positive-order coefficients gain a square root of the radius

TorusEuler.exists_parentResidualLabelJet.text: Given nonnegative velocity-jet constants, this produces constants controlling a band-limited residual composed with the actual parent flow. A positive slab of length at most one, smooth periodic velocity, forward and inverse deformation bounds, and higher velocity jets are assumed. A residual of amplitude $A$ supported below $4D$ gains the bound $C_m A D^{6m}$ in label derivatives.
TorusEuler.exists_parentResidualLabelJet.summary: Pulling back the residual costs powers of the parent scale

TorusEuler.exists_parentResidualWeighted.text: Let $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge1$, $\lambda\ge1$, $\ell_*\ge0$, $\ell_*\mathsf D^6\le1$, and let $X$ be the flow of a smooth unit-periodic $U$, with $\|DX\|,\|DX^{-1}\|\le\mathsf D$. Fix nonnegative $V_n$ and assume $\|D^kU\|_\infty\le V_n\mathsf D^k$ for all $n\ge2$ and $2\le k\le n$. For any family of continuous torus fields $R(t)$ with Fourier radius $4\mathsf D$ and $\|R(t)\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$, every scaled label norm of $R\circ X$ is finite and $\|R\circ X\|_{[n]}\le C_n\lambda^{-5/2}$, uniformly on $[0,T]$. The constants $C_n$ depend only on the sequence $V_n$ and are chosen before $U$, $X$ and the fields. This need not be the momentum residual of $U$; that identification is supplied in the application.
TorusEuler.exists_parentResidualWeighted.summary: The pulled-back residual retains its small amplitude

TorusEuler.exists_parentVelocityJetBound.text: There is a nonnegative sequence $V_n$, chosen before the field and $\mathsf D$, with the following property. Let $g$ be continuous on the unit torus, have Fourier support $|k|\le4\mathsf D$, and satisfy $\|Dg\|_\infty\le\mathsf D$ with $\mathsf D\ge1$. Then $\|D^kg\|_\infty\le V_n\mathsf D^k$ for every $1\le k\le n$. Derivatives refer to the periodic lift and use multilinear operator norms. Finite Fourier support supplies spatial smoothness; no time dependence or Euler equation is required. The result gives no bound for the undifferentiated field.
TorusEuler.exists_parentVelocityJetBound.summary: A Fourier band and gradient bound control higher derivatives

TorusEuler.exists_parent_coefficientJetB.text: Let $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge1$, and let $X$ be the flow of a smooth unit-periodic $U$. Assume $\|D_aX\|,\|(D_aX)^{-1}\|\le\mathsf D$ and $\|D^jU\|_\infty\le R_n\mathsf D^j$ for every $1\le j\le n$, where the nonnegative sequence $R_n$ is fixed before the flow. Put $F=DX$, $G=F^{-1}$, $M=DU\circ X$ and $\kappa=G^Tk_*$. Suppose $t_0\in[0,T]$ and $|\kappa(t_0,0)|=\lambda>0$. There are $C_n\ge0$, fixed before the flow, bounding the order-$n$ derivatives of $F$, $G$ and $G^T$, $M$, $\kappa/\lambda$, $\lambda^2/|\kappa|^2$, and $P_\kappa$ by $C_n$ times $\mathsf D^{5n+1}$, $\mathsf D^{7n+1}$, $\mathsf D^{6n+1}$, $\mathsf D^{7n+2}$, $\mathsf D^{16n+4}$, and $\mathsf D^{16n+8}$, respectively. All bounds are uniform in time and label. No residual, pressure or coercivity assumption is used.
TorusEuler.exists_parent_coefficientJetB.summary: Each coefficient has explicit polynomial derivative growth

TorusEuler.exists_parent_coefficient_lab.text: A nonnegative derivative family $R$ fixes a common constant before the smooth periodic parent and frequency are chosen. Under the stated flow, inverse bounds and positive reference frequency, label differences of forward deformation, inverse deformation and material gradient are bounded with powers $D^6,D^8,D^7$. The transported covector has relative loss $D^{11}$, and its transverse projection has absolute loss $D^{24}$.
TorusEuler.exists_parent_coefficient_lab.summary: Parent derivative budgets control all localization coefficients

TorusEuler.exists_parent_genericLeading_.text: Fix parent derivative bounds $\|D^jU\|\le W_n\mathsf D^j$ for $1\le j\le n$. Suppose $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$, $\lambda\ge1$, the smooth periodic parent flow and its inverse have derivative norm at most $\mathsf D$, and $|\kappa(t_0,0)|=\lambda$, $|k_*|\le\mathsf D\lambda$. Let the central seed satisfy (5.5) and $|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le\lambda^{-3/4}$. For sufficiently large integer $a$ and $\ell_*^{-1}=\mathsf D^a$, every localized seed smooth jointly in $(t,a)$ on $[t_0,T]\times\mathbb R^3$ and every admissible cutoff yield $D_x^2\mathsf p_1^\natural\le C\mathsf D^{2a+74}\lambda^{-1/4}I$ on $[0,T]$. The periodic continuation is constructed from this local regularity. Constants precede the parent. The conclusion is an upper quadratic-form bound for the leading pressure only; it does not bound its absolute Hessian norm or the complete pressure correction.
TorusEuler.exists_parent_genericLeading_.summary: Obtain a one sided Hessian estimate uniformly in the activation

TorusEuler.exists_parent_leading_pressur.text: Chooses $A\ge30$ and $C\ge0$ before the parent, carrier and exponent $a$. Given the table $W$ of parent derivative bounds, $A\le a$, $0<T\le1$, $D\ge2$, frequency at least one, normalized launch covector, $\|k\|\le D\,\mathrm{freq}$, deformation bounds, a central wave and regular seed with $\ell^{-1}=D^a$, proves $D_x^2p_1\le C D^{2a+74}\lambda^{-1/4}I$ as quadratic forms. The central amplitude cap is a hypothesis. This bounds the leading pressure from above, not its absolute Hessian norm.
TorusEuler.exists_parent_leading_pressur.summary: Uniform upper bound for the leading pressure

TorusEuler.exists_parent_projectedMoment.text: From the smooth solenoidal parent, its Fourier band, and its actual closed-slab projected residual, this theorem constructs torus representatives of advection and residual. It proves the residual band and smoothness, the gradient bounds $\mathrm{old}^9$ and $\mathrm{old}^{18}$, and a residual gradient bound $K\mathrm{old}^5\mu^{-3}$. The representatives agree with the original physical fields on the slab.
TorusEuler.exists_parent_projectedMoment.summary: Actual projected residuals determine all needed parent bounds

TorusEuler.exists_parent_scaledPhasePote.text: For a fixed nonnegative sequence of parent jet controls, chooses an order-dependent nonnegative constant before any parent flow, carrier, or frequency. Smooth periodic parents with bounded deformation and the stated normalized center covector then yield smooth scaled potential coefficients with jet bound $C(n)\mathsf D^6/\lambda$ at order $n$, where $\lambda$ is the frequency. Radius smallness $\ell\,\mathsf D^{16}\le1$ is required on the entire closed time slab.
TorusEuler.exists_parent_scaledPhasePote.summary: Actual parent potential coefficients have uniform finite jet budgets

TorusEuler.exists_periodicFarMultiplierJ.text: For compact periodically separated target and source sets, a common open target neighborhood supports measurable kernel jets, a uniform norm bound at every order, and the actual next-order derivative relations. The source measure is arbitrary. Compactness of the difference region and smoothness off the lattice supply all the analytic hypotheses needed by the far-integral theorem.
TorusEuler.exists_periodicFarMultiplierJ.summary: The actual periodic kernel satisfies the separated integral hypotheses

TorusEuler.exists_periodicPressure_of_le.text: A periodic half Hölder field $f$ has a periodic mean-zero potential whose gradient is $\mathbb P f-f$. The normalization is the integral over the cube $[-1/2,1/2]^3$. This theorem recovers a pressure for the negative complement, with the sign matching the Euler equation. It assumes the genuine Hölder domain rather than trusting the raw projection formula.
TorusEuler.exists_periodicPressure_of_le.summary: The Leray complement is a normalized pressure gradient

TorusEuler.exists_periodic_meanZero_pres.text: Uniform gradient convergence on $I$ times the centered cell, periodicity of the approximants and limit, and spatial differentiability give a pressure family whose slices have zero mean and gradient $g(t)$. The conclusion is for each $t\in I$. It asserts no joint time continuity or time differentiability of the selected family; those require later arguments.
TorusEuler.exists_periodic_meanZero_pres.summary: Recover a normalized pressure separately at every time

TorusEuler.exists_periodic_meanZero_pres.text: For differentiable periodic pressures whose gradients converge uniformly to $g$, the theorem constructs a periodic pressure with zero cell mean and gradient exactly $g$. It does not assume convergence of the original pressure values: constants are first normalized at one point, then the final mean is removed. Smoothness is a separate conclusion requiring regularity of $g$.
TorusEuler.exists_periodic_meanZero_pres.summary: A uniform gradient limit has a normalized periodic potential

TorusEuler.exists_periodic_offOrigin_cut.text: Let $K\subset\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3$ be compact, representing observation points away from the torus origin. The formal statement produces a smooth period-one function $0\le\chi\le1$, an open neighbourhood of $K$ on which $\chi=1$, and an open neighbourhood of the entire integer lattice on which $\chi=0$. The closed support of $\chi$ avoids the lattice. Moreover, for $x\in K$ and $y$ in the closed support of $1-\chi$, the difference $x-y$ is never an integer lattice vector. Thus the source and observation points are separated on the torus, not merely in one chosen cube. This is the cutoff used for the local and far pressure split in Proposition 8.4.
TorusEuler.exists_periodic_offOrigin_cut.summary: Separate a compact observation set from the torus origin smoothly

TorusEuler.exists_periodically_separated.text: If every difference between points of compact target and source sets avoids the integer lattice, their periodic separation remains uniformly positive on a closed thickening of the target. The proof applies compact off origin separation to the difference set. This provides a common open region on which derivatives of the far kernel are bounded.
TorusEuler.exists_periodically_separated.summary: Source separation persists near the compact observation region

TorusEuler.exists_perturbedLabelFlows.text: Jointly $C^1$ periodic fields $U$ and $b$ have a family of flows for $U+\varepsilon b$ on the same closed interval, for every real parameter $\varepsilon$. The output is a choice of pointwise flows. The theorem does not yet assert continuity or differentiability of that family with respect to the perturbation parameter.
TorusEuler.exists_perturbedLabelFlows.summary: Flows for every scalar velocity perturbation

TorusEuler.exists_phaseJetBound_scaledRa.text: A fixed number of radius-normalized envelope derivatives has a bound that depends on the derivative order alone.
TorusEuler.exists_phaseJetBound_scaledRa.summary: Envelope derivatives are bounded after radius normalization

TorusEuler.exists_projectedHilbertSoluti.text: Let $E$ be a real Hilbert space, $H\subseteq E$ a closed subspace and $A$ a bounded linear operator on $E$. Suppose $c>0$ and $c\|u\|^2\le\langle Au,u\rangle$ for every $u\in H$. Then for every $f\in E$ there is $u\in H$ with $\langle Au,w\rangle=\langle f,w\rangle$ for all $w\in H$ and $\|u\|\le\|f\|/c$, and any $v\in H$ satisfying the same tested equation equals $u$. This is the Lax–Milgram step; regularity and identification with the Euler correction are separate.
TorusEuler.exists_projectedHilbertSoluti.summary: A coercive operator on a closed subspace has a unique weak solution with bound $\|f\|/c$

TorusEuler.exists_radial_scaledPhaseSlow.text: For $0<r\le1$, multiplying a smooth slow factor by the radial envelope and evaluating at the rescaled label preserves finite derivative bounds up to a constant depending only on $n$. The envelope becomes the unit envelope under this rescaling. The input bound $A$ must be nonnegative, and the conclusion also records smoothness.
TorusEuler.exists_radial_scaledPhaseSlow.summary: Localization preserves the rescaled slow derivative budget

TorusEuler.exists_realFourierCutoffPoiss.text: On a positive closed slab, starts with a smooth periodic solenoidal approximate velocity satisfying its momentum equation and matching torus representatives for velocity and residual. For an even cutoff symbol it constructs a jointly smooth, periodic, mean-zero pressure for the truncated field. Its Poisson equation and equality of the true residual with the cutoff projected residual are certified together.
TorusEuler.exists_realFourierCutoffPoiss.summary: The cutoff receives its actual normalized Euler pressure

TorusEuler.exists_realTruncatedParentPro.text: On a nondegenerate closed slab, assume smooth periodic $V$ and $R_V$, divergence-free $V$, and the momentum identity $\partial_tV+(V\cdot\nabla)V+\nabla p=R_V$ with the supplied smooth periodic pressure $p$. For an even smooth cutoff, supported in the radius-two ball and one on the unit ball, constructs representatives and identifies actual projected momentum. For $P\ge2$ and $\Lambda\ge1$, put $\varepsilon=\Lambda^{2-P}(1+\sup_t\|V(t)\|_{C^{P,1/2}})^2$. The order-two tail is at most $C_t\varepsilon$; the order-one momentum norm is at most $C_r\sup_t\|R_V(t)\|_{C^{1,1/2}}+C_t\varepsilon$. The prefactor $C_r$ precedes $P$, and $C_t$ precedes $\Lambda$.
TorusEuler.exists_realTruncatedParentPro.summary: Bound the actual truncated parent momentum

TorusEuler.exists_scaledFlow_on_Icc.text: For a complete normed space, a jointly continuous field with uniform size and spatial Lipschitz bounds has a two-time family satisfying the initial and trajectory equations throughout the closed interval. The theorem makes no claim about times outside that interval. If the interval is empty, the restricted conditions are vacuous.
TorusEuler.exists_scaledFlow_on_Icc.summary: Bounded Lipschitz fields have flows on the whole slab

TorusEuler.exists_scaledFlow_with_deform.text: A bounded smooth finite-dimensional field with derivative bound $K$ and projected derivative bound $M$ has a two-time flow on a time slab $[l,r]$ when $K(r-l)\le1/2$. The output includes restart, differentiability, derivative norm at most two, and projected-displacement derivative at most $2M|t-s|$. These are properties of an actual constructed flow rather than estimates for a hypothetical variational matrix.
TorusEuler.exists_scaledFlow_with_deform.summary: A scaled flow with quantitative derivative control

TorusEuler.exists_scaled_wavePhaseJetBou.text: At every finite order, a constant at least one bounds the mixed jets of both $F_h(hs)$ and its normalized primitive $P_h(hs)$ by $Ch$, uniformly for $0<h\le1$. The profiles are independent of the label variable. The same chosen constant covers both functions, which allows the velocity and pressure estimates to share one phase budget.
TorusEuler.exists_scaled_wavePhaseJetBou.summary: Both normalized phase profiles have uniformly small jets

TorusEuler.exists_scheduledEulerConstruc.text: Given uniform physical estimates and a schedule-selection hypothesis, constructs scheduled Euler data for every sufficiently large initial frequency. The schedule may impose an additional property depending on the radius exponent. The conclusion fixes one exponent parameter and one monotone threshold function before that frequency is varied, and it retains the requested radius floor and additional property.
TorusEuler.exists_scheduledEulerConstruc.summary: A compatible numerical schedule gives one physical construction

TorusEuler.exists_scheduledEulerConstruc.text: For a finite index type and uniform physical estimates, uses the general numerical schedule theorem to construct a scheduled Euler sequence above any prescribed initial-frequency floor. It fixes the exponent parameter and monotone threshold function uniformly for all sufficiently large initial frequencies. The strength constant is the explicit value $18e^3$.
TorusEuler.exists_scheduledEulerConstruc.summary: The basic schedule satisfies all selected physical budgets

TorusEuler.exists_slabTimeJet_torusFouri.text: Let $a<b$, $R\in\mathbb R$, and let $f(t,x)$ be jointly smooth on $[a,b]\times\mathbb R^3$ and periodic in space for $t\in[a,b]$. Suppose for each $t\in[a,b]$ a continuous torus field $g(t)$ represents $f(t,\cdot)$ and has vanishing Fourier coefficients at all integer $k$ with $|k|>R$. Then for every $q$ there are continuous torus fields $g_q(t)$ such that, for every $t\in[a,b]$, $g_q(t)$ represents $\partial_t^qf(t,\cdot)$, the time derivative taken within $[a,b]$, and has vanishing Fourier coefficients for $|k|>R$.
TorusEuler.exists_slabTimeJet_torusFouri.summary: Time differentiation preserves a fixed Fourier band

TorusEuler.exists_smoothExtensionOfClose.text: Smooth extension in both time directions, retaining agreement at the left endpoint of the original closed slab.
TorusEuler.exists_smoothExtensionOfClose.summary: Extending a smooth field beyond the closed time slab

TorusEuler.exists_smooth_meanZero_L2_app.text: Given $T>0$, $\varepsilon>0$, and an $L^2$ path $v$ with zero interval integral, there is a globally smooth path with the same zero integral and $L^2$ error below $\varepsilon$. The conclusion does not require the approximant to retain compact support after subtracting its mean.
TorusEuler.exists_smooth_meanZero_L2_app.summary: Approximating zero mean paths by smooth ones

TorusEuler.exists_spatialHolderHalfNorm_.text: Smooth spatially periodic fields on a nondegenerate compact time slab have a uniform spatial half-Hölder norm at every finite order.
TorusEuler.exists_spatialHolderHalfNorm_.summary: Smooth periodic fields have uniform finite Hölder norms

TorusEuler.exists_spatialHolderHalfNorm_.text: Fix an integer $n\ge0$. Suppose a periodic field and all its ordered coordinate derivatives through order $n$ are represented by half-Hölder fields, with the actual differentiation identities, and every such field has norm at most $K\ge0$. Then the $C^{n,1/2}$ norm of the original field is at most $C_nK$, where $C_n$ is chosen before the fields and $K$. This converts the differentiated-equation estimates in Lemma A.2 into the paper's full higher norm. Arbitrary bounded fields with derivative labels would not satisfy the required differentiation hypotheses.
TorusEuler.exists_spatialHolderHalfNorm_.summary: Control the higher Hölder norm using genuine derivatives

TorusEuler.exists_spatiallyPeriodic_cont.text: Let $J\subset\mathbb R$ be open and $A\subset\mathbb R$ any time set, and let $g(t,x)$ be smooth on $J\times(\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3)$ with $g=f$ on $A\times(\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3)$, where $f(t,\cdot)$ is periodic under integer translations for every $t\in A$. Then there is $G$, smooth on $J\times(\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3)$, with $G=f$ on $A\times(\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3)$ and $G(t,\cdot)$ periodic under integer translations for every real $t$. No equation or divergence condition is asserted for $G$.
TorusEuler.exists_spatiallyPeriodic_cont.summary: A smooth extension can be made spatially periodic

TorusEuler.exists_sub_latticeVector_mem_.text: Every point of the lift has a representative in the centered cell.
TorusEuler.exists_sub_latticeVector_mem_.summary: Every spatial point has a centered representative

TorusEuler.exists_summable_bound_dyadic_.text: For dyadic kernels with numerator scale $2^{j(3+m)}$ and decay order $m+4$, bounded observation points separated from every lattice singularity admit a summable majorant over both scale and translation. One surplus decay power produces geometric decay in $j$; the spatial exponent exceeds dimension three. Positive separation is essential.
TorusEuler.exists_summable_bound_dyadic_.summary: Separation makes the scale and lattice sum converge together

TorusEuler.exists_summable_bound_lattice.text: A kernel with decay order above three has a summable lattice majorant uniform for observation points with norm at most $R$. The assumptions require nonnegative amplitude and radius and scale at least one. The triangle inequality compares translated distances with lattice size, giving a bound independent of the observation point.
TorusEuler.exists_summable_bound_lattice.summary: Polynomial decay uniformly controls all translates on bounded sets

TorusEuler.exists_switchRate_threshold.text: Given nonnegative constants $C$ and $K$, one threshold works for every parent frequency $\mu$ above it and every $0\le L\le(\log\mu)^2$. If $r\le K\mu^{1/8}L$, then $Cre^3\le\mu$. The proof absorbs the logarithmic factor into $\mu^{7/8}$; it does not require a separate positivity hypothesis on $r$.
TorusEuler.exists_switchRate_threshold.summary: A logarithmic growth rate fits below the parent frequency

TorusEuler.exists_switchedLeadingProfile.text: For each order, chooses one constant controlling the rescaled leading velocity and frequency-weighted pressure. The hypotheses explicitly assume smoothness and jet budgets for the slow envelope-amplitude factor and the pressure coefficient; those budgets are not derived here from a parent flow. Multiplication by the scaled phase profiles supplies the remaining frequency factor, giving bounds proportional to $\gamma\lambda^{-5/4}$.
TorusEuler.exists_switchedLeadingProfile.summary: Slow factor bounds produce the full leading jet estimates

TorusEuler.exists_tendstoUniformlyOn_cut.text: For a compact target, a continuous cutoff between zero and one, and periodic separation from the complementary support, uniform convergence of continuous velocities on the closed cell yields convergence of every far pressure gradient jet on one open target neighborhood. No convergence of source derivatives is required. The proof combines an integrable tensor difference with the smooth separated kernel bound.
TorusEuler.exists_tendstoUniformlyOn_cut.summary: Uniform velocity limits suffice for every separated pressure derivative

TorusEuler.exists_tendstoUniformlyOn_pre.text: Smooth periodic velocities converging uniformly on the closed cell and in every jet on compact sets off the lattice have pressure gradients converging in every jet on an open neighborhood of each compact target contained in $\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3$. The limit velocity is continuous globally, smooth off the lattice and periodic. A smooth local limiting pressure is constructed by adding the near multiplier pressure to the far kernel pressure.
TorusEuler.exists_tendstoUniformlyOn_pre.summary: Global values and local jets determine the terminal pressure gradient

TorusEuler.exists_terminalBorelAtom_fder.text: Let $\beta_{n,\varepsilon}(t)=\varepsilon^n\phi_n(t/\varepsilon)$, where $\phi_n(t)=(t^n/n!)\chi(t)$ and $\chi$ is a fixed smooth bump equal to one for $|t|\le1$ and vanishing for $|t|\ge2$. For every pair of orders $n,k$ there is a constant $A\ge0$ such that for every scale $\varepsilon>0$ and every time $t$, $\|\beta_{n,\varepsilon}^{(k)}(t)\|\le A\,\varepsilon^n\varepsilon^{-k}$. The constant is independent of $\varepsilon$ and $t$, and no ordering of $k$ and $n$ is required.
TorusEuler.exists_terminalBorelAtom_fder.summary: Derivative bounds for a shrinking Borel atom

TorusEuler.exists_terminalBorelAtom_fder.text: Let $\beta_{n,\varepsilon}(t)=\varepsilon^n\phi_n(t/\varepsilon)$, where $\phi_n(t)=(t^n/n!)\chi(t)$ and $\chi$ is a fixed smooth bump equal to one for $|t|\le1$ and vanishing for $|t|\ge2$. For orders $k\le n$ there is a constant $A\ge0$ such that $\|\beta_{n,\varepsilon}^{(k)}(t)\|\le A\,\varepsilon^{n-k}$ for every $\varepsilon>0$ and every time $t$. For $k=n$ there is no small factor; strictly lower orders become small as $\varepsilon\to0$.
TorusEuler.exists_terminalBorelAtom_fder.summary: Lower derivative bounds gain a positive scale power

TorusEuler.exists_terminalBorelAtom_fder.text: Let $\beta_{n,\varepsilon}(t)=\varepsilon^n\phi_n(t/\varepsilon)$, where $\phi_n(t)=(t^n/n!)\chi(t)$ and $\chi$ is a fixed smooth bump equal to one for $|t|\le1$ and vanishing for $|t|\ge2$. Given nonnegative weights $W_k$ ($k\ge0$) and a tolerance $\delta>0$, there is $\varepsilon$ with $0<\varepsilon\le1$ such that $W_k\|\beta_{n,\varepsilon}^{(k)}(t)\|\le\delta$ for every order $k<n$ and every time $t$. When $n=0$ the requirement is empty.
TorusEuler.exists_terminalBorelAtom_fder.summary: One radius makes all lower derivatives small

TorusEuler.exists_terminalBorelExtension.text: Let $E$ be a real normed space and $F$ a complete real normed space. For every sequence $a_0,a_1,\dots$ of smooth compactly supported maps $E\to F$, there is a jointly smooth $G:\mathbb R\times E\to F$ such that for every $n$ and every $x\in E$, the $n$-th derivative of $t\mapsto G(t,x)$ at $t=0$ equals $a_n(x)$. This is an existence statement, not a continuous linear extension operator.
TorusEuler.exists_terminalBorelExtension.summary: A smooth field with prescribed time derivatives at zero

TorusEuler.exists_terminalBoundaryLocali.text: Let $E$ be finite-dimensional, $t_0<T$, $O\subseteq E$ open, $f$ smooth on $[t_0,T]\times O$, and $x\in O$. Then there are an open set $V$ with $x\in V\subseteq O$ and smooth compactly supported maps $g_0,g_1,\dots$ on $E$ such that for every $n$ and every $y\in V$, $g_n(y)$ equals the $n$-th time derivative of $f$ at $(T,y)$ computed within $[t_0,T]\times O$. One neighbourhood $V$ serves all orders at once.
TorusEuler.exists_terminalBoundaryLocali.summary: Localizing all terminal time derivatives near one point

TorusEuler.exists_terminalCutoffStress_h.text: Fix a smooth unit cutoff multiplier and depth $d\ge2$. A nonnegative constant $A$ is chosen before the radius and the two input fields. For positive $\Lambda$ and spatially $C^{d,1/2}$ inputs $g,h$, the divergence of $S_\Lambda g\otimes S_\Lambda h-S_\Lambda(g\otimes h)$ has $C^{1,1/2}$ norm at most $A\Lambda^{2-d}$ times their $C^{d,1/2}$ norms. The two-derivative loss accounts for divergence and the final Hölder order.
TorusEuler.exists_terminalCutoffStress_h.summary: Bound the divergence of a bilinear cutoff stress

TorusEuler.exists_terminalFlowLinearJetB.text: Given constants $R(n),W(n)\ge0$ and a time order $q$, there are constants $C(n)\ge0$ such that the following holds. Let $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge1$, $A\ge1$, let $U$ be jointly smooth on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3$ and periodic in space, and $X$ a flow of $U$ on $[0,T]$. Assume $\|D_xX(0,t,x)\|\le\mathsf D$ and $\|D_yX(t,0,y)\|\le\mathsf D$ at $y=X(0,t,x)$ for $t\in[0,T]$; $\|D_x^jU(t,x)\|\le R(n)\mathsf D^j$ for $1\le j\le n$; and $U$ satisfies the mixed bounds on $[0,T]$ through time order $q$ with slope $1$, amplitude $A$ and constants $W(n)$. Let $k$ be a vector, $\lambda>0$, $t_0\in[0,T]$ with $|G(t_0,0)^{\mathsf T}k|=\lambda$, where $G(t,x)=D_yX(t,0,y)$ at $y=X(0,t,x)$. Then the forward deformation $D_xX(0,t,x)$, the inverse deformation $G(t,x)$, the material gradient $D_xU(t,X(0,t,x))$ and the normalized covector $\lambda^{-1}G(t,x)^{\mathsf T}k$ all satisfy the mixed bounds on $[0,T]$ through time order $q$ with slope $16$, constants $C(n)$ and amplitude $g+f+\mathsf Df$, where $g=A\mathsf D(1+\mathsf DA)^q$ and $f=\mathsf D g^q$.
TorusEuler.exists_terminalFlowLinearJetB.summary: The flow coefficients share one spatial growth slope

TorusEuler.exists_terminalMaterialIterat.text: For nonnegative sequences $C_U,C_0$ and orders $j,q$ there is a nonnegative sequence $C$ such that: if $a<b$, $\mathsf D,A,A_U\ge0$, $U$ and $f$ are smooth on $[a,b]\times\mathbb R^3$, and through time order $q+j$ one has $\|D_x^n\partial_t^iU\|\le C_U(n)A_U\mathsf D^{pn}$ and $\|D_x^n\partial_t^if\|\le C_0(n)A\mathsf D^{pn}$, then $(\partial_t+U\cdot\nabla)^jf$ satisfies, through time order $q$, $\|D_x^n\partial_t^i(\cdot)\|\le C(n)\,A(1+\mathsf D^pA_U)^j\,\mathsf D^{pn}$.
TorusEuler.exists_terminalMaterialIterat.summary: Material iteration preserves a fixed spatial derivative slope

TorusEuler.exists_terminalMaterialPullba.text: For nonnegative sequences $C_U,C_0,C_X$ and an order $q$ there is a nonnegative sequence $C$ such that: if $T>0$, $\mathsf D\ge1$, $A,A_U\ge0$, $X$ is the flow of $U$ on $[0,T]$, $U,f$ are smooth, $U(t)$ is periodic, through time order $q$ one has $\|D_x^n\partial_t^iU\|\le C_U(n)A_U\mathsf D^n$ and $\|D_x^n\partial_t^if\|\le C_0(n)A\mathsf D^n$, and $\|D^jX(0,t)\|\le C_X(j)\mathsf D^{5j}$ for $j\ge1$, then $(t,x)\mapsto f(t,X(0,t,x))$ satisfies, through time order $q$, $\|D_x^n\partial_t^i(\cdot)\|\le C(n)\,A(1+\mathsf DA_U)^q\,\mathsf D^{6n}$.
TorusEuler.exists_terminalMaterialPullba.summary: Pullback time derivatives have spatial slope six

TorusEuler.exists_terminalMeanCoefficien.text: For fixed $q$ and nonnegative input constants, this selects three constant families for the algebraic mean coefficients. Smooth matrix fields $F,M$ with common mixed bound of amplitude $A$ and spatial slope $p$ yield amplitude $A^2$ for $F^*F$ and $A^3$ for the vorticity form and $2F^*MF$. It assumes neither that $F$ is a flow derivative nor that $F_t=MF$; applications supply that interpretation.
TorusEuler.exists_terminalMeanCoefficien.summary: Mean coefficients inherit the supplied mixed derivative bounds

TorusEuler.exists_terminalMeanParentInve.text: For every sequence $R_n\ge0$ there exist integers $p,s_0$ with $2(p+9)\le s_0$ and a sequence $H_n\ge0$ such that the following holds. Let $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$, $0\le L\le\mathsf D$, let $U$ be jointly smooth on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3$ and periodic in space with label flow $X$ on $[0,T]$, with $\|D_aX_{0\to t}\|\le\mathsf D$ and $\|D X_{t\to0}(X_{0\to t}(a))\|\le\mathsf D$, and $\|D^kU(t,x)\|\le R_n\mathsf D^k$ for $1\le k\le n$. Let $F,M$ be smooth matrix fields on the torus slab with $F=D_aX_{0\to t}$ and $M=D_xU\circ X_{0\to t}$. Then every recovered physical mean solution with these data carries the inverse data of the preceding structure with power $\mathsf D^p$, and for every $s\ge s_0$ and every word $q$ with $|q|\ge1$, with $\ell=\mathsf D^{-s}$, $\ell^{|q|}\big(\sup_{[0,T]}\|K_q\|_{C^{1/2}}+\sup_{[0,T]}\|\Omega_q\|_{C^{1/2}}\big)\le H_{|q|}\mathsf D^9\sqrt\ell$, where $K_q,\Omega_q$ are the recovered half-Hölder words of $K=F^{\mathsf T}F$ and $\Omega=F^{\mathsf T}(M^{\mathsf T}-M)F$.
TorusEuler.exists_terminalMeanParentInve.summary: The parent flow supplies both inverse bounds and word bounds

TorusEuler.exists_terminalSmoothExtensio.text: Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional real normed space, $F$ a real Banach space, $O\subset E$ open, and $a<T$. If $f:[a,T]\times O\to F$ is jointly smooth up to the time boundary, the formal statement gives $g$ smooth on $(a,\infty)\times O$ and equal to $f$ on the entire original closed slab. Values of $g$ are defined elsewhere but have no asserted regularity there. This is the extension step needed in the auxiliary note. Seeley's theorem on page 625 supplies a continuous linear extension operator; this formal conclusion asserts existence for each field and does not state linearity or continuity of a choice of extension. It imposes no differential equation beyond $T$.
TorusEuler.exists_terminalSmoothExtensio.summary: Smooth boundary data extend to every later time

TorusEuler.exists_terminalTimeCutoffResi.text: This chooses a nonnegative constant $C_r$ and costs $C_t(q,P)$ before the stage, radius, or fields. For a smooth periodic approximate velocity and residual, positive $T$ and $\Lambda$, $i\le q$, and depth $P\ge2$, a common depth-norm bound $M$ on velocity jets through order $i$ gives a $C^{1,1/2}$ residual bound $C_r\|\partial_t^iR_V\|+C_t\Lambda^{2-P}M^2$ at every slab time. The input residual norm has order one. Only $C_t$ may depend on the time order and depth.
TorusEuler.exists_terminalTimeCutoffResi.summary: Choose uniform constants for the differentiated cutoff residual

TorusEuler.exists_terminalWaveRelayGeome.text: Fix a nonnegative cost array and time order. A single output array is chosen before the positive slab and scales $\mathsf D,A\ge1$. Mixed bounds for a smooth inverse coframe $G$ and strain $M$ yield all three geometric row bounds with common amplitude $|\ell^{-1}|A^2$ and spatial slope sixteen. The statement permits label width $\ell=0$, when both the rows and the displayed amplitude vanish algebraically.
TorusEuler.exists_terminalWaveRelayGeome.summary: One mixed bound controls all geometric relay rows

TorusEuler.exists_terminalWaveRelayPoten.text: From a nonnegative input cost array $C_n$ and fixed time order $q$, this chooses one nonnegative output array before the slab or coefficient fields. On a positive time slab $[0,T]$, assume smooth nonvanishing covectors $k$, smooth strain $M$, scales $\mathsf D,A\ge1$, and mixed bounds for $M$, $k$ and $|k|^{-2}$ with amplitude $A$ and spatial slope sixteen. The four actual relay coefficients are smooth and satisfy mixed bounds with common amplitude $A^6$ and spatial slope sixteen, that is, with factor $\mathsf D^{16n}$ at spatial order $n$.
TorusEuler.exists_terminalWaveRelayPoten.summary: All normalized potential and pressure coefficients share a bound

TorusEuler.exists_theorem11Witness_of_in.text: Chooses a universal base-frequency threshold. Above it, any compatible stage family and matching central waves yield a positive common terminal time, an Euler velocity and pressure satisfying all conclusions of Theorem 1.1, together with closed-slab uniform convergence of the original stages. The family and matching waves remain hypotheses. This theorem does not independently construct the local successor steps.
TorusEuler.exists_theorem11Witness_of_in.summary: Compatible stages produce one Euler singularity witness

TorusEuler.exists_truncatedParentPoisson.text:
Let $T>0$ and let a continuous torus velocity have a smooth lift $u$ on $[0,T]	imes\mathbb R^3$, with $\operatorname{div}u=0$ and Fourier support $|\xi|\le2\Lambda$ at every time. A jointly smooth periodic pressure $p$ exists with zero integral over the centered unit cell and $\Delta p=-\operatorname{tr}((
abla u)^2)$. Moreover $u_t+u\cdot
abla u+
abla p=u_t+\mathbb P(u\cdot
abla u)$ on the closed interval, with time derivatives taken from within it. This supplies the pressure choice and projected residual formula in §5.1. The theorem does not require $u$ to solve Euler and does not conclude that this residual vanishes.
TorusEuler.exists_truncatedParentPoisson.summary: Construct the periodic Poisson pressure and identify the projected residual

TorusEuler.exists_truncatedParent_T1.text: From a smooth periodic odd divergence-free velocity on a nondegenerate closed slab, chooses continuous torus representatives and proves the cutoff has joint smoothness, oddness, incompressibility and the retained frequency band. The symbol is assumed even, but its scale is arbitrary here. The chosen representatives are zero outside the slab; every representation and regularity claim is restricted to the slab.
TorusEuler.exists_truncatedParent_T1.summary: Truncation supplies the smooth odd incompressible parent

TorusEuler.exists_uniformJetBounds_of_co.text: For a globally smooth family $f$, periodic in its spatial argument, compactness of the parameter set $K$ gives nonnegative constants $B_m$ controlling both joint and spatial derivatives of every order. Periodicity reduces arbitrary labels to the centered cell. The constants depend on the family and $K$, not on the chosen parameter or label.
TorusEuler.exists_uniformJetBounds_of_co.summary: Uniform derivative bounds for a periodic family

TorusEuler.exists_uniformLimit_of_summab.text: In a complete metric target, a summable sequence $b_n$ bounding consecutive distances $d(F_n(x),F_{n+1}(x))$ on $s$ from grade $N$ gives a uniform limit on $s$ and the explicit tail bound $\sum_kb_{n+k}$. Outside $s$, the constructed function is assigned the value of the first approximant $F_0$. The proof requires no global continuity and asserts convergence only on the specified set.
TorusEuler.exists_uniformLimit_of_summab.summary: Summable increments produce a uniform limit and tail bound

TorusEuler.exists_uniformLimit_of_vanish.text: When each consecutive increment splits as $F_{n+1}-F_n=B_n+O_n$, and the oscillatory part $O_n$ vanishes on $s$ from grade $N$, summable bounds on $B_n$ give uniform convergence and the corresponding tail estimate. The hypotheses are pointwise on the stated set. No smallness of oscillations outside that set is used.
TorusEuler.exists_uniformLimit_of_vanish.summary: Vanishing oscillations leave a summable correction series

TorusEuler.exists_uniform_concrete_freez.text: For a fixed angular derivative budget $J\ge1$, one nonnegative constant works across the quantified real Hilbert spaces and their complexifications. The symbol must be a smooth homogeneous symmetric projection with five controlled derivatives; the strong projector must have its Fourier law and pairing. Positive coercivity and spatial Lipschitz bounds then give the compressed inverse estimate with power $145$.
TorusEuler.exists_uniform_concrete_freez.summary: One inverse constant works for all permitted coefficient spaces

TorusEuler.exists_uniform_freezingHalfHo.text: Let $r(\xi)$ be orthogonal projections on a real Hilbert space with a compatible complete complexification, smooth for $\xi\ne0$, with $\|D^ir(\xi)\|\le D^i$ for $0\le i\le5$ on $1/2\le|\xi|\le2$, where $D\ge1$. Suppose $B$ has coercivity $\mu>0$ on every projected range, including the zero-frequency range. Put $Q=2+\mu^{-1}+\|B\|$. The formal statement bounds the two Fourier operators constructed from the inverse symbols by $CQ^{11}$ on $C^{0,1/2}$. For $r_0>0$ and a source vanishing in the closed $r_0$-ball about $a$, the second operator has increments at most $KQ^{11}r_0^{-1}\|f\|_\infty d(a,b)$ when $d(a,b)\le r_0/4$. The constants depend only on $D$ and the fixed cutoff. Identifying these operators with $A_0(D)^{-1}$ and $A_0(D)^{-1}\mathcal R$ uses the separate Fourier identity, which also assumes degree-zero homogeneity. This estimate alone does not impose homogeneity; the paper's Leray symbols have it.
TorusEuler.exists_uniform_freezingHalfHo.summary: Control the inverse and its action away from the source

TorusEuler.exists_uniform_log_gain_budge.text: For finitely many nonnegative constants, natural gain powers, and positive frequency exponents, one threshold works for the entire family. Above it, every $0\le L\le(\log\mu)^2$ satisfies $C_kL^{p_k}\le\mu^{a_k}$. Finiteness of the index type is essential to choosing a common threshold; the bound does not cover an arbitrary infinite family.
TorusEuler.exists_uniform_log_gain_budge.summary: A finite family of logarithmic losses shares one threshold

TorusEuler.exists_waveSwitch_iteratedDer.text: There is one nonnegative array $C_q$ such that, for every positive rate $r$, activation time $t_0$, and time $t$, the absolute value of the $q$th derivative of the switch is at most $C_qr^q$. The constants are chosen before all clock parameters. Compactness of $[0,1]$ bounds positive derivatives of the transition, while order zero uses its bound by one.
TorusEuler.exists_waveSwitch_iteratedDer.summary: Choose switch derivative constants independently of the physical clock

TorusEuler.exists_waveSwitch_scheduled_w.text: There is a fixed constant $C\ge0$ depending only on the chosen smooth time transition. Let $r>0$, $\lambda_+>0$, and suppose $|\gamma(t)|\le e^{3-4\log\lambda_+}$ on $[t_0,t_0+1/r]$. If $Cre^3\le\mu$, the formal theorem gives $|\widetilde\chi'(t)|\,|\gamma(t)|\le\mu\lambda_+^{-4}$ for every real $t$, where $\widetilde\chi(t)=1-\chi(1+r(t-t_0))$. The weight need not be continuous or bounded outside the switching interval, because the cutoff derivative vanishes there. With $\lambda_+=\lambda_{j+1}$ this is the numerical implication used in (7.10), conditional on the early-gain and rate bounds.
TorusEuler.exists_waveSwitch_scheduled_w.summary: Combines the early amplitude gain with the cutoff derivative

TorusEuler.exists_waveSwitch_weighted_it.text: Choose nonnegative constants uniformly in the clock and weight. For positive $q$ and $r$, if $|\gamma|\le G$ only on the closed switching interval $[t_0,t_0+1/r]$ and $G\ge0$, then the $q$th switch derivative times $|\gamma(t)|$ is bounded everywhere by $C_qr^qG$. No continuity or bound on $\gamma$ outside that interval is required because the derivative vanishes there.
TorusEuler.exists_waveSwitch_weighted_it.summary: A small weight is needed only during switching

TorusEuler.exists_weighted_iteratedFDeri.text: For each derivative order $m$, there is a positive constant $C$ such that $\ell^m\|D^mg_\ell(x)\|\le C$ for every radius $\ell>0$ and every label $x$, where $g_\ell$ is the radial envelope of radius $\ell$. Multiplication by $\ell^m$ cancels the inverse-radius factor from the raw derivative estimate. Uniformity concerns radius and position; the theorem does not give one common constant across all derivative orders.
TorusEuler.exists_weighted_iteratedFDeri.summary: Radius-weighted envelope derivatives have a uniform bound

TorusEuler.farKernelIntegral.text: The expression integrates the action of an operator-valued kernel $K(x,y)$ on a density $P(y)$ over the supplied measure. The definition itself accepts arbitrary inputs. Its later estimates establish integrability, measurability, and uniform kernel bounds so that the expression represents the intended far pressure contribution.
TorusEuler.farKernelIntegral.summary: A separated kernel acts on an integrable source density

TorusEuler.farPressureCutoffTensor.text: The far tensor field is $(1-\chi)v\otimes v$ in complex coordinates. It is the density integrated against the pressure kernel on the separated source portion of the fundamental cell. Bounds $0\le\chi\le1$ later make its difference no larger than the uncut quadratic tensor difference.
TorusEuler.farPressureCutoffTensor.summary: Keep the quadratic tensor outside the near cutoff

TorusEuler.farPressureCutoffTensor_eq_ze.text: At a point of the kernel cell outside the far source set, the far tensor is zero. Since that point already lies in the cell closure, it must lie outside the topological support of $1-\chi$, forcing the scalar factor to vanish. This support certificate allows the multiplier integral to be restricted to the source set.
TorusEuler.farPressureCutoffTensor_eq_ze.summary: The far density vanishes outside its source enclosure

TorusEuler.farPressureSourceSet.text: The far source set is the intersection of the closure of the half-open kernel cell with the topological support of $1-\chi$. Including the closure makes this set compact. Actual far integration still uses its intersection with the half-open cell, avoiding duplicate lattice boundary representatives.
TorusEuler.farPressureSourceSet.summary: The far source occupies a compact portion of one cell

TorusEuler.fderivWithin_hierarchyProfile.text: For positive slab length, a profile with reflection multiplier $\epsilon$, so that $f(t,-a,-s)=\epsilon f(t,a,s)$, has a derivative obeying the reflected chain rule. At the reflected point, the derivative applied to the reflected direction equals $\epsilon$ times the original derivative. The statement allows an arbitrary real $\epsilon$, with its compatibility supplied by the reflection hypothesis on $f$.

If a direction $d$ is sent to $-d$ by the reflection $(a,s)\mapsto(-a,-s)$, differentiating a profile of reflection multiplier $\epsilon$ in that fixed direction gives multiplier $-\epsilon$. This follows from the reflected derivative identity and linearity in the direction. Spatial label and phase directions are the intended applications.
TorusEuler.fderivWithin_hierarchyProfile.summary: A reversed direction reverses the derivative’s parity

TorusEuler.fderiv_fourierMode.text: The derivative of the Fourier mode $e^{2\pi ik\cdot x}$ in the real direction $v$ equals $2\pi i(k\cdot v)$ times that mode. The direction need not be a coordinate vector. This is the basic differential-symbol formula used to identify divergence, gradient, and Laplacian on finite Fourier sums.
TorusEuler.fderiv_fourierMode.summary: A directional derivative multiplies by the frequency pairing

TorusEuler.fderiv_fourierMode_single.text: The derivative of the mode $e^{2\pi ik\cdot x}$ along the coordinate unit vector $e_i$ is the mode multiplied by the derivative symbol $2\pi ik_i$. This is the coordinate specialization of the directional formula. It fixes the derivative convention subsequently used to compute the divergence and gradient of synthesized polynomials.
TorusEuler.fderiv_fourierMode_single.summary: Coordinate differentiation applies the Fourier derivative symbol

TorusEuler.fderiv_frozenSymbol_inverse_a.text: Let $r$ be an orthogonal projection on a real Hilbert space, and suppose $\langle Bw,w\rangle\ge\mu\|w\|^2$ on its range, with $\mu>0$. Set $A=rBr+I-r$. The derivative of the inverse as $r$ varies in direction $h$ is $D(A^{-1})[h]=-A^{-1}(hBr+rBh-h)A^{-1}$. Coercivity ensures that $A$ is invertible at the point of differentiation. The formal statement concerns variations of the real operator $r$; composing with the frequency-dependent projection and passing to complex Fourier coefficients are additional steps needed in Appendix A.1.
TorusEuler.fderiv_frozenSymbol_inverse_a.summary: Differentiate with respect to the projection operator

TorusEuler.fderiv_gradient_add_three_pre.text: The graph pressure Hessian is the sum of the three physical Hessians.
TorusEuler.fderiv_gradient_add_three_pre.summary: The pressure Hessian splits into three contributions

TorusEuler.fderiv_gradient_single_coord.text: Let $f:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ be $C^2$, $x\in\mathbb R^3$ and $i,j\in\{1,2,3\}$. Then the $j$th component of the derivative of $\nabla f$ at $x$ in the direction $e_i$ equals $\partial_i(\partial_jf)(x)$. This identifies the matrix-valued Hessian with scalar mixed derivatives in the stated order, without using symmetry of mixed partials.
TorusEuler.fderiv_gradient_single_coord.summary: A Hessian entry is the corresponding mixed partial derivative

TorusEuler.fderiv_halfHolderProjectionLi.text: For periodic $f$ of class $C^{1,1/2}$, the Fréchet derivative of its projected lift equals the lift of its derivative projected directionwise. The hypothesis that $P$ commutes with actual line derivatives supplies the commutation. The proof reconstructs a Fréchet derivative from continuous directional derivatives, so the equality is backed by differentiability rather than by the default zero value of an undefined derivative.
TorusEuler.fderiv_halfHolderProjectionLi.summary: Differentiation commutes with the lifted projection

TorusEuler.fderiv_liftConvolution_eq_lif.text: For an integrable scalar kernel and a $C^1$ function with globally bounded value and derivative, the Fréchet derivative of the lift convolution equals convolution with the derivative. The bounds $M$ on the value and $M'$ on the derivative provide domination for differentiation under the integral. The result is an operator-valued derivative equality, not merely a directional estimate.
TorusEuler.fderiv_liftConvolution_eq_lif.summary: One bounded derivative passes through convolution

TorusEuler.fderiv_lift_finiteFourierSum_.text: The coordinate derivative of a finite Fourier synthesis is the synthesis of its coefficients multiplied by the corresponding derivative symbols. The same finite frequency set is used on both sides. This makes differentiation compatible with the algebraic mode calculations without any interchange of infinite sums.
TorusEuler.fderiv_lift_finiteFourierSum_.summary: Differentiating a polynomial multiplies each coefficient

TorusEuler.fderiv_lift_realVectorFourier.text: Let $g$ and $d$ be continuous $\mathbb R^3$-valued fields on $\mathbb T^3=\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3$.
