TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_holde.text: For $0<\ell\le1$, smooth fields and bounded supremum jet sets through order $n+1$, the half-Hölder word norm at order $n$ is at most four times the next-order supremum norm divided by $\sqrt\ell$. The explicit factor four reflects the value term and three label directions under the max convention for Hölder norms.
TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_holde.summary: One derivative controls the half-Hölder finite norm

TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_le_of.text: Suppose continuous torus words through order $N$ lift to the actual spatial derivatives of a smooth velocity, and each weighted time norm is at most $B$. The finite half-Hölder label norm of that velocity is at most the number of admissible words times $B$. The lift identities are essential: arbitrary bounded auxiliary fields would not control these derivatives.
TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_le_of.summary: Recovered torus words bound the label norm

TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_linea.text: An all-order bound for the normalized linear relay assembled from the actual curl, its commutator, and the inverse-coframe gradient. Each row has its own coefficient budget and every primitive profile is used at order $n+1$. The single inverse frequency is common to them.
TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_linea.summary: All-order derivative bounds for the linear relay

TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_mono_.text: Adding higher orders can only increase the finite mixed norm.
TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_mono_.summary: Increasing the derivative order increases the finite norm

TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_phase.text: For smooth profiles with one-periodic, zero-mean phase slices and bounded admissible derivative words, the normalized phase primitive has finite word norm at most twice that of the input. Every constant weighted direction is retained. This is the supremum version of the finite norm, without Hölder quotients, not its Hölder extension.
TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_phase.summary: Phase integration costs at most a factor of two

TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_physi.text: A smooth operator field multiplying a smooth recovered label velocity has a finite supremum-word bound controlled by the operator's half-Hölder norm and the common weighted bound on actual recovered derivative representatives. The hypotheses explicitly identify those representatives with derivatives of $v$. The operator field is generic here; its role as $D_aX$ in the physical mean is supplied by the application.
TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_physi.summary: The deformation converts the recovered bound to physical velocity

TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_pulle.text: A pulled-back curl costs one weighted label derivative and one coframe coefficient. The inverse frequency commutes with all spatial and phase derivatives.
TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_pulle.summary: A slow curl costs one weighted label derivative

TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_restr.text: Composing the time index with any map from a parameter set $S$ into the original time set cannot increase the finite-word norm, provided the original measurement sets are bounded above. Every sample in the restricted family is already a sample in the original family. The map need not be injective or represent an interval inclusion.
TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_restr.summary: Restricting the time parameter cannot enlarge the measurement

TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_sup_l.text: A common bound on the pointwise mixed jets controls their exact sum with only the number of admissible multi-indices as a factor.
TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_sup_l.summary: A common derivative bound controls the finite sum

TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_unitL.text: At label radius one, smooth fields whose jets through order two satisfy $C_mD^{pm+q}$ have order-one half-Hölder norm bounded by an explicit sum of constants times $D^{2p+q}$. Only the first three derivative orders are assumed. This is used to bound the coefficient norm entering the low-order mean inverse.
TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_unitL.summary: Two derivatives bound the low-order coefficient input

TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_waveC.text: The divergence correction built from the wave potential is bounded in the finite supremum word norm by an explicit constant times $\lambda^{-1}$. The hypotheses supply smooth periodic zero-mean velocity, coefficient budgets for the normalized potential and inverse-coframe rows, a nonzero label scale, and positive frequency. The velocity budget is needed at order $n+1$.
TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_waveC.summary: The actual curl correction gains inverse frequency at finite order

TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_waveL.text: The actual four-term relay formed from potential, potential-time profile, and phase pressure has finite word norm bounded by an explicit order constant times $K^2\lambda^{-1}(V_0+F_0)$. The theorem assumes smooth periodic zero-mean profiles, their order-$(n+1)$ bounds, and all named normalized coefficient budgets. It estimates a spatial expression; identifying it with the actual time derivative requires the separate derivative lemmas.
TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_waveL.summary: The full linear relay retains one inverse-frequency factor

TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordSeminorm.text: A linear slice map with smooth values and bounded measurement sets gives a seminorm by summing the actual real suprema over admissible words. The boundedness hypothesis is required for every input and relevant word. This establishes triangle inequality and absolute homogeneity, rather than merely naming an arbitrary real-valued expression a norm.
TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordSeminorm.summary: The finite derivative measurements form a genuine seminorm

TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordSeminorm_a.text: Evaluating the constructed finite-word seminorm gives exactly the finite-word norm, the sum of suprema over admissible words, of the linear slice map’s output. The equality is definitional. Its smoothness and boundedness arguments certify that the underlying real suprema have the intended analytic meaning, while the formula itself is unchanged by the seminorm construction.
TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordSeminorm_a.summary: The seminorm evaluates to the actual sum of suprema

TorusEuler.hierarchyGraphPoint.text: For any label map $A(t,x)$ and carrier $k_*\in\mathbb R^3$, the graph point associated with $(t,x)$ is $(t,A(t,x),k_*\cdot A(t,x))$. In §5.6, $A(t,x)=X_{t,0}(x)$ is the inverse parent flow, so a profile evaluated here becomes its Eulerian field $f^\natural$. This formula imposes no regularity, periodicity or flow equation on $A$ and makes no approximation. Smoothness and chain-rule conclusions require the later hypotheses on the chosen parent flow. The phase is a real number; its periodic dependence belongs to the profile rather than to this graph-point definition.
TorusEuler.hierarchyGraphPoint.summary: Specify the label and phase at which the profile is evaluated

TorusEuler.hierarchyHigherPressureGradie.text: The proposed gradient profile is the coframe adjoint applied to the slow label gradient plus the longitudinal projection of $F-2M(V)$, where $F$ is the force. It rewrites the expensive phase derivative using the transverse pressure equation. This is a definition for arbitrary inputs; the subsequent transport theorem proves it equals a physical gradient under the required identities.
TorusEuler.hierarchyHigherPressureGradie.summary: Use the transverse equation for the fast pressure gradient

TorusEuler.hierarchyInactiveRegion.text: The underlying domain is $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ and the label set is denoted $S$. For closed $S$, the condition is open relative to this time slab. The inactive region consists of points in the time interval with $t<t_0$ or label outside the envelope support. It is independent of phase and describes the vanishing asserted in Proposition 5.4. The strict time inequality matches the proof; vanishing at the activation time itself follows from continuity where that endpoint is approached from below.
TorusEuler.hierarchyInactiveRegion.summary: Separate times and labels where oscillations must vanish

TorusEuler.hierarchyInactiveThroughActiv.text: Defines the points in the closed profile slab whose time is at most $\tau$ or whose label lies outside $S$. This differs from the strict inactive region, which uses times $t<\tau$. Extending a vanishing statement to the activation slice requires continuity and positive activation; the definition alone asserts no such vanishing.
TorusEuler.hierarchyInactiveThroughActiv.summary: The inactive region includes the activation slice

TorusEuler.hierarchyInductiveMeanExponen.text: Explicitly the exponent is $-7/4-2(p-1)/3$, with real subtraction after converting the integer level. This is a definition of a power, not a norm estimate. The induction measures the mean with the oscillatory exponent minus $1/2$, corresponding to $\lambda^{1/2}\|B_p\|_{[n]}$ in (5.40). This allows a factor $\lambda^{1/12}$ compared with the sharper mean estimate (5.35). The smallness assumption uses that allowance to remove the parent power before estimating the next supplementary transverse source.
TorusEuler.hierarchyInductiveMeanExponen.summary: Remove the parent loss by weakening the mean decay slightly

TorusEuler.hierarchyJetValues.text:
Quantities measured by the supremum at each word. The half-Hölder choice also includes all half-power difference quotients at fixed time, with the maximum convention of the endpoint half-Hölder norm.

The set explicitly contains zero, so it is nonempty. At coincident points the difference quotient is $0/0$ and takes the value zero assigned to division by zero. Boundedness of this set is a separate hypothesis whenever its real supremum is used to control values.
TorusEuler.hierarchyJetValues.summary: Values sampled by each derivative supremum

TorusEuler.hierarchyJetValues_le_of_reco.text: A recovered half-Holder curve representing an actual spatial derivative word controls the corresponding weighted lift supremum and half-Holder increments. The scale may be zero here; the theorem only multiplies by its nonnegative power.
TorusEuler.hierarchyJetValues_le_of_reco.summary: Converting recovered Holder words to weighted label bounds

TorusEuler.hierarchyJetValues_true_label.text: Uniform bounds $A,B$ on adjacent jets give both boundedness of the weighted word's half-Hölder jet set and a supremum bound $\ell^m(A+\sqrt{2AB})$. This includes the empty word, unlike the radius-gain lemmas. Nonnegative radius and constants and smooth time slices ensure all values and difference quotients are covered.
TorusEuler.hierarchyJetValues_true_label.summary: Adjacent jets bound the entire Hölder range

TorusEuler.hierarchyJetValues_true_label.text: For a nonempty word and adjacent power bounds, the entire half-Hölder jet range is bounded by $(C_m+\sqrt{2C_mC_{m+1}})D^{p+q}\sqrt\ell$. The radius restriction implies $\ell\le1$, allowing the value bound's factor $\ell$ to be replaced by $\sqrt\ell$. The theorem returns boundedness as well as the supremum inequality.
TorusEuler.hierarchyJetValues_true_label.summary: The full positive-word norm gains a radius factor

TorusEuler.hierarchyLabelDirection.text: This defines constant vector fields on $\mathbb R^3$ for any real $\ell_*$. At $\ell_*=0$, every positive-order scaled directional derivative is zero. The three label derivative directions are $\ell_*\partial_{a_i}$. Consequently, an order-$m$ derivative carries the factor $\ell_*^m$ used in the coefficient norm of Appendix D. These directions are used for phase-independent fields, particularly the parent coefficients and mean correction. The positive radius allows their estimates to be compared with ordinary label derivatives.
TorusEuler.hierarchyLabelDirection.summary: Each label derivative carries the envelope radius

TorusEuler.hierarchyLabelJetValues_endpo.text: For each time slice smooth in space, proves boundedness and a nonincreasing supremum of the selected label-word measurements. A switch determines whether half-Hölder quotients are included. The original measurement set must be bounded above; its built-in zero supplies nonemptiness and nonnegativity even when the time set is empty.
TorusEuler.hierarchyLabelJetValues_endpo.summary: The weighted jet supremum cannot grow under parity selection

TorusEuler.hierarchyLabelWord_endpointPa.text: Extends the coordinate-word reflection identity to the hierarchy's label directions scaled by $\ell$. Each derivative contributes one minus sign under reflection, while the scalar factor $\ell$ commutes with averaging. Smoothness is explicit; the equality holds for arbitrary real $\ell$ and does not assume a positive envelope scale.
TorusEuler.hierarchyLabelWord_endpointPa.summary: Weighted label derivatives have the same parity rule

TorusEuler.hierarchyLatticeShift.text: The joint translation associated with an integer lattice vector $n$ leaves time fixed, translates the label by $n$, and changes the phase by its inner product $k_*\cdot n$ with the carrier $k_*$. This is the compatibility shift satisfied by transported periodic profiles. It is distinct from an ordinary label translation at fixed phase.
TorusEuler.hierarchyLatticeShift.summary: A lattice translation carries its phase shift

TorusEuler.hierarchyLatticeShift_vadd_sl.text: Translation by any carrier-dependent lattice shift maps the whole profile slab to itself. The result is stated as equality of translated sets and holds for every real $T$. It lets the domain appearing in a within-slab derivative be replaced after translating both label and phase.
TorusEuler.hierarchyLatticeShift_vadd_sl.summary: The slab is invariant under the twisted translation

TorusEuler.hierarchyLeibnizSplits.text:
Assign each derivative in an ordered word to one of the two factors. The list retains multiplicity when equal coordinate directions recur.

Repeated derivative letters retain combinatorial multiplicity. The empty word has one split into two empty words, so the zeroth product rule is not lost.
TorusEuler.hierarchyLeibnizSplits.summary: All assignments of a derivative word to two factors

TorusEuler.hierarchyLeibnizSplits_order_.text: A Leibniz split assigns the original word's derivatives to two factors. If its first word is nonempty, the second word has strictly smaller length than the original. The membership hypothesis records an actual split, including repeated directions. This strict decrease is what makes differentiated coefficient equations amenable to induction.
TorusEuler.hierarchyLeibnizSplits_order_.summary: Differentiating the coefficient lowers the solution order

TorusEuler.hierarchyLeibnizSplits_spec.text: Every split produced by the ordered Leibniz list consists of two subwords whose lengths add to the original word length. Repeated letters retain their multiplicity in the list; this is the combinatorial bookkeeping behind the product rule.
TorusEuler.hierarchyLeibnizSplits_spec.summary: Leibniz subwords preserve the total derivative order

TorusEuler.hierarchyLevelConstant.text:
Constants for the full finite hierarchy. Their only quantitative inputs are the derivative-order constant bound, the depth and the level.

The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.
TorusEuler.hierarchyLevelConstant.summary: Constants accumulated through the finite depth

TorusEuler.hierarchyLevelConstant_monoto.text: For nonnegative $K$, the sequence of level constants built from $K$ at depth $P$, starting from $1+K+K^2$, is monotone in its level index. Each new step cap retains the previous constant and adds nonnegative terms. This allows all lower levels to be bounded by one coefficient during the strong induction; it does not give uniformity in depth.
TorusEuler.hierarchyLevelConstant_monoto.summary: The chosen constants can grow with the hierarchy level

TorusEuler.hierarchyLevelConstant_one_le.text: The recursively defined level constant is at least one when its input bound K is nonnegative. This permits later estimates to absorb unit factors without changing the level or frequency exponents.

TorusEuler.hierarchyLevelPairs.text:
The quadratic pairs contributing to the retained source at level $p$.

Finite sums and index sets are defined at zero order or empty ranges as well. The paper use supplies the intended order and level restrictions.

TorusEuler.hierarchyLevelPairs_eq_of_ret.text: If the target level $p$ is at most $Q$, and $Q\le P$, the quadratic interaction pairs for that level are identical at depths $P$ and $Q$ when the shift is at most one. The index constraints already keep every retained interaction within the smaller depth. This is exact independence, not an inequality between truncated sums.
TorusEuler.hierarchyLevelPairs_eq_of_ret.summary: Retained interactions do not depend on the final depth

TorusEuler.hierarchyLevelPairs_two_fast.text: For retained depth at least two, the fast pairs at level two consist only of $(2,1)$. This identifies the interaction of $C_2$ with the phase derivative of the first oscillation. The conclusion is an equality of finite sets, not a bound on that interaction.
TorusEuler.hierarchyLevelPairs_two_fast.summary: The first fast product uses the first completion

TorusEuler.hierarchyLevelPairs_two_slow.text: If $2\le P$, the slow pairs at level two form exactly the singleton $(1,1)$. Thus the first slow source contains only the interaction of the leading profile with itself. The lower bound on retained depth ensures that this pair is present in the truncated index set.
TorusEuler.hierarchyLevelPairs_two_slow.summary: The first slow product uses two leading waves

TorusEuler.hierarchyLinearRelayAt.text:
The exact four slow terms after commuting the time derivative through the pulled-back curl. $Q_t$ is the potential-time profile computed from (5.33), and $p$ is the oscillatory phase pressure.

The raw fields are arbitrary functions, and the label derivative expressions are zero wherever the function is not differentiable. The analytic relay identity and bounds assume smoothness and the momentum relation separately.

TorusEuler.hierarchyLinearRelayAt_eq_coo.text: The four slow relay terms can be regrouped into three coordinate sums: the potential-time curl, the material curl commutator, and the pressure gradient. A nonzero label scale cancels its reciprocal in the coefficient rows. This exact rewrite prepares the relay for uniform finite-word estimates.
TorusEuler.hierarchyLinearRelayAt_eq_coo.summary: The linear relay splits into curl and pressure coordinate terms

TorusEuler.hierarchyLinearRelayAt_freque.text: Scaling the covector by a positive frequency scales the entire four-term linear relay by its reciprocal. The statement assumes differentiability of the primitive and pressure profiles needed by the slow derivatives.
TorusEuler.hierarchyLinearRelayAt_freque.summary: Every linear relay term gains one inverse frequency

TorusEuler.hierarchyLinearRelayAt_input_.text: Scaling both input slices by a real number $r$ scales the complete linear relay by $r$, including the curl commutator and pressure gradient. The proof first scales the three primitive profiles and then each label derivative. No regularity in time is required for $r$, because it is a scalar on the fixed label–phase slice.
TorusEuler.hierarchyLinearRelayAt_input_.summary: A fixed-time weight passes through the entire relay

TorusEuler.hierarchyLinearRelayAt_smul.text: At a point where the potential, its prescribed time profile, and the pressure are differentiable, multiplying all three by one real scalar multiplies the entire relay by that scalar. The coframe and strain remain fixed. This justifies pulling a frequency factor or a fixed-time amplitude weight outside the spatial relay expression.
TorusEuler.hierarchyLinearRelayAt_smul.summary: A common scalar scales the entire linear relay

TorusEuler.hierarchyLinearRelayAt_sub_tr.text: For a transverse force $F$, subtracting the pulled-back curl of its potential from the forced relay gives the zero-forcing relay. Continuity and the two stated differentiability assumptions justify splitting label derivatives. The pressure contribution of $F$ is zero, so its only remaining contribution is precisely the subtracted curl completion.
TorusEuler.hierarchyLinearRelayAt_sub_tr.summary: Removing the force completion leaves the homogeneous relay

TorusEuler.hierarchyLongitudinalProjecti.text:
The longitudinal projection used in the transverse pressure equation.

At κ=0 the totalized inverse squared norm makes the operator zero, rather than a rank-one projection. The analytic uses supply a nonzero covector.

TorusEuler.hierarchyMeanExponent.text: The definition accepts every nonnegative integer $p$, converting it to a real number before subtracting $2$; the mean estimates themselves use only $p\ge2$. The mean and its source have frequency exponent $-5/2-2(p-2)/3$ for $p\ge2$, as in (5.35). This is stronger by $\lambda^{-1/12}$ than the mean bound propagated without parent powers in (5.40). Keeping both estimates is what permits the next source to be controlled without accumulating parent losses.
TorusEuler.hierarchyMeanExponent.summary: Record the sharper frequency scale for each mean level

TorusEuler.hierarchyMixedDirection.text: The definition permits arbitrary real scales, although the physical estimates take $\ell_*>0$ and $h>0$. Derivative indices are ordered only to represent each multi-index once. The derivative directions are the three operators $\ell_*\partial_{a_i}$ and the phase operator $h\partial_s$. Thus mixed derivatives acquire exactly the weights $\ell_*^m h^j$ in (D.1). This is the scaling convention behind the finite expansion estimates; it specifies how derivatives are measured and is not itself a bound on a field.
TorusEuler.hierarchyMixedDirection.summary: Spatial localization and phase width set derivative weights

TorusEuler.hierarchyOscExponent.text: For a nonnegative integer level $p$, the formal definition assigns the real exponent $-5/4-2(p-1)/3$ to the oscillation and its transverse source. The subtraction is performed after $p$ is read as a real number, so the expression also has its usual arithmetic meaning at $p=0$. At $p=1$ it is $-5/4$; at the first omitted level $P+1$ it is $-5/4-2P/3$. Thus the later estimates have the depth gain $\lambda^{-2P/3}$ described in §1.3. This assignment of exponents is not itself a bound on any profile or remainder.
TorusEuler.hierarchyOscExponent.summary: Each additional level gains two thirds of a frequency power

TorusEuler.hierarchyOscExponent_antitone.text: The exponent $-5/4-2(p-1)/3$ decreases as the natural-number level increases. Decreasing here means that $i\le j$ implies the exponent at $j$ is at most the exponent at $i$. A separate lower bound on the frequency is needed to turn this comparison of exponents into decay of powers.
TorusEuler.hierarchyOscExponent_antitone.summary: Oscillatory powers decrease with the hierarchy level

TorusEuler.hierarchyParentResidualConsta.text: The parent-residual coefficient is $K$ when the optional loss is absent and $Kc$ when a loss factor $c$ is present. This isolates the residual’s possible extra parent factor from the primitive solver constants. The generalized recurrence theorem later requires this coefficient to be bounded by $KL^5$.
TorusEuler.hierarchyParentResidualConsta.summary: Allow a separate loss in the level-two residual

TorusEuler.hierarchyPeriodicProfileSubmo.text:
The smooth slab profiles that are periodic under one phase translation.

The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.
TorusEuler.hierarchyPeriodicProfileSubmo.summary: Smooth profiles periodic in the phase variable

TorusEuler.hierarchyPhasePeriod.text:
One period in the phase direction of the joint profile domain.

The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.

TorusEuler.hierarchyPhasePeriod_vadd_sla.text: Translating the entire slab by one phase period yields the same set. This set-level equality complements the pointwise membership lemma. It is used when the domain of a derivative within the slab is translated, including derivatives at either time endpoint.
TorusEuler.hierarchyPhasePeriod_vadd_sla.summary: The slab is invariant under phase translation

TorusEuler.hierarchyPressureLabelGradien.text: This function takes the Fréchet derivative of the pressure, as a function of the pair $(a,s)$, at $(a,s)$ and retains only its label component. The output is a vector in three-dimensional space. The definition itself accepts any pressure function; later gradient identities and derivative estimates impose the smoothness needed for its calculus interpretation.
TorusEuler.hierarchyPressureLabelGradien.summary: The pressure gradient with phase held fixed

TorusEuler.hierarchyProfileReflection.text:
The joint reflection fixes time and reverses both label and phase.

The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.
TorusEuler.hierarchyProfileReflection.summary: Reversing label and phase while fixing time

TorusEuler.hierarchyProfileReflectionPar.text: Multiplying a profile by any real function of time preserves its simultaneous label-phase reflection sign. The reflection does not change time, so only commutation of scalar multiplication is needed. No smoothness or support assumption on the multiplier is required for this algebraic statement, which applies in particular to cutoff derivatives.
TorusEuler.hierarchyProfileReflectionPar.summary: A time-only multiplier leaves the reflection sign unchanged

TorusEuler.hierarchyProfileReflection_ap.text: Profile reflection maps (t,a,s) to (t,−a,−s). Time is unchanged, so reflecting a profile preserves the same physical time slab.
TorusEuler.hierarchyProfileReflection_ap.summary: The coordinate formula for profile reflection

TorusEuler.hierarchyProfileReflection_me.text: The joint reflection fixes time while negating label and phase, so it preserves the slab condition in both directions. This membership equivalence lets reflection identities be checked on the slab and extended through zero representatives. It also preserves the domain of derivative calculations at boundary times.
TorusEuler.hierarchyProfileReflection_me.summary: Reflection preserves membership in the time slab

TorusEuler.hierarchyProfileSlab.text:
The time, label and phase domain of the finite expansion.

If T<0 the slab is empty; if T=0 it has only one time. The analytic constructors requiring unique within-slab derivatives explicitly assume T>0.

TorusEuler.hierarchyQuadraticConstant.text: The product constant is twice the number of admissible sorted words times $2^n$. It depends only on the derivative order and the finite ordered index type. It accounts for the word count, the choices in Leibniz's rule, and the two-factor difference estimate when a bilinear map has norm at most one.
TorusEuler.hierarchyQuadraticConstant.summary: An explicit constant counts the product terms

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayCurlRow.text:
The coefficient of one weighted derivative of the pulled-back curl.

The row contains $\ell^{-1}$, which is zero when $\ell=0$ under totalized field inversion. All uses that undo the radius weighting require a positive radius.

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayGeometricCoeffi.text: With $\mathsf D\ge1$, $\ell\mathsf D^{16}\le1$, and the stated label-jet bounds for $G$ and $M$, all curl, material-commutator, and pressure rows satisfy one mixed-derivative budget. The strain and coframe powers are absorbed by the label width, leaving the explicit $|\ell^{-1}|\mathsf D^2$ factor. The theorem proves coefficient bounds, not the relay estimate itself.
TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayGeometricCoeffi.summary: Parent bounds control all geometric relay coefficients

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayGeometricRowBud.text: Writing $A=\sum_{j\le n}C_j$, this definition takes $(n+1)(A+2\,2^nA^2)|\ell^{-1}|D^2$. The linear terms control curl and pressure rows, while the quadratic term allows the strain–coframe commutator. It is an explicit finite-order allowance rather than a universal numerical constant.
TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayGeometricRowBud.summary: A common allowance for the three geometric row types

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayLabelJet.text:
Compose the Fréchet derivative of a label–phase function with the inclusion of label directions. The resulting continuous linear map differentiates only the three label coordinates at fixed phase.

The Fréchet derivative is a total function and becomes zero at nondifferentiability points. The relay estimates supply differentiability or smoothness before using this as a classical label derivative.
TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayLabelJet.summary: The label component of a profile derivative

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayMaterialRow.text:
This row is M composed with the curl row minus the curl row formed with GM. It records the commutator contribution to the material derivative of the divergence correction.

This combines the two curl rows algebraically and inherits their inverse-radius convention. Radius positivity is part of the analytic use, not of this raw row definition.

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayPotentialCoeffi.text:
The coefficient of the potential after normalizing the covector by the central frequency.

The raw inverse squared norm is total and gives zero at k=0. The wave-potential interpretation in the construction requires k≠0.
TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayPotentialCoeffi.summary: The vector-potential coefficient after normalizing frequency

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayPotentialCoeffi.text: Scaling a covector by a positive frequency multiplies its potential coefficient by the reciprocal frequency. The squared norm contributes two inverse factors, while the cross-product operator contributes one positive factor. The equality is valid even for the zero covector because the total coefficient definition is used; positivity is required only for the scaling parameter.
TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayPotentialCoeffi.summary: Potential coefficients gain one inverse frequency

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayPressureAmplitu.text:
The scalar row sends v to −2⟨k,Mv⟩/‖k‖². It is the amplitude contribution to the transverse pressure slope, before taking the mean-zero phase primitive.

At k=0 totalized inversion makes this scalar row zero. Pressure recovery uses a nonzero transported covector and the solution equation.
TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayPressureAmplitu.summary: The amplitude contribution to the pressure slope

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayPressureRow.text:
This scalar-to-vector map is multiplication by the coframe-transformed coordinate vector, with a factor $\ell^{-1}$. It restores the unweighted slow derivative from the radius-weighted derivative norm.

The inverse label radius is total at zero. Applications use $\ell>0$; the raw definition alone is not an invertible rescaling.
TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayPressureRow.summary: The pressure-gradient row with inverse radius

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayPressureSourceC.text:
The scalar row sends f to ⟨k,f⟩/‖k‖². The complementary amplitude row supplies the other term in the transverse pressure slope.

At k=0 this row is zero under the totalized formula. The transverse pressure construction requires nonzero covectors before interpreting the row as division by squared length.
TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayPressureSourceC.summary: The forcing contribution to the pressure slope

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayTimeAmplitudeCo.text:
This continuous linear operator collects the terms involving M, the covector and the amplitude in the time derivative of the normalized vector potential. Its inverse powers of the covector norm require nonvanishing when it is used analytically.

The formula contains inverse powers of ‖k‖². Nonzero covectors are supplied by the parent geometry in the relay estimates; the raw expression at k=0 is not a time derivative of a physical wave potential.
TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayTimeAmplitudeCo.summary: The amplitude coefficient in the potential time derivative

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayWordBound_label.text: A smooth operator-valued coefficient bounded through order $n$, applied to one weighted label derivative of a profile bounded through order $n+1$, has budget $2^nAC$. The label index ranges over the three label coordinates; the phase coordinate is excluded. Reciprocal label scale is accounted for in the supplied coefficient rather than differentiated separately.
TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayWordBound_label.summary: A coefficient times a label derivative loses one order

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayWordBound_linea.text: Smooth phase-independent operator coefficients acting on smooth periodic zero-mean velocity and forcing profiles produce a smooth normalized primitive with an explicit word bound. The constant combines the two coefficient budgets and the factor from phase integration. Time is only an arbitrary index, so no time regularity of coefficients or forcing is assumed.
TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayWordBound_linea.summary: A linear combination of profiles has a bounded phase primitive

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayWordBound_of_fi.text: If every sampled derivative set is bounded above, the finite mixed norm bounds each word of order at most n. Boundedness is explicit because the norm is a finite sum of real suprema.
TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayWordBound_of_fi.summary: The finite norm bounds all normalized words

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayWordBound_of_ph.text: A normalized label-jet bound gives the same mixed-word bound for the phase-independent lift of the coefficient.
TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayWordBound_of_ph.summary: Label bounds also control phase-independent mixed words

TorusEuler.hierarchyScaledCoframeRow.text: This definition composes one coordinate projection with the operator field $A$ and multiplies it by $\ell^{-1}$. Applied to an advector, it is the chosen component of $Az$ divided by the label radius. It pairs with a radius-weighted coordinate derivative in the slow-advection estimate.
TorusEuler.hierarchyScaledCoframeRow.summary: A coframe row carries the reciprocal label radius

TorusEuler.hierarchyScaledPhaseCoefficie.text: The coefficient is the linear form $z\mapsto h^{-1}\langle\kappa,z\rangle$. Factoring this reciprocal width out of the weighted phase derivative recovers the physical fast-advection term. The definition permits arbitrary real $h$; the later identity cancelling the width assumes $h\ne0$.
TorusEuler.hierarchyScaledPhaseCoefficie.summary: The phase coefficient carries the reciprocal width

TorusEuler.hierarchySeminorm_remainder_l.text: The exact algebraic remainder is bounded in an arbitrary seminorm from separate estimates for its linear, slow-product, completion-phase, and mean-phase terms. The assumptions include $\lambda\ge1$, nonnegative constants, and $L\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$ for the loss factor $L$. The conclusion counts the retained tail pairs explicitly; the analytic product estimates are hypotheses here.
TorusEuler.hierarchySeminorm_remainder_l.summary: Component estimates control the exact finite remainder

TorusEuler.hierarchySeminorm_velocity_su.text: Given all measured level bounds through depth $P\ge1$, this theorem bounds the total oscillation at $\lambda^{-5/4}$, its part beyond the first velocity at $\lambda^{-23/12}$, and the total mean at $\lambda^{-5/2}$. Constants retain the number of levels and explicit powers of the loss factor $L$. The norms are arbitrary seminorm families satisfying the supplied nonnegativity conditions.
TorusEuler.hierarchySeminorm_velocity_su.summary: Summing levels separates the leading oscillation from corrections

TorusEuler.hierarchySlowAdvectionCompone.text: With nonzero label radius, this bounds the component $(Az)_i\partial_{a_i}g$ using the scaled coframe-row norm, the advector norm, and one extra order of the advected field. Smoothness and bounded jet sets are required for each input. The bound on the scaled coframe row is assumed; this statement does not establish the deformation estimates itself.
TorusEuler.hierarchySlowAdvectionCompone.summary: Slow advection uses one coframe row and derivative

TorusEuler.hierarchySmoothProfileSubmodu.text:
A smooth slab profile is represented by its zero extension. Values of this representative outside the slab do not enter any derivative or equation.

The representative is deliberately zero outside the slab. Smoothness is required within the slab, and no smooth zero extension across the time endpoints is claimed. If the slab is empty the stored function must be zero everywhere.
TorusEuler.hierarchySmoothProfileSubmodu.summary: Smooth slab profiles stored by zero extension

TorusEuler.hierarchyStepCap.text:
The order-dependent constants grow with depth through finitely many terms, independently of the frequency and parent loss.

The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.

TorusEuler.hierarchyTailPairs.text: This is a finite index set, not an estimate. Both indices are positive and at most $P+1$; phase-advection indexing starts the first index at two. After cancellation through depth $P$, label interactions remain when $i+j\ge P+1$, and phase interactions remain when $i+j\ge P+2$. These are the ranges in (5.30), with positive indices up to the last correction level. The formal sum omits initial phase factors that are identically zero under the expansion conventions.
TorusEuler.hierarchyTailPairs.summary: Select the quadratic terms above the retained depth

TorusEuler.hierarchyTwistedMixedWord.text: This recursively defines linear differentiation by a word in four coordinate directions. The first three directions carry the label scale and the last carries the phase scale; the empty word leaves the profile unchanged. Each step differentiates the previously obtained profile while preserving smoothness and both periodicity conditions.
TorusEuler.hierarchyTwistedMixedWord.summary: Apply a sequence of scaled label and phase derivatives

TorusEuler.hierarchyTwistedMixedWord_app.text: At any fixed time in the slab, the recursively constructed mixed derivative has exactly the value of the corresponding composition of label and phase derivatives applied to the ordinary label-phase slice. Induction on the word uses the slice derivative identity. This confirms that the norm infrastructure measures actual derivatives, rather than independent stored jet data.
TorusEuler.hierarchyTwistedMixedWord_app.summary: The profile operator equals the actual derivative word

TorusEuler.hierarchyTwistedMixedWord_bdd.text: A bounded time-only multiplier preserves the boundedness of all samples used for the finite norm, over any subset of the closed time slab.
TorusEuler.hierarchyTwistedMixedWord_bdd.summary: Bounded time weights preserve bounded spatial derivatives

TorusEuler.hierarchyTwistedMixedWord_exi.text: Every fixed mixed word has a common bound for its values and half-Hölder differences over the slab. The proof bounds a difference both by twice the uniform value bound and by a derivative bound times distance, then takes their geometric mean. The result supplies bounded measurement sets for the optional Hölder seminorm.
TorusEuler.hierarchyTwistedMixedWord_exi.summary: Interpolate bounded values and derivatives to a half-Hölder bound

TorusEuler.hierarchyTwistedMixedWord_exi.text: For positive slab length, each mixed label-phase derivative word of a twisted profile is uniformly bounded on the slab. The derivative word is itself represented by a smooth twisted profile, so compact-cell boundedness applies. The theorem gives existence of a constant for that word, without a quantitative frequency estimate.
TorusEuler.hierarchyTwistedMixedWord_exi.summary: Every fixed derivative word has a uniform bound

TorusEuler.hierarchyTwistedProfileSubmod.text:
The actual phase-periodic profiles compatible with the label lattice.

This imposes a simultaneous lattice-and-phase identity on already phase-periodic smooth slab profiles. For k=0 it reduces to ordinary spatial periodicity; physical launch conditions decide whether that special case is relevant.
TorusEuler.hierarchyTwistedProfileSubmod.summary: Phase profiles compatible with the label lattice

TorusEuler.hierarchyTwistedProfile_exist.text: Every smooth twisted profile has a nonnegative uniform bound over the full closed time slab and all labels and phases. Lattice and phase periodicity move each point into a compact centered cell times one phase period. Continuity on that compact set supplies the bound without requiring an a priori norm estimate.
TorusEuler.hierarchyTwistedProfile_exist.summary: A twisted profile is bounded on the closed slab

TorusEuler.hierarchyTwistedProfile_exist.text: For positive slab length, one nonnegative Lipschitz constant controls every label-phase slice of a twisted profile on the slab. The derivative profile is uniformly bounded by compactness, and the global spatial mean-value estimate gives the Lipschitz property. The bound may depend on the whole profile and time interval.
TorusEuler.hierarchyTwistedProfile_exist.summary: All time slices share a finite Lipschitz bound

TorusEuler.hierarchyTwistedSliceDerivati.text: For positive slab length, this linear profile operator takes the full derivative within the slab and restricts its directions to label and phase. The output is again a smooth twisted profile, now valued in bounded linear maps on the label-phase space. Time differentiation is excluded by construction.
TorusEuler.hierarchyTwistedSliceDerivati.summary: Differentiate the profile with time held fixed

TorusEuler.hierarchyTwistedSliceDerivati.text: At an on-slab time, the value of the profile-space slice derivative equals the ordinary Fréchet derivative of the fixed-time label-phase slice. The equality connects the profile-space operation with the genuine derivative on the unrestricted spatial domain. Positive slab length is retained for constructing the profile-valued derivative.
TorusEuler.hierarchyTwistedSliceDerivati.summary: Read the ordinary derivative of a time slice

TorusEuler.hierarchy_absorb_mean_parent_.text: For frequency $\lambda\ge1$ and a nonnegative loss factor $L$, the smallness condition $L\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$ absorbs the parent factor in the mean estimate. The mean exponent differs from the inductive mean exponent by exactly $1/12$. The conclusion is a scalar power inequality at any natural level, not a mean-solver theorem.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_absorb_mean_parent_.summary: The mean loses its parent factor before reuse

TorusEuler.hierarchy_absorb_parent_loss.text: More generally, assume $\lambda\ge1$, $L\ge0$, $L\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$ and $\delta\ge1/12$. Then $L\lambda^{e-\delta}\le\lambda^e$ for every real $e$. Under $\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, any available decay of at least $\lambda^{-1/12}$ absorbs the fixed parent factor. This is the arithmetic behind the choice of $\lambda^{-2/3}$ decay per level in Theorem 5.6. The identity concerns numerical powers; the product and solve estimates supply the bounds to which it is applied.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_absorb_parent_loss.summary: The spare frequency gain pays for the parent coefficients

TorusEuler.hierarchy_advection_filtratio.text: The identity holds for arbitrary summands in any commutative additive setting and any nonnegative depth and shift; the paper uses shifts zero and one. The full quadratic sum splits exactly into the interactions at levels two through $P$ and the remaining tail. The same identity treats label and phase derivatives with their respective level conventions. In Proposition 5.4 the first group cancels against the solved equations, leaving the two quadratic sums in (5.30).
TorusEuler.hierarchy_advection_filtratio.summary: Partition the finite quadratic sum by interaction level

TorusEuler.hierarchy_collar_of_support_b.text: Let $f(a,q)$ depend on a label $a\in\mathbb R^3$ and a phase $q$, and let $\bar f(a)$ be a phase-independent field, with values in any set. Assume $\ell\ge0$, $2\ell<1/2$, and $f(a,q)=\bar f(a)$ for every $q$ whenever $|a|>2\ell$ (Euclidean norm). Then there is $\delta$ with $0<\delta\le1/2$ such that $f(a,q)=\bar f(a)$ for every $q$ whenever some coordinate satisfies $|a_i|>1/2-\delta$. The proof takes $\delta=1/2-2\ell$, using $|a_i|\le|a|$.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_collar_of_support_b.summary: Small radial support gives an agreement collar near the cell faces

TorusEuler.hierarchy_completion_previous.text: For an integer $p\ge1$, the formal statement proves that the exponent of the correction generated by level $p-1$ is the oscillatory exponent at level $p$ minus $1/3$. In paper notation this says that $C_p$, inherited from $V_{p-1}$, fits at level $p$ with an additional factor $\lambda^{-1/3}$. The oscillatory exponent is $-5/4-2(p-1)/3$, and a correction subtracts one further power from the generating oscillation. The assumption $p\ge1$ prevents truncation in the nonnegative-integer index $p-1$. This is arithmetic among assigned exponents; an estimate for the actual correction requires the analytic bounds.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_completion_previous.summary: The inherited correction has an extra third of frequency decay

TorusEuler.hierarchy_correction_level_bo.text: This specializes the correction-level estimate to the recurrence’s default residual loss. The coefficient $K$ is automatically at most $KL^5$ when $K,L\ge1$. The analytic recurrence, previous-level bounds, smallness condition, and three-order derivative reserve remain hypotheses of the resulting bound.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_correction_level_bo.summary: Close a correction step with the standard residual budget

TorusEuler.hierarchy_correction_level_bo.text: Given the analytic norm recurrence and bounds at all earlier positive levels through order $N$, this obtains the full measured bound at a retained correction level and order $n$. It requires $n+3\le N\le H$, a controlled optional residual loss, and the sixth-power parent smallness condition. The conclusion uses the explicit finite step constant built from the previous constant, $K$, and the slow and fast pair counts.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_correction_level_bo.summary: Close one correction level with three derivative orders reserved

TorusEuler.hierarchy_depth_tail_of_measu.text: Per-level bounds at order $n+1$, terminal-level comparisons, and measured product and linear estimates yield the exact remainder bound at the oscillation exponent of level $P+1$, namely $\lambda^{-5/4-2P/3}$. The smallness condition is $L^6\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$. The coefficient records the tail-pair count and $2K(C+1)^2$; the theorem does not derive its analytic operator estimates.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_depth_tail_of_measu.summary: Measured products give the remainder rate at every depth

TorusEuler.hierarchy_fastAdvection_timeF.text: If each fixed-time slice of $g$ in label and phase is differentiable, scalar factors depending only on time can be pulled out of the fast advection term $(\kappa\cdot z)\partial_sg$. The two scalars combine as $r(t)q(t)$. No time regularity is required: the derivative in this equality is taken only in the phase direction.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_fastAdvection_timeF.summary: Time factors leave phase differentiation unchanged

TorusEuler.hierarchy_fast_completion_exp.text: Here $i\ge1$ is assumed before forming the predecessor $i-1$, so the natural-number subtraction equals ordinary integer subtraction; the physical correction interactions have $i\ge2$. For an interaction with $i+j=p+1$, the phase cost $\lambda^{3/2}$ combined with $C_i$ and $Y_j$ leaves an extra factor $\lambda^{-1/12}$ beyond the target level-$p$ oscillatory bound. This is the weakest surplus in the induction for Theorem 5.6 and determines the frequency smallness needed to absorb the parent powers.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_fast_completion_exp.summary: Fast transport by the correction leaves one twelfth

TorusEuler.hierarchy_fast_mean_exponent.text: This is a numerical identity for nonnegative indices; all frequency exponents use real subtraction, and it asserts no bound for a profile by itself. When $i+j=p+1$, the induction bound for $B_i$, the oscillatory bound for $Y_j$, and one fast derivative give the target level-$p$ exponent with an extra $\lambda^{-1/4}$. This includes the term involving $B_p$ and $V_1$. It is the frequency calculation used for $f_p^S$ near the end of the induction.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_fast_mean_exponent.summary: The supplementary source leaves a quarter-power surplus

TorusEuler.hierarchy_label_inputs_previo.text: If two positive indices satisfy $i+j=p$, each is strictly smaller than $p$. The hypotheses $i\ge1$ and $j\ge1$ exclude a zeroth-level input. This elementary fact makes the label-advection part of the hierarchy recursive in already constructed levels, without making any estimate on the associated fields.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_label_inputs_previo.summary: Label advection uses strictly earlier levels

TorusEuler.hierarchy_label_product_expon.text: This equality is valid for all nonnegative integer indices, since those indices are treated as real numbers inside the exponents. Adding the oscillatory frequency exponents at levels $i$ and $j$ gives the mean exponent at level $i+j$. It also leaves a surplus $\lambda^{-7/12}$ relative to the oscillatory target at that level. This arithmetic supplies the power used for label-advection products in the proof of Theorem 5.6 after applying (5.39).
TorusEuler.hierarchy_label_product_expon.summary: Two oscillatory scales give the required mean scale

TorusEuler.hierarchy_level_analysis_cost.text: If the requested order $m$ and depth $P$ lie in the threshold range, the analytic cost at order $m+3P$ is bounded by a threshold built from the shifted cost table. The shift is part of the table before taking the finite maximum. No uniform bound over all orders is asserted.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_level_analysis_cost.summary: Include the derivative reserve in the cost table

TorusEuler.hierarchy_level_bounds.text: Let nonnegative arrays $O,F,G,B,C,Y,Z$ measure respectively oscillation plus pressure, transverse source, mean source, mean, correction, and the two level sums. For $\lambda,L,K\ge1$ and depth $P$, assume through derivative order $H$: $O_{n1}\le KL\lambda^{-5/4}$, $F_{n1}=G_{n1}=B_{n1}=C_{n0}=0$, $G_{np}\le KL\sum_{i+j=p}(Y_{n+1,i}Y_{n+1,j}+O_{n+1,i}Y_{n+1,j}+B_{n+1,i}B_{n+1,j})+\mathbf1_{p=2}K\lambda^{-5/2}$, $B_{np}\le KL G_{n+1,p}$, $F_{np}\le KL[\lambda^{-1}(O_{n+1,p-1}+F_{n+1,p-1})+\sum_{i+j=p}Z_{n+1,i}Z_{n+1,j}+\lambda^{3/2}\sum_{i+j=p+1,i\ge2}(C_{n,i-1}+B_{ni})Y_{n+1,j}]$, $O_{np}\le KL F_{np}$, $C_{np}\le KL\lambda^{-1}O_{n+1,p}$, $Y_{np}\le O_{np}+C_{n,p-1}$, and $Z_{np}\le Y_{np}+B_{np}$. Indices are positive; solve bounds start at $p=2$, correction and sum bounds at $p=1$, and an occurrence of $n+1$ requires $n+1\le H$. If $L^6\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, constants $A_p$ depending only on $P,K$ give, whenever $1\le p\le P$ and $n+3(p-1)+1\le H$, $F_{np}\le A_p\lambda^{e_p}$, $O_{np}\le A_pL\lambda^{e_p}$, $G_{np}\le A_pL^5\lambda^{m_p}$, $B_{np}\le A_p\min(\lambda^{e_p-1/2},L^6\lambda^{m_p})$, $C_{np}\le A_pL^2\lambda^{e_p-1}$ and $Y_{np},Z_{np}\le A_pL^2\lambda^{e_p}$. Here $e_p=-5/4-2(p-1)/3$, $m_p=-5/2-2(p-2)/3$, with real subtraction.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_level_bounds.summary: The measured recurrence yields all required level bounds

TorusEuler.hierarchy_level_bounds_throug.text: A single finite order budget controls every requested order through the retained depth. The internal derivative reserve is included in the order argument of the analytic cost table.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_level_bounds_throug.summary: One finite derivative reserve controls the retained hierarchy

TorusEuler.hierarchy_level_bounds_withRe.text: The norm recurrence yields bounds at every retained level $1\le p\le P$ whenever $n+3(p-1)+1\le H$. Three extra orders are spent per correction level and one on the leading completion. The common constant depends on depth, the derivative-order constant bound, and level; parent-loss control and frequency smallness remain explicit assumptions.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_level_bounds_withRe.summary: Iterate the measured bounds through every retained level

TorusEuler.hierarchy_level_budget_of_ste.text: For $\mathsf D$, $\lambda$ and $\Gamma$ at least one, assume $6p\le b$ and the step inequality $\Gamma\mathsf D^b\le\lambda^{1/32}$. Then $(\mathsf D^p)^6\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$. This is the smallness condition used by the level recurrence, derived from the stronger budget already imposed for the step.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_level_budget_of_ste.summary: The step inequality absorbs the hierarchy parent loss

TorusEuler.hierarchy_mean_inductive_shif.text: Explicitly, $[-5/2-2(p-2)/3]+1/12=-7/4-2(p-1)/3$ for every nonnegative integer $p$, with real subtraction throughout. The exponent in the sharper mean estimate (5.35), increased by $1/12$, equals the mean exponent used in (5.40). Thus replacing a parent factor by $\lambda^{1/12}$ gives exactly the induction bound stated in the paper. This is an algebraic identity; the actual mean estimate is supplied by the endpoint solve.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_mean_inductive_shif.summary: One twelfth separates the two mean decay rates

TorusEuler.hierarchy_mean_product_expone.text: Explicitly, adding $-7/4-2(i-1)/3$ and $-7/4-2(j-1)/3$ gives $-5/2-2(i+j-2)/3-1$. The equality itself needs no flow or solution. Adding the induction exponents for two means gives the mean exponent at their combined level minus one. Once the label-advection estimate is applied, their product is therefore smaller by $\lambda^{-1}$ than the leading averaged oscillatory terms. This is the comparison of the third sum with the first two sums after (5.42).
TorusEuler.hierarchy_mean_product_expone.summary: Two means gain an extra inverse frequency in their product

TorusEuler.hierarchy_phaseMean_apply_eq_.text: A continuous linear map applied pointwise to a continuous profile with zero phase mean still has zero phase mean. The ambient normed spaces are complete so the phase integral commutes with the map. This is the averaging step used for phase-independent coefficients in the hierarchy source cancellation.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_phaseMean_apply_eq_.summary: Linear maps preserve a vanishing phase mean

TorusEuler.hierarchy_phaseMean_completio.text: The hypotheses give periodic differentiable phase profiles and the identity $\partial_s\langle\kappa,C\rangle=-\mathrm{divV}$. Integration by parts over one period then identifies the mean of $\langle\kappa,C\rangle Y_s$ with the mean of $\mathrm{divV}\,Y$. Continuity assumptions justify the integrals; this identity removes the costly phase derivative in the mean source.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_phaseMean_completio.summary: Averaging exchanges the fast derivative for divergence

TorusEuler.hierarchy_phaseMean_labelDeri.text: For a jointly smooth function of label and phase, assume its phase average vanishes at every label. The average of the label derivative in any direction $v$ then vanishes as well. The proof differentiates the parameter-dependent integral over a fixed period, rather than assuming cancellation only at the selected label.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_phaseMean_labelDeri.summary: Label differentiation preserves a vanishing phase mean

TorusEuler.hierarchy_phaseMean_supplemen.text: Fix vectors $B$ and $\kappa$ independent of phase. Let $Y(s)$ have period one, and suppose $Y'(s)$ exists for every phase and is continuous. The formal statement proves $\int_0^1(B\cdot\kappa)Y'(s)\,ds=0$. The endpoint values cancel by periodicity. At each fixed time and label this is the average cancellation for the supplementary term $(B_2\cdot\kappa)\partial_s(\widetilde\chi A_1)$ in (1.12). No zero-mean assumption on $Y$ is needed, and no amplitude or derivative estimate is concluded. The result uses phase independence of $B,\kappa$; it would not apply to arbitrary phase-dependent factors.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_phaseMean_supplemen.summary: A phase derivative contributes nothing to the averaged equation

TorusEuler.hierarchy_phase_inputs_previo.text: For $i\ge2$, $j\ge1$, and $i+j=p+1$, the completion level $i-1$ and the advected level $j$ are below $p$, while $i\le p$. Equality $i=p$ occurs exactly when $j=1$. Thus the same-level mean contribution is confined to its interaction with the leading wave.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_phase_inputs_previo.summary: Only the leading wave reaches the current mean

TorusEuler.hierarchy_slowAdvection_timeF.text: The coefficient operator is linear in the advecting vector, and the derivative of $g$ is taken in a label-coordinate direction. Consequently time-only factors on the two profiles factor out as their product. Differentiability of each fixed-time slice of $g$ is assumed; this identity does not differentiate either time factor or the coefficient field.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_slowAdvection_timeF.summary: Time factors leave label differentiation unchanged

TorusEuler.hierarchy_sum_fast_previous.text: Assuming $p\le P$, summing a function at $(i-1,j)$ over the fast pairs gives the corresponding sum over slow pairs. The statement holds in any additive commutative monoid, so it uses no analytic estimate. It supplies the precise reindexing after phase integration by parts replaces $C_i$ by the divergence of $V_{i-1}$.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_sum_fast_previous.summary: Shift the completion index in the finite sum

TorusEuler.hierarchy_weighted_coefficien.text: If a derivative of positive order $m$ costs at most $C D^{k(m+1)}$ and $\ell D^k\le1$, then its weighted size is at most $C D^{2k}\ell$. The assumptions include $D\ge1$ and nonnegative radius and constant. Keeping one factor of $\ell D^k$ produces the gain used in coefficient thresholds.
TorusEuler.hierarchy_weighted_coefficien.summary: A positive coefficient derivative retains a radius factor

TorusEuler.higherPressureGradientBudget_.text: Let $\lambda\ge1$ and $\alpha_p=-5/4-2(p-1)/3$. Suppose for $2\le p\le P$ that $F_p\le C\lambda^{\alpha_p}$, $V_p\le CL\lambda^{\alpha_p}$, $\lambda q_p\le CL\lambda^{\alpha_p}$ with $q_p\ge0$, and $g_p\le c_FF_p+c_VV_p+c_qq_p$. Assume $C,L,c_F,c_V,c_S\ge0$ and $c_q\le c_S\lambda$. Then $\sum_{p=2}^{P}g_p\le(P-1)C[c_F+(c_V+c_S)L]\lambda^{-23/12}$ for $P\ge2$; when the index set is empty the bound is zero. This is the numerical summation used before (5.52). Identifying these scalar quantities with pressure-gradient, source and velocity norms requires the preceding analytic estimates.
TorusEuler.higherPressureGradientBudget_.summary: The least decay occurs at the first higher level

TorusEuler.higherPressureGraphCost_le.text: With $\lambda\ge1$, positive label length and phase width $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, assume inverse length and carrier size bounds. The explicit graph differentiation cost is then bounded by a constant times $\lambda^{3/2}$. This numerical step is applied only once after reconstructing the pressure gradient from the transverse equation.
TorusEuler.higherPressureGraphCost_le.summary: One physical derivative costs three half frequency powers

TorusEuler.higherPressure_prefactor_le_p.text: The hypotheses bound the jet, carrier, inverse-length and loss factors by specified powers of a parent parameter $\mathsf D\ge1$. The conclusion bounds their combined Hessian prefactor by an explicit power of $\mathsf D$; dependence on retained depth appears through the cardinality of levels two through $P$. No frequency estimate is established by this algebra alone.
TorusEuler.higherPressure_prefactor_le_p.summary: Keep the higher-pressure parent exponent independent of depth

TorusEuler.holderBridge_exists_close_lif.text: Any two torus labels admit Euclidean representatives whose separation is at most twice their torus distance. The proof chooses a centered representative of their difference and estimates its Euclidean norm from its coordinate bounds. This is a controlled choice of lifts, not a claim that arbitrary representatives are close or that the metrics are isometric.
TorusEuler.holderBridge_exists_close_lif.summary: Nearby torus points have controlled Euclidean representatives

TorusEuler.homogeneousDyadicBlocks.text: Construct certified dyadic blocks from a symbol smooth away from zero by applying the fixed annular localization. The cutoff gives compact support, cancellation at zero, and the required frequency band. No degree-zero homogeneity hypothesis is needed to form these blocks; that hypothesis enters the theorem identifying their sum with the intended symbol.
TorusEuler.homogeneousDyadicBlocks.summary: Annular localization supplies the nonzero frequency blocks

TorusEuler.homogeneousHalfHolderMultipli.text: Define a bounded operator by summing the annular dyadic blocks and adding the constant field obtained from $A(0)$ applied to the input mean. Only smoothness away from zero is required to construct it. The separate hypothesis that $A$ is homogeneous of degree zero away from zero, assumed in the Fourier-action theorem, is essential before identifying this operator with the symbol $A$ at nonzero frequencies.
TorusEuler.homogeneousHalfHolderMultipli.summary: Sum annular blocks and add the prescribed mean action

TorusEuler.homogeneousHalfHolderMultipli.text: Assume positive-scale homogeneity of $A$, and that a supplied bounded $L^2$ operator $B$ acts on Fourier coefficients by the same formula. Then embedding the constructed half-Hölder output equals applying $B$ to the embedded input. Fourier uniqueness proves the equality; the theorem does not construct or estimate the separate $L^2$ operator.
TorusEuler.homogeneousHalfHolderMultipli.summary: Matching symbols identify the Hölder and weak operators

TorusEuler.homogeneousOffOriginMultiplie.text: This definition annularly localizes an operator symbol using the fixed dyadic cutoff, packages the compact smooth localization as a Schwartz map, and forms its full periodic kernel. Only smoothness away from zero is a formal input here. Homogeneity and the zero mode are separately relevant when identifying the resulting multiplier with a desired Fourier symbol.
TorusEuler.homogeneousOffOriginMultiplie.summary: The fixed annular partition selects an off diagonal kernel

TorusEuler.imagPartL2Vec3.text: Lift the coordinatewise imaginary-part map to vector-valued L² for a general measure. This gives a real continuous linear projection from complex paths to real paths. Together with the real-part map and embedding, it enables componentwise extension of operators that act on entire time paths.
TorusEuler.imagPartL2Vec3.summary: Take imaginary parts of vector valued L² paths

TorusEuler.imagPartL2Vec3_I_smul.text: The imaginary part of $iv$ equals the real part of $v$ in the $L^2$ quotient. This is the complementary component identity to the negative-real-part formula. Together they control multiplication by $i$ in the concrete path complexification without making pointwise choices of representatives.
TorusEuler.imagPartL2Vec3_I_smul.summary: Multiplication by i turns real paths into imaginary parts

TorusEuler.imagPartL2Vec3_apply_ae.text: The representative of the $L^2$ imaginary part of $v$ equals the coordinatewise imaginary part of $v$ almost everywhere for $\mu$. The statement records representative compatibility for a bounded map acting on an $L^2$ quotient. It is used alongside real-part compatibility to prove reconstruction and the squared-norm splitting of complex paths.
TorusEuler.imagPartL2Vec3_apply_ae.summary: Path imaginary parts agree with pointwise imaginary projection

TorusEuler.imagPartL2Vec3_complexify.text: The imaginary part of a complexified real L² path is the zero L² path. The proof compares the induced representatives and uses the vanishing imaginary part of each embedded real coordinate. This is a structural identity for arbitrary measure, independent of any PDE or endpoint constraint.
TorusEuler.imagPartL2Vec3_complexify.summary: Embedded real paths have no imaginary component

TorusEuler.inductionCrossingStrengthCons.text: The numerical constant $18e^3$ is at least two, and its reciprocal is no greater than $e^{-1}/4$. These inequalities allow first-wave and later crossing strength bounds to share one induction convention. The theorem is a numerical comparison only; it contains no wave or schedule hypotheses.
TorusEuler.inductionCrossingStrengthCons.summary: One strength constant works for the whole induction

TorusEuler.inductionHalfLength.text: Defines the half length for wave $i+1$ as $\lambda_i^{-1/8}(4\log\lambda_{i+3})^3$. The index shift accounts for the future logarithmic gain in the paper’s formula. This definition accepts any real-valued frequency sequence; positivity and geometric decay of the resulting lengths require the separate schedule and largeness theorem.
TorusEuler.inductionHalfLength.summary: The half length of the next wave

TorusEuler.inductionHalfLength_zero_le_q.text: If the base frequency is at least $4^{16}$ and the first half-length is bounded by its negative one-sixteenth power, that half-length is at most one quarter. The negative power reverses the frequency comparison. This elementary numerical step leaves room for the first child endpoint within the stationary time interval.
TorusEuler.inductionHalfLength_zero_le_q.summary: The first endpoint fits inside the stationary slab

TorusEuler.inductionPressure_endpointHes.text: Let $u$ be jointly $C^2$ on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3$, with $T>0$, and let $X$ satisfy $\dot X=u(t,X)$ at the time considered. Assume $D_x^2p$ exists there, $\lambda_0\ge4$, $\lambda_{n+1}\ge2\lambda_n$, and $D_x^2p(t,X)\le(\sum_{i<j}\lambda_i^{-1})I$. If the spatial derivative of the momentum residual has operator norm at most $1/2$, the formal theorem gives $H\le I$ for $H=-\dot A-A^2$, $A=D_xu(t,X)$. The frequency assumptions bound the reciprocal sum by $1/2$. This is a local bound along the indicated trajectory and time; it does not assume that the approximate parent solves Euler exactly or assert an endpoint inverse by itself.
TorusEuler.inductionPressure_endpointHes.summary: Pressure and residual bounds give the effective Hessian upper bound

TorusEuler.inductionPressure_eulerianCoe.text: Assumes a base frequency at least four, at least doubling frequency growth, the accumulated one-sided pressure-Hessian bound, and residual-gradient norm at most one half. It proves the quadratic-form upper bound for pressure Hessian minus residual gradient by the identity matrix. The pressure budget and residual budget each contribute at most one half.
TorusEuler.inductionPressure_eulerianCoe.summary: The pressure and residual budgets give endpoint coercivity

TorusEuler.inductionPressure_sum_le.text: Let $\lambda_0>0$ and suppose $2\lambda_i\le\lambda_{i+1}$ for every nonnegative integer $i$. For every $j\ge0$, the formal statement proves $\sum_{i=0}^{j-1}\lambda_i^{-1}\le2/\lambda_0$. This is the sum $\sum_{i=1}^{j}\lambda_{i-1}^{-1}$ appearing in (T3), written with indices starting at zero. When $j=0$ the sum is empty and equals zero. Positivity of every frequency follows from the hypotheses, so all reciprocals are ordinary positive reciprocals. The statement only bounds the numerical allowance; an estimate for the pressure Hessian must already have been established separately.
TorusEuler.inductionPressure_sum_le.summary: Geometric frequency growth bounds the sum of reciprocal frequencies

TorusEuler.induction_approximate_child_c.text: Suppose the approximate velocity splits into parent, primary wave, oscillatory remainder, and mean. Differentiability hypotheses and the exact primary gradient $\chi\,\mathbf a\otimes k$ identify the remaining central error as the sum of the last two derivatives at the origin. The bound by $C_{step}\lambda^{-5/12}$ on those two derivatives, with $C_{step}\le\lambda^{1/32}$, makes that error at most $\lambda^{-1/3}$.
TorusEuler.induction_approximate_child_c.summary: Separate the leading rank-one gradient from corrections

TorusEuler.induction_child_center_error_.text: If $\lambda\ge2^{12}$ and $\lambda_+\ge\lambda$, then $\lambda^{-1/3}+\lambda_+^{-5}\le\lambda^{-1/4}$. The statement is a numerical estimate for positive real frequencies, with no gradient field among its data. In §7.2 the two summands bound the central error of the approximate solution and the derivative of the Fourier tail. Once their sum bounds $|E_{c,j}|$, this inequality gives the error allowance in (T4). The explicit threshold $2^{12}$ replaces the phrase “for large $N$” for this individual comparison; the construction still has other threshold requirements.
TorusEuler.induction_child_center_error_.summary: Combines the expansion and truncation error scales

TorusEuler.induction_child_center_split.text: At a time in the given interval, suppose the child velocity is the approximate field plus the tail, both summands are differentiable at the origin, and the approximate field has the supplied rank-one splitting. Combining an error of size $\lambda^{-1/3}$ with a tail gradient bounded by $\lambda_{next}^{-5}$ gives central error at most $\lambda^{-1/4}$ under the stated frequency bounds $2^{12}\le\lambda\le\lambda_{next}$.
TorusEuler.induction_child_center_split.summary: Add the cutoff gradient to the central error

TorusEuler.induction_child_cutoffTail_bu.text: A full-depth tail estimate with cutoff $\lambda^5$, together with the smallness budget $\mu(\lambda^5)^{2-P}(1+\text{size})^2\le\lambda_{next}^{-5}$, implies that the tail is at most $\lambda^{5m}\lambda_{next}^{-5}$. The theorem uses integer powers for the potentially negative order difference and nonnegative size parameters. It works at orders zero and one as well as higher orders.
TorusEuler.induction_child_cutoffTail_bu.summary: Reduce the full-depth cutoff estimate to low orders

TorusEuler.induction_child_flow_tail_bud.text: If $1\le\lambda\le\lambda_{next}$, then the fifth inverse power of the next frequency is bounded by the child frequency to power $-5/2$. Monotonicity in the positive base and the negative exponent gives the estimate. It is the scalar comparison used to supply the cutoff perturbation’s smallness.
TorusEuler.induction_child_flow_tail_bud.summary: The next cutoff tail fits the flow estimate

TorusEuler.induction_child_increment_bud.text: For $\lambda\ge4$ and $\lambda_{next}\ge\lambda$, the sum $\lambda^{-3/2}+\lambda_{next}^{-4}$ is at most $\lambda^{-1}$. The proof bounds both terms by half of the target through the square-root lower bound. This combines the two nonoscillatory contributions to the tower increment.
TorusEuler.induction_child_increment_bud.summary: The mean and cutoff tail fit one inverse frequency

TorusEuler.induction_child_oscillation_a.text: If $\lambda\ge1$ and $C_{step}\le\lambda^{1/32}$, the oscillatory bound becomes at most $\lambda^{-1}$, while the deformation bound becomes at most $\lambda$. The statement is an inequality for real powers. It does not construct either an oscillation or a flow; later lemmas insert those quantities.
TorusEuler.induction_child_oscillation_a.summary: Absorb the step constant into the child frequency

TorusEuler.induction_child_oscillation_l.text: For an odd periodic parent flow with deformation bound $D$, assume $\mu\ge2$, $\mu\le D$, and $\ell\le D^{-3}$. A localized transported profile nonzero at $x$ must lie within $\mu^{-1}$ of some lattice vector. The label-support hypothesis, vanishing for $|a|>2\ell$, is explicit, and the flow assumptions establish that the center remains fixed.
TorusEuler.induction_child_oscillation_l.summary: The transported support lies near a lattice origin

TorusEuler.induction_child_oscillation_z.text: If the switching rate is nonnegative and the higher profile $C$ vanishes at every time up to $t_0$, then the localized transported sum of the primary wave and $C$ is zero there. The result includes the activation time itself. It uses the cutoff’s zero branch and periodization of the zero function.
TorusEuler.induction_child_oscillation_z.summary: The transported oscillation vanishes through activation

TorusEuler.induction_child_velocity_boun.text: Let $\mu\ge2$, $\lambda\ge2\mu$ and let $U_+,U,O:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ satisfy $|U(x)|\le\mu$ and $|O(x)|\le\lambda^{-1}$. Assume $U_+-U-O$ has finite spatial $C^{0,1/2}$ norm at most $\lambda^{-1}$. Then $|U_+(x)|\le\lambda$ for every $x$. This proves the final velocity bound used in (T2), after the oscillation and remaining increment have been controlled. The formal statement is for a single spatial field and does not itself take a supremum in time. The intermediate triangle-inequality bound $\mu+2\lambda^{-1}$ is used in the proof. The $C^{0,1/2}$ norm is $\sup|f|+[f]_{1/2}$.
TorusEuler.induction_child_velocity_boun.summary: The parent and two small increments fit the next velocity bound

TorusEuler.induction_comparison_error_bu.text:
Let $\mu\ge1$, $
u\ge1$, $c,L>0$, $L_+\ge0$, $A\ge0$ and $r\ge c\mu^{1/8}$. Suppose $0\le B\le\mu^{1/32}$, $B_t\le\mu^{1/16}$ and $E\le\mu^{-1/4}$ are numerical bounds, and $\delta\le A[2\mu^{-1/8}L_+^3(B^2+B_t)/(
u L^{-2})+B/r+E/
u]$. The formal theorem concludes $\delta\le A(5+c^{-1})[L^2L_+^3\mu^{-1/16}+\mu^{-3/32}+\mu^{-1/4}]$. This is the substitution of the scheduled bounds into (6.6), with an explicit resulting constant. It assumes the initial comparison estimate and the older-gradient bounds; it does not establish them for an Euler construction. In the application $L=L_j$, $L_+=L_{j+1}$ and $L^2=\varepsilon^{-1}$.
TorusEuler.induction_comparison_error_bu.summary: Combines older-strain, correction and time-scale bounds

TorusEuler.induction_normalized_comparis.text: Bounds $c\mu^{1/8}\le r\le C\mu^{1/8}L$ on the physical scaling rate $r$ yield the bounds $2cL_{next}^3\le2r\mu^{-1/8}L_{next}^3\le2CL_{next}^4$ on the normalized window. Positive frequency cancels the reciprocal powers. The upper estimate uses $L\le L_{next}$ and $L_{next}\ge0$; the lower coefficient $c$ is not assumed positive in this algebraic lemma.
TorusEuler.induction_normalized_comparis.summary: The normalized window lies between cubic and quartic gain bounds

TorusEuler.induction_older_gradient_scal.text: Let $b\ge1$ and $q\ge0$ be integers, let $\lambda_{\rm old}\ge1$, and put $\mu=\lambda_{\rm old}^{320b(q+1)}$. If numerical bounds satisfy $B\le\lambda_{\rm old}^9$ and $B_t\le\lambda_{\rm old}^{18}$, then $B\le\mu^{1/32}$ and $B_t\le\mu^{1/16}$. In §7.2 the inputs are uniform norms of the gradient and its time derivative for the older velocity, with $\lambda_{\rm old}=\lambda_{j-2}$. This theorem supplies the change of frequency scale only. It neither produces those analytic derivative estimates nor assumes that $B,B_t$ are themselves functions or matrices.
TorusEuler.induction_older_gradient_scal.summary: Expresses the older derivative bounds in the parent frequency

TorusEuler.inductiveEuler_terminal_trace.text: Starting with the specified uniform limit $u$ on a positive common closed slab, proves continuity and periodicity of its terminal slice, global uniform velocity convergence, and convergence of every spatial derivative on compact sets away from the lattice $\mathbb Z^3$. It uses summable correction derivatives and shrinking oscillation supports. Uniqueness of uniform limits identifies this chosen $u$ with the abstractly constructed limit.
TorusEuler.inductiveEuler_terminal_trace.summary: The chosen limit has a smooth terminal trace away from the lattice

TorusEuler.inductive_oscillations_eventu.text: Let $K\subset\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3$ be compact. Suppose radii $r_n\to0$, and for every $0\le t\le T$, any point where $O_{n+1}(t)$ is nonzero lies within distance $r_n$ of an integer lattice point. Then there is an open neighbourhood $V$ of $K$, avoiding the lattice, and an index $N$ such that $O_{n+1}(t,x)=0$ for all $n\ge N$, $t\in[0,T]$ and $x\in V$. No smoothness is required for this support argument. In Proposition 8.4 the radii are $\lambda_n^{-1}$. Vanishing on a neighbourhood, uniformly in time, allows the spatial derivatives of the later oscillations to vanish near $K$ as well.
TorusEuler.inductive_oscillations_eventu.summary: Shrinking supports give uniform vanishing on an open spatial neighbourhood

TorusEuler.inductive_oscillations_eventu.text: Assume $t_n\to T_\infty$ and $O_n(t,\cdot)=0$ for every $n\ge2$ and $0\le t\le t_n$. For each fixed $S<T_\infty$, there is an index $N$ such that $O_{n+1}(t,x)=0$ for every $n\ge N$, $t\in[0,S]$ and $x\in\mathbb R^3$. Neither monotonicity of the activation sequence nor smoothness of the fields is needed for this assertion. Proposition 8.1 combines this eventual vanishing with the correction estimates to obtain convergence in higher spatial norms. The formal statement supplies some sufficiently large index; it does not identify that index with the particular $j_0$ chosen in the paper to control both time and derivative order.
TorusEuler.inductive_oscillations_eventu.summary: All sufficiently late oscillations vanish on each fixed earlier interval

TorusEuler.initialLocalizedCompletedWave.text: For positive $r$ with $2r<1/2$, width $0<h\le1$, nonzero wave vector $k$, and transverse amplitude $b$ (so $k\cdot b=0$), the periodized localized potential has a smooth periodic divergence-free curl. On the inner ball it equals the plane wave exactly. At the origin its derivative is the rank-one map $v\mapsto(k\cdot v)b$.
TorusEuler.initialLocalizedCompletedWave.summary: The initial curl completion preserves the central plane wave gradient

TorusEuler.inner_cross3_left.text: The cross product $k\times a$ has zero inner product with $k$ for arbitrary vectors in three-dimensional Euclidean space. No nonzero or transverse assumption is needed. This algebraic orthogonality supports both the moving frame and the terminal projection that removes the newest wave from the vorticity.
TorusEuler.inner_cross3_left.summary: A curl is perpendicular to its wave vector

TorusEuler.inner_endpointL2Operator_self.text: For a path $v$ whose time integral vanishes, pairing $Bv$ with $v$ equals the endpoint energy $\|Fv\|^2+\langle\Omega v,Jv\rangle$. The zero-integral hypothesis removes the boundary term in the adjoint identity for the time primitive. No positivity of the energy is proved here. The result identifies the operator's quadratic form so the separate coercivity theorem can be applied.

TorusEuler.inner_firstWaveTransportedCov.text: The pairing of the explicit first-wave covector with $v$ is $\lambda v_1-\lambda z v_2$. Only the first two components contribute. This exact formula is used to verify perpendicularity of the smooth seed and to simplify the numerator of the affine pressure and amplitude coefficients.
TorusEuler.inner_firstWaveTransportedCov.summary: Pairing the transported covector with a vector
