It is used in the version of (5.20) for data defined only after activation, without requiring fields at earlier times.
TorusEuler.paperHierarchyActiveVelocityN.summary: The active norm differentiates labels and phase only

TorusEuler.paperHierarchyActiveWord_bddA.text: For a smooth twisted-periodic profile on $[t_0,T]$ with $t_0<T$, every fixed mixed derivative word has bounded samples after multiplication by any time weight bounded on a subset of that interval. The subset may be the launch singleton. The proof shifts the interval to start at zero and uses a zero continuation only outside the slab; it claims smoothness on the slab, not across that continuation's boundary.
TorusEuler.paperHierarchyActiveWord_bddA.summary: All active mixed derivative samples are bounded

TorusEuler.paperHierarchyLaunchValueNorm.text: Defines the finite mixed spatial and phase derivative norm on the singleton time slice $\{t_0\}$. The direction fields already carry the label scale and phase width, and the norm uses no Hölder difference quotients or amplitude weight. It measures the launch datum retained in the active inverse estimate, rather than replacing that datum by zero.
TorusEuler.paperHierarchyLaunchValueNorm.summary: The launch trace has its own unweighted norm

TorusEuler.paperHierarchySumCost.text: Defines twice the number of retained indices in $\{1,\dots,P\}$ times a common coefficient $C$. This turns a uniform per-level estimate into the summed hierarchy estimate. The depth and coefficient are explicit parameters; the definition itself asserts neither nonnegativity nor the validity of the individual level bounds.
TorusEuler.paperHierarchySumCost.summary: Counting the cost of summing retained levels

TorusEuler.paperHierarchyTailCost.text: Defines the explicit tail prefactor using $K$, the square of $C+1$, and the cardinalities of the two omitted-interaction pair sets. The extra constant term accounts for the remaining linear contribution. It is a bookkeeping coefficient for a finite-depth remainder bound, not a statement that the remainder has the required size.
TorusEuler.paperHierarchyTailCost.summary: Counting the interactions in the hierarchy tail

TorusEuler.paperLemma13_slowOrders.text: Let $b\ge1$ be an integer, $K(s)=320b(s+1)$, and $\mathcal B(s)>0$ satisfy $\log\mathcal B(s)\ge4K(s+1)^3$ for $s\ge1$. Suppose $\lambda_0\ge\mathcal B(1)$, $q_1=1$, $\lambda_j=\lambda_{j-1}^{K(q_j)}$, and $q_{j+1}=\max\{1\le s\le q_j+1:\mathcal B(s)\le\lambda_{j-1}\}$. Then $q_j\le q_{j+1}\le q_j+1$, $q_j\to\infty$, and $4\log\lambda_{j+2}\le(\log\lambda_{j-1})^2$ for $j\ge1$. Thus the last expression is exactly (1.15), since $L_{j+1}=4\log\lambda_{j+2}$. The formal statement omits threshold monotonicity and analytic-cost domination from §1.5; the arithmetic result therefore applies under fewer assumptions.
TorusEuler.paperLemma13_slowOrders.summary: The same recurrence yields all conclusions of Lemma 1.3

TorusEuler.paperLemma31_waveProfile.text: The theorem supplies smooth one-periodic profiles $F_h,P_h$ for $0<h\le1$, with $F_h$ odd, $P_h'=F_h$, and $P_h$ of mean zero. One constant $C>0$, independent of $h$ and phase $s$, satisfies $F_h'(0)=1$, $-Ch\le F_h'(s)\le1$ and $|F_h(s)|\le Ch$. For each integer $j\ge2$, a constant $C_j>0$ is chosen before $h,s$ and gives $|F_h^{(j)}(s)|\le C_jh^{1-j}$. The exponent $1-j$ is an integer and may be negative; it is not truncated to zero. These are the existence and uniformity assertions of Lemma 3.1. No regularity in the parameter $h$ is asserted.
TorusEuler.paperLemma31_waveProfile.summary: One family realizes the normalization and derivative bounds

TorusEuler.paperLemma57_periodicGraphFro.text: At a fixed time, let $A$ be a smooth lattice-equivariant label map with continuous inverse. Let smooth $f(a,s)$ equal a smooth spatially periodic mean whenever some $|a_i|>1/2-\delta$, with $0<\delta\le1/2$. Evaluate $f$ at $s=k_*\cdot a$ in the centered cell and repeat using $A$; the resulting field $g$ is smooth and periodic. Assume $\ell_*,h>0$, $\mathsf D,\lambda,L\ge1$, $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, $|k_*|\le\mathsf D\lambda$, $\ell_*^{-1}\le\mathsf D^a$, and smooth $B$ with $B\circ A=DA$, $\ell_*^j\|D^jB\|_\infty\le L\mathsf D$ for $j\le m+1$. For each $n\le m+1$, every derivative through order $n$ of $f(\ell_*a,hs)$ is bounded by $\gamma N_n$, where $\gamma,N_n\ge0$. Put $K_n=[3\,2^n(2L)]^nN_n\mathsf D^{(\max(a,1)+1)n}\gamma\lambda^{3n/2}$. The sum over ordered order-$m$ coordinate derivatives is at most $3^mK_m$, and $\|g\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\le3(m+1)K_{m+1}$. This statement is spatial at one time; it asserts no joint time regularity.
TorusEuler.paperLemma57_periodicGraphFro.summary: The phase dependent part vanishes before neighboring cells are joined

TorusEuler.paperLemma61_exists_firstWave.text: Assume $0<\rho\le1$, $T\ge0$, $\lambda>0$ and $T\|B_\rho\|\le1/8$, where $B_\rho=2\pi(e_1+\rho e_3)\otimes e_2$. The formal theorem gives a first central wave with $\kappa(0)=\lambda e_1$, positive initial amplitude along $e_2$, nonzero transversality and attained peak $\lambda^{-3/4}$. It satisfies $\lambda^{1/4}/2\le|\kappa(0)||\mathbf a(0)|\le\lambda^{1/4}$ and, for every $\mathsf D\ge2$, $\nu\ge\mathsf D^{-1}$ and $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for transverse solutions and $0\le t'\le t\le T$, with $\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a|$. Unlike the numbered formal statement of Lemma 6.1, this version allows $T=0$ and every positive frequency, including frequencies below one. At $T=0$, derivatives within the singleton interval impose no evolution equation beyond the stipulated values.
TorusEuler.paperLemma61_exists_firstWave.summary: Constructs a normalized first wave satisfying all central requirements

TorusEuler.paperLemma61_firstWave.text: Let $\kappa,\mathbf a$ be any first central wave over $B_\rho=2\pi(e_1+\rho e_3)\otimes e_2$, with initial covector $\lambda e_1$, positive initial amplitude along $e_2$, nonzero transversality and attained peak $\lambda^{-3/4}$ on $[0,T]$. If $0<\rho\le1$, $\lambda>0$ and $T\|B_\rho\|\le1/8$, its initial strength lies in $[\lambda^{1/4}/2,\lambda^{1/4}]$. For every $\mathsf D\ge2$ it satisfies $\nu(t)\ge\mathsf D^{-1}$ and $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for transverse amplitude solutions and ordered times, where $\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a|$. This statement assumes the wave has already been given and proves the estimates for every such choice. It does not require $\lambda\ge1$.
TorusEuler.paperLemma61_firstWave.summary: Every normalized first wave satisfies the three required estimates

TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_mixed.text: The time-path clause of Lemma A.2, restricted to time-mean-zero fields by the same mixed projection as Appendix A.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_mixed.summary: A polynomial bound for the time-path inverse

TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_mixed_higher.text: This is the path-valued version of the higher spatial inverse on the normalized interval. The coercivity hypothesis is required only on paths $w$ with zero time integral over $[0,1]$. Both datum and solution lie in the fixed space of the mixed projection, which imposes spatial solenoidality and zero time mean. The derivative words through order $n$ concern spatial labels, not time differentiability.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_mixed_higher.summary: The mixed inverse preserves derivative words

TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_mixed_holder.text: Let $H=L^2([0,1];\mathbb R^3)$ and $\mathcal R=\mathbb P\mathcal Q$, with $\mathcal Q$ subtracting the time average. Suppose $B\in C^{1,1/2}(\mathbb T^3;\mathcal L(H))$ and $\langle B(a)w,w\rangle\ge\mu\|w\|^2$ for zero-mean paths, with $\mu>0$. Then $\mathcal RB$ is invertible on $\mathcal RC^{0,1/2}$ and $\|v\|\le C(2+\mu^{-1}+\|B\|_\infty+\|D_aB\|_\infty)^{145}\|\mathcal RBv\|$. This is only the time-path case of Lemma A.2. The constant is independent of the coefficient and datum; higher regularity and the spatial-vector case are separate results.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_mixed_holder.summary: Apply freezing to divergence-free paths of zero time mean

TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_mixed_holder_bou.text: Let $H=L^2([0,1];\mathbb R^3)$, $\mathcal R=\mathbb P\mathcal Q$, and $B\in C^{n,1/2}(\mathbb T^3;\mathcal L(H))$ for an integer $n\ge0$. Then $v\mapsto\mathcal R(Bv)$ maps projected $C^{n,1/2}$ fields to the same class, with norm at most $C$ times the input norm. The constant may depend on $B$ and $n$, but is chosen before $v$. Time remains an $L^2$ variable. This is the forward bound in Lemma A.2 and needs no coercivity assumption or inverse theorem.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_mixed_holder_bou.summary: Bound multiplication and projection in the same spatial class

TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_mixed_holder_bou.text: Let $H=L^2([0,1];\mathbb R^3)$ and $\mathcal R=\mathbb P\mathcal Q$. Suppose $B\in C^{k,1/2}(\mathbb T^3;\mathcal L(H))$ for an integer $k\ge1$, and $\langle B(a)w,w\rangle\ge\mu\|w\|^2$ on zero-time-mean paths with $\mu>0$. There is a base half-Hölder inverse of $\mathcal RB$ that maps every projected $C^{k,1/2}$ datum to a solution in that class with bound $\|v\|_{C^{k,1/2}}\le C\|f\|_{C^{k,1/2}}$. The constant may depend on $B,k,\mu$, not on $f$. The formal order is written $k=n+1$, covering precisely the positive integer orders.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_mixed_holder_bou.summary: Preserve the source regularity when solving on time paths

TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_mixed_holder_hig.text: This gives the analogous unique solution on the fixed space of the mixed spatial and time-mean projection. The coefficient’s coercivity is required only on zero-time-mean paths, and the higher regularity is with respect to spatial labels. It does not produce time derivatives or a continuous-in-time representative; those are later parts of the endpoint recovery.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_mixed_holder_hig.summary: The mixed inverse preserves the ordinary Hölder class

TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_mixed_holder_res.text: With $H=L^2([0,1];\mathbb R^3)$ and $\mathcal R=\mathbb P\mathcal Q$, assume $B\in C^{k,1/2}$, integer $k\ge1$, and positive coercivity on zero-time-mean paths at each label. Then $\mathcal R(Bv)$ belongs to $C^{k,1/2}$ whenever projected $v$ does, and every projected datum $f$ in that class has a unique projected solution $v$ of $\mathcal R(Bv)=f$ in the same class. This is the higher existence and uniqueness assertion of Lemma A.2 for time paths. The statement does not include a numerical norm bound; that bound is proved separately.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_mixed_holder_res.summary: Give a unique preimage in the same spatial Hölder class

TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_spatial.text: The spatial clause of Lemma A.2, with a fixed polynomial in the coercivity, sup-norm and Lipschitz constants.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_spatial.summary: A polynomial bound for the spatial inverse

TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_spatial_higher.text: Under positive coercivity and a nonnegative Lipschitz bound for $B$, the spatial compressed equation has a unique solution carrying actual coordinate derivative words through order $n$ whenever coefficient and datum carry those words. The hypotheses on $B$ and $f$ assert that their spatial derivative words through order $n$ exist and are half-Hölder. The result is qualitative and uses the same order-zero inverse; conversion to the usual lifted Hölder norm is proved later.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_spatial_higher.summary: The spatial inverse preserves derivative words

TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_spatial_holder.text: Suppose $B\in C^{1,1/2}(\mathbb T^3;\mathcal L(\mathbb R^3))$ and $B(a)w\cdot w\ge\mu|w|^2$ for every label and vector, with $\mu>0$. Then $v\mapsto\mathbb P(Bv)$ is invertible on divergence-free $C^{0,1/2}$ fields, with $\|v\|\le C(2+\mu^{-1}+\|B\|_\infty+\|D_aB\|_\infty)^{145}\|\mathbb P(Bv)\|$. The constant is chosen before $B,\mu$ and the datum. This proves the spatial-vector case of Lemma A.2 and fixes a polynomial exponent where the paper leaves it unspecified. The time-path case and higher norms are separate statements.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_spatial_holder.summary: Apply freezing to the spatial Leray equation

TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_spatial_holder_b.text: For an integer $n\ge0$, suppose the matrix coefficient $B$ belongs to $C^{n,1/2}(\mathbb T^3)$. If $v$ is divergence free and in the same class, then $\mathbb P(Bv)$ belongs to $C^{n,1/2}$ and $\|\mathbb P(Bv)\|_{C^{n,1/2}}\le C\|v\|_{C^{n,1/2}}$. The constant may depend on $B,n$, but is uniform in $v$. This is the forward-map bound used in the final assertion of Lemma A.2. Coercivity is unnecessary for multiplication and projection; it is needed only for the inverse direction.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_spatial_holder_b.summary: Bound the projected product without a coercivity hypothesis

TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_spatial_holder_b.text: Let $B\in C^{k,1/2}(\mathbb T^3;\mathcal L(\mathbb R^3))$, where $k\ge1$ is an integer, and assume $B(a)w\cdot w\ge\mu|w|^2$ for all $a,w$, with $\mu>0$. The base half-Hölder inverse of $\mathbb PB$ maps every divergence-free $C^{k,1/2}$ datum to a solution in the same class, with $\|v\|_{C^{k,1/2}}\le C\|f\|_{C^{k,1/2}}$. The constant is uniform in $f$ but may depend on $B,k,\mu$. The formal positive order is written as $n+1$. No single polynomial estimate uniform over all higher orders is asserted.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_spatial_holder_b.summary: Control the inverse in each available Hölder norm

TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_spatial_holder_h.text: For positive coercivity and a Lipschitz coefficient, the spatial compressed equation has a unique solution in the lifted order-$n$ half-Hölder class whenever coefficient and datum belong to that class. The proof converts their ordinary regularity to derivative words and back. This statement is qualitative; boundedness in the higher norm is established later in the formalization.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_spatial_holder_h.summary: The spatial inverse preserves the ordinary Hölder class

TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_spatial_holder_r.text: For an integer $k\ge1$, let $B\in C^{k,1/2}(\mathbb T^3;\mathcal L(\mathbb R^3))$ satisfy the positive pointwise quadratic lower bound with constant $\mu>0$. Then $v\mapsto\mathbb P(Bv)$ preserves divergence-free $C^{k,1/2}$ fields, and every divergence-free datum of that regularity has a unique preimage in the same class. This is the higher regularity solvability assertion of Lemma A.2 for spatial vectors. The formal order $n+1$ ranges over all positive integers; quantitative higher norm bounds are supplied by separate results.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaA2_spatial_holder_r.summary: Solve the projected equation in the datum regularity class

TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_bernstein.text: Let $\psi$ be smooth, zero outside the radius-two ball and one on the unit ball. For each integer $m\ge0$, the formal statement supplies $C_m\ge0$ such that, for $\Lambda\ge1$ and a continuous complex Banach-valued torus field with no frequencies above $4\Lambda$, the sum of the supremum norms of all ordered $m$-fold coordinate derivatives is at most $C_m\Lambda^m\|f\|_\infty$. Spatial derivatives are taken on the periodic lift to $\mathbb R^3$. Mixed partials occur repeatedly in this sum, whereas (B.1) counts each multi-index once. The estimate therefore implies the multi-index bound for this target class, but it does not state the paper's arbitrary real normed-space version.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_bernstein.summary: Bounds a sum over all coordinate differentiation sequences

TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_bernstein_real.text: Chooses a nonnegative constant for each derivative order and cutoff symbol, uniformly over all real normed value spaces and $\Lambda\ge1$. The sum over all ordered coordinate words of length $m$ is at most $C\Lambda^m\|g\|$ for a $4\Lambda$-band-limited function. Ordered words include repetitions of mixed multi-indices, so this directly controls the paper’s smaller multi-index sum.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_bernstein_real.summary: Bernstein estimate for real normed values

TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_bernstein_real_m.text: Fix a smooth symbol equal to one on the unit ball and zero outside the radius-two ball. For every integer $m\ge0$, the formal statement chooses $C_m$ before the real normed target space, the frequency $\Lambda\ge1$, and the continuous torus field $f$. If every scalar measurement of $f$ has Fourier coefficients zero above $4\Lambda$, it proves $\sum_{|\beta|=m}\|\partial^\beta f\|_\infty\le C_m\Lambda^m\|f\|_\infty$. Derivatives use the periodic lift to $\mathbb R^3$, and increasing coordinate sequences count each multi-index once. No completeness assumption on the real target is needed. This is the scope and counting convention of (B.1).
TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_bernstein_real_m.summary: Counts every multi-index once for arbitrary real normed targets

TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_LInfinity.text: Let $g$ be an almost-everywhere strongly measurable, essentially bounded field on $\mathbb T^3=\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3$ with values in a complex normed space. For a smooth symbol $\psi$ vanishing outside radius two and $\Lambda>0$, the formal statement gives $\|S_\Lambda g\|_{L^\infty}\le\|\check\psi\|_{L^1(\mathbb R^3)}\|g\|_{L^\infty}$. The measure has total mass one and these are essential suprema. No completeness hypothesis appears: for an incomplete target the formal integral convention assigns zero, so this generality must not be read as a theorem about ordinary integration in an arbitrary incomplete space. For a Banach target it has the usual Fourier-integral interpretation. The numbered Lemma B.1 restricts its complex branch to that complete setting. The result contains no Hölder estimate.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_LInfinity.summary: Controls the cutoff on measurable essentially bounded fields

TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_aeBound.text: Let $g$ be an integrable complex normed-space-valued field on the unit-volume three-dimensional torus, with $|g|\le M$ almost everywhere and $M\ge0$. For a smooth symbol supported in the radius-two ball and $\Lambda>0$, the formal statement proves $|S_\Lambda g(x)|\le M\|\check\psi\|_{L^1}$ at every point. The output is a finite Fourier sum, so its bound is pointwise. Completeness of the target is not assumed; if the target is incomplete, the formal integral convention assigns zero and the formula need not describe ordinary Fourier integration in that space. The paper's finite-dimensional targets avoid this issue. This is the value estimate behind the $L^\infty$ bound, with no spatial-increment conclusion.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_aeBound.summary: Turns an almost-everywhere input bound into a pointwise output bound

TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_commutes_.text: Let $g$ be a continuous complex Banach-valued field on $\mathbb T^3$, whose periodic lift $f$ to $\mathbb R^3$ is $C^m$. Assume $\psi$ is smooth and zero outside the radius-two ball, and $\Lambda>0$. The formal statement proves $D^m(S_\Lambda f)=K_\Lambda*D^mf$, with $K_\Lambda(y)=\Lambda^3\check\psi(\Lambda y)$. Both sides are multilinear derivative tensors. Periodicity and continuity bound the derivatives on all of $\mathbb R^3$. To write the right side as $S_\Lambda(D^mf)$, one also uses the convolution representation for that tensor field. The result supplies spatial commutation only; time differentiation is treated separately.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_commutes_.summary: Differentiates the convolution representation at every finite spatial order

TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_congr_ae.text: If two torus functions agree almost everywhere for the unit-mass measure on $\mathbb T^3$, their Fourier cutoffs agree as functions at every output point. Each Fourier coefficient is unchanged by almost-everywhere replacement, so the finite reconstruction is identical. No integrability hypothesis appears here, because the integral expression is defined for all functions.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_congr_ae.summary: The cutoff respects almost everywhere equality

TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_derivativ.text: Let $g$ be a continuous complex Banach-valued torus field whose periodic lift $f$ belongs to $C^{m,1/2}$. For $\Lambda>0$ and a smooth symbol supported in the radius-two ball, the formal statement gives $D^m(S_\Lambda f)=K_\Lambda*D^mf$, where $K_\Lambda(y)=\Lambda^3\check\psi(\Lambda y)$. The Hölder hypothesis includes differentiability and bounded derivatives through order $m$. The conclusion is an identity of derivative tensors on $\mathbb R^3$ and supplies a spatial commutation step in Appendix B. It neither differentiates in time nor proves the entire tail estimate; a separate result gives the same identity under the weaker $C^m$ assumption. The norm sums, over orders $i\le m$, the supremum and half-Hölder seminorm of the full derivative tensor $D^if$.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_derivativ.summary: Differentiates the cutoff under the stated spatial Hölder hypothesis

TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_holder.text: Let $f$ be the periodic lift of a continuous complex Banach-valued torus field and assume $f\in C^{0,1/2}$. If $\psi$ is smooth and zero outside the radius-two ball and $\Lambda>0$, the formal statement proves $S_\Lambda f\in C^{0,1/2}$ and $\|S_\Lambda f\|_{C^{0,1/2}}\le\|\check\psi\|_{L^1}\|f\|_{C^{0,1/2}}$. Here the Hölder norm is the sum of the uniform norm and half-Hölder seminorm of the periodic lift. The constant does not depend on $\Lambda$ or $f$. No plateau or evenness assumption is needed. This is the Hölder bound in Lemma B.1, not its separate measurable-input essential-supremum estimate.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_holder.summary: Bounds values and increments by the same kernel constant

TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_sup.text: Let $g$ be continuous on $\mathbb T^3=\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3$ with values in a complex Banach space. For $\Lambda>0$ and a smooth real symbol $\psi$ zero outside the radius-two ball, the formal statement gives $\sup_x|S_\Lambda g(x)|\le\|\check\psi\|_{L^1(\mathbb R^3)}\sup_x|g(x)|$. The supremum on the output may be taken over its periodic lift. Compactness guarantees boundedness of the input, while rapid decay makes the kernel integral finite. This proves the continuous-input uniform bound in Appendix B; it is not itself a claim about all measurable $L^\infty$ inputs or the half-Hölder norm.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_sup.summary: Controls continuous torus fields by the kernel integral

TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_support_p.text: Let $g$ be a continuous complex Banach-valued torus field and let the real symbol $\psi$ be even. The formal statement proves that the finite cutoff has no Fourier modes outside $|\xi|\le2\Lambda$ and preserves any relation $g(-x)=c\,g(x)$ with real $c$. Taking $c=-1$ gives oddness and $c=1$ gives evenness. These conclusions follow from the symmetric finite frequency set and the even symbol; smoothness, a plateau and positivity of $\Lambda$ are unnecessary for this algebraic statement. It supplies two parts of Lemma B.1, but it contains no assertion about divergence.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_support_p.summary: Preserves reflection parity and the cutoff frequency band

TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_tail.text: Let $\psi$ be smooth, zero outside the radius-two ball and equal to one on the unit ball. For each integer $M\ge0$, the formal statement supplies $C_M\ge0$ such that, for $\Lambda\ge1$, $0\le s\le M$, and a continuous complex Banach-valued torus field with periodic lift $f\in C^{M,1/2}$, the remainder belongs to $C^{s,1/2}$ and satisfies $\|(I-S_\Lambda)f\|_{C^{s,1/2}}\le C_M\Lambda^{s-M}\|f\|_{C^{M,1/2}}$. The exponent $s-M$ is an integer difference, so negative exponents mean reciprocal powers. These norms sum uniform and Hölder bounds for derivative tensors through the indicated order. The constant is uniform in $s$, frequency and field. This result concerns the complex cutoff; the real-velocity estimate is separate. The derivative tensors are the full iterated derivatives, measured in operator norm.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_cutoff_tail.summary: Controls the loss of derivatives uniformly in the lower order

TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_realBanachCutoff.text: Let $g$ be an almost-everywhere strongly measurable, essentially bounded field on the unit-volume torus $\mathbb T^3=\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3$, with values in a real normed space. Let $\Lambda>0$ and let $\psi$ be smooth and zero outside radius two. Define $H_\Lambda(z)=\sum_{|k|\le2\Lambda}\psi(k/\Lambda)e^{2\pi i k\cdot z}$ and $S^\mathbb R_\Lambda g(x)=\int_{\mathbb T^3}\operatorname{Re}H_\Lambda(x-z)g(z)\,dz$. The formal statement proves $\|S^\mathbb R_\Lambda g\|_{L^\infty}\le\|\check\psi\|_{L^1(\mathbb R^3)}\|g\|_{L^\infty}$. For an even symbol and a Banach target, this is the paper's multiplier. Without evenness, taking the real part symmetrizes the symbol. Completeness is not assumed in the formal estimate; its integral convention assigns zero for incomplete targets. The ordinary Banach-valued integral interpretation therefore uses a complete target. This construction uses the scalar spectral kernel, not a complexification of the target. No Hölder estimate is included.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_realBanachCutoff.summary: Bounds the real-part spectral kernel on essentially bounded fields

TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_realBanachCutoff.text: For a smooth supported symbol and positive scale, an almost-everywhere bound $\|g\|\le M$ with $M\ge0$ gives the pointwise output bound $\|K\|_1M$. Unlike the vector predecessor, this theorem has no integrability hypothesis on $g$ and omits completeness. It bounds the vector-valued integral expression; membership in $L^\infty$ is supplied when using the result as the paper’s $L^\infty$ operator estimate.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_realBanachCutoff.summary: The real kernel gives a uniform pointwise bound

TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_realCutoff_LInfi.text: Let $g:\mathbb T^3\to\mathbb R^3$ be measurable and essentially bounded for the torus measure of total mass one. If $\psi$ is smooth and zero outside the radius-two ball and $\Lambda>0$, the formal statement proves $\|S_\Lambda g\|_{L^\infty}\le\|\check\psi\|_{L^1(\mathbb R^3)}\|g\|_{L^\infty}$. The cutoff is defined by complex Fourier coefficients followed by the real part, and its output is a finite Fourier sum. This supplies the measurable real-input estimate mentioned in Lemma B.1. It is broader in input regularity than the continuous real-velocity supremum clause inside the numbered formal statement.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_realCutoff_LInfi.summary: Bounds the real cutoff without requiring continuous input

TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_realCutoff_admis.text: Let $g$ be a continuous real velocity on $\mathbb T^3$ with smooth periodic lift to $\mathbb R^3$, and let $\psi$ be even. The formal statement says that the real cutoff preserves oddness and divergence freeness whenever the input has those properties, and that every output Fourier coefficient outside $|\xi|\le2\Lambda$ vanishes. These are conditional conclusions, not assumptions that every input is odd or incompressible. No radiality, smoothness of the symbol or positive-scale hypothesis is required for this finite-sum identity. It supplies the velocity properties needed in Subsection 5.7, but evenness preservation is stated in the separate parity result.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_realCutoff_admis.summary: Preserves oddness and incompressibility of smooth real velocities

TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_realCutoff_aeBou.text: For an integrable real velocity representative bounded almost everywhere by $M\ge0$, its cutoff is bounded at every point by $\|K\|_1M$. The symbol is smooth with radius-two support and the scale is positive. The conclusion is stronger than merely an almost-everywhere output bound, while integrability remains an explicit hypothesis.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_realCutoff_aeBou.summary: A pointwise bound from an essential velocity bound

TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_realCutoff_parit.text: Suppose $g:\mathbb T^3\to\mathbb R^3$ is continuous and satisfies $g(-x)=c\,g(x)$ for a real constant $c$, and suppose $\psi$ is even. The formal statement proves the same reflection identity for the real cutoff $S_\Lambda g$. In particular, it preserves oddness when $c=-1$ and evenness when $c=1$. The result concerns a finite Fourier sum and holds for every real scale, without a smoothness or support condition on the symbol. The paper uses the positive-scale cutoff with its prescribed smooth symbol. This declaration proves parity only, not divergence preservation or operator estimates.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_realCutoff_parit.summary: Preserves reflection identities for continuous real velocity fields

TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_realCutoff_sup.text: Let $g:\mathbb T^3\to\mathbb R^3$ be continuous, let $\psi$ be smooth and zero outside the radius-two ball, and let $\Lambda>0$. The formal statement gives $\sup_x|S_\Lambda g(x)|\le\|\check\psi\|_{L^1(\mathbb R^3)}\sup_x|g(x)|$, with the output evaluated on its periodic lift. The real cutoff is the real part of the corresponding complex Fourier sum. The bound is uniform in $\Lambda$ and $g$, and requires neither a plateau nor evenness. It is a continuous-input supremum bound; the essential-supremum estimate for measurable real velocities is a distinct result.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaB1_realCutoff_sup.summary: Bounds the continuous real cutoff by the kernel integral

TorusEuler.paperLemmaD1_derivatives.text: Let $f(t,a,s)$ be smooth in label and phase, let $\ell_*,h>0$, and assume all weighted mixed derivatives through order $n+1$ are bounded uniformly in time, label and phase. The formal statement proves $\sum_{i=1}^3\|\partial_{a_i}f\|_{[n]}\le3\ell_*^{-1}\|f\|_{[n+1]}$ and $\|\partial_sf\|_{[n]}\le h^{-1}\|f\|_{[n+1]}$. Each multi-index is counted once in the finite norms. Applying the inequalities to $f/\gamma(t)$ gives (D.3), because the weight depends only on time. This declaration itself is unweighted and does not assume periodicity or positivity of an amplitude function.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaD1_derivatives.summary: Costs one derivative and the inverse coordinate scale

TorusEuler.paperLemmaD1_phaseAverage.text: Let $f(t,a,s)$ take values in a real Banach space and be smooth in $(a,s)$, one-periodic in $s$, and have bounded derivatives through order $n$ along a fixed finite ordered family of constant directions. The formal statement proves $\|\langle f\rangle_s\|_{[n]}\le\|f\|_{[n]}$ and $\|f-\langle f\rangle_s\|_{[n]}\le2\|f\|_{[n]}$, where the derivative sum uses that specified family. Choosing the scaled label and phase directions gives the norms of Appendix D, and applying the result to $f/\gamma(t)$ gives their weighted form. The time set is arbitrary and all suprema include it. The normalized primitive estimate in (D.5) is not part of this declaration.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaD1_phaseAverage.summary: Bounds phase averaging and removal of the phase average

TorusEuler.paperLemmaD1_phasePrimitive.text: Let $f(t,a,s)$ take values in a real Banach space and be smooth, one-periodic in $s$, have zero phase average at every $(t,a)$, and have bounded derivatives through order $n$ along a fixed finite family of constant directions. The formal statement proves that its normalized phase primitive has finite derivative expression at most twice that of $f$. With directions $\ell_*\partial_{a_i}$ and $h\partial_s$, this is the primitive estimate of (D.5); applying it to $f/\gamma(t)$ yields the positive-amplitude weighted version. The supremum includes the whole chosen time set. This declaration is the derivative-norm estimate, whereas periodicity and recovery of the input by phase differentiation are established separately.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaD1_phasePrimitive.summary: Retains the factor two through every finite derivative order

TorusEuler.paperLemmaD1_product.text: For smooth fields $f,g$, a continuous bilinear map $B$, and smooth prescribed differentiation directions, assume their finite derivative families are bounded, with the second field measured after division by $\gamma(t)$. The formal statement bounds the finite norm of $B(f,g)/\gamma$ by $2^{n+1}N_n\|B\|$ times the product of those two finite norms, where $N_n$ counts the increasing derivative sequences of length at most $n$. It applies to supremum norms and to the maximum convention for half-Hölder norms. Unlike the paper's amplitude weight, $\gamma$ need not be positive here: division by zero gives the zero field at that time. For $\gamma>0$ and the scaled coordinate directions, it yields (D.4).
TorusEuler.paperLemmaD1_product.summary: Controls a product after division by a time weight

TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_inverse.text: Let $\mathsf D\ge1$ and let $q$ be a nonnegative integer. Suppose $c(t,a)$ is smooth in the label, $\|D_a^mc(t,a)\|\le C_m\mathsf D^{q(m+1)}$ uniformly in time and label for every $m$, and every $c(t,a)$ is invertible in a complete real normed algebra. If $\|c(t,a)^{-1}\|\le\mathsf D^q$, the formal statement gives analogous derivative-tensor bounds for $c^{-1}$ with exponent $3q$. Invertibility is required at every point, so the inverse is the usual algebra inverse throughout the domain. The constants are obtained for the fixed coefficient and parent parameter; their uniform selection over varying inputs is stated separately in the full Lemma D.2.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_inverse.summary: Bounds derivatives of the inverse in a complete normed algebra

TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_inverse_coordina.text: In a complete normed algebra, a family with coefficient exponent $a$ has inverse exponent $3a$ if $D\ge1$, every coefficient is invertible, and its inverse norm is bounded by $D^a$. The invertibility hypothesis rules out the assigned fallback value of the inverse at noninvertible elements. The proof transfers the operator-norm inverse theorem through the coordinate equivalence.

TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_inverse_multiInd.text: Let $\mathsf D\ge1$, let $q$ be a nonnegative integer, and let $c:I\times\mathbb R^3\to A$ be smooth with values in a complete real normed algebra. Assume $|c|_m\le C_m\mathsf D^{q(m+1)}$ for every $m$, with bounded coordinate derivatives, pointwise invertibility, and $\|c^{-1}\|_\infty\le\mathsf D^q$. The formal statement gives $|c^{-1}|_m\le C'_m\mathsf D^{3q(m+1)}$, counting each multi-index once. Supremum bounds include every time in $I$. The constants are asserted for the fixed coefficient and parent parameter, not uniformly across families. The numbered Lemma D.2 supplies that stronger quantifier order.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_inverse_multiInd.summary: Controls the summed coordinate derivatives of the inverse

TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_mul.text: Let $\mathsf D\ge1$ and $q\ge0$ be an integer. Suppose two coefficients $c,d:I\times\mathbb R^3\to A$ are smooth and their spatial derivative tensors have uniform bounds $\|D^mc\|\le C_m\mathsf D^{q(m+1)}$ and $\|D^md\|\le C'_m\mathsf D^{q(m+1)}$, with $A$ a real normed algebra. The formal statement proves the same form of estimate for $cd$ with exponent $2q$. It measures the operator norms of derivative tensors, not directly the coordinate sums $|c|_m$. An equivalence theorem converts between these measurements. Constants are asserted for the fixed inputs; the full Lemma D.2 separately states uniformity before choosing the parent parameter and fields.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_mul.summary: Doubles a common integer exponent for coefficient multiplication

TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_mul_coordinate.text: For $D\ge1$, two coefficient families with coordinate exponent $a$ have a product family with exponent $2a$. The theorem converts to operator-norm bounds, applies the product estimate, and converts back. Constants are allowed to depend on derivative order; the conclusion is a fresh coefficient-power condition rather than a fixed numerical table.

TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_mul_multiIndex.text: Let $\mathsf D\ge1$ and let $q$ be a nonnegative integer. For smooth phase-independent coefficients $c,d:I\times\mathbb R^3\to A$ in a real normed algebra, assume bounded derivatives of every order and estimates $|c|_m\le C_m\mathsf D^{q(m+1)}$, $|d|_m\le C'_m\mathsf D^{q(m+1)}$. The formal statement gives $|cd|_m\le C''_m\mathsf D^{2q(m+1)}$ for all $m$, with each spatial multi-index counted once. All time and label values enter the suprema. This proves product closure for the fixed parent parameter and fields. It does not by itself assert constants uniform over those choices, or retain an arbitrary fixed real exponent without enlargement.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_mul_multiIndex.summary: Preserves polynomial growth with a doubled integer exponent

TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_weighted.text: Suppose $\mathsf D\ge1$, $q$ is a nonnegative integer, $\ell_*\ge0$, and $\ell_*\mathsf D^q\le1$. Let a smooth coefficient satisfy $\|D_a^mc\|\le C_m\mathsf D^{q(m+1)}$ uniformly in time and label. The formal statement bounds $\ell_*^m\|D_a^mc\|$ by $C_m\mathsf D^q$, and for $m\ge1$ by $C_m\mathsf D^{2q}\ell_*$. It also bounds the corresponding finite coordinate-derivative norm by an order-dependent constant times $\mathsf D^q$. Unlike the paper's positive radius and fixed real exponent, this result permits zero radius and only integer $q$. The constants are obtained after fixing the parent parameter and coefficient. Thus it supplies the algebraic gain in D.2(c) with those precise conventions.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_weighted.summary: Leaves a radius factor when a coefficient is differentiated

TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_weighted_coordin.text: Assumes $D\ge1$, $\ell\ge0$, $\ell D^a\le1$ and the coordinate coefficient-power predicate. It gives an order table controlling both the full weighted derivative sum by a multiple of $D^a$ and each positive-order term by $C_mD^{2a}\ell$. The second bound retains one radius factor for the derivative-lifting argument.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_weighted_coordin.summary: Retaining a radius in differentiated coefficients

TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_weighted_multiIn.text: Let $\mathsf D\ge1$, let $q$ be a nonnegative integer, and assume $0\le\ell_*$ and $\ell_*\mathsf D^q\le1$. If a smooth coefficient has bounded derivatives and $|c|_m\le C_m\mathsf D^{q(m+1)}$ for every $m$, the formal statement yields $\sum_{m\le n}\ell_*^m|c|_m\le(\sum_{m\le n}C_m)\mathsf D^q$ and $\ell_*^m|c|_m\le C_m\mathsf D^{2q}\ell_*$ for $m\ge1$. The derivative sums count each multi-index once and include the chosen time set. This is the coefficient-radius calculation of D.2(c), allowing zero radius and using integer exponents. Replacing the paper's fixed real exponent by its ceiling can require a strictly smaller radius.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaD2_weighted_multiIn.summary: Retains one radius factor in every positive derivative order

TorusEuler.paperLemmaD3_lifting.text:
Let $\mathcal Lv=L_0v+\sum_
u B_
u(c_
u,v)=f$ in real vector spaces with seminorms $p_A,p_E,p_F$ and a finite ordered derivative family. Assume principal commutation, the product rule, commuting forcing derivatives, $p_F(B_
u(a,u))\le b_
u p_A(a)p_E(u)$, and $p_E(u)\le C_{m low}p_F(\mathcal Lu)$ for every $u$, with $C_{m low}\ge0$. Suppose nonnegative $S_m$ satisfy $C_{m low}\sum_
u b_
u p_A(D_wc_
u)\le S_m$ for every derivative sequence $w$ of length $1\le m\le n$. The formal statement proves $\|v\|_{[n]}\le N_n(1+2^n\sum_{m=0}^nS_m)^nC_{m low}\|f\|_{[n]}$, where $N_n$ counts nondecreasing derivative sequences through order $n$ and the norms sum their seminorms. Coefficient and solution derivatives need not commute in this helper. Weighted coordinate derivatives and appropriate zero-order seminorms give the paper's application. Unlike (D.7), its coefficient hypothesis bounds each sequence separately; the exact-order sum implies those bounds. It estimates an existing solution.
TorusEuler.paperLemmaD3_lifting.summary: Transfer a uniform inverse bound to higher orders

TorusEuler.paperMeanBaseScale.text: Defines the sum of the inverse-deformation bound $D$, velocity-gradient bound $L$, and the size and Lipschitz bounds for the kinetic and vorticity coefficients. This is the scale used to express a common polynomial cap for the endpoint and fixed-time inverses. Positivity and lower bounds are hypotheses of the comparison lemmas, not properties imposed by the definition.
TorusEuler.paperMeanBaseScale.summary: Combine the physical coefficient size controls

TorusEuler.paperMeanIntegratedInverse_of.text: For $0<T\le1$, continuous Hölder coefficients with positive spatial and mixed coercivity yield a unique integrated velocity and a fixed-time inverse. Exact mixed coefficient actions and nonnegative size and Lipschitz bounds are explicit inputs. A single absolute prefactor gives the common cap with exponent $291$, chosen independently of duration and source. Uniqueness is on the closed slab; this declaration does not yet recover the scalar pressure potential.
TorusEuler.paperMeanIntegratedInverse_of.summary: Construct and bound the integrated endpoint inverse

TorusEuler.paperMeanIntegratedMomentum.text: For coefficient curves $K,\Omega$ in operator-valued $C^{0,1/2}(\mathbb T^3)$, a source $L$ in the vector-valued space and divergence-free $v$, define $F(t)=K(t)v(t)-\int_0^t\Omega(s)v(s)\,ds+L(t)$. Multiplication acts pointwise in the spatial label; the integral takes values in the half-Hölder function space. The curves are defined for every real time. If the integrand is not integrable on the oriented interval, this integral expression is assigned zero. For the continuous curves on the positive compact interval used in the endpoint theorem, it is the ordinary vector-valued integral. This defines the left side of (4.9). It does not assert $F=c+\nabla\phi$, zero time mean of $v$, or existence of a solution.
TorusEuler.paperMeanIntegratedMomentum.summary: Form the left side of the endpoint equation

TorusEuler.paperMean_contDiff_one_of_has.text: If $q$ has the specified half-Hölder field as its gradient at every Euclidean point, then $q$ is continuously differentiable. The hypothesis asserts an actual gradient, which includes differentiability. The proof identifies the Fréchet derivative through the inner-product duality map and obtains its continuity from the torus field’s continuous lift.
TorusEuler.paperMean_contDiff_one_of_has.summary: A represented Hölder gradient gives a continuous derivative

TorusEuler.paperMean_inverse_scale.text: Let $D\ge1$ and let $L,C_K,C_\Omega,L_K,L_\Omega$ be nonnegative. Set $Q=D+L+C_K+C_\Omega+L_K+L_\Omega$. Then $Q\ge1$ and $4+D^2+2D^2(1+L)^2+C_K+C_\Omega+L_K+L_\Omega\le16Q^4$. In Theorem 4.2, $D$ bounds the inverse deformation, $L$ the transported gradient, and the remaining quantities bound coefficients and their first spatial derivatives. This elementary inequality combines reciprocal ellipticity and displacement coercivity into one polynomial scale. It does not establish any of those analytic bounds.
TorusEuler.paperMean_inverse_scale.summary: Bound reciprocal coercivity by the parent coefficient controls

TorusEuler.paperMean_normalized_potentia.text: Two potentials with the same represented half-Hölder gradient and zero integral over the centered cell are equal everywhere. Actual gradient witnesses make both potentials continuously differentiable, so their difference is constant and their cell integrals are genuine integrals. The cell has volume one, forcing the constant to vanish. Periodicity of the potentials is not required by this theorem.
TorusEuler.paperMean_normalized_potentia.summary: Equal gradients determine the normalized pressure

TorusEuler.paperMean_projection_C1_gradi.text: Let $q$ be a continuously differentiable $\mathbb Z^3$-periodic scalar function on $\mathbb R^3$, and suppose its gradient represents a $C^{0,1/2}$ vector field $g$ on $\mathbb T^3$. Then $\mathbb Pg=0$. This is the pressure-removal step in Appendix A. A zero-mean normalization of $q$ is not needed. Periodicity is needed: a constant vector field is a gradient of a nonperiodic affine function, but the torus Leray projection preserves that constant field.
TorusEuler.paperMean_projection_C1_gradi.summary: Remove the gradient of a periodic scalar potential

TorusEuler.paperMean_projection_gradient.text: A half-Hölder field whose lift is the gradient of a smooth periodic potential has zero solenoidal projection. This supplies the pressure cancellation needed to pass between projected and unprojected mean equations.
TorusEuler.paperMean_projection_gradient.summary: The spatial Leray projection kills pressure gradients

TorusEuler.paperPhysicalStepExponent.text: For nonnegative integer exponents $a,r,a_{\rm mean}$, define $b=6r+5a+2a_{\rm mean}+160$. The terms correspond to the envelope scale, hierarchy loss and the coefficient cost in the mean-pressure estimate. This is one sufficient numerical exponent used for $C_{\rm step}=\Gamma_P\mathsf D^b$ in §5.6. The formula itself does not prove that any estimate is dominated; the subsequent inequalities verify that fact and choose $\Gamma_P$. It contains no dependence on derivative order, frequency or expansion depth. Depth dependence is allowed in the separate coefficient $\Gamma_P$.
TorusEuler.paperPhysicalStepExponent.summary: Choose an integer exponent that dominates all required parent powers

TorusEuler.paperProposition511_physicalC.text: Fix a smooth even symbol $\psi$, equal to one on $|\xi|\le1$ and zero on $|\xi|>2$. Let $P\ge2$, $T>0$, $\Lambda\ge1$, with $V,R_V$ smooth periodic fields, $V$ odd and divergence free, and a pressure $\Pi$ smooth and periodic at each time. Assume $V_t+V\cdot\nabla V+\nabla\Pi=R_V$ and $D^2(\Pi-p_U)\le sI$, with $p_U$ spatially $C^2$. The formal statement constructs $u=S_\Lambda V$ and zero-mean pressure $p$ solving $\Delta p=-\operatorname{tr}((Du)^2)$. Both $u,R_u$ are odd and divergence free, with Fourier radii $2\Lambda,4\Lambda$. Set $\varepsilon=\Lambda^{2-P}(1+\|V\|_{C_tC^{P,1/2}})^2$ and $e=C\|R_V\|_{C_tC^{1,1/2}}+C_P\varepsilon$. Then $\|u-V\|_{C_tC^{2,1/2}}\le C_P\varepsilon$, $\|R_u\|_{C_tC^{1,1/2}}+\|D^2(p-\Pi)\|_{C_tC^{0,1/2}}\le e$, and $D^2(p-p_U)\le(s+e)I$. The exponent $2-P$ is signed integer arithmetic. Constants may depend on the fixed symbol, not the fields or $\Lambda$.
TorusEuler.paperProposition511_physicalC.summary: The cutoff controls velocity error, residual and added pressure curvature

TorusEuler.paperProposition51_parentCoef.text: Let $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge1$, and let $X$ be the flow of a smooth unit-periodic $U$. Assume $\|D_aX\|,\|(D_aX)^{-1}\|\le\mathsf D$ and $\|D^jU\|_\infty\le R_n\mathsf D^j$ for every $1\le j\le n$, where the nonnegative sequence $R_n$ is fixed before the flow. Put $F=DX$, $G=F^{-1}$, $M=DU\circ X$, $\kappa=G^Tk_*$, and suppose $|\kappa(t_0,0)|=\lambda>0$ at $t_0\in[0,T]$. A sequence $C_m\ge0$, chosen before the flow, gives $\|D_a^m\Phi\|_\infty\le C_m\mathsf D^{16m+16}$ for every $m\ge0$ and every $\Phi\in\{F,G,M,\kappa/\lambda,\lambda^2/|\kappa|^2,P_\kappa\}$. Norms are multilinear operator norms, uniform in time and label. This supplies (5.6) with one explicit exponent. Unlike the numbered proposition, this analytic helper assumes the velocity derivative bounds directly and requires no pressure, residual or coercivity condition.
TorusEuler.paperProposition51_parentCoef.summary: All six coefficient families share one derivative bound

TorusEuler.paperProposition51_parentComp.text: Let $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge1$, and let $X$ be the flow of a smooth unit-periodic $U$. Assume $\|D_aX\|,\|(D_aX)^{-1}\|\le\mathsf D$ and $\|D^jU\|_\infty\le R_n\mathsf D^j$ for every $1\le j\le n$, where the nonnegative sequence $R_n$ is fixed before the flow. Fix a nonnegative sequence $C'_m$ before the flow. Let $f(t,\cdot)$ be smooth with values in a real normed space and satisfy $\|D^mf(t)\|_\infty\le C'_mA_f\mathsf D^m$ for every $m\ge0$, uniformly in $t$, with $A_f\ge0$. Then a nonnegative sequence $C_m$, chosen before the flow and $f$, satisfies $\|D_a^m(f\circ X)\|_\infty\le C_mA_f\mathsf D^{6m}$. No periodicity or time regularity of $f$ is required beyond these uniform spatial hypotheses. Spatial derivatives use multilinear operator norms.
TorusEuler.paperProposition51_parentComp.summary: The chain rule preserves polynomial derivative growth

TorusEuler.paperProposition51_weightedCo.text: Let $\mathsf D\ge1$, $\ell_*\ge0$, $A_f\ge0$ and $C_j\ge0$. Suppose $\ell_*\mathsf D^6\le1$ and, uniformly for $t\in[0,T]$, $\|D^jf(t)\|_\infty\le C_jA_f\mathsf D^{6j}$ for every $j\ge0$. Then $\sum_{j=0}^n\ell_*^j\|D^jf(t)\|_\infty\le(\sum_{j=0}^nC_j)A_f$. The conclusion uses the sum of the supplied constants, not their $n$th member. The statement is a weighted summation of given bounds; it does not itself establish the composition estimate for $f\circ X$. Its derivative norms are multilinear operator norms.
TorusEuler.paperProposition51_weightedCo.summary: The radius weights leave only the original amplitude

TorusEuler.paperTheorem71.text: The theorem chooses an integer $b\ge1$, a nondecreasing positive threshold $\mathcal B$ satisfying (1.13), and $N_1\ge\mathcal B(1)$. For every $N\ge N_1$, it constructs a scheduled sequence with initial frequency $N$ and strength constant $18e^3$. The velocities are smooth, odd and divergence free, with controlled residuals, localized oscillations, small spatial Hölder corrections, prescribed central crossings, and activation times accumulating at a finite positive time before every stage endpoint. This is an existence theorem for one selected threshold. The later paper statement of Theorem 7.1 quantifies over all thresholds above a chosen analytic majorant and records further identifications with the finite expansion; those assertions are not part of this shorter conclusion.
TorusEuler.paperTheorem71.summary: One threshold works at every sufficiently large initial frequency

TorusEuler.paperTheorem71_of_constructio.text: Given an inductive construction, a large initial-frequency bound and the required stationary-start identity, produces a finite terminal time and the full set of conclusions of Theorem 7.1. The proof transfers regularity, Fourier support, inverse deformation, pressure, central splitting, crossings and increment estimates from the actual stages. This is the retained frozen correspondence, not the formalization's current conditional route to the main result.
TorusEuler.paperTheorem71_of_constructio.summary: One physical construction supplies all common-sequence conclusions

TorusEuler.paperTheoremA1.text: On $[0,1]\times\mathbb T^3$, let $K,\Omega$ be time-continuous in $C^{0,1/2}$, spatially differentiable, with uniform value and first derivative bounds. Assume $K\ge\kappa I$ as quadratic forms, $\kappa>0$, and $\int(Kz_t\cdot z_t+\Omega z_t\cdot z)\ge\mu\int|z_t|^2$, $\mu>0$, for all $H^1_0$ paths. Every $L\in C_tC^{0,1/2}$ gives a unique velocity, zero endpoint displacement, constant solenoidal field and pressure gradient satisfying $Kv-J(\Omega v)+L=c+\nabla\phi$, where $Jv(t)=\int_0^tv$. The velocity bound is $CQ^{291}\|L\|_0$, with $Q=2+\kappa^{-1}+\mu^{-1}$ plus the four coefficient bounds. A zero-mean periodic potential is supplied; smooth data give smooth $z,c,\nabla\phi$. Unlike the numbered Theorem A.1, this result does not separately require symmetric $K$ or skew-symmetric $\Omega$.
TorusEuler.paperTheoremA1.summary: Solve without separately imposing coefficient symmetry

TorusEuler.paper_mean_columns.text: Let $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$, and let $X$ be the flow of a smooth unit-periodic $U$. Assume $\|D_aX\|,\|(D_aX)^{-1}\|\le\mathsf D$ and $\|D^jU\|_\infty\le R_n\mathsf D^j$ for every $1\le j\le n$, where the nonnegative sequence $R_n$ is fixed before the flow. Put $F=DX$, $M=DU\circ X$ and require $\|M\|\le L\le\mathsf D$, $L\ge0$, and $-(M_t+M^2)\le I$. Let smooth periodic $B,z,\mathsf q,f_{\rm lab}$ satisfy $B=Fz_t$, $\operatorname{div}_az_t=0$, $z(0)=z(T)=0$ and $B_t+MB+F^{-T}\nabla_a\mathsf q=f_{\rm lab}$. There exist integers $b,s_0\ge0$ and constants $C_n\ge0$, chosen before the flow, such that for $s\ge s_0$, $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-s}$, $\|B\|_{[n]}\le C_n\mathsf D^{b+2+2s}\|f_{\rm lab}\|_{[n+1]}$. The norms sum scaled label-derivative suprema over the full interval. This estimates existing endpoint solutions.
TorusEuler.paper_mean_columns.summary: The endpoint mean loses one derivative uniformly in order

TorusEuler.paper_mean_hardy.text: In a complete real Hilbert space, let $0<T\le1$, $F_t=MF$, and let $M_t$ be continuous. Suppose $H^\#=-(M_t+M^2)\le I$ as quadratic forms. For any $v\in L^2([0,T])$ with zero integral, put $z=Jv$ and $\xi=Fz$. Then $\int H^\#\xi\cdot\xi\le\frac12\int|\xi_t|^2$ and $\int(F^TFv\cdot v+F^T(M^T-M)Fv\cdot z)\ge\frac12\int|\xi_t|^2$. This is the general theorem behind Lemma 4.1. It requires neither invertibility of $F$ nor a realization of $F$ as a particle-flow derivative. Here $Jw(t)=\int_0^tw(s)\,ds$.
TorusEuler.paper_mean_hardy.summary: Prove the energy inequalities without a particle-flow assumption

TorusEuler.paper_mean_inverse.text: On $[0,T]$, let $F,G,M$ be smooth unit-periodic matrix fields with $GF=FG=I$, $F_t=MF$, $\|G\|\le D$, $\|M\|\le L$, and $-(M_t+M^2)\le I$. Put $K=F^TF$, $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$. Assume $0<T\le1$, $D\ge1$, $L\ge0$, and nonnegative suprema $K_0,K_1,\Omega_0,\Omega_1$ for $K,D_aK,\Omega,D_a\Omega$. There is an absolute $C\ge0$ such that $A=C(D+L+K_0+K_1+\Omega_0+\Omega_1)^{1164}$ bounds $\|(\mathbb PK(t))^{-1}\mathbb P\|$ and gives $\|v\|_{C_tC^{0,1/2}}\le A\|L_{\rm src}\|_{C_tC^{0,1/2}}$ for every continuous half-Hölder source. The constructed fields satisfy $Kv-J(\Omega v)+L_{\rm src}=c+\nabla_a\phi$, $z=Jv$, $z(0)=z(T)=0$, with solenoidal $v,c$, $z\in C^1_tC^{0,1/2}$, continuous pressure gradient and spatial mean-zero periodic $\phi$. Here $J$ integrates from zero. The stated uniqueness identifies $v$ and $c$; it does not assert uniqueness of the scalar potential.
TorusEuler.paper_mean_inverse.summary: Continuous Hölder sources have unique endpoint velocities and constant fields

TorusEuler.paper_mean_inverse_smooth_for.text: Let $0<T\le1$, $D\ge1$, $L\ge0$. Suppose smooth periodic matrix fields satisfy $F_t=MF$, $G=F^{-1}$, $\|G\|\le D$, $\|M\|\le L$, and $-(M_t+M^2)\le I$. Every smooth periodic label force $f_{\mathrm{lab}}$ gives smooth periodic $z,v,B,\mathsf q$ with $z_t=v$, $z(0)=z(T)=0$, $\operatorname{div}_av=0$, $B=Fv$ and $B_t+MB+G^T\nabla_a\mathsf q=f_{\mathrm{lab}}$. The pressure has zero mean on the unit torus. To obtain the physical equation of Theorem 4.2 one must identify $F,M$ with the actual incompressible flow and set $f_{\mathrm{lab}}=f\circ X$.
TorusEuler.paper_mean_inverse_smooth_for.summary: Solve the forced equation in particle labels

TorusEuler.paper_mean_inverse_smooth_for.text:
Let $0<T\le1$, and let $U$ be smooth, periodic and divergence free with flow $X$. Assume $\|(D_aX)^{-1}\|\le D$, $D\ge1$, $\|D_xU\|\le L$, $L\ge0$, and $-(M_t+M^2)\le I$ along trajectories. For every smooth periodic force $f$, the formal statement constructs smooth periodic $b,q$ solving $b_t+(U\cdot
abla)b+(b\cdot
abla)U+
abla q=f$ and $\operatorname{div}b=0$. It first constructs label fields $z,v,B=Fv$ with $z_t=v$ and $z(0)=z(T)=0$, then sets $b=B\circ X^{-1}$. The label pressure has zero spatial mean. This is existence with the endpoint choice used in §1.2; uniqueness and a quantitative Hölder bound are not conclusions of this particular theorem.
TorusEuler.paper_mean_inverse_smooth_for.summary: The endpoint solution yields a periodic linearized Euler correction

TorusEuler.paper_section_8_of_inductiveE.text: There is an initial-frequency threshold, chosen before the compatible approximate stages and central waves, above which they admit one finite positive accumulation time $T$ and one Euler limit $u,p$. Compatibility includes the prescribed schedule, smooth odd divergence-free periodic velocities, projected residual bounds, shrinking oscillation supports, small corrections and the central-wave crossing data. The conclusion gives uniform velocity convergence on $[0,T]$, convergence in every spatial Hölder order on each earlier interval, bounded velocity, central vorticity blow-up, maximality and both infinite integrals, and local $C^m$ limits for $u$ and $\partial_tu$ away from the torus origin. Every stage lasts beyond $T$ and $t_j\to T$. This theorem assumes the compatible stages and waves; it does not construct them from arbitrary initial data.
TorusEuler.paper_section_8_of_inductiveE.summary: One compatible sequence gives all four Section 8 conclusions together

TorusEuler.parentResidualFourierBand_of_.text: Let $U$ be a torus velocity whose lift is smooth on $[0,T]$, with $T>0$ and Fourier support in $|\xi|\le2\mathsf D$ for every time, where $\mathsf D\ge0$. At a fixed time, identify its advection with a half-Hölder torus field and suppose the within-interval time derivative equals $-\mathbb P(U\cdot\nabla U)+R_U$. Then $R_U$ has Fourier support in $|\xi|\le4\mathsf D$. Time differentiation preserves the velocity band, products add frequency supports, and the spatial projection preserves each frequency. This proves the support implication used in §5.1 once the residual is identified with projected momentum. It does not choose the pressure or prove that identification.
TorusEuler.parentResidualFourierBand_of_.summary: Quadratic advection doubles the parent frequency radius

TorusEuler.parentResidual_invCube_le_par.text: For frequency $\Lambda\ge1$, the bound $\Lambda^{-3}\le\Lambda^{-5/2}$ holds, since the exponent $-3$ is smaller. The formal statement writes $-5/2$ as the mean-velocity exponent $-5/2-2(p-2)/3$ at $p=2$. This scalar comparison lets the preceding stage's stronger residual estimate supply the next stage's parent-smallness hypothesis.
TorusEuler.parentResidual_invCube_le_par.summary: Cubic decay supplies the required parent smallness

TorusEuler.periodicComplexLeray.text: This is the orthogonal projection onto the Fourier-defined solenoidal subspace of complex spatial $L^2$. Unlike the earlier finite-mode formulas, it acts on every Hilbert-space field. The later mode and coefficient identities establish that this all-field operator has the intended Fourier symbol.
TorusEuler.periodicComplexLeray.summary: Orthogonal Leray projection on all complex L2 fields

TorusEuler.periodicComplexLeray_mode.text: Applying the full $L^2$ Leray projection to one inserted Fourier mode gives the same mode with its coefficient orthogonally projected onto the complex plane perpendicular to the frequency $k$. The proof checks the projected candidate and its longitudinal error using orthogonality. This certifies the intended Fourier symbol rather than assuming it.
TorusEuler.periodicComplexLeray_mode.summary: The Hilbert projection has the prescribed Leray mode action

TorusEuler.periodicComplexSolenoidal.text: This submodule consists of spatial complex $L^2$ fields orthogonal to the longitudinal Fourier span. It is the Fourier definition of the solenoidal space. Later lemmas characterize membership by transverse coefficients and connect real weakly divergence-free fields with this complex Hilbert formulation.
TorusEuler.periodicComplexSolenoidal.summary: The Hilbert space orthogonal to longitudinal modes

TorusEuler.periodicComplexifyL2.text: This bounded real-linear map applies coordinatewise complexification to a real spatial $L^2$ field. It retains the underlying real velocity while placing it in the complex Hilbert space suited to Fourier analysis. Its following evaluation theorem states the representative relation almost everywhere.
TorusEuler.periodicComplexifyL2.summary: Embedding real spatial fields into complex L2

TorusEuler.periodicComplexifyL2_apply_ae.text: The image of a real spatial $L^2$ field under complexification agrees almost everywhere with coordinatewise complexification of its representative. This is the standard representative formula for the bounded map on $L^2$. It supports the comparison of real weak tests with complex Fourier mode inner products.
TorusEuler.periodicComplexifyL2_apply_ae.summary: Complexified Hilbert fields agree pointwise almost everywhere

TorusEuler.periodicComplexifyL2_injectiv.text: The embedding of real spatial L² fields into complex spatial L² is injective. Its left inverse is the real-part map proved in the previous identity. Thus any equality obtained after complexification can be pulled back to real fields; the statement concerns L² equivalence classes, not arbitrary pointwise representatives.
TorusEuler.periodicComplexifyL2_injectiv.summary: Complexification distinguishes real square integrable fields

TorusEuler.periodicComplexifyL2_mem_sole.text: A real spatial L² field belongs to the weak gradient kernel exactly when its complexification belongs to the complex Fourier solenoidal subspace. One direction uses weak tests to constrain coefficients; the other uses projection and real parts. The equivalence connects two definitions without assuming a classical derivative for the field.
TorusEuler.periodicComplexifyL2_mem_sole.summary: Weak real solenoidality is Fourier transversality after embedding

TorusEuler.periodicComplexifyL2_mem_sole.text: If a real spatial $L^2$ field is weakly divergence free, in the sense of lying in the weak solenoidal subspace, its complexification belongs to the Fourier solenoidal subspace. Each longitudinal mode pairing reduces to a vanishing coefficient supplied by the preceding Fourier-test lemma. The theorem proves this direction of compatibility, not an equivalence by itself.
TorusEuler.periodicComplexifyL2_mem_sole.summary: Weak real divergence freedom implies Fourier solenoidality

TorusEuler.periodicComplexifyL2_realLera.text: Complexifying the real weak Leray projection of $v$ gives the complex Fourier Leray projection of the complexified $v$. The proof first compares real parts and then shows the imaginary part vanishes. This establishes the Fourier realization of the real projection on arbitrary spatial $L^2$ fields.
TorusEuler.periodicComplexifyL2_realLera.summary: Complexification commutes with the real Leray projection

TorusEuler.periodicComplexifyVector.text:
Coordinatewise complexification of the real Euclidean spatial vector.

The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.
TorusEuler.periodicComplexifyVector.summary: Embedding real vectors into complex Euclidean space

TorusEuler.periodicComplexifyVector_appl.text: The complex Euclidean embedding of a real vector has coordinate $i$ equal to the complex cast of its original real coordinate. This evaluation identity makes the representation concrete. It is used when comparing real divergence pairings with complex longitudinal inner products.

TorusEuler.periodicFarMultiplierJet.text: At target $x$ and source $y$, this operator takes the order $d$ derivative of the periodic kernel at $x-y$ and applies the chosen real output action. It is the derivative kernel used in far pressure integrals. The analytic derivative interpretation is guaranteed only when the difference avoids the integer lattice.
TorusEuler.periodicFarMultiplierJet.summary: A far kernel derivative acts on a source density

TorusEuler.periodicFarPressure.text: This real scalar field integrates the periodized pressure kernel against a complex tensor density over $S$ intersected with the half open fundamental cell $[0,1)^3$. Separation is not part of the raw definition. Later theorems prove that integrable sources separated from the target make this the actual smooth far pressure contribution.
TorusEuler.periodicFarPressure.summary: The actual pressure kernel is integrated over a separated source

TorusEuler.periodicHierarchyProfile.text: For an inverse-label map $A$, carrier vector $k$, profile $f(t,a,s)$ and phase-independent mean $\bar f(t,a)$, the physical field at time $t$ is $x\mapsto\bar f(t,A(t,x))+\bigl(f(t,c,k\cdot c)-\bar f(t,c)\bigr)$, where $c$ is the representative of $A(t,x)$ with every coordinate in $[-1/2,1/2)$. Thus the mean is composed directly with $A$ and only the oscillation $f-\bar f$ is extended periodically from the centered cell. The definition does not require $\bar f$ to be the phase average, nor any smoothness; later results add periodicity of the mean and agreement $f=\bar f$ near the cell faces.
TorusEuler.periodicHierarchyProfile.summary: The Eulerian field: transported mean plus the periodized oscillation

TorusEuler.periodicHierarchyProfile_hold.text: Fix $t$. Assume $A(t,\cdot)$ is smooth with a continuous two-sided inverse $X$, and $A(t,x+n)=A(t,x)+n$ for $n\in\mathbb Z^3$; the profile $(a,s)\mapsto f(t,a,s)$ and the mean $\bar f(t,\cdot)$ are smooth, and the mean is $\mathbb Z^3$-periodic; for some $0<\delta\le1/2$, $f(t,a,s)=\bar f(t,a)$ for all $s$ whenever some $|a_i|>1/2-\delta$; and $M\ge0$ bounds the operator norms of all derivatives of order at most $m+1$ of the transported profile $x\mapsto f(t,A(t,x),k\cdot A(t,x))$. Then the physical field $g(x)=\bar f(t,A(t,x))+(f-\bar f)(t,c,k\cdot c)$, with $c$ the centered representative of $A(t,x)$, is periodic, is $C^m$ with bounded derivatives and bounded half-Hölder quotients through order $m$, and its spatial $C^{m,1/2}$ norm is at most $3(m+1)M$.
TorusEuler.periodicHierarchyProfile_hold.summary: A jet bound through order $m+1$ gives the periodic $C^{m,1/2}$ estimate

TorusEuler.periodicHierarchyProfile_jetB.text: For a smooth inverse-label map with a continuous two-sided inverse and affine lattice equivariance, a smooth profile agreeing with a periodic mean in a positive cell-face collar has a smooth periodic physical extension. Any jet bound on the raw graph evaluation transfers with the same constant. Continuity extends the interior estimate to the closed cell faces.
TorusEuler.periodicHierarchyProfile_jetB.summary: Periodization preserves smoothness and the exact jet constant

TorusEuler.periodicImagPartVector.text: Take the imaginary part of every complex coordinate and repackage the result as a real Euclidean three-vector. The resulting map is real-linear and continuous. It supplies the imaginary projection of the concrete spatial complexification, complementing the previously defined real-part map.
TorusEuler.periodicImagPartVector.summary: Coordinatewise imaginary parts of complex velocities

TorusEuler.periodicImagPartVector_apply.text: The $i$th coordinate of the imaginary part of a complex vector $v$ equals $\operatorname{Im}v_i$. This definitional identity removes the Euclidean-space conversion maps from subsequent calculations. It allows reconstruction and norm splitting to be proved by the elementary real and imaginary coordinate identities for complex numbers.
TorusEuler.periodicImagPartVector_apply.summary: The imaginary projection acts coordinate by coordinate

TorusEuler.periodicL2Coefficient.text: The bounded Fourier coefficient map is defined as the Hilbert adjoint of inserting one mode. It maps a spatial $L^2$ field to its complex Euclidean coefficient. This operator definition is convenient for transferring self-adjoint projection identities; a later theorem identifies it with the usual integral coefficient.
TorusEuler.periodicL2Coefficient.summary: Fourier extraction as the adjoint of mode insertion

TorusEuler.periodicL2Coefficient_eq_mFou.text: The bounded adjoint-based coefficient map equals the standard integral Fourier coefficient of the chosen $L^2$ representative. The proof compares all coefficient inner products and commutes a bounded linear functional with the integrable Fourier expression. This establishes that the Hilbert construction uses the expected sign and normalization.
TorusEuler.periodicL2Coefficient_eq_mFou.summary: Adjoint coefficient extraction equals the Fourier integral

TorusEuler.periodicL2Coefficient_leray.text: For every spatial $L^2$ field and integer frequency, the Fourier coefficient after Leray projection is the Leray symbol applied to the original coefficient. Self-adjointness and the single-mode action prove the formula. No claim of pointwise convergence of a Fourier series is needed.
TorusEuler.periodicL2Coefficient_leray.summary: The all-field Leray operator acts coefficient by coefficient

TorusEuler.periodicL2Coefficient_realLer.text: At lattice frequency $k$, the Fourier coefficient of the complexified real projection equals the orthogonal projection of the original complexified coefficient onto the plane perpendicular to $k$. This is the explicit multiplier formula for the real weak operator. It includes the zero mode, whose projection is the identity rather than being removed.
TorusEuler.periodicL2Coefficient_realLer.summary: Every Fourier coefficient receives the Leray mode projection

TorusEuler.periodicL2Coefficient_sub_rea.text: For a real $L^2$ vector field $v$ on the unit torus and each $k\in\mathbb Z^3$, the formal theorem identifies the Fourier coefficient of $v-\mathbb Pv$ with the coefficient of $\nabla\Delta^{-1}\operatorname{div}v$. Using the basis $e^{2\pi i k\cdot x}$, the scalar coefficient is $-(2\pi i\,k\cdot\widehat v(k))/(4\pi^2|k|^2)$ for $k\ne0$, and is zero at $k=0$. Thus the removed vector coefficient is $k(k\cdot\widehat v(k))/|k|^2$. Constant velocity modes are retained. The statement is an equality of Fourier coefficients in $L^2$, not a pointwise identity of classically differentiable fields; smooth versions require the corresponding regularity.
TorusEuler.periodicL2Coefficient_sub_rea.summary: The Leray complement equals the gradient mode by mode

TorusEuler.periodicL2Mode.text: This bounded complex-linear map sends a coefficient vector to the spatial $L^2$ class of the corresponding Fourier character times that coefficient. It provides a genuine Hilbert-space mode rather than an unevaluated formal series. The following lemma identifies the represented field almost everywhere.
TorusEuler.periodicL2Mode.summary: Inserting one vector Fourier coefficient into L2

TorusEuler.periodicL2Mode_apply_ae.text: The $L^2$ mode insertion agrees almost everywhere with the torus character multiplied by its Euclidean coefficient. This statement gives the representative formula for a Hilbert-space element. It is used to compute inner products and to relate mode insertion to integral Fourier coefficients.
TorusEuler.periodicL2Mode_apply_ae.summary: A Hilbert mode represents its character times coefficient

TorusEuler.periodicLerayHolderLift.text:
The actual half-Hölder Leray projection, expressed as a map on periodic Euclidean lifts.

The underlying lift construction explicitly returns the zero function unless the input is both spatially periodic and of finite zeroth half-Hölder regularity. The paper applications establish those conditions before using the projection identities.
TorusEuler.periodicLerayHolderLift.summary: The periodic Leray projection on Euclidean lifts

TorusEuler.periodicLerayHolderLift_add.text: For two periodic order-zero half-Hölder fields, the lifted Leray projection of their sum equals the sum of their projections. The proof descends both fields and uses linearity of the actual torus operator. Both domain hypotheses matter because the total lifted definition returns zero on inadmissible inputs.
TorusEuler.periodicLerayHolderLift_add.summary: The Leray lift is additive on its stated domain

TorusEuler.periodicLerayHolderLift_add_c.text: The periodic Leray projection removes the Fourier-truncated pressure gradient.
TorusEuler.periodicLerayHolderLift_add_c.summary: The Leray projection removes the truncated pressure gradient

TorusEuler.periodicLerayHolderLift_eq_se.text: A smooth periodic vector field whose divergence vanishes is fixed by the concrete periodic Leray lift. Smooth periodicity first supplies a genuine half-Hölder torus representative. The divergence identity then places that representative in the solenoidal subspace, where the bounded projection acts as the identity.
TorusEuler.periodicLerayHolderLift_eq_se.summary: The projection fixes smooth solenoidal fields

TorusEuler.periodicLerayHolderLift_gradi.text: The actual Euclidean lift of the periodic Leray projection sends the gradient of a smooth periodic scalar potential to zero. The proof first establishes that this gradient is periodic and half-Hölder, then uses its orthogonality to the solenoidal subspace. The conclusion therefore follows inside the intended projection domain, rather than from the zero value the lift assigns to inadmissible inputs.
TorusEuler.periodicLerayHolderLift_gradi.summary: The lifted Leray projection removes smooth periodic gradients

TorusEuler.periodicLerayHolderLift_holde.text: The periodic Leray Hölder bound used in the estimate of (5.58).
TorusEuler.periodicLerayHolderLift_holde.summary: The order-one Hölder bound for the Leray projection

TorusEuler.periodicLerayHolderLift_pullb.text: On the lift of a torus half-Hölder field, the projection is its actual torus Leray projection.
TorusEuler.periodicLerayHolderLift_pullb.summary: The lifted projection agrees with the torus projection

TorusEuler.periodicLerayHolderLift_slice.text: The within time derivative of a jointly smooth periodic divergence-free velocity on a nondegenerate closed slab is fixed by the actual periodic Leray projection. The proof differentiates its pairing with gradients of test potentials. Smoothness and periodicity put the derivative in the valid half Hölder domain, including at both time endpoints.
TorusEuler.periodicLerayHolderLift_slice.summary: The time derivative of a solenoidal field is projected identically

TorusEuler.periodicPoissonPressure_uniqu.text: Let $p,q:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ be smooth and $\mathbb Z^3$-periodic. If $\Delta p=\Delta q$ pointwise and both integrals over the centered unit cell vanish, then $p=q$. The difference is a periodic harmonic function and hence constant, and its zero mean removes the additive constant. This is a spatial uniqueness theorem; it can be applied independently at each time. Proposition 5.11 uses it to identify the constructed pressure with the normalized solution of $\Delta p=-\operatorname{tr}((\nabla u)^2)$. The theorem applies to any common Poisson source and asserts no existence or time regularity.
TorusEuler.periodicPoissonPressure_uniqu.summary: Equal periodic Laplacians and zero means determine the same pressure

TorusEuler.periodicProjectedEuler_of_sta.text: On a positive closed prefix, smooth periodic approximants with uniformly converging values and every spatial jet, a uniformly vanishing residual, and the actual stage evolution yield the integrated projected equation, its within derivative, and joint smoothness of the limit. Smooth spatial slices of the limit are also assumed. This theorem does not yet introduce pressure.
TorusEuler.periodicProjectedEuler_of_sta.summary: Stage limits satisfy the actual projected evolution smoothly

TorusEuler.periodicProjectedMomentum.text: The bilinear expression is $-\mathbb P\operatorname{div}(u\otimes v)$ on the Euclidean lift, formed by differentiating the momentum tensor and applying the periodic Leray lift. The minus sign matches the evolution equation. This raw definition accepts arbitrary functions; agreement with an actual analytic projection requires its periodic Hölder domain.
TorusEuler.periodicProjectedMomentum.summary: The signed projected tensor divergence drives Euler evolution

TorusEuler.periodicProjectedMomentumJets.text: The bounded bilinear momentum map extends from genuine smooth tuples to their closure, mapping two order $m+2$ inputs to an order $m$ output. Density and completeness justify the extension. On embedded smooth velocities it returns the actual signed projected tensor divergence, as the following agreement theorem proves.
TorusEuler.periodicProjectedMomentumJets.summary: Momentum extends to completed compatible derivative data

TorusEuler.periodicProjectedMomentumJets.text: For smooth periodic inputs, each component of the extended momentum output equals the actual derivative of the signed projected tensor divergence. The index ranges through order $m$, while the two inputs are stored through $m+2$. This is the exact interpretation needed by the integrated jet bootstrap.
TorusEuler.periodicProjectedMomentumJets.summary: The extended map returns the actual momentum derivatives

TorusEuler.periodicRealLeray.text: Define the real spatial Leray operator as the orthogonal projection onto the closed subspace annihilating all smooth gradient tests. Its codomain is the ambient real L² space, so ordinary operator composition is available. The later theorems identify this weak definition with the familiar Fourier-symbol projection.
TorusEuler.periodicRealLeray.summary: The real orthogonal projection onto solenoidal fields

TorusEuler.periodicRealLeray_realPart_eq.text: Projecting the real part of a complex spatial L² field equals taking the real part after the complex Leray projection. The proof characterizes orthogonal projection by range membership and orthogonality of the discarded part. The real/complex inner-product identity supplies the orthogonality transfer.
TorusEuler.periodicRealLeray_realPart_eq.summary: Taking real parts commutes with the Leray projection

TorusEuler.periodicRealPartL2.text: Apply the coordinatewise real-part map to complex vector-valued spatial L² fields. The result is a real continuous linear map between the corresponding Haar L² spaces. It is defined on equivalence classes using the bounded pointwise map; its representative formula is established separately and holds almost everywhere.
TorusEuler.periodicRealPartL2.summary: Real parts of spatial square integrable fields

TorusEuler.periodicRealPartL2_apply_ae.text: The $L^2$ representative of the real-part map agrees almost everywhere with taking the coordinatewise real part of the input representative. This is the standard compatibility of composing an $L^2$ class with a bounded linear map. It allows later inner-product calculations to use ordinary pointwise complex algebra while preserving the quotient-space meaning of the operators.
TorusEuler.periodicRealPartL2_apply_ae.summary: Real parts agree almost everywhere with pointwise evaluation

TorusEuler.periodicRealPartL2_complexify.text: Complexify a real spatial L² field and then take its real part; the original L² field is recovered exactly. The equality is between equivalence classes and follows from almost-everywhere coordinate calculations. It supplies a left inverse for complexification, so no information is lost when passing to Fourier coefficients.
TorusEuler.periodicRealPartL2_complexify.summary: Taking real parts recovers an embedded real field

TorusEuler.periodicRealPartL2_leray_mem_.text: The real part of the complex Leray projection of any spatial L² field belongs to the weak real solenoidal subspace. It is first proved on Fourier modes, whose projected amplitudes are transverse, then extended by density through each continuous gradient-testing functional. No smoothness of the original L² field is assumed.
TorusEuler.periodicRealPartL2_leray_mem_.summary: Projected complex fields have solenoidal real parts

TorusEuler.periodicRealPartVector.text:
Coordinatewise real part on the complex Euclidean spatial vector.

The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.
TorusEuler.periodicRealPartVector.summary: Taking real parts of complex Euclidean vectors

TorusEuler.periodicRealPartVector_apply.text: The $i$th coordinate of the real part of a complex vector $v$ is the real part of the $i$th complex coordinate of $v$.
