The statement imposes no restriction on $t$ or $\rho$ and makes no assertion that the first and third coordinates are conserved.
TorusEuler.stationaryShearFlow_second.summary: Each shear trajectory keeps its second spatial coordinate

TorusEuler.stationaryShearFourierCoeff.text: This coefficient function is $1/(2i)$ times the complex shear direction at the positive second-coordinate unit frequency, its negative at the opposite frequency, and zero elsewhere. It is an explicitly finite spectral description. A later coefficient theorem proves that it is the Fourier transform of the actual shear.
TorusEuler.stationaryShearFourierCoeff.summary: The stationary shear has two opposite sine coefficients

TorusEuler.stationaryShearGradient.text: The formal definition is the linear map $B_\rho v=2\pi v_2(e_1+\rho e_3)$ on $\mathbb R^3$, for every real $\rho$. Equivalently, $B_\rho=2\pi(e_1+\rho e_3)\otimes e_2$, with $(a\otimes b)v=(b\cdot v)a$. This is the gradient at the origin of $U_0(x)=\sin(2\pi x_2)(e_1+\rho e_3)$, rather than its spatially constant gradient everywhere: at a general point the gradient is $\cos(2\pi x_2)B_\rho$. Coordinates follow the paper's ordering after shifting the formal indices by one. This definition alone states no bound on $\|B_\rho\|$.
TorusEuler.stationaryShearGradient.summary: Defines the constant gradient at the central particle

TorusEuler.stationaryShearGradient_adjoi.text: The adjoint shear matrix sends $ce_1$ to $2\pi c e_2$, independently of the third-direction shear parameter. The proof compares inner products against an arbitrary vector. This identity simplifies inverse-transpose transport of the first wave vector into a formula involving only the first two coordinate directions.
TorusEuler.stationaryShearGradient_adjoi.summary: The adjoint sends the first direction into the second

TorusEuler.stationaryShearGradient_apply.text: Applying the central stationary-shear gradient to $v$ gives $2\pi v_2(e_1+se_3)$. This is the explicit rank-one action of the matrix in the manuscript. The identity holds for arbitrary shear parameter and vector, and makes the first-wave amplitude equation an elementary component calculation.
TorusEuler.stationaryShearGradient_apply.summary: The shear matrix reads the second component

TorusEuler.stationaryShearGradient_coupl.text: For any real $\rho$, let $D_0=2\pi(e_1+\rho e_3)\otimes e_2$, the central gradient of the initial sine shear. The formal theorem proves $e_1\cdot D_0e_2=2\pi$ and $e_3\cdot D_0e_2=2\pi\rho$. Thus the coordinate-frame couplings in §1.1 are $\nu=2\pi$ and $\eta=2\pi\rho$, with ratio $\eta/\nu=\rho$. Positivity of $\eta$ follows only after requiring $\rho>0$; no smallness assumption is needed for these identities. The theorem states the two entries of the linear map. Its identification with the derivative of the actual periodic shear is a separate derivative identity.
TorusEuler.stationaryShearGradient_coupl.summary: The coordinate-frame entries are two pi and two pi times tilt

TorusEuler.stationaryShearGradient_origi.text: For $U_0(x)=\sin(2\pi x_2)(e_1+\rho e_3)$ and any real $\rho$, the formal theorem proves $D_xU_0(0)=2\pi(e_1+\rho e_3)\otimes e_2$. The derivative is a linear map on Euclidean three-space; on a vector $v$ it acts as $2\pi v_2(e_1+\rho e_3)$. This specifies the paper’s convention $(\nabla U_0)_{ij}=\partial_j(U_0)_i$ and identifies the actual periodic velocity with the linear background used at the center. Positivity or smallness of $\rho$ is unnecessary for this derivative identity, although used later to select the amplification regime.
TorusEuler.stationaryShearGradient_origi.summary: Differentiating the sine shear yields the initial linear map

TorusEuler.stationaryShearGradient_sq.text: For $B_\rho=2\pi(e_1+\rho e_3)\otimes e_2$, the formal statement proves $B_\rho\circ B_\rho=0$ as a linear map on $\mathbb R^3$, for every real $\rho$. The reason is the perpendicularity $e_2\cdot(e_1+\rho e_3)=0$. Consequently the candidate deformation maps $I+cB_\rho$ and $I-cB_\rho$ are inverse for every real scalar $c$. That consequence explains the inverse formula in (6.2), although this declaration itself concludes only the square-zero identity. No frequency, time or tilt bound is required.
TorusEuler.stationaryShearGradient_sq.summary: The rank-one central gradient has square zero

TorusEuler.stationaryShearMode.text: This integer frequency has value one in the second coordinate and zero in the other two. Together with its negative it supports the sinusoidal stationary parent. Naming this explicit frequency lets the formalization prove exact Fourier support and compare it with the initial truncation band.
TorusEuler.stationaryShearMode.summary: The unit frequency in the second coordinate

TorusEuler.stationaryShearTorus.text: Forms the real part of the two-mode complex Fourier representation of the stationary shear and packages it as a continuous torus map. The continuity proof uses finiteness of the Fourier sum. The next theorem identifies its Euclidean lift with the explicit sine shear used to begin the physical induction.
TorusEuler.stationaryShearTorus.summary: The stationary shear as a continuous torus field

TorusEuler.stationaryShearTorus_lift.text: Shows that evaluating the torus map at the quotient image of a Euclidean point gives the explicit stationary shear. This holds for every real parameter and spatial point. It transfers known differential and symmetry properties of the sine formula to the continuous torus representation required by stage records.
TorusEuler.stationaryShearTorus_lift.summary: The torus representation equals the explicit sine shear

TorusEuler.stationaryShear_advection.text: For $U_0(x)=\sin(2\pi x_2)(e_1+\rho e_3)$, the formal theorem proves $D U_0(x)[U_0(x)]=0$ for every real $\rho$ and every $x\in\mathbb R^3$. This is the paper's $(U_0\cdot\nabla)U_0=0$: the field depends only on its second coordinate and has zero component in that direction. The derivative is the full spatial linear map evaluated on the velocity. The result requires no parameter or time restriction. Choosing zero pressure then gives the stationary Euler equation, but the pressure and residual are not themselves part of this theorem's conclusion.
TorusEuler.stationaryShear_advection.summary: The stationary shear has zero nonlinear transport term

TorusEuler.stationaryShear_base_T1.text: Let $\lambda_0\ge1$ and let $\rho$ be any real number. The velocity $U_0(t,x)=\sin(2\pi x_2)(e_1+\rho e_3)$ is jointly smooth on $[0,1]\times\mathbb R^3$, periodic under integer translations, odd, and divergence free. Its Fourier coefficients vanish outside the band of radius $2\lambda_0^5$. These are the formal conclusions needed for (T1) at the base stage. Periodic fields are represented by functions on $\mathbb R^3$ descending to $\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3$. This statement gives support in the prescribed larger band, not the sharper claim that the only nonzero modes are exactly $\pm e_2$. No bound on $|\rho|$ is needed for these regularity properties.
TorusEuler.stationaryShear_base_T1.summary: The shear supplies the base regularity and Fourier support

TorusEuler.stationaryShear_base_T2.text: Assume $|s|\le1$ and $1+4\pi\le\lambda_0$ for the base frequency $\lambda_0$. The velocity and both actual flow Jacobians on $[0,1]$ are bounded by $\lambda_0$. The residual norm is at most the successor-frequency budget $\lambda_1^{-3}$ because it is exactly zero; no positivity assumption on $\lambda_1$ is needed for that last inequality.
TorusEuler.stationaryShear_base_T2.summary: The initial parent satisfies velocity deformation and residual budgets

TorusEuler.stationaryShear_base_T3.text: The derivative of the gradient of the zero pressure is the zero operator at every point. This supplies the index-zero Hessian condition, where the accumulated pressure budget is empty. The theorem concerns the explicit constant pressure and does not assert a corresponding fact for arbitrary stationary parents.

TorusEuler.stationaryShear_closed_residu.text: The sum of its within-interval time derivative, self-advection, and the gradient of zero pressure vanishes. The theorem is stated for every real evaluation time, since the velocity is time-independent and its self-advection is zero. It provides the residual identity also at the closed slab endpoints.
TorusEuler.stationaryShear_closed_residu.summary: The stationary parent has zero momentum residual on the slab

TorusEuler.stationaryShear_isLabelFlowOn.text: The transition from start time $r$ to time $t$ is the explicit shear flow evaluated at duration $t-r$. It satisfies the initial identity and within-set trajectory equation on any time set $J$. The underlying flow formula is globally defined, so this particular parent needs no local existence argument.
TorusEuler.stationaryShear_isLabelFlowOn.summary: The explicit shear gives a two time flow on any set

TorusEuler.stationaryShear_mFourierCoeff.text: The Fourier coefficient of the complex torus stationary parent at every integer frequency equals the explicitly defined coefficient function. Finite synthesis gives exact coefficient recovery, and the outside-band cases reduce to zero. This certifies the two-mode representation used for the initial truncation condition.
TorusEuler.stationaryShear_mFourierCoeff.summary: The parent Fourier coefficients are the prescribed pair

TorusEuler.stationaryShear_mFourierCoeff.text: For any real $\rho$, regard $U_0(x)=\sin(2\pi x_2)(e_1+\rho e_3)$ as a field on $\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3$ and allow its Fourier coefficients to have complex vector components. The formal statement proves that the coefficient at an integer frequency $k$ is nonzero if and only if $k=e_2$ or $k=-e_2$. Thus it establishes exact support, not merely containment in these modes. Neither coefficient can vanish because the first component of $e_1+\rho e_3$ is one. Complexifying the coefficients is the usual Fourier representation of a real field; it does not change the underlying velocity.
TorusEuler.stationaryShear_mFourierCoeff.summary: The Fourier support is exactly the second coordinate pair

TorusEuler.stationaryShear_normalized_pr.text: The constant zero pressure has zero centered-cell mean and its Laplacian equals minus the trace of the square of the stationary velocity gradient. The square vanishes everywhere by the preceding lemma. This verifies the normalized pressure equation for the actual parent rather than only asserting that zero is an admissible value.
TorusEuler.stationaryShear_normalized_pr.summary: Zero pressure satisfies the parent Poisson normalization

TorusEuler.stationaryShear_on_flow.text: Evaluating the stationary shear along its explicit trajectory gives the original shear at the starting label. The second coordinate remains fixed, and that is the only coordinate on which the velocity depends. The identity holds for all real times, enabling the simple affine-in-time flow formula.
TorusEuler.stationaryShear_on_flow.summary: The shear velocity stays constant along its trajectories

TorusEuler.stationaryShear_second.text: For $U_0(x)=\sin(2\pi x_2)(e_1+\rho e_3)$ and every real $\rho$, the formal theorem proves $(U_0(x))_2=0$ at every $x\in\mathbb R^3$. Its coordinate numbered one is the paper's second coordinate, since the formal indexing starts at zero. The field may depend on $x_2$ even though its second velocity component vanishes. This is the pointwise observation used to show that the nonlinear advection is zero and that the second coordinate is conserved along its flow; those conclusions require separate identities.
TorusEuler.stationaryShear_second.summary: The stationary shear has no velocity in the second direction

TorusEuler.strongLabelMomentum_of_integr.text: On $[0,T]$, $T>0$, suppose $F_t=MF$, $v_t$ exists, $\Omega v$ and $g$ are continuous, and $Kv-J(\Omega v)-Jg=c+P$, where $K=F^TF$ and $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$. If the pressure term has derivative $P_t=-Q$, then $Kv_t+Q=g-2F^TMFv$. This is the differentiation giving (4.11), including endpoint derivatives taken within the interval. The formal statement assumes the derivative relation for the pressure term; it does not prove time differentiability of an arbitrary scalar potential or construct its normalization. Here $Jw(t)=\int_0^tw(s)\,ds$.
TorusEuler.strongLabelMomentum_of_integr.summary: Obtain strong label momentum under a pressure derivative hypothesis

TorusEuler.sum_spatialDerivativeWord_sup.text: Let $g:\mathbb R^3\to E$ be smooth with every derivative of order at most $m$ bounded in operator norm by $M$. Then the sum over all ordered sequences $(i_1,\dots,i_m)\in\{1,2,3\}^m$ of $\sup_x|\partial_{i_1}\cdots\partial_{i_m}g(x)|$ is at most $3^mM$. The sum runs over ordered sequences, so each mixed derivative appears with its multiplicity, which dominates the multi-index sum.
TorusEuler.sum_spatialDerivativeWord_sup.summary: A Fréchet jet bound controls the sum over ordered coordinate derivatives

TorusEuler.sum_weighted_labelJets_le_of_.text: Suppose $v_j\le C_j A D^{pj}$ for $j\le n$, with nonnegative amplitude, radius and constants, and $\ell D^p\le1$. Then the weighted sum $\sum_{j\le n}\ell^j v_j$ is at most $A\sum_{j\le n}C_j$. The factor $(\ell D^p)^j$ pays for each successive derivative.
TorusEuler.sum_weighted_labelJets_le_of_.summary: Small radius absorbs the derivative powers

TorusEuler.summable_inv_one_add_latticeV.text: The sequence $(1+\|n\|)^{-p}$ over the three-dimensional integer lattice is summable for $p>3$. Away from the origin it is dominated by the reciprocal norm power from the preceding lemma. The added one keeps the expression finite and positive at the origin, without changing the summability threshold.
TorusEuler.summable_inv_one_add_latticeV.summary: A nonsingular lattice majorant is summable

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_clm_apply_.text: Suppose the operator fields $A_n$ and vector fields $v_n$ converge uniformly on a set $s$ to $B$ and $w$. Uniform nonnegative bounds $C$ and $M$ for the two limits ensure that their applications converge uniformly too. The bounds are explicit hypotheses; uniform convergence alone on an unbounded domain would not supply them.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_clm_apply_.summary: Uniformly converging factors give a uniformly converging product

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_cutoff_smu.text: For a compact cell $C$, a fixed smooth cutoff $\chi$ supported off the lattice, and fields $C^m$ there, convergence of their jets through order $m$ on $C\cap\operatorname{supp}\chi$ implies convergence of the cutoff-product jets on all of $C$. A finite Leibniz sum is bounded on the compact cell; outside the support both products vanish locally.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_cutoff_smu.summary: Local convergence on cutoff support becomes global cell convergence

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_dyadicPeri.text: On a compact punctured set, finite sums of periodic dyadic block derivatives converge uniformly to the corresponding derivative of the full kernel. Absolute summability over the product index justifies regrouping scales and lattice translates. This uniform derivative convergence is used when identifying the far integral with the bounded Fourier multiplier.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_dyadicPeri.summary: Finite dyadic sums converge with every derivative off the lattice

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_eulerAdvec.text: On a compact space-time set $K$, assume uniform convergence of the velocities and of their displayed spatial derivative fields $D_xu$, together with continuity of the limiting fields. Then the corresponding advection expressions converge uniformly. The theorem uses these derivative expressions as supplied; it does not derive differentiability or the derivative convergence from velocity convergence alone.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_eulerAdvec.summary: Pass to the limit in the advection expression

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_farKernelI.text: A common kernel norm bound over the observation set turns convergence to zero of the integral density error into uniform convergence of far-kernel outputs. Every density and the limit must be integrable, and each kernel action must be measurable. The result is uniform in the observation point because its bound does not depend on that point.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_farKernelI.summary: Integral source convergence gives uniform far-field convergence

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_farKernelI.text: Uniform convergence of continuous velocities on a compact source set gives uniform convergence of a bounded measurable far-kernel integral of their tensors. The limit velocity is continuous too, so all tensor densities are integrable. The kernel bound is uniform over the target, and the source measure is locally finite.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_farKernelI.summary: Continuous velocity limits control the far pressure field

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_farKernel_.text: For an open target region and compact source set, uniform convergence of continuous velocities passes to the actual derivatives of the far contribution through every prescribed finite order. The kernel jet tower must be measurable, uniformly bounded, and compatible under differentiation. The theorem also proves regularity of the limiting far field; the near pressure contribution is handled separately.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_farKernel_.summary: Global velocity convergence controls every separated pressure derivative

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_iteratedFD.text: On a compact set inside an open neighborhood, uniform convergence of both input jet towers through order $d$ gives convergence of the order $d$ derivative after a fixed bounded bilinear map. The approximants need only eventually be $C^d$ on the neighborhood. The proof preserves the order of the two arguments in the bilinear error decomposition.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_iteratedFD.summary: Local derivative convergence passes through bilinear products

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_iteratedFD.text: For a localized profile transported by an origin-fixing Lipschitz lattice-equivariant flow, assumes the set $S$ stays a common positive distance beyond the transported support radius. Then every fixed directional derivative of its cutoff converges uniformly to zero on $S$ as the cutoff scale grows. The continuous torus representative is supplied explicitly, and the conclusion concerns a fixed time and profile.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_iteratedFD.summary: Localized cutoff tails vanish beyond the transported support

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_iteratedFD.text: Uniform convergence of scalar derivatives of order $d+1$ implies uniform convergence of gradient derivatives of order $d$ on the same set. The identification of multilinear maps and the Riesz identification are continuous linear maps. The result is a representation statement and does not independently assume or prove smoothness of the scalar fields.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_iteratedFD.summary: One additional scalar derivative controls gradient convergence

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_iteratedFD.text: For a fixed bounded periodic field that vanishes in balls of a common radius around every point of $S$, each fixed directional derivative of its cutoff converges uniformly to zero on $S$ as the scale tends to infinity. The proof chooses moment order $m+1$, leaving a reciprocal-scale bound. No compactness of $S$ is required once the common gap is given.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_iteratedFD.summary: Cutoff derivatives vanish uniformly beyond a common support gap

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_iteratedFD.text: On a compact set off the lattice, uniform convergence of every velocity jet to those of a locally smooth limit implies uniform convergence of each quadratic tensor jet. Both approximants and limit are smooth off the lattice. Compactness bounds the limit jets, and the difference is split into two bilinear terms each containing a small velocity-jet error.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_iteratedFD.summary: Velocity jet convergence passes to the quadratic tensor

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_lift_farPr.text: Under the same continuous cutoff, separation and uniform velocity hypotheses, far pressure multipliers represented by half Hölder tensors converge in each gradient jet on the compact target. The torus representatives need match the cutoff tensors only eventually along the filter. Their limit is expressed by the actual kernel integral of the terminal tensor, without requiring a half Hölder representative of that limit.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_lift_farPr.summary: The far Fourier pressure inherits the kernel jet limit

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_periodicFa.text: For continuous velocities converging uniformly on a compact source set separated from the compact target, integration against the actual periodic kernel gives convergence of every prescribed far-field derivative on an open target neighborhood. The theorem also proves regularity of the limiting field. A bounded bilinear tensor map and output action are retained as explicit inputs.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_periodicFa.summary: The constructed periodic kernel carries velocity limits to far jets

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_periodicFa.text: Continuous velocities converging uniformly on a compact source set give uniform convergence of the actual far pressure gradient derivatives through order $m$ on an open neighborhood of a separated compact target. The scalar kernel theorem is applied at order $m+1$, then the gradient representation removes one stored scalar derivative.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_periodicFa.summary: Uniform velocity convergence gives all far pressure gradient limits

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_periodicPr.text: Uniform convergence of completed velocity tuples through order two, together with continuity of the limiting tuple, gives uniform time convergence of signed projected momentum at a fixed spatial point. The argument uses the bounded quadratic map and zeroth evaluation. The conclusion is pointwise in space, although the jet hypotheses use spatial uniform norms.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_periodicPr.summary: Two orders of jet convergence pass through projected momentum

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_periodicVe.text: Uniform convergence of actual derivatives through order $m$ for smooth periodic inputs gives uniform convergence of their completed compatible jet tuples. The proof applies the finite component comparison and the metric inherited by the subspace of compatible tuples. It does not require convergence of derivatives above the finite order being stored.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_periodicVe.summary: Actual derivative convergence passes to the completed jet norm

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_spatialHol.text: Uniform convergence of derivatives through order $m+1$ on the time set and the entire lift implies uniform convergence to zero of the order $m$ half Hölder norm of the difference. Smooth spatial slices are assumed for both approximants and limit. A finite simultaneous error estimate feeds the previous quantitative comparison.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_spatialHol.summary: Convergence of one extra derivative gives Hölder convergence

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_spatialJet.text: If every evaluated component of a finite bounded jet tuple converges uniformly over time and all spatial points, the tuples converge uniformly in their product norm. Finiteness allows the componentwise eventual estimates to hold simultaneously. The statement is a norm comparison and does not require the tuple entries to be compatible derivatives.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_spatialJet.summary: Uniform component convergence gives convergence of finite tuples

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_spatial_fd.text: Uniform convergence of the first iterated spatial derivatives implies uniform convergence of the ordinary Fréchet derivatives on the same time and space set. The proof applies the canonical isometry between one argument continuous multilinear maps and continuous linear maps. This changes only the representation of the derivative, with no added regularity hypothesis.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_spatial_fd.summary: The first multilinear jet gives derivative convergence

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_terminal_o.text: A jointly continuous field on $[0,T]\times K$, with $K$ compact and $T\ge0$, converges uniformly on $K$ to its value at $T$ along the preterminal filter. Compactness turns continuity into uniform continuity. At $T=0$ that filter has no preterminal points, so the conclusion is vacuous rather than an existence assertion.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_terminal_o.summary: A continuous closed slab has a uniform terminal trace

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformly_lift_smoothF.text: A smooth cutoff symbol $\psi$ supported in the radius-two ball and satisfying $\psi(0)=1$ gives uniform convergence of its cutoffs at scales $n+1$ to any continuous torus field lifted to Euclidean space. The proof uses its integrable Schwartz kernel and mass-one normalization. It does not assume absolute convergence of the original Fourier series.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformly_lift_smoothF.summary: Smooth spectral cutoffs converge uniformly on the periodic lift

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformly_of_spatially.text: If every approximating field and the limiting field are periodic, uniform convergence on the centered cell $[-1/2,1/2]^3$ implies uniform convergence on all of $\mathbb R^3$. Every point can be translated into that cell without changing any of the values being compared. The period hypothesis for the limit is required explicitly.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformly_of_spatially.summary: Convergence on one cell controls the entire periodic lift

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformly_pressureTens.text: Smooth periodic tensors whose every spatial jet converges uniformly on the centered cell to those of a smooth periodic limit have globally uniformly convergent pressure jets. For output order $d$, only input orders $d$ and $d+1$ determine the eventual error. Periodicity propagates their small cell errors globally, and pressure linearity allows estimating the difference.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformly_pressureTens.summary: Convergent tensor jets give globally convergent pressure jets

TorusEuler.tendsto_atTop_of_activationBo.text: If activation times converge to $T$ from below and a sequence of lower bounds tends to infinity, eventual uniform lower bounds throughout each half-open successive interval force $f(t)\to\infty$ as $t\uparrow T$. Monotonicity of the times is not assumed: the proof finds the first later crossing of each nearby time.
TorusEuler.tendsto_atTop_of_activationBo.summary: Bounds on successive intervals give a full terminal limit

TorusEuler.tendsto_halfHolder_torusTrans.text: As nonzero $h$ tends to zero, translation by the torus image of $hu$ converges to the original field in the value supremum norm. The half-Hölder increment estimate gives this directly. The theorem does not claim convergence in the complete half-Hölder norm, whose difference-quotient component need not vanish under translation.
TorusEuler.tendsto_halfHolder_torusTrans.summary: Small directional translations converge uniformly to the field

TorusEuler.tendsto_l1_tensor_of_uniform_.text: Uniform convergence on a compact set of finite measure, with continuous limit, makes the integral of the tensor difference norm tend to zero. The tensor map is bounded bilinear. The theorem does not itself assume measurable approximants; genuine integrability is supplied by continuity in its subsequent far-kernel application, avoiding reliance on the totalized integral.
TorusEuler.tendsto_l1_tensor_of_uniform_.summary: Uniform velocity convergence makes the tensor error integral vanish

TorusEuler.tendsto_nearPressure_of_bound.text: Given a bounded bilinear tensor map and bounded linear cutoff, divergence and Leray maps, convergence of velocities in the normed space $V$ implies convergence of the signed near nonlinearity in the normed space $E$. The maps are explicit inputs; the theorem does not establish their boundedness for a particular norm. It applies continuity of the diagonal tensor map followed by those linear maps.
TorusEuler.tendsto_nearPressure_of_bound.summary: Bounded nonlinear and linear maps preserve the near limit

TorusEuler.tendsto_operatorLiftConvoluti.text: At each Euclidean point, partial sums of the scaled-kernel lift convolutions tend to the value of the certified dyadic multiplier at the corresponding torus point. The proof evaluates convergence of the continuous-function series. Its conclusion is pointwise convergence of these partial sums, with uniform convergence available from the earlier summability result.
TorusEuler.tendsto_operatorLiftConvoluti.summary: Finite sums of lifted convolutions converge to the multiplier value

TorusEuler.tendsto_sup_norm_zero_of_tend.text: For an arbitrary filtered family, eventual boundedness of the full half-Hölder norm and convergence of its Haar $L^2$ norm to zero imply convergence of the value supremum norm to zero. Local averaging supplies the interpolation estimate. The conclusion deliberately concerns the supremum of values; it does not claim convergence of the Hölder seminorm itself.
TorusEuler.tendsto_sup_norm_zero_of_tend.summary: Uniform Hölder control upgrades L2 convergence to uniform convergence

TorusEuler.tendsto_torusDifference_coeff.text: Assume the difference quotients of $B$ are eventually bounded in half-Hölder norm by $\|B'\|$ and converge to $B'$ in supremum norm. Multiplying them by the translated fixed field $v$ then converges uniformly to $B'v$. This validates the coefficient-error limit without requiring the difference quotients to converge in full Hölder norm.
TorusEuler.tendsto_torusDifference_coeff.summary: The differentiated coefficient product converges uniformly

TorusEuler.tensorDivergenceMode.text: The tensor divergence at frequency $k$ is the vector whose component $i$ sums the derivative symbol in coordinate $j$ times tensor entry $(i,j)$. It is the single-divergence part of the pressure and Leray mode comparison. The formula is finite and keeps the two coordinate roles explicit.
TorusEuler.tensorDivergenceMode.summary: A Fourier derivative contracts one tensor index

TorusEuler.terminalBorelAtom.text: Defines the atom $\varepsilon^n b_n(t/\varepsilon)$ from the fixed cutoff monomial. For positive scale it retains the normalized polynomial near zero while shrinking support and controlling lower derivatives. The raw definition is total at every real scale; positivity is a hypothesis of the subsequent jet and scaling theorems.
TorusEuler.terminalBorelAtom.summary: Shrinking the support of a prescribed time jet

TorusEuler.terminalBorelAtom_eventuallyE.text: For $\varepsilon>0$, the rescaled atom and $t^n/n!$ agree eventually in the neighborhood filter of zero. Positivity ensures the rescaled argument remains inside the bump’s unit region near zero and permits cancellation of powers of the scale. The equality is local, not an identity on the whole time axis.
TorusEuler.terminalBorelAtom_eventuallyE.summary: The atom agrees with its polynomial near zero

TorusEuler.terminalBoundaryTimeJet.text: For a map $f$ on $\mathbb R\times E$, a set $s$, a time $T$ and an order $n$, this is the spatial function $y\mapsto D^nf(T,y)\big((1,0),\dots,(1,0)\big)$: the $n$-th derivative of $f$ within $s$ at $(T,y)$, applied $n$ times to the pure time direction. The definition assumes no regularity; where the derivative is not defined it is assigned the value zero.
TorusEuler.terminalBoundaryTimeJet.summary: The pure time derivatives on a terminal slice

TorusEuler.terminalCurl_tendsto_atTop_of.text: Assume $t_j\to T$, every $t_j<T$, lower bounds $b_j\to\infty$ and errors $e_j\to0$. For every sufficiently large $j$ and every $r\in[t_j,t_{j+1})$, suppose $|\operatorname{curl}U_j(r,0)|\ge b_j$ and $\|\nabla u(r,0)-\nabla U_j(r,0)\|\le e_j$. Then $|\operatorname{curl}u(r,0)|\to\infty$ as $r\uparrow T$ within $[0,T)$. The loss is at most $Ce_j$, where $C$ is the norm of the fixed matrix-to-curl map. Monotonicity of the activation sequence is not an explicit hypothesis. The bounds must hold throughout each sufficiently late interval, not merely at its endpoints. The result does not establish integral divergence or any Euler equation. At a spatial point without a derivative, the derivative expression is assigned zero; this convention does not assert differentiability.
TorusEuler.terminalCurl_tendsto_atTop_of.summary: Interval bounds pass to the limit when derivative errors vanish

TorusEuler.terminalCutoffStress.text: The stress is the tensor product of the two cutoff velocities minus the cutoff of their original tensor product: $Sg\otimes Sh-S(g\otimes h)$. It is unprojected and contains no divergence. This grouping makes time differentiation a bilinear Leibniz sum, whose terms can be estimated independently before applying divergence and the Leray projection.
TorusEuler.terminalCutoffStress.summary: The bilinear difference between cutoff tensor products

TorusEuler.terminalCutoffTailCost.text: This selects the order-$d$ uniform Hölder tail constant of the Schwartz kernel belonging to the fixed dyadic multiplier. It depends on the derivative depth $d$ and the chosen cutoff, not on a stage, a solution, or its frequency radius. Later scheduling estimates must dominate this cost; the definition itself contains no such domination.

TorusEuler.terminalCutoffTailCost_nonneg.text: Every natural cutoff depth has a nonnegative dyadic tail cost. Unfolding the fixed-kernel absolute-moment formula proves the sign. This permits multiplication of a depth-norm bound by the tail cost when estimating the true child-minus-parent increment. It does not claim the cost is small or uniformly bounded as depth increases.
TorusEuler.terminalCutoffTailCost_nonneg.summary: The chosen dyadic tail cost is nonnegative

TorusEuler.terminalCutoffVector.text: This field evaluates the real vector Fourier cutoff $S_\Lambda g$ at the image of $x$ in the unit torus. It is the spatial operator used on each time derivative of an approximate velocity or residual. The definition allows an arbitrary multiplier $\psi$ and radius $\Lambda$; it alone does not say the operation approximates the identity or preserves a particular frequency band.
TorusEuler.terminalCutoffVector.summary: Lift the vector Fourier cutoff to Euclidean space

TorusEuler.terminalCutoffVector_holder.text: For a smooth multiplier equal to one on the unit ball and zero beyond radius two, a positive cutoff radius, and a $C^{m,1/2}$ lift of a torus field, the cutoff remains $C^{m,1/2}$. Its norm is bounded by one plus the order-$m$ tail constant times the input norm. The argument adds the controlled cutoff difference back to the original field.
TorusEuler.terminalCutoffVector_holder.summary: The Fourier cutoff preserves the spatial Hölder estimate

TorusEuler.terminalFlowTimeAmplitude.text: Defines a common amplitude using $g=AD(1+DA)^q$ and $c=Dg^q$, then taking $g+c+Dc$. These terms accommodate the material gradient, the deformation matrices, and the normalized transported covector. The expression depends on the fixed time order and parent scale and amplitude, while the spatial order is left to a separate constant.
TorusEuler.terminalFlowTimeAmplitude.summary: A common polynomial amplitude for the flow coefficients

TorusEuler.terminalGraphCostEnvelope.text: For a cost table, a row, and orders $s,m,d$, this is the number $\sum_{q=0}^{s}\sum_{A=0}^{s}|\mathrm{cost}(\mathrm{row},q,A,m,d)|$, summing over every time order and every parent velocity exponent up to $s$. It depends only on the table.
TorusEuler.terminalGraphCostEnvelope.summary: One finite envelope includes the parent time exponent

TorusEuler.terminalGraphReadoutCost.text: This scalar collects the finite dimension factor $3(N+1)+6$, the repeated advection factor $(1+2^{N+q}C)^q$ with parent cost $C$, the parent cost, and all four profile conversion costs. It includes $q!$ for extracting time derivatives and $e^3$ for the switch envelope. Keeping their complete product in one threshold entry is what allows a single remaining parent-frequency power after absorption.
TorusEuler.terminalGraphReadoutCost.summary: The full fixed-order scalar in the graph estimate

TorusEuler.terminalGraphReadoutPower.text: With parent power $B$ and profile power $E$, the remaining natural-number exponent is $1+Bq+\max(B,q+E)$. The first one pays for the whole fixed scalar cost, the product $Bq$ accounts for repeated advection, and the maximum covers the parent and extracted profile amplitudes. Neither the spatial reserve nor the hierarchy depth appears among its arguments.
TorusEuler.terminalGraphReadoutPower.summary: The parent exponent left after graph-cost absorption

TorusEuler.terminalGraphReadoutScalars_l.text: Assume $\mu\ge1$, a positive slab length $T$ with $T^{-1}\le\mu$, child frequency $\lambda\ge1$, nonnegative profile coefficients, and the full graph cost at most $\mu$. For $i\le q$, $m\le N$, depth $6K$ and next frequency $\lambda^K$, the theorem bounds the mean, velocity, and residual scalar factors by one parent power. The mean retains $\lambda^{-5/2}$ and the residual retains $(\lambda^K)^{-4}$.
TorusEuler.terminalGraphReadoutScalars_l.summary: Absorb all graph scalars into one parent power

TorusEuler.terminalIteratedDerivWithin_c.text: Let $s\subset\mathbb R$ be a set on which derivatives within $s$ are unique, $A$ a bounded linear map between normed spaces and $f$ a smooth curve on $s$. Then for every $n$ and every $t\in s$, the $n$th derivative within $s$ of $t\mapsto A(f(t))$ equals $A$ applied to the $n$th derivative of $f$ within $s$. Nothing is asserted at points outside $s$.
TorusEuler.terminalIteratedDerivWithin_c.summary: A fixed bounded linear map commutes with time derivatives

TorusEuler.terminalIteratedDerivWithin_c.text: On a set $s\subset\mathbb R$ with unique derivatives, let $C(t)$ be a smooth operator curve (bounded linear maps) and $u(t)$ a smooth vector curve on a path in $s$. Then for every $n$ and every $t\in s$, the $n$th derivative within $s$ of the operator applied to the path, $t\mapsto C(t)u(t)$, is the binomial sum $\sum_{i=0}^n\binom niC^{(i)}(t)u^{(n-i)}(t)$, with all derivatives taken within $s$. Both factors must be smooth on $s$.
TorusEuler.terminalIteratedDerivWithin_c.summary: The Leibniz rule for an operator curve applied to a vector curve

TorusEuler.terminalLabelTimeSeminormCost.text: For constants $C(j)$ and orders $q,n$, this is the number $(q+1)\,W_n\sum_{j=0}^nC(j)$, where $W_n$ is the number of multi-indices $(\alpha,j)$ in the three label directions and the phase with $|\alpha|+j\le n$. It is the constant used when mixed derivative bounds are transferred to the factorially weighted time norm.
TorusEuler.terminalLabelTimeSeminormCost.summary: Finite constants for the coefficient time norm

TorusEuler.terminalLabelTimeSeminormCost.text: If $C(j)\ge0$ for every $j$, then for all orders $q,n$ the constant $(q+1)\,W_n\sum_{j=0}^nC(j)$ is nonnegative, where $W_n$ is the number of multi-indices $(\alpha,j)$ in the three label directions and the phase with $|\alpha|+j\le n$.
TorusEuler.terminalLabelTimeSeminormCost.summary: The coefficient time norm constant is nonnegative

TorusEuler.terminalLinearODECost.text: For a continuous bilinear map $B$ and constant sequences $C,C_0$, these are the constants $M_q(n)$ defined by $M_0=C_0$ and $M_{q+1}(n)=M_q(n)+2^q\|B\|\sum_{j=0}^n\binom nj C(j)\,M_q(n-j)$. They depend only on the orders, $B$ and the given constants, not on any particular solution.
TorusEuler.terminalLinearODECost.summary: Constants for repeated time differentiation of a linear equation

TorusEuler.terminalLinearODECost_nonneg.text: If both input spatial constant functions are nonnegative, every recursively defined linear-equation constant is nonnegative at every time and spatial order. The proof follows the recursion and the nonnegativity of the bilinear product cost. It does not require a differential equation, a solution, or a frequency parameter.

TorusEuler.terminalLogScale_tendsto_atTo.text: If a real frequency sequence tends to positive infinity, the shifted gain $4\log(\mathrm{freq}(j+1))$ also tends to positive infinity. There is no requirement that all earlier frequencies be positive; divergence gives eventual positivity. The index shift is retained explicitly because the induction reads gains from later frequencies.
TorusEuler.terminalLogScale_tendsto_atTo.summary: Diverging frequencies give diverging logarithmic gains

TorusEuler.terminalMaterialIterate.text: Applies the same material derivative operator $f\mapsto\partial_tf+D_xf\,[U]$, with time derivative within $[a,b]$, exactly $q$ times to $f$. The parent velocity $U$ remains fixed as a function throughout this iteration. At order zero the result is $f$. Regularity and agreement with derivatives along trajectories are separate theorems.
TorusEuler.terminalMaterialIterate.summary: Repeated material derivatives on a closed time slab

TorusEuler.terminalMaterialIterate_succ.text: For any interval, velocity $U$, order $q$ and field $f$, the material iterate of order $q+1$ equals one material derivative $g\mapsto\partial_tg+D_xg\,[U]$ applied to the iterate of order $q$. This is an identity of function iteration and asserts no differentiability.
TorusEuler.terminalMaterialIterate_succ.summary: The next material derivative repeats the same operator

TorusEuler.terminalMaterialIterate_zero.text: The zeroth iterate of material differentiation is exactly the original field, as an equality of functions. There are no interval or regularity assumptions: this follows from zero iterations of an operator. It supplies the base case for the later smoothness induction and for the identity between material derivatives and trajectory derivatives.
TorusEuler.terminalMaterialIterate_zero.summary: Zero material derivatives leave the field unchanged

TorusEuler.terminalMaterialStep.text: For a velocity $U$ and a field $f(t,x)$, this defines $D_tf(t,x)=\partial_tf(t,x)+D_xf(t,x)\,U(t,x)$, where the time derivative is taken within $[a,b]$ with the point $x$ held fixed and $D_xf(t,x)$ is the spatial derivative of $f(t,\cdot)$ at $x$. The definition assumes neither smoothness nor $a<b$; derivative expressions take their assigned default value zero where the derivative does not exist.
TorusEuler.terminalMaterialStep.summary: Material derivative on a closed time interval

TorusEuler.terminalMeanGainPolynomial_le.text: Let $\mathsf D\ge1$ and $A,B,G,Z\ge0$, and let $A_0,B_0,G_0,C_0\ge0$ satisfy $A\le A_0\mathsf D^p$, $B\le B_0\mathsf D^a$, $G\le G_0\mathsf D^{a+e}Z$ and $C\le C_0\mathsf D^a$, with nonnegative integers $p,a,e,q$. Then $C(1+A(1+B))^{q+1}G\le C_0(1+A_0(1+B_0))^{q+1}G_0\cdot\mathsf D^{(p+a)(q+1)+2a+e}Z$. No sign condition is placed on $C$ beyond its upper bound.
TorusEuler.terminalMeanGainPolynomial_le.summary: A triangular mean estimate stays polynomial in the parent scale

TorusEuler.terminalMeanProductWords_time.text: Let $T>0$ and let $K_w$ (half-Hölder matrix coefficients) and $f_w,g_w$ (half-Hölder vector fields) be smooth word families on $[0,T]$ for word lengths $|w|\le N$, with exact strong spatial derivative relations: $K_{jw},f_{jw},g_{jw}$ are the derivatives in direction $u_j$ of $K_w,f_w,g_w$ for $|w|<N$. Suppose the base field is the product, $g_\varnothing=K_\varnothing f_\varnothing$ on $[0,T]$. Let the scaling $\ell$ and caps $A,B$ be nonnegative, with scaled time derivatives $\ell^{|w|}\|\partial_t^iK_w(t)\|\le A$ and $\ell^{|w|}\|\partial_t^if_w(t)\|\le B$ through time order $i\le q$ and word lengths $|w|\le N$. Then the corresponding words of $g$ obey $\ell^{|w|}\|\partial_t^ig_w(t)\|\le2^{N+1+q}AB$ for the same $i,w$ and $t\in[0,T]$; no extra spatial order is consumed.
TorusEuler.terminalMeanProductWords_time.summary: Time derivatives of product words keep the spatial order

TorusEuler.terminalMeanSpatialInverse_cl.text: Assumes the projected equation, coercivity, derivative families and inverse cap uniformly on $[0,T]$, with $T\ge0$. Continuous coefficient and source curves make their closed-time suprema valid pointwise bounds. For positive radius, their weighted norm hypotheses yield the same one-inverse-factor bound for the velocity's closed-time norm. No continuity assumption on the supplied velocity words is needed for this final supremum estimate.
TorusEuler.terminalMeanSpatialInverse_cl.summary: The mean inverse estimate is uniform on the closed slab

TorusEuler.terminalMeanSpatialInverse_ra.text: If the weighted coefficient is bounded by $H D^b\sqrt\ell$ and $A_{\rm inv}D^b\sqrt\ell\le1$, proves its projected contribution costs at most $2\|P\|H$ after multiplication by the inverse cap. The only sign hypotheses are $A_{\rm inv},H\ge0$. Although intended for positive-order coefficient words, this arithmetic theorem does not assume that the natural order is positive or that $\ell>0$.
TorusEuler.terminalMeanSpatialInverse_ra.summary: A radius threshold absorbs the coefficient inverse loss

TorusEuler.terminalMeanSpatialInverse_wo.text: Under the fixed-time inverse and derivative hypotheses, assumes all weighted source words through order $N$ are bounded by $B$ and every positive-order coefficient word, including its inverse factor, costs at most $C$. For $\ell\ge0$, the velocity word bound is $A_{\rm inv}\|P\|B(1+2^NC)^{|q|}$. Only one leading inverse factor remains, because the smaller-radius coefficient hypothesis has absorbed the others.
TorusEuler.terminalMeanSpatialInverse_wo.summary: The spatial hierarchy keeps one leading inverse factor

TorusEuler.terminalMeanSpatialInverse_wo.text: Given a coercive kinetic coefficient, a supplied continuous linear inverse equivalence with norm cap, the projected base equation and genuine coefficient, source and velocity derivative families through order $N$, bounds every velocity word by its source plus lower velocity words multiplied by positive-order coefficient words. The ordered product rule retains its multiplicities. The theorem uses the supplied inverse; it does not construct an inverse from coercivity alone.
TorusEuler.terminalMeanSpatialInverse_wo.summary: Each mean derivative obeys a triangular inverse estimate

TorusEuler.terminalMeanTimeBound.text: This is a scalar induction for a triangular recurrence. Let $V(i,C)$ be any bound predicate in a time order $i$ and a real $C$, monotone in $C$ (if $C\le C'$ then $V(i,C)$ implies $V(i,C')$), and let $A,B,G\ge0$. If order zero holds at $AG$, that is $V(0,AG)$, and for each $n<q$ and $C\ge0$ the bounds $V(j,C)$ for all lower orders $j\le n$ give the next order $V(n+1,A(G+BC))$, then the geometric bound $V(i,(1+A(1+B))^{i+1}G)$ holds for every order $i\le q$.
TorusEuler.terminalMeanTimeBound.summary: A triangular recurrence gives a geometric bound

TorusEuler.terminalMeanWordProduct.text: Defines the complete word product as the undifferentiated coefficient acting on the velocity word, plus every ordered product-rule term with positive coefficient order. Keeping the correction list preserves multiplicities of repeated derivative choices. For arbitrary coefficient and velocity families this is just an algebraic field; genuine derivative interpretation requires the subsequent coherence hypotheses.
TorusEuler.terminalMeanWordProduct.summary: The full ordered product includes the undifferentiated coefficient

TorusEuler.terminalMeanWordProduct_close.text: For $T\ge0$ and positive radius, continuous coefficient and velocity word curves with uniform weighted closed-time bounds $K,V$ give the same product bound $2^{|w|+1}KV$ in the closed-time norm. Continuity supplies bounded source suprema, and the nonempty interval lets the pointwise estimate pass to its supremum. Positive radius is used when dividing by its target-order power.
TorusEuler.terminalMeanWordProduct_close.summary: The weighted product bound holds uniformly in time

TorusEuler.terminalMeanWordProduct_nil.text: At the empty derivative word, the full product reduces to the undifferentiated coefficient multiplying the undifferentiated velocity. The positive-coefficient correction list is empty, so its sum is zero. This establishes the base value for identifying the recursively generated products with genuine spatial derivatives.
TorusEuler.terminalMeanWordProduct_nil.summary: The empty word is the original coefficient product

TorusEuler.terminalMeanWordProduct_norm_.text: For nonnegative radius and bounds $K,V$ on all weighted coefficient and velocity words through the target length, proves the weighted product norm is at most $2^{|w|+1}KV$. One factor of two comes from half-Hölder multiplication, while $2^{|w|}$ counts all binary placements of derivative letters. The bound is algebraic and does not require the families to be actual derivatives.
TorusEuler.terminalMeanWordProduct_norm_.summary: Every binary derivative choice contributes to the product bound

TorusEuler.terminalMeanWordProduct_spati.text: If the coefficient and velocity word families have the prescribed torus derivatives through order $N$, differentiating the product at a word of length below $N$ gives the product at the word with that direction prepended. The proof differentiates the coefficient action and every correction term, preserving the original ordered multiplicities. No commutation or deduplication of derivative words is assumed.
TorusEuler.terminalMeanWordProduct_spati.summary: The ordered products are genuine spatial derivatives

TorusEuler.terminalMeanWords_timeJet_bou.text: Let $T>0$ and let $K_w,\Omega_w$ (matrix), $g_w$ (vector) and $v_w$ (divergence-free) be half-Hölder word families, smooth on $[0,T]$ for $|w|\le N$, each closed under directional derivatives $u_j$ for $|w|<N$. Assume for $n<q$ and $t\in[0,T]$ the differentiated projected equation $\mathbb P(K\partial_t^{n+1}v)=\mathbb P\big(\sum_i\binom ni\partial_t^i\Omega\,\partial_t^{n-i}v+\partial_t^ng-\sum_i\binom{n+1}{i+1}\partial_t^{i+1}K\,\partial_t^{n-i}v\big)$ for the base words. Assume $e(t)z=\mathbb P(K(t)z)$ with $\|e(t)^{-1}\|\le A_{\rm inv}$; $\langle K(t,a)z,z\rangle\ge\mu|z|^2$, $\mu>0$; $\ell,K_{\rm cost},C_{\rm coef},G,A_0\ge0$; $A_{\rm inv}\ell^{|w|}2\|\mathbb P\|\|K_w(t)\|\le K_{\rm cost}$ for $1\le|w|\le N$; $\ell^{|w|}\|\partial_t^iK_w\|,\ell^{|w|}\|\partial_t^i\Omega_w\|\le C_{\rm coef}$ for $i\le q$; $\ell^{|w|}\|\partial_t^ig_w\|\le G$ for $i<q$; and $\ell^{|w|}\|v_w\|\le A_0G$. With $A=\max(A_0,A_{\rm inv}\|\mathbb P\|(1+2^NK_{\rm cost})^N)$ and $B=2^{N+1}(2^q+2^q)C_{\rm coef}$, one has $\ell^{|w|}\|\partial_t^iv_w(t)\|\le(1+A(1+B))^{i+1}G$ for all $i\le q$, $|w|\le N$, $t\in[0,T]$.
TorusEuler.terminalMeanWords_timeJet_bou.summary: Higher time derivatives of the mean velocity cost no further spatial order

TorusEuler.terminalMixedJetBound_inv_nor.text: Say $g$ satisfies a mixed bound of time order $q$, slope $p$, scale $\mathsf D$, amplitude $A$ and costs $C_n$ on $[a,b]$ if $\|D^n_x\partial_t^ig(t,x)\|\le C_nA\,\mathsf D^{pn}$ for all $i\le q$, all $n$, $t\in[a,b]$ and $x$. Let $a<b$, $\mathsf D,A,B\ge0$, $C_n,C^0_n\ge0$, and let the covector $\kappa(t,x)$ be jointly smooth on $[a,b]\times\mathbb R^3$ and nowhere zero, with a mixed bound of order $q$ (amplitude $A$, costs $C$), while the reciprocal squared length $|\kappa|^{-2}$ has a mixed bound of order $0$ (amplitude $B$, costs $C^0$). Then $|\kappa|^{-2}$ has a mixed bound of order $q$ and slope $p$ with amplitude $W_q$, where $W_0=B$ and $W_{j+1}=W_j+A^2W_j^2$, and costs given by the reciprocal cost recursion started from $C^0$ with input costs $2^q\|\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle\|\sum_{j\le n}\binom njC_jC_{n-j}$; here $\|\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle\|$ is the norm of the inner product as a bilinear map, which is at most one.
TorusEuler.terminalMixedJetBound_inv_nor.summary: Time and space derivatives of the reciprocal squared length of a covector

TorusEuler.terminalMixedJetBound_of_line.text: Let $B$ be a fixed continuous bilinear map and $f,g$ smooth fields on $[a,b]\times\mathbb R^3$, $a<b$, satisfying the linear equation $\partial_tg=B(f,g)$ on the slab. Combine a zeroth-time mixed bound for $g$ (slope $p$, amplitude $A_0\ge0$, constants $C_0(n)\ge0$) with a coefficient mixed bound for $f$ through order $q$ (amplitude $A\ge1$, constants $C(n)\ge0$), with $\mathsf D\ge0$. Then $g$ obeys the mixed bound through order $q$ with amplitude $A_0A^q$ and the recursive constants $M_0=C_0$, $M_{q+1}(n)=M_q(n)+2^q\|B\|\sum_{j=0}^n\binom njC(j)M_q(n-j)$. This uses the differentiated equation and the existing solution; it is not an existence theorem.
TorusEuler.terminalMixedJetBound_of_line.summary: Differentiating a linear equation using lower time orders

TorusEuler.terminalMixedJetBound_of_reci.text: With mixed bounds as in the preceding statement, let $a<b$, $\mathsf D,A,B\ge0$, $C_n,C^0_n\ge0$, and let $f(t,x)$ be real, jointly smooth on $[a,b]\times\mathbb R^3$ and nowhere zero, with $1/f$ satisfying a mixed bound of time order $0$, slope $p$, amplitude $B$ and costs $C^0$. If $f$ satisfies a mixed bound of order $q$, slope $p$, amplitude $A$ and costs $C$, then $1/f$ satisfies a mixed bound of order $q$ and slope $p$ with amplitude $W_q$ and costs $M_q$, where $W_0=B$, $W_{j+1}=W_j+AW_j^2$, $M_0=C^0$, $M_{j+1}(n)=M_j(n)+2^j\|{-m}\|\sum_{l\le n}\binom nlC_l\,S_j(n-l)$ and $S_j(n)=2^j\|m\|\sum_{l\le n}\binom nlM_j(l)M_j(n-l)$, with $m$ real multiplication as a bilinear map (norm one).
TorusEuler.terminalMixedJetBound_of_reci.summary: Reciprocal time derivatives keep the same spatial slope

TorusEuler.terminalMixedProductCost.text: For a time order $q$, a continuous bilinear map $B$, constant sequences $C,C'$ and a spatial order $n$, this is the number $2^q\|B\|\sum_{j=0}^n\binom njC(j)C'(n-j)$. The factor $2^q$ bounds the sum of the time binomial coefficients through order $q$; amplitudes and powers of $\mathsf D$ enter separately.
TorusEuler.terminalMixedProductCost.summary: Constants for the mixed derivative product rule

TorusEuler.terminalMixedProductCost_nonn.text: If $C(n)\ge0$ and $C'(n)\ge0$ for all $n$, then for every time order $q$, continuous bilinear map $B$ and spatial order $n$, the constant $2^q\|B\|\sum_{j=0}^n\binom njC(j)C'(n-j)$ is nonnegative.
TorusEuler.terminalMixedProductCost_nonn.summary: The mixed product constant is nonnegative

TorusEuler.terminalProjectedHigherTimeDe.text: Let $P:Y\to X$ be bounded linear, with $X$ real normed and $Y$ real Banach. For smooth operator curves $K,\Omega:X\to Y$ and smooth curves $v,g$ on $[0,T]$, $T>0$, assume $P(Kv)=c+P\int_0^t(\Omega v+g)$. The formal statement isolates $P(Kv^{(n+1)})$ as $P[\sum_{i=0}^n\binom ni\Omega^{(i)}v^{(n-i)}+g^{(n)}-\sum_{i=0}^n\binom{n+1}{i+1}K^{(i+1)}v^{(n-i)}]$. Derivatives are taken within the closed interval. Only source derivatives through order $n$ occur. To obtain the auxiliary note's formula one must identify $P$ with the Leray projection and use $\Omega=K_t-\mathcal D$, then regroup the sums. These geometric identifications are not assumptions of this general identity.
TorusEuler.terminalProjectedHigherTimeDe.summary: The highest velocity derivative remains under the projection

TorusEuler.terminalProjectedTimeDerivati.text: Let $T>0$, $P$ a bounded linear map, $c$ a constant, $K(t)$ smooth and $\Omega(t)$ continuous on $[0,T]$, $v$ smooth and the source $g$ continuous on $[0,T]$. Assume the integrated mean equation $P(K(t)v(t))=c+P\int_0^t\Omega(r)v(r)\,dr+P\int_0^tg(r)\,dr$ for all $t\in[0,T]$. Differentiating within $[0,T]$ gives $P\,\partial_t(Kv)(t)=P(\Omega(t)v(t)+g(t))$ at every $t\in[0,T]$. The source is needed only continuously, and the constant initial trace $c$ disappears under differentiation.
TorusEuler.terminalProjectedTimeDerivati.summary: Differentiating the integrated projected mean equation

TorusEuler.terminalRealAdjoint.text: Packages the real adjoint operation on linear maps of $\mathbb R^3$ as a continuous linear map. This permits the mixed-derivative bound machinery to treat transposition as a fixed linear operation with its operator norm as a cost. The real scalar field matters: over complex scalars, taking adjoints is conjugate linear.
TorusEuler.terminalRealAdjoint.summary: Take adjoints as a bounded linear operation

TorusEuler.terminalReciprocalTimeAmplitu.text: For real numbers $A,B$, this defines the amplitude for reciprocal time derivatives: starting from $W_0=B$, the amplitude at the next time order is $W_{q+1}=W_q+A\,W_q^2$, where $W_q$ is the previous amplitude. It mirrors the reciprocal identity $\partial_t(1/f)=-\partial_tf\,(1/f)^2$ and is a scalar sequence only.
TorusEuler.terminalReciprocalTimeAmplitu.summary: Amplitudes for the time derivatives of a reciprocal

TorusEuler.terminalReciprocalTimeAmplitu.text: If $A\ge0$ and $B\ge0$, then every term of the sequence $W_0=B$, $W_{q+1}=W_q+AW_q^2$ is nonnegative.
TorusEuler.terminalReciprocalTimeAmplitu.summary: Nonnegative inputs give nonnegative reciprocal amplitudes

TorusEuler.terminalReciprocalTimeCost.text: For cost sequences $C_n$ and $C^0_n$, this defines costs $M_q(n)$ by $M_0=C^0$ and $M_{q+1}(n)=M_q(n)+2^q\|{-m}\|\sum_{l\le n}\binom nlC_l\,S_q(n-l)$, where $S_q(n)=2^q\|m\|\sum_{l\le n}\binom nlM_q(l)M_q(n-l)$ and $m$ is real multiplication viewed as a bilinear map, of norm one.
TorusEuler.terminalReciprocalTimeCost.summary: Spatial costs for successive time derivatives of a reciprocal

TorusEuler.terminalReciprocalTimeCost_no.text: When both input spatial cost arrays are nonnegative, the reciprocal cost is nonnegative for every time and spatial order. The proof follows the recursive construction and uses nonnegativity of the mixed bilinear product cost. It is a property of the cost arrays alone and does not construct reciprocal estimates.
TorusEuler.terminalReciprocalTimeCost_no.summary: Nonnegative reciprocal costs remain nonnegative at every order

TorusEuler.terminalSpatialDerivative_ite.text: For two half Hölder curves that are $C^n$ on $[0,T]$, the supplied strong spatial derivative relation survives all within-time derivatives of order $m\le n$. The strict positivity of $T$ handles uniqueness at the endpoints. This theorem assumes the spatial relation and the time regularity of both curves; it does not infer them from pointwise bounds.
TorusEuler.terminalSpatialDerivative_ite.summary: Every available time derivative preserves the spatial relation

TorusEuler.terminalSpatialDerivative_of_.text: Let $T>0$, $t\in[0,T]$ and $u\in\mathbb R^3$, and let $f(r),df(r)$ be curves of half-Hölder torus fields such that, for every $r\in[0,T]$, $df(r)$ is the derivative of $f(r)$ in direction $u$ along every line $s\mapsto a+[su]$. If $f$ has derivative $f_t$ and $df$ has derivative $df_t$ at $t$ within $[0,T]$, in the half-Hölder norm, then $df_t$ is the derivative of $f_t$ in direction $u$ in the same sense.
TorusEuler.terminalSpatialDerivative_of_.summary: Time differentiation preserves a spatial derivative relation

TorusEuler.terminalTimeConvolution_le.text: Let $T>0$, let $q$ be a nonnegative integer, and let $u_i,v_i\ge0$. Write $w_i=T^i/i!$. The formal statement proves $\sum_{n=0}^q w_n\sum_{i=0}^n\binom ni u_iv_{n-i}\le(\sum_{i=0}^q w_iu_i)(\sum_{j=0}^q w_jv_j)$. The factorial identity changes each weighted binomial coefficient into $w_iw_{n-i}$. The left sum then uses only pairs whose total order is at most $q$, whereas the product includes every pair with both orders at most $q$. Nonnegativity permits the enlargement. This is the scalar estimate behind the auxiliary product bound; applying it to profiles additionally requires the appropriate spatial product inequality.
TorusEuler.terminalTimeConvolution_le.summary: Factorial weights bound the full Leibniz sum

TorusEuler.terminalTimeJet.text: For a curve $f$ with values in a normed space, a real $T$ and a nonnegative integer $n$, this denotes the $n$th iterated derivative of $f$ within $[0,T]$. The curve may take values in a space of half-Hölder fields. No regularity is assumed; where a derivative fails to exist the expression takes its assigned default value zero.
TorusEuler.terminalTimeJet.summary: Iterated time derivatives on the closed interval

TorusEuler.terminalTimeJetWeight.text: The scalar coefficient of time order $i$ is $T^i/i!$. Factorials compensate for binomial coefficients when the product rule is summed over all derivative orders up to $q$. The definition is available for every real $T$; positivity, which is needed to make the resulting weighted sum a seminorm, is established under $T>0$.
TorusEuler.terminalTimeJetWeight.summary: Factorial weights for the time derivative norm

TorusEuler.terminalTimeJetWeight_mul_cho.text: For any real $T$ and integers $0\le i\le n$, the formal statement proves $(T^n/n!)\binom ni=(T^i/i!)(T^{n-i}/(n-i)!)$. The condition $i\le n$ ensures that natural-number subtraction agrees with the ordinary difference. Factorials are positive, so no zero denominator occurs. Unlike the later estimate for sums of norms, this algebraic identity does not require $T>0$ and is valid also at $T=0$. It explains the choice of factorial weights in the auxiliary time norms; it contains neither a product estimate for fields nor assumptions about the Euler construction.
TorusEuler.terminalTimeJetWeight_mul_cho.summary: The time weights cancel the binomial coefficient

TorusEuler.terminalTimeJetWeight_pos.text: If $T>0$, then $T^i/i!$ is strictly positive for every natural $i$. The proof combines positivity of powers with positivity of natural factorials viewed as real numbers. Strict positivity is used to extract an individual derivative from the time norm; nonnegativity alone is enough for summing inequalities.
TorusEuler.terminalTimeJetWeight_pos.summary: Positive slab duration makes every time weight positive

TorusEuler.terminalTimeJetWeight_zero.text: The weight for time order zero is exactly one for every real slab parameter $T$, since $T^0=1$ and $0!=1$. Consequently the time norm always includes the original spatial seminorm without scaling. This identity supplies the base case of the transverse time induction and the order-zero norm simplification.

TorusEuler.terminalTimeJet_coefficientMu.text: Let $T>0$, let $K(t)$ be a curve of half-Hölder matrix fields on the torus and $v(t)$ a curve of half-Hölder vector fields, both smooth on $[0,T]$. For every $n$ and $t\in[0,T]$, the $n$-th time derivative within $[0,T]$ of the pointwise product $K(t)v(t)$ equals $\sum_{i=0}^n\binom ni K^{(i)}(t)\,v^{(n-i)}(t)$, as an identity of half-Hölder fields, including the endpoints.
TorusEuler.terminalTimeJet_coefficientMu.summary: Half-Hölder coefficient products obey the time Leibniz rule

TorusEuler.terminalTimeJet_coefficientMu.text: For a smooth half-Hölder coefficient curve $K$ on $[0,T]$, $T>0$, and a time $t$ in the closed slab, the $n$-th time jet of its operator-valued multiplication curve $r\mapsto(v\mapsto K(r)v)$ equals multiplication by the same time jet of $K$, $v\mapsto K^{(n)}(t)v$. No additional product terms occur, since the operator is not yet applied to a time-dependent vector field.
TorusEuler.terminalTimeJet_coefficientMu.summary: Differentiate the coefficient before forming its multiplication operator

TorusEuler.terminalTime_cutoff_depth_eve.text: For a schedule of inductive Euler parameters with initial frequency $\lambda_0>1$, any fixed spatial order $m$ and real exponent $e$ eventually satisfy both cutoff depth inequalities: $5m+5+e\le3d_j$ for the step depth $d_j$, and $16+2e\le K$ for the frequency exponent $K$ at order $q_{j+2}$. The threshold may depend on these fixed inputs. The proof uses growth of the frequencies to make the selected orders unbounded; it does not assert one starting index works simultaneously for all derivative orders.
TorusEuler.terminalTime_cutoff_depth_eve.summary: The prescribed depths eventually absorb fixed derivative costs

TorusEuler.terminalTime_cutoff_residual_.text: Assume $\lambda\ge2$, a nonnegative exponent $e$, $\lambda_+=\lambda^k$, $k\ge16+2e$, and both scalar costs at most $\lambda$. At cutoff radius $\lambda^5$ and depth $6k$, the projected residual term and quadratic tail together are at most $\lambda_+^{-5/2}$. The proof bounds each by $\lambda_+^{-3}$ and absorbs their sum using $\lambda_+\ge4$.
TorusEuler.terminalTime_cutoff_residual_.summary: Absorb both terms of the new residual bound

TorusEuler.terminalTime_cutoff_tail_rate.text: Let $\lambda\ge2$, let $C,\psi$ be real numbers with $C\le\lambda$, and let $m,P$ be nonnegative integers satisfying $5m+5+\psi\le3P$. The formal statement proves $C(\lambda^5)^{m-P}\lambda^{2(P+1)+\psi}\le\tfrac12\lambda^{-1}$. Here $m-P$ is an ordinary integer exponent, so a negative value denotes a reciprocal power. The declaration does not require $m\le P$ or $C\ge0$; those conditions enter the analytic tail application separately. This is the numerical step in the auxiliary truncation argument. It gives an explicit sufficient depth inequality at one stage, rather than itself proving that the inequality holds eventually along the schedule.
TorusEuler.terminalTime_cutoff_tail_rate.summary: A fixed depth inequality gives the half-size bound

TorusEuler.terminalTime_cutoff_velocity_.text: If $\lambda\ge2$ and $C\le\lambda$, then $C\lambda^{2+e}\le\lambda^{e+3}$ for every real exponent $e$. No lower bound on $C$ or on the exponent is required for this scalar inequality. Its application uses a nonnegative cutoff cost already controlled by the schedule.
TorusEuler.terminalTime_cutoff_velocity_.summary: The cutoff velocity costs one further frequency power

TorusEuler.terminalTime_neBot.text: For T>0, the neighborhood filter 𝓝[Ico 0 T] T is not the bottom filter. Thus a terminal Tendsto statement is a genuine left-hand limit from physical times, rather than a limit along an empty approach. The proof uses that T lies in the closure of [0,T). It is a topology lemma supporting the interpretation of the paper’s t↑T limits.
TorusEuler.terminalTime_neBot.summary: Approaching the terminal time is nonvacuous

TorusEuler.terminalVelocityBound_of_exte.text: Let $w$ be continuous on $[0,T]\times[-1/2,1/2]^3$, and suppose $u(t,x)=w(t,x)$ there for $0\le t<T$. Then one finite constant bounds the essential supremum of $|u(t,x)|$ over that cube at every time before $T$. This follows from compactness of the closed time interval and spatial cell. Periodicity and the Euler equations are not hypotheses of this elementary assertion; they give its interpretation as a velocity bound on $\mathbb T^3$ in Proposition 8.2. Continuity and agreement with $w$ are assumed here, rather than established by this theorem.
TorusEuler.terminalVelocityBound_of_exte.summary: A continuous extension over one closed period bounds the velocity

TorusEuler.terminal_contDiffOn_materialI.text: For a nondegenerate closed interval and jointly smooth $U$ and $f$, every finite material iterate is jointly smooth on the same slab. Induction uses the previous preservation theorem and the zeroth-iterate identity. No quantitative norm bound or frequency information is concluded; these regularity facts make the subsequent chain-rule and product estimates applicable.
TorusEuler.terminal_contDiffOn_materialI.summary: All material derivatives remain jointly smooth

TorusEuler.terminal_contDiffOn_materialS.text: Assume $a<b$ and that $U(t,x)$ and $f(t,x)$ are jointly smooth on $[a,b]\times\mathbb R^3$. Then the material derivative $\partial_tf+D_xf\,U$, with the time derivative taken within $[a,b]$, is again jointly smooth on $[a,b]\times\mathbb R^3$.

TorusEuler.terminal_contDiffOn_spaceDeri.text: If $a<b$ and $f(t,x)$ is jointly smooth on $[a,b]\times\mathbb R^3$, then $(t,x)\mapsto D_xf(t,x)$, the spatial derivative of $f(t,\cdot)$ at $x$, is jointly smooth on $[a,b]\times\mathbb R^3$.

TorusEuler.terminal_contDiffOn_timeSlice.text: Joint smoothness on the slab gives within-interval smoothness of $t\mapsto f(t,x)$ for each fixed $x$. The proof composes with $t\mapsto(t,x)$. This is regularity relative to the closed time interval, not the choice of an extension across its endpoints; derivative identities at those endpoints are established by separate lemmas.
TorusEuler.terminal_contDiffOn_timeSlice.summary: Every fixed-point time curve is smooth within the interval

TorusEuler.terminal_contDiff_spaceSlice.text: If $f(t,x)$ is jointly smooth on $[a,b]\times\mathbb R^3$ and $t\in[a,b]$, then $x\mapsto f(t,x)$ is smooth on $\mathbb R^3$. The interval is not required to be nondegenerate.
TorusEuler.terminal_contDiff_spaceSlice.summary: Every spatial slice of a jointly smooth field is smooth

TorusEuler.terminal_derivWithin_fderiv_c.text: Let $a<b$ and let $f(t,x)$ be jointly smooth on $[a,b]\times\mathbb R^3$. For every $t\in[a,b]$, including both endpoints, and every $x$, the time derivative within $[a,b]$ of $r\mapsto D_xf(r,x)$ equals the spatial derivative at $x$ of $y\mapsto\partial_tf(t,y)$, the latter time derivative also taken within $[a,b]$.
TorusEuler.terminal_derivWithin_fderiv_c.summary: One time derivative commutes with the spatial derivative

TorusEuler.terminal_iteratedDerivWithin_.text: On a nondegenerate closed slab, $a<b$, let $f$ be a jointly smooth field on $[a,b]\times\mathbb R^3$. For every order $q$, every time $t\in[a,b]$ and every spatial point $x$, the spatial Fréchet derivative commutes with the order-$q$ time derivative: $\partial_t^q$ (within $[a,b]$, at fixed point) of $D_xf$ equals $D_x$ of $\partial_t^qf(t,\cdot)$ at $x$. Endpoint times are included at every order.
TorusEuler.terminal_iteratedDerivWithin_.summary: All time derivatives commute with a spatial derivative

TorusEuler.terminal_poincare_integral.text: Let $T\ge0$ and let a path $f$ have continuous derivative $f'$ on $[0,T]$, the derivative taken within $[0,T]$, and terminal vanishing $f(T)=0$. Then the integrated displacement is controlled: $\int_0^T|f(t)|^2\,dt\le\frac{T^2}2\int_0^T|f'(s)|^2\,ds$. Neither initial vanishing nor $T\le1$ is required.
TorusEuler.terminal_poincare_integral.summary: Terminal vanishing bounds the integrated displacement

TorusEuler.terminal_poincare_pointwise.text: Let $f$ be a path in a real Banach space on $[0,T]$, with $T\ge0$, a continuous derivative on that interval, and $f(T)=0$. For every $t\in[0,T]$, the formal theorem proves $|f(t)|^2\le(T-t)\int_0^T|f'(s)|^2\,ds$. The pointwise estimate displayed before (1.9) instead integrates from $t$ to $T$ and is therefore sharper. The proof obtains that sharper bound before enlarging the interval, but the exported conclusion is the weaker one stated here. Applying it to $f(t)=\xi(t,a)$ and then integrating in time and labels still requires the corresponding regularity and integrability hypotheses; those space-time steps are not this theorem’s conclusion.
TorusEuler.terminal_poincare_pointwise.summary: A vanishing endpoint controls the path by its derivative

TorusEuler.terminal_waveRelayGeometry_co.text: If the inverse coframe $G$ and strain $M$ are jointly smooth on the slab $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3$, then their curl, material, and pressure-gradient relay rows are jointly smooth there for every fixed real label width $\ell$. The proof uses their unit-width linear or bilinear formulas followed by multiplication by the fixed scalar $\ell^{-1}$. No nondegenerate-slab or positive-width assumption is needed merely to preserve smoothness.
TorusEuler.terminal_waveRelayGeometry_co.summary: The three geometric relay rows are jointly smooth

TorusEuler.theorem11.text: The formal assertion is the existence of smooth odd divergence-free periodic data $u_0$, a finite time $T_*>0$, and a smooth odd maximal Euler solution $u,p$ on $[0,T_*)$ with $u(0)=u_0$. It requires bounded velocity, central vorticity tending to infinity, divergence of the time integrals of the gradient and vorticity norms, and spatial $C^m$ limits of velocity and its time derivative on every compact set away from the torus origin. Pressure is normalized to have zero mean. The numbered version of Theorem 1.1 additionally states uniqueness of the maximal velocity and its lifespan. That comparison is not an explicit conjunct of this shorter assertion.
TorusEuler.theorem11.summary: The shorter theorem gives all stated singularity properties

TorusEuler.theorem11Witness_of_solution_.text: Let $(u,p)$ be a smooth periodic Euler solution on $[0,T)$. Assume each $u(t)$ is odd, $\operatorname{ess\,sup}|u(t)|\le C$ for one $C$ and all $t$, $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\to\infty$ as $t\uparrow T$, $u$ and $\partial_tu$ have locally uniform limits with all derivatives on compact sets away from the origin, and $\int_0^T\|\operatorname{curl}u(t)\|_{L^\infty}dt=\infty$. Then $u(0),T,u,p$ satisfy all conclusions of Theorem 1.1: smooth odd periodic divergence-free data, maximality, oddness for all times, divergence of both the gradient and curl integrals, bounded velocity, central blow-up and both limit statements.
TorusEuler.theorem11Witness_of_solution_.summary: The terminal bounds certify the constructed solution

TorusEuler.theorem11_library.text: Proves the existence statement of Theorem 1.1 by choosing the established record of later pressure and activation costs and passing it through the uniform-stage construction and limit argument. This is the retained proof following the frozen manuscript of 18 November 2026. The formalization's main statement of Theorem 1.1 is instead obtained from the latest proof organized along the paper's sections; this declaration does not claim to follow that newer conditional-proof route or export its uniqueness clause.
TorusEuler.theorem11_library.summary: The retained direct proof gives the existence theorem

TorusEuler.theorem11_of_continuation_and.text: Let $u,p$ solve smooth periodic Euler on $[0,T)$, $T>0$, with mean-zero pressure and odd velocity. Assume uniformly bounded velocity, $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\to\infty$, and local $C^m$ terminal limits for both $u$ and $\partial_tu$ on every compact set avoiding the torus origin. Assume additionally that a finite vorticity integral would yield a smooth Euler continuation agreeing with $u$ to some $S>T$. The formal statement then gives the existence conclusion of Theorem 1.1, including both infinite integrals and maximality. The continuation criterion is an input, not a theorem proved here. The main Section 8 proof follows a different route, using quantitative vorticity estimates and crossing durations. This link therefore cannot certify the general periodic Beale–Kato–Majda criterion.
TorusEuler.theorem11_of_continuation_and.summary: A continuation criterion is an explicit hypothesis of this implication

TorusEuler.theorem11_of_inductiveEulerLo.text: Above a universal base-frequency threshold, lifetime bounds, a certified initial pair and a local compatible successor imply the existence statement of Theorem 1.1. The proof first forms a common infinite family and then applies the terminal assembly. This is a conditional reduction of the headline theorem, not a standalone proof that the required local constructions exist.
TorusEuler.theorem11_of_inductiveEulerLo.summary: The local construction suffices for the headline theorem

TorusEuler.theorem11_of_inductiveEulerSt.text: Deduces the existence statement of Theorem 1.1 from the singularity witness, once a compatible stage family, its central waves and a sufficiently large initial frequency have been supplied. The threshold is existential and uniform in the family. This conditional assembly belongs to the frozen library route and is distinct from the current unconditional entry point organized along the paper's sections.
TorusEuler.theorem11_of_inductiveEulerSt.summary: The stage construction implies the headline existence statement

TorusEuler.theorem11_of_laterPrimaryCost.text: A supplied record of these later-wave primary costs yields the frozen existence proposition of Theorem 1.1 by first proving uniform physical estimates and then applying the schedule-and-limit theorem. This short theorem exposes the last hypothesis of the retained direct route. Its unconditional closure is the formalization's proof of Theorem 1.1, which supplies the cost record using the two analytic existence results.
TorusEuler.theorem11_of_laterPrimaryCost.summary: The later primary estimates complete the direct existence route

TorusEuler.theorem11_of_quantitative_act.text: Let $u$ be an Euler solution on $[0,T)$ that is odd at each time, agrees on the centred cell with a field continuous on the closed slab $[0,T]\times[-1/2,1/2]^3$, and has off-origin limits for $u$ and $\partial_tu$. Suppose activation times $t_j$ increase to $T$ from below, $\mu_j,L_j\to\infty$, and eventually $t_j\ge0$, $2L_j^2\le r_j(t_{j+1}-t_j)$, $r_j\le C\mu_j^{1/8}L_j$ and $|\operatorname{curl}u(s,0)|\ge c\mu_j^{1/8}-B\mu_j^{1/32}-B$ on $[t_j,t_{j+1})$, with $c,C>0$. Then Theorem 1.1 holds. Compactness bounds velocity, interval coverage gives central vorticity blowup, and interval mass gives integral divergence. The solution and extension are explicit hypotheses.
TorusEuler.theorem11_of_quantitative_act.summary: A supplied Euler solution inherits all terminal conclusions

TorusEuler.theorem11_of_solution_and_ter.text: Existentially packages the given solution $(u,p)$, its lifespan $T$ and its initial velocity $u(0)$ to prove the existence statement of Theorem 1.1. The hypotheses are those of the witness assembly: oddness, a uniform bound on $u$, central curl blow-up, off-origin limits of $u$ and $\partial_tu$, and divergence of the curl integral. This declaration is conditional and does not assert uniqueness.
TorusEuler.theorem11_of_solution_and_ter.summary: The same terminal bounds imply the existence statement

TorusEuler.theorem11_of_uniformPhysicalE.text: Assumes the uniform physical stage estimates, indexed by a finite set, and concludes the existence statement of Theorem 1.1. It chooses a numerical schedule large enough for the independent stage-to-limit theorem, constructs the corresponding stages and central waves, then applies that theorem. The uniform estimates remain a genuine hypothesis here; their construction occurs in a later part of the formalization.
TorusEuler.theorem11_of_uniformPhysicalE.summary: Uniform physical estimates imply the frozen existence theorem

TorusEuler.timeDerivative.text: For a velocity $u(t,x)$ and a real $T$, the formal definition differentiates $t\mapsto u(t,x)$ at fixed spatial point within the set $[0,T)$. When $T>0$ and $u$ is smooth on that slab, this is the usual time derivative for $0<t<T$ and the right derivative at $t=0$. The expression is defined even without differentiability, assigning zero when no derivative exists. It also has values at times outside the slab, which do not describe an Euler evolution there. Theorem 1.1 uses only its values before $T_*$ when asserting the off-origin spatial limit as $t\uparrow T_*$, not a derivative through the singular time.
TorusEuler.timeDerivative.summary: The time derivative is taken within the solution interval

TorusEuler.timeDerivative_eq_of_prefix_d.text: If an evolution derivative identity holds on every earlier closed prefix, then the time derivative of $u$ within $[0,T)$ equals its prescribed derivative throughout $[0,T)$. For each time the proof chooses a strictly later prefix endpoint still below $T$. That prefix is a within-neighborhood of the time, which justifies changing the derivative's domain.
TorusEuler.timeDerivative_eq_of_prefix_d.summary: Closed-prefix dynamics determine the half-open derivative

TorusEuler.toUnitTorus.text:
The quotient of the periodic Euclidean lift by the integer lattice.
