The denominator is a fixed nonzero complex number; the next lemma certifies that the resulting coefficient does not vanish.
_private.TorusEuler.BaseParentData.0.Tor.summary: The coefficient of the positive sine frequency

_private.TorusEuler.BaseParentData.0.Tor.text: The scalar $1/(2i)$ is nonzero because its numerator and denominator are nonzero complex numbers. This elementary guard combines with the nonzero shear direction to show that each of the two assigned Fourier coefficients is present for every parameter value.

For any complex argument, the positive exponential multiplied by $1/(2i)$ plus the negative exponential multiplied by its negative equals the complex sine. This exact identity is used after evaluating the two shear characters. It confirms the coefficient sign convention before identifying the real parent field.

If the radius $r$ satisfies $r\le1/2$, the open Euclidean ball about zero is contained in the interior of the centered unit cell. Each coordinate is bounded by the vector norm, giving the cell inclusion. The open-ball property upgrades that inclusion to the cell interior; negative radii simply give an empty ball.
_private.TorusEuler.BaseParentData.0.Tor.summary: A ball of radius at most one half lies inside the cell

_private.TorusEuler.BaseParentData.0.Tor.text: The positive unit frequency in the second coordinate is not equal to its negative. The proof reads the second component, where the equality would say one equals negative one. This guarantees that finite synthesis over the two signed modes contains two distinct terms.

At every spatial point, composing the shear velocity gradient with itself gives the zero operator. The gradient is a cosine scalar times the same square-zero central rank-one map. This makes the quadratic trace source in the parent pressure Poisson equation vanish identically.
_private.TorusEuler.BaseParentData.0.Tor.summary: The stationary velocity gradient squares to zero everywhere

_private.TorusEuler.ChildFlowDeformation.text: Sum the three coordinate evaluations of a linear map on the matching coordinate directions. This packages the trace as a continuous linear map on spatial endomorphisms, so it can commute with integrals and derivatives. Applied to a vector field's Fréchet derivative, it recovers the divergence used in the phase cancellation.
_private.TorusEuler.ChildFlowDeformation.summary: The trace as a continuous linear functional

_private.TorusEuler.ChildFlowDeformation.text: The label-divergence functional applied to the Fréchet derivative of $c$ at $a$ equals $\operatorname{div}c(a)$. The equality holds for arbitrary $c$, because both sides use the same derivative expression, assigned zero where $c$ is not differentiable. Analytic differentiability must still be supplied when this identity is used as a classical divergence formula.
_private.TorusEuler.ChildFlowDeformation.summary: Applying the trace functional gives divergence

_private.TorusEuler.ChildFlowDeformation.text: At a differentiability point of a function on a product of a normed space and one real coordinate, bounds $A$ and $B$ for the two partial derivatives give the full derivative bound $A+B$. The product derivative is split into its two linear components. This justifies combining label and phase derivative estimates.
_private.TorusEuler.ChildFlowDeformation.summary: The full derivative is controlled by both partial derivatives

_private.TorusEuler.ChildFlowDeformation.text: For a function differentiable at a label-phase point, a bound on its full Fréchet derivative also bounds the derivative of the slice obtained by fixing phase. The spatial inclusion has norm at most one. This helper extracts the label derivative estimate without introducing a new geometric scale.
_private.TorusEuler.ChildFlowDeformation.summary: A label derivative inherits the joint derivative bound

_private.TorusEuler.ChildFlowDeformation.text: The operator norm of the functional extracting label divergence from a label-phase derivative is at most three. Each coordinate evaluation has norm at most one, and the triangle inequality sums the three contributions. This numerical constant enters the rescaled divergence estimate used to control the longitudinal phase velocity.
_private.TorusEuler.ChildFlowDeformation.summary: Three coordinate traces cost at most three

_private.TorusEuler.ChildFlowDeformation.text: The sole assumption $Kw\le1/2$ bounds the product of $K$ and $w$, which implies $\exp(Kw)\le2$. Neither factor is individually required to be nonnegative. This elementary numerical estimate converts the scaled-gradient smallness condition into the uniform factor-two flow bounds used later.

For the same homogeneous derivative inequality, the norm at $t$ is bounded by its value at any allowed $s$ multiplied by $\exp(K|t-s|)$. Both times belong to the supplied slab. Reversing time gives the backward estimate needed to control inverse as well as forward transitions.
_private.TorusEuler.ChildFlowDeformation.summary: Exponential growth between any two allowed times

_private.TorusEuler.ChildFlowDeformation.text: A normed-space curve whose within-interval derivative satisfies $\|x'\|\le K\|x\|$ obeys the exponential bound from its value at the left endpoint. The evaluation time is required to lie in that interval. This homogeneous Grönwall estimate underlies the stability of the scaled particle trajectories.
_private.TorusEuler.ChildFlowDeformation.summary: Exponential growth from the left endpoint

_private.TorusEuler.ChildFlowDeformation.text: This continuous linear functional evaluates a label-phase derivative on each of the three label directions, reads the matching output component, and sums. The phase direction is omitted. It packages label divergence on the enlarged profile space, allowing one fixed norm bound to control all three coordinate contributions.
_private.TorusEuler.ChildFlowDeformation.summary: Trace only the label part of the full derivative

_private.TorusEuler.ChildFlowDeformation.text: The scaled label-divergence functional is exactly the sum of the three diagonal evaluations of a linear map on the label directions with zero phase component. This makes its omission of the phase derivative explicit. The identity is purely linear algebra and holds without regularity assumptions on an underlying profile.
_private.TorusEuler.ChildFlowDeformation.summary: The label trace is the three diagonal evaluations

_private.TorusEuler.CoframeDerivativeBou.text: For a $C^2$ periodic parent flow on a nondegenerate slab, the forward transition derivative is invertible. Its algebraic inverse equals the reverse transition derivative evaluated at the transported point. Both times must lie in the slab. This identifies the algebraic inverse, which is defined (with value zero at noninvertible elements) for every matrix, with the geometric inverse before differentiating it.
_private.TorusEuler.CoframeDerivativeBou.summary: The reverse Jacobian is the genuine algebraic inverse

_private.TorusEuler.CutoffResidual.0.Tor.text: This continuous linear map sums the three diagonal coordinate evaluations of an endomorphism of Euclidean three-space. Packaging trace in this way permits it to commute with differentiation and linear combinations in the cutoff-divergence calculation. The definition applies to every operator, regardless of whether it arose as a derivative.
_private.TorusEuler.CutoffResidual.0.Tor.summary: The trace bundled as a bounded linear map

_private.TorusEuler.CutoffResidual.0.Tor.text: For any continuous linear endomorphism, the coordinate trace functional (the sum of diagonal entries) agrees with the coordinate-free trace of the underlying linear map. This identifies the implementation with the trace used in divergence formulas. It is a finite-dimensional algebraic identity and carries no smoothness or invertibility assumptions.
_private.TorusEuler.CutoffResidual.0.Tor.summary: The coordinate functional equals the intrinsic trace

_private.TorusEuler.DyadicHolder.0.Torus.text: The real square-root power of $2^j$ equals $(\sqrt2)^j$ for each natural number $j$. Since the base is positive, the real-power convention agrees with the usual positive square root. This converts the multiplier hypotheses into geometric sequences that the series estimates can sum explicitly.
_private.TorusEuler.DyadicHolder.0.Torus.summary: Real half-powers agree with geometric half-scales

_private.TorusEuler.DyadicHolder.0.Torus.text: The negative half-power of $2^j$ is the $j$th power of $1/\sqrt2$. This identity rewrites the high-frequency size bounds into a decreasing geometric sequence. The positive dyadic base ensures that the real exponent and reciprocal conventions have their ordinary analytic meanings.
_private.TorusEuler.DyadicHolder.0.Torus.summary: Inverse half-powers form a geometric decay sequence

_private.TorusEuler.DyadicHolder.0.Torus.text: For a distance $d$ strictly between zero and one, choose an index $n$ so that the low-frequency contribution $d(\sqrt2)^n$ and high-frequency contribution $(1/\sqrt2)^n$ are both controlled by multiples of $\sqrt d$. The same index satisfies both inequalities, enabling a half-Hölder estimate for the full series.
_private.TorusEuler.DyadicHolder.0.Torus.summary: One frequency split balances both increment estimates

_private.TorusEuler.DyadicHolder.0.Torus.text: The numerical inequality $4/3\le\sqrt2$ supplies a convenient lower bound for the ratio between adjacent half-order dyadic scales. It has no variable hypotheses. Its reciprocal form gives a rational majorant for the decreasing geometric series used to estimate the high-frequency tail.
_private.TorusEuler.DyadicHolder.0.Torus.summary: A rational lower bound for the dyadic ratio

_private.TorusEuler.DyadicHolder.0.Torus.text: The reciprocal dyadic half-scale ratio is at most three quarters. This numerical comparison makes the geometric tail summable with an explicit constant. The square root is the ordinary positive square root of two, so the inverse never encounters a zero-denominator case.
_private.TorusEuler.DyadicHolder.0.Torus.summary: A rational upper bound for the reciprocal ratio

_private.TorusEuler.DyadicHolder.0.Torus.text: The sum of $(\sqrt2)^j$ for indices $j<n$ is at most three times $(\sqrt2)^n$. This finite geometric estimate controls the low-frequency part of a difference after applying the Lipschitz bound to each block. The same splitting index is used for the complementary decaying tail.
_private.TorusEuler.DyadicHolder.0.Torus.summary: The low-frequency prefix costs one final scale

_private.TorusEuler.DyadicHolder.0.Torus.text: The sequence of powers of $1/\sqrt2$ is summable. This is the scalar convergence input for the uniform majorant of the Banach-valued dyadic blocks. It ensures that the infinite sum used later is a genuine convergent series rather than the value zero that an infinite sum is assigned when the series is not summable.

The sum of all powers of $1/\sqrt2$ is at most four. Together with each block's geometric supremum bound, this yields the uniform size bound for the reconstructed function. Summability is established separately before the infinite-series formula is evaluated in this estimate.
_private.TorusEuler.DyadicHolder.0.Torus.summary: The decreasing half-scale series is bounded by four

_private.TorusEuler.DyadicHolder.0.Torus.text: For every natural index $j$, the square of $(\sqrt2)^j$ is $2^j$. This exact identity converts between half-order scales and the original dyadic frequency. It is used in the estimates choosing the splitting index for a spatial increment and involves no real-power ambiguity.
_private.TorusEuler.DyadicHolder.0.Torus.summary: Squaring the half-scale recovers the dyadic scale

_private.TorusEuler.DyadicMultiplierKern.text: A Fourier mode evaluated at $x-y$ factors into its value at $x$ and the negative-frequency exponential in $y$. The identity uses the whole-space Fourier normalization with $2\pi$. It prepares the calculation in which an operator-valued kernel acts on a single torus Fourier coefficient.
_private.TorusEuler.DyadicMultiplierKern.summary: The translated mode exposes the transform's exponential

_private.TorusEuler.DyadicMultiplierKern.text: For a Schwartz kernel, its norm multiplied by the square root of spatial distance is integrable over Euclidean three-space. Rapid decay controls the tail, while the square-root weight is harmless near zero. This is the finiteness hypothesis required by the zero-mean-kernel half-Hölder estimate.
_private.TorusEuler.DyadicMultiplierKern.summary: Schwartz decay makes the half-order moment finite

_private.TorusEuler.DyadicMultiplierKern.text: A positive dilation of Euclidean three-space, multiplied by the cubic normalization, leaves the total Bochner integral unchanged. The target may be any real normed space. This change-of-variables identity is used for operator-valued kernels as well as scalar ones; it does not separately assert that the input is integrable.
_private.TorusEuler.DyadicMultiplierKern.summary: Normalized dilation preserves a Banach-valued integral

_private.TorusEuler.DyadicMultiplierKern.text: For a Schwartz symbol with values in a complete complex normed space, the inverse-transform kernel and its first derivative obey weighted bounds through spatial weight order five. The constant is $(1+2\pi)4^5$ times the derivative mass. The hypotheses $d\le1$ on the derivative order and $n\le5$ on the weight order explicitly limit the two orders covered by this estimate.
_private.TorusEuler.DyadicMultiplierKern.summary: Integrations by parts control weighted kernel derivatives

_private.TorusEuler.DyadicMultiplierKern.text: For weight exponent $d\le1$ and derivative order $n\le5$, the corresponding rectangular partial sum of weighted derivative integrals is at most the full multiplier mass. Every summand is nonnegative. This helper lets each integration-by-parts estimate use the same single constant, independently of the selected derivative and weight orders.
_private.TorusEuler.DyadicMultiplierKern.summary: Partial derivative sums fit inside the full mass

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointCoefficientC.text: Every value of a half-Hölder coefficient field has operator norm at most the field norm, hence the same bound holds almost everywhere for Haar measure. This supplies essential boundedness for the spatial $L^2$ multiplier. The estimate concerns the coefficient itself, without any ellipticity assumption.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointCoefficientC.summary: The coefficient norm bounds almost every torus value

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointCoefficientC.text: The pointwise coefficient field extracted from a bundled half-Hölder field is almost-everywhere strongly measurable for torus Haar measure. Continuity of the bundled field provides the claim. This is one of the two certificates required to define its multiplication operator on spatial $L^2$.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointCoefficientC.summary: Half Hölder coefficients are measurable for Haar integration

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointCoefficientC.text: Package the continuous function $x\mapsto K(x)v(x)$ as a half-Hölder field, using the preceding value and increment bounds. The definition is the unbundled-input stage of coefficient multiplication. It preserves the actual pointwise product rather than choosing a representative in a quotient space.

The difference $K(x)v(x)-K(y)v(y)$ is bounded by $2\|K\|\|v\|\sqrt{d(x,y)}$. Splitting it into $K(x)(v(x)-v(y))+(K(x)-K(y))v(y)$ separates the two sources of variation. This estimate applies to bounded linear maps between different real normed spaces, not only to the three-dimensional kinetic coefficient.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointCoefficientC.summary: Variable coefficient products preserve half Hölder increments

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointCoefficientC.text: For a half-Hölder coefficient field $K$ and vector field $v$, the norm of $K(x)v(x)$ is bounded by $2\|K\|\|v\|$. The extra factor two matches the increment bound used in the half-Hölder norm of the product. The argument only needs the ordinary operator-norm estimate and the evaluation bounds.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointCoefficientC.summary: A coefficient product has a uniform value bound

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointCoefficientC.text: For a bundled half-Hölder field, its norm bounds every value and every increment divided by the square root of distance. The theorem returns both bounds together and uses no compactness assumption on the domain. It unpacks the precise norm convention needed to estimate multiplication by variable coefficients.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointCoefficientC.summary: The norm controls values and half Hölder increments

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointCoefficientC.text: Evaluating the constructed half-Hölder product at $x$ gives $K(x)$ applied to $v(x)$ exactly. The equality unfolds the definition and is pointwise, unlike the $L^2$ compatibility equalities proved later. It is used to prove linearity of multiplication in the vector-field input.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointCoefficientC.summary: Evaluation gives the ordinary coefficient product

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointComplexifica.text: For a complex scalar $c$ and vector $z$, scalar multiplication satisfies $cz=(\operatorname{Re}c)z+(\operatorname{Im}c)(iz)$. The statement uses the compatible real and complex scalar structures. It lets real linearity and commutation with $i$ imply full complex linearity in the extension construction.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointComplexifica.summary: Complex scalar multiplication splits into two real operations

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointComplexifica.text: Extend a real bounded operator $A$ to the complexified space by applying it to real and imaginary parts and then reconstructing. At this stage the result is only a real continuous linear map. Compatibility with multiplication by $i$ is proved before it is repackaged as a complex-linear operator.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointComplexifica.summary: Apply a real operator separately to both parts

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointComplexifica.text: The real-linear extension satisfies $A_{\mathbb C}(iz)=iA_{\mathbb C}(z)$. Compatibility of the complexification projections with multiplication by $i$ makes the two components exchange with the correct sign. Along with real linearity, this is the missing algebraic property needed to construct a complex-linear extension.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointComplexifica.summary: The extension commutes with multiplication by i

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointComplexifica.text: The real-linear extension of $A$ at $z$ is the embedding of $A(\operatorname{Re}z)$ plus $i$ times the embedding of $A(\operatorname{Im}z)$. This exposes the defining finite sum. It is used to establish compatibility with projections and complex scalar multiplication without assuming any extra properties of $A$.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointComplexifica.summary: The real extension has the two part formula

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointComplexifica.text: Taking the imaginary part after extending $A$ gives $A$ applied to the input imaginary part. The real summand contributes zero, while multiplication by $i$ turns the embedded imaginary input into the correct component. The formula holds for every bounded real operator, without self-adjointness or positivity.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointComplexifica.summary: The imaginary part receives the original operator

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointComplexifica.text: Applying the real-linear extension of $A$ to $z$ has norm at most $\|A\|\|z\|$. Squared-norm splitting separates the real and imaginary components, each controlled by the usual operator bound. This avoids a factor two and prepares the norm-preserving complex extension used in quantitative multiplier estimates.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointComplexifica.summary: The extension obeys the original operator bound

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointComplexifica.text: Taking the real part after the real-linear extension of $A$ gives $A$ applied to the original real part. The imaginary summand contributes zero by the complexification identities. This identity is one half of the component calculation used to control the extension norm and prove its algebraic properties.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointComplexifica.summary: The real part receives the original operator

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointComplexifica.text: For an element $u$ of $L^2(\mu;E)$, the squared norm equals the integral of the squared norm of its representative. Only a normed additive group structure on $E$ is needed here; the proof uses the $L^p$ norm formula rather than an inner product. It prepares the real and imaginary energy decomposition.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointComplexifica.summary: The path norm is the integral of squared magnitude

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointComplexifica.text: The squared norm of a complex Euclidean three-vector equals the sum of squared norms of its real and imaginary projections. The proof sums the corresponding scalar complex identity over coordinates. This supplies the exact orthogonal norm splitting required by the spatial complexification structure.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointComplexifica.summary: Complex Euclidean energy splits into two real energies

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointConcreteInve.text: Given an idempotent $P$ and an invertible map $e$ on the range of $P$ equal to the compression of $B$, the theorem constructs a fixed vector $v$ of $P$ satisfying $P(Bv+f)=0$. The norm is at most $M\|Pf\|$, assuming the inverse of $e$ has norm at most $M$. The construction therefore solves with the negative projected source and preserves that sign explicitly.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointConcreteInve.summary: Solve the projected residual with the correct source sign

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointConcreteProj.text: If the real operator symbol $P$ is smooth away from the origin, its complex-linear extension is smooth on the same punctured set. The extension is a bounded real linear map between operator spaces. This result supplies the complex-symbol regularity needed by the Fourier multiplier construction without requiring any behavior at zero.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointConcreteProj.summary: Complexification preserves smoothness of the angular symbol

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointConcreteProj.text: The inner product after passing from label-valued time paths to joint space-time $L^2$ equals the pairing after the Haar embedding into label $L^2$. Both expressions integrate the same pointwise inner products, with the integration order handled by the mixed-space isometry. This preserves the energy calculation across the two representations.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointConcreteProj.summary: The two mixed Hilbert realizations have the same pairing

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointConcreteProj.text: Take the real part of a complex half-Hölder vector field and embed it in real $L^2$. The result equals taking the real part after its complex torus $L^2$ embedding. This compatibility compares the two quotient-space constructions through their almost-everywhere values and supports the identification of the strong real Leray projection.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointConcreteProj.summary: Real parts commute with the spatial Hilbert embedding

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointConcreteProj.text: The real vector associated with the negative integer lattice mode is the negative of the original lattice vector. This elementary compatibility keeps the signs consistent when passing between Fourier characters and homogeneous real symbols. It is used with evenness of the projection symbol to recover real-valued multiplier actions.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointConcreteProj.summary: Negating a Fourier mode negates its real frequency

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointConcreteSpat.text: The joint space-time $L^2$ norm of a label-valued time-path field equals its norm under the Haar embedding. The two realizations differ only in how the product integration is represented. This equality transfers the weak contraction estimate for the mixed constraint projection into the form required by the spatial bootstrap.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointConcreteSpat.summary: Both mixed representations have the same Hilbert norm

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointDensity.0.To.text: For an $L^2$ path, the norm of its Bochner integral is bounded by the square root of the measure of $(0,T]$, times its $L^2$ norm. There is no positivity assumption on $T$ in this auxiliary estimate. It uses finite-measure inclusion of $L^2$ into $L^1$.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointDensity.0.To.summary: Time integration is bounded on square integrable paths

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointDensity.0.To.text: Under $T\ge0$, the real-valued measure of the whole restricted time space is $T$. The measure is Lebesgue measure restricted to $(0,T]$. This normalization turns the abstract finite-measure integration estimate into the familiar factor $\sqrt T$ in the endpoint path bounds.

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointInstantaneou.text: Identifies the fixed space of the strong spatial Leray projection with the canonical half-Hölder solenoidal subspace. The map is an isometric linear equivalence obtained from equality of the underlying submodules; it does not solve an equation. This changes the space used by the freezing inverse without changing the represented field or its norm.

Applying the identification between the Leray fixed space and the half-Hölder solenoidal space leaves the underlying value unchanged. The argument $u$ already lies in the fixed subspace, so the statement is an identity of underlying fields, rather than a claim that an arbitrary field is divergence free. It permits equations for the original inverse to be rewritten on the recovery space.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointInstantaneou.summary: Changing solenoidal spaces preserves the field

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointInstantaneou.text: The inverse identification also leaves the underlying half-Hölder field unchanged. Here $u$ belongs to the canonical solenoidal subspace. The proof uses the forward value identity and the inverse law of the equivalence, allowing the norm and coefficient equation of the freezing inverse to survive conjugation between the two presentations.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointInstantaneou.summary: Returning to the fixed space preserves values

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointJointHaarReg.text: For every member of a finite list, suppose a mixed field represents its associated time curve. Then the sum of those mixed fields represents the sum of the curves. The proof uses the zero and addition representation lemmas, and supports the finite product-rule sums in spatial commutators.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointJointHaarReg.summary: A finite represented family sums to its time curve

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointJointHaarReg.text: A finite sum of terms $C_{p_1}(t)v_{p_2}(t)$ is $C^n$ on the time set if the coefficient and vector curves for every listed pair have that regularity. The lemma is stated for arbitrary real normed spaces. Induction over the list supplies the regularity of commutator corrections in the spatial derivative hierarchy.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointJointHaarReg.summary: Finite correction sums preserve time regularity

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointJointHaarReg.text: Evaluation of a half-Hölder field at $a+\pi(shu)$, where $\pi:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb T^3$ is the quotient map, is continuous in the real segment parameter $s$. The result works in any real normed target space and imposes no condition on $h$ or $u$. It ensures that segment averages used to recover derivatives are ordinary integrable continuous functions.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointJointHaarReg.summary: Evaluating a Hölder field along a segment is continuous

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointJointHaarReg.text: If $K$ and $\Omega$ have torus directional derivatives $dK$ and $d\Omega$, then the path coefficient $K-J\Omega$ has derivative $dK-Jd\Omega$. The temporal primitive is a fixed bounded linear operator, so it commutes with this spatial differentiation. Nonnegative duration is the only time assumption needed here.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointJointHaarReg.summary: Spatial differentiation passes through the primitive coefficient

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointJointHaarReg.text: The negative mixed Leray projection of a field has the projected negative derivative whenever the original field has a torus directional derivative. Positive duration supplies the Haar-space contraction estimate used by the derivative-preservation theorem. This validates the projected forcing derivative in the mixed spatial solve, rather than presuming formal commutation.

If all nonzero directional difference quotients of a half-Hölder field equal segment averages of another half-Hölder field, that second field is its torus directional derivative. The average error tends to zero as the step tends to zero. The statement gives a genuine derivative at every label along every line, not merely an almost-everywhere derivative.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointJointHaarReg.summary: Segment averages determine the actual spatial derivative

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointJointHaarReg.text: The difference between a half-Hölder field’s segment average and its value at the starting label is bounded by $\|z\|\sqrt{|h|\|u\|}$. The estimate follows from the half-Hölder increment bound and integration over a unit interval. It quantifies the error needed to identify a spatial derivative from segment averages.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointJointHaarReg.summary: A segment average approaches its starting value

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointJointTimePro.text: Let $U$ be a subspace with an orthogonal projection and let $Q$ be a continuous real-linear map. If $Q$ is symmetric and preserves $U$, then $Q$ commutes with the orthogonal projection onto $U$. No idempotence assumption on $Q$ is needed. Symmetry also preserves the orthogonal complement, which proves the identity.

This auxiliary result equips the endpoint submodule with an orthogonal projection. It first obtains completeness from the closedness of the endpoint space (weakly solenoidal fields with zero time integral), then uses the Hilbert-space projection theorem. The subspace already contains both endpoint constraints. This result supplies the operator's existence in the formalization, rather than a formula for its action or a regularity estimate.

This private instance gives the joint solenoidal submodule an orthogonal projection. Its closedness makes it complete as a subspace of joint $L^2$, after which the standard Hilbert-space instance applies. The declaration constructs typeclass evidence for every T; it neither adds an extra divergence assumption nor chooses a smooth representative.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointJointTimePro.summary: Orthogonal projection onto the solenoidal space

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointJointTimePro.text: For an $L^2$ time path f, the fixed-label mean-removal operator agrees almost everywhere with $f(t)-T^{-1}\int f$. The theorem is valid for any real T, including an empty measured interval. It provides the representative formula used when comparing mean removal before and after embedding a spatial Hölder family of paths.

This private definition places a spatial $L^2$ field in the joint time–torus space by making it independent of time. The measure is Lebesgue measure restricted to $(0,T]$ times normalized Haar measure. The input v is an equivalence class, so the displayed formula specifies a representative only almost everywhere. No sign condition on T is required to construct this class.

The joint $L^2$ element constructed from v agrees almost everywhere with $(t,a)\mapsto v(a)$. Equality is with respect to the product measure, and is not a pointwise identity of the selected representatives. This is the evaluation fact used to identify the adjoint of time integration by testing inner products.

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointJointWordReg.text: Packages evaluation of a half-Hölder field along $a+\pi(ru)$, with $\pi:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb T^3$ the quotient map, as a bounded continuous function of the real parameter $r$. The resulting map is continuous linear in the field. This allows convergence in the half-Hölder norm to imply uniform convergence along the line when interchanging time and spatial differentiation.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointJointWordReg.summary: A field viewed along an entire torus line

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointJointWordReg.text: Evaluating the torus-line map at $s$ gives the original field at the translated label. This is a definitional identity, valid for arbitrary directions and parameters. It removes the bounded-continuous-function packaging in the proof that limits of temporal difference quotients preserve spatial derivative relations.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointJointWordReg.summary: The line operator evaluates the original field

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointJointWordReg.text: Packages a half-Hölder torus field as a bounded continuous function on Euclidean three-space by composing with the quotient map. The construction is continuous linear and retains the field’s periodic values. It provides a normed target in which time differentiation can be combined with spatial evaluation for the joint smoothness proof.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointJointWordReg.summary: The bounded periodic lift of a spatial field

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointJointWordReg.text: The bounded Euclidean lift of a half-Hölder field evaluates at $x\in\mathbb R^3$ to that field's value at the torus point $\pi(x)$. The statement is a definitional equality and holds with no smoothness assumptions. It lets the joint-derivative proof replace the packaged lift by the manuscript's periodic spatial function.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointJointWordReg.summary: The lifted word is evaluation at the quotient label

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointJointWordReg.text: A time derivative in the norm of bounded continuous functions, together with a spatial Fréchet derivative at the evaluation point, yields the joint derivative on the time-set product. Its linear map adds the time component and the spatial component. The uniform function norm controls the cross term, so separate pointwise differentiability alone would not supply this conclusion.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointJointWordReg.summary: Combining time and spatial derivatives of evaluation

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointJointWordReg.text: Each standard coordinate direction in the three-dimensional Euclidean space has norm one. This normalization is used in the coordinate-path proof reconstructing a Fréchet derivative from line derivatives. It depends on the Euclidean norm of $\mathbb R^3$, not on a derivative or regularity assumption about the field itself.

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointL2Coercivity.text: Continuity of an operator field on $[0,T]$ supplies an almost-everywhere norm bound for the measure restricted to $(0,T]$. Compactness supplies the constant, and the restricted measure is supported inside the closed interval. No positivity of $T$ is assumed here; an empty restricted interval makes the almost-everywhere assertion vacuous.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointL2Coercivity.summary: A continuous time coefficient is essentially bounded

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointL2Multiplier.text: Bundle evaluation of a continuous linear operator on a vector as a continuous bilinear map. Its two arguments are the operator and the vector, in that order. This allows Mathlib's Hölder construction to multiply an essentially bounded operator field by an $L^2$ vector field and obtain an $L^2$ output.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointL2Multiplier.summary: Operator evaluation as a bounded bilinear map

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMeanFubini.0.text: The partial integral becomes a real linear map from joint $L^2$ to spatial $L^2$. Addition and scalar multiplication are verified using Fubini to pass product almost-everywhere identities to almost every time path. This quotient-level argument prevents the definition from depending on arbitrary values along exceptional fibers.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMeanFubini.0.summary: Partial time integration is linear on product classes

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMeanFubini.0.text: For a joint $L^2$ field on a nonnegative time interval, the spatial $L^2$ norm of its partial time integral is at most $\sqrt T$ times the joint norm. Cauchy–Schwarz is applied along almost every label path and then integrated in labels. This proves continuity of the linear partial-integral map.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMeanFubini.0.summary: Partial integration costs the square root of duration

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMeanFubini.0.text: Given a joint time-label $L^2$ class on a nonnegative interval, integrate its representative in time at each label and bundle the resulting label function into spatial $L^2$. The membership theorem justifies this construction. Subsequent identities are almost everywhere in labels, because representatives may differ on exceptional fibers.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMeanFubini.0.summary: The time integral represented in spatial L²

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMeanFubini.0.text: A representative of the spatial $L^2$ value equals the time integral of the joint representative for almost every label. This is the exact representative guarantee for passing from a square-integrable function to its $L^2$ class, with the exceptional set measured by $\nu$. It does not assert that every individual label fiber has an integrable or canonical representative.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMeanFubini.0.summary: The spatial quotient agrees with the partial time integral

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMeanFubini.0.text: For an $L^2$ equivalence class on an arbitrary measure space, its norm squared equals the integral of the squared norm of its representative. This general identity is independent of the time-product setting. It allows the partial-integral proof to compare input and output norms after applying Fubini and Cauchy–Schwarz.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMeanFubini.0.summary: Any L² norm squared equals its integral energy

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedConcret.text: Any two labels in the unit three-torus are at distance at most one for the product metric used here. The proof bounds each circle coordinate by half its period and then uses the product distance estimate. This geometric bound converts spatial Lipschitz control into the half-Hölder control needed for the half-Hölder coefficient space.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedConcret.summary: The unit label torus has bounded diameter

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedConcret.text: On the unit label torus, a nonnegative spatial Lipschitz constant $L$ also bounds increments by $L\sqrt{\operatorname{dist}(a,b)}$. The proof uses the torus diameter bound to compare distance with its square root. The estimate is uniform in time only because the Lipschitz bound for $K$ is assumed at every time in the slab.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedConcret.summary: Lipschitz control gives half-Hölder control on labels

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedConcret.text: A uniform pointwise bound $C$ for $K$ yields the same operator-norm bound for its temporal multiplier at each label. The other bound $M$ and the increment hypothesis are used only to construct the mixed half-Hölder coefficient. The independent parameter $C$ permits a sharper supremum estimate than the combined construction budget.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedConcret.summary: A pointwise coefficient bound controls each path operator

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedConcret.text: If every fixed-label time slice of a coefficient is continuous on $[0,T]$, each slice is almost-everywhere strongly measurable for the measure on $(0,T]$. Compactness and restriction to a measurable subinterval supply the result. This converts the coefficient regularity into the measurability required by the temporal $L^2$ construction.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedConcret.summary: Continuous label slices define measurable path multipliers

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedConcret.text: A coefficient continuous jointly on the closed time-label slab gives a continuous time curve when the label is fixed. The proof composes with the map $t\mapsto(t,a)$ and checks that it stays inside the slab. This supplies the temporal multiplier hypotheses for every label without an almost-everywhere restriction.

Bounds the difference between $M^*-M$ and $N^*-N$ by $2\|M-N\|$. The proof rewrites that difference as the skew part of $M-N$ and applies the preceding norm estimate. It transfers a spatial modulus for the velocity gradient to its skew part.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedConcret.summary: Differences of skew parts have the same factor two

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedConcret.text: Bounds the norm of $M^*-M$ by $2\|M\|$ on a complete real Hilbert space. This follows from the triangle inequality and the isometry of adjoint. It controls the unpulled vorticity coefficient before multiplying on both sides by the deformation.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedConcret.summary: The skew part is bounded by twice the gradient

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedConcret.text: Bounds $\|UB-CD\|$ by $\|U-C\|\|B\|+\|C\|\|B-D\|$ for continuous linear operators. The proof inserts the intermediate product $CB$ and uses submultiplicativity. This elementary inequality supplies the spatial difference estimates for the kinetic and pulled-back vorticity coefficients in the mean inverse.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedConcret.summary: A product difference splits into two errors

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedEmbeddi.text: Suppose the time path $f(a)$ agrees with the joint field $v$ almost everywhere in time for almost every label $a$. Then the squared joint norm equals the Haar integral of the squared path norms. Fubini applies to the already square-integrable joint field; the conclusion does not assume arbitrary pointwise representatives are jointly measurable.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedEmbeddi.summary: Joint energy is the integral of the path energies

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedEmbeddi.text: Given slice representations of two joint fields by path families $f$ and $g$, the path difference represents their joint difference almost everywhere in both variables. The proof tracks the representative rules for subtraction in each $L^2$ space. This permits joint norm differences to be estimated through labelwise path differences.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedEmbeddi.summary: Subtraction agrees between joint fields and their path slices

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedEmbeddi.text: Select a joint L² realization of the half-Hölder path field using the proved existence theorem. The choice is noncomputable, but slice agreement determines the joint equivalence class uniquely. This intermediate value is later shown linear and bounded before it is packaged as the mixed-to-joint continuous linear map.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedEmbeddi.summary: Choose the joint realization of a mixed field

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedEmbeddi.text: The selected joint $L^2$ field agrees with the mixed field's time paths almost everywhere in time at almost every label. This is the defining property of the field chosen from the existence theorem. It is the only representative specification needed for the later norm, linearity, and embedding compatibility proofs.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedEmbeddi.summary: The chosen joint field realizes the mixed time paths

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedEmbeddi.text: Every spatial half-Hölder field with values in time L² admits a joint L² realization with the prescribed paths almost everywhere in labels and time. Continuity provides strong measurability and the half-Hölder norm bounds all path norms. The theorem supplies existence before the next definition selects a realization.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedEmbeddi.summary: A half Hölder family of paths has a joint realization

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedEmbeddi.text: For a real vector time path, its squared $L^2$ norm equals the time integral of the squared pointwise norm over the restricted interval. This Hilbert-space identity is used to compare slice energies with joint energy. It holds for all real $T$, including the trivial space obtained from an empty interval.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedEmbeddi.summary: Time path energy equals the squared L² norm

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedEmbeddi.text: For a simple function $s$ from labels to time $L^2$, form the joint representative $(t,a)\mapsto s(a)(t)$ and prove it square integrable using the uniform bound on $s$. Finite simple-function structure supplies joint measurability. This construction starts the approximation of continuous path-valued fields without assuming representatives vary measurably for arbitrary families.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedEmbeddi.summary: A bounded simple family of paths gives a joint field

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedEmbeddi.text: For almost every label, the time slice of the joint field built from a bounded simple family $s$ agrees almost everywhere with the path selected by $s$. This is the representative guarantee of the initial simple-function construction. It allows norm comparisons and Cauchy estimates to be made in terms of the original path-valued simple functions.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedEmbeddi.summary: The joint simple field has the prescribed paths

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedEmbeddi.text: If $f$ and $g$ are strongly measurable label-to-path maps bounded by the same $M$, the squared path-norm difference is Haar integrable. The bound $(M+M)^2$ provides an integrable constant majorant because Haar measure has finite mass. This prepares dominated convergence for the simple approximations.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedEmbeddi.summary: Bounded measurable path families have integrable squared differences

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedEmbeddi.text: A strongly measurable family of $L^2$ time paths, uniformly bounded by a nonnegative $M$, has a joint $L^2$ field realizing its slices almost everywhere. The proof constructs a Cauchy sequence from bounded simple approximations, takes its joint $L^2$ limit, and compares subsequences in measure. It does not assert a pointwise representative identity at every label.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedEmbeddi.summary: A bounded measurable family admits a joint L² realization

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedEmbeddi.text: For a strongly measurable family $f$ bounded by a nonnegative $M$, its standard bounded simple approximations have integrated squared path error tending to zero. An equality hypothesis identifies the exact approximation sequence. Dominated convergence uses their shared bound, rather than assuming uniform convergence in the label variable.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedEmbeddi.summary: Bounded simple approximations converge in integrated path energy

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedEmbeddi.text: The joint L² norm of the chosen realization is bounded by the half-Hölder norm of the path-valued field. Slice energy gives the joint norm as an integral over labels, and each path norm is bounded by the mixed norm. Normalized Haar mass one prevents an additional volume constant.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedEmbeddi.summary: Joint realization does not increase the mixed norm

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedOperato.text: The uniform spatial half-Hölder coefficient estimate implies continuity of the label-to-time-operator map in operator norm. The proof squeezes the norm difference by $M\sqrt{d(a,b)}$. This conclusion is continuity in the spatial label; the construction does not require or establish operator dependence on a varying terminal time.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedOperato.summary: The path operator family is continuous in the label

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedOperato.text: For a fixed label, form the bounded time $L^2$ multiplication operator associated with $t\mapsto K(t,a)$. The hypotheses supply time measurability and a uniform slab bound. Spatial regularity is not needed to define this individual operator; it is needed later to assemble the family over labels.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedOperato.summary: A coefficient at one label multiplies time paths

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedOperato.text: Fix a label $a$. The uniform coefficient bound on the closed slab implies $\|K(t,a)\|\le M$ for almost every time under the restricted measure. The statement uses only the slab bound, not spatial Hölder continuity. It supplies essential boundedness for the labelwise time $L^2$ multiplier.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedOperato.summary: A slab bound gives an almost everywhere path coefficient bound

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedOperato.text: Applying the time-path coefficient at label $a$ agrees almost everywhere with $K(t,a)f(t)$. The theorem identifies the representative of the induced $L^2$ multiplier. It retains the explicit measurability and slab-bound inputs used in its construction, without assuming continuity in time.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedOperato.summary: The path operator multiplies by the given time coefficient

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedOperato.text: Assuming $M\ge0$, the time-path multiplier at each label has operator norm at most $M$. The bound is obtained from the pointwise coefficient bound on the closed slab. It is uniform in the label and involves no factor depending on the interval length.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedOperato.summary: The path multiplier inherits the slab coefficient bound

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedOperato.text: Assuming $\|K(t,a)-K(t,b)\|\le M\sqrt{d(a,b)}$ on the slab, the difference of the time-path multipliers at labels $a$ and $b$ has operator norm at most $M\sqrt{d(a,b)}$. The proof compares their actions on an arbitrary $L^2$ path almost everywhere in time. Nonnegative $M$ makes this a valid half-Hölder bound on the operator-valued family.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedOperato.summary: Spatial coefficient increments control path operator increments

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedProject.text: The projection from joint time-label space onto its time coordinate is measure preserving. Normalized torus Haar measure has total mass one, so adding or removing that independent label variable does not rescale the time measure. This permits a time L² path to be lifted isometrically to the joint space.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedProject.summary: Forgetting the torus label preserves the time measure

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedProject.text: For $v$ in the weak endpoint space, an inserted spatial character with a constant vector time amplitude has zero pairing with $v$. Fubini reduces the inner product to the time integral of $v$ at each label, which vanishes. No transversality of the constant amplitude is needed for this orthogonality.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedProject.summary: Constant time amplitudes are orthogonal to endpoint fields

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedProject.text: The joint $L^2$ inner product of an inserted character-path mode with $v$ equals the integral of their explicit pointwise pairing. The formula uses the insertion representative identity and the definition of the $L^2$ inner product. It is the starting point for separating time-mean and longitudinal contributions.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedProject.summary: Pairing an inserted mode is a joint integral

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedProject.text: If the path amplitude is almost everywhere a scalar multiple of the spatial frequency, its inserted real-character mode pairs to zero with every endpoint-constrained field. The character times the frequency is a smooth gradient, so the weak divergence tests apply at almost every time. This handles the longitudinal complement of the projection.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedProject.summary: Longitudinal amplitudes are orthogonal to solenoidal endpoint fields

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedProject.text: A time path $w$ produces a joint field in the weak endpoint space when $w$ has zero time integral and is almost everywhere orthogonal to the selected spatial frequency. The first condition enforces the terminal displacement constraint; the second supplies every weak gradient test. No positivity assumption on $T$ is needed for this implication.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedProject.summary: Zero mean transverse paths give admissible joint modes

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedProject.text: At a joint point, multiply the identity operator on real three-vectors by the value of a fixed continuous spatial character. The coefficient depends only on the label, not time. It is the bounded multiplication field used to insert a time path as a separated spatial Fourier mode.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedProject.summary: A spatial character acts as scalar multiplication

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedProject.text: The scalar identity coefficient associated with a continuous spatial character is almost-everywhere strongly measurable for the joint measure. It is continuous as a function of the label coordinate and constant in time. This provides the measurability certificate required by the L² multiplier used in mode insertion.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedProject.summary: The character weight is measurable in time and space

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedProject.text: For each real Fourier character there is a smooth periodic potential whose gradient equals that character times the real frequency vector. The construction divides by $2\pi i$, with its nonzero proof supplied explicitly. At zero frequency the requested gradient is zero, so no division by the frequency itself is needed.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedProject.summary: A character times its frequency is a smooth gradient

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedProject.text: The explicit joint function pairing a character times a time path with a joint L² field is integrable. This follows from the L² inner-product integrability theorem after replacing the inserted mode by its almost-everywhere representative. The certificate justifies the Fubini rearrangements used in the orthogonality arguments.

The operator norm of the character weight is at most the continuous character’s supremum norm almost everywhere in the joint measure. The proof uses the norm bound for the identity and pointwise evaluation of a continuous map. This is essential boundedness for the separated-mode insertion map.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedProject.summary: The character norm bounds the coefficient multiplier

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedProject.text: If the real vector $z$ is orthogonal to the frequency vector, the Haar pairing of its character-weighted wave with any smooth potential gradient is zero. The proof embeds the amplitude into the complex transverse mode space. This connects a finite-dimensional transversality condition with the weak real solenoidal tests.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedProject.summary: A transverse real Fourier mode annihilates every gradient

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedProject.text: A real spatial $L^2$ field is zero if all its cosine and sine Fourier moments vanish. The proof tests each real coordinate, combines both moment families into complex Fourier coefficients, and uses uniqueness of the $L^2$ Fourier expansion. Both the cosine and the sine hypotheses are required; one family alone does not separate arbitrary fields.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedProject.summary: Cosine and sine moments determine a real L² field

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedSource..text: A temporal $L^2$ path bounded almost everywhere by $C$ has norm at most $\sqrt T\,C$ when both $T$ and $C$ are nonnegative. The factor comes from the measure of $(0,T]$. This supplies the duration dependence when a continuous spatial source is represented as a Hölder field of time paths.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedSource..summary: A bounded path gains a square-root time factor

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedTimeRec.text: Slicing the joint field $u-v+w$ in space equals the corresponding combination of the three spatial slices for almost every time. Because $L^2$ elements use representatives, the proof also combines the almost-everywhere identities for addition and subtraction. This bookkeeping step permits the weak residual equation to be read one time slice at a time.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMixedTimeRec.summary: Spatial slicing respects subtraction and addition almost everywhere

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMomentum.0.T.text: For a continuous $f$ on $[0,T]$ and $t$ in that interval, its primitive from zero has derivative $f(t)$ within the same interval. The statement covers the endpoints by using derivatives within the interval. It supplies the fundamental theorem of calculus step when differentiating the integrated label momentum equation.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointMomentum.0.T.summary: Differentiate the time primitive within the closed interval

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalInve.text: The distance between two points of the product unit torus is at most one. The proof uses the coordinatewise metric and the half-period bound on each circle. This is a coarse diameter estimate used to convert a torus Lipschitz bound into a half-Hölder bound; it is not the Euclidean cube's diagonal length.

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalJetD.text: For nonnegative duration and bound $C$, a temporal path bounded almost everywhere by $C$ has $L^2$ norm at most $\sqrt T\,C$. This local copy of the finite-measure estimate is used for source-jet difference quotients. It supplies the duration factor missing from a mere pointwise remainder estimate.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalJetD.summary: A uniform source bound controls its temporal L² norm

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalJetD.text: Translating the entire slab by a space-time vector with zero time component leaves the set unchanged. The spatial factor is all Euclidean space, so only the time coordinate constrains membership. This elementary set identity allows within-slab derivative congruence to respect lattice translations.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalJetD.summary: Spatial translations leave the closed slab unchanged

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalJetE.text: Applying a slab derivative word whose letters have been mapped by $d$ is exactly the same as differentiating the original word with the direction family precomposed by $d$. The recursive identity carries no smoothness assumptions. It aligns the geometric jet-data indexing with the coordinate words used by the finite norms.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalJetE.summary: Relabelling directions relabels the derivative word

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalJetE.text: If $df$ is the torus directional derivative of $f$, then $-df$ is that derivative of $-f$. The assertion follows by negating the derivative identity along every torus line. It transfers the sign in the integrated source $L=-\int g$ to each spatial derivative word.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalJetE.summary: Negation preserves the torus derivative relation

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalJetE.text: Two half-Hölder fields satisfying the same torus directional derivative relation for a common field and direction are equal. Evaluating the line-derivative identities at parameter zero gives pointwise uniqueness, and extensionality gives equality of fields. This identifies the differentiated source with the prescribed force derivative in the primitive argument.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalJetE.summary: A torus directional derivative has unique values

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalJetE.text: The norm of a sum indexed by a finite list is bounded by the sum of the norms of its entries. The target needs only a normed additive structure. Here it controls the list of differentiated coefficient corrections without dropping the multiplicities coming from repeated derivative directions.

The kinetic correction sum plus $T$ times the vorticity correction sum equals a single list sum of the word costs $2(\|K_q\|+T\|\Omega_q\|)$, with closed-time half-Hölder norms of the kinetic and vorticity words $q$. This is an exact algebraic rearrangement, with no continuity or positivity assumptions. It puts the two analytic estimates into the form required by the common derivative recurrence.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalJetE.summary: Combine the two correction sums into one cost

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalMean.text: Restricting a jointly smooth field to one time in the closed slab gives a globally smooth function of the spatial variable. The result is polymorphic in the normed target space and requires no spatial periodicity. It supplies the slice regularity used to compare derivative-word norms of the recovered mean.

An exact polynomial identity rewrites the nested product from the mean estimate into an order-dependent factor times $R d^2 f$. It holds for arbitrary real arguments, without sign assumptions. The purpose is to identify the defined finite order constant before applying the separate inequality that bounds inverse and radius losses by a power of $D$.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalMean.summary: Separate the scalar factors in the mean bound

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalMean.text: Composes a jointly smooth time-space field with the map that fixes time and negates space. The closed time slab is invariant under this map, so smoothness within that slab is preserved. This helper does not extend the field smoothly beyond the time endpoints or impose a reflection parity.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalMean.summary: Spatial reflection preserves smoothness on the time slab

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalMean.text: For a differentiable vector field, the divergence of its odd part at $x$ is half the sum of the original divergences at $x$ and $-x$. Taking the trace of the derivative formula proves the identity. In particular, a divergence-free field retains that property when its odd component is selected.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalMean.summary: The divergence of the odd part is the even divergence

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalMean.text: Restricts joint smoothness on the closed time-space slab to a fixed time $t$ in the slab. Since the spatial factor is all Euclidean space, the resulting slice is globally smooth in space. The membership hypothesis matters: smoothness on the slab says nothing about slices outside its time interval.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalMean.summary: A smooth slab field has smooth spatial slices

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalMean.text: For any real-valued function, the integral of its reflected version over the centered cell equals the original integral. Negation preserves volume and the cell itself. The statement uses the total Bochner integral convention, so it does not by itself certify integrability; the pressure-normalization application supplies continuity on the compact cell.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalMean.summary: Reflection preserves the integral over the centered cell

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalMean.text: Identifies the Euclidean lattice vector of the negated integer index with the negative of the original lattice vector. The proof is coordinatewise, using integer-cast negation. This allows the reflected field’s periodicity to use the original periodicity statement with the lattice index replaced by its negative.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalMean.summary: Integer lattice negation agrees with spatial negation

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalMean.text: Shows that the inverse image of the centered fundamental cube under spatial negation is the same cube. Each coordinate interval is symmetric about zero. This geometric identity is used in the measure-preserving change of variables that keeps the pressure mean unchanged when selecting its even component.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalMean.summary: The centered fundamental cell is reflection invariant

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalMean.text: Assuming differentiability at both $x$ and $-x$, computes the derivative of the reflection average. The reflected derivative gains a minus sign from the chain rule, producing the coefficient $-\varepsilon$. This explicit derivative later yields the formulas for divergence and the gradient of the selected pressure.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalMean.summary: A spatial derivative reverses the reflection sign

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalMean.text: If both vectors have norm at most $D$ and the sign has absolute value at most one, their signed half-average also has norm at most $D$. The triangle inequality proves the result. The hypotheses themselves force a compatible nonnegative bound; no independent assumption $D\ge0$ is required.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalMean.summary: A signed average does not increase a common norm bound

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalMean.text: Given bounded sets of pointwise norms and half-Hölder quotients, proves boundedness of the corresponding sets after reflection averaging and bounds both real suprema by their originals. The bounded-above hypotheses are essential because a real supremum of an unbounded set is assigned the value zero. The zero-displacement quotient is handled separately, without dividing by a positive number there.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalMean.summary: The spatial suprema remain finite under parity selection

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalMean.text: If the lifted velocity is infinitely differentiable on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3$, its within-slab derivative in the time direction is infinitely differentiable there too. The strict inequality $T>0$ supplies unique differentiation on the interval. This is the regularity input for the label momentum pressure recovered from the differentiated equation.

Restricting a jointly continuous velocity on the closed slab to a fixed spatial point gives a continuous time curve on $[0,T]$. The inclusion map sends each admissible time into the product slab. This supplies the elementary continuity hypothesis needed to differentiate the primitive of the pulled-back force.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalMean.summary: A continuous force has continuous time slices

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalMean.text: Two continuous half-Hölder curves representing the same mixed field almost everywhere in time agree at every point of $[0,T]$. Their primitives coincide by the two representation identities. Differentiating those equal primitives within the nondegenerate interval removes the exceptional-time ambiguity, including at both endpoints.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalMean.summary: Continuous representatives agree at every slab time

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalMean.text: Packages integration of continuous vector functions on $[0,1]$ as a continuous linear map with operator norm at most one. The function is extended to the real line by clamping the argument to $[0,1]$; the integral only sees the original interval. This bounded map lets the joint primitive proof differentiate a curve of continuous functions.

Evaluating a solenoidal half-Hölder field through the torus quotient gives a periodic function on the Euclidean lift. The curve $g$ is arbitrary and no time regularity is assumed. Integer translation leaves the torus point $\pi(x)$ unchanged, so periodicity holds for every real time, including times outside the interval used by the mean solver.

For a continuous solenoidal curve $g$ and $t\in[0,T]$, evaluating its Banach-valued primitive at a torus label equals integrating the evaluated vector velocity. Continuity provides interval integrability, and the solenoidal subspace is complete because it is closed. This identity transfers the abstract zero endpoint primitives to the actual displacement field.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalMean.summary: Integrating before evaluating gives the same displacement

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalMean.text: If evaluating the $C^1$ half-Hölder source curve gives minus the primitive of a continuous vector function, evaluating its within-interval derivative gives the negative of that function. The evaluation identity is required at all slab times. Strict positivity of $T$ identifies the two within derivatives, including at the endpoints.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalMean.summary: The integrated force differentiates to its negative

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalMean.text: A derivative of the solenoidal half-Hölder curve $g$ within $[0,T]$ evaluates to the time derivative of its lifted velocity at any fixed spatial point. Evaluation composed with the inclusion of the solenoidal subspace is a continuous linear map. The assumption is an explicitly given derivative; this lemma does not infer differentiability from an arbitrary curve.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalMean.summary: Time differentiation commutes with label evaluation

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalMean.text: For a velocity jointly smooth on the closed slab, its time derivative at fixed position is the within-slab Fréchet derivative applied to $(1,0)$. The hypothesis that $t$ lies in the slab keeps the base point on the slab. The conclusion is a derivative within the slab, so it includes one-sided endpoint derivatives and does not assert an extension to an open time interval.

A coefficient family with a uniform spatial Lipschitz bound induces mixed time-path operators with the same bound. A hypothesis identifies each operator action almost everywhere with pointwise multiplication by the time slice. The proof uses the $L^2$ multiplication estimate, so no pointwise representative is selected for a general path.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalMean.summary: Spatial Lipschitz bounds lift to path operators

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalMean.text: From actual physical jet data, deformation evolution, inverse bounds and $H^\#\le I$, this helper constructs a jointly smooth label velocity with zero endpoint primitive. It also returns the kinetic and mixed coercivity estimates, with constants $D^{-2}$ and $[2D^2(1+L)^2]^{-1}$, and all finite recovered-word families. The hypotheses include $0<T\le1$, $D\ge1$ and $L\ge0$.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalMean.summary: Physical coefficient jets recover the endpoint velocity

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalTime.text: Assume a jointly continuous bounded coefficient, exact agreement with its strong half-Hölder time representation, and the prescribed mixed path action. The mixed coefficient applied to a field then agrees on almost every time slice with the weak spatial multiplier. This is an almost-everywhere identity; continuous time recovery is a separate step.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPhysicalTime.summary: Identify the multiplier on almost every spatial slice

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPressureReco.text: The real Lebesgue volume of the centered periodic cell is exactly one. This follows from the product of three intervals of length one, with the Euclidean-coordinate measure normalization. The identity makes a zero-mean pressure equal to its average difference from its values on that cell.

The map sending a Euclidean displacement to the translated continuous torus field is continuous in the supremum norm. Compactness of the torus lets joint continuity give continuity into the continuous-function space. This result concerns continuous fields, avoiding the stronger and generally different issue of translation continuity in the full Hölder norm.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPressureReco.summary: Continuous fields vary continuously under translation

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPressureReco.text: The quotient map from Euclidean vectors to three unit circles is continuous. The proof combines continuity of each coordinate map with continuity of the circle quotient. This basic topological fact lets the convolution argument treat translated torus fields as continuous functions of their Euclidean translation parameter.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPressureReco.summary: The periodic quotient is continuous in every coordinate

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPressureReco.text: For positive $\Lambda$, evaluating the continuous-field kernel average at the image of $x$ in the torus equals convolution of the periodic lift with the scaled kernel. The argument commutes evaluation with the vector-valued integral and changes variables by the dilation. Positivity of the scale justifies the inverse and the three-dimensional Jacobian factor.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPressureReco.summary: Identify the kernel average with the scaled lifted convolution

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPressureReco.text: If the complex kernel $K$ is continuous and integrable, its scalar product with any rescaled translation of $g$ is integrable as a function with values in continuous fields. The uniform shift norm bound gives the majorant $|K(y)|\,\|g\|$. The real scale $a$ is unrestricted here; no division by that scale occurs.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPressureReco.summary: An integrable kernel dominates the translated field integral

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPressureReco.text: Assuming $\Lambda>0$, integrating $\Lambda^3 f(\Lambda y)$ over three-dimensional space gives the integral of $f$. The positive scale fixes the Jacobian factor and permits the change of variables. This is the normalization used to relate the fixed kernel approximate identity to the scaled convolution in the cutoff construction.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPressureReco.summary: A positive dilation preserves the normalized kernel integral

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPressureReco.text: For a continuous integrable complex kernel of integral one, and scales $a_n$ tending to zero, the kernel average of translated copies of $g$ converges to $g$ in the continuous-function norm. Completeness of the target supports the vector-valued integral. Dominated convergence uses the shift bound; no positivity of the kernel is required.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPressureReco.summary: A mass one kernel recovers the field as shifts shrink

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPressureReco.text: Every translated continuous torus field has supremum norm bounded by the norm of $g$. The proof evaluates at an arbitrary label and uses the original global bound. This supplies a displacement-independent dominating function for the kernel integral, which is essential for the later dominated convergence argument.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPressureReco.summary: Translation does not enlarge the continuous field supremum

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPressureReco.text: This continuous torus field evaluates $g$ at $z-[y]$, where $[y]$ is the image of $y\in\mathbb R^3$ in the torus. The minus sign matches the convolution convention used for smoothing. Continuity is included in the constructed object. The definition applies to every displacement and makes no Fourier or differentiability claim by itself.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPressureReco.summary: Translate a continuous field by a Euclidean displacement

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPressureReco.text: At displacement zero, the shifted continuous torus field is exactly $g$. This follows from the quotient map sending zero to zero and the subtraction identity. In the approximate-identity argument it identifies the pointwise parameter limit of translations before dominated convergence is applied to the kernel integral.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPressureReco.summary: Zero displacement gives the original continuous field

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPressureReco.text: Embedding the complexified continuous field into complex $L^2$ gives the same class as complexifying its real $L^2$ embedding. The equality is verified through the almost-everywhere value formulas. It connects the continuous Fourier coefficients used for pressure reconstruction with the weak real Leray constraint.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPressureReco.summary: Complexification agrees before and after passage to Hilbert classes

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPressureReco.text: For every real spatial $L^2$ field, the Fourier-defined real Leray projector equals the ambient vector underlying the weak solenoidal orthogonal projection. The latter initially has a subtype-valued codomain. This identification transfers a vanishing weak projection into modewise statements about the Fourier pressure correction.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPressureReco.summary: The real Fourier projection is the weak spatial projection

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPressureReco.text: Multiplying a vector coefficient by a real scalar commutes with first taking its pressure correction and then its gradient mode. The identity holds for every mode and scalar, including the zero mode under its explicit convention. It lets a real-valued spectral cutoff preserve the modewise potential compatibility.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPressureReco.summary: Real cutoff weights preserve the gradient mode identity

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPressureReco.text: Every point in the centered three-dimensional cell has Euclidean norm at most one. Its three coordinates lie between minus one half and one half, so the squared norm is at most three quarters. The convenient bound one is used to control oscillations of a pressure on a representative cell.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPressureReco.summary: The centered cell lies in the unit Euclidean ball

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPrimitive.0..text: Bundle the primitive construction as a real linear map on $L^2$ velocities. The proof checks addition and scalar multiplication through almost-everywhere representatives and uses invariance of integrals under null-set changes. Continuity is supplied in the next construction from its quantitative norm bound, rather than assumed in this linear-map definition.

For every $L^2$ input on a nonnegative interval, the linear primitive map has output norm at most $T$ times the input norm. This follows by taking square roots of the integral estimate. It supplies a valid continuity constant even at $T=0$, when the quotient domain is trivial.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPrimitive.0..summary: The primitive operator grows at most linearly with duration

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPrimitive.0..text: Given an $L^2$ velocity on a nonnegative interval, form its anchored primitive and bundle that function into the same $L^2$ space using the established integrability proof. The construction selects the quotient class of the continuous primitive. Equality with a displayed representative is subsequently stated almost everywhere.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPrimitive.0..summary: The primitive represented as an L² equivalence class

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPrimitive.0..text: A representative of the $L^2$ class formed from the anchored primitive equals the anchored integral of the input representative almost everywhere on the time interval. The equality is measure-relative, as is any statement about a representative of an $L^2$ class. It does not select or promise a canonical pointwise representative at every time.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPrimitive.0..summary: The bundled primitive agrees almost everywhere with its formula

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPrimitive.0..text: For a square-integrable velocity on $[0,T]$, the squared $L^2$ norm of its primitive is bounded by $T^2$ times the velocity's squared $L^2$ norm. This general estimate does not require zero terminal mean and is not the sharper endpoint Poincaré factor from Lemma 4.1. It suffices to bundle the primitive as a bounded operator.
_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPrimitive.0..summary: Time integration is bounded by the slab length

_private.TorusEuler.EndpointPrimitive.0..text: For an $L^2$ equivalence class on the restricted time measure and nonnegative $T$, its norm squared equals the interval integral of the squared norm of its chosen representative.
