The flow equation supplies the derivative used in the estimate. This statement needs a velocity bound, not a spatial derivative bound.

_private.TorusEuler.LabelVariational.0.T.text: If two real times $s,t$ lie in the same closed interval $[l,r]$, their absolute difference is at most its length $r-l$. This elementary estimate replaces trajectory-dependent elapsed times by one bound valid throughout the slab in the subsequent flow regularity arguments.

A field satisfying $V(b+n)=V(b)$ for every $b$ and every $n\in\mathbb Z^3$ has the same Fréchet derivative at $a$ and at $a+n$. No differentiability assumption is needed for this equality of the formal total derivative values, which are zero where the field is not differentiable. The result transports derivative bounds from a compact label cell to the periodic lift.

When the initial size is zero, multiplying the forcing parameter $\varepsilon$ of the Grönwall bound $\varepsilon(e^{Kt}-1)/K$ (or $\varepsilon t$ when $K=0$) by $c$ multiplies its value by $c$. This is an algebraic identity for all real arguments, including the separate zero-growth-rate branch. It lets the variational argument factor out a squared label increment without adding positivity hypotheses.

For nonnegative growth rate $K$, forcing size $D$, and elapsed time $d$, the Grönwall bound starting from zero is nonnegative. This positivity fact supports later products and monotonicity estimates. It concerns the explicit bounding expression and does not itself construct a solution to a differential equation.

With nonnegative $K$ and $D$, a curve on $[l,r]$ with $f(l)=0$, derivative within the interval at every point, and $\|f'\|\le K\|f\|+D$ is bounded at every time $t$ of the slab by the Grönwall value at its full length $r-l$. These hypotheses are explicit; monotonicity in elapsed time removes dependence on the particular time $t$.

The hypothesis gives differentiability of $V$ on the product of a closed time interval and all labels. At any allowed time $t$, fixing time yields an ordinary Fréchet derivative in the label variable. Its value is the within-domain derivative composed with the inclusion into the second factor, so no extension beyond the temporal endpoints is required.
_private.TorusEuler.LabelVariational.0.T.summary: Spatial differentiation of a slab-restricted function

_private.TorusEuler.LabelVariational.0.T.text: A derivative bound $\|f'\|\le K\|f\|+\varepsilon$ on $[l,r]$ and a size bound $\|f(s)\|\le\delta$ at any time $s$ of the interval control the curve at every time $t$ of the interval by the Grönwall bound with initial size $\delta$ and elapsed time $|t-s|$. The proof reverses time when necessary. The conclusion remains confined to the closed interval supplied by the derivative hypothesis.

For a vector-valued curve on a closed interval $[l,r]$, suppose it has a derivative within that interval at each point and the derivative is bounded by $K\|f\|+\varepsilon$. The initial bound $\|f(l)\|\le\delta$ then gives the corresponding Grönwall estimate at every time $t$ of the interval. Time elapsed is $t-l$, so this version starts specifically at the left endpoint.

For a differentiable map whose Fréchet derivative is Lipschitz with constant $L$, the error after subtracting the linear approximation at $x$ is at most $L\|y-x\|^2$. The estimate uses a segment in a closed ball. It supplies the quadratic error needed to identify the variational solution with the actual derivative of a flow.
_private.TorusEuler.LabelVariational.0.T.summary: A quadratic error after first differentiation

_private.TorusEuler.LaterPhysicalAmplifi.text: If the endpoint is $t_{\rm finish}=t_{\rm start}+2h$, the normalized window $2rh$ maps exactly to $t_{\rm finish}$, and its full interval maps into the physical slab. This variant keeps the endpoint as an explicit parameter. Rate positivity and monotonicity of the affine clock justify the cancellation and containment.
_private.TorusEuler.LaterPhysicalAmplifi.summary: An arbitrary named endpoint matches the normalized window

_private.TorusEuler.LaterPhysicalAmplifi.text: The actual comparison error is nonnegative because its suprema involve norms or absolute values and its denominators are the positive rate and first coupling. This private lemma does not supply an upper bound. It is used as a sign premise when the schedule makes the error small.
_private.TorusEuler.LaterPhysicalAmplifi.summary: The physical error expression is nonnegative

_private.TorusEuler.LaterPhysicalLeading.text: If a twisted profile agrees on the slab with a phase-independent field $f$ and has even joint reflection parity, then each slab slice of $f$ is even in the label. Evaluating the reflection identity at phase zero removes the phase reflection. The hypothesis identifying the profile’s values with $f$ on the slab is required to transfer the result to $f$.
_private.TorusEuler.LaterPhysicalLeading.summary: Even profile reflection implies even label slices

_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.text: An assertion $Q$ valid for every point of the centered label cell extends over the whole slab if it is preserved by the simultaneous lattice and carrier-phase shift $(a,s)\mapsto(a+n,s+k_*\cdot n)$. Each label is translated into the centered cell, and the phase is shifted back with it. No continuity of $Q$ is required.
_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.summary: Translate a cellwise assertion to every label

_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.text: Two twisted profiles are equal if they agree for all phases and slab times at labels in the centered cell. The preceding lattice-shift argument extends equality to all labels, and profile extensionality finishes the proof. This uses skew periodicity already contained in the profile types, not ordinary label periodicity at fixed phase.
_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.summary: Twisted profiles are determined by their centered cell

_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.text: Constructs a twisted hierarchy profile from a centered phase periodization that is smooth on the slab and from one-periodicity of the raw phase field. The periodic and skew-shift conditions follow from the periodization identities. Smoothness is an input hypothesis; this helper does not establish that an arbitrary raw field glues smoothly at cell faces.
_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.summary: Wrap a smooth periodized field into the profile space

_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.text: At $t\in[0,T]$, evaluating the wrapped profile returns the centered phase periodization of the raw field. The proof unwraps the smooth-profile construction on its defining slab. No corresponding equality is asserted outside that slab, where the profile representation uses zero regardless of the raw field’s values.
_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.summary: Recover the wrapped field inside the time slab

_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.text: Defines the unlocalized pressure profile using the negative pressure coefficient with envelope factor one and the periodic pressure primitive. This isolates the coefficient whose smoothness depends on the covector staying nonzero. Multiplication by the radial envelope, and then by the time cutoff, recover the actual leading pressure.
_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.summary: Leading pressure before multiplying by the envelope

_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.text: The regularity bundle gives smooth strain, covector, and amplitude, and a nonzero covector at every active point. These facts make the quotient by the squared covector norm smooth. Multiplication by the smooth pressure primitive then gives joint smoothness in time, label, and phase on $[t_0,T]$.
_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.summary: The unlocalized pressure is smooth on the active slab

_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.text: For $0<h\le1$, differentiating the switched leading pressure in phase gives the switched envelope and wave profile $\chi(t)g(a)W_h(s)$ times the oscillatory pressure slope with zero forcing, $-2\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a/|\kappa|^2$. The calculation uses that the pressure primitive differentiates to the wave profile. It is algebraic in the seed coefficients and has no time-slab restriction.
_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.summary: Differentiate the switched pressure in phase

_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.text: At a time in $[t_0,T]$, and with $0 < h \le  1$, the switched seed has within-time derivative equal to switch forcing minus strain and phase-pressure terms. The product rule combines the seed ODE with the switch derivative. This active-interval statement is later joined to the zero field before activation.
_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.summary: The active leading wave satisfies its time equation

_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.text: For a nonnegative switch rate and $t\le t_0$, the switched leading wave has derivative zero within the half-line $(-\infty,t_0]$. This follows because the switched wave is identically zero there. It is a one-sided derivative statement used to join the inactive interval to the active seed equation at activation.
_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.summary: The leading wave has zero left time derivative

_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.text: Under the hierarchy regularity conditions, the field formed by multiplying the seed amplitude by the phase profile $W_h(s)$ is smooth on the active time slab and all label-phase variables. The proof composes the seed’s joint smoothness with the coordinate projection and multiplies by the smooth scalar profile. The radial envelope and time cutoff are absent at this stage.
_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.summary: Smoothness of the seed times the phase profile

_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.text: Under the phase-scale conditions in the hierarchy regularity assumptions, the pressure primitive of the odd wave profile is even. The proof changes variables in the integral from zero to the reflected phase and uses oddness of the integrand. Subtracting the phase mean does not alter evenness.

For arbitrary time, label, and phase, the raw leading pressure equals the radial envelope $g(a)$ times the bare pressure $-c(\kappa,\mathbf a,M)\,\Pi_h(s)$, formed with envelope one. The proof only rearranges the scalar coefficient and multiplication. It imposes no positivity or nonvanishing assumption because it is an algebraic identity between the everywhere-defined formulas, not a regularity or PDE assertion.
_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.summary: Factor the envelope out of the leading pressure

_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.text: For a seed with the regularity bundle, the leading switch profile is one-periodic in phase. The derivative of the time cutoff and radial envelope are scalar factors independent of phase. Periodicity therefore follows from the chosen wave profile, regardless of the time or label at which the formula is evaluated.
_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.summary: The activation source has period one in phase

_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.text: For any real scalar and constant vector, the phase mean of their product with the wave profile $W_h$ is zero under the regularity conditions’ phase assumptions. The proof moves the continuous linear map through the interval integral and uses the scalar profile’s zero mean. This supplies the transverse input’s phase-average condition.
_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.summary: Scalar multiples of the wave profile have zero mean

_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.text: If every label slice of a raw field is one-periodic and has zero phase mean, its centered phase periodization also has zero mean at every label. At a fixed label, wrapping only changes the label representative and translates phase. Integration over a full period is invariant under that translation.
_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.summary: Centered phase wrapping preserves a zero mean

_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.text: A reflection identity established on the time slab gives the global reflection-parity predicate for a twisted profile. Reflection preserves slab membership; outside the slab both sides are zero by representation. This helper makes parity proofs on actual seed values sufficient without asserting any continuation of those values beyond the slab.
_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.summary: Extend a reflection law through the zero representation

_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.text: For a seed with the regularity bundle, the switched leading pressure is one-periodic in phase for every time and label. The cutoff and pressure coefficient are phase independent, so only periodicity of the pressure primitive is used. This statement does not require the time to lie in the active interval.
_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.summary: The leading pressure has period one in phase

_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.text: Proves joint slab smoothness for the periodized derivative-cutoff source. The derivative of the switch is itself smooth and vanishes through activation, so the flat-activation argument applies to it as well as to the switch. The radial envelope stays strictly inside the cell, allowing the label periodization to glue smoothly.
_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.summary: The wrapped activation source is smooth on the slab

_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.text: Uses the active seed’s smoothness, a flat nonnegative-rate switch, and an envelope strictly inside the centered cell to prove smoothness of the phase-periodized leading velocity on $[0,T]$. The localization handles cell faces while flat activation handles the time seam. This proves the input needed by the twisted-profile constructor.
_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.summary: The wrapped leading velocity is smooth on the slab

_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.text: Factors the leading pressure into the flat time switch, radial envelope, and smooth bare pressure, then applies the periodization theorem for flat activation. The envelope fitting condition handles the label-cell boundary. The conclusion is joint smoothness on the closed slab; it does not assert smoothness of the profile’s separate zero extension beyond $T$.
_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.summary: The wrapped leading pressure is smooth on the slab

_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.text: The centered closed label cell is a set of unique differentiability over the reals. It is convex and has nonempty interior, witnessed by a ball around the origin. This permits equal differentiable functions on that closed cell to have equal within derivatives even at its boundary, which is used for the completion formula.
_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.summary: The closed label cell determines derivatives uniquely

_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.text: For any covector $\kappa$, real scalar, and phase field $V$, applying the phase potential $\partial_s^{-1}(-|\kappa|^{-2}\kappa\times V)$ after scalar multiplication is the same as multiplying the potential by that scalar. The proof uses linearity of the cross product and of the mean-corrected phase primitive. No nonzero-covector or smoothness premise is needed for this algebraic identity.
_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.summary: A fixed scalar commutes with the phase potential

_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.text: Suppose a raw field vanishes when the label norm is at least $2 \cdot  \ell$, with $2 \cdot  \ell < 1/2$. At any label in the centered cell, its phase-centered periodization equals the raw field. The radial bound forces vanishing on the faces where the choice of centered representative could otherwise matter.
_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.summary: A localized field agrees with its centered wrapping

_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.text: The derivative of the time switch $\chi(t)$ is smooth on the real line for arbitrary $t_0$ and $r$. This uses the smoothness of the chosen switch and differentiation of a smooth real function. A nonnegative rate is unnecessary for this regularity statement, although it is needed for the subsequent vanishing-before-activation result.

For a nonnegative rate $r$ and $t\le t_0$, the ordinary derivative of the switch $\chi(t)=\psi(r(t-t_0))$, with $\psi$ the smooth transition, is zero. The proof compares its derivative on the left half-line with that of the constant zero function. Smoothness of the switch and unique differentiability of the half-line include the endpoint $t=t_0$.
_private.TorusEuler.LaterWaveHierarchyIn.summary: The switch derivative vanishes before activation

_private.TorusEuler.LaterWavePrimaryPres.text: For $D,b,\ell\ge1$ and nonnegative seed and pressure constants, bounds the expanded Hessian coefficient by a fixed prefactor times $D^{2a+74}$. Here $\ell$ is an auxiliary coefficient, not the envelope radius. The proof collects powers and uses monotonicity for $D\ge1$; it supplies no analytic pressure estimate by itself.

_private.TorusEuler.LinearFlowExistence..text: Assuming the initial time $t_0$ lies in $[a,b]$ and $K\ge0$, bounds every path value by $\|x(t_0)\|e^{K(b-a)}$. The derivative bound holds throughout the closed interval. Times before $t_0$ are handled by reversing time, so this is a two-sided compact-interval estimate rather than only a forward evolution bound.
_private.TorusEuler.LinearFlowExistence..summary: Uniform growth bound from any initial time

_private.TorusEuler.LinearFlowExistence..text: Assumes a path has within-interval derivative $d$ with $\|d(t)\|\le K\|x(t)\|$ on $[a,b]$. At each $t$ there it obtains $\|x(t)\|\le\|x(a)\|e^{K(t-a)}$ by Gronwall. No separate sign assumption on $K$ appears in this local statement. Membership of the queried time supplies the nonempty interval.
_private.TorusEuler.LinearFlowExistence..summary: Exponential growth bound from the left endpoint

_private.TorusEuler.LinearFlowExistence..text: For $R>0$, gives the two estimates $\|c_R(x)\|\le R$ and $\|c_R(x)\|\le\|x\|$ for the radial truncation $c_R(x)=Rx/\max(\|x\|,R)$. The first bounds the truncated ODE vector field uniformly; the second preserves the linear growth bound needed for Gronwall. Positivity makes the denominator strictly positive before either division estimate is used.
_private.TorusEuler.LinearFlowExistence..summary: Truncation bounds both radius and original size

_private.TorusEuler.LinearFlowExistence..text: Defines the auxiliary truncation $x\mapsto R x/\max(\|x\|,R)$ used to obtain an ODE solution on a whole compact interval. For positive $R$, it fixes the radius-$R$ ball and maps every vector into that ball. Its definition itself accepts every real $R$; all geometric estimates below explicitly assume $R>0$.

For positive radius $R$, proves a global Lipschitz bound with constant two for the radial truncation in an arbitrary normed real space. The proof separates the change in the vector from the change in its scalar denominator. This estimate permits Picard–Lindelöf to be applied to the truncated linear vector field over the full time interval.

_private.TorusEuler.LinearODEHigherParam.text: This private abbreviation names the closed real interval $[0,T]$ used as the time domain for path-valued solutions. It is a set, which Lean may also coerce to the subtype of its members. The definition does not assume a positive duration; integration and ODE constructors impose the needed bound separately.

This abbreviation denotes continuous maps from the closed-slab subtype to the target space. When the target is normed, compactness supplies the uniform path norm used in the ODE construction. Time values outside the interval are not part of a path's domain; extension to real time is a separate operation.

The real-time function obtained by applying the clamped coefficient path to the clamped vector path is continuous everywhere. The conclusion is continuity on the whole real line, not only on the closed slab. This follows directly from continuity of the two extensions and continuous evaluation of an operator on a vector.
_private.TorusEuler.LinearODEHigherParam.summary: The extended Volterra integrand is globally continuous

_private.TorusEuler.LinearODEHigherParam.text: The clamped real-time extension of a continuous slab path is continuous on all of $\mathbb R$. It is the composition of the path with the continuous interval projection. Nonnegative duration is required to define that projection; smoothness outside or across the endpoints is not part of this result.

For a nonnegative duration, a continuous slab path is evaluated at the nearest point of $[0,T]$. Thus the extended function agrees with the path on the slab and is constant beyond each endpoint. This gives a globally defined continuous function for interval integration without asserting a differentiable continuation outside the original interval.

If $(I-JA)x=g$ in the path space, the real-time difference between the clamped paths $x$ and $g$ has within-slab derivative $A(t)x(t)$. No differentiability of $g$ is assumed, so the conclusion is about the difference rather than $x$ alone. The fundamental theorem of calculus applies to its integral representation.
_private.TorusEuler.LinearODEHigherParam.summary: The integral equation identifies the derivative of its difference

_private.TorusEuler.LinearODEHigherParam.text: A continuous path of linear operators acts pointwise on a continuous vector-valued path. The definition packages this action as a continuous linear map between path spaces, bounded by the uniform norm of the coefficient path. It is the multiplication part of the Volterra operator used to formulate the linear ODE.
_private.TorusEuler.LinearODEHigherParam.summary: Multiply a path by its time-dependent operator

_private.TorusEuler.LinearODEHigherParam.text: The operation sending an operator-valued path to its pointwise action is itself a continuous linear map, with norm bounded by one. It records linear dependence on the coefficient path separately from linearity in the solution path. This lets smooth parameter dependence of coefficients pass to the Volterra equation operator.
_private.TorusEuler.LinearODEHigherParam.summary: Coefficient paths act linearly on the path space

_private.TorusEuler.LinearODEHigherParam.text: Applying a continuous coefficient path $A$ pointwise to a continuous path $x$ on the slab, and evaluating at a slab time $t$, gives exactly $A(t)x(t)$. This definitional identity connects the path-space operator with ordinary multiplication in the target space. It carries no derivative or ODE assumptions; those enter when the action is composed with time integration.

This bounded linear map takes a vector to the constant path with that value on the closed interval. Its operator norm is at most one. Together with the forcing primitive, it forms the right-hand side of the Volterra equation whose solution carries the desired initial condition.

This constructs the bounded linear operator sending a continuous path to its time primitive from zero. The output is another continuous path on the same closed slab, and its operator norm is bounded using the duration $T$. The target is a Banach space, so the integrals of the continuous extension have their ordinary meaning.
_private.TorusEuler.LinearODEHigherParam.summary: Integrate a continuous path from the initial time

_private.TorusEuler.LinearODEHigherParam.text: At a slab time, the primitive operator equals the interval integral from zero of the clamped path extension. This is a definitional equality exposing the concrete operator. It allows the ODE proof to apply the fundamental theorem of calculus to the Banach-valued integral on the closed interval.
_private.TorusEuler.LinearODEHigherParam.summary: Evaluate the path primitive as an integral

_private.TorusEuler.LinearODEHigherParam.text: This continuous linear map sends a coefficient path $A$ to the Volterra operator $x\mapsto\int_0^t A(s)x(s)\,ds$. It is built by composing the primitive operator with pointwise coefficient action. Nonnegative duration and a complete target support the integration, while linearity in $A$ provides parameter regularity later.
_private.TorusEuler.LinearODEHigherParam.summary: Compose coefficient multiplication with time integration

_private.TorusEuler.LinearODEHigherParam.text: This operator sends $x$ to $x-J(Ax)$ on the continuous path space. Solving its equation with right-hand side $x_0+Jf$ is equivalent to the forced linear ODE with initial data. The definition only forms the operator; bijectivity is established separately from ODE existence and uniqueness.
_private.TorusEuler.LinearODEHigherParam.summary: Write the integral equation as identity minus Volterra

_private.TorusEuler.LinearODEHigherParam.text: For any continuous coefficient path on a nonnegative closed slab, identity minus the Volterra operator is bijective. Injectivity follows from uniqueness for a homogeneous linear ODE with zero initial value. Surjectivity solves an auxiliary inhomogeneous ODE and adds the arbitrary continuous right-hand side, which need not itself be differentiable.
_private.TorusEuler.LinearODEHigherParam.summary: Every continuous right-hand side has a unique Volterra solution

_private.TorusEuler.LinearODEHigherParam.text: At each slab time, the Volterra operator is the integral of the clamped coefficient acting on the clamped solution path. The identity is definitional. On the interval of integration the clamping agrees with the original paths, so it exposes the integral equation used to derive the within-slab ODE.
_private.TorusEuler.LinearODEHigherParam.summary: The Volterra operator has its expected integral formula

_private.TorusEuler.LinearODEParameterDe.text: Multiplying both the initial size and forcing size of the Grönwall expression by $d$ multiplies the final expression by $d$. This holds algebraically for all real inputs, with the zero-growth-rate branch handled separately. It is used to factor the distance between parameters from the comparison estimate for two ODE solutions.
_private.TorusEuler.LinearODEParameterDe.summary: Scaling initial data and forcing together

_private.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitudeCo.text: Viewed as a map into ambient vectors rather than into the fixed plane $k^\perp$, the coordinate reader built from $k$ and the inverse coframe $G$ is exactly $G P_{G^*k}$. Its additional orthogonal projection onto the fixed plane acts trivially because the inverse-coframe image already lies there. This formula lets subsequent calculations use ordinary vectors and operator norms while retaining the fixed-coordinate map with values in the plane.
_private.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitudeCo.summary: The coordinate reader has the expected ambient value

_private.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitudeCo.text: For a continuous coframe $F$, two-sided inverse identities and a positive uniform bound $D$ on $G$ imply continuity of $G$ on the same set. The resolvent identity gives $\|G(u)-G(t)\|\le D^2\|F(u)-F(t)\|$. This avoids differentiating the inverse in the parent-to-seed construction, while supplying the time continuity needed by the coordinate reader.
_private.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitudeCo.summary: A bounded inverse varies continuously with the coframe

_private.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitudeCo.text: For any linear map $G$ and launch covector $k$, applying $G$ after projection perpendicular to $G^*k$ lands in the plane perpendicular to $k$. This follows from the adjoint inner-product identity, with the degenerate transported covector handled algebraically as well. It justifies treating the coordinate reader as a map into the fixed transverse plane $k^\perp$.
_private.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitudeCo.summary: The inverse coframe returns projected vectors to the fixed plane

_private.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitudeCo.text: For compatible continuous linear maps, the gap between two compositions is bounded by the first outer-map norm times the inner-map gap, plus the outer-map gap times the second inner-map norm. The proof adds and subtracts the mixed composition and applies submultiplicativity. Repeated use estimates the three factors in the fixed transverse generator.
_private.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitudeCo.summary: Composition differences obey a two term operator bound

_private.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitudeCo.text: For each derivative order $j$, chooses a positive constant uniform in the phase and all widths $0<h\le1$. The estimate $h^j|F_h^{(j)}|\le C h$ cancels the derivative loss from the narrow phase transition. The constant may depend on $j$, but neither on $h$ nor the evaluation phase; this feeds the rescaled profile jet bounds.
_private.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitudeCo.summary: Scaled phase derivatives retain the small profile size

_private.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitudeCo.text: For a real frequency at least one, the phase width $\lambda^{-1/2}$ equals $\lambda^{-5/4}\lambda^{3/4}$. Positivity of the frequency permits the real-power addition rule. This identity converts the small scalar wave profile into the weighted leading size after division by the seed weight $\lambda^{3/4}\|a_0\|$.
_private.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitudeCo.summary: The phase width gives the weighted leading scale

_private.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitudeCo.text: A globally smooth function on the label space with first Fréchet derivative bounded by $C$ satisfies $\|f(a)-f(b)\|\le C\|a-b\|$. The proof identifies the first iterated derivative norm with the ordinary derivative norm and applies the convex-space mean-value estimate. This converts coefficient jet bounds into the nearby-label errors used in localization.
_private.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitudeCo.summary: A uniform first derivative bound controls label differences

_private.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitudeCo.text: A smooth scalar function with bounds $h^j\|f^{(j)}\|\le C$ through order $n$ gives, for $g(a,s)=f(hs)$, the bound $\|\nabla^jg\|\le C$ on all Fréchet derivatives of orders $j\le n$ at every point. The spatial coordinate is ignored, and the positive scale $h$ is the phase derivative factor. The result lifts one-variable derivative estimates into the mixed label and phase norm used by the hierarchy.
_private.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitudeCo.summary: Scalar phase derivatives control the rescaled product jet

_private.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitudeCo.text: For smooth scalar and vector functions on label-phase space, nonnegative jet bounds $A$ and $B$ through order $n$ imply a bound $2^nAB$ for their scalar product. The binomial product rule supplies the factor $2^n$. This general estimate combines a slowly varying envelope-amplitude factor with the rapidly varying scalar phase profile.
_private.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitudeCo.summary: Multiplying profiles combines their finite jet bounds

_private.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitudeCo.text: For nonzero vectors $k$ and $a$, a normalized first coupling at least $D^{-1}$ implies a raw contraction at least $D^{-1}\|k\|\|a\|$. Multiplication by the positive norm product justifies removing the denominator. The statement itself places no sign restriction on $D$; positive quantitative use is supplied by the center-wave hypotheses.
_private.TorusEuler.LocalizedAmplitudeCo.summary: Central normalized coupling gives a raw lower bound

_private.TorusEuler.LocalizedPhaseBounds.text: A function smooth on two closed sets is smooth on their union when both sets admit unique differentiation and every iterated within derivative agrees on their intersection. The proof glues the two Taylor series. This supplies the general mechanism for joining the active wave to its zero extension at the activation time.
_private.TorusEuler.LocalizedPhaseBounds.summary: Matching all derivatives glues smooth closed pieces

_private.TorusEuler.LocalizedPhaseBounds.text: If a globally smooth time cutoff vanishes for all times up to $a$, then every joint derivative of its time-only lift vanishes at $(a,x)$. The result holds for every natural derivative order and every point in the normed spatial space. Continuity of each derivative extends its zero value from earlier times to the endpoint.
_private.TorusEuler.LocalizedPhaseBounds.summary: Every cutoff derivative vanishes at activation

_private.TorusEuler.LocalizedSeedRegular.text: A jointly smooth selected seed on the active slab, multiplied by the smooth scalar phase profile with $0<h\le1$, is jointly smooth in time, label and phase. This version omits the radial envelope. It exposes the smooth factor needed by the cell-gluing theorem, which handles the envelope and flat activation independently.
_private.TorusEuler.LocalizedSeedRegular.summary: The smooth phase factor preserves seed regularity

_private.TorusEuler.LocalizedSeedRegular.text: Rewrites the switched leading profile as successive scalar multiplication by the time switch, radial envelope and phase profile, followed by the selected amplitude. The equality is unconditional for all real parameters and all arguments. Its role is to match the generic smooth gluing theorem’s input shape without changing the underlying profile or selecting a new seed.
_private.TorusEuler.LocalizedSeedRegular.summary: The switched profile factors into its three scalar parts

_private.TorusEuler.LocalizedSeedRegular.text: Smooth material gradient and covector fields give jointly smooth amplitude operators and transverse projections wherever the covector is nonzero. Both formulas involve the reciprocal squared covector norm; the explicit hypothesis that the covector is nonzero at every point of the set removes its singular set. The proof writes the operators using rank-one maps and ordinary smooth multiplication, producing the coefficients required by parameter-dependent linear ODE regularity.
_private.TorusEuler.LocalizedSeedRegular.summary: Nonzero covectors make the seed operators smooth

_private.TorusEuler.LocalizedSeedRegular.text: A jointly continuous time-label function on $J\times\mathbb R^3$ is continuous as a function of time after any fixed label is substituted. The target only needs a topology; no linear structure or differentiability is assumed. This restriction supplies the time continuity hypotheses for uniqueness of the selected seed and its reflected counterpart.
_private.TorusEuler.LocalizedSeedRegular.summary: Fixing a label gives a continuous time coefficient

_private.TorusEuler.LocalizedSeedRegular.text: On a uniquely differentiable set, a smooth map $F$ with invertible within derivatives gives a smooth continuous right inverse $G$, provided $G$ maps the set into itself and $F\circ G$ is the identity there. The proof first identifies the within derivative of $G$ and then bootstraps all finite orders. No global inverse outside the set is asserted.
_private.TorusEuler.LocalizedSeedRegular.summary: A continuous right inverse inherits smoothness on the set

_private.TorusEuler.LocalizedSeedRegular.text: For positive radius $r$ with $2r<1/2$, constructs a globally smooth vector map equal to the centered label (the representative of $x$ with each coordinate in $[-1/2,1/2)$) wherever the periodized radial envelope is nonzero. It also proves that the periodized envelope is smooth. A larger compactly supported bump leaves a strict collar before the cell walls, allowing supported profiles to be expressed through globally smooth maps.
_private.TorusEuler.LocalizedSeedRegular.summary: A smooth proxy replaces the discontinuous centered label

_private.TorusEuler.MeanCoefficientBudge.text: A smooth field of linear operators remains smooth after taking adjoints pointwise. The adjoint is a continuous linear equivalence over the real numbers. This supplies the regularity of $F^T$ and $M^T$ before forming the kinetic coefficient and the antisymmetric part used in the vorticity coefficient.

Suppose smooth time slices have jets $C_m A D^{6m}$, with $D\ge1$, $\ell>0$, and $\ell D^6\le1$. The order-$n$ half-Hölder finite norm is bounded by $4A/\sqrt\ell$ times a sum of constants through order $n+1$. This combines the weighted supremum estimate with the one-derivative Hölder comparison.
_private.TorusEuler.MeanCoefficientBudge.summary: Power bounds give the half-Hölder norm at every order

_private.TorusEuler.MeanCoefficientBudge.text: For a smooth field, the operator norm of the derivative of a spatial word of length $m$ is bounded by its full Fréchet jet of order $m+1$. The proof inserts the arbitrary test direction alongside the unit coordinate directions. This yields the Lipschitz estimate needed to control each word's Hölder quotient.
_private.TorusEuler.MeanCoefficientBudge.summary: One more full jet bounds the derivative of a word

_private.TorusEuler.MeanCoefficientBudge.text: Applying the adjoint operation to an operator-valued field preserves the norm of each iterated Fréchet derivative. The adjoint is a real linear isometry on these operators, so the identity holds directly through composition. This keeps the transpose deformation and vorticity coefficients within the same derivative budgets.

Given smooth $F,M$ with jets bounded by $CD^{5i+1}$ and $CD^{6i+1}$, this bounds the order-$n$ jets of the kinetic and vorticity forms. The resulting powers are $D^{5n+2}$ and $D^{6n+3}$, with explicit constants from repeated product estimates. The input inequalities are pointwise at the specified label and require $D\ge1$.
_private.TorusEuler.MeanCoefficientBudge.summary: Product estimates bound the two mean coefficients

_private.TorusEuler.MeanCoefficientBudge.text: For a smooth field, the norm of a spatial derivative word is at most the norm of the corresponding iterated Fréchet derivative. The coordinate vectors all have norm one, so evaluation of the multilinear derivative costs no additional factor. This compares one coordinate word, not the sum over all words.
_private.TorusEuler.MeanCoefficientBudge.summary: A coordinate word is bounded by the full jet

_private.TorusEuler.MeanCoefficientBudge.text: A differentiable field with nonnegative global bounds $A$ on its values and $B$ on its derivative has half-Hölder increment constant $\sqrt{2AB}$. The proof multiplies the uniform increment bound by the Lipschitz bound. This private interpolation lemma is reused for the positive weighted label derivatives of mean coefficients.
_private.TorusEuler.MeanCoefficientBudge.summary: Combine a value bound with a derivative bound

_private.TorusEuler.MeanCoefficientBudge.text: If $m=|w|>0$, the weighted derivative word is bounded by $\ell A D^{p+q}$ under a jet bound $A D^{pm+q}$ and $\ell D^p\le1$. The hypotheses include $D\ge1$, nonnegative radius and amplitude, and smoothness. The positive-order assumption permits retaining one factor of the small radius.
_private.TorusEuler.MeanCoefficientBudge.summary: A positive derivative order keeps one radius factor

_private.TorusEuler.MeanDerivativeLiftin.text: For a word of length $m$, the correction-pair list has $2^m-1$ entries, expressed without subtraction as its length plus one equals $2^m$. The omitted term is the undifferentiated coefficient multiplying the highest derivative of the unknown. List multiplicity counts repeated derivative directions correctly.

Multiplying a real-valued list sum by $c$ equals summing the products by $c$. This requires no positivity assumptions and is proved by induction on the list. It is used to move the radius and inverse-cost factors inside the sum of correction terms in the derivative-lifting recurrence.
_private.TorusEuler.MeanDerivativeLiftin.summary: Distribute a scalar through a finite list sum

_private.TorusEuler.MeanDerivativeLiftin.text: Summing a constant real value over a list gives that value times the real coercion of the list length. The proof preserves list multiplicity rather than replacing the list by a set. This evaluates the common upper bound on all correction terms after the derivative induction has bounded them individually.
_private.TorusEuler.MeanDerivativeLiftin.summary: Evaluate a constant list sum by its length

_private.TorusEuler.MeanPressureHessian..text: This private abbreviation names continuous linear endomorphisms of three-dimensional Euclidean space. It is the target space for the parent gradient, mean gradient and forcing gradient in the half-Hölder estimates. The abbreviation adds no derivative certificate: an arbitrary operator is a value of this type.

A field that is $C^n$ on the closed slab, jointly in time and space, is $C^n$ in space on all of $\mathbb R^3$ at each slab time. The target may be any normed real space. This permits the purely spatial Poisson calculation to be applied to the time-dependent mean equation.
_private.TorusEuler.MeanPressureHessian..summary: Restrict joint regularity to a time slice

_private.TorusEuler.MeanPressureHessian..text: If both vector fields are twice continuously differentiable, the map sending $x$ to $DF(x)\,G(x)$ is once continuously differentiable. This regularity level permits a further divergence calculation. The theorem supplies differentiability of a product term without assuming the fields solve an equation.
_private.TorusEuler.MeanPressureHessian..summary: Two derivatives make cross advection differentiable

_private.TorusEuler.MeanPressureHessian..text: At a point where both vector fields are differentiable, divergence of their sum equals the sum of the divergences. The proof uses linearity of the Fréchet derivative and trace. It is applied when taking divergence of the physical linearized momentum equation for the mean correction.
_private.TorusEuler.MeanPressureHessian..summary: Divergence distributes over differentiable vector sums

_private.TorusEuler.MeanPressureHessian..text: Evaluation of the bundled gradient-composition field at a point gives the first operator composed with the second. This is a definitional equality that removes the Hölder wrapper before comparing the source to the physical Poisson equation. It clarifies the multiplication order appearing under the trace.
_private.TorusEuler.MeanPressureHessian..summary: Evaluate the Hölder product as operator composition

_private.TorusEuler.MeanPressureHessian..text: This construction packages the pointwise operator product of two half-Hölder fields as another half-Hölder field, using the preceding value and increment estimates. It records composition in the order $U$ after $V$. The fields are called gradients for their role; the inputs need not themselves come from differentiable vector fields.
_private.TorusEuler.MeanPressureHessian..summary: Compose two gradient fields in the Hölder space

_private.TorusEuler.MeanPressureHessian..text: For two half-Hölder operator fields, their pointwise product is bounded in value and in square-root-distance increments by twice the product of their norms. The second inequality uses the difference-of-products decomposition. These bounds construct the operator-composition field before taking its trace in the Poisson source.
_private.TorusEuler.MeanPressureHessian..summary: The product of two Hölder gradients is Hölder controlled

_private.TorusEuler.MeanPressureHessian..text: This definition sums the three diagonal coordinate evaluations of a continuous linear endomorphism of Euclidean space. The result is a continuous linear map to the reals, suitable for mapping half-Hölder fields. The following identity checks that this coordinate expression agrees with the basis-independent linear-map trace.
_private.TorusEuler.MeanPressureHessian..summary: The matrix trace as a continuous linear map

_private.TorusEuler.MeanPressureHessian..text: Applying the bundled trace map to a gradient operator gives its ordinary linear-algebra trace. This identity validates the coordinate construction used in the Hölder-space source formula. It holds for any continuous linear operator, independently of whether it is realized as the gradient of a divergence-free field.
_private.TorusEuler.MeanPressureHessian..summary: The coordinate sum is the ordinary matrix trace

_private.TorusEuler.MeanPressureHessian..text: The half-Hölder norm of the constructed composition field is at most twice the product of the input norms. The estimate combines its uniform value and square-root-distance increment bounds. This is the quantitative ingredient for controlling the mixed-gradient contribution to the mean-pressure source.
_private.TorusEuler.MeanPressureHessian..summary: The Hölder composition norm is bounded by the product

_private.TorusEuler.MeanPressureHessian..text: The continuous linear trace map on three-dimensional endomorphisms has operator norm at most three. Each diagonal coordinate evaluation is controlled by the operator norm, and there are three coordinates. This explicit dimension factor appears in the estimate for the pressure Poisson source.

The order-zero spatial half-Hölder norm is nonnegative when the function is bounded with bounded half-Hölder increment quotient. The proof combines nonnegativity of the controlled supremum and increment terms. This sign fact is used when multiplying and enlarging constants in the pressure-Hessian estimate.
_private.TorusEuler.MeanPressureHessian..summary: The finite order-zero Hölder norm is nonnegative

_private.TorusEuler.MeanPressureHessian..text: For a bounded function with bounded half-Hölder increment quotient (the order-zero case of $C^{m,1/2}$ membership), the corresponding spatial half-Hölder seminorm is nonnegative. The regularity hypothesis provides the boundedness needed for the real supremum. This prevents later inequalities from treating the supremum's default value for an unbounded set as an actual Hölder bound.

If a vector field has one order of spatial half-Hölder regularity, its Fréchet derivative has order-zero half-Hölder regularity and norm bounded by the original order-one norm. This supplies the gradient fields needed by the pressure Poisson multiplier from estimates on the mean velocity and forcing.
_private.TorusEuler.MeanPressureHessian..summary: One Hölder derivative controls the derivative field

_private.TorusEuler.MovingAmplitudeCoeff.text: If all four entries of a time-dependent two-by-two matrix are continuous on $J$, its associated bounded linear operator on real pairs is continuous there. The proof assembles the two rows from coordinate projections and scalar multiplication. It establishes operator-valued continuity only; no ODE, invertibility, or norm estimate is part of the conclusion.
_private.TorusEuler.MovingAmplitudeCoeff.summary: Continuous entries give a continuous two-component operator

_private.TorusEuler.MovingAmplitudeCoeff.text: Builds an orthonormal basis from a family of three orthonormal axes in three-dimensional Euclidean space. The cardinality equals the dimension, so linear independence yields spanning. This construction supplies norm-preserving coordinates for the pressure denominator calculation. It does not select axes from a wave or establish their orthogonality; orthonormality of the three axes is a hypothesis.
_private.TorusEuler.MovingAmplitudeCoeff.summary: Promote three orthonormal axes to a basis

_private.TorusEuler.MovingAmplitudeCoeff.text: For any vector and an orthonormal three-axis frame, returns its expansion along the axes with inner-product coefficients. The proof uses the orthonormal basis built from those three axes. In the amplitude calculation, transversality later determines the third coefficient, but this reconstruction identity itself assumes no wave vector, no pressure law, and no relation among the coefficients.
_private.TorusEuler.MovingAmplitudeCoeff.summary: Reconstruct amplitude vectors from their frame projections

_private.TorusEuler.MovingAmplitudeCoeff.text: Assuming $Z\ne0$, proves positivity of $X^2+Q^2/S^2+Z^2$, the normalized squared wave-vector length. No hypothesis on $S$ appears here: its squared-denominator term is nonnegative even under the convention that division by zero gives zero. This narrow positivity fact does not validate the scaled coordinates at $S=0$; their reconstruction theorems require nonzero $S$.
_private.TorusEuler.MovingAmplitudeCoeff.summary: A nonzero third component prevents a zero pressure denominator

_private.TorusEuler.MovingAmplitudeCoeff.text: With orthonormal axes, nonzero $\lambda$, $S$ and $Z$, and a transverse amplitude, writes $\langle k,Ma\rangle$ as $(\lambda/S)(c_UU+c_VV)$ for explicit pressure coefficients $c_U,c_V$ built from the matrix entries of $M$. The operator $M$ is arbitrary; the lemma does not yet specialize it to older strain plus shear and error. The sign convention $U=-\alpha_1$ means $c_U$ corresponds to the negative of the paper’s first coefficient.
_private.TorusEuler.MovingAmplitudeCoeff.summary: Express the pressure numerator through two amplitude coefficients

_private.TorusEuler.MovingAmplitudeCoeff.text: Expresses a frame component of $Ma$ through matrix entries and the two free variables $U,V$. It assumes an orthonormal frame, nonzero $\lambda$, $S$ and $Z$, and perpendicularity of $k$ and $a$. The third amplitude coefficient is $(XU-QV)/(SZ)$. The formalization uses $U=-\alpha_1$ and $V=\alpha_2$, so its signs must be translated before comparison with the paper’s amplitude rows.
_private.TorusEuler.MovingAmplitudeCoeff.summary: Apply the strain using the two free amplitude components

_private.TorusEuler.MovingAmplitudeCoeff.text: With nonzero carrier scale $\lambda$ and shear factor $S$, gives the identities $\langle E_1,k\rangle=\lambda X$, $\langle E_2,k\rangle=\lambda Q/S$, and $\langle E_3,k\rangle=\lambda Z$. These follow by cancelling the defining denominators. The frame need not be orthonormal for the equalities themselves, though orthonormality is necessary for subsequent vector and norm reconstructions.
_private.TorusEuler.MovingAmplitudeCoeff.summary: Three wave-vector projections recover their scaled values

_private.TorusEuler.MovingCoordinateWave.text: Assuming $S\ge1$, proves $|a/S|\le|a|$ for any real numerator. The lower bound makes $S$ positive and permits replacement of its absolute value by itself. This is used to discard harmless inverse-shear factors when collecting the coefficients of the moving wave-vector residual.
_private.TorusEuler.MovingCoordinateWave.summary: Division by the shear scale does not enlarge magnitude

_private.TorusEuler.MovingCoordinateWave.text: If $f(0)=0$ and the absolute derivative is at most $M$ throughout $[0,T]$, bounds $|f(\tau)|$ by $MT$ at a member $\tau$ of the interval. The derivative is within the closed interval. The proof first uses the sharper distance $\tau$ and then bounds it by $T$; the hypotheses themselves force $M\ge0$ on the nonempty interval.
_private.TorusEuler.MovingCoordinateWave.summary: A bounded derivative controls displacement from zero

_private.TorusEuler.MovingCoordinateWave.text: If the three scalar coefficients have absolute value at most $M$, bounds the absolute value of $ax+bq+cz$ by $M(|x|+|q|+|z|)$. Each hypothesis is retained separately, and no sign assumptions on the coordinates are needed. This triangle-inequality estimate converts rowwise coefficient control into the residual bound used by the wave-vector comparison.
_private.TorusEuler.MovingCoordinateWave.summary: Bound a linear combination by its coordinate sum

_private.TorusEuler.MovingCoordinateWave.text: In an orthonormal frame, expresses the pairing of $A^*k$ with axis $j$ using column $j$ of the frame matrix of $A$ and the scaled coordinates $(X,Q/S,Z)$. Both $\lambda$ and $S$ must be nonzero. The adjoint relation moves $A$ onto the basis vector before the scaled decomposition is substituted.
_private.TorusEuler.MovingCoordinateWave.summary: Express the adjoint action through one matrix column

_private.TorusEuler.MovingCoordinateWave.text: In an orthonormal three-dimensional frame, every vector equals the sum of its three coordinate projections. This local copy of the expansion lemma builds an orthonormal basis from the frame and uses the finite dimension to prove spanning. It underlies the scaled wave-vector decomposition; it assumes neither a wave equation nor positive coordinate scales.
_private.TorusEuler.MovingCoordinateWave.summary: Resolve a vector along all three frame axes

_private.TorusEuler.MovingCoordinateWave.text: For nonzero $\lambda$ and $S$, rewrites each pairing with $k$ as $\lambda$ times the corresponding entry of $(X,Q/S,Z)$. This is cancellation of the coordinate definitions and does not require the frame to be orthonormal. Orthogonality enters only when the three pairings are used to reconstruct the vector or its norm.
_private.TorusEuler.MovingCoordinateWave.summary: Recover frame pairings from the scaled coordinates

_private.TorusEuler.MovingCoordinateWave.text: Defines the remainder $r_Q$ in $Q\prime=-\varepsilon Z+r_Q$. The term $\varepsilon-2Sb_{32}-Sd_{32}$ measures the deviation of the third coupling from its frozen value, while the other terms contain the older diagonal entry and scaled error entries. The formalization indexes axes from zero, so its entry in row 2, column 1 is the paper’s $b_{32}$.
_private.TorusEuler.MovingCoordinateWave.summary: Second-coordinate error beyond the limiting coupling

_private.TorusEuler.MovingCoordinateWave.text: Defines the remainder $r_X$ in $X\prime=-Q+r_X$ from older-strain entries $b$, error entries $d$, and the relative preceding strength $\sigma$. Its three terms multiply $X,Q,Z$, respectively. The coefficient of $Q$ includes the difference between the current and initial shear strength. This is an algebraic definition for arbitrary entries, with no smallness assumptions built in.
_private.TorusEuler.MovingCoordinateWave.summary: First-coordinate error beyond the limiting shear

_private.TorusEuler.MovingCoordinateWave.text: Defines the entire right-hand side of the $Z$ equation, since the reference third coordinate is constant. The expression combines the error’s first and third entries with the difference $b_{23}-b_{32}$ in the coefficient of $Q/S$. It accepts arbitrary entries and coordinates; identifying it with an actual derivative requires the moving-frame equations.
_private.TorusEuler.MovingCoordinateWave.summary: Third-coordinate error beyond a constant reference component

_private.TorusEuler.MovingCoordinateWave.text: Bounds each of the three residuals by $5T\delta(|X|+|Q|+|Z|)$. It assumes $T,S\ge1$, nonnegative $\delta$, entrywise bounds on $b$, $d$ and $Sd$, relative-strength error at most $2T\delta$, and the third-coupling error at most $\delta$. No bound on $X,Q,Z$ is assumed. These explicit row estimates supply the perturbative coefficient bound before the bootstrap closes.
_private.TorusEuler.MovingCoordinateWave.summary: All wave-vector residuals satisfy one coefficient bound

_private.TorusEuler.MovingFrame.0.TorusE.text: Assuming perpendicular unit axes $u,v$, simplifies the cross-product derivative formed from $u\prime=-\nu v-\gamma(u\times v)$ and $v\prime=\nu u-\eta(u\times v)$ to $\gamma u+\eta v$. This is a pointwise algebraic identity in arbitrary real rates. It does not itself assume differentiable paths; the preceding product-rule theorem supplies those derivatives.
_private.TorusEuler.MovingFrame.0.TorusE.summary: The third axis follows from the first two

_private.TorusEuler.MovingFrame.0.TorusE.text: Expands any vector as the sum of its three inner products with an orthonormal frame multiplied by the corresponding axes. Orthonormality and the dimension-three setting ensure that the axes span the space; no completeness assumption must be supplied separately. This identity lets the frame proof express the action of $B$ and its adjoint by matrix entries.

For arbitrary three-dimensional vectors $u,v$, proves $\langle v,u\times v\rangle=0$. The statement includes degenerate and zero vectors and needs no hypothesis. Together with the first-factor orthogonality and the norm formula, it establishes that crossing two perpendicular unit axes produces the third member of the moving orthonormal frame.
_private.TorusEuler.MovingFrame.0.TorusE.summary: A cross product is perpendicular to its second vector

_private.TorusEuler.MovingFrame.0.TorusE.text: Identifies the real Euclidean inner product with the coordinate dot product of the underlying coordinate triples. This is an unconditional representation identity for vectors in $\mathbb R^3$. It permits coordinate cross-product theorems to be used in the frame proof without changing the underlying geometric inner product or orientation.
_private.TorusEuler.MovingFrame.0.TorusE.summary: Euclidean inner products equal coordinate dot products

_private.TorusEuler.MovingFrame.0.TorusE.text: Let $v$ be a path in a real inner-product space and assume $v\ne0$ at a time where its relative derivative is $v'=|v|w$. The formal statement proves $(\log|v|)'=(v/|v|)\cdot w$. Substitution of $w=v'/|v|$ gives the logarithmic-norm identity displayed in the proof of Lemma 2.2. It applies to any such path, rather than only to the wave vector or amplitude. The norm is positive under the hypothesis, so the logarithm and division have their ordinary mathematical meanings. The wave equations must be substituted separately to obtain $-B_{11}$ and $-B_{22}$.
_private.TorusEuler.MovingFrame.0.TorusE.summary: The radial component gives the logarithmic derivative of a nonzero norm

_private.TorusEuler.MovingFrame.0.TorusE.text: If $v\prime(t)=\|v(t)\|w$ within the set $s$ and $v(t)\ne0$, computes the length derivative as $\|v(t)\|\langle\widehat v(t),w\rangle$. The vector $w$ is the normalized instantaneous derivative, not a path. The proof differentiates the squared norm and its square root; it is valid in any real inner-product space.
_private.TorusEuler.MovingFrame.0.TorusE.summary: Differentiate the length of a nonzero vector

_private.TorusEuler.MovingFrame.0.TorusE.text: Let $v$ be a path in a real inner-product space, nonzero at the evaluated time, with derivative $v'=|v|w$ relative to a time set. Put $\widehat v=v/|v|$. The formal statement proves $\widehat v'=w-(\widehat v\cdot w)\widehat v$. Taking $w=v'/|v|$ gives $(\operatorname{Id}-\widehat v\widehat v^T)v'/|v|$, the normalization formula in the proof of Lemma 2.2. The conclusion is local in time and does not assume a wave equation. Nonvanishing is essential: normalization is defined as zero at a zero vector, but no derivative formula there is claimed.
_private.TorusEuler.MovingFrame.0.TorusE.summary: Projecting away the radial part differentiates a nonzero normalized vector

_private.TorusEuler.MovingFrame.0.TorusE.text: Given $\|u\|=\|v\|=1$ and $\langle u,v\rangle=0$, proves that the list $[u,v,u\times v]$ is orthonormal. All three geometric hypotheses are explicit. The list positions are numbered $0,1,2$ in the formalization, corresponding to the paper’s axes $E_1,E_2,E_3$. The cross product fixes the orientation of the final axis.
_private.TorusEuler.MovingFrame.0.TorusE.summary: Two perpendicular unit axes determine an oriented frame

_private.TorusEuler.MovingFrame.0.TorusE.text: For any orthonormal frame and continuous linear operator on three-dimensional Euclidean space, identifies its trace with the sum of the three diagonal frame entries. Trace freeness is not an assumption of this lemma. In the moving-frame proof, the separate hypothesis that the trace vanishes converts $-B_{11}-B_{22}$ into $B_{33}$.

_private.TorusEuler.MultiplierOffSupport.text: For every positive radius $\rho$, chooses an integer $k$ at which $\rho 2^k$ first reaches one. If $k$ is nonzero, the same quantity is at most two. This separates the low-frequency geometric growth from the high-frequency geometric decay in the finite derivative-kernel sum; no upper or lower restriction on the original radius is imposed.

Proves integrability of the function equal to $|z|^{-4}$ when $|z|\ge1$ and zero otherwise. The comparison uses a constant multiple of $(1+|z|)^{-4}$, whose exponent exceeds the ambient dimension three. This verifies that the named unit-tail integral is an ordinary finite integral rather than a value supplied by total integration outside its analytic domain.

For a strictly positive radius $r$, proves integrability of the indicator of $|z|\ge r$ multiplied by $|z|^{-4}$ and identifies its integral as $r^{-1}$ times the unit-tail constant. The exponent comes from combining the three-dimensional Jacobian with the fourth inverse power. Positivity of $r$ excludes the singular origin and legitimizes the dilation.

Assume a differentiable operator kernel satisfies $\|DK(w)\|\le C|w|^{-4}$ away from zero, with $C\ge0$. If $x,y$ lie in the radius-$r/2$ ball around $a$ and $|z-a|\ge r>0$, the kernel difference at $x-z,y-z$ is bounded by $16C|z-a|^{-4}\|x-y\|$. The segment stays at least half as far from the source as $z$ does from $a$.
_private.TorusEuler.MultiplierOffSupport.summary: Control kernel differences away from the source

_private.TorusEuler.MultiplierOffSupport.text: For a finite family of integrable operator kernels and a continuous source bounded globally by $M$, convolution with the kernel sum equals the sum of the individual convolutions. The source bound ensures each operator-valued application is integrable. This permits a single off-support estimate for the summed kernel to control every finite dyadic approximation.
_private.TorusEuler.MultiplierOffSupport.summary: Move a finite kernel sum through convolution

_private.TorusEuler.MultiplierOffSupport.text: Rewrites the lifted convolution at $x$ as an integral of $K(x-z)$ applied to $f(z)$, instead of integrating the kernel at $z$ against the translated source. The substitution is translation followed by reflection. This equality holds for the total integral without integrability hypotheses, so subsequent norm estimates separately prove the needed integrability.
_private.TorusEuler.MultiplierOffSupport.summary: Rewrite convolution by translating the kernel

_private.TorusEuler.MultiplierOffSupport.text: For Euclidean representatives $x,a$, expresses the auxiliary torus distance as the norm built from the coordinate differences $x_i-a_i$ after subtracting their nearest integers. This uses the circle-distance formula and makes the shortest-lift construction explicit. Ties in rounding do not affect the squared distances, so the identity needs no uniqueness assertion.
_private.TorusEuler.MultiplierOffSupport.summary: Coordinate rounding computes torus lift distance

_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMomentumLim.text: For a function $C^d$ on an open neighborhood of a compact set, all actual derivatives through order $d$ have one common nonnegative bound on that compact set. Continuity of each derivative gives a bound, and a finite sum combines them. No global boundedness outside the neighborhood is asserted.
_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMomentumLim.summary: A compact region bounds a finite smooth derivative tower

_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMomentumLim.text: For two fields with smooth preterminal spatial slices and off origin limits, their negative sum has off origin limits as well. The proof intersects the two limiting neighborhoods so both local representatives are defined together. Actual derivative rules for negation and subtraction transfer the uniform jet convergence to that common region.
_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMomentumLim.summary: Linear combinations preserve local terminal spatial limits

_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMomentumLim.text: If two fields are $C^d$ on an open set and all their derivatives through order $d$ at $x$ are bounded by $C$ and $D$, the order $d$ bilinear expression is bounded by $\|B\|2^dCD$. The first bound is assumed nonnegative. The factor $2^d$ sums the binomial coefficients in the Leibniz rule.
_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMomentumLim.summary: The product rule bounds a bilinear derivative

_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMomentumLim.text: Uniform convergence of order $d+1$ derivatives implies convergence of order $d$ derivatives of the Fréchet derivative map. The proof uses the canonical isometry identifying a $(d+1)$-linear map with a $d$-linear map into linear maps. This is a representation identity for derivative operators defined at every point, and needs no extra smoothness hypothesis of its own.
_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMomentumLim.summary: A higher jet identifies the corresponding gradient jet

_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMultiplierK.text: This abbreviation denotes the integer span of the coordinate basis in Euclidean space. It is the same unit lattice indexed elsewhere by integer triples. Treating it as a lattice submodule allows the proof to use a measurable fundamental-domain decomposition before returning to the explicit frequency indexing.
_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMultiplierK.summary: Integer combinations of the coordinate periods

_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMultiplierK.text: This complex continuous linear functional extracts entry $(i,j)$ from a complex pressure tensor. It is a composition of two finite product projections. The pressure symbol is assembled by weighting these coordinate functionals and summing them, which keeps continuity and linearity explicit.
_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMultiplierK.summary: Select one tensor coordinate as a bounded linear functional

_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMultiplierK.text: Each coordinate pressure weight is smooth on the complement of zero. The numerator is polynomial and the squared norm has a nonzero denominator on that set. The proof explicitly excludes the origin; it does not assert continuity of the direction-dependent quotient across zero.
_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMultiplierK.summary: The angular weight is smooth at nonzero frequencies

_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMultiplierK.text: Every actual derivative of the full periodic kernel is continuous on $\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3$. This follows from the established smoothness on that open set. The lemma is used to obtain measurable kernels and uniform bounds on compact sets of separated target and source differences.
_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMultiplierK.summary: Kernel derivatives are continuous on the punctured lift

_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMultiplierK.text: When $x-y$ lies off the lattice, differentiating the order $d$ kernel action in the target gives the order $d+1$ action, read as a linear map into order $d$ actions. The source point and density vector are held fixed. The proof combines kernel smoothness with the derivative of translation and bounded linear output evaluation.
_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMultiplierK.summary: Successive far kernel jets are actual derivatives

_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMultiplierK.text: For a Schwartz symbol, the order $d$ inverse Fourier kernel derivative multiplied by $\|y\|^n$ is bounded by its explicit weighted derivative mass at order $p$, provided $n\le p$. Reflection turns inverse Fourier transform into Fourier transform. The Schwartz structure supplies every smoothness and integrability assumption required by integration by parts.
_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMultiplierK.summary: Weighted inverse Fourier derivatives are controlled by symbol moments

_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMultiplierK.text: This bounded linear construction applies the output action $L$ to a kernel jet and leaves a separate source-density argument. It reorganizes the multilinear and linear argument order without changing values. The purpose is to use the same kernel derivatives for complex, real, scalar, or vector output actions.
_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMultiplierK.summary: A linear output action passes through a multilinear kernel jet

_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMultiplierK.text: Applying the reorganized jet action to a density and a tuple of spatial directions equals applying $L$ to the original kernel jet evaluated on those directions, then to the density. This definitional identity fixes the argument order used in later derivative and operator-norm estimates.
_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMultiplierK.summary: The reorganized kernel action evaluates in the intended order

_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMultiplierK.text: This private definition names the ordinary Euclidean coordinate basis of the three-dimensional lift. The periodization argument uses it to invoke fundamental-domain results stated for general lattice bases. It introduces no new lattice orientation or scale beyond the unit coordinate convention already used by the torus.
_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMultiplierK.summary: The coordinate basis identifies the periodization lattice

_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMultiplierK.text: This equivalence sends an integer triple to its Euclidean lattice vector and proves bijectivity onto the integer span of the coordinate basis. Surjectivity recovers integer coordinates from lattice membership. The equivalence permits sums from general fundamental-domain theorems to be reindexed by the explicit frequencies used throughout the construction.
_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMultiplierK.summary: Integer triples enumerate the full coordinate lattice

_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMultiplierK.text: The forward map of the equivalence between integer triples and the lattice sends $n\in\mathbb Z^3$ exactly to the vector $(n_1,n_2,n_3)\in\mathbb R^3$. This definitional equality lets the periodization proof rewrite general lattice translations into the explicit vector expressions used by the Fourier kernels. It carries no convergence or measure assertion of its own.
_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMultiplierK.summary: The lattice equivalence has the expected forward value

_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMultiplierK.text: The chosen half open coordinate fundamental domain is measurable. This private fact is used when restricting Lebesgue measure and changing integral domains in the periodization argument. It ensures those operations refer to an ordinary measurable source cell, including the convention on its boundary.

The fundamental cell has finite Lebesgue measure because it lies in the compact coordinate parallelepiped. This private estimate supports integration of bounded fields on the cell and domination of integral norms by a summable series. An exact numerical value for the volume is unnecessary for those arguments.

For an integer vector $k$, the norm of $x+k$ equals the distance from $x$ to the lattice point $-k$. This identity aligns the translation convention in the kernel series with the geometric separation convention for $\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3$. It is an algebraic rewrite, with no lower bound asserted.
_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMultiplierK.summary: Translated lengths are distances from the singular lattice

_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMultiplierK.text: The order $d$ derivative of a dyadic kernel is bounded by the explicit decay constant times $2^{j(3+d)}$, divided by $(1+2^j\|x\|)^p$. The denominator is strictly positive. This rearrangement puts the scaled Schwartz estimate into the form needed by the lattice and scale summability lemmas.
_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMultiplierK.summary: Every dyadic derivative has the required rescaled decay

_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMultiplierK.text: For bounded continuous periodic input, convolution with one dyadic Euclidean kernel equals integration over the fundamental cell against that dyadic periodic block. Schwartz decay supplies the summable translate bound needed by the general periodization theorem. This private identity is applied before taking the infinite sum over scales.
_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMultiplierK.summary: A dyadic Euclidean convolution equals its periodic block integral

_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMultiplierK.text: The coordinate weight is $\xi_i\xi_j/\|\xi\|^2$. Away from zero it is a smooth function of direction and unchanged by positive dilation. At zero Lean’s division convention makes the weight zero. The pressure symbol sums these weights with a minus sign against the tensor entries.
_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMultiplierK.summary: The angular weight of the pressure symbol

_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMultiplierK.text: At an integer frequency, the complex pressure weight equals the product of the two Fourier derivative symbols and the inverse Laplacian mode. The proof treats zero separately and cancels the $2\pi i$ factors for nonzero frequency. This checks both the normalization convention and the signs of the Fourier calculation.
_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMultiplierK.summary: Angular weights match derivative and inverse Laplacian factors

_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMultiplierK.text: The pressure weight $\xi_i\xi_j/|\xi|^2$ at $c\xi$ equals its value at $\xi$ whenever $c>0$. The two numerator and denominator powers of $c$ cancel. This includes the zero frequency under the convention that division by zero gives zero, while positivity guarantees the cancellation factor is nonzero.
_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMultiplierK.summary: Positive scaling leaves the angular pressure weight unchanged

_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMultiplierK.text: The sum over integer triples of the reciprocal Euclidean norm to power $p$ converges when $p>3$. The origin contributes the value zero, by the convention that the inverse of zero is zero. The proof identifies the integer triples with a rank-three lattice and applies the lattice summability theorem; the single zero term does not affect convergence.
_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginMultiplierK.summary: Inverse lattice powers are summable above dimension three

_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginNearPressur.text: The sum of squared coordinate sines is infinitely differentiable on all of Euclidean space. The proof composes each continuous linear coordinate projection with multiplication by $\pi$, sine and squaring, then sums the three smooth functions. No exclusion of the lattice is needed for this auxiliary detector.
_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginNearPressur.summary: The lattice detector is smooth everywhere

_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginNearPressur.text: The scalar function sums $\sin^2(\pi x_i)$ over the three coordinates. It is nonnegative, smooth and spatially periodic, and its zero set is exactly the integer lattice. Its positive minimum on a compact set off the lattice supplies the scale for the periodic cutoff in Proposition 8.4.
_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginNearPressur.summary: A smooth function detects every lattice point

_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginNearPressur.text: The detector $\sum_i\sin^2(\pi x_i)$ vanishes exactly at points represented by an integer lattice vector. Nonnegativity forces every squared sine to vanish; the zero set of sine then gives an integer for each coordinate. Conversely, an integer coordinate makes its sine term zero. This connects the analytic cutoff construction to the geometric definition of $\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3$.
_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginNearPressur.summary: Vanishing of the detector characterizes the lattice

_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginNearPressur.text: Every summand in the lattice detector is a real square, so its value is nonnegative at each point. This supports the later compact-minimum argument: excluding the lattice changes nonnegativity into strict positivity. By itself this lemma gives no positive lower bound away from a specified compact target.
_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginNearPressur.summary: The lattice detector never takes negative values

_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginNearPressur.text: Adding any integer lattice vector leaves the detector unchanged. Although sine itself may change sign under a unit shift, its square is periodic with period one. The proof uses the double-angle cosine identity to avoid tracking coordinate-dependent signs. Periodicity is later inherited by the cutoff built from this detector.
_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginNearPressur.summary: Integer translations preserve the cutoff detector

_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginPressureAss.text: This local abbreviation gives the nine-coordinate complex pressure tensor type a shorter name in the convolution estimates. It does not impose reality, symmetry, spatial regularity or periodicity. Those properties belong to the supplied tensor field and the hypotheses of later lemmas identifying the dyadic operator with physical pressure.
_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginPressureAss.summary: The dyadic pressure accepts complex tensor coordinates

_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginPressureAss.text: For a $C^2$ complex scalar field, its complex Laplacian equals the sum of the three diagonal coordinate Hessian entries at every point. The proof differentiates the coordinate projections of the complex gradient. This links the bundled gradient-divergence definition to the coordinates needed for Fourier integration by parts.
_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginPressureAss.summary: The complex Laplacian is the sum of diagonal mixed partials

_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginPressureAss.text: This raw function sums all nonnegative dyadic pressure blocks at each point of the Euclidean lift. Bounded smooth inputs produce an absolutely convergent series together with every derivative, by the preceding half-moment bounds. Subsequent lemmas identify this series with the bounded torus Fourier pressure multiplier on periodic inputs.
_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginPressureAss.summary: Sum the dyadic blocks into a complex pressure lift

_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginPressureAss.text: For a continuous cutoff and continuous velocity, the far pressure is smooth on any target set separated from its compact source enclosure. Their far tensor is continuous on the compact source and hence integrable. The kernel regularity theorem then differentiates only in the target variable; no smoothness of the source velocity is assumed.
_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginPressureAss.summary: Continuous velocity suffices for smooth separated far pressure

_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginPressureAss.text: On an open spatial set, an infinitely differentiable real scalar field has an infinitely differentiable gradient. The proof differentiates within the open set, then applies the inverse Riesz map to turn covectors into vectors. Openness identifies these derivatives with the ambient gradient used elsewhere in the pressure assembly.
_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginPressureAss.summary: A smooth scalar pressure has a smooth gradient

_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginPressureAss.text: If velocity is smooth on a spatial set $U$, its quadratic pressure tensor is smooth on that set. The bounded bilinear map is smooth, and evaluation against the same smooth velocity supplies its two arguments. The set need not be open for this within-set regularity statement.
_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginPressureAss.summary: The quadratic tensor preserves local smoothness

_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginPressureAss.text: For a smooth tensor input with global bounds on every jet, the complex dyadic pressure sum is smooth and each derivative equals the sum of block derivatives. Summable half-moment majorants hold at every order. The proof applies the general smooth-series theorem on all Euclidean space and thereby removes the raw infinite-sum ambiguity.
_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginPressureAss.summary: The full dyadic pressure series is smoothly differentiable

_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginPressureAss.text: A smooth cutoff whose topological support lies off the lattice turns the quadratic tensor of an off-origin smooth velocity into a globally smooth field. The proof applies the cutoff smoothing lemma at every finite order. No value or regularity of the original velocity on the lattice enters the conclusion.
_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginPressureAss.summary: The near tensor is smooth across the excluded lattice

_private.TorusEuler.OffOriginPressureAss.text: Each dyadic pressure block is smooth when the input is smooth and each input jet has a global bound.
