_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyTim.text: For any seminorm $N$ on a real vector space, any finite index set $s$ and any family $f_i$, one has $N\big(\sum_{i\in s}f_i\big)\le\sum_{i\in s}N(f_i)$. This is the triangle inequality for finite sums.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalHierarchyTim.summary: A finite expansion is bounded by the sum of its norms

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalLeadingTime..text: For a positive switching rate $r$, the derivative of the wave switch is zero outside $[t_0,t_0+1/r]$. Before the ramp the switch is locally zero, and after the ramp it is locally one, so both cases use derivatives of constant functions. This statement excludes the endpoints from its hypothesis rather than relying on an endpoint convention.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalLeadingTime..summary: The switch derivative vanishes outside its closed ramp

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalLeadingTime..text: The scaled enveloped amplitude has a genuine within-time derivative given by the original affine-wave generator at the scaled label acting on that amplitude. The evaluation time belongs to the seed’s active interval. The proof multiplies the seed’s derivative witness by a time-independent envelope and uses linearity; no extra derivative of the envelope appears.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalLeadingTime..summary: The fixed envelope preserves the amplitude equation

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalLeadingTime..text: For a seed with the hierarchy regularity data, the radius-scaled envelope amplitude $(t,x)\mapsto g(\ell x)\,\mathbf a(t,\ell x)$ is infinitely differentiable on $[t_0,T]\times\mathbb R^3$. It is the smooth amplitude composed with $(t,x)\mapsto(t,\ell x)$, multiplied by the smooth envelope.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalLeadingTime..summary: The scaled envelope amplitude is jointly smooth

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalLeadingTime..text: When both $[a,b]$ and $[c,d]$ have positive length and the latter lies inside the former, a field smooth on the larger slab has identical active time derivatives computed on either interval at points of $[c,d]$. The proof restricts actual derivative witnesses. This includes the smaller interval’s endpoints and supports transfer from the full stage to its active portion.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalLeadingTime..summary: Restricting the active interval preserves its time derivatives

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalLeadingTime..text: For a smooth amplitude $f(t,a)$ and a smooth time-independent scalar factor $\phi(a,s)$, the order-$i$ time derivative of $\phi f$ is bounded in parameter derivatives by $2^nCA$ when the two factors have bounds $C,A$ through order $n$. Only the selected derivative of $f$ is required. The phase factor is not differentiated in time.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalLeadingTime..summary: A time-independent phase factor costs no time derivatives

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalLeadingTime..text: At a time in the nondegenerate interval, the order-$i$ active time derivative of a jointly smooth field is smooth as a function of its remaining parameter. The proof takes a spatial slice of the preceding joint-smoothness result. This justifies ordinary Fréchet derivative estimates in scaled labels and phase after the time differentiation.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalLeadingTime..summary: Active time derivatives are smooth in the remaining variables

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalLeadingTime..text: For $a<b$ and a field $f$ jointly smooth on $[a,b]\times X$, every time derivative of $f$ within $[a,b]$, with the parameter held fixed, is again jointly smooth on $[a,b]\times X$. At the endpoints the within-interval derivatives are one-sided and uniquely determined.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalLeadingTime..summary: Active time derivatives preserve joint smoothness

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalLeadingTime..text: Joint smoothness of $f$ on $[a,b]\times X$ implies within-interval smoothness of $t\mapsto f(t,x)$ at each fixed parameter $x$. The proof composes with the constant-parameter inclusion. This provides the regularity required by time Leibniz identities without moving the label or the independent phase during differentiation.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalLeadingTime..summary: A fixed parameter gives a smooth time curve

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalLeadingTime..text: The bilinear map $(A,x)\mapsto A(x)$ has operator norm at most one for the given normed spaces. The proof applies the defining operator-norm inequality twice. This is the precise bound required to instantiate the generic product estimate with the amplitude generator acting on the amplitude field.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalLeadingTime..summary: Applying an operator has bilinear norm at most one

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalLeadingTime..text: If $\|c\|\le A$, then the constant field $x\mapsto c$ on $\mathbb R^3$ has all derivatives of order at most $n$ bounded by $A$, for every $n$: the value is bounded by $A$ and all positive-order derivatives vanish.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalLeadingTime..summary: A constant field satisfies every parameter derivative bound

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMaterialCoef.text: For a nonnegative sequence $C$ and integers $j\le n$, one has $C(j)\le1+\sum_{r\le n}C(r)$. The term $C(j)$ is one summand of a nonnegative sum, so no monotonicity of $C$ is needed.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMaterialCoef.summary: The finite order cap dominates each earlier constant

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMaterialCoef.text: The number one plus the finite sum of nonnegative constants through order $n$ is at least one. This scalar observation creates a usable common bound for flow-composition estimates. It imposes no monotonicity on the original constant sequence; the finite sum supplies a positive dominating quantity at the selected order.

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMaterialGrap.text: If $L\ge1$, then the number $(3\cdot2^NL)^N4^N$ is a nondecreasing function of the nonnegative integer $N$: for $m\le n$, $(3\cdot2^mL)^m4^m\le(3\cdot2^nL)^n4^n$. This lets an estimate at order $m\le N$ use the factor chosen for order $N$.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMaterialGrap.summary: The graph factor increases with the order

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanHolderJe.text: Let $0<\ell\le1$ and let $f_t$ be smooth fields on $\mathbb R^3$, indexed by $t$ in an arbitrary set, whose scaled derivative values $\ell^{|\beta|}|\partial^\beta f_t(x)|$ are bounded for every multi-index with $|\beta|\le N+1$. If $w$ is a coordinate word of length at most $N$ and $u$ is a half-Hölder torus field whose value at the torus point of every $x$ is $\partial^wf_t(x)$, then $\ell^{|w|}\|u\|_{C^{1/2}}\le4R/\sqrt\ell$, where $R=\sum_{|\beta|\le N+1}\ell^{|\beta|}\sup_{t,x}|\partial^\beta f_t(x)|$, each multi-index counted once.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanHolderJe.summary: One extra label order bounds each half-Hölder word

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanParentIn.text: If a coefficient field is jointly smooth on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3$, then at any time in the interval its spatial slice is smooth everywhere. This is composition with the map $x\mapsto(t,x)$. The helper supplies ordinary spatial differentiability when constructing Hölder and Lipschitz caps for the actual mean coefficients.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanParentIn.summary: A smooth coefficient has smooth fixed-time spatial slices

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanSpatialI.text: Defines a linear isometry between the fixed space of the actual spatial Leray projection and the half-Hölder solenoidal subspace. It is obtained from the proved equality of these subspaces, so the underlying vector field and its norm are unchanged. This lets the abstract compression estimate be applied to the concrete fixed-time mean inverse.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanSpatialI.summary: The Leray fixed space is the solenoidal space

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanSpatialI.text: The inverse isometry from the solenoidal subspace to the Leray fixed space leaves the underlying half-Hölder field unchanged. The proof combines the forward value identity with the inverse law of an isometry equivalence. It supplies the reverse rewriting needed when conjugating the supplied fixed-time inverse into the abstract fixed space.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanSpatialI.summary: The inverse subspace identification also preserves the field

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanSpatialI.text: The forward isometry from the Leray fixed space to the solenoidal subspace has exactly the same underlying half-Hölder field. This follows from its construction by equality of subspaces. The identity is needed to compare the abstract compressed coefficient multiplication with the concrete projected kinetic operator on actual fields.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanSpatialI.summary: Changing the subspace type preserves the field

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanSpatialI.text: If two half-Hölder fields both represent the directional derivative of the same field along a fixed torus direction, they are equal. The proof evaluates each derivative on the same line at parameter zero and uses ordinary derivative uniqueness, then field extensionality. It allows the spatial bootstrap's derivative family to be identified with the actual supplied derivatives.

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanSpatialT.text: For every half-Hölder field $f$ on the unit torus, every torus point $a$, every direction $u\in\mathbb R^3$ and every real $h$, the map $s\mapsto f(a+[shu])$, where $[y]$ is the torus point of $y\in\mathbb R^3$, is continuous on $\mathbb R$. No differentiability of $f$ is assumed.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanSpatialT.summary: Half-Hölder fields vary continuously along torus segments

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanSpatialT.text: The difference between the segment average of $z$ and its value at $a$ is at most $\|z\|\sqrt{|h|\|u\|}$. This estimate uses only the bundled half Hölder norm and is valid for zero or negative $h$. The bound tends to zero with the displacement, providing the remainder estimate used to recover a spatial derivative.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanSpatialT.summary: Segment averages approach the starting value

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanSpatialT.text: Constructs a continuous linear map sending a half Hölder field to its integral along $s\mapsto a+[(sh)u]$ for $0\le s\le1$. The map has norm at most one, proved from the pointwise evaluation bound. It replaces spatial difference quotients by integrals when commuting strong spatial differentiation with time differentiation.

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanTime.0.T.text: Let $T>0$, $t\in[0,T]$ and let $K(r)$ be a smooth curve on $[0,T]$ of half-Hölder matrix fields. Then the $i$th time derivative within $[0,T]$ at $t$ of the operator curve $r\mapsto(z\mapsto K(r)z)$ on half-Hölder vector fields is multiplication by the $i$th time derivative of $K$ at $t$.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanTime.0.T.summary: Coefficient multiplication commutes with time derivatives

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanTimeBoun.text: The sum of $\binom{n+1}{i+1}$ over $0\le i\le n$ is at most $2^{n+1}$. This omits the zeroth-index term from the full binomial sum. It bounds the kinetic-coefficient derivatives on the right side of the higher mean equation, where the highest velocity derivative has already been moved to the left.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanTimeBoun.summary: Positive-index binomial terms fit the same total bound

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanTimeBoun.text: The sum of the real casts of $\binom ni$ for $0\le i\le n$ is exactly $2^n$. Lean obtains this from the natural-number binomial identity. The equality bounds the number and weights of terms produced when differentiating a product in time, keeping that combinatorial cost dependent only on the chosen time order.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanTimeBoun.summary: All binomial coefficients sum to a power of two

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanTimeBoun.text: If every summand has scaled norm $a\|f_i\|\le B$ with $a\ge0$, then the scaled norm of the finite natural-weighted sum is at most $B$ times the sum of its weights. No positivity assumption on $B$ is separately needed. This converts time Leibniz sums into scalar binomial totals in the mean bounds.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanTimeBoun.summary: Bound a natural-weighted sum in half Hölder norm

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanTimeBoun.text: Given three strong derivative relations in the same direction, the derivative relation for $a+b-c$ has value $a\prime+b\prime-c\prime$. This follows from linearity in the half Hölder space. The auxiliary mean recurrence uses it to combine the differentiated vorticity product, the forcing term, and the kinetic commutator terms.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanTimeBoun.summary: Strong spatial derivatives preserve addition and subtraction

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanTimeBoun.text: Let $V$ be a finite index set, $k_i$ nonnegative integers, and $f_i,g_i$ half-Hölder torus fields such that for each $i\in V$, $g_i$ is the derivative of $f_i$ in direction $u$ along every line. Then $\sum_{i\in V}k_ig_i$ is the derivative of $\sum_{i\in V}k_if_i$ in direction $u$ in the same sense.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMeanTimeBoun.summary: Directional derivatives pass through weighted finite sums

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedDerivat.text: Assume $g$ is jointly differentiable on the slab $[a,b]\times\mathbb R^3$, and fix a time $t\in[a,b]$ and a spatial point $x$. Then the time slice $r\mapsto g(r,x)$ has a derivative within $[a,b]$ at $t$, namely the joint within-slab derivative of $g$ at $(t,x)$ applied to $(1,0)$. No uniqueness is claimed, so a degenerate time interval is allowed.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedDerivat.summary: A time slice inherits its joint derivative

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedDerivat.text: Let $g$ be differentiable within $[a,b]\times\mathbb R^3$, $t\in[a,b]$ and $x\in\mathbb R^3$. Then $y\mapsto g(t,y)$ is differentiable at $x$, with derivative $v\mapsto Dg(t,x)(0,v)$, where $Dg$ is the joint derivative within $[a,b]\times\mathbb R^3$. No condition $a<b$ is needed.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedDerivat.summary: A spatial slice inherits its joint derivative

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.text: Let $T>0$, a time $t\in[0,T]$ and a spatial point $x$, and suppose a genuine joint within-slab derivative witness: $f$ has at $(t,x)$ the derivative within $[0,T]\times E$ given by its selected joint derivative. Then the within-time derivative of the fixed spatial time slice $r\mapsto f(r,x)$ at $t$ equals the time partial of $f$ at $(t,x)$, the joint derivative applied to $(1,0)$.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.summary: The time derivative of a fixed spatial slice

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.text: Let a time $t\in[0,T]$ and a spatial point $x$ be fixed, and suppose a supplied joint derivative: $f$ has at $(t,x)$ the derivative within $[0,T]\times E$ given by its selected joint derivative. Then the ordinary spatial derivative at $x$ of the fixed time slice $y\mapsto f(t,y)$ is the spatial partial of $f$ at $(t,x)$, $v\mapsto Df(t,x)(0,v)$. Positivity of $T$ is not needed.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.summary: The spatial derivative of a fixed-time slice

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.text: Let $T>0$, let $f$ be jointly smooth on $[0,T]\times E$ with values in a normed space, let $C\ge0$, $t\in[0,T]$ and $x\in E$. If $\|D_y^m\partial_t^qf(t,y)|_{y=x}\|\le C$ for every pair $q,m$ with $q+m=n$, with time derivatives within $[0,T]$ at the fixed spatial point, then the $n$th joint derivative of $f$ within $[0,T]\times E$ at $(t,x)$ has norm at most $2^nC$.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.summary: A common mixed derivative bound controls the joint derivative

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.text: For a smooth function on a positive-length slab, the norm of its joint derivative of order $n+1$ is at most the sum of the order-$n$ joint derivative norms of its time and spatial partials. The proof decomposes a product-space direction into $(t,0)$ and $(0,x)$ and applies the triangle inequality. Evaluation stays on the slab.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.summary: Split the next joint derivative into time and space

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.text: Takes the joint within-slab derivative of $f$ and restricts it to the spatial directions. The result is a function valued in continuous linear maps from $E$ to the target. This operation defines notation for the mixed derivative proof; it does not, by itself, show that a spatial slice is differentiable.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.summary: Extract the spatial partial from the joint derivative

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.text: Let $T>0$ and let the original function $f$ be smooth on $[0,T]\times E$. Then the extracted spatial partial, the spatial component $v\mapsto Df(t,x)(0,v)$ of the joint within-slab derivative, is again jointly smooth on $[0,T]\times E$.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.summary: The spatial part of the joint derivative is jointly smooth

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.text: Let $T>0$ and let $f$ be smooth on $[0,T]\times E$. At each slab point $(t,x)$, $t\in[0,T]$, extracting a time partial after a spatial partial equals extracting them in the reverse order: the time partial (direction $(1,0)$) of the spatial partial of $f$ equals the spatial partial of the time partial of $f$. The time endpoints $0$ and $T$ are covered.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.summary: The time and spatial parts of the joint derivative commute

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.text: Defines a continuous linear map that sends a joint derivative $L$ to $v\mapsto L(0,v)$. This separates the spatial component without changing the target space. The operation itself is purely linear algebra; later theorems identify its value on an actual joint derivative with the ordinary Fréchet derivative of the fixed-time spatial slice.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.summary: Restrict a joint derivative to spatial directions

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.text: Defines the continuous linear map that evaluates a joint derivative on $(1,0)$. Its input is a linear map from time and space to the target, and its output is the corresponding time-direction vector. It performs no differentiation itself; it is used to extract time partials from the joint within-slab derivative.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.summary: Read the time component of a joint derivative

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.text: For a function $f(t,x)$ on $\mathbb R\times E$, a nonnegative integer $q$ and a point $p=(t,x)$, this defines the $q$th derivative of $r\mapsto f(r,x)$ within $[0,T]$, evaluated at $r=t$. The spatial coordinate $x$ is held fixed during the differentiation.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.summary: Time derivatives at a fixed spatial point

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.text: On a positive-length slab, $T>0$, let $f$ be jointly smooth on $[0,T]\times E$. For every order $q$, the fixed-spatial-point time derivative $\partial_t^q$ of $r\mapsto f(r,x)$ within $[0,T]$ at $t$ agrees, at every slab point $(t,x)$, with the $q$-fold repeated application of the extracted time partial $g\mapsto Dg(\cdot)(1,0)$ to $f$.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.summary: Slice time derivatives equal iterated time parts of the joint derivative

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.text: Let $T>0$, let $f$ be jointly smooth on $[0,T]\times E$, and let $t\in[0,T]$. For every $q$, the function $y\mapsto\partial_t^q\big(Df(\cdot,y)(0,\cdot)\big)(t)$, the $q$th time derivative at fixed $y$ of the spatial part of the joint derivative, equals the spatial derivative of $y\mapsto\partial_t^qf(t,y)$, time derivatives taken within $[0,T]$.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.summary: Slice time derivatives commute with the spatial part of the derivative

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.text: At an allowed time $t\in[0,T]$ on a positive-length slab, $T>0$, with $f$ jointly smooth on $[0,T]\times E$: taking $q$ slice time derivatives of the extracted time partial $Df(\cdot)(1,0)$ at the fixed point $y$ is the same as taking $q+1$ slice time derivatives of $f$, for every $y$. So one extracted time partial raises the slice time order by one.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.summary: One time part of the derivative raises the time order by one

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.text: Takes the joint within-slab derivative of $f$ on $[0,T]\times E$ and evaluates it on $(1,0)$. This is an encoding of the time partial on the closed slab. The definition makes sense for arbitrary $T$ and $f$; identification with the derivative of a time slice requires the later smoothness and positive-length hypotheses.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.summary: Extract the time partial from the joint derivative

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.text: If two functions agree throughout the closed slab, their extracted within-slab time partials also agree there. This is a congruence statement for the selected derivative and needs no smoothness or positive-length assumption. It allows local equalities to be substituted under repeated within-slab differentiation without asserting anything outside the domain.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.summary: Agreement on the slab preserves the extracted time partial

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.text: If the original function $f$ is jointly smooth on a positive-length closed slab $[0,T]\times E$, $T>0$, then iterating the extracted time-partial operator $g\mapsto Dg(\cdot)(1,0)$ any finite number $q$ of times gives a function that is still jointly smooth on that slab.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.summary: Repeated time parts of the derivative remain smooth

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.text: Let $T>0$ and let $f$ be jointly smooth on $[0,T]\times E$. Then the extracted time partial $(t,x)\mapsto Df(t,x)(1,0)$, obtained from the joint derivative within $[0,T]\times E$ by evaluation at the time direction, is jointly smooth there, so time differentiation can be repeated.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.summary: The time part of the joint derivative is jointly smooth

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.text: If $T>0$, then the set $[0,T]\times E$ has unique derivatives at each of its points: a derivative within this set, when it exists, is uniquely determined, including at the times $0$ and $T$.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBrid.summary: The closed slab has unique derivatives

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalParentTimeBa.text: A jointly smooth field on a closed slab has a smooth ordinary spatial slice at each time belonging to the interval. The proof is composition with the fixed-time inclusion and does not require positive interval length. This local helper is used when treating stage velocity and residual as continuous functions on the spatial torus.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalParentTimeBa.summary: Fixed-time slices preserve the stage field regularity

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalPeriodicExte.text: For $x\in\mathbb R^3$ and integer vectors $k,j\in\mathbb Z^3$, regarded as points of $\mathbb R^3$, one has $(x+k)-j=x-(j-k)$. The index change $j\mapsto j-k$ is a bijection of $\mathbb Z^3$, which is how sums over lattice translates are reindexed.

For integer vectors $k,l\in\mathbb Z^3$, the point of $\mathbb R^3$ with coordinates $k+l$ is the sum of the points with coordinates $k$ and $l$; that is, the inclusion of $\mathbb Z^3$ into $\mathbb R^3$ is additive.
For every real $R$, the set of integer vectors $k\in\mathbb Z^3$ whose Euclidean norm satisfies $|k|\le R$ is finite.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalPeriodicExte.summary: Only finitely many lattice points lie in a ball

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalPeriodicExte.text: The lattice-vector embedding sends subtraction of integer triples to subtraction of their spatial vectors. This algebraic identity converts between translated spatial arguments and index differences. It is used to show that periodizing a local extension respects every integer translation.

The supports of all lattice translates of a fixed smooth compactly supported bump form a locally finite family. Near any spatial point, only lattice vectors within a bounded radius can contribute, and there are finitely many of them. This permits smooth summation of the translated extensions without requiring convergence of an infinite derivative series.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalPeriodicExte.summary: Translated bump supports are locally finite

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalPeriodicExte.text: If $x\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3$ and $k\in\mathbb Z^3$, then $x-k\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3$. Here the removed set is the whole integer lattice, which represents the single torus origin.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalPeriodicExte.summary: Lattice translation preserves the punctured lift

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalPhysicalTime.text: Let $0<T\le1$, $i\le q$, and let $N$ be a seminorm on twisted vector profiles on $[0,T]$. If $\sum_{j=0}^q\frac{T^j}{j!}N(\partial_t^jf)\le M$, then $N(\partial_t^if)\le q!\,T^{-q}M$.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalPhysicalTime.summary: The factorial time norm bounds each individual time derivative

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalPoincare.0.T.text: Let $a\le b$ and let $g$ be a real function, continuous on $[a,b]$ and nonnegative at every real point. Then $\big(\int_a^bg\big)^2\le(b-a)\int_a^bg^2$.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalPoincare.0.T.summary: Cauchy–Schwarz for a squared time integral

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalRelayCoeffic.text: For every twisted profile $f(t,a,s)$ on $[0,T]$, the function $(t,a)\mapsto f(t,a,0)$ is jointly smooth on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3$. Phase independence is not assumed.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalRelayCoeffic.summary: A smooth profile read at phase zero is smooth

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalRelayCoeffic.text: Let $f(t,a,s)$ be a twisted profile, so $f(t,a+n,s+k\cdot n)=f(t,a,s)$ for $n\in\mathbb Z^3$, which is moreover independent of $s$ on $[0,T]$. Then for every $t\in[0,T]$, the label field $a\mapsto f(t,a,0)$ is invariant under all integer translations.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalRelayCoeffic.summary: A phase-independent profile is periodic in the label

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalScheduledGra.text: If $K\ge0$, the finite profile-sum cost at any depth $d$ is nonnegative. The number of levels is nonnegative, and the hierarchy level constant is at least one. This sign fact allows the common sixth-power loss to enlarge the oscillatory and mean bounds without reversing an inequality.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalScheduledGra.summary: The profile sum cost is nonnegative

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalScheduledGra.text: For $K\ge0$, the explicit remainder factor is nonnegative at every depth. Its formula consists of $2K$, a squared shifted level constant $(C+1)^2$, and nonnegative counts of omitted interaction pairs. The result justifies inserting an additional parent-frequency factor when placing the tail estimate under the same common loss as the other profile estimates.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalScheduledGra.summary: The profile remainder cost is nonnegative

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalScheduledMea.text: For a phase-independent mean source, the time jet of order at most $q$ of a spatial derivative word of length at most $m$, scaled by $\ell$ to the word length, is bounded by its order-$(m+1)$ factorial time norm times $4q!\mathsf D^{q+a}$. The hypotheses require $0<T\le1$, $0<\ell\le1$, $T^{-1}\le\mathsf D$, and $\ell^{-1}\le\mathsf D^a$. The extra spatial order converts finite label norms to half-Hölder control; the factor $\mathsf D^q$ pays for time extraction.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalScheduledMea.summary: Read the mean source in half-Hölder word norms

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalScheduledMea.text: Given joint smoothness on the closed slab, a mixed coefficient bound, and compatible endpoint half-Hölder jets, the theorem bounds every time jet of order $i\le q$ of a spatial word of length at most $n$. The scaled norm costs the mean word constant $6\sum_{j\le n}(C_j+C_{j+1})$ times $\mathsf D^{e+p}$, with $p$ the scale exponent. It assumes positive slab length and label width, $\mathsf D\ge1$, and $\ell\mathsf D^p\le1$, plus nonnegative arrays with $C'\le C$.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalScheduledMea.summary: Turn raw coefficient jets into half-Hölder word bounds

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalScheduledMea.text: This scalar is $6\sum_{j\le m}(C_j+C_{j+1})$, six times the sum of adjacent-order costs through order $m$. It gathers the two adjacent derivative orders needed to control half-Hölder norms of all label words of length at most $m$. The shift by one records the extra spatial derivative used in the Hölder comparison.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalScheduledMea.summary: One coefficient cost for all shorter spatial words

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalScheduledMea.text: If $C$ is nonnegative and $C'_j\le C_j$ for every $j$, then every included adjacent-order cost $6(C'_m+C'_{m+1})$ is bounded by the majorant $6\sum_{j\le n}(C_j+C_{j+1})$, provided $m\le n$. The array $C'$ need not be nonnegative for this comparison. The proof uses a single summand of the larger finite sum.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalScheduledMea.summary: The word majorant covers a smaller coefficient array

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalScheduledMea.text: When every entry $C_j$ is nonnegative, the mean word constant $6\sum_{j\le m}(C_j+C_{j+1})$ is nonnegative at every reserve $m$. Each summand contains two nonnegative adjacent-order costs, and the overall factor is six. This elementary sign result supports all subsequent multiplication and monotonicity steps in the mean time-derivative bound.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalScheduledMea.summary: The mean coefficient word cost is nonnegative

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalScheduledPar.text: For $\mathsf D\ge2$ and a natural exponent $B$, the elementary estimate $1+\mathsf D\,\mathsf D^B\le\mathsf D^{B+2}$ holds. First bound the added one by the existing positive term, then absorb the factor two into $\mathsf D$. This is a scalar comparison used to replace nested coefficient amplitudes by one fixed power of the parent scale.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalScheduledPar.summary: Absorb one plus a parent-scale power

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalScheduledSta.text: If a statement holds at $n+1$ for all sufficiently large natural indices $n$, then it holds at $n$ for all sufficiently large $n$, without that shift. The proof increases the threshold by one and writes each later index as a successor. No assertion is made about the finitely many excluded initial stages.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalScheduledSta.summary: Remove one shift from an eventual stage statement

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalSeeleyExtens.text: For $a<0$, an open spatial set $O$ and a jointly smooth field on $[a,0]\times O$, this constructs a smooth field on $(a,\infty)\times O$ agreeing with it on $(a,0]\times O$. The proof localizes boundary jets, realizes them by a Borel series, glues along zero, and patches local extensions. Finite-dimensional space and a complete value space are inherited assumptions.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalSeeleyExtens.summary: Extending a smooth slab through the zero boundary

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalStageFromGra.text: For any real constant $C$, the child frequency $\lambda_{n+2}$ is at least $C$ for all sufficiently large $n$. This is the divergence of the scheduled frequency sequence after a fixed index shift. It lets later cutoff arguments absorb fixed numerical constants while excluding only finitely many initial stages.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalStageFromGra.summary: The child frequency eventually exceeds any fixed threshold

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalStageFromGra.text: For any natural constant $C$, the exponent $K(q_{n+3})$ is at least $C$ for all sufficiently large $n$. The proof shifts the established divergence of adjacent frequency exponents. This supplies enough hierarchy depth for the cutoff tail and enough next-frequency decay to absorb the fixed residual-growth exponent.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalStageFromGra.summary: The next frequency exponent eventually exceeds any fixed order

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalSwitchTime.0.text: For positive derivative order $q$, the $q$th derivative of the standard smooth transition function (zero below $0$, one above $1$) vanishes at every point outside $[0,1]$. On either complementary open half-line the function agrees locally with a constant, so its iterated derivatives vanish. This auxiliary lemma does not yet include the two endpoint values; a later continuity argument adds them.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalSwitchTime.0.summary: Positive derivatives vanish outside the transition interval

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTimeAdvectio.text: For any real constant $A$, summing $\binom qi A$ over $0\le i\le q$ gives $2^qA$. The auxiliary lemma factors out $A$ and uses the finite binomial sum. It needs no sign hypothesis because the conclusion is an equality; nonnegativity enters only when later estimates replace individual terms by a common bound.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTimeAdvectio.summary: Binomial coefficients sum to a power of two

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTimeCutoffBo.text: The stress built from two continuous torus inputs is differentiable as a field on $\mathbb R^3$. No positivity of the cutoff radius or regularity of the multiplier is needed for this algebraic statement: the implemented cutoff is a finite Fourier synthesis. Approximation estimates later add the multiplier and radius hypotheses that make it a genuine cutoff.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTimeCutoffBo.summary: The cutoff stress is spatially differentiable

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTimeCutoffBo.text: Spatial differentiation followed by the row-wise divergence of the momentum tensor commutes with the finite binomial sum of cutoff stresses. The factors $U_j$ and $U_{q-j}$ are independent continuous periodic inputs. Their Fourier cutoffs are smooth, so differentiating the sum is legitimate; the divergence contraction is a continuous linear map. No time regularity is claimed by this algebraic identity.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTimeCutoffBo.summary: Divergence distributes over the differentiated stress sum

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTimeCutoffBo.text: For an arbitrary multiplier $\psi$, radius $\Lambda$, and continuous fields $g,h$ on $\mathbb T^3$, the lifted cutoff stress $S_\Lambda g\otimes S_\Lambda h-S_\Lambda(g\otimes h)$ is spatially periodic. Every term depends on the point through its image in the unit torus. This provides the periodicity required when applying the Leray estimate to the divergence of the differentiated stress.

If the field $f$ has spatial $C^{m,1/2}$ regularity, multiplying it by the natural number $n$ preserves that regularity and bounds its norm by $n$ times the original norm. The proof uses the exact triangle estimate inductively. The natural scalar form matches the binomial coefficients in the differentiated cutoff stress.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTimeCutoffBo.summary: Natural multiples scale the spatial Hölder bound

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTimeCutoffBo.text: If each field indexed by a finite set is spatially $C^{m,1/2}$, their sum has that regularity and norm at most the sum of the individual norms. Both regularity and the numerical estimate are concluded. Empty sums use the zero-field case, so no nonempty-set assumption is hidden in the aggregation.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTimeCutoffBo.summary: Finite sums preserve the spatial Hölder bound

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTimeCutoffBo.text: The zero vector field has spatial $C^{m,1/2}$ regularity and exactly zero spatial Hölder norm for every natural order $m$. The proof establishes the regularity condition before simplifying the supremum-based formula. This supplies the empty-sum case when the cutoff residual estimate combines finitely many differentiated stress terms.

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTimeCutoffRa.text: For $\lambda>0$, the integer power $(\lambda^5)^{m-d}$ equals the real power $\lambda^{5(m-d)}$, with the depth $d$ and order $m$ subtracted as integers. Positivity permits conversion between natural, integer, and real exponents. This auxiliary identity is used to compare the cutoff tail with the growing hierarchy depth; it contains no asymptotic assertion itself.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTimeCutoffRa.summary: Rewrite the cutoff radius as a real frequency power

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTimeCutoffRe.text: When $g(t)$ represents a jointly smooth field $V$ on a positive-length closed slab, the lifted Fourier cutoff $S_\Lambda g(t)$ is jointly smooth there. The proof obtains smoothness of its Fourier coefficients from the smoothness of $V$ and the representation. The family $g$ need not carry a separate global-in-time smoothness assumption outside the slab.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTimeCutoffRe.summary: A represented Fourier cutoff is jointly smooth

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTimeCutoffRe.text: A fixed continuous linear map $L$ commutes with every within-slab time derivative of a jointly smooth field, at each time in a positive-length interval. The proof inducts on the derivative order and uses the derivative equation of the previous time derivative. The conclusion concerns the given slab only, without requiring a globally smooth extension of the field.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTimeCutoffRe.summary: Fixed linear maps commute with slab time jets

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTimeCutoffRe.text: Given torus representatives $g_j$ of all time derivatives of a smooth velocity $V$, the $q$th time derivative of $S_\Lambda(V\otimes V)$ is $\sum_{j=0}^q\binom qj S_\Lambda(g_j\otimes g_{q-j})$. The proof works column by column, combining the bilinear time rule with fixed-cutoff commutation.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTimeCutoffRe.summary: Differentiate the cutoff momentum tensor by Leibniz

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTimeCutoffRe.text: For a smooth velocity whose time derivatives are represented by $g_j$, the $q$th time derivative of its self-stress is $\sum_{j=0}^q\binom qj\,\mathrm{St}(g_j,g_{q-j})$, where $\mathrm{St}(g,h)=S_\Lambda g\otimes S_\Lambda h-S_\Lambda(g\otimes h)$. This identity holds at the chosen closed-slab time and spatial point. Independent left and right stress inputs are essential because the two factors generally receive different derivative orders.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTimeCutoffRe.summary: Time derivatives split into bilinear cutoff stresses

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTimeCutoffRe.text: If $g$ represents a jointly smooth velocity on a positive-length slab, the self-stress $S_\Lambda g(t)\otimes S_\Lambda g(t)-S_\Lambda(g(t)\otimes g(t))$ is jointly smooth in time and space there. Both the tensor of cutoff velocities and the cutoff momentum tensor are shown smooth. Their difference can therefore be differentiated repeatedly in the residual identity without relying on default derivatives.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTimeCutoffRe.summary: The quadratic cutoff stress is jointly smooth

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTimeCutoffRe.text: For a natural number $n$, the cutoff of $ng$ equals $n$ times the cutoff of $g$ at every torus point, $S_\Lambda(ng)=nS_\Lambda g$. This is proved by viewing the multiple as a finite sum of equal inputs. The identity moves binomial coefficients through the cutoff in the differentiated momentum tensor calculation.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTimeCutoffRe.summary: The Fourier cutoff respects natural scalar multiples

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTimeCutoffRe.text: This algebraic identity rewrites the projected cutoff residual (5.58) as $\mathbb P\bigl[S_\Lambda R+\operatorname{div}\mathrm{St}(g,g)\bigr]$, the Leray projection of the cutoff input residual plus the divergence of the self-stress $\mathrm{St}(g,g)=S_\Lambda g\otimes S_\Lambda g-S_\Lambda(g\otimes g)$. It is valid for arbitrary continuous torus inputs and cutoff parameters. The proof expands definitions and cancels tensor terms; it supplies neither an Euler equation nor a bound on the resulting field.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTimeCutoffRe.summary: Express the projected residual using the cutoff stress

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTimeCutoffSp.text: For any Schwartz kernel and natural order $m$, the uniform Hölder tail constant is nonnegative. The proof unfolds its absolute-moment formula and uses positivity of the constituent norms and integrals. This sign is needed when multiplying the analytic cutoff estimate by upper bounds for the differentiated input fields.

If $V$ is spatially $C^{d,1/2}$ and $m\le d$, then $V$ has spatial $C^{m,1/2}$ regularity and its order-$m$ norm is at most its order-$d$ norm. Boundedness in the $C^{d,1/2}$ hypothesis justifies all real suprema. The proof compares the nonnegative derivative sums rather than treating the displayed norm formula as meaningful for arbitrary unbounded fields.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTimeCutoffSp.summary: Lower the spatial order of a Hölder bound

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTimeJetNorms.text: For nonnegative sequences $u$ and $v$, $\sum_{i+j\le q}u_iv_j\le\bigl(\sum_{i\le q}u_i\bigr)\bigl(\sum_{j\le q}v_j\bigr)$. The auxiliary proof embeds the triangular index set into the square of all pairs. No analytic convergence is involved: every sum is finite, and nonnegativity justifies adding the omitted pairs.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTimeJetNorms.summary: The triangular convolution is bounded by the full product

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTimeMixedWor.text: Prepending one of the four directions (three label directions and the phase direction) to a mixed word is the same as applying the corresponding constant spatial-or-phase directional derivative to the remaining word. The time component of this direction is zero. The parameters $\ell$ and $h$ are fixed real weights, and $T>0$ supplies the nondegenerate closed slab on which the smooth profile is differentiated.

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTimeVelocity.text: For a jointly smooth velocity on the closed slab, fixing a spatial point yields a smooth time function on $[0,T]$. This restriction uses only composition with the constant-space inclusion. It does not need $T>0$ because no derivative is extracted here; derivative calculations elsewhere add the nondegenerate-interval condition.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTimeVelocity.summary: Fixing space preserves smoothness of the time slice

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTransverseCo.text: The affine-wave amplitude operator equals minus the strain plus twice the strain followed by projection in the covector direction, written with the rank-one operator and $(\|\kappa\|^2)^{-1}$. This algebraic identity holds even at zero covector because both sides use totalized inversion. Nonzero covectors are required separately when this expression is interpreted as the transverse geometric projection.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTransverseCo.summary: Separate the strain and projected strain terms

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTransverseCo.text: For any continuous bilinear map $B$, combining two jointly smooth coefficient fields on the same set yields another jointly smooth field there. The set need not be a nondegenerate slab, since this statement only preserves already supplied regularity. The auxiliary statement proves smoothness before mixed derivative estimates are applied to coefficient products.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTransverseCo.summary: Bilinear combinations of smooth coefficients stay smooth

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTransverseCo.text: A constant coefficient field $v$ satisfies the mixed bound $|D^n\partial_t^iv|\le C_nA\mathsf D^{pn}$ with amplitude $A=1$ and cost sequence constantly equal to $|v|$, whenever $\mathsf D\ge1$. Every positive-order derivative vanishes, so the only nonzero case is time and spatial order zero. This includes the identity coefficient in the transverse projection without assuming a positive time duration in the statement.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTransverseCo.summary: Constant coefficients satisfy the mixed derivative bound

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTransverseCo.text: This continuous bilinear map turns two vectors into a rank-one endomorphism by combining the inner-product functional with scalar multiplication. Its diagonal gives the operator used in the projection along the covector. Bundling it as a bilinear map lets the mixed derivative product theorem estimate that projection without inventing a new calculus rule.

Applying the continuous bilinear map $(v,w)\mapsto v\otimes w$ to the same vector twice gives exactly the rank-one operator $v\otimes v$, acting by $x\mapsto(v\cdot x)v$. The equality is definitional and holds also at zero. It connects the continuous bilinear representation used in the estimates to the geometric rank-one projection expression used in the transverse amplitude equation.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTransverseCo.summary: The diagonal bilinear map is the rank-one operator

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTransverseCo.text: For positive $\lambda$, evaluating the pressure-slope formula $(\kappa\cdot f-2\kappa\cdot MV)/|\kappa|^2$ at $\lambda^{-1}\kappa$ multiplies its unnormalized value by $\lambda$. This isolates the inverse-carrier gain in the pressure estimate. The algebraic identity also handles $\kappa=0$ by a separate case using the convention $x/0=0$, so it must not be mistaken for a theorem asserting nonvanishing of the wave covector.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalTransverseCo.summary: Normalize the covector in the pressure slope

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalWaveRelayTim.text: A family $f$ of relay coefficients has degree $d$ when there is one nonnegative spatial cost sequence $K_n$ such that every admissible input $s$ yields a coefficient field $f_s$ smooth on its slab $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3$ with mixed bound $\|D_x^n\partial_t^if_s\|\le K_nA^d\mathsf D^{16n}$ for $i\le q$, where $A$ and $\mathsf D$ are the scales of $s$. The existential choice of $K$ precedes the input $s$. This ordering expresses uniformity over stages, rather than permitting each stage to choose a new cost.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalWaveRelayTim.summary: One cost sequence controls a family of relay coefficients

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalWaveRelayTim.text: Two relay coefficient families with the same amplitude power can be added while retaining that power and spatial slope. Their nonnegative cost sequences are added pointwise, and smoothness is preserved on every admissible slab. This is used after smaller powers have been enlarged to a common degree in the relay coefficient formulas.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalWaveRelayTim.summary: Add relay families with the same amplitude exponent

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalWaveRelayTim.text: Combining two relay families of amplitude powers $d$ and $d'$ through a fixed continuous bilinear map gives power $d+d'$. Their amplitudes multiply, and $A^dA^{d'}=A^{d+d'}$. The mixed product estimate supplies a single nonnegative output cost array. Spatial slope sixteen remains unchanged because Leibniz distributes the spatial order between the factors.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalWaveRelayTim.summary: Bilinear relay combinations add amplitude exponents

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalWaveRelayTim.text: If two coefficient families agree pointwise for every admissible input, every time, and every spatial point, the uniform relay bound of one transfers to the other with the same degree. The proof uses equality of functions, so it changes only the expression of the field. It does not weaken the bound, alter the cost sequence, or create an estimate from equality alone.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalWaveRelayTim.summary: Replace a relay coefficient family by an equal formula

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalWaveRelayTim.text: A fixed continuous linear map $L$ applied to a relay coefficient family preserves its amplitude power $d$ and spatial slope. The new uniform cost sequence is the old sequence multiplied by the operator norm $\|L\|$. Smoothness and mixed estimates are transported for each admissible input, while the cost is chosen once before that input.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalWaveRelayTim.summary: Fixed linear maps preserve a relay family bound

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalWaveRelayTim.text: If a relay family is controlled with amplitude exponent $d$ and $d\le d'$, it is also controlled with exponent $d'$. The proof uses $A\ge1$ from every admissible input. The cost array and smoothness are unchanged, allowing several coefficient formulas of different algebraic degrees to share one larger amplitude power.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalWaveRelayTim.summary: Increase the allowed amplitude power of a relay family

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalWaveRelayTim.text: Multiplying a relay family by a fixed real scalar preserves its amplitude exponent and uniform-family property. The proof treats scalar multiplication as a continuous linear map, so its absolute size enters the cost array. This accounts for fixed factors such as minus one, two, and minus two in the normalized potential and pressure coefficients.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalWaveRelayTim.summary: Scale a relay coefficient family by a fixed scalar

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalWaveRelayTim.text: The difference of two relay families with equal amplitude powers is again a family at that power. The proof applies the scalar-multiplication rule with minus one and then the addition rule. This retains one uniform cost sequence for the two terms of the time derivative of the normalized potential.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalWaveRelayTim.summary: Subtract relay families without changing the common exponent

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalWaveRelayTim.text: This record collects a positive slab length $T$, scales $\mathsf D,A\ge1$, strain $M$ and covector $k$ jointly smooth on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3$, nonvanishing of $k(t,x)$ at every slab point, and three mixed bounds through the fixed time order $q$ with the input cost array. The bounds cover $M$, $k$ and the reciprocal squared norm $|k|^{-2}$, all with amplitude $A$ and spatial slope sixteen. They are supplied components of the record, not conclusions obtained by constructing it.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalWaveRelayTim.summary: Admissible strain and covector data for relay coefficients

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalWaveRelayTim.text: For admissible relay data with covector $k$, this is the scalar field $(t,x)\mapsto |k(t,x)|^{-2}$. It is one of the three primitive coefficient factors used in the relay polynomial estimates. The input record already carries its mixed jet bound, so the definition does not derive reciprocal estimates from a covector bound alone.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalWaveRelayTim.summary: The reciprocal squared norm of the relay covector

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalWaveRelayTim.text: The reciprocal squared covector norm $|k|^{-2}$ of admissible relay data is jointly smooth on its time-label slab $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3$. Smoothness of $|k|^2$ follows from the supplied smoothness of $k$, and the supplied nonvanishing of $k$ justifies inversion at every slab point. This regularity statement is separate from the already supplied mixed bound on $|k|^{-2}$; neither one is inferred from the other.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalWaveRelayTim.summary: The relay reciprocal is smooth on the valid slab

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalWaveRelayTim.text: The geometric curl row at label width $\ell$ equals $\ell^{-1}$ times the unit-width continuous linear row applied to the inverse coframe $G$. No positivity or nonzero-width hypothesis is needed for this algebraic equality. Its use as an estimate of an actual rescaled derivative requires the positive label scale supplied by the construction.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalWaveRelayTim.summary: Extract the inverse label width from the curl row

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalWaveRelayTim.text: The material relay row at label width $\ell$ is $\ell^{-1}$ times its fixed unit-width bilinear expression in the inverse coframe $G$ and strain $M$. This identity holds for every real width, including zero, where the convention $0^{-1}=0$ makes both sides vanish. It separates a fixed scalar cost from the two parent coefficients before mixed derivative bounds are applied.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalWaveRelayTim.summary: Extract the inverse label width from the material row

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalWaveRelayTim.text: The geometric pressure-gradient row at label width $\ell$ is $\ell^{-1}$ times the unit-width continuous linear row of the inverse coframe. This equality separates the label normalization from the field dependence. It is valid even at zero width as an algebraic identity under the convention $0^{-1}=0$, and does not claim that a degenerate width represents a meaningful spatial rescaling.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalWaveRelayTim.summary: Extract the inverse label width from the pressure row

_private.TorusEuler.TerminalWaveRelayTim.text: This continuous bilinear map takes an inverse coframe $G$ and strain $M$ to the unit-width material relay row. Writing $P_i$ for the unit-width curl-row map, its value is $M\circ P_i(G)-P_i(G\circ M)$. Thus strain acts after the curl row in the first term. Packaging it as one bilinear map lets the mixed product estimate account for both coefficient factors.
_private.TorusEuler.TerminalWaveRelayTim.summary: The unit-width material row is a bilinear map

_private.TorusEuler.Theorem11FromInducti.text: Proves monotonicity of the activation times including the artificially stored index zero and the two equal initial activations. For successor indices it uses the nonnegative activation increments recorded in the stage family, rather than needing a fresh crossing argument. The distinction between monotonicity here and strict increase after the initial pair matters when forming the terminal-time sequence.
_private.TorusEuler.Theorem11FromInducti.summary: The entire activation sequence is nondecreasing

_private.TorusEuler.Theorem11FromInducti.text: The clock $\tau\mapsto t_{j+2}+\tau/r$ maps the normalized interval $[0,\Theta_j]$ into the actual physical interval for wave $j+2$, which runs from activation $t_{j+2}$ to the end of slab $j+2$. The rate $r$ is positive, and the recorded window equality identifies the right endpoint. This verifies the domain hypothesis needed before applying normalized wave-comparison estimates to the stored physical crossing.
_private.TorusEuler.Theorem11FromInducti.summary: The normalized clock stays inside its physical slab

_private.TorusEuler.Theorem11FromInducti.text: Defines the leading curl coefficient as $e^{-1}C^{-1}/(6A^2)$, where $C$ is the common strength constant and $A$ the comparison-window coefficient. The factor $e^{-1}$ records retained preceding-wave strength. Its strict positivity is proved separately, allowing the positive frequency power to dominate the error terms.
_private.TorusEuler.Theorem11FromInducti.summary: The positive leading coefficient in the curl estimate

_private.TorusEuler.Theorem11FromInducti.text: Proves strict positivity of the explicit leading curl coefficient. Positivity of the exponential, inverse strength constant and squared window coefficient supplies the result. This is the nondegeneracy condition used when the eventual power lower bound is converted into divergence of the central vorticity.
_private.TorusEuler.Theorem11FromInducti.summary: The leading curl contribution has positive coefficient

_private.TorusEuler.Theorem11FromInducti.text: Abbreviates three times the operator norm of the continuous linear map taking a velocity derivative to its curl. This constant controls the accumulated error terms in the central vorticity lower bound. It does not depend on the stage family or the index, and no positivity stronger than the needed norm properties is built into its name.
_private.TorusEuler.Theorem11FromInducti.summary: A common coefficient for converting gradient errors to curl

_private.TorusEuler.Theorem11FromInducti.text: For all sufficiently large $j$, gives $t_{j+2}\ge0$ and a central-curl lower bound $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\ge c\lambda_{j+1}^{1/8}-B\lambda_{j+1}^{1/32}-B$ on the half-open interval $[t_{j+2},t_{j+3})$: a positive multiple of frequency $j+1$ to power $1/8$, minus an error of power $1/32$ and a constant. Hypotheses include $\lambda_0\ge2$, containment of every slab in a common one and activations before $T$, half-length bounds $\tau_j\le\lambda_j^{-1/16}$, and uniform first-derivative convergence on every earlier compact time interval.
_private.TorusEuler.Theorem11FromInducti.summary: The limit retains a growing curl on activation intervals

_private.TorusEuler.Theorem11FromInducti.text: Expresses the physical first coupling $\nu$ as the frame entry $B_{12}$ of the central derivative $\nabla u_j(t,0)$ of stage $j$ at activation $t_{j+2}$. The preceding pair determines the frame, and the recorded equality of background matrices identifies the background matrix at activation. This is the bridge from the physical comparison notation to the coupling inequalities carried by the stage family.
_private.TorusEuler.Theorem11FromInducti.summary: The first coupling uses the actual older gradient

_private.TorusEuler.Theorem11FromInducti.text: Identifies the physical comparison initial strength with the product $|k_{j+1}||\mathbf a_{j+1}|$ of the recorded preceding wave-vector and amplitude norms at activation $t_{j+2}$. The equality uses both recorded identifications of the preceding vector and amplitude. It is a compatibility fact, ensuring that the stored strength bounds concern the same pair used in the comparison.
_private.TorusEuler.Theorem11FromInducti.summary: The comparison strength uses the recorded preceding wave

_private.TorusEuler.Theorem11FromInducti.text: Under the base-frequency lower bound, every stage frequency is at least two and therefore nonzero. This elementary consequence is stated separately because the scaled wave coordinates divide by the carrier frequency. It prevents those formulas from relying on Lean’s totalized value for division by zero.

Shows that the order at every positive stage index is at least one. At the first stage this is the initial-order equality; later it is part of the maximal admissible-order condition. The result licenses order-one correction estimates throughout the central curl argument, even before using eventual growth of the orders.
_private.TorusEuler.Theorem11FromInducti.summary: The construction always retains first derivatives

_private.TorusEuler.Theorem11FromInducti.text: Rewrites the physical active interval as the closed interval from activation $t_{j+2}$ to the end of slab $j+2$. The only substantive identification is the stored clock endpoint equality. This lets estimates stated on the stage interval satisfy hypotheses phrased using the physical amplification object.
_private.TorusEuler.Theorem11FromInducti.summary: The comparison interval equals the recorded stage slab

_private.TorusEuler.Theorem11FromInducti.text: Assuming the base frequency satisfies $\lambda_0\ge2$, bounds the normalized comparison window $\Theta_j$ by the common window coefficient $2\sqrt{8C\pi}$ times $(4\log\lambda_{j+4})^4$. The proof uses the actual clock endpoint, strength and coupling bounds, and the scheduled physical half-length. The conclusion concerns normalized time, not the duration of the physical interval itself.
_private.TorusEuler.Theorem11FromInducti.summary: Each comparison window has a logarithmic upper bound

_private.TorusEuler.Theorem11FromInducti.text: Defines the positive coefficient $2\sqrt{8C\pi}$ from the common strength constant $C$ of the central waves. It is independent of the stage index. The following estimates use it to bound normalized window lengths by fourth powers of logarithmic gains, with positivity proved separately from the recorded lower bound $C\ge2$.
_private.TorusEuler.Theorem11FromInducti.summary: A fixed coefficient for comparison-window bounds

_private.TorusEuler.Theorem11FromInducti.text: Uses the common strength lower bound $C\ge2$ and positivity of $\pi$ to show that the window coefficient $2\sqrt{8C\pi}$ is positive. This justifies later divisions by its square in the vorticity coefficient. The theorem concerns one explicit constant and supplies no bound on the physical window until the separate comparison estimate is invoked.
_private.TorusEuler.Theorem11FromInducti.summary: The window coefficient is strictly positive

_private.TorusEuler.Theorem11FromInducti.text: Extracts the pointwise bound $\|D^m(u_{n+1}-u_n-w_{n+1})(t,x)\|\le\lambda_{n+1}^{-1}$ for the order-$m$ spatial derivative of the nonoscillatory correction, where $w_{n+1}$ is the oscillatory increment. The hypotheses restrict $m$ to at most the scheduled order of stage $n+1$, and time to the child slab. The proof uses the accompanying half-Hölder regularity statement to justify reading the finite norm as a derivative bound.
_private.TorusEuler.Theorem11FromInducti.summary: The correction controls each spatial derivative

_private.TorusEuler.Theorem11FromInducti.text: For all sufficiently large stages $n$, bounds the derivative $\nabla u_n(t,0)$ of the lifted velocity at the origin by $\lambda_n^9$, throughout its closed slab. Bernstein bounds use the stored Fourier support and velocity norm. The conclusion is eventual in the stage index, not an assertion that every stage satisfies this bound under $\lambda_0\ge2$ alone.
_private.TorusEuler.Theorem11FromInducti.summary: The older central gradient has a polynomial bound

_private.TorusEuler.Theorem11FromInducti.text: Assuming $\lambda_0\ge2$, proves $\lambda_n^{288}\le\lambda_{n+1}$: the next frequency is at least the current frequency raised to the natural power 288. The scheduled exponent $K=320b(q+1)$ is at least 320, so this deliberately weaker exponent follows by monotonicity of powers above one. It later absorbs the older gradient into a much smaller power of the next scale.
_private.TorusEuler.Theorem11FromInducti.summary: Successive frequencies dominate a fixed large power

_private.TorusEuler.Theorem11FromInducti.text: Proves $4\log\lambda_{i+3}\le(\log\lambda_i)^2$. The stage record supplies the threshold floor (1.13) and greatest-admissible-order rule used by the schedule lemma. This is an algebraic scheduling estimate; it does not require adding a new base-frequency hypothesis to this declaration.
_private.TorusEuler.Theorem11FromInducti.summary: Three later frequencies obey the logarithmic bound

_private.TorusEuler.Theorem11FromInducti.text: Carries the lower bound two from the initial frequency to every index: $\lambda_n\ge2$. The proof combines the assumption $\lambda_0\ge2$ with frequency monotonicity. This small fact supplies positivity for inverses, real powers and logarithms; it should not be read as a separate analytic estimate on a stage velocity.
_private.TorusEuler.Theorem11FromInducti.summary: Every frequency exceeds the initial floor

_private.TorusEuler.Theorem11FromInducti.text: Assuming $\lambda_0\ge2$, the power recurrence $\lambda_{i+1}=\lambda_i^{K}$ makes the full frequency sequence monotone. The exponent parameter $b\ge1$ already has this positive lower bound in the record. This is a schedule consequence, independent of the velocity fields, and is repeatedly used to transfer a base-frequency threshold to every later stage.
_private.TorusEuler.Theorem11FromInducti.summary: The stage frequencies never decrease

_private.TorusEuler.Theorem11FromInducti.text: Shows $\lambda_n\to+\infty$ as $n\to\infty$, assuming the initial frequency satisfies $\lambda_0\ge2$. The result follows from the prescribed power recurrence. It supports eventual absorption of fixed constants and shrinking localization radii, rather than asserting any finite numerical cutoff index.
_private.TorusEuler.Theorem11FromInducti.summary: The frequency sequence escapes every bound

_private.TorusEuler.ThresholdSelection.0.text: This noncomputable real sum adds the absolute values of a finite family of costs over derivative and depth indices up to $7\,\mathrm{frequencyExponent}(b,s)$ inclusive. Absolute values make each included cost bounded by the sum. The function places no restriction on how the original costs depend on order or depth.

_private.TorusEuler.TorusFourier.0.Torus.text: The Fourier mode equals $\exp(2\pi i\,k\cdot x)$, the complex exponential of the linear phase $x\mapsto2\pi i\,k\cdot x$. This reformulation exposes a composition of a smooth exponential with a bounded real linear map. It is an internal bridge used by the smoothness and derivative proofs, with no restriction on the integer frequency.
_private.TorusEuler.TorusFourier.0.Torus.summary: Writing the Fourier character as exponential of phase

_private.TorusEuler.TorusFourier.0.Torus.text: This real continuous linear map sends a label vector to the complex number $2\pi i\,k\cdot x$. It packages the phase in a form accepted by Fréchet differentiation. The scalar field for differentiation is real even though the output and subsequent exponential are complex.
_private.TorusEuler.TorusFourier.0.Torus.summary: The linear phase of an integer Fourier character

_private.TorusEuler.TorusFourier.0.Torus.text: Evaluation of the phase map gives $2\pi i$ times the sum of the three products $k_i x_i$. The integer frequency and real label coordinates are cast into complex numbers. This calculation reconciles the Euclidean inner-product implementation with the coordinate formula used for Fourier differentiation.
_private.TorusEuler.TorusFourier.0.Torus.summary: Expanding the complex linear phase in coordinates

_private.TorusEuler.TorusFourier.0.Torus.text: At a point $x$, the derivative of the mode $e^{2\pi ik\cdot x}$ is its complex value at $x$ multiplying the linear phase map $v\mapsto2\pi i\,k\cdot v$. The statement packages the entire derivative, not just coordinate derivatives. Real differentiation and complex scalar multiplication are reconciled explicitly in the proof.
_private.TorusEuler.TorusFourier.0.Torus.summary: The Fourier character derivative is its value times phase

_private.TorusEuler.TorusFourier.0.Torus.text: Embedding the negative integer frequency into real Euclidean space gives the negative of its embedding. This coordinatewise cast identity underlies symmetry of frequency balls and parity arguments for Fourier sums. It does not use any bound on the frequency or any property of a field.
_private.TorusEuler.TorusFourier.0.Torus.summary: Embedding integer frequencies commutes with negation

_private.TorusEuler.TorusLabelFlow.0.Tor.text: Assume a uniform spatial Lipschitz bound on a closed interval, two solutions of $\dot x=U(t,x)$ within that interval, and equality at one time $s$ in it. The trajectories then agree throughout the interval. The proof uses forward or backward uniqueness according to the order of the comparison time.
_private.TorusEuler.TorusLabelFlow.0.Tor.summary: Lipschitz trajectories with one common value agree on the interval

_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage..text: For a time in the closed slab, restricts joint all-order smoothness to the corresponding spatial slice. The statement is generic over real normed target spaces. It supplies the ordinary spatial differentiability used throughout the child pressure and residual proofs, without requiring an open time extension.
_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage..summary: A slab-smooth function has smooth spatial slices

_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage..text: Identifies the Fourier coefficient obtained by complexifying the underlying continuous function with the coefficient defined by complexifying the bundled half-Hölder object. Evaluation commutes with the continuous linear complexification. This compatibility allows the strong Leray multiplier coefficient identity to be used by the finite-band Fourier reconstruction theorem.
_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage..summary: Both Fourier interfaces compute the same coefficients

_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage..text: Reads the underlying continuous torus function from a bundled half-Hölder vector field. This permits the finite-band Fourier interface to consume an object originally built for the bounded Leray operator. The operation preserves the actual pointwise function; it merely forgets the extra regularity data from its type.
_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage..summary: Forget the Hölder bound but retain the function

_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage..text: Expands the divergence of a sum at a point where both vector fields are differentiable. The finite coordinate trace is additive once the Fréchet derivative addition rule applies. This local helper is used twice when splitting the true residual into time derivative, advection and pressure gradient.
_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage..summary: Divergence is additive at differentiability points

_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage..text: Proves evenness of the totalized Fréchet derivative of an odd vector function, with no separate differentiability assumption. Reflection is an invertible continuous linear map, so its derivative transformation rule remains valid when a derivative is absent. In the child construction the velocity is smooth, giving this identity its classical differential meaning.
_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage..summary: The derivative of an odd function is even

_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage..text: If a half-Hölder torus field is finite band and its Euclidean lift is odd, proves that the lift of its concrete Leray projection is odd. Fourier coefficients transform with a minus sign under reflected frequency, while the angular Leray symbol is even. Exact finite reconstruction transfers coefficient symmetry to pointwise symmetry.
_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage..summary: Leray projection preserves odd finite-band fields

_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage..text: Identifies the torus image of the negative Euclidean point with the negative of its torus image. The proof is coordinatewise compatibility of the additive-circle quotient with negation. This algebraic identity translates oddness of physical lifts into the reflection relation needed for Fourier coefficients.
_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage..summary: Spatial reflection descends to torus negation

_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage..text: For a smooth spatially periodic vector field, constructs a half-Hölder torus representative of its actual Fréchet derivative. The representative agrees after lifting at every spatial point, and its norm is at most the original order-one spatial norm times the square root of two. The estimate accounts for the representation change.
_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage..summary: The velocity derivative has a controlled torus representative

_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage..text: Extracts half-Hölder order zero for the Fréchet derivative of a field with half-Hölder order one, together with a norm bound by the original order-one norm. The derivative is contracted with the identity argument map. This moves the velocity estimate into the matrix-valued space used by pressure multipliers.
_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage..summary: One derivative lowers the available Hölder order

_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage..text: Assuming the field has half-Hölder regularity through order $P$, proves nonnegativity of the level expression $\sup|D^mf|+[D^mf]_{1/2}$ at each $m\le P$. The argument separately controls the supremum of derivative norms and the supremum of Hölder quotients. The regularity hypothesis provides the boundedness needed to interpret the real suprema, which are otherwise assigned values.
_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage..summary: Certified spatial Hölder levels are nonnegative

_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage..text: From half-Hölder regularity through order $P$ and $m\le P$, obtains regularity through order $m$ and bounds the lower spatial norm $\|f\|_{C^{m,1/2}}$ by the higher one $\|f\|_{C^{P,1/2}}$. The proof uses nonnegativity of the individual levels. It does not compare arbitrary real supremum expressions without the regularity and boundedness hypothesis.
_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage..summary: Lower derivative orders have smaller certified norms

_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage..text: Proves that negation preserves half-Hölder regularity at a fixed finite order and leaves its spatial norm unchanged. Iterated derivatives change sign, while norms and difference-quotient norms do not. The result supports rewriting cutoff error fields in whichever orientation the pressure or residual calculation requires.
_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage..summary: Negation preserves spatial Hölder norms exactly

_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedParentAdmis.text: Abbreviates the product of three unit additive circles used by continuous cutoff inputs. This is the spatial quotient of the Euclidean lift, with its existing topology and measure structures. The abbreviation introduces no velocity condition, no frequency restriction and no additional mathematical object beyond that torus.

Packages the real cutoff function as a continuous torus map. Continuity follows because its complex synthesis contains only finitely many continuous Fourier modes, followed by a continuous real-part map. The packaging is available for arbitrary symbol and scale; positivity and approximation properties are not part of this definition.
_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedParentAdmis.summary: The real cutoff as a continuous torus field

_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedParentAdmis.text: Embedding a continuous real torus field into $L^2$ and then complexifying gives the same $L^2$ element as complexifying pointwise first. Equality is established by the almost-everywhere formulas for both embeddings. This ensures that Fourier characterization of solenoidality applies to the same real field used by the cutoff construction.
_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedParentAdmis.summary: Complexification agrees before and after the L² embedding

_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedParentAdmis.text: On a nondegenerate closed interval $[a,b]$, if each curve $d_n$ has within-interval derivative $d_{n+1}$, then $d_0$ is smooth there. Differentiability supplies continuity of every curve, and induction identifies iterated within-derivatives. The strict inequality $a<b$ provides uniqueness of those derivatives at the endpoints.
_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedParentAdmis.summary: A complete time-derivative hierarchy gives smoothness on the interval

_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedParentAdmis.text: For a continuous torus field with smooth Euclidean lift, membership of its $L^2$ embedding in the endpoint solenoidal space is equivalent to vanishing classical divergence everywhere on the lift. The proof passes through integration against potential gradients. Smoothness is essential to this classical interpretation; arbitrary $L^2$ members only satisfy the weak condition.
_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedParentAdmis.summary: Weak solenoidality matches classical divergence for smooth fields

_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedParentAdmis.text: A jointly smooth velocity on a nondegenerate closed slab yields a sequence of time derivatives of each Fourier-coefficient integrand. The zeroth term is the negative Fourier mode times the complexified velocity; all jets are jointly continuous on the centered spatial cell. Their within-interval derivative relations hold at every spatial point, preparing differentiation under the integral.
_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedParentAdmis.summary: The Fourier integrand has compatible time jets

_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedParentAdmis.text: For a continuous torus field in a complete complex normed space, taking any continuous complex-linear scalar coordinate commutes with its Fourier coefficient. The proof moves the linear map through the Bochner integral after proving integrability on the compact torus. This reduces vector Fourier identities to their scalar coordinate versions.
_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedParentAdmis.summary: Linear coordinates commute with Fourier coefficients

_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedParentAdmis.text: The Fourier coefficient of the $L^2$ element associated to a continuous complex torus field equals its continuous-function Fourier coefficient. The proof uses the almost-everywhere equality between the bundled field and its $L^2$ representative inside the integral. This avoids treating a chosen representative as pointwise identical to the original field.
_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedParentAdmis.summary: Continuous and L² Fourier coefficients coincide

_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedParentAdmis.text: Applying a continuous complex-linear scalar coordinate to the cutoff field equals applying the scalar cutoff to that coordinate of the input. The identity holds for arbitrary real symbol and scale parameters, because the synthesis is a finite sum. It is used to prove that an even real symbol preserves real-valued vector data.
_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedParentAdmis.summary: Linear coordinates commute with finite Fourier synthesis

_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedParentAdmis.text: The quotient map takes a negated Euclidean vector to the negation of its torus label. This coordinatewise additive identity lets oddness of a lifted field be expressed as oddness on the torus. It is the geometric substitution used in the even-symbol parity argument for the real cutoff.
_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedParentAdmis.summary: Spatial reflection descends to torus reflection

_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedParentPoiss.text: Turns all-order smoothness of a real scalar function into all-order smoothness of its gradient. The gradient is the derivative transported through the Euclidean duality isomorphism. This justifies using ordinary divergence and Leray identities on the pressure-gradient term in the finite-band projection argument.

For a complex vector field differentiable at the evaluation point, identifies divergence after real-part conversion with the real part of complex divergence. Differentiation commutes with the continuous real-linear conversion, and the finite coordinate sum commutes with real parts. The regularity assumption makes this an actual differential identity.
_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedParentPoiss.summary: Real parts commute with vector divergence

_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedParentPoiss.text: At a point where both vector fields are differentiable, identifies the divergence of their sum with the sum of divergences. The proof expands the Fréchet derivative and finite coordinate trace. The differentiability hypotheses matter because addition rules for totalized derivatives do not hold without appropriate regularity.
_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedParentPoiss.summary: Divergence distributes over a differentiable sum

_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedParentPoiss.text: Shows pointwise that the divergence of a negative vector field equals the negative divergence. The theorem is valid without a differentiability hypothesis because the underlying totalized derivative respects negation. It converts the positive finite-potential Poisson identity into the negative-divergence equation needed for the child pressure.

Defines the continuous real-linear map from the coordinate presentation of complex vectors to real Euclidean vectors. It first changes the finite-product norm representation and then takes coordinatewise real parts. This map makes differentiation of complex finite Fourier sums compatible with the real gradient and divergence used in Euler.
_private.TorusEuler.TruncatedParentPoiss.summary: Real coordinates from complex Fourier vectors
